    (hw : ∀ s∈slots,0<w s) (hwm : ∀ s∈slots,w s≤mesh)
    (hL : 0<∑ s∈slots,w s) (hz : 0≤z) (hzL : z≤∑ s∈slots,w s)

      (∑ s∈selected,w s)≤z ∧

    (bin : HeckeDetectorFiberPartition.BinLabel slots (δ/2) mesh)
    (hδ : 0 < δ) (hδtop : δ ≤ 3/4) (hk : 7/10≤κ) (hk1 : κ≤3/4) (hU : 1 ≤ U)
    (hw : ∀j∈slots,0 ≤ width j) (hL : 0 < ∑j∈slots,width j)
    (C loss : ℝ) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hne : (HeckeDetectorAmplitudeFirst.amplitudeRows rows slots U (δ/2) mesh hm width Q bin).Nonempty)
    (hcard : ((HeckeDetectorAmplitudeFirst.amplitudeRows rows slots U (δ/2) mesh hm width Q bin).card:ℝ) ≤
      C*U^(countingR κ δ (HeckeDetectorAmplitudeFirst.classMean slots (δ/2) mesh width bin/δ)+loss)) :
    let g := HeckeDetectorFiberPartition.binValue slots (δ/2) mesh bin

    (J R : Finset α) (hR : R ⊆ J) (θ : α → RayQuotient.Characters M H)
    (w σ v : α → ℝ) (t height κlow : ℝ) (B : α → ℝ)

    (hheight : 0 ≤ height) (hv : ∀ i, |v i| ≤ height) (hB : ∀ i ∈ R, 0 ≤ B i)
    (s : NaturalState Z Bmask bΦ) (hQ : s.fixedModulus = internalQ Q η₀)
    (hs : s.width ≤ Mcap) (low : O → Prop) (p : Profiles a b) (X₁ X₂ : ℝ)

This follows from exact vanishing of every gcd-row integral, arbitrary fixed-order 2D Poisson summation for d<=x^(a−delta), and complete reduced-progression Möbius cancellation for larger d. At a prescribed target c, choosing a_c=c/(2−alpha0) permits a wider exactly cancelled distinct-semiprime plateau while keeping the full correction within x^(1−c+epsilon). The whole higher-output residual estimate remains open.

hypotheses.completion: L^z(L^-z)''=z^2 A_chi^2+z A_chi'; averaging divided by z gives A_chi'. The forward prefix is bounded only after the same combined coefficient extraction, without shifting individual fractional powers across zeros or branch points.
hypotheses.nodes: 0<r<1, integer N>=2; z_j=r exp(2pi i j/N). Q=(1/N)sum_j f(z_j)/z_j. Total coefficient norm is1/r and Q is real by conjugate pairing.
hypotheses.polynomial: mu_z(p^e)=(-1)^e binom(z,e), d_z(p^e)=binom(z+e-1,e), both multiplicative. f_(n,R)(z)=sum_(d|n,d>R)mu_z(d)d_z(n/d)log^2d. Its degree<=Omega(n), f(0)=0 and f'(0)=-1_(n>R)Lambda(n)log n, including all prime powers and cofactor overlaps.
hypotheses.profile: Use the packet's fixed real signed smooth Phi supported[ell,v],0<ell<v<2/3, with Hcal(s)=K_*(s)(1-2^(1-s))^2(1-2^(1-2s))^2 and its stated growing-line decay. Hcal has double zeros at1,1/2, is nonzero in1/2<Re(s)<1 and positive at real points there. This is the actual fixed packet profile, not an arbitrary replacement.

quantitative_returns.full_spectrum: For fixed N>=2 and derivative r, |partial_s^r E(sigma+it)|<<epsilon^(2sigma+N-1)(1+|log epsilon|)^r(1+|t|)^N on buffered strips sigma>1/2. quantitative_returns.parent_norm: At theta>1/2, M_theta=sum |mu(d)|d^-2theta=zeta(2theta)/zeta(4theta), M_theta,1=M_theta sum_p log p/(p^(2theta)+1). Reconstruction cost N0^theta/2{M_theta K_U+[log N0 M_theta+2M_theta,1]K_AC}; constants may diverge at theta down to1/2.

For fixed sufficiently large j, sum m_chi(rho)^2 Ctilde has nonzero real part and at real zeros is positive real by conjugate pairing. One-sided full-source bounds for every fixed q,j give ordinary zero exclusion above theta>=1/2, conditional on the open arithmetic estimate.

raw_source_record.statement: For fixed complex theta(c)=eta0+eta1 c+eta2 c^2 with eta0 nonzero, the same-time nine-state linear cancellation constructs the complete centered cubic source, including zero Fourier channels without division. With the actual prime weight Q^(-5/6), its principal mass T_theta/(eta0 A1 A2) tends to one with power-decaying error, so complex normalization and every fixed Euler derivative cost only logarithmic powers. The full physically weighted AA operator is the repaired cubic Gauss kernel and the total source is AA plus three disjoint row/prime-label collision channels, with all cross terms retained. The original positive theta=1+(1/2)Re c has an active constant mode; the admissible complex choice theta=1-c changes active c to c-c^2. Bounded-complex actual-energy contracts give the complete incumbent upper bound, without any improved AA covariance or changed ordinary return.

raw_source_record.statement: Transporting complete Dirichlet convolution through heat regularization defines an entire associative product in which the ordinary forward and Mobius sources are exact inverses. Their ordinary product has a complete regularized Duhamel defect, including the principal forward-heat correction. Reciprocal forward heat obeys a nonlinear evolution and retains nearby zeros. The associated Gaussian weighted convolution algebra has only augmentation as a continuous multiplicative functional, while every finite-s ordinary evaluation is unbounded.

raw_source_record.statement: For the complete products B=M(D;W)S_sf(N;V) and C=M(N;V)S_sf(D;W), both B+C and B−C are large at the same selected zero. Their exact coefficients are supported on cube-free n=g^2h, with opposite mu(h) parity and every shared prime retained. Relative sixth powers force equality, so their entire cross diagonal is zero. A derivative-controlled finite mesh fixes genuinely common profiles before the signed Poisson source. The valid enclosing count inequality is U^[delta(r+m)−loss] times selected count <= X+L, where X is the complete real cross source and L=sum_all_rows |C|^2 is its full negative correction. Partitioning added rows by their own enlarged-height zero bins pays L<=U^(31/30+epsilon) over the entire central recalibrated witness region. The target exponent has reserve 1/75 above this correction. The remaining complete opposite-parity signed radical source is explicitly specified and remains open; no automatic positivity, norm improvement, or all-bin leakage improvement is claimed.

statement:
### Complete norm error

The exact signed product difference is

    U_iU_j-V_iV_j=Delta_i U_j+U_i Delta_j-Delta_i Delta_j. (D04.3)

Use |eta(a+it)|<=|a+it|/a, the fixed Gaussian exp(-t^2/2) and Plancherel of the inverse Mellin transform with the difference restricted to[-T,T]. It is valid for arbitrary L2 Fourier data; there is no truncation error in this step. The shell factor costs at most(2X)^a. Equations D04.1--2 therefore give

    ||Z_X-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X]
       << X^(q_smooth+o(1)),
    q_smooth=max(101/200+(99/200)beta-delta,1-2delta).   (D04.4)

For example X^a D_i^(1-a)D_j^(beta-a) equals
D_i D_j^beta X^o(1). The maximal allocation puts exponent.505
on the trivial collar factor and.495 on the beta factor; the reverse
single-boundary term has the same maximum. The double-boundary term
costs X^(1-2delta+o(1)). The component count and all Gaussian height
polynomials are subpower. This prices EVERY replaced endpoint and
their ordered mixed interactions, rather than dropping a boundary square.

Current G20 pays ||G-Z_X|| at exponent-1+epsilon. Thus

    ||G-Zpsi_X||_[X,2X] << X^(q_smooth+epsilon)+X^(-1+epsilon). (D04.5)

For any fixed gamma>.5 and q_smooth<gamma, the every-epsilon norm target
||Zpsi_X||<<X^(gamma+epsilon) is equivalent to the original complete
Gaussian shell norm target. Choose epsilon smaller than the fixed
margin to use the triangle inequality in both directions. No global
Mellin transform of the moving psi family is asserted: D04.5 returns
to the fixed G BEFORE zero exclusion.

All choices are fixed once per target, with constants depending on
them. Exact conservative budgets using beta=.8749:

| gamma | Conditional c | delta | first collar exponent | double collar exponent | gamma-q_smooth |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 | .1252 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0007245 |
| .87449 | .12551 | .064 | .8740755 | .872 | .0004145 |
| 5/6 | 1/6 | .106 | .8320755 | .788 | .001257833333... |
| 3/4 | 1/4 | .19 | .7480755 | .62 | .0019245 |

These are PAID COMPLEMENT budgets, not achieved moments. OPEN-SMOOTH
is the complete signed norm of Zpsi_X at its row's gamma for every
epsilon and all sufficiently large dyadic X. It is still open. The
original Gaussian pole-exclusion return is G1--G3 after D04.5.
No fixed-character or Hecke completion is deduced from a zeta-only
alternating source: those need their exact existing adapters.

Strongest objection: endpoint smoothing is often paid back by derivatives.
Here the collars are paid without derivatives; an ensuing analytic proof
of OPEN-SMOOTH must STILL debit X^(k delta) for k-th cutoff derivatives.
Even this smooth source has |V_i|<=|U_i|+|Delta_i| and only reproduces
the baseline moment exponent absent new signed arithmetic cancellation.
It is not a power gain generated by smoothness. Near gamma=.87449,
any proposed integration-by-parts saving must outweigh its.064-per-
derivative loss and establish the full two-height/component norm.

Ancestry: U-SCALE, old thin-annulus TA and native sharp-mask/Sobolev
adapters, plus W35's literal Gaussian completion. TA concerns a different
capped three-Möbius source and is not imported as this estimate. [research revision]
hybrid smoothing changes fixed kernels and is not the same moving
endpoint collar. The narrow claimed delta is this explicit literal
four-diagonal replacement and complete numerical complement price;
no literature novelty claim or new cancellation mechanism.

Functional signature: actual G11 interval factors / interior endpoint
tapers / retain signed four-diagonal sum / unpaid OPEN-SMOOTH / fixed-G
return with q_smooth and all height/TypeI/product complements paid.
Next action: seek a genuine two-height mean for these smooth factors
whose derivative cost fits the fixed margin, or stop if it cannot beat
the original sharp mean. Re-proving the collar bound is not arithmetic progress.

statement:
### New continuum-dilation variant

Replace (T10.1) by
\[
\int_X^{2X}\int_2^3|\Delta_bM(x)|^2\,db\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T10.3}
\]
The same conclusion follows by taking the Mellin integral in \(L^2([2,3],db)\). Its multiplier vector is \(m_s(b)=b^s-b^\alpha\). It vanishes as a vector only for \(s=\alpha\): a nonconstant exponential in \(\log b\) cannot be identically one on an interval.

This compact continuum also provides a useful quantitative calibration absent from the discrete two-multiplier claim. Put
\[
G_\alpha(s)=\int_2^3|b^s-b^\alpha|^2\,db.
\]
For \(\sigma\) in any fixed compact real interval,
\[
G_\alpha(\sigma+it)\gg1\qquad(|t|\ge1), \tag{T10.4}
\]
with a constant depending on that interval and \(\alpha\). Expanding the square, the cross term is
\[
2\Re\int_2^3 b^{\sigma+\alpha+it}\,db=O((1+|t|)^{-1}),
\]
uniformly in the compact \(\sigma\)-interval; the two diagonal integrals have a positive lower bound. This proves the assertion for large \(t\). Continuity and the absence of zeros prove it on the remaining compact set \(1\le|t|\le T_0\). Near \(s=\alpha\),
\[
G_\alpha(s)=|s-\alpha|^2
\int_2^3 b^{2\alpha}(\log b)^2\,db
 +O(|s-\alpha|^3).
\]
Thus the sole calibration zero is known and simple at the multiplier level; zeta is nonzero there. The proposed continuum energy is nevertheless an open Möbius estimate.

The same hypothesis has a quantitative consequence: on every compact strip \(a<\sigma_0\le\Re s\le\sigma_1\), with \(|\Im s|\ge1\),
\[
 |1/\zeta(s)|\ll_{\sigma_0,\sigma_1,\alpha}1+|\Im s|. \tag{T10.5}
\]
Indeed the shell bounds give an absolutely convergent Bochner Mellin integral \(F(s)\) whose norm is uniformly bounded on that strip; its defining norm integral has no imaginary-height growth. The exact identity is \(\|F(s)\|=\sqrt{G_\alpha(s)}/|s\zeta(s)|\). Combine it with (T10.4). This is conditional on the same open continuum energy, not on any additional arithmetic hypothesis.

On logarithmic scale, \(f(t)=e^{-\alpha t}M(e^t)\) converts \(\Delta_bM(e^t)\) to \(b^\alpha e^{\alpha t}[f(t+\log b)-f(t)]\). An averaged finite-difference/Poincaré approach is therefore an explicit next construction. It must estimate these actual increments, not invoke a generic inequality to create a Möbius power saving.

**Sources:** BA D11 for the discrete construction; continuum construction developed and independently proved during the merge.
title: New continuum-dilation variant

source_terms.handling: Original author notices and upstream licenses control; no proof bodies copied by public export.

statement:
### 2.2 Kernel coefficients and convergence

Let K_6(s)=sum k_6(n)n^(-s), with local factors

    p=2,3:  (1-z)^2,
    p>=5:   (1-z)^2/(1-2z)
           = 1 + z^2/(1-2z)
           = 1 + sum_{j>=2} 2^(j-2) z^j.                 (2.3)

Its formal Dirichlet inverse J_6(s)=sum j_6(n)n^(-s) has

    p=2,3:  (1-z)^(-2) = sum_{j>=0}(j+1)z^j,
    p>=5:   (1-2z)/(1-z)^2
           = 1 - z^2/(1-z)^2
           = 1 - sum_{j>=2}(j-1)z^j.                    (2.4)

In particular the p>=5 inverse has zero coefficient at p, and all
its coefficients at p^j, j>=2, are negative; they are not alternating.

Fix sigma>1/2 and set r_p=p^(-sigma). Since

    2 r_p <= 2*5^(-sigma) < 2/sqrt(5) < 1,

all geometric sums in (2.3) converge absolutely. Their exact absolute
Dirichlet norms are

    sum_n |k_6(n)| n^(-sigma)
      = (1+r_2)^2 (1+r_3)^2
          product_{p>=5} (1 + r_p^2/(1-2r_p)) < infinity, (2.5)

    sum_n |j_6(n)| n^(-sigma)
      = (1-r_2)^(-2) (1-r_3)^(-2)
          product_{p>=5} (1 + r_p^2/(1-r_p)^2) < infinity.(2.6)

The denominators are bounded away from zero at this fixed sigma,
and sum_p p^(-2sigma)<infinity. These facts prove convergence of
the positive products, hence of the absolute coefficient sums.

The candidate local poles 1-2p^(-s)=0 have

    Re(s) = log(2)/log(p) <= log(2)/log(5)
          = 0.4306765580... < 1/2.                       (2.7)

The inverse's possible local zeros have exactly those real parts.
The factors 1-p^(-s) have no zeros at positive real part. Thus there
are no omitted local zeros or poles in Re(s)>1/2. Normal convergence
of the products, or the absolutely convergent identity K_6 J_6=1,
also rules out an infinite-product zero there. The factor at 2 has
no denominator 1-2*2^(-s): that factor was common to G and F and
has been cancelled as a coefficient identity on Re(s)>1.

The choice to exclude 3 matters for the advertised threshold. If
3 were allowed, its corresponding geometric factor would have a
pole at log(2)/log(3)=0.6309297535... . This objection does not
apply to the actual (de,6)=1 cell.

At sigma=1/2 the products (2.5)--(2.6) do not converge absolutely:
their logarithms have a divergent prime harmonic contribution.
No endpoint absolute-convergence claim is made.
title: 2.2 Kernel coefficients and convergence

statement:
### F26.O — Fredholm models with every compensator retained

The prime diagonal \(T_s=\mathrm{diag}(p^{-s})\) has \(\det(I-T_s)=1/\zeta(s)\) in \(\Re s>1\). Its Hilbert–Schmidt regularization extends farther, but
\(1/\zeta(s)=\det_2(I-T_s)e^{-P(s)}\): the omitted prime compensator carries the unresolved continuation. Bounded similarity does not repair the trace-class failure. A non-diagonal arithmetic operator remains a permissible new construction only after an exact determinant identity, prime-power coefficients and every factor where a zero can hide are supplied. The arithmetic residue resolvent in §9 is a different valid operator, with its own unproved source-specific estimate.
title: F26.O — Fredholm models with every compensator retained

source_terms.handling: Original author notices and upstream licenses control; no proof bodies copied by public export.

statement:
## 4. Exact restorations and the author's two estimates

For an ideal q define

    A_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Then sum_(q|g) A_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G), A_G(q)=0 below G, and |A_G(q)|<=tau(q). Since the original inverse index a is squarefree, every contributing q|a is squarefree. With a=qc,b=qd the author's exact identity is

    B_g=sum_(q sf) A_G(q)mu(q)phi(q)^2/(Nq)
                    M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/Nq).              (R7)

M^(q) has the extra condition (c,q)=1. The b/q index has no such condition. The original profiles and all character zeros remain literal.

The mask is restored by the full q-smooth series

    M^(q)(E)=sum_(h q-smooth) phi(h)/sqrt(Nh) M(E/Nh). (R8)

At p|q, its local inverse coefficient is mu*(1,1,1,...), which equals the unit sequence. Every p^j is necessary. Complete multiplicativity with zero extensions proves R8 even when p is a row hole. For each actual annulus the sum is finite. After taking absolute values its full mass is at most

    product_(p|q) (1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <= C_e (Nq)^e.

Separate finitely many small primes, then bound each remaining factor by (Np)^e. A polynomial fixed inverse puncture can be included with q; its total mass is still a freely allocated U^epsilon. Slots keep their original frozen holes in MI's bounded coefficients. No quotient of a possibly zero character value is taken.

Hilbert Minkowski, R4 and R6 give

    ||B_g Q|| <= H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2)
        sum_(Nq>=G) (Nq)^(-1-beta/2+small)
      <= H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2) G^(-beta/2).   (R9)

Ideal counting on dyadic shells is O(X), from the underlying fixed lattice. Extracted row-dependent character phases have absolute value at most one and act only as contractions in the positive norm; they do not become new MI column coefficients. All divisor, restoration and finite-support losses are extracted as U^epsilon before a convergent positive extension. Squaring gives the first author estimate. The q^-1 alone would not yield this power; the same-bin shortened plain contributes the additional q^(-beta/2).

For s_2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2), k|s_2(b) iff k^2|b. The corresponding exact expansion is

    S_bad(D)=sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi(k^2)/(Nk)
                              S(D/(Nk)^2).

Here k is not squarefree. R4 and ideal counting give

    |S_bad(D)| <= H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2) H^(-beta),  (R10)

including all prime powers and equality at H. This pays M S_bad Q by R6. It does not by itself pay the signed subtraction of the large-gcd intersection.

For that intersection let q be squarefree and L=lcm(q,k^2). At each prime write i=v_p(q) in{0,1} and j=v_p(k)>=0. Then

    v_p(L)=max(i,2j)=i+2j-min(i,j),
    L=q k^2/(q,k).

Writing a=qc,b=Ld gives exactly the author's formula (15), with coefficient A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL), inverse M^(q)(R/Nq), and plain S(D/NL). No coprimality between c and d is inserted. After R8, R4 and R6 the remaining positive weight is, in norm notation,

    w_beta(q,k)=q^(-1/2)L^(-(1+beta)/2)
       =q^(-1-beta/2)k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2).    (R11)

Its local factors are p^(-1-beta/2) for i=1,j=0; p^(-j(1+beta)) for i=0; and p^(-1/2-j(1+beta)) for i=1,j>=1. These exhaust all valuations. In particular q=k=p has weight p^(-3/2-beta), not p^(-2-3beta/2). The falsely independent lcm would omit the positive correction p^((1+beta)/2).

For fixed q, put d=(q,k), k=de. Drop only positive coprimality restrictions after the exact split. Uniformly for beta in its compact interval,

    sum_(Nk>=H) k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
      <= C sum_(d|q) d^(-(1+beta)/2)
                         max(1,H/Nd)^(-beta)
      <= C H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) d^((beta-1)/2)
      <= C H^(-beta) tau(q).                          (R12)

For Nd<=H, this is the e-tail from H/Nd. For Nd>H, use the complete e sum and the inequality d^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)d^((beta-1)/2). Thus large common divisors are included, not silently omitted. beta<1 makes the remaining divisor exponent negative. Combining R11--12 with q-tail counting proves

    sum_(q sf,Nq>=G,Nk>=H) w_beta(q,k)
       <= U^epsilon G^(-beta/2) H^(-beta)              (R13)

on the actual polynomial support; bounded divisor weights and the restoration mass are included in the small loss. Therefore

    ||B_gs Q||^2 <= H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)
                                 G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).

Now B_s=M S_bad-B_gs is an exact signed difference. Hilbert triangle, not signed-subset monotonicity, proves the author's second bound since G>=1. I found no missing shared-prime exponent in this step.
title: 4. Exact restorations and the author's two estimates

statement:
## What remains usable for a new zero-free estimate

For every fixed h,q,r and proposed gamma<1, choose a sufficiently large
FIXED admissible u with theta(u,r)>gamma, then let N grow. This gives
an obstruction uniform over admissible band placements. It does not say
one prescribed fixed-u family's exponent equals1, or that every natural
residual fails. Bands with theta<=gamma, cross-prime correlations,
changing profiles and growing collars remain outside that conclusion.

Subtracting a truncated deterministic Buchstab mean W_q=H+E preserves
the complete E response on a finite quotient block[a,b]:

    -E(N/(pa))Delta_a+E(N/[p(b+1)])Delta_b
       -sum_(m=a+1)^b E(N/(pm))(Delta_m-Delta_(m-1)).    (77.14)

The identical H expression must be restored. Arbitrary bounded defects
can have variation of order the state count. Fixed K gives only the stated
logarithmic accuracy; growing K requires new uniform estimates, transition
and collar payments, plus the restored H contribution.

A sufficient complete return still needs, for EACH fixed ordinary
character, every epsilon>0 and ALL large N, both |F(N,1)| and the entire
signed defect in(77.1) bounded by N^(gamma+epsilon). Then the actual
Mertens bound follows, with noninteger x handled by flooring. Abel/Mellin
continuation of 1/L pays all finite heights and derivatives, ramified and
imprimitive zeros, and the principal pole. No Hecke or moving-conductor
extension is inferred. The current first-gain requirement is

    gamma<.8748540364; theta(u,r)>1-c iff u>r/c-r-1.

Nearer gains,1/6 and1/4 use this same complete budget. The old frozen
.125143/.125145 conditional examples no longer improve the incumbent.
No new arithmetic input for that return is proved here.

This pass discovered six mechanisms before developing the actual renewal
source and a signed repair. It resolves a live missing prerequisite and
redirects a concrete approach. Next use a proved relation across prime
bands or a fully controlled varying profile/collar; another fixed profile
alone cannot supply the hoped-for power. The full29-family/109-child
portfolio and the discarded mechanisms remain. Tenenbaum/Alladi retain
the friable-asymptotic credit, G92/W49 the source and coalescence credit,
and the independent review its C1 completion and BV extension. Literature
priority is not asserted. Original09:20/09:50 deadlines remain missed;
same-owner recovery preserved the completed source, evidence and handoff.
title: What remains usable for a new zero-free estimate

statement:
### 7.2 Calibration and full remaining price

The complete parameter rows remain:

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2187/2500=.8748 | 7 | 6/7 | .1252 |
| 5/6 | 6 | 5/6 | 1/6 |
| 3/4 | 4 | 3/4 | 1/4 |

The nearer prospective gain over c11 is 135091/2500000000=.0000540364. Equality at the latter two low-source endpoints is permitted; (5.4) even removes their low-source epsilon loss. The arithmetic input must still hold for every epsilon. These are not accepted endpoint increases or new source admissions.

For squarefree n, J^omega(n)=d_J(n). The complete residual obeys |r_J(n)|<=C_J d_J(n) on that support and zero elsewhere. Elementary repeated harmonic summation gives sum_(n<=x)d_J(n)<<_J x log^(J-1)(2x). Paying every filter term yields the entire bound

    |T_(p,J)(x)| <<_(p,J)x log^(J-1)(2x).                  (7.2)

Every p^a coefficient p^a meets its actual argument x/p^a; their powers cancel in this estimate. Terms with x/p^a<1 are empty. The bound proves only exponent one, including in shell L1 and L2. It misses each target by 1-gamma plus logarithms. Nothing in the new observation criterion, determinant dimension, positive permanent or fixed-color calculation supplies that power.

The next color t=8 has the available exponent 7/8, above gamma11 by .0001459636. A better bound for that one color would pay one extra sector; it would still leave every higher chain depth. This proximity does not calculate a new zero-free constant.

## A growing high moment with an explicitly paid arithmetic sector

Take K=2m. The polynomial L bound just used and a Gaussian square completion imply

  H_(X,K)(sigma)<=exp(O_(q,sigma,tau)(Klog(K+2))) Q_(m,Y)(sigma),
  Q_(m,Y)(sigma)=integral_R e^(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt. (N22)

Here the constant may be fixed before X and m. Expand M_Y^m exactly. If N_(m,Y)(n) denotes the number of ORDERED factorizations n=d_1...d_m with each d_i<=Y squarefree, then

  [n^(-s)]M_Y(s)^m=lambda(n)chi(n)N_(m,Y)(n),               (N23)

where lambda(n)=(-1)^Omega(n). This follows since every surviving product of Möbius signs equals lambda(n). All factorizations at a fixed n have the SAME phase; their multiplicities do not cancel internally. Repeated primes between different factors and squareful output integers remain. Ramified outputs have chi(n)=0 exactly. Also N_(m,Y)(n)<=d_m(n), with support n<=N:=Y^m=X^(1/2+o(1)).

Gaussian integration, with no frequency selection, gives

  Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_(n,k<=N)
    lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)conj(chi(k)) N_(m,Y)(n)N_(m,Y)(k)
      (nk)^(-sigma) exp(-(log(n/k))^2/tau).                (N24)

All ordered pairs and both conjugate terms are present. The full sum is real and nonnegative because it is the integral defining Q; individual sectors need not be nonnegative.

The diagonal is bounded by

  sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_n d_m(n)^2 n^(-2sigma)
      <=sqrt(4pi/tau) zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)=X^o(1).           (N25)

For completeness d_m(p^j)^2<=d_(m^2)(p^j): a pair of weak compositions of j into m parts can be realized as the row and column margins of a nonnegative integer m-by-m matrix. Choose one such matrix deterministically for each pair. Different margins give different matrices, so this is an injection into the m^2-part weak compositions. Multiply over primes. The exponent m^2=O((log X)^(2/3)) is why this growing order still has a subpower diagonal. A bound stated only for fixed m would not suffice.

Write n=ga,k=gb with (a,b)=1. The exact phase is lambda(a)lambda(b)chi(a)conj(chi(b))|chi(g)|^2. The absolute price of the sector g>=G, including any diagonal it contains, is bounded uniformly for1<=G<=N by

  P_(g>=G) <<_(sigma,tau,epsilon) X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G.    (N26)

Proof: d_m(uv)<=d_m(u)d_m(v), as follows prime by prime by deterministically splitting each composition of j+k into compositions of j and k. For any fixed delta>0, drop coprimality and the Gaussian, use N_(m,Y)<=d_m, and bound each residual sum by

  sum_(a<=N/g) d_m(a)a^(-sigma)
    <=(N/g)^(1-sigma+delta) zeta(1+delta)^m.

Consequently its price is at most

  C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta) zeta(1+delta)^(2m)
          sum_(g>=G) d_m(g)^2 g^(-2-2delta)
   <=C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta) G^(-1-delta)
                              zeta(1+delta)^(m^2+2m).

Because log N=(1/2+o(1))log X and m^2=o(log X), choose delta sufficiently small for the requested epsilon, then take X large. This proves(N26), with constants uniform in the K-band. No fixed-conductor dependence is needed for this upper bound beyond |chi|<=1.

The absolute price with |log(n/k)|>=(log X)^(2/3) is O_A(X^-A) for every A. Its Gaussian contributes exp(-(log X)^(4/3)/tau), whereas the unrestricted positive mass is at most N^(2-2sigma+2delta)zeta(1+delta)^(2m)=exp(O(log X)). This pays the full ratio tail, including all pairs outside a nominal comparable-product box.

Let gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, and fix0<kappa<gamma-1/2. Choose G=X^(c+kappa), which stays below N for large X. Define Core to be exactly the sum in(N24), including its sqrt(4pi/tau), restricted to

  n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G, |log(n/k)|<(log X)^(2/3).               (N27)

It is real, because the domain is closed under exchanging n and k. Then a ONE-SIDED signed upper bound

  Core <=O_(epsilon,chi,sigma,tau,kappa)(X^(eta+epsilon))    (N28)

uniformly in the specified scales and orders is sufficient. The diagonal is X^o(1), the removed common-divisor sector is at most X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), and the ratio tail is arbitrarily small. Thus(N28) implies Q<=X^(eta+epsilon), then(N22),(N18),(N14)--(N16), and finally the fixed Gaussian zero-exclusion return. An absolute bound on Core is stronger than needed. This is the remaining arithmetic inequality, with every other sector paid. No old fixed-order correlation or original Type I/II/III moment is assumed to apply to these growing-order weights.

### The family really preserves the denominator

For K=Q(i), fixed excluded primes S and chi2((d))=alpha(d)^2, let F_K(X)=sum_c mu_K(c) k(log(Nc/X)). Then the source's family is exactly

    F_t(X)=sum_d chi2(d) Nd^(1+it) F_K(X/Nd²),
    Mellin F_t(s)=M(s) L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2)/zeta_K^S(s).

Every ideal has unique m=c d² with c squarefree; c and d need NOT be coprime. At squarefree m, d=1 and the coefficient is unchanged. This is not an ordinary Hecke twist of the whole denominator.

The return assumes M(s) is nonzero on the required Re(s)>a. Merged lines48–54 stipulate the inherited profile and its zero-free range without reproducing that profile or proof; I have not identified it with another detector merely by notation. This remains an explicit input, including for a=3/4. A possible fully specified replacement is the infinite convolution of uniform probability densities on [-2^-j,2^-j], j>=1: it is C-infinity, supported in [-1,1], with M(s)=product_j sinh(2^-j s)/(2^-j s), nonzero for Re(s)>0. Normal convergence follows from sum_j 2^-2j<infinity; arbitrarily many box factors give arbitrary Fourier decay. Using this replacement requires the actual period and arithmetic estimate for this fixed profile, not transfer of an unspecified profile's bound.

For a fixed positive-length bounded I, a bound

    int_I ||F_t||²_[X,2X] dt << X^(2a+epsilon)

gives an L2(I)-valued holomorphic Mellin transform for Re(s)>a, by dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz. Continue the multiplication identity with zeta_K^S(s). At any hypothetical zero rho with Re(rho)>a, its left side is zero; its right side is the vector

    N_rho(t)=M(rho)L_K^S(2rho-1-it,chi2).

This vector is nonzero: the fixed L-function cannot vanish on a vertical interval without vanishing identically, and M is nonzero by the explicit profile hypothesis above. This handles arbitrary finite multiplicity and proves the strict half-plane without dividing by a scalar numerator. The arithmetic moment, including all d,e and ideal/source cross terms, is still open.

### C: actual rough-prime zero law

The full two-variable product `(1-z)(1-w)` has no zero in the open unit polydisk; deleting its top face gives `1-z-w`, with the zero (1/2,1/2). For k singleton variables the maximal common open polydisk radius is 1/k, by the triangle inequality and the equal-coordinate witness. This is an elementary coefficient calculation, not an application of Lee–Yang theory.

The actual polynomial `sum_(n<=5)mu(n)n^-s=1-2^-s-3^-s-5^-s` is negative at 1 and positive at 2, with positive derivative on the real line. Its unique real zero above 1 belongs to this cutoff polynomial; it says nothing contradictory about 1/zeta.

For the stronger scalable example, retain exactly

    H_N(s)=sum_(n<=N, P^-(n)>sqrt N)mu(n)n^-s
          =1-sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^-s.                    (R12)

P^-(1)=infinity. Any composite with every prime factor strictly above sqrt N exceeds N; equality at a lower prime boundary is excluded. For large N this source also has the actual f3 values, since all retained nonunit primes exceed 3. Thus the prime-power, strict-endpoint and sign identities are literal.

The only external analytic input needed is `pi(t)=li(t)+o(t/log t)`, a consequence of the prime number theorem stated in [NIST DLMF 27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12#E5), independently opened on 12 October 2026. No latest-error claim or power saving is imported. Put `L=log N`, `f_lambda(t)=t^(-1+lambda/L)`, with lambda in a fixed compact set. Stieltjes integration against the prime-counting error E gives endpoint errors `o(1/L)` and

    |integral_(sqrt N)^N E(t)f_lambda'(t)dt|
       <= C sup_(t>=sqrt N)(|E(t)|log t/t)
                    integral_(sqrt N)^N dt/(t log t)=o(1).

The constants are uniform on that compact lambda set. Substitution `t=N^v` in the main term gives

    sum_(sqrt N<p<=N)p^(-1+lambda/L)
       =I(lambda)+o(1), I(lambda)=integral_(1/2)^1 e^(lambda v)dv/v.
                                                               (R13)

I(0)=log2<1, I is strictly increasing, and I tends to infinity. Its unique positive solution I(lambda*)=1 traps the finite crossing by uniform convergence. The finite prime sum decreases strictly with real s, is >1 at s=0 and eventually <1 at s=1. Therefore its unique positive crossing satisfies

    sigma_N=1-lambda*/log N+o(1/log N), lambda*>0.      (R14)

The numerical lambda value is diagnostic only. R14 is a complete written proof based on R13. It refutes blanket inheritance of Euler-product nonvanishing by these precise rough cutoff cells. It also exhibits an exact wall between the unit term and the aggregate prime block that a tropical argument must pay. It does not show that every tropical decomposition or compensated partition source fails, or estimate the complete signed f3 Gaussian energy. The omitted small-prime/composite contributions may be indispensable cancelling terms.
title: C: actual rough-prime zero law

## G84. Exact moment and genuine paid sectors

For 1/2<sigma<1 and even K=2m, put

    M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)a(n)n^(-s),
    Q(X,K)=integral_R exp(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt.

The full Mellin majorant H for C satisfies

    H=integral exp(-tau t^2/2)|1-sigma-it|^(K-1)
          |L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt,
    ||C||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) << X^sigma H,
    H <= exp(O_(chi,tau,sigma)(Klog(K+2))) Q.

Consequently Q<<X^(eta+epsilon) supplies gamma=sigma+eta, with no
square root of Q. The full |t|>3sqrt(L)/tau tail of H is O(X^(-3));
the central part remains an arithmetic problem.

The coefficient of M_Y^m is exactly lambda(n)chi(n)N_(m,Y)(n), where
N_(m,Y) counts ordered factorizations into m squarefree positive integers
at most Y. Unit factors, repeated primes across factors and squareful
outputs remain. With N=Y^m=X^(1/2+o(1)),

    Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_(n,k<=N) lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)conj(chi(k))
        N_(m,Y)(n)N_(m,Y)(k)(nk)^(-sigma)
        exp(-(log(n/k))^2/tau).

This is the complete double sum. Its total is nonnegative, but its signed
sectors need not be. The independent proof bounds:

- Diagonal: at most a fixed Gaussian constant times zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)
  =X^o(1), by N_(m,Y)<=d_m and d_m(p^j)^2<=d_(m^2)(p^j).
- Large gcd: its coefficientwise absolute price, for 1<=G<=N, is
  <<_epsilon X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G. Divisor submultiplicativity and
  Rankin summation retain the costs zeta(1+delta)^m and
  zeta(1+delta)^(m^2); both are X^o(1) in the stated bands.
- Large ratio: |log(n/k)|>=L^(2/3) has price O_A(X^(-A)) for every A.

Set gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, choose
0<kappa<gamma-1/2 and G=X^(c+kappa). Let Core be the same signed
double sum, including its Gaussian constant, with n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G
and |log(n/k)|<L^(2/3). Then

    Core <= X^(eta+epsilon)  for every epsilon>0

is equivalent at the exponent level to the Q bound: the discarded gcd
sector costs X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), the diagonal X^o(1), and the ratio
tail decays faster than any power. The inequality is one-sided.

Taking termwise absolute values cannot prove it. A positive-density
squarefree unit-phase class in [B/2,B], B=floor X^(1/K), yields a
positive subcollection with price X^(1-sigma-o(1)). Grouping products
in logarithmic windows of length1 pays the Gaussian. Removing the
diagonal and large gcd sector leaves this exponent unchanged. These
products lie inside the balanced product window because W/K tends to
infinity. This is an actual coefficientwise-price obstruction, not a
lower bound for signed Core, Q or the physical norm; cancellation between
different actual phases can still pay the desired estimate.

    |sum_w xi_e(w)Phi(Nw/V)|<<min(V,sqrt(Q)).          (R17)

Nonunit fixed-S sectors, when present, can first be separated by their finitely many free-row S-valuations; their scales and phases have fixed costs. ### 2.3 A paid transport repair with a complete Mellin return

The preceding optimal matching is finite and leaves an index. A different
mechanism uses one fixed GLOBAL pairing for each q, with every positive-Mobius
squarefree q-unit paired to a negative-Mobius squarefree q-unit of the same
residue class. Such pairings exist: each class has infinitely many negative
members given by primes in that class; fixing a prime r=1 mod q and multiplying
distinct primes in the class by r gives infinitely many positive members.
Increasing-rank matching is one definite construction. Existence alone bounds
no displacement.

Write an oriented pair as (u,v), mu(u)=1,mu(v)=-1, u=v mod q. Let
a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v), and define its total displacement in a dyadic minimum
shell by

    D_q(X)=sum_(pairs with X<=a<2X) (b-a), X=1,2,4,....          (19.5)

All partners, however far away, enter this sum. This is a finite sum in each
shell; it does not truncate or ignore a partner outside2X. Suppose that for one
common 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0,

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every sufficiently large dyadic X and every fixed q.               (T)

Then all ordinary Dirichlet L(s,chi) are zero-free in Re(s)>gamma. Here is the
complete return. On Re(s)>1, absolute convergence permits regrouping the full
reciprocal Dirichlet series into these pairs:

    1/L(s,chi)=sum_(pairs) chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).              (19.6)

Natural zeros, squareful zeros and every n=1 contribution are already in the
source. For sigma=Re(s)>0,

    |u^(-s)-v^(-s)| <= |s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1).                (19.7)

Thus(T), summed over dyadic minimum shells, gives normally convergent pair sums
on every compact subset of Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon smaller than the compact
horizontal margin. Uniform convergence of holomorphic terms suffices; no
uncontrolled logarithm of the far endpoint is needed. The resulting holomorphic
F equals1/L on Re>1 and L F=1 meromorphically throughout the connected half-plane.
At an L-zero this identity is impossible. At a principal pole, F has a removable
zero; no pole is declared a zero. Original imprimitive L and its factors were
never replaced by a primitive function. Character-dependent constants and finite
height are unrestricted. This proves the claimed ordinary-character scope.

This route has an honest large loss allowance: ideal mean displacement of order
X^(1/2+epsilon), summed over O(X) actual pairs per shell, would meet gamma=1/2.
To reach the weaker c=1/4 it suffices to prove total displacement
X^(7/4+epsilon). For c=1/6 the budget is X^(11/6+epsilon). A nearby gamma=.87485
requires X^(1.87485+epsilon), giving c=.12515, a gain .0000040364 over c11.
These are conditional calibrations, not derived displacement estimates.

The strongest objection is concrete: same-residue arithmetic pairing may cost
precisely the unproved cancellation. For monotone pairing, the number of pair
intervals crossing a cutoff t is exactly |I_a(t)| in each residue class. Indeed
the kth positive and kth negative lists leave E_a(t)-O_a(t) unmatched indices
at that cut, all crossing in one orientation. Tonelli therefore gives

    sum_(pairs) length([a,b] intersect [A,B])
       =integral_A^B R_q(t)dt                              (19.8)

for this particular pairing. This is a proof of the cost identity, not an
independent bound. D_q in(19.5) charges the COMPLETE future interval of every
pair starting in a shell, so one cannot replace it by the left side of(19.8)
on that shell without paying intervals outside it. An arithmetic rule with a
proved complete D_q budget, or a new localized crossing estimate with its own
return, is the next action. The ancestry includes W01 signed transport,
[research revision]'s priced coupling and [research revision] G135's exact rank-displacement target.
Under G135's equivalent summatory/rank bounds at gamma>1/2, the kth endpoints
are comparable to k and have difference O(k^gamma); there are O(X) pairs in a
minimum shell. This immediately implies D_q(X)=O(X^(1+gamma)), also with
epsilon losses. Thus(T) is a separately priced sufficient total-displacement
contract, not an unconditionally achieved weaker arithmetic estimate. The
Hodge formulation and complete future-partner Mellin bill do not remove the
older matching target's open cancellation input.

There is also a complete ACTUAL arithmetic failure of the simplest global
construction. Fix r=1 mod q and pair every squarefree q-unit m with r not
dividing m to rm, with orientation determined by mu(m). This pairs the entire
source and preserves each residue class. Its minimum endpoint is m and its
length is(r-1)m, so

    D_q(X)=(r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           =(3/2)(r-1)d_(qr)X^2+O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).       (19.9)

The last identity follows by partial summation of the proved squarefree count;
half-open endpoints change at most O(X), already inside the error. The leading
coefficient is positive. This global neutral-prime rule therefore does not meet
any gamma<1 in(T), despite its exact phase cancellation and spectral gap1.
This rejects the named rule's positive displacement certificate, not every
same-residue matching or the signed Mertens target. To reach a subtrivial
exponent one needs genuinely closer cross-integer partners or a different
signed pricing rule with a proved complete return.

## 2. Why the larger amplifier is actually admissible

### The actual prime pool and slot gap

PR9 B3.7, manuscript lines 2356--2393, puts `ell_*=sigma/3`, requires mesh below `sigma/6`, and uses good primes in `(Z^(ell_*)/2,Z^(ell_*)]`. The exact source does not assume `sigma` tends to zero with the requested local epsilon:

```
eventually_original_amplification:
  sigma > 0, loss > 0, Mmax >= 0, profile upper endpoint b >= 0,
  eta_mesh < sigma/6;
  bounded masks R,s; retained dyadic row logarithm <= Mmax.
```

It then supplies the actual nonempty prime pool, its cardinality saving, source character families with conductor bounds, and the main/error energy inequality. The constant `(Mmax+2 sigma)/(sigma/6)` is a fixed multiplicity constant, not a new exponent. Any fixed positive sigma works. Polynomial mask sizes and row bounds can be enclosed uniformly on the compact local geometry. For `a=M/160`, choosing mesh below `a/10` is stronger than the required mesh below `a/2=sigma/6`. The finitely many original slots are smaller than every amplifier prime eventually. Removing support, row, mask, and first-projector primes omits only `O(log Z)` choices. There is no prime-supply or fixed-small-prime-cutoff obstruction.

This does **not** substitute `sigma=3M/160` into the old proof of the global `9/2` moment. In that proof, B3.10 (lines 2631--2656) chooses a small internal sigma so terminal costs `3 sigma + 5 sigma/3` fit an arbitrary epsilon. The new local proof calls the completed old theorem with its own chosen small loss, and therefore its own internal induction parameters. Its separate, fixed outer amplifier cost is paid by the local strict reserves. Conflating these two sigma choices would invalidate the extension; keeping them separate is legitimate and is what PLA already does for `M/2000`.

The main amplified term retains the original columns and coefficients. The amplifier prime does not become a new varying parent in its density dictionary. The three extracted errors do retain the appropriate moving-prime characters and conductor contribution; they are bounded by the old moment and the original extraction ledger, never by the fixed-parent density theorem.

### Genuine radius, transform, and widths

Use the actual ball

```
K_main = K0 + (d-c)_+ + 6a + omega,
K0 = 2A-c-d+R+E-M,
omega = retained-frequency padding + positive support-doubling reserve.
```

`AmplifiedRetainedRadius.main_energy_common` constructs the domination, including eventual `2 <= Z^reserve`; its hypotheses do not constrain sigma above. Thus this is not an unproved relabeling of the old radius. `GaussEnergy.gaussEnergy_poisson` requires `Kphys>0`, with no fixed exponent ceiling. A power of positive Z meets that condition even when its logarithm is negative. Raw frequency tails still have fixed polynomial envelopes because every exponent in this local proof remains in a bounded range.

PLA LA.6--LA.8 / RC give exactly

```
M' = M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2,
(A'-M')-(A-M) <= 6a+omega,
Delta = b2-p2+B_c+a >= a.
```

These formulas are affine identities for the real parameter a. The additional support, frequency, and fixed-conductor paddings are chosen afterward, smaller than the strict reserve. Actual moving-support cancellation can make `d_*=M_actual-M'` negative; this is not repaired by replacing it with zero. Use the exact inequality

`d_* + r(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2 + r F_+`, for `d_*<=delta2` and `0<=r<=1`.

The actual source `SecondActualWidth.actual_width_bound` checks a nonempty retained row before removing the max; a nominally negative unsupported window is empty. Bounded nonempty end windows cost the declared support padding. No positivity premise for a nominal width has been silently dropped.

The low-bin restriction is imposed only after both transforms on a positive allocated child energy. The literal coefficient/mask/relative-character identities in RC are unchanged. Slot deletion retains original canonical slots; it does not create arbitrary coefficients. The low indicator is removed only after paying each removed slot's pointwise cost. Empty selected slots use the unrestricted old zero-slot theorem, with no invented residual affine plain-capacity condition.

### Character, density, and profile restrictions remain the same

The signed row remains `w=u0 e F G V h'`, with residues `1+t` and `1-t` modulo six. A zero residue is an Euler hole. The fixed ideal is the original `Q_*`; the moving child does not replace the anchor. Parent translates remain separate for eligibility and zero maxima. The natural source constructor gives `conductor <= K Nw` with fixed K. Extra polynomial Euler holes are paid separately and do not enter a supposedly fixed modulus or finite dictionary.

The first projector and genuine second common primes divide w. The second projector need not divide w and is still paid by its dyadic count and two extraction scalars. The joint density/reconstruction remains

```
rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],  .7<=delta<=.75,
W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a,
joint count <= Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta)*(1+T)^J.
```

Increasing a only reduces the supported row bound W. If W is near or below zero, use the already stated bounded-window/empty-window rule. `rho>=2/7>1/6` is unchanged, so the sixth-power lift remains summable. The actual density statement handles all heights with one threshold; its internal height exponent is chosen before the separate external truncation exponent. There is no new detector cutoff or conductor condition depending on a.

The same common Fourier majorant and diagonal contraction apply. Smooth cutoffs are placed on fixed normalized boxes; Euler derivatives of `K(A product y_i^e_i)` remain uniform for all positive A. Changing a changes the bounded power envelope but not the finite profile mechanism. The four derivative-profile pairs required for scale supremum are retained. Small losses can be chosen from a numerical reserve before target/dictionary/finite-slot count; finite orders, constants, and the eventual threshold may depend on the fixed family, but must precede all live scales, subsets, masks, heights, and normalized slot widths. None of this is weakened by the larger amplifier.

statement:
### 2.1 Uncut coprime identity

For Re(s)>1, the uncut field's coefficient Dirichlet series is

    eta(s) product_{p>=5}(1-2p^(-s)),
    eta(s) = sum_{l>=1} b(l)l^(-s)
           = (1-2^(1-s)) zeta(s).                         (2.1)

At each prime p>=5, coprimality allows exactly three squarefree
allocations to (d,e): neither, d only, or e only. Their local sum is
1-p^(-s)-p^(-s). Primes 2 and 3 are forbidden in both d and e.
This preserves the actual ordered-pair multiplicity 2.

The local Dirichlet factors of f_3 are

    p=2:    (1-2z)/(1-z),
    p=3:    1/(1-z),
    p>=5:   (1-2z)/(1-z),                  z=p^(-s).

These are exactly the local factors in (2.1). Therefore

    F_6(x) = sum_{d,e>=1; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                 mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).                 (2.2)

Equation (2.1) is an absolutely convergent identity on Re(s)>1.
It is not an assertion that its first-order Euler product converges
absolutely throughout Re(s)>1/2.

statement:
## 2. Protected high-reach19: phase-preserving supersymmetry and the exact index bill

All constructions in this section use the complete actual squarefree source,
not f3 or the original H packet. Fix q>=1. Let V_X have the orthonormal basis e_n
for squarefree n<=X with (n,q)=1, including n=1. Its parity operator is
Gamma e_n=mu(n)e_n. For each character chi modulo q, retain natural zero extension
by having excluded only nonunits, and put W_chi e_n=chi(n)e_n. Thus

    Str(W_chi)=Tr(Gamma W_chi)=M_chi(X).

This is a replacement architecture with its own return. It does not inherit any
signed-submask estimate for a different detector.

### 2.1 A neutral-prime realization works, but its harmonic price is linear

Choose a prime r with r not dividing q and chi(r)=1 for the particular character.
For all characters modulo q simultaneously, choose r=1 mod q. Such primes exist
by Dirichlet's theorem; see [NIST DLMF27.11](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11). Pair each
squarefree q-unit m<=X/r with r not dividing m to rm. The pairings are disjoint.
On each pair orient a differential d from the even-parity basis vector to the
odd-parity vector, with coefficient1; set d=0 on odd vectors and unpaired vectors.
Then d is odd, d^2=0, and it commutes with W_chi. The Laplacian
Delta=dd*+d*d is identity on every pair and zero on every unpaired vector. Its
positive spectral gap is exactly1 whenever X>=r. No estimate of the arithmetic source has been
used in obtaining that gap.

The unpaired basis is exactly

    r not dividing m, (m,q)=1, mu(m)^2=1, X/r<m<=X.

Consequently for every t>=0,

    M_chi(X)=Str(W_chi exp(-t Delta))
            =sum_(X/r<m<=X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)chi(m).       (19.1)

Both endpoints and the empty-face atom have been accounted for: every m<=X/r
is paired and cancels because chi(r)=1. For chi(r)!=1 the exact extra term is
(1-chi(r)) sum_(m<=X/r,r not dividing m) mu(m)chi(m); it cannot be discarded.

Write d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q) p/(p+1), with empty product1. Elementary
square-divisor counting gives

    #{m<=y:mu(m)^2=1,(m,D)=1}=d_D y+O_D(sqrt(y)).

For completeness, expand mu(m)^2=sum_(d^2|m)mu(d); only (d,D)=1 contributes,
count k<=y/d^2 coprime to D as (phi(D)/D)y/d^2+O_D(1), sum d<=sqrt(y), and
bound the omitted d-tail by O_D(sqrt(y)). Its Euler product is d_D. Hence

    dim ker Delta=d_(qr)(1-1/r)X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X))
                 =d_q (r-1)/(r+1) X+O_(q,r)(sqrt(X)). (19.2)

Thus phase-preserving cross-integer pairing does repair the chain-map defect,
but its unsigned harmonic price is still linear. This is not a lower bound on
M_chi. At q=1,r=2 its leading rank is2X/pi^2, agreeing with the known squarefree
complex. Björner's [Theorems3.1/3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704v1) give the
classical topology and a stronger error; no literature novelty is claimed for
that case. W27's fixed simplicial contraction and [research revision] G74 already explain
related harmonic obstructions. Our next calculation allows a different
differential and therefore does not import their fixed-complex rank floor.

### 2.2 Exact minimum over all character-preserving pairings

For each unit residue a modulo q define

    E_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=1},
    O_a(X)=#{n<=X:n squarefree,n=a mod q,mu(n)=-1},
    I_a(X)=E_a(X)-O_a(X).

Consider ANY odd differential d on V_X satisfying d^2=0 and commuting with every
W_chi modulo q. Characters separate unit residue classes: if an n,m matrix entry
of d is nonzero then chi(n)=chi(m) for every chi, whence n=m mod q. Thus d splits
into the residue blocks. Since W_chi is unitary, d* also commutes with W_chi, and
the harmonic subspace of Delta=dd*+d*d splits in the same way.

For each residue block the even-minus-odd harmonic dimension is I_a(X). One
elementary proof decomposes the finite complex into im d, im d* and ker Delta:
the first two have equal dimensions with opposite parity, via d restricted to
im d*. Therefore

    dim ker Delta >= R_q(X):=sum_(a mod q,(a,q)=1)|I_a(X)|.       (19.3)

This lower bound is attained. In each residue class pair the first
min(E_a,O_a) even/odd basis vectors in increasing order and use the two-state
differential above. The remaining |I_a| vectors are harmonic and all positive
eigenvalues equal1. Thus the EXACT minimum harmonic dimension in this class of
differentials is R_q(X), with an attaining gap1 realization whenever any pairs exist.

Character orthogonality gives

    M_chi(X)=sum_a chi(a)I_a(X),
    I_a(X)=1/phi(q) sum_(chi mod q) conjugate(chi(a)) M_chi(X),
    max_chi |M_chi(X)| <= R_q(X)
       <= sum_chi |M_chi(X)| <= phi(q)max_chi |M_chi(X)|.         (19.4)

For each fixed q these are fixed constants. Therefore a power bound for the
optimal unsigned harmonic rank is equivalent to the same common power bound for
all characters modulo q. A gap theorem alone is vacuous here: gap1 was obtained
without bounding R_q. Optimizing the differential has not made an independent
arithmetic estimate. This conclusion is limited to this complete source and
character-preserving finite parity complexes; it does not prohibit a different
signed readout, a noncommuting differential with a paid commutator, or a new
analytic source.

Late source audit: the newly integrated [research revision] G135 already proves the full
fixed-modulus character/residue discrepancy equivalence, its increasing-rank
matching version, and the exact unmatched-index price. The finite Hodge minimum
above is an operator formulation of that same index bill. It is not a new
arithmetic matching principle or an independent cancellation mechanism. This
overlap was found after the original seeds and random selections were frozen;
none of their eligibility or choices has been revised.

The exact diagnostic at X=80,q=5 gives indices (0,-3,-4,1) in residues1,2,3,4.
The minimum harmonic rank is8. The four character traces are -6,-1+i,8,-1-i,
exactly equal to the corresponding literal M_chi(80). A neutral-prime r=2
complex for the principal character has14 harmonic states instead. This checks
the finite indexing and shows why a14-state rank floor from one complex is not
valid for every changed differential. No asymptotic saving follows from80.

### 2.3 A paid transport repair with a complete Mellin return

The preceding optimal matching is finite and leaves an index. A different
mechanism uses one fixed GLOBAL pairing for each q, with every positive-Mobius
squarefree q-unit paired to a negative-Mobius squarefree q-unit of the same
residue class. Such pairings exist: each class has infinitely many negative
members given by primes in that class; fixing a prime r=1 mod q and multiplying
distinct primes in the class by r gives infinitely many positive members.
Increasing-rank matching is one definite construction. Existence alone bounds
no displacement.

Write an oriented pair as (u,v), mu(u)=1,mu(v)=-1, u=v mod q. Let
a=min(u,v), b=max(u,v), and define its total displacement in a dyadic minimum
shell by

    D_q(X)=sum_(pairs with X<=a<2X) (b-a), X=1,2,4,....          (19.5)

All partners, however far away, enter this sum. This is a finite sum in each
shell; it does not truncate or ignore a partner outside2X. Suppose that for one
common 0<gamma<1 and every epsilon>0,

    D_q(X) <<_(q,epsilon) X^(1+gamma+epsilon)
    for every sufficiently large dyadic X and every fixed q.               (T)

Then all ordinary Dirichlet L(s,chi) are zero-free in Re(s)>gamma. Here is the
complete return. On Re(s)>1, absolute convergence permits regrouping the full
reciprocal Dirichlet series into these pairs:

    1/L(s,chi)=sum_(pairs) chi(u)(u^(-s)-v^(-s)).              (19.6)

Natural zeros, squareful zeros and every n=1 contribution are already in the
source. For sigma=Re(s)>0,

    |u^(-s)-v^(-s)| <= |s|(b-a)a^(-sigma-1).                (19.7)

Thus(T), summed over dyadic minimum shells, gives normally convergent pair sums
on every compact subset of Re(s)>gamma: choose epsilon smaller than the compact
horizontal margin. Uniform convergence of holomorphic terms suffices; no
uncontrolled logarithm of the far endpoint is needed. The resulting holomorphic
F equals1/L on Re>1 and L F=1 meromorphically throughout the connected half-plane.
At an L-zero this identity is impossible. At a principal pole, F has a removable
zero; no pole is declared a zero. Original imprimitive L and its factors were
never replaced by a primitive function. Character-dependent constants and finite
height are unrestricted. This proves the claimed ordinary-character scope.

This route has an honest large loss allowance: ideal mean displacement of order
X^(1/2+epsilon), summed over O(X) actual pairs per shell, would meet gamma=1/2.
To reach the weaker c=1/4 it suffices to prove total displacement
X^(7/4+epsilon). For c=1/6 the budget is X^(11/6+epsilon). A nearby gamma=.87485
requires X^(1.87485+epsilon), giving c=.12515, a gain .0000040364 over c11.
These are conditional calibrations, not derived displacement estimates.

The strongest objection is concrete: same-residue arithmetic pairing may cost
precisely the unproved cancellation. For monotone pairing, the number of pair
intervals crossing a cutoff t is exactly |I_a(t)| in each residue class. Indeed
the kth positive and kth negative lists leave E_a(t)-O_a(t) unmatched indices
at that cut, all crossing in one orientation. Tonelli therefore gives

    sum_(pairs) length([a,b] intersect [A,B])
       =integral_A^B R_q(t)dt                              (19.8)

for this particular pairing. This is a proof of the cost identity, not an
independent bound. D_q in(19.5) charges the COMPLETE future interval of every
pair starting in a shell, so one cannot replace it by the left side of(19.8)
on that shell without paying intervals outside it. An arithmetic rule with a
proved complete D_q budget, or a new localized crossing estimate with its own
return, is the next action. The ancestry includes W01 signed transport,
[research revision]'s priced coupling and [research revision] G135's exact rank-displacement target.
Under G135's equivalent summatory/rank bounds at gamma>1/2, the kth endpoints
are comparable to k and have difference O(k^gamma); there are O(X) pairs in a
minimum shell. This immediately implies D_q(X)=O(X^(1+gamma)), also with
epsilon losses. Thus(T) is a separately priced sufficient total-displacement
contract, not an unconditionally achieved weaker arithmetic estimate. The
Hodge formulation and complete future-partner Mellin bill do not remove the
older matching target's open cancellation input.

There is also a complete ACTUAL arithmetic failure of the simplest global
construction. Fix r=1 mod q and pair every squarefree q-unit m with r not
dividing m to rm, with orientation determined by mu(m). This pairs the entire
source and preserves each residue class. Its minimum endpoint is m and its
length is(r-1)m, so

    D_q(X)=(r-1) sum_(X<=m<2X,(m,qr)=1) mu(m)^2 m
           =(3/2)(r-1)d_(qr)X^2+O_(q,r)(X^(3/2)).       (19.9)

The last identity follows by partial summation of the proved squarefree count;
half-open endpoints change at most O(X), already inside the error. The leading
coefficient is positive. This global neutral-prime rule therefore does not meet
any gamma<1 in(T), despite its exact phase cancellation and spectral gap1.
This rejects the named rule's positive displacement certificate, not every
same-residue matching or the signed Mertens target. To reach a subtrivial
exponent one needs genuinely closer cross-integer partners or a different
signed pricing rule with a proved complete return.

## G93: a greedy boundary obstruction and a paid moving square mask

For a prime p0 with chi(p0)=1, match every still-unmatched squarefree
q-unit pair m,p0*m within n<=x. The exact remaining support is

    U_x={n<=x:mu(n)!=0,(n,q)=1,p0 does not divide n,x/p0<n}.

No later larger eligible prime joins two vertices of U_x. Thus this
specific increasing, never-revisit greedy procedure stops after its first
prime. Its signed boundary is exactly M_chi(x); its unsigned size is

    kappa_(qp0)(1-1/p0)x+O_(q,p0)(sqrt x),
    kappa_Q=(phi(Q)/Q)product_(p not dividing Q)(1-p^-2)>0.

This follows from the elementary squarefree indicator and its complete
d^-2 tail. For q=1,p0=2 the coefficient is2/pi^2. It is not a signed
lower bound. Revisiting vertices, close-ratio swaps and other matchings
remain open. The distinct all-power f3 Gaussian matching is unaffected.

A different source pays a full prime-square complement. Put

    a_(Y,chi)(n)=lambda(n)chi(n)product_(p<=Y)(1-1_(p^2|n)),
    A_(Y,chi)(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_(Y,chi)(n).

Every nonzero difference from mu(n)chi(n) has modulus<=1 and is supported
on a prime square p^2|n with p>Y. Thus, including all overlaps,

    |A_(Y,chi)(x)-M_chi(x)|<=sum_(p>Y)floor(x/p^2)<=x/Y.

The separate exact signed expansion is

    A_(Y,chi)(x)=sum_(d<=sqrt x,P^+(d)<=Y)
                     mu(d)chi(d)^2 L_chi(x/d^2).

No(d,m)=1 restriction is inserted; d can exceed Y, and all overlapping
square terms remain. For gamma>1/2 choose eta>0 with
delta=1-gamma+eta<1/2 and fix Y_X=ceil(X^delta) throughout each dyadic
shell. Its complete shell error is<=2X^(gamma-eta). Consequently the
every-shell SUP exponent gamma is equivalent to the fixed Mertens bound,
for each fixed chi with a common exponent and character-dependent constants.
First gain now requires gamma<.87485739;1/6 and1/4 remain prospective c.

The moving source returns to fixed mu*chi before Mellin transformation.
Abel summation then makes1/L(s,chi) holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma,
paying every finite height and imprimitive zero, with the principal pole
excepted. No Hecke or growing-conductor extension is inferred. The complete
signed square-divisor sum remains open. Existing full Liouville/Mobius
square-kernel equivalence at weights>1/2 and W24's different divisor-cutoff
theorem retain their credit and scope.

## 3. Development16: the entire sign survives in harmonic degree

The local complex has one even vector e0, two odd vectors e+,e-, and d(e+)=d(e-)=e0. Its Laplacian has eigenvalues2 on e0 and the odd symmetric vector, and0 on the odd antisymmetric vector. Its Euler characteristic and heat supertrace are-1; the normalized harmonic vector is(e+-e-)/sqrt2. A one-even/one-odd acyclic pair instead has supertrace0 and erases the intended coefficient.

The graded tensor product over DISTINCT p|n,p!=3 retains every repeated power without adding a coordinate;2 is included,3 is not. For n=1 and powers of3 there is one even factor. Koszul signs give d^2=0. The Laplacian is the sum of commuting local ones: one harmonic vector in degree omega(n/3^v3(n)), and all other eigenvalues positive multiples of2. Hence

    Str(e^-tDelta_n)=Str(P_n)=f3(n).

On the complement, h=d*Delta^-1 has norm<=1/sqrt2, since d d*<=Delta and the gap is2. Its exact identity is dh+hd=I-P, never I; applying an I identity to the nonzero harmonic vector is a contradiction.

In the direct sum, W_(x,chi) is scalar chi(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) on C(n). Since3^omega(n/3^v3(n))<=n^2, Gaussian decay justifies trace class and all sums. The complete field is

    F=Tr(Gamma W e^-tDelta)=Tr(Gamma W P), every t>=0. (R8)

The positive harmonic price is sum_(n,q)=1 g_tau(log(n/x)). Bounded-variation Riemann sums in fixed residue classes, with h(t)=g_tau(log t),h(0)=0, give

    Tr(|W|P)=(phi(q)/q)e^(tau/2)x+O_(q,tau)(1).      (R9)

This is exponent1 for the ABSOLUTE price, not a lower bound on F or its moment. Heat time infinity leaves F unchanged. The author correctly rejects only cancellation inferred from the complement's gap.

Different-integer differentials remain eligible. In an acyclic two-state edge of gap lambda, the weighted supertrace is w+-w-, and integral_0^infinity lambda e^-lambda t(w+-w-)dt equals that same difference. Increasing the gap does not pay Gaussian or character mismatch. W43's native H filling audit already retained a harmonic/boundary bill; W46 adds this literal f3 realization. statement:
## 2. The coupled \(d,a\) arithmetic and the sixth-power-free moment

The zero-preserving identity needed here is different from freezing the quadratic twist in SR6:

\[
\boxed{\overline{\vartheta_c(d a^2)}
       =\overline{\vartheta_c(d)}\,\vartheta_c(a).}
\tag{MQ8}
\]

On units it is the order-three identity \(\overline{z^2}=z\). At a prime dividing both the core and either \(d\) or \(a\), both sides are zero. Thus it is valid when \(d,a\) share primes. It is also valid at a prime where the combined exponent in \(d a^2\) is three: the canceled phase still has its natural zero.

First take an annular \(F\) and a sharp row ball \(q_n\le H\). Freeze \(d\). The inner coefficient for the cubic sieve in \(a\) is

\[
z_c=X^{-1/2}\mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(d)}
  \mathbf1_{(c,R)=1}\mathbf1_{q_c\in\mathcal I}F(q_c/X).
\]

Its squared coefficient mass is \(O_F(1)\), uniformly in \(d,R,\mathcal I\). The phase depending on \(d\) is a permitted arbitrary column coefficient in MQ1. It is not a new fixed character datum in UM.

If \(n=d a^2\) is sixth-power-free, \(a\) is cube-free. The exact cubic-sieve row length is

\[
A_d=(H/q_d)^{1/2}.
\]

It is the norm of \(a\), determined by MQ2; no conductor has replaced the norm of \(n\). MQ1 bounds the contribution for this \(d\) by

\[
(HX)^\epsilon\{(H/q_d)^{1/2}+X+
                         (HX^2/q_d)^{1/3}\}.
\]

Sum the squarefree representatives \(q_d\le\Delta\). Ideal counting gives

\[
\sum_{q_d\le\Delta}q_d^{-1/2}\ll\Delta^{1/2},\quad
\#\{d:q_d\le\Delta\}\ll\Delta,\quad
\sum_{q_d\le\Delta}q_d^{-1/3}\ll\Delta^{2/3}.
\tag{MQ9}
\]

This proves the three terms of MQ4. There is no extra Cauchy--Schwarz in \(d\), and no appeal to separate moments of size \(H\) for each twist.

For the stated version with every fixed-prime valuation, write the fixed-prime part of \(a\) as a member of the finite cube-free \(S\)-orbit times an \(S\)-supported cube. The finite orbit supplies fixed coefficient twists and exact bounded scale constants. Each remaining sixth-power row multiplier has norm \(q_t^6\). Replace \(H\) by \(H/q_t^6\) in the estimate just proved. The first and third terms have summable weights \(q_t^{-3}\) and \(q_t^{-2}\). The middle term counts at most a logarithmic power of \(H\), because \(t\) is supported on the fixed finite \(S\). That loss is included in \((HX)^\epsilon\). Element units give only finitely many components.

The original cut \((d,a)=1\), if a smaller cube-free-row sector is desired, is a restriction of the positive outer sum and may be retained. It was not assumed in the proof.
title: 2. The coupled \(d,a\) arithmetic and the sixth-power-free moment

statement:
### Independent completion: the criterion is exactly equivalent for this source

The classical inputs used here are canonical inner/outer factorization and cyclicity of outer functions. Their statements, including the singular-inner measure representation, are given in Garcia and Ross, *Model spaces: a survey*, Theorems2.12,2.16,2.20 and formula2.10. The following constrained minimization and source-specific boundary argument are proved here. [Primary source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1312.5018).

For any nonzero F in H-infinity with F0!=0, write F=I O, I inner and O outer. The closure of polynomial multiples of F is I H2. Any limit g=Iu of admissible pF still has g(0)=F0, hence u(0)=F0/I(0)=O(0); I(0)!=0. Thus ||g||^2>=|O(0)|^2. Conversely, outer cyclicity gives polynomials q_k with Fq_k->I O(0). Continuity of evaluation at0 gives q_k(0)->1; rescaling q_k/q_k(0) provides admissible polynomials with the same limit. Monotonicity over all degrees therefore proves

    d_infinity=|O(0)|^2=|F0|^2/|I(0)|^2,
    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2(|I(0)|^-2-1).              (R8)

For an arbitrary bounded analytic source, absence of disk zeros is insufficient: a nonconstant singular inner factor still causes a gap. We now remove that possibility for (R1), rather than silently assuming it.

F extends holomorphically across every circle point zeta other than1: its finite Cayley image has real part gamma>0, where (R1) is holomorphic. The boundary zeros away from1 are isolated and form a countable set. In the factorization F=B S_nu O the outer factor is bounded by ||F||_infinity. The singular factor has nontangential limit0 at nu-almost every point, so boundedness of B and O implies F also has limit0 there. Analytic continuation consequently forces nu to be supported on those countably many boundary zeros together with1. It is thus purely atomic.

An atom of mass c>0 at zeta gives along z=r zeta

    |F(r zeta)|<=||F||_infinity exp[-c(1+r)/(1-r)].    (R9)

At zeta!=1 this contradicts the finite order of a zero of the continued nonzero analytic function. At zeta=1, put sigma=s(r). The literal Dirichlet series gives L(sigma,chi)->1 and therefore F_chi(sigma)~1/sigma. Since (1+r)/(1-r)=(sigma-gamma)/a, this too contradicts (R9). All atoms vanish, and nu=0. This proof uses the actual coefficient chi(1)=1 and the pole-corrected source, not a generic zero-free Hardy assumption.

Accordingly I is, up to a unimodular constant, exactly the Blaschke product over the L-zeros rho_j with Re rho_j>gamma, counted with multiplicity. Let w_j=z(rho_j). The bounded-source Blaschke condition and F0!=0 make the product below positive. Equations(R8)-(R9) give the exact census

    Delta_infinity=|F0|^2[product_j |w_j|^-2-1].       (R10)

The empty product is1. Each nonempty factor is>1. Thus Delta_N->0 if and only if this fixed L_chi has no zero in Re s>gamma. Zeros on the boundary are allowed and create no atom. This adds the converse missing from the cautious author formulation. It proves no convergence rate or arithmetic estimate: the complete prediction target has precisely the original zero-exclusion difficulty at this source. Applying it to every fixed chi at a common gamma gives exactly the corresponding ordinary-character family statement, with no growing-q uniformity inferred.

### 2.3 Exact coincident aliases and their coefficient energy

For a near alias write h/m=u/v in lowest terms, u,v positive and coprime. Then m=vj,h=uj. Crucially the ENTIRE function Z_(h/m)(x), including its support and damping, depends only on u/v,N,x. The ONLY separate original-m factor is1/m in (4). Thus define the x-independent grouped coefficient

 C_(u/v)=sum_(j>=1: vj in I_M) A_(vj) beta_(uj)/(vj).             (8)

The complete stationary bank is exactly

 sum_(r=u/v in R_N, v<=2M) C_r Z_r(x)
                       exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4).   (9)

Truncation m<=D, skipped aliases beta_h=0, all coincidences and arbitrary coefficient phases stay in (8). There is no averaging or assumption that beta_(uj) is constant. Since j lies in a factor2 interval, |C_(u/v)|<<A||b||inf/v. Also u>=1 and r<=C_Q T/N force v>=N/(C_Q T). Counting possible positive numerators and then dropping coprimality only in an upper bound gives

 sum_r |C_r|^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_Q T))<=v<=2M)
                     [vT/N+1]/v^2
  << A^2||b||inf^2 (T/N)log(2M).                              (10)

The lower denominator cutoff is essential. Without it the +1 term would falsely leave N^2/T in the final energy. The sum v^-2 from that cutoff is O(min(1,T/N)), which is <=O(T/N) in both regimes. If the denominator range is empty there is no main bank.

## 6. The other three author first tests

**W49-16: causal shell compression.** On integer coefficient vectors put S_p e_n=e_(pn). A finite Euler product E=product_p(I-chi(p)S_p) is supported on forward dilations; its coefficient from n to m is mu(m/n)chi(m/n) when the quotient is supported on the included primes. On the HALF-OPEN shell I=[X,2X), every nonidentity integer dilation leaves I to the right. Thus P_I E P_I=I, and there is no future-to-shell or shell-to-past block. Its proposed future Schur feedback is zero. Past-to-shell injection still contains the original arithmetic. Closing both endpoints adds the genuine n=X,m=2X atom where integral, and cannot silently be called the same identity. This is the G69 causal mechanism specialized to the finite Mobius source; it gives no contraction of the full field. Independent audit20 below strengthens the exact cutoff statement.

**W49-22: fixed-pair kernel flatness.** The JN9/JN9b unit-character factors for ONE fixed ordered prime pair are chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4. They separate into H(h)S(s)T(s') times the fixed CRT/Gauss phase and normalization. The CRT phase is chi_pi((pi')^(-1))^3 chi_pi'(-pi^(-1))^3; it is retained. For fixed s' their nonzero rectangle cross ratio is1. Ramified or other zero vertices cannot be divided by; a zero prefactor supplies no holonomy. The author is correct about that bare separable kernel.

This is NOT a flatness statement for the complete H matrix. In the literal source the coprimality projectors act on the original arithmetic variables before Fourier transformation; generally they do not merely delete frequency vertices. The complete transformed amplitude is not a rank-one character. In the checked native source, W_d retains h(d)A_0(du) conjugate(A_0(dv)), xi(u)conjugate(xi(v)), both original mark arrays divided by their roots, the full original or accepted transported common profile consistently, the sharp supports, ray/natural zeros, chi_R(uv)^3, and the coprimality factors

    1_(R,d)=1 1_(P,Rdu)=1 1_(P',Rdv)=1.

The complete rooted sums over D|(P,R), D'|(P',R), with mu(D)mu(D'), are taken before the transform. The normalized transform contains the signs

    Q^(-1) sum_(R,P,P') W_d e(-Rh/(pi pi')-Ps/pi+P's'/pi'),

where e is the original Eisenstein additive character, and the finite groups have total size Q^2. Conjugation is already reflected in the plus sign on the second mark; the denominator is pi', not a substituted conjugate modulus. The external b_pi conjugate(b_pi'), zeta phase and C_0(pi)conjugate(C_0(pi')) remain; so do the full sum over d and all frequency variables, q_pi != q_pi', and the actual far mask when that branch is selected. The centered Jacobi subtraction is a paid term, not zero. A comparison across different prime pairs also needs compatible identifications of their different residue spaces, which are not supplied. Accordingly I accept only bare fixed-pair flatness, not a norm gain, cancellation estimate, or a full projected-H obstruction. The first test does not erase other H branches.

**W49-23: full graph identity.** Let T be the actual complete matrix, B_v,B_w incidence maps, L_i=B_i^*B_i, P_i their kernel projectors, and Q_i=L_i^+L_i. Then the Q_w T Q_v block has exactly the factorization

    w^*Q_w T Q_v v
      =(B_w w)^* [B_w L_w^+ T L_v^+ B_v^*](B_v v).       (R13)

The three other P/Q blocks still have to be paid. These graph projectors are not the native arithmetic projectors. Rescaling B_v by a>0 and B_w by b>0 scales the middle operator by1/(ab) and its two endpoint factors by ab, leaving the full bound unchanged. No gain follows from normalizing an incidence gap. This is already S65-4. A generic two-vertex check verifies algebra, not any estimate of the full native coefficients, masks, heights, core/restoration terms or outer normalization. I retain the exact identity and reject an unpriced spectral-gap conclusion.

## 4. A pointwise removal of small sixth-free column cores

Uniquely write `l=c a^6`, with c sixth-power-free as an ideal. This classification has nothing to do with excluding sixth-power ROWS. By (C7),

    N(rad(ca))>R, hence (Nc)(Na)>R.                    (C8)

Let `C0=U^lambda<R`, and let F_lo be the sum (C6) over `Nc<=C0`. Absolute counting, including all natural zeros as contractions, gives for each individual u and every required derivative

    |partial F_lo,u(s)|
     << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
         sum_(Nc<=C0) (Nc)^(-sigma)
            sum_(Na>R/Nc) (Na)^(-6sigma)
     << H_J U^((sigma-1/2)v+epsilon)
              R^(1-6sigma) C0^(5sigma).              (C9)

Indeed ideal counting yields `sum_(Na>A) (Na)^(-6sigma)<<A^(1-6sigma)` for A>=1. The remaining c-sum is bounded by the sum over *all* ideals of `(Nc)^(5sigma-1)`, at most `C0^(5sigma)`. The genuine sixth-free restriction only contracts it. This pays unequal roots in each class, the unit core, all column dyads, and possible coincidence of their row phases. It uses no row oscillation and applies to every fixed-inducing row and the target unit row too.

Consequently

    ||F_lo||_U^2
      << H_J U^[1+2t(1-6sigma)+10sigma lambda
                         +(2sigma-1)v+epsilon].       ([research revision])

Take t=4/3 and lambda=6/5. The exponent in ([research revision]) has sigma-derivative `-4+2v<0`, so the lower real edge controls the entire integral. At the nominal lower edge `2sigma-1=delta`, its exponent is

    L_lo(delta,v)=5/3-2delta+delta v.                  ([research revision])

This is increasing in v, and Section7 pays it against the CURRENT E_K. Set `F_hi=F-F_lo`. In the Sobolev Hilbert space,

    ||F||_U <= ||F_hi||_U + ||F_lo||_U.                ([research revision])

This pays *all low/high cross terms*. It does not omit them from an expanded square or assume their sign. Fixed constants in squaring ([research revision]) have no exponent cost. A direct zero-row application can equivalently use (C9), followed by this positive norm inequality; no division by a tiny slot value is needed.

Without the actual cancellation (C5), the cutoff would be `Na> (R/Nc)^(1/6)` and (C9) would not follow. Thus this is a source-specific use of the completed Möbius sum, not a consequence of divisor boundedness or the old same-class diagonal alone.
