statement:
# Quaternion norm and determinant: user-directed intake

13 October 2026. The user explicitly proposed the complex-pair decomposition
q=z+w j, multiplicativity of N, and the matrix realization below. This note
records the exact elementary consequences and the prior QRH overlap. The
actual-source application is under separate investigation; no arithmetic
saving, new zero-free constant or repair of PR15 is claimed.

## Prior work and the remaining question

[[research revision] S44](../[research revision]/sol-post52-02/seeds.md) proposed quaternionic
embeddings of character phases. Both its
[Sol review](../[research revision]/sol-post52-02-sol-review/report.md) and
[Astra review](../[research revision]/sol-post52-02-astra-review/report.md) left it
untested, observing that an embedding alone does not supply cancellation.
That is not a rejection of a useful factorization using the norm identity.

There is a more concrete adjacent application. Section9 of
[sixth-forced-divisors](../sixth-forced-divisors.md) uses

    k(g)=t [[conj(d),-conj(c)],[c,d]],  t=(|c|^2+|d|^2)^(-1/2).

In the user's convention this is M(t conj(d)-t conj(c)j), a unit
quaternion. Sections9/17 use its two SU(2) components in the angular
intertwiner and spinor estimates; [[research revision]](../review-cycle-7.md) records
the associated fixed-family vertical-bound argument and its unsummed
divisor limitations. This identifies an existing use of the same matrix
structure, not an independently new validation of that entire argument.
The earlier S44 record does not develop a two-channel norm-factorization
estimate for the current complete signed source.

## Exact algebra in the user's convention

For jz=conj(z)j and j^2=-1, direct multiplication gives

    (A+Bj)(C+Dj) = (AC-B conj(D)) + (AD+B conj(C))j.

Consequently M(q)=[[z,w],[-conj(w),conj(z)]] is multiplicative,
M(conj(q))=M(q)^*, and

    M(q)^* M(q)=N(q) I,  det M(q)=N(q)=|z|^2+|w|^2.

Here N is the squared Euclidean norm, as in the user's notation. Taking
determinants proves N(pq)=N(p)N(q). In particular

    |AC-B conj(D)|^2 + |AD+B conj(C)|^2
      = (|A|^2+|B|^2)(|C|^2+|D|^2).                 (Q1)

These calculations fix the signs and conjugations without relying on
matrix-convention matching. The standard algebraic framework and
norm/determinant correspondence are also in Keith Conrad's
[Quaternion Algebras, section2](https://kconrad.math.uconn.edu/blurbs/ringtheory/quaternionalg.pdf),
consulted13October2026. The arguments below are explicit deductions here,
not claims quoted from that source.

For a nonnegative measure dnu and square-integrable expressions in (Q1),
write E=AC-B conj(D) and T=AD+B conj(C). Integration gives

    integral |E|^2 dnu
      = integral (|A|^2+|B|^2)(|C|^2+|D|^2) dnu
        - integral |T|^2 dnu.                     (Q2)

A certified upper bound P for the first integral and lower bound L for
the complete companion energy give the useful upper bound P-L for the
target. Both bounds must have enough joint precision to leave the desired
remainder. Dropping T gives only P. Thus the concrete opening is an exact
factorization of an actual QRH target with an estimable companion, including
all masks, coefficients, support, heights and residual terms. Positivity
alone supplies neither that factorization nor the required lower bound.

For an arbitrary two-channel lift with the original coefficients in its
first channel, additivity gives the equally exact identity

    N(sum_n (a_n+b_n j))=|sum_n a_n|^2+|sum_n b_n|^2. (Q3)

There is no cancellation between the two nonnegative channel energies.
This does not forbid estimating the pair more effectively through an
additional structure. It specifies what that new estimate must pay.

## Complex-height and multiplicative-source requirements

At a fixed complex s, the pointwise matrix M(F(s)+G(s)j) has positive
determinant |F(s)|^2+|G(s)|^2. Its conjugate entries are generally
antiholomorphic. More precisely, a holomorphic matrix-valued function
whose values remain in this quaternionic real subalgebra on a connected
complex open set is constant: its entries include F, G, conj(F), conj(G),
so both functions and their conjugates are holomorphic and their complex
derivatives vanish. This is compatible with using the matrix pointwise in
energy integrals, but it prevents silently using its positive norm as a
nonconstant holomorphic determinant in a Mellin or zero-exclusion argument.

On a reflection-invariant domain define F#(s)=conj(F(conj(s))) and similarly
G#. The genuinely holomorphic lift

    H(s)=[[F(s),G(s)],[-G#(s),F#(s)]]

has determinant F(s)F#(s)+G(s)G#(s). It agrees with the positive norm on
the real axis, not generally at complex heights. For example F(s)=s,
G(s)=1 gives determinant s^2+1, which vanishes at s=+/-i although the
pointwise quaternion norm is |s|^2+1>0. Also, pointwise positivity of the
pair would only exclude simultaneous zeros of F and G; recovering
nonvanishing of F requires an additional implication.

Finally a genuine homomorphism Q(mn)=Q(m)Q(n) from positive integers
under multiplication has commuting images, since mn=nm. Commuting
quaternions lie in one complex slice unless all are real: fix a nonreal
image a+u; the imaginary part v of every commuting quaternion satisfies
u cross v=0, so it belongs to R+R u. Thus this particular way of importing
noncommutativity collapses to a complex-valued source. The same restriction
applies to the prime images of an ordinary coprime-multiplicative source.
An ordered prime product or a noncommutative indexing object is a different
source and needs its own exact scalar return. No assertion is made that
every possible quaternionic construction has this obstruction.

## Next mathematical action

Construct or rule out (Q2) for a literal complete QRH source, with all
companion and recovery costs explicit. The root's bounded collaborator
owns [restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/quaternion-norm; its report is not automatically
accepted mathematics. Retain a useful identity or obstruction even if it
does not improve the conditional benchmark. This is an amendment to the
continuing research objective, not a replacement of the active source
repair, pending reviews or full PR library.

# Actual two-color source: a paid first-dual sector and an unresolved terminal estimate



The useful candidate proved below is a restricted estimate for the **actual signed fully squarefree, coprime part** of G181's R4. Expand the sixth-power-free row indicator, apply primitive Poisson, and retain first dual frequencies of norm at most U^(3/2). This signed scalar sector satisfies

    |R_unique,low| << H_J U^(5/2-(r+s)/3+epsilon).          (A)

The original slots are included. Against the inherited target T, the displayed exponent has raw margin at least857/16875>.0507 on the stated box. The proof uses the unconditional squarefree cubic large sieve with separated coefficients after conditioning on actual labels and original slots. It does not invoke the forbidden arbitrary-coefficient version of PR9(B3.6).

The complete residual is

    R4 = R_nonunique + R_unique,high + R_unique,low.       (B)

The first two terms are OPEN, signed and potentially mutually canceling. Neither (A) nor the stronger coefficient identities below bound R4 or a whole positive norm. No larger c follows. The accepted source-relative c11=.1251459636 and every inherited analytic, positive-slot and external admission obligation remain unchanged.

## 1. Exact inputs and scope

`source-pins.json` was frozen and read before substantive analysis; its SHA256 is df1d699ca3bb9427fdb023d6f99d2e8be261a4817c2d092cce195b85b37ca2bc. It pins [research revision] G179-G181, [research revision] G155-G157, [research revision] G146-G148, the maintained proof/index and PR9 paper at58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b. The source relative character, squareful/nonunit zeros, real roots, slot coefficients, profiles and endpoint conventions are those inputs. The controller subsequently updated its reservation file with native/claim readbacks; that mutable ownership receipt is not a changed mathematical source.

Use Eisenstein ideals through the original primary generators, all original unit sectors, fixed excluded S and finite ray dictionary. Write q_n=Nn and

    phi_u(n)=nu(n) chi_n(u)^e, e in {+1,-1},
    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n) phi_u(n) W(q_n/D),
    F_u=M_u(D1;W1) M_u(D2;W2) Q_u,
    D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v, N0=D1 D2 P0.

Here Q is the ORIGINAL normalized slot product, from disjoint prime pools, with all its coefficients, separate heights and common profile. It may meet either inverse in F. W1,W2 have the original common real parameter and TWO independent heights t1,t2. A primed copy in |F|^2 conjugates the complete product, retaining t1 on W1 and t2 on W2; it does not replace the two heights by one or resample them. Aligning e conjugates the entire slot product when required. Every character power is zero on a nonunit, including exponent0 or6.

Rows have exactly G181's nonzero sixth-power-free row enclosure and original fixed smooth nonnegative ball weight. Original divisor weights were dominated BEFORE expansion, as in G179. This report adds no signed physical row selector. Fixed finite ray/unit pieces are handled by the same finite expansions as PR9(B3.5),(B3.33)-(B3.36); they change fixed constants and the fixed dual lattice, not powers of U.

The physical parameter box is

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, 0<=v<=1/20.

Keep K=28114053/6250000 with its preceding-family ancestry. Set h0=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h0), k0=rho+delta-1,

    DK=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    aK=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h0 DK),
    bK=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/DK,
    EK=rho+delta v-min(3k0 v,aK+bK v),
    T=delta(r+s)+EK.

Use the already accepted EK>=rho>=19/54 and T>=123353/67500. G147's same-zero/common-annulus/plain restrictions remain additional restrictions on the actual witness. The larger box is used only for upper estimates.

## 2. The exact squarefree two-color coefficient

Write the oriented slot polynomial as

    Q_u=P0^(-1/2) sum_P b(P) chi_P(u)^e,

where P denotes the actual ordered slot tuple as well as its squarefree product. The lists remain disjoint; b(P) retains every original slot factor. On squarefree merged n=d1 d2 P the factors d1,d2,P are pairwise coprime. Since all these columns are S-good, nu(P) has modulus1. Defining b_tilde(P)=b(P) conjugate(nu(P)) only multiplies a fixed slot coefficient by a fixed unit; it never inverts a natural row zero. If j is the fixed slot count, the squarefree part of F is exactly

    F_sf,u=N0^(-1/2) (-1)^j sum_(n sf) mu(n)nu(n)
                                  chi_n(u)^e A(n),       (2.1)
    A(n)=sum_(original P|n) b_tilde(P)
           sum_(de=n/P) W1(q_d/D1;t1) W2(q_e/D2;t2).

The inner sum is over ordered splits, including a unit when the original support permits it. It has no independent Möbius signs: mu(d)mu(e)=(-1)^j mu(n). At t1=t2=0 with nonnegative inverse profiles, splits have the same inverse sign. This does not imply positivity when the original coefficients/heights are restored.

Define R_unique to be the portion of R4 with n,n' squarefree and (n,n')=1. Define R_nonunique=R4-R_unique. These are exhaustive signed scalar pair sums; the second includes every surviving repeated prime or nontrivial cross-column common prime. For sufficiently large U the unique conditions imply all six gcd cuts and the high-conductor cuts: each gcd is1, n!=n', Q1=q_n q_n'~N0^2, Q2=Q3=1. Thus R_unique is precisely the coprime pair expansion of (2.1) in the original row enclosure, with no additional pair mask silently omitted.

For these pairs the primitive good relative character is

    chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e)
     = conjugate(chi_(nn')(u)^e) chi_n(u)^(2e).           (2.2)

Its good conductor is the full squarefree nn', with local exponents1,5 (or5,1), and all natural zeros are retained. Equation(2.2) also holds at a nonunit because both sides vanish. It is a factorization, not an averaging argument.

## 3. The exact first-dual split

First use the finite identity

    1_(u sixth-power-free)=sum_(a^6|u) mu(a).

In the fixed row ball only q_a<<U^(1/6) occurs. Put u=a^6 z. The natural character contributes exactly 1_((a,nn')=1); freeze this as a column puncture. The row scale is U_a=U/q_a^6. The relevant primitive character modulo nn' is nonprincipal, so its zero Fourier frequency is ZERO. This assertion concerns the relative character, and does not delete individual principal inducing rows of the original family.

Apply masked primitive Poisson, with the literal finite ray/reciprocity computation of PR9(B3.5),(B3.33)-(B3.36), on coprime n,n'. Up to fixed source normalizations, a summand has the factor

    (U_a/N0^2) * [bounded smooth profile]
    * b_tilde(P) conjugate(b_tilde(P'))
    * a0(n)nu_1(n) chi_n(ell)
    * conjugate(a0(n')nu_2(n') chi_n'(ell)),             (3.1)

where a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n)) gamma_2(n), |a0(n)|=1 on squarefree good n. Either complete conjugate orientation can occur; it is retained. The profile includes the exact real factor N0/sqrt(q_n q_n') and the original Fourier kernel at U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), plus all original inverse and slot profiles. The prefactor follows directly from N0^(-1) in the original pair coefficient and U_a/sqrt(q_n q_n') in primitive Poisson. Fixed ray phases of the ratio n/n' are expanded in the original finite dictionary. No estimate for the merged coefficient has been applied here.

Equation(3.1) is summed over the actual ordered tuples n=d1*d2*P and n'=d1'*d2'*P'. Its bounded smooth profile is the tuple profile, not a claim that the merged arithmetic function A(n) is smooth or uniformly bounded. The slot coefficients remain outside it, in their original product form.

In particular, the cross-copy CRT factor for e=+1 is chi_n(n') conjugate(chi_n'(n))=R(n,n'), the fixed ray sign of PR9(B1.1)-(B1.5). It is NOT an extra cubic phase joining a color from the first copy to a color from the second. Before the finite ray expansion, the two arithmetic factors, with the original nu(n) conjugate(nu(n')) understood, are literally

    e=-1: R(n,n') chi_n(-1) conjugate(G(n)) G(n')
           * a0(n) conjugate(a0(n')) chi_n(ell) conjugate(chi_n'(ell)),
    e=+1: R(n,n') G(n) conjugate(G(n')) chi_n'(-1)
           * conjugate(a0(n)) a0(n') conjugate(chi_n(ell)) chi_n'(ell).

These follow from mu(z)gamma_-1(z)=a0(z)chi_z(-1)conjugate(G(z)) and mu(z)gamma_1(z)=conjugate(a0(z))G(z). All G, chi_z(-1) and R factors belong to the fixed ray dictionary. Expand that finite matrix before extending coprimality; either line becomes a finite sum of products of the displayed kind(3.1). The inverse profiles remain W1(t1)W2(t2) on the left and conjugate(W1(t1)W2(t2)) on the right in both lines. This is precisely the exact arithmetic part of PR9(B3.33)-(B3.36); the canonical inequality there is not imported.

The first frequency ell lies in the actual fixed dual lattice; clearing its fixed S-supported denominator gives an equivalent norm bound up to a fixed constant. Define the low sector by q_ell<=Y with Y=U^(3/2), in each literal Poisson summand, and define the high sector by its exact complement. In particular Y does not depend on the current n,n',a, heights or slot tuple. The full Schwartz kernel is kept on both sides. Taking the real part after summing conjugate orientations is harmless and makes the definition independent of how those finite orientations are enumerated. Thus R_unique=R_unique,low+R_unique,high exactly.

This is a signed scalar Fourier restriction AFTER the exact row expansion. It is not deletion of terms from a positive norm. The high sector still includes its full infinite frequency tail; no tail is declared paid in this report.

### Natural holes at the new frequency

At a prime dividing n or n', the primitive finite Fourier transform is zero when that prime divides ell. There is no factor sqrt((ell,nn')) or other gcd size: the character is primitive at every good conductor prime, with exponent1 or5. When slots are conditioned on below, a slot prime dividing ell simply kills that term. Fixed S factors have only the original fixed-modulus price.

To remove the remaining mutual coprimality, first define (3.1), its full profile and formal product conductor on all individually squarefree columns, retaining all individual zeros. THEN insert the complete identity

    1_((n,n')=1)=sum_(f|n,f|n') mu(f).

No Poisson formula is asserted for the artificial noncoprime conductors. The full Möbius sum annihilates precisely those artificial pairs. On n=f m,n'=f m', squarefreeness gives (m,f)=(m',f)=1, and

    a0(fm)=a0(f)a0(m) chi_m(f)^4.                        (3.2)

The extracted frequency factor is chi_f(ell) conjugate(chi_f(ell))=1_((ell,f)=1). It is a contraction; it is NOT replaced by a gcd magnitude or divided out. All remaining factors involving ell stay separately on m and m'.

## 4. Pointwise cubic-sieve bound with the actual colors and slots

The unconditional input is Heath-Brown's squarefree cubic large sieve, stated in the pinned PR9 inputs and independently in [Dunn-Radziwill arXiv2109.07463v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3), equation(1.11)/Theorem9.1:

    sum_(d sf,q_d<<D) |sum_(e sf,q_e<<E) beta_e chi_e(d)^4|^2
      << (DE)^epsilon [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] sum_e |beta_e|^2. (4.1)

Replacing a cubic symbol by its conjugate changes nothing. Both variables are squarefree. beta can be any sequence independent of d. This is not an estimate for an arbitrary joint matrix beta_(d,e).

For separated coefficients of size bounded by fixed seminorm factors, Cauchy in d followed by (4.1) gives the normalized pointwise bound

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(d,e sf) alpha_d beta_e chi_e(d)^4|^2
       << H_J [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] (DE)^epsilon.             (4.2)

The coprimality (d,e)=1 is already present as the zero of the cubic symbol. Additional fixed punctures in either color, finite ray coefficients, angular Gauss phases, independent norm twists and natural zeros at ell are permissible separated coefficients. Conditioning on f,a,ell and on a slot tuple does not change this contract.

Here is how the original source, including slots, enters (4.2). Allocate each prime of extracted f to its actual inverse color or to an original slot; left and right copies allocate independently. The number of allocations is at most tau(f)^C for a fixed C depending on the eventual original slot count. Assigned slot primes divide f and retain their original coefficients. The remaining inverse lengths on a given side are D1'=D1/q_f1 and D2'=D2/q_f2. The remaining slot product has nominal length P'=P0/q_fP, and

    f=f1 f2 fP, (f1,f2,fP) pairwise coprime,
    D1' D2' P' = N0/q_f =: X_f.                         (4.3)

There is no arbitrary choice of these labels: each comes from an actual ordered tuple in(2.1). Empty support is omitted. A nonempty nominal subunit inverse window is clipped by a bounded dilation, as in PR9's convention. Each remaining slot retains its ORIGINAL pool and profile. P' differs from the product of their original nominal lengths only by bounded original annular ratios of the extracted slot primes; those ratios are kept in the profile. Unit residual colors are included in the elementary finite part of(4.2), with the same bound. H_J denotes one fixed polynomial height/seminorm envelope, enlarged finitely when bounding both copies.

For clarity, the four original inverse factors map as follows. In the first copy d1=f1*x and d2=f2*y, so the HB variables are x,y of lengths D1/q_f1,D2/q_f2. In the conjugate copy d1'=f1'*x' and d2'=f2'*y', with HB variables x',y' of lengths D1/q_f1',D2/q_f2'. The same common ideal satisfies f=f1*f2*fP=f1'*f2'*fP', but its two allocations need not agree. We bound each Gauss column separately and then their product. No HB variable is xx', yy', xy' or yx'. All same-color and opposite-color cross-copy coprimality conditions are supplied together by the COMPLETE mutual-gcd identity of Section3. Their artificial violations cancel in that full identity; no residual cross-copy coprimality is silently dropped from an individual norm. The within-copy x,y coprimality is instead the cubic-symbol zero in(4.4).

Freeze an actual surviving tuple P. In the remaining squarefree column m=d e P, the factors d,e,P are pairwise coprime, and twisted multiplicativity gives

    a0(deP)=a0(d)a0(e)a0(P) chi_e(d)^4 chi_(de)(P)^4.    (4.4)

The factors chi_d(P)^4 and chi_e(P)^4 retain the P-punctures and separate. The f-puncture, a-puncture, finite characters and chi_(de)(ell) likewise separate. The coefficient of d is now independent of e and vice versa. Thus (4.2) applies to these actual colors. A general joint coefficient would invalidate this step; none has been introduced.

The common-profile lemma PR9(B3.3) separates the coupled smooth norm factors before any live label is chosen. Dyadically localize a and the nonzero ell with fixed unit windows and nominal lengths A,H; the sharp condition q_ell<=Y remains an OUTER restriction. Use the full ambient box of the original inverse and individual slot norms on BOTH copies, together with q_a/A and q_ell/H. The kernel has the form K(C*y_ell/(y_a^6*product(y_columns))), C=UH/(A^6*N0^2), where C depends only on nominal sector lengths. Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded for every C>0 by the original Schwartz seminorms. The Fourier measure is therefore fixed before the actual a,f,ell or slot tuple. Substitute d_i=f_i*x_i only afterward. Extracted imaginary powers have modulus1, and the residual tests have the actual shortened scales. The O(log U)^2 nominal sectors have subpower total cost. Real inverse roots enter that profile once. This produces separated norm twists with finite weighted Fourier L1 mass and polynomial dependence on the original independent heights. No arithmetic pair mask is smoothed away.

For each fixed P, (4.2) bounds the centrally normalized two-inverse Gauss sum. Hilbert triangle (or pointwise triangle here) over the ORIGINAL remaining slot tuples costs at most

    (P')^(-1/2) sum_P |b(P)| << H_J (P')^(1/2+epsilon).

Ideal counting suffices; no prime theorem or slot independence is assumed. Consequently the entire normalized remaining column polynomial B_f(ell), for each allocation and each Fourier component, satisfies

    |B_f(ell)|^2
      << H_J P' [D1'+D2'+(D1'D2')^(2/3)] U^epsilon
      << H_J P0 [D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)] U^epsilon.         (4.5)

Both original height weights are still on their original colors. On the right side of a correlation, the whole column is conjugated. Equation(4.5) applies to either orientation separately; their product is bounded by the geometric mean. If ell shares any source, slot or f prime, its zero is retained as described in Section3 and the same inequality holds without a new gcd factor.

## 5. Exact label payment and proof of(A)

In(3.1), after n=fm,n'=fm', each remaining unnormalized column sum has scale X_f^(1/2). Converting BOTH copies to B_f therefore multiplies U_a/N0^2 by X_f, giving the exact factor

    U/(q_a^6 N0 q_f).                                  (5.1)

This is the important normalization: there is one q_f^(-1), not q_f^0, after both roots. The independent color allocations do not change X_f, since their product identities(4.3) are the same on both sides. Their heights add unit phases or enter the original normalized profiles. They do not introduce q_f to a positive fixed power. The two sides may have different shortened D1',D2', but each is bounded by its original length in(4.5).

The full common Fourier integral is restored before bounding the scalar. Absolute values now cost

    sum_(q_a<<U^(1/6)) q_a^(-6) << 1,
    sum_(q_f<<N0) tau(f)^C/q_f <<_epsilon U^epsilon,
    #{ell:0<q_ell<=Y} << Y.                             (5.2)

The first sum is an absolutely convergent ideal sum. For the second, tau(f)^C<<_eta q_f^eta and ideal counting O(X) give O_eta N0^(2eta), and eta is chosen afterward small enough for the fixed polynomial scale cap. This explicitly includes BOTH independent allocation multiplicities and conjugate-side profile losses. Natural masks only reduce these absolute sums. There is no uncounted average over f or slot labels. All bounds are uniform over the fixed original profiles/heights through H_J.

Combining(4.5),(5.1),(5.2) gives the source estimate, for 1<=Y<=U^(B_*) with any fixed polynomial scale cap B_*,

    |R_unique,<=Y|
      << H_J U^(1+epsilon) Y/(D1D2)
                      [D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].            (5.3)

The P0 factor in(4.5) cancels the P0 inside N0 in(5.1); the original slots were paid, not discarded. In the actual box s>r and s<2r. Hence the bracket is O((D1D2)^(2/3)), and Y=U^(3/2) proves(A).

For a deliberately coarse certificate, r+s>217/100 gives exponent at most533/300. Therefore

    T-[5/2-(r+s)/3] >= 123353/67500-533/300
                      =857/16875 >1/20.                (5.4)

Using EK>=rho and differentiating also gives the sharper lower margin26011/341250>.0762, but this is unnecessary. The fixed threshold Y precedes suprema and is not differentiated. Finite Sobolev derivatives change the inverse tests by the original operators, including -W/2-yW'; the same proof applies. Freely small arithmetic/Fourier/height shares can leave a margin1/100. This margin is for this free signed sector only.

The typical first dual scale for small a is N0^2/U, whose exponent is2(r+s+v)-1>3.34, far beyond1.5. Thus (5.3) pays a genuine but limited portion of the fully coprime high-conductor source. It is not a proof that the unpaid sector is small.

## 6. Why direct canonical merging remains open

The narrow forbidden import is **equation(B3.6) in sectionB3.2**, not later sectionB3.6. Its squarefree column coefficient is exactly a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)chi_n(k)chi_n(f)^4 d_I(n), where d_I is an original finite product-prime mark. It explicitly permits no further coefficient on n.

For a squarefree unmarked n, double Mellin inversion of its original two-divisor profile gives the multiplicative weight

    eta_(z,w)(n)=product_(p|n)(q_p^(-z)+q_p^(-w)).        (6.1)

The two Mellin variables retain the two independent height coordinates and their original annuli; replacing them by one variable is not valid. With original slots the weight is sum_(P|n) b_tilde(P) eta_(z,w)(n/P). One may retain this deleted-prime form. If one instead factors eta(n), choose separated real contours Re z=kappa, Re w=-kappa, kappa>0 fixed and arbitrarily small. Then

    |eta_(z,w)(p)|>=q_p^kappa(1-q_p^(-2kappa))>0.

Division at forced slot primes is now legitimate and bounded by a fixed kappa-dependent factor per slot. No natural character value is divided out. Eta costs at most tau(n)q_n^kappa; choose kappa only after the bounded scale and finite-depth loss budgets. On coincident real contours eta(p) may vanish, so the same division would be invalid.

This structure survives a COPRIME extraction: eta(fn)=eta(f)eta(n). Thus the two exact Poisson transformations in PR9(B3.12)-(B3.29) retain eta or its conjugate on the residual column; extracted eta(f) factors have divisor/small-power cost. With a completed cube index, primes shared with its cube variable must first be assigned and extracted as in the original proof. These algebraic observations do not prove the full inductive estimate.

Cube inversion(B3.8) itself works for ANY mark d_*(A): on putting c=hb, d_*(nc^3) is independent of h|c and sum_(h|c)mu(h) kills c!=1. So cube inversion is not the missing analytic step. Choose the useful extension eta(p^a)=q_p^(-az)+q_p^(-aw), a>=1. Then eta(A) is the sum over unitary two-color splits A=A1 A2,(A1,A2)=1, with each entire prime power assigned to one color.

If A_i=n_i b_i^3 is the completed theta index, the exact cross coefficient is

    a0(n1n2)=a0(n1)a0(n2) chi_n2(n1)^4,
    chi_A2(A1)^4=chi_n2(n1)^4.                          (6.2)

The equality uses coprimality; cube exponents contribute multiples of6, whose zeros could not be erased without that condition. Thus the weighted completed source is a **coupled coprime convolution of two completed theta coefficient systems**, with the cross phase in(6.2). It is not a product of two independent theta sums. For actual primary primes -2-3omega and1-3omega of norms7 and13, chi_(1-3omega)(-2-3omega)^4=omega, already a nontrivial coupling.

The first unlicensed analytic gate is the terminal application of RE to this weighted completed theta source. PR9(B2.6)-(B2.15) reflects the specified theta Fourier coefficients and allowed product-prime masks. Its permission for a bounded remaining tuple coefficient arises AFTER slot assignment; it does not authorize multiplication of every primal Fourier coefficient by eta. No reflection law for the coupled source(6.2) has been proved here.

Two affordable checks delimit this attempt. For an uncompleted Gauss source with two fixed colors D=Z^x,E=Z^y and row cap Z^M, (4.2) gives energy at most Z^M[D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] up to small powers. This is exactly what pays the restricted sector above, but not the full first dual range. Alternatively, Cauchy over the shorter color, followed by canonical(B3.7) where its margins hold, costs Z^(x+y+min(x,y)). The whole shorter-color factor is real; label averaging in(B3.6) does not remove it.

Even an optimistic extension giving the unchanged single-inverse free-row exponent e(L)=(1+5L)/6 at merged inverse length L=r+s would not by itself meet the present target. Since EK<=rho+delta v,

    e(r+s)-T >= 1/6+(5/6-delta)(r+s)-rho-delta v
              >=1867/27000>.0691;                     (6.3)

with v=0 the lower gap is703/6750>.1041. The right side decreases in delta on this box, increases in r+s and decreases in v, so the bounds follow at delta=.7,r+s=2.17,v=.05 or0. This is an inadequacy of that merged-norm route, not a lower bound on actual R4 and not permission to dominate a signed subset by a full norm. A successful full approach must retain extra two-color/dual structure, or improve more than just the coefficient contract.

## 7. Euler identity: useful, but no hidden inverse-square estimate

On absolute lines Re s1,Re s2>1 the original signed coprime inverse product is exactly

    sum_((d,e)=1) mu(d)mu(e)phi_u(de)/(q_d^s1 q_e^s2)
      = product_p(1-X_p-Y_p)
      = [L_u(s1)L_u(s2)]^(-1) H_u(s1,s2),              (7.1)
    X_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s1), Y_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s2),
    H_p=1-X_pY_p/[(1-X_p)(1-Y_p)].

The exact formal coefficients are H_(a,b)=-phi_u(p)^(a+b) for a,b>=1, and zero when precisely one exponent is positive. H converges absolutely, uniformly in u, when the two real parts are bounded below by a positive constant and their sum exceeds1 by a fixed amount. Nonunit factors phi_u(p)=0 give H_p=1. On the equal-variable diagonal the squarefree coefficient is (-2)^omega(n); off that diagonal both variables are necessary.

Equation(7.1) is the controller-suggested identity verified at its literal source. It replaces the coprime product by a joint inverse-square-type object plus higher-prime-power corrections. It does not estimate the required fourth moment, shift through zeros, erase the independent annuli or resolve the terminal theta gate. No result is imported from a scalar Euler-product analogy.

## 8. Complete return, objections, novelty and next action

Combine(B) with G181's existing equality:

    ||F_<||_U^2 = R_nonunique + R_unique,high
                    + O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)),       (8.1)

after absorbing the stronger low-dual estimate. This preserves the ENTIRE complement. A one-sided estimate for the SUM R_nonunique+R_unique,high, with some fixed saving xi, would still be needed. Only then would G181 give free OPEN-MIX with every strict margin below min(xi,1/200), and G147's two actual inverse signals/counting would retain a margin below min(xi,1/200,1/2000). No possibly zero slot is divided out.

Both signed physical projectors, family reconstruction, root/slot holes, exceptional and inducing rows,6a/9a radii, K_phys,5/6 amplification, clipped rectangles, shortenings, Euler shifts, principal branches, actual suprema, common mesh and all detector tails still require their full licensed payment. Internal buffered witnesses may exceed delta=.70; this report never replaces their signal extraction by the physical-bin inequality. The centered reserve is unspent. There is no xi-to-c map, no attained near endpoint, and no licensed extrapolation to c=1/6 or1/4.

Strongest objections checked: (i) HB needs separated squarefree colors—(4.4) gives exactly those after fixed-label/profile separation; (ii) ell meeting a source prime supplies a primitive zero, not a lost gcd factor; (iii) both normalizations and both allocation multiplicities leave the explicit harmonic f mass(5.1)-(5.2); (iv) the low sector remains signed and its high/nonunique complements are retained; (v) the general eta extension still lacks terminal RE. Independent review should especially challenge these five points and the exact placement of the first dual cut.

Credit: G155-G157 first established the actual separated inverse source and its signed relative-conductor remainder; G179-G181 paid the full four-cross-gcd extension. Earlier [research revision] MG concerns a different rational completed source. The early index's [research revision]-HG small-dual payment is an antecedent for the strategy, on its own source; no old theorem is transferred without checking its source. The proposed addition here is the explicit original-slot two-color cubic-sieve payment of the low first-dual sector of the unique G181 source. No literature priority is claimed. The retained eta/Euler identities are supporting structure and failures, not separate arithmetic cycles.

A sparse primary-source check read Dunn-Radziwill arXiv2109.07463v3,14May2024, equation(1.11)/Theorem9.1, whose squarefree upper bound is unconditional; its GRH-dependent sharper conclusions were not used. Dunn arXiv2403.13151v3's bilinear theorem concerns cuspidal cubic metaplectic forms; it was inspected and not imported for this noncuspidal theta source. Source URLs and locations are in the supplemental source manifest.

`check_source.py` verifies exact finite character zeros and relative factorizations, actual-prime cross phases, cube inversion with shared primes, the unitary two-color identity, signed slot merging, formal bivariate Euler coefficients and rational exponent prices. Its receipt is finite algebra/price evidence, not a proof of an infinite moment or of the whole canonical induction. The argument above is the mathematical evidence.

Next mathematical action: retain the coupled colors and study the high first-dual range with its actual kernel, initially a band immediately above U^(3/2), while preserving the nonunique companion term. A terminal reflection theorem for(6.2) would be valuable, but merely extending canonical coefficients at the old exponent is quantitatively insufficient. ## The quantitative obstruction to the selected bridge

Apply(B) to Theorem M's fixed sequence with H=floor(X^theta), theta<beta. Since F_a(X)=C_tau X^beta+O(X^sigma), C_tau!=0, the replacement error O(H) is smaller than the leading term. Therefore, for every sufficiently large X,

  E_a(X,H) >= c_{a,tau,theta} X^(2*beta-1+theta).     (O)

Thus an energy estimate E<<X^(1+delta+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 is impossible in this class when theta-delta>2(1-beta). This is a strict exponent comparison. Equality is not ruled out, and no equality/strict-reserve impossibility is asserted for the epsilon-loss endpoint problem.

Numerically choose gamma=.87449, beta=.8747 and a summatory calibration exponent .8748<b6. These choices all satisfy the theorem. At theta=.26 the proposed target energy exponent is1.00898, whereas(O) forces at least1.0094, a gap.00042. For ANY proposed first-gain exponent gamma<b6, choose beta strictly between gamma and b6 and then a calibration exponent strictly between beta and b6. The same obstruction works. statement:
### R39-A. Complex-polynomial interpolation is valid

For a complex polynomial P of degree <=N on a unit interval, with
|P|<=m almost everywhere on a measurable set of measure >=delta,
the bound

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N m                            (R39.2)

is valid. Use the closed sublevel set of P, of measure Delta>=delta,
and choose its N+1 interior measure quantiles. Its distribution
function is 1-Lipschitz, so x_j-x_i>=(j-i)delta/(N+1). The Lagrange
denominator at node j is at least
(delta/(N+1))^N j!(N-j)!, while each numerator factor on I is <=1.
The sum of absolute interpolation weights is therefore at most
((N+1)/delta)^N 2^N/N! <=(4e/delta)^N. Complex values require no
extra sign or real-root assumption. Essential suprema are handled
by enlarging m and taking a limit. The case N=0 is immediate.

Now suppose a fixed complex-growth bound is available:

    |F(u+iv)| <= C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), u>=0,    (R39.3)

with fixed b>gamma. In every sufficiently large integer interval
I_j=[j,j+1], suppose a measurable E_j has measure >=c j^-kappa and
essential supremum <=C_0 exp(gamma j). The same conclusion holds
with arbitrarily small exponent allowances, as specified below.

Take N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j), center j+1/2 and radius
R=sqrt(tau(N+1)). For large j, the whole disk lies in u>=0.
The maximum on that disk has logarithm

    <=bj+R^2/(2tau)+bR+O(K log(1+R)+1).

Cauchy's coefficient estimate for the Taylor polynomial P_N gives
on the whole real interval the **complete** remainder

    r_j <= M_R (1/(2R))^(N+1)/(1-1/(2R)),
    log r_j <= bj-(N/2)log N+O(N+sqrt N+K log N)
             =gamma j+o(j).                             (R39.4)

The o(j) includes the positive j*loglog j/log j correction; it is
not silently removed before interpolation. On E_j, |P_N| is at
most C_0 exp(gamma j)+r_j. Apply R39.2 to P_N and then add the
remainder outside E_j. Both errors survive:

    sup_I |F| <= L_j C_0 exp(gamma j)+(L_j+1)r_j,
    log L_j <= 2kappa(b-gamma)j+o(j).

Thus the complete output exponent is

    gamma+2kappa(b-gamma).                               (R39.5)

This verifies W39.3--8, including the coefficient 2 and both
amplified remainders. It does not prove this coefficient optimal.
For kappa>=1/2 this estimate does not improve the prior b; it is
not an impossibility theorem for all observation methods.

For kappa=0, a fixed positive measure in **every** unit interval
already preserves gamma for an arbitrary bounded-coefficient fixed
Gaussian. A derivative bound for each fixed order does not suffice
in its place: this proof uses orders N growing like j/log j and a
quantitative complex bound on disks of radius about sqrt(j/log j).
A merely fixed-width analytic strip likewise does not give R39.4.
title: R39-A. Complex-polynomial interpolation is valid

## Independent reconstruction

The author and independent Astra reviewer stopped before integration.
The frozen review is40,420 bytes, SHA256
ccdb8ce3a52cf1cc793b09e20239b1f7bc9beba0718b16c13309e986b88ce7bf.
All three W35 source files are copied without editing; source hashes and
the previous proof/scorecard snapshots are recorded separately.

1. **Detector and zero bridge.** Direct Gaussian integration gives
   exp(tau*s^2/2)(1-2^(1-s))/zeta(s). The negative log-time tail is
   Gaussian, while an all-shell logarithmic L2 bound makes the positive
   transform holomorphic to the claimed open half-plane. Multiplying
   by zeta exposes a zero there because the other factors have no
   zeros in the open critical strip. Fixed tau, all dyads and arbitrary
   epsilon are required. Zeros of the numerator on Re s=1 are treated
   by the inherited right-boundary theorem, not ignored.
2. **Convolution signs.** Since mu*b=q_2, expansion of
   (mu-m_Y)^2*b gives A-2m_Y*q_2+m_Y^2*b. Hence G=R+2L-I.
   The genuine Gaussian short term is nonzero, with a paid negative
   quadratic log exponent. The Type-I term uses a complete ell sum.
3. **Growing derivative constants.** In Cauchy's formula the complex
   log disk gives exp(pi^2/(8tau)); the two completed Gaussian
   integrals give 2*2^m*2^(m-1)=4^m. The half-integer Poisson sum is
   2(2^m-1)zeta(m), which gives the stated upper coefficient
   2K_tau zeta(m)(4/pi)^m. This checks the normalization and the
   m-dependent exponential needed for m of order sqrt(log X) or log X.
4. **Original-label rectangle payment.** i+j<-2 implies
   de<X exp(-kappa sqrt L), even at half-open endpoints. Conversely,
   i+j>floor((log B-L)/H) implies de>B. If d>B/(Y+1), the strict
   lower cut on e also implies de>B. These are the exact discarded
   sources. A surviving rectangle can include lower products than
   the literal de cut; its complete ell field is retained. The later
   n-cap therefore has restoration2 exp(3kappa sqrt L), versus
   2 exp(2kappa sqrt L) for the literal product cut.
5. **Mellin and local energy.** The ell transform is first established
   on Re s>1 and continued from its paid tails, so eta(a+it) is not
   obtained by interchanging an absolutely divergent series.
   Local integration gives ((2X)^(2a+i(t-t'))-X^(2a+i(t-t')))/
   (2a+i(t-t')). Both heights and every ordered component cross term
   survive. Global Plancherel yields only a stronger sufficient
   component target. No converse is asserted.
6. **Fixed-A extension.** Setting kappa=C=sqrt(2tau(1+A)) and
   D=sqrt(2(1+A)/tau) gives exponent-A in the product, total-label
   and height tails. Growing derivative/factorial losses are o(log X)
   for fixed parameters. J=floor(1+log2/(kappa sqrt L))=1 eventually;
   increasing fixed cutoffs leaves four diagonals and subpower
   auxiliary costs. For tau=1, kappa=C=D=2 gives-A=-1.
   No parameter is allowed to grow with X in this conclusion.
7. **Scalar mixed terms.** The Mertens calibration gives ||G||<=X^beta.
   Thus the exact polarization comparison is at most
   2||G||||G-R||+||G-R||^2, with exponent beta+q for q<beta.
   Norm equivalence, not an unnecessarily coarse scalar estimate,
   is the correct return for much lower conditional exponents.
8. **Physical Gram.** Multiplying the two Gaussian densities gives
   g_(2tau)(log(n/m))g_(tau/2)(u-log(sqrt(nm)/X)) with the stated
   constants. The d_3^2<=d_9 inequality follows by encoding each
   pair of three-part compositions as margins of a canonical
   nonnegative3-by-3 matrix; different margins remain distinct.
   The far-pair cost2-r^2/(4tau) uses the complete absolute coefficient
   mass. It never supplies an absolute bound for the near scalar.

These checks reconstruct the argument. They are not numerical evidence

statement:
## 1. Kernel and transfer: independent derivation

Let a_j=2^(-j), U_j uniform on [-a_j,a_j], and S=sum_j U_j.
Absolute convergence holds for every outcome because
sum_j |U_j|<=1. The characteristic functions converge on compact
t intervals to the characteristic function of S, by dominated
convergence. Each factor is sinc(a_j t). For any fixed integer
L, its first L factors satisfy

\[
 \left|\prod_{j=1}^L\frac{\sin(a_jt)}{a_jt}\right|
 \le C_L(1+|t|)^{-L};
 \qquad
 \left|\prod_{j>L}\frac{\sin(a_jt)}{a_jt}\right|\le1.
 \tag{DPR1}
\]

For |t|>=1 one may take a constant at least
prod_(j<=L) a_j^(-1); for bounded t enlarge that constant.
To obtain the m-th derivative of the density, choose L>m+1.
Fourier inversion then gives a continuous m-th derivative. This
proves k is C-infinity for every finite m, without a derivative
order that grows with J. The density represents a probability
law, is nonnegative and even, has mass one, and vanishes outside
[-1,1]. Smoothness on the whole real line includes flat boundary
jets at both support endpoints.

The bounded random variable S has entire Laplace transform
M(s)=E exp(sS). Independence first on finite partial sums and
dominated convergence give DP3. On any compact s set, the sum
of absolute deviations of the factors from one converges,
because it is bounded by a constant times sum_j 4^(-j).
Every individual factor is nonzero off the imaginary axis.
At such a fixed s, a summable-deviation product of nonzero
factors has a nonzero limit: the logarithms of its sufficiently
late factors converge absolutely. Thus M(s) is nonzero for
Re s>0. This is a qualitative nonvanishing statement; no
uniform lower bound on high vertical lines is asserted.

The tail after J has exactly the law 2^(-J)S, independently
of its first J uniforms. Hence k=h_J*k_delta at
delta=2^(-J), with h_J a probability density supported in
[-1+delta,1-delta]. Substituting v=log(n/x) gives DP5 with
the correct sign xe^t. All n appearing for a fixed x and all
t in that compact support lie in one finite set, so exchanging
the sum and the t integral needs no infinite arithmetic
convergence assumption.

The full weighted Jensen calculation is

\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_X^{2X}|F_{B,1}(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 &\le\int h_J(t)
       \int_{Xe^t}^{2Xe^t}|F_{B,\delta}(y)|^2\frac{dy}{y}\,dt\\
 &=\int |F_{B,\delta}(y)|^2 w_X(y)\frac{dy}{y},\\
 w_X(y)&=\int h_J(t)1_{\{Xe^t\le y\le2Xe^t\}}dt.
 \end{split}
 \tag{DPR2}
\]

Here 0<=w_X<=1 and its support is inside [e^(-1)X,2eX].
This proves DP6 with constant one for every J. The variable
delta on this entire right side is the one selected using X,
not a width reselected using y. The floor in DP7 gives the
claimed inequalities exactly. No comparison of two different
moving widths has been used.

For OPEN-DP and any compact set Re s>=a+g, g>0, take
epsilon<2g. The contribution of [2^j,2^(j+1)] to the
absolute Mellin integral of F_(A,1) is at most
C_epsilon 2^(j(a+epsilon/2-Re s)). These bounds are summable;
extra fixed powers of log x remain summable on a smaller
positive gap. Since the function vanishes below e^(-1),
this proves locally uniform holomorphy in Re s>a.

In Re s>1, the substitution u=n/x gives the identity

\[
 \int_0^\infty V_1(n/x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
       =n^{-s}M(s).
 \tag{DPR3}
\]

The interchange with A(n) is absolutely convergent there
because |A(n)|<=3. Consequently DP12 is correctly normalized.
On a<Re s<1, the factor 1-2^(1-s) cannot vanish, since its
second term has modulus greater than one; M does not vanish
there either. The meromorphic identity
zeta(s) mathscr F(s)=M(s)(1-2^(1-s)) continues from Re s>1
to Re s>a. A zero of zeta inside that open strip would make
its left side zero and its right side nonzero. The accepted
baseline handles Re s>=1, including the distinction between
the pole at one and a zero. This proves the stated conditional
bridge, without a moving Mellin transform or a lower bound
for |M(s)| at large height.

## G156. Complete diagonal and two off-diagonal sectors

Merge only after the tuple cut:

\[
B_{<G}(u)Q_u=\sum_n c(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1},\qquad
n=d_1d_2\prod_ip_i,\quad N_0=D_1D_2P_0.
\]

The coefficient c contains every Möbius sign, fixed character, pool,
profile, independent height, normalization and original tuple gcd cut.
Each prime valuation of n is 0,1,2 or3, including all collisions. Hence
\(n/n'\) is a sixth power as an ideal only when \(n=n'\): the valuation
difference lies in [-3,3]. Finite unit/root phases remain in their fixed
sectors. This fact does not apply to older completions with unbounded
prime powers. Divisor bounds give
\(|c(n)|\ll H_JN_0^{-1/2}U^\epsilon\) and
\(\sum_n|c(n)|^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon\). The **complete** paired diagonal is
therefore \(O(H_JU^{1+\epsilon})\); this is not a lower bound for the full
norm.

For an off-diagonal pair let \(e_{\mathfrak p}=v_{\mathfrak p}(n)-
v_{\mathfrak p}(n')\), let q_j be the radical of primes with
\(|e_{\mathfrak p}|=j\), and write

\[
Q_j=Nq_j,\quad Q=Q_1Q_2Q_3,\quad V=Q_1Q_2^2Q_3^3.
\]

Retain the full oriented integer vector. Although signs +3 and -3 have
the same sextic phase, their integer ratios differ; the finite allocation
cost must not be discarded. Every nonzero exponent has nonprincipal
primitive local phase at a good prime. The fixed factor \(\nu\) stays
in c and is not falsely treated as order six.

Write \(n=ga,n'=gb,(a,b)=1\). Then \(NaNb=V\) and
\(Ng\ll N_0/\sqrt V\), so for one full relative vector

\[
\sum_{(n,n')\text{ inducing it}}|c(n)c(n')|
\ll H_JU^\epsilon V^{-1/2}.
\]

This includes all shared slot/inverse collisions. Counting vectors in
fixed dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 boxes gives mass
\(\ll H_JU^\epsilon(Q_1/Q_3)^{1/2}\). Empty subunit gcd ranges remain
empty, with fixed endpoint constants retained.

The row kernel includes **all** natural-zero holes E from shared primes
whose character phases cancel, and all retained frozen punctures not
already in the primitive conductor. Cancellation of phase does not
remove a hole. Here NE is polynomial in U. Applying the existing masked
Poisson formula, whose primitive prefactor is X/\(\sqrt Q\) and dual
scale XNh/Q, gives \(\min(X,\sqrt Q)\), with zero dual term absent.
Expand sixth-power-freeness and full holes by
\(b^6\mid u\) and \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}E\), respectively, putting
\(X=U/((Nb)^6Nd)\). Splitting at
\(Nb=(U/(Nd\sqrt Q))^{1/6}\) yields

\[
|\mathcal K(n,n')|\ll H_JU^\epsilon
\min(U,U^{1/6}Q^{5/12}).                              \tag{G156.1}
\]

The hole Euler product with exponent -1/6 is subpower. Thresholds below
one use the complete tail; conductor-sharing natural zeros and fixed
excluded/ray sectors are retained. Finitely many inducing free-row
deletions cost O(1) per kernel, already absorbed. This is not a blanket
deletion license for the raw physical row set.

Separate the paired sum disjointly: full diagonal; then Q≤\(U^{9/5}\);
then the remaining pairs with \(Q_1/Q_3\le U^{8/5}\). The low-Q sum uses
V≥Q and the divisor count to sum \(Q^{-1/12+\epsilon}\); its total is
\(\ll H_JU^{109/60+\epsilon}\). The ratio sector uses the U branch of
(G156.1) and costs \(\ll H_JU^{9/5+\epsilon}\), with every Q2 and all
holes included. Polynomial conductor ranges cost only logarithmic boxes.

| Paid part | Exponent | Minimum gap below T | Spare after .001+.002+.005 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete diagonal | 1 | 55853/67500 | 55313/67500 |
| Total conductor Q≤U^(9/5) | 109/60 | 182/16875 | 47/16875 |
| Remaining ratio Q1/Q3≤U^(8/5) | 9/5 | 1853/67500 | 1313/67500 |

Each raw gap exceeds 1/100 and pays the retained 1/200 margin. These are
upper bounds for paid sectors, using absolute values there; no sign or
positivity is asserted for the residual. Masked Poisson and relative-mass
machinery are reused from the exact PR9/[research revision] sources, rather than
counted as newly proved general theorems.

## D48: accept signed block transport and fixed-source pole preservation

The adjacent physical Gaussian vectors v_s(u)=g_tau(s-u), u in [0,log2], s=log(n/X), n in [X,2X], have separation epsilon=log(1+1/n). The exact Schur pivot expansion is

    epsilon^2 (||v'_s||^2-|<v_s,v'_s>|^2/||v_s||^2)+O(epsilon^3)
    =epsilon^2 ||v_s||^2 Var_(v_s^2)(u)/tau^2+O(epsilon^3).

The variance is uniformly positive on the compact physical interval, so the pivot is comparable to n^-2. Gaussian translate independence ensures positive definiteness. Whitening can amplify a perturbation by order n. This local computation does not provide an actual full arithmetic bad direction or a lower bound for H; it correctly warns against uniform Gram inversion.

For any fixed |a_n|<=1, let b_B(j)=sum_((j-1)B<n<=jB)a_n and retain EVERY block. Replacing its points by the upper endpoint Bj gives V_B(x). The variation of k_x(t)=g_tau(log(t/x)) on t>0 is exactly 2g_tau(0). The fundamental theorem of calculus, each distance at most B and disjoint blocks yield

    |F_a(x)-V_B(x)| <= 2B g_tau(0), uniformly for x>0.

This includes both infinite tails and all endpoint conventions. It does not use cancellation. Block masses can have size B; fewer coordinates do not imply smaller amplitudes. If B_X=floor(X^theta) is fixed throughout each dyadic shell, theta<gamma makes the complete error subordinate to X^gamma, with all signed interblock terms retained. Thus the moving-block complete bound is equivalent to the original complete bound, before any Mellin transform. Recompute B only between shells.

For actual f3 the prime powers are f3(3^k)=1 and f3(p^k)=-1 for p!=3, k>=1. In particular

    b_2(j)=f3(2j-1)+(1-2*1_(2 does not divide j))f3(j).

This includes powers of2, rather than silently assigning squarefree values. For f3(n)chi(n), all ramified zeros remain zero within the signed block masses. The transport bound applies unchanged to this literal source.

For FIXED B, e_B(n)=B ceil(n/B) and

    E_B(s)=sum_n a_n[n^-s-e_B(n)^-s]

converge normally on Re s>0: on compact sets each summand is O(|s|B n^(-Re s-1)). Thus D_B=D_a-E_B preserves every reciprocal pole. With a=f3 chi the pinned actual identity is D_a=W_chi/L(s,chi), with

    W_chi=(1-2 chi(2)2^-s)/[(1-chi(2)2^-s)^2(1-chi(3)3^-s)^2]
           times product_(p>=5)(1-2 chi(p)p^-s)/(1-chi(p)p^-s)^2.

The product converges normally and is nonzero for Re s>.5. For finite primes p>=5 numerator zeros have real part log_p2<.5; the p2 numerator zeros have real part1 when chi(2)!=0. Natural zero extension at ramified primes makes the corresponding factors1. Denominator zeros have real part0. Therefore W_chi has no zero in .5<Re s<1. At a supposed L zero there, L D_B=W_chi-L E_B cannot vanish if D_B is holomorphic. This proves the fixed-source zero return at an assumed complete block exponent gamma>.5. The moving B version must return to F_a through the variation bound FIRST; inserting B_X into E_B(s) would not define this fixed Dirichlet series.

Validity: accepted ordinary fixed-character representation transfer, with all quantifiers and signed masses. Novelty: concrete physical-block specialization and native pivot price; the underlying total-variation transport is elementary and has paid-transport ancestry. Potential: exposes within-block variation cheaply, while the entire signed block-sum mode remains unpaid. This does not justify Hecke/Eisenstein transfer, uniform growing conductor constants or an exponent gain.

# [research revision] independent review: exceptional valuation reserve



## Verdict

Accept the two new valuation inequalities as written mathematics under the source's literal arithmetic conventions, with the first-transform phase repaired:

\[
 F_{2,\mathrm{sharp}}\ge b_2,
 \qquad F_{1,\mathrm{base}}+T_{1,C}/6+S\ge c.
\]

The all-multiplicity proofs below do not depend on a finite enumeration. The forced residues remain valid after bounding a partition by one and after the full residual projector, provided every natural zero and frozen scalar is retained as stipulated.

Accept the resulting conditional parent saving of \(M/24\) **for the centered equal-product difference**, after the same first-label Cauchy step and an independently established opposite-side Gauss target. For the physical main its old \(4a\) cost remains; for the errors the old \(9a\) cost remains admissible. The appropriate physical opposite-side import is the **joint first-label estimate** (forward manuscript (2.13), Gao (LA.4)); the high branch does not supply a per-label estimate of the same strength.

Two scope repairs are needed if this result is recorded as a reusable lemma:

1. State explicitly that its input is the centered difference whose four original plain scales have lower length \(L=M/4\), with identical whole-product characters, masks and norm powers in the equal-product rectangles. Do not read the broad wording in support G as covering the uncentered stage.
2. Distinguish the retained ball and its declared full-support width from the possibly smaller canonical child width. The row count uses the actual enclosing ball \(N(h')\le Z^{m'+\delta_2}\); any nonexceptional import still uses the original canonical-width correction.

The PR9 first-transform display has a literal sign inconsistency under its stated Gauss convention. It is repaired by the old D.10 orientation, which is also the orientation independently described in Gao's `SignedReconstruction.tex`. This is an erratum to an identity, not evidence of a changed mathematical model or a reason to declare every source estimate invalid. No numerical inequality used for accepted source-relative \(c_6=.125139\) needs the incorrect inverse factor. Its exact coefficient transport must use the corrected orientation (or a complete consistent exchange of the sides).

There is **no increase of c** from this refinement in the current assembly. More specifically than a comparison of existing reserves: the binding nonexceptional low/high ledgers contain an allowed sector with both genuine common supports empty, where all valuation refinements disappear and both current scalar constraints are unchanged. Section 7 proves this obstruction and states the exact missing transfer.

## 1. Evidence and conventions

The four frozen author files match the task's hashes. The author's eight source receipts also match the local files on independent readback. Primary sources used here are:

- PR9 `paper.md`, pinned head `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`: conventions 124-141; B1.12-B1.19 at 988-1057; B3.50-B3.80 at 2287-2629.
- The preserved old manuscript, Appendix D, D.10-D.12 at 1732-1776; its exact long path is in `source-receipts.json`.
- Gao PR15 at `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`: `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex`, `SignedReconstruction.tex`, and `FixedDictionaryBridge.tex`, all in the pinned v3 source directory. The physical assembly explicitly says it is a source-level composition, not an independent verification of its imports.
- The accepted forward manuscript, (2.13)-(2.24), for the current c6 assembly and actual bottlenecks. Its filename's handoff label does not change the written source-relative status used in this review.

PR9 uses \(\psi_k(n)=\tau(n)\chi_n(k)\), with the original squared product ordered as a C column times the conjugate of a D column. It defines

\[
 \mathcal G_\chi(m,h)=N(m)^{-1/2}\sum_{x\bmod m}\chi(x)e(hx/m),
\]

and every sextic power, including zero or six, remains zero on nonunits. Reciprocity is
\(\chi_v(w)=R(v,w)\chi_w(v)\), where \(R\) is a fixed ray sign. These conventions determine the phase calculation; there is no need to infer it from a theorem name.

## 2. The first phase: an exact repair, and its impact

Write the full products as \(Ca,Db\), with complete common support in \(C,D\). Then \((a,b)=(ab,CD)=1\). At a common prime with multiplicities \(i,j\), the original row factor is \(\chi_P(k)^{i-j}\). On its active radical r the primitive character is therefore

\[
 \xi=\prod_{P\mid r}\chi_P^{i-j}.
\]

For any character extended by zero and any unit t modulo m, the substitution \(y=tx\) gives
\(\mathcal G_\chi(m,th)=\overline{\chi(t)}\mathcal G_\chi(m,h)\), including nonunit h. The CRT coordinate at r is multiplied by \((ab)^{-1}\); hence its contribution is **\(\xi(ab)\)**. The full exact identity is

\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal G_{\xi\chi_a\bar\chi_b}(rab,h)
={}&\xi(ab)\chi_a(rb)\overline{\chi_b(ra)}\,
\mathcal G_\xi(r,h)\mathcal G(a,h)
\overline{\mathcal G(b,-h)}.
\end{split}
\]

The substitution \(k=ek'\) supplies the frozen common scalar \(\mu(e)\xi(e)\tau(C)\overline{\tau(D)}\) and the separate e factors. Reciprocity then yields

\[
 \tau_C(a)=\tau(a)\chi_a(er)\xi(a),\qquad
 \tau_D(b)=\tau(b)\chi_b(er)\overline{\xi(b)}.
\]

These are exactly old D.10's two displayed twists. They give first-prime exponents \(1+i-j\) and \(1-i+j\), respectively, modulo six, together with fixed ray factors.

PR9 lines 2314 and 2323 instead put an inverse xi factor on the C coefficient and in the CRT product while retaining \(\mathcal G_\xi\). With the above declared row and Gauss character this is not the same identity. Replacing h by -h changes a fixed unit factor and does not invert \(\xi(ab)\). Defining xi to mean the inverse common character would also require replacing the Gauss label by the inverse character. Exchanging C and D is possible only if the entire ordered transform, common character and conjugations are exchanged consistently. A scalar frozen independently of a,b cannot absorb this discrepancy.

This is best classified as a **repairable written phase inconsistency**, rather than a demonstrated intentional model change. Gao's `SignedReconstruction.tex` explicitly derives left residue \(1+t\), right residue \(1-t\), and says that assigning the conjugate coefficient to the C side requires a consistent exchange of side names. It therefore provides independent primary-source corroboration of the repair.

The effect on c6 is limited and precise. PR9's old exceptional count uses only newly forced second-support residues and disjointness from old support; its first F1 inequality uses \(\widetilde q\ge R\), not the sign of xi. The first target and balance use only c,d,p,R,E. Gao's high estimate permits either signed residue and uses the bound \(L_c\le5(R-R_0)\); its finite dictionary treats the two first-side orientations separately. Low-bin deletion also uses the actual natural family and width, not a preferred residue sign. Therefore the repaired coefficient is within the exact classes used in the accepted source-relative assembly, with unchanged costs. The correction does matter for the **new** T1 gain, which cannot be derived by keeping the incorrect inverse C phase with the original c,d labeling.

No assertion about the implementation or validity of any proof-assistant artifact is made here. The finite CRT derivation is sufficient for this written repair.

## 3. Transforms, supports, projectors and normalization

The first transform's prefactor is
\(H/[X N(e)\sqrt{N(r)}]\). It follows from the Poisson factor \(H/[N(e)N(r)N(a)N(b)]\), three Gauss roots and the original squared central factor \(X^{-1}\). The inverse column roots and the central normalizers of the two Gauss norms cancel in the Cauchy conversion. With the source first targets

\[
 \mathcal N_C\ll Z^{A-c+\widetilde q+B_c-s_0+\epsilon},
 \quad \widetilde q=q+R+E,
 \quad B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6,
\]

the outside exponent plus both targets and the first-label cost is exactly

\[
 M-S/2,\qquad
 S=c+d-2p-R-B_c-B_d\ge0.
\]

The inequality S>=0 is PR9 B3.56's primewise balance. It is a genuine available saving; the new proof spends it once at the final Cauchy return.

For the second transform, put \(a_0=A-c-w\). Direct expansion of B1.14-B1.15 gives the prefactor \(Z^{K+g-\ell-a_0}\), the inverse roots \(1/\sqrt{N(u)N(v)}\), and the literal correlation \(F(u,v;j)\). B1.19 then gives

\[
 F(D_2a,E_2b;j)=F(D_2,E_2;j)
 R(a,E_2)R(b,D_2)R(a,b)\chi_a(j)\overline{\chi_b(-j)}.
\]

Thus the two second children of a *fixed first side* have whole character \(\tau_1(n)\chi_n(j)\), up to fixed ray/unit twists. Their good-prime residues agree. A whole-character conjugation must also conjugate its fixed factor and reflect its height; no inversion of j on just one child is available.

The literal ledger is

\[
 -a_0+(K+g-a_0)-\ell+(p_2-s_0)+(g_2-t_2)+(a_0-b_2).
\]

Subtracting it from
\(\Lambda_c=a_0+\widetilde q+w_o+w+B_c-s_0\)
gives

\[
 M'+\Delta,\quad

 \Delta=b_2-p_2+w+B_c+\ell,
\]

where \(J=d-c+(K_0-K)-2w+w_o\). This independently checks the density and normalizers: neither \(-\ell\) nor either central factor can be omitted.

All disjointness needed by the new count is present **before** any positivity enlargement. Old moving-support primes and all first common primes puncture all surviving factors. An allocation meeting an old zero has zero frozen scalar and is discarded as zero. Hence genuine second common primes are disjoint from old and first supports. The auxiliary amplifier prime is chosen outside frozen supports, and its extraction punctures the residual factors. It cannot later be a genuine second common prime. Fixed dictionary conductor primes belong to the fixed excluded set S, so none is a new good common prime.

Both coprimality projectors must be the complete sums. At the first one, s divides both subsequent full columns and hence their genuine second common support; this justifies p2-s0. At the second one, an individual artificial t term does **not** make its primes genuine second common primes or frequency divisors. Extracting a selected plain divisor leaves an unrestricted quotient. The author retains these distinctions. Such an extraction changes a frozen scalar, not the whole row character whose forced residues are counted. A zero scalar remains zero. Bounding the genuine partition by one admits more rows, but every admitted exceptional row still obeys the same row-character congruences.

The retained row ball is \(N(h')\le Z^{m'+\delta_2}\), where
\(m'=2a_0-K-g-g_2-V\), \(0\le\delta_2<\xi\). A negative supported upper length is empty. The notation \(M'+\delta_2\) is a valid declared full-support enclosure; it must not erase the c6 correction that the actual canonical width can be smaller after cancellation. This refinement counts rows directly and does not need to identify those two widths. Nonexceptional imports still retain forward (2.16)/Gao (LA.9).

The first zero frequency, the added zero Gauss row, and the genuine second diagonal are separate. No new gain has been proved for any of them.

## 4. Forced rows and the all-multiplicity second inequality

At each good prime, a fixed-inducing row has sextic exponent zero modulo six, since its primitive inducing character is unramified there. Fix all outer labels. On the C side the first common prime contributes

\[
 \alpha_C=
 \begin{cases}
 1+i-j\pmod6,&6\nmid i-j,\\
 1,&P\mid e,\\
 0,&\text{otherwise},
 \end{cases}
 \qquad \rho_C=(-\alpha_C)\bmod6\in\{0,\ldots,5\}.
\]

Let \(T_{1,C}=\sum\rho_C\log_ZN(P)\). For the first D norm interchange i,j, including their width labels. At a second common prime the old twist is unramified, and the fixed factor \(G_cV\) has valuations i, i+1, i or j0 in the four source cases. Therefore the forced residual valuations and resulting local F2 values are:

| Genuine second common case | Required residue of vP(h') | F2sharp | b2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Equal i, 6 does not divide i, unit | (-i) mod 6 | i+ceil(i/6) | i |
| Equal i, 6 does not divide i, nonunit | (-i-1) mod 6 | i+floor(i/6) | i |
| Equal i=6k | 0 | 7k-1 | 6k |
| Unequal i>j0=6k, unit | 0 | i+k-1 | (i+j0)/2 |

The first row is actually empty on the genuine exceptional partition: unit requires vP(h')=0, whereas its displayed nonzero residue is required by exceptionality. Keeping it after a partition enlargement is nevertheless a valid upper bound. In the last row k>=1 and the difference is \((i-j_0)/2+k-1\ge1/2\). Every other row is also at least b2, with equality possible for nonunit i=1,...,5 and equal i=6. This proves \(F_{2,\mathrm{sharp}}\ge b_2\) for every multiplicity.

First and second supports are disjoint. The complete fixed row presentation also fixes residues at all other good primes. Consequently, within finitely many fixed unit/S sectors,

\[
 (h')=h_0v^6,\qquad N(h_0)\ge Z^{T_{1,C}+T_2}.

\[
 \#h'\ll Z^{(m'+\delta_2-T_{1,C}-T_2)/6+o(1)}.
\]

Other frozen supports, including amplifier support, can only impose more residues and increase the initial norm; omitting their benefit is safe. Live slot labels are not recounted by this ideal bound.

The source's f/6 allowance used only half the already-mentioned multiplicity-one residue gain. Replacing it by T2/6 and adding T1/6 is legitimate for this fixed-inducing count. It is not a count for a nonexceptional zero bin.

## 5. The first inequality and the centered return

In the unamplified nominal comparison take w=wo=ell=0, K=K0, g=(d-c)+. Then

\[
 F_{1,\mathrm{base}}=\min\{c,(c+5d)/6\}+\widetilde q/6+B_c.
\]

If c<=d, adding S and T1/6 is immediately at least c. If c>=d, Bd=0 and six times the difference from c is

\[
 c+11d-12p-5R+E+q+T_{1,C}.
\]

For one first common prime its non-q part is
\(H=i+11j-12-5r+e+\rho_C\), where r is the active-radical indicator. For j>=2, \(H\ge i+5\). For j=1, if i is 1 modulo 6, \(H=i-1+6e\ge0\); otherwise e=0 and
\(H=i-6+((-i)\bmod6)=6\lceil i/6\rceil-6\ge0\).
This proves the claimed inequality without restricting local order i>=j. Hence global c>=d does not conceal an unjustified primewise order assumption. The proof for the first D side follows by a complete exchange of i,j and c,d; S is symmetric.

The first dyad costs at most \(5\delta_1/6\), since the base F1 is increasing in K0-K with slope between 0 and 5/6. The source amplifier alternatives then give, as in the proposal,

\[
 F_{1,\mathrm{sharp}}+S\ge c+w-3\sigma-5\delta_1/6.
\]

This bound is conservative. For errors the direct perturbation is at least \(w/3+w_o-5\sigma/6\); after comparison with c+w its loss is less than 3sigma using the actual source bounds on w,wo. No density credit has been used twice.

The centered cancellation is indispensable. Write x=min(c2,d2), L=M/4 and
\(r_*=(L-c-w-x)_+\). Source B3.77-B3.79 gives paired normalized absolute volume
\(Z^{a_0-b_2-r_*+2\theta_N+o(1)}\).
It uses the identical leading lattice coefficient on the two equal-product rectangles. Independent input heights may remain in the fixed profiles; the new whole-product norm power remains common. The second-projector count and both extraction scalars are paid by

\[
 t_- -r_1-r_2-(r_*-r_1)_+
 =(t_--r_2)-\max(r_*,r_1)\le\omega_2-r_*.

As b2>=x,

\[

 \ge c+w+x+(L-c-w-x)_+-\mathrm{loss}

\]

The exact second-ledger identity is

\[
 (m'-T_1-T_2)/6+a_0-b_2-(M'+\Delta)
 =A-5M/6-F_{1,\mathrm{sharp}}-F_{2,\mathrm{sharp}}.

Thus the refined C exceptional excess is at most
\(A-13M/12+S+\mathrm{loss}\), while the original centered estimate remains
\(A-M+\mathrm{loss}\). The actual ball contributes delta2/6 and the existing support/profile errors, all retained in loss.

In a fixed common-width sector, summing the per-label exceptional estimate pays the first labels once and gives the corresponding **joint** first-side target plus this excess. Pair it with the independently available opposite-side joint target. The final exponent is at most

\[
 M-S/2+\frac{A-M+\mathrm{loss}}2
       +\frac{\min\{0,S-M/12\}}2
 \le M-M/24+\frac{A-M+\mathrm{loss}}2.
\]

This also bounds a term where both sides choose exceptional estimates: use the refinement on one side and the established full target on the other. The statement is about terms in a positive Cauchy upper bound. It does not define an orthogonal exceptional subspace of the original row norm. Nor can a target at a new proposed capacity be imported from the target currently being proved.

The uncentered extrapolation is unsupported. With both common supports empty, q=0, w=0 and no centered difference, the same source ledger gives exceptional excess \(A-5M/6\), up to the small step losses. At A=5M/6 this is zero. There is no r*=M/4 lattice subtraction. It therefore cannot yield the proposed parent expression \(M-M/24+(A-M)/2\), which at that endpoint is 7M/8. The refinement is accepted only with its centered input, which the c6 physical use actually has.

## 6. Physical main, errors and source-relative status

For Gao's actual main ball,

\[
 K_{\rm main}=K_0+(d-c)_++6a+\omega,\qquad\ell=a.
\]

Substitution gives
\(F_{1,\mathrm{sharp}}+S\ge c-4a-5\omega/6\): the radius contributes -5a and density contributes +a. Hence the conditional centered parent exponent becomes

\[
 M-M/24+(A-M+4a)/2+\mathrm{small}.
\]

The extracted errors keep the actual unamplified radius increment 3a plus padding. They retain exactly (w,wo)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda), their squared extraction coefficients, the normalized prime average, and the phase \(\chi_P(n)^{2i}\). At i=6 the phase still carries its puncture. Their first/second-support congruences above are unaffected, because the extracted amplifier prime is separate and punctures every residual column. The source's old 9a bound is conservative for the new inequality and gives

\[
 M-M/24+(A-M+9a)/2+\mathrm{small}.
\]

The ball has not been renamed to a smaller radius, and the error prime average is not recounted. The actual finite source families, masks, positive-slot pointwise gates, common Fourier measures, uniform profile bounds and partner target remain imports. The reviewer checked the displayed arithmetic and ledgers; this task does not establish the full analytic ancestry, F0/applicability, positive-slot uniformity or root-definition binding. Accepted c0 and written source-relative c6 keep their prior status.

## 7. Exact obstruction to transferring this reserve to the binding bins

Consider the nominal genuine sector

\[
 c=d=p=R=E=s_0=c_2=d_2=b_2=p_2=g_2=t_2=V=0.
\]

The first column pair and the second column pair are coprime, both full common parts are 1, and one may select the t=1 residual projector term. The source has no rule excluding this sector. Nonzero generic second rows are nonexceptional. No assertion that high zeros exist or that an analytic bound is attained is needed: this is an allowed sector that the current proof must bound, and its ledger has no valuation reserve.

For the main branch its quantities are exactly

\[
 M'=M-6a,\quad\Delta=a,\quad F=g+6a,
 \quad w=u_0h',\quad W=M-6a,
\]

before reserved padding. Thus the low bound still has reserve

\[
 L(a,g)=a-(2q_0/9)(g+6a)
       =a(1-4q_0/3)-(2q_0/9)g,
\]

and the high bound still has reserve

\[
 H(a,A)=M(1-\rho_0)-q_0A-a(5-6\rho_0).
\]

At the accepted q0=17/25, rho0=103/273 these are

\[
 L=(7/75)a-(34/225)g,\qquad
 H=(170/273)M-(17/25)A-(249/91)a.
\]

In particular L>=0 still requires a>=(34/21)g. Eliminating a still leaves

\[
 (170/273)M-(17/25)A-(249/91)(34/21)g\ge0.
\]

This is the existing low/high tradeoff from which the current affine envelope is built. The new exceptional inequality appears nowhere in it. Taking an arbitrarily strong exceptional estimate, even zero exceptional contribution, leaves this constraint unchanged.

The same obstruction is visible before exponent optimization: after Cauchy the positive upper bounds contain a nonexceptional/nonexceptional term. Reducing the exceptional terms cannot subtract a positive amount from that term. Keeping the conditional M/24 saving therefore cannot justify a stronger full norm or a reduced slot deletion price.

A concrete transfer target would be an actual saving on this allowed empty-common-support nonexceptional sector. For example, if an independently proved low-bin bound saved tau from its current deletion bill, then reducing a by 75tau/7 would preserve its low margin and improve the high margin by (249/91)(75tau/7). That is an exact useful interface. The valuation argument supplies no such tau: its congruence condition is precisely fixed induction, which the low/high sector excludes. Alternatively, a stronger high density or a changed actual amplifier radius/density relation could change the tradeoff, but neither follows from exceptional residue counting.

This is an impossibility **within the unchanged assembly and its stated bounds**, not an impossibility theorem for all future analytic arguments. It identifies where the next successful c-improvement must enter without reopening a general baseline audit.

## 8. Handoff boundary

Completed: independent finite phase derivation; all-multiplicity residue proof on both first sides; literal second correlation and normalizer check; natural-zero/projector/actual-ball review; centered conditional Cauchy return with the joint partner import; exact physical 4a/9a ledger; source-convention diagnosis and c6 dependency impact; empty-support obstruction to a nonexceptional transfer.

Remaining: root integration of the accepted written refinement and its two scope clarifications, if useful; a genuinely new bound for a binding nonexceptional sector before any larger c is claimed. Source files and the frozen author packet are unchanged.
