The independent rectangle proof uses exact tensor interpolation in a Bernstein basis rather than the author's symbolic power-to-Bernstein conversion. The interpolation is an identity because the numerator's degree is proved in Section 8. Positivity at sampled points is not the proof. Every rational cell of each partition has exact once-only coverage and all 180 reconstructed coefficients are positive. Every exact leaf minimum and maximum matches the frozen author receipt. This is meaningful arithmetic verification, not a re-verification of the entire upstream framework.

## 3. Original plain cap, source scope and fixed-family quantifiers

B3.4 and LA require the natural extended sextic row times a fixed finite ray character, fixed ray modulus and anchor, and Q_*=internalQ(Q,eta0) proper, nonzero and contained in (72). Keep the literal non-FixedInducingRow gate, every natural nonunit zero, allowed relative characters, genuine canonical prime pools and one common annular slot profile. The polynomial-size common puncture is row-independent, but may depend on frozen outer labels. No positive-width moving parent support is added. The old nontrivial initialization 51/100<=beta_*<=7/8 is unchanged.

The upper plain edge N=4223/10000=.4223 restricts the original .44 edge, and .034 restricts the original .03 lower slot edge. Neither weakens an amplification-interface hypothesis. For the pair originally entering the theorem put S=(n1+n2)/M, t=z/M. Both S<=2N and S<=1-Ct hold, hence

    A/M=S+t<=min(2N+t,1-(C-1)t).

The old lower geometry survives: A/M>=2*.41+.034=.854>.85. The new finite envelope gives A/M<=.8802<.9. Comparison still uses z/M<=.04. Its second plain may exceed N, and daughters need not retain N; both use old estimates. This proof never assumes the cap survives reflection or extraction. The invariant original A is what enters the transform ledger.

The amplifier depends only on original t and fixed constants, not on differentiated plain scales or a row-dependent S. Physical scale boxes have a strict n_max<N buffer; annular and box padding are chosen smaller than it. Thus the narrower cap introduces no scale-supremum gap. Section 7 pays every short-slot and short-plain complement, including cutoff equality.

`eventually_original_amplification`, FirstAmplificationChoice lines 712-740, requires positive fixed sigma and loss, nonnegative Mmax and b, and eta_mesh<sigma/6. It has no upper smallness hypothesis on sigma. Its threshold at line 718 precedes OriginalData at 725, live slot widths at 728, and t,T and dyadic scales at 730. The pool is literally `primePool ... (1/2) 1 (Z^(sigma/3))`; both sharp norm endpoints and the actual normalization are retained. Its cardinality is a theorem for this pool, not for an arbitrary prime subset.

AmplifiedRetainedRadius lines 220-255 add Csec>=1, xi>=0 and positive support reserve. The theorem quantifies actual positive physical scales and retained dyads, and supplies mainCommonRadius and errorCommonRadius. A negative displayed logarithmic exponent still defines a positive physical radius; use the actual smooth ball rather than declaring the frequency family empty.

SecondExceptionalFixedQSource lines 61-80 choose finite profile/height orders before Q, then a Q-dependent constant and eventual threshold before live original data. It permits every positive Kphys subject to fixed polynomial caps and explicitly charges Kphys^(5/6). Both fixed annular endpoints lo,hi and support bounds are retained. They are not chosen from live rows, and discontinuous arithmetic or cutoff indicators are not differentiated. All changed exponents remain in fixed bounded ranges, allowing one cap for the finite atlas.

Normalize to U=Z^M for parameter selection. The thirty relative sigma values are fixed in U-units. This is the source's fixed/bounded normalized geometry, not one Z-threshold for M tending to zero. In the endpoint U=Z^d, d>=1/200 and d<=h+10^-10; thus Z>=U0^200 gives U>=U0 uniformly. A smaller fixed U-loss supplies the requested Z-loss throughout this compact interval. The source does not choose its threshold after a live original width.

## 4. Amplifiers, comparison, joint Cauchy and actual radii

Set s=17/500, e=1/5000, k=309/1000, r=9/2-C=33/250 and b_j=s+je, j=0,...,30. At t=z/M=s choose j=1; otherwise choose b_(j-1)<t<=b_j. Set

    a_j/M=k b_j, sigma_j=3a_j,
    A/M<=A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)),
    g/M<=g_j=r b_j,
    g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+.

The amplifier is selected from original slot width before rows, transforms, extraction, bins and scale derivatives. Both equal-product rectangles use the same j. The ceiling loss is paid even at the left endpoint. On a cell the cap envelope increases, so use its upper endpoint; the capacity envelope decreases, so use its lower endpoint. Each bounds every point of the cell; their minimum is therefore a valid upper bound, without asserting it equals the true continuous maximum. The thirty choices have

    a_min/M=52839/5000000, a_max/M=309/25000,
    A_max=4401/5000, g_max=33/6250.

A common relative mesh below a_min/(10M) implies every eta_mesh<sigma_j/(6M), separates original prime scales from amplifier pools eventually, and may be reduced to fit all budgets. The pool stays (Z^a_j/2,Z^a_j]. Excluding row, projector, support and mask primes removes O(log Z) choices; the eventual prime count absorbs these. The representation factor (Mmax+2sigma)/(sigma/6) is bounded over this finite atlas and adds no power. Also 7a_max/M=.08652<1/4, with reserve 4087/25000.

Choose the atlas and common loss/mesh first; fix the finite original slot system and arithmetic family; take the maximum of thirty thresholds and finite smooth/height orders, including all four derivative pairs. The original data and live scales follow that threshold. In an endpoint amplitude class the selector's I, hence z and j, remain fixed during the plain scale suprema. No derivative crosses an atlas boundary and no growing reconstruction label is introduced.

For comparison take L=M/4. Both original plains exceed L. Preserve the whole-product character, two profiles, natural slots and masks in the two equal-product rectangles. For the comparison alone, exact Euler deletion costs Z^o(1); its first plain is at most M/4. Reflect the second only if its length exceeds M/2. The exact natural-character reflection/restoration gives retained second length <=M/2+xi; lower annuli have summable central weights and upper tails are rapid. Therefore the old budget is

    M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=.93M+xi,

with reserve .07M. Nonempty subunit scales are clipped by bounded dilation. Empty slot families use unrestricted nonprincipal zero-slot input. No newly chosen indicator is put inside Poisson summation of the original centered difference.

In the first transform keep the complete signed projector and all first common labels inside the Hilbert direct sum. Write c,d,p,R,E,s0 for source widths, B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6 and B_d its exchanged version. The required side bounds are

    sum_lambda N_C,lambda << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+epsilon),
    sum_lambda N_D,lambda << Z^(p+A-d+R+E+B_d+epsilon).

The outside power M-A-R/2-E and joint Cauchy give total exponent

    M+p-(c+d)/2+R/2+(B_c+B_d)/2 <= M

by the source primewise balance. Per-label branches retain -s0 and multiply once by Z^(p+s0+epsilon); the high branch proves the joint bounds directly. No independent label count follows them.

The main physical ball has logarithmic exponent

    Kmain=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega,
    K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M.

Here omega includes retained-frequency padding and positive support-doubling reserve. This covers the genuine amplified first range. Error branches keep their own exponent

    K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a+delta1+reserve.

Substituting the main radius gives nominal second width

    M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2,

and the exact identity

    (A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
      =6a+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <=6a+omega.

The second projector, signed priority allocation, extraction scalars and clipping remain intact. Its inner allowance Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a is at least a. These are original-source radius and normalization identities, not optimized declarations.

## 5. Low/high branches, missing labels and all-height scope

Low indicators are imposed only after both transforms on positive allocated child energies. RC's `commonChild_energy` and `common_clipped_energy` permit the keep predicate. Use the actual moving child character with the original fixed anchor Q_*; do not insert that child into the anchor. In each fixed parent translate mask transport preserves the literal row gate and positive-real zeros. Whole-character conjugation reflects height; conjugating only its fixed factor would change the family.

A removed canonical slot of width dz costs squared exponent (7/10+O(buffer))dz in a low bin. Greedily remove slots until old 9/2 capacity holds or the slots run out. Drop the low indicator only after this payment and use the old full eligible family. Exhaustion uses unrestricted zero-slot input even if the plain sum exceeds the width. Bounded prime lengths are estimated directly; the large-length contour premise is not applied at length one.

Actual canonical width minus M', denoted d_*, can be negative after support cancellation; only d_*<=delta2 is known. For 0<=v<=1,

    d_*+v(F-d_*)_+ <=delta2+v F_+.

Use v=7/45 and nominal defect F<=g+6a+small losses. The low reserve is a/15-7g/45. On case j its normalized lower bound is exactly b_j/15000, with minimum 57/25000000. This pays frequency/support padding, one greedy overshoot, bin buffering and aggregate finite-slot losses by choosing a smaller common budget. The slot list is fixed before the final threshold; there is no growing count hidden in that aggregate budget.

For high bins delta in [7/10,3/4], set rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]. The actual nonzero row is w=u0 e F_c G_c V h'. Active left/right residues are 1+t and 1-t modulo six, and a zero residue retains the natural puncture. Retain u0 among six fixed unit sectors. With canceled active radical width R0 and L_c=log_Z NF_c, L_c<=5(R-R0), and the actual support gives

    log_Z Nw<=W+small losses,
    W=M-R-(c-d)_++L_c-6a.

Every genuine second common prime and the first projector divides w. The missing first common radical has width <=p-R-E+R0. For fixed w and missing radical the remaining common labels, including arbitrary valuations, are divisor-many by the source Rankin product estimate. A finite valuation table alone would not prove this. The second residual projector need not divide w; its dyadic count is paid by the two extraction scalars and original priority allocation. A possibly zero extracted character value stays outside, and no new coprimality condition is imposed on quotient plains.

The fixed-dictionary density has a threshold before all heights and live norm bounds, and primitive conductor O_fixed(Nw). Polynomial Euler holes are separate from that conductor and dictionary size. Within the actual parent translate, the upper buffered zero maximum controls each surviving factor; a member of a fixed finite list realizes the lower maximum needed for density. A union over that fixed list costs a constant; a union over live arithmetic labels is not taken. Sixth-power lifting converges because rho>=2/7>1/6. Thus the joint count is

    Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+epsilon)(1+T)^J.

A slightly negative nominal W with a supported row is enlarged to its O(epsilon) supported bound. If the supported bound is negative, the range is empty. No nonempty integral row range is assigned a population bound below one.

The source pointwise factor and outside normalization yield this excess over the joint side target:

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)
    +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c+rho L_c+R0
    +g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+small losses.

Using min(c,d)>=p>=R, L_c<=5(R-R0), rho+delta>1 and 5rho>1 bounds the middle line by

    (4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c <=-79p/270-E-B_c.

The last line is <=-delta b2-t2. The remaining normalized reserve is

    H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-k b_j(5-6rho),
    A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)).

Its derivative is 50(1-6k b_j)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-A_j. The safe extrema a_max/M=309/25000 and A_max=4401/5000 give the uniform lower bound 188591/607500>0. Thus its minimum is at delta=.7, where

    H_j(.7)=35/54-(7/10)A_j-(26/9)k b_j.

The cap envelope is smaller for j=1,...,8 and the capacity envelope for j=9,...,30. The reserve decreases on the first segment by [7/10+(26/9)k]/5000 per step; it increases on the second by [(7/10)(C-1)-(26/9)k]/5000. The adjacent cases are

    j=8: A_8=4401/5000, H_8=967/4218750;
    j=9: A_9=275031/312500, H_9=40919/337500000.

The exact finite minimum is 40919/337500000 at case 9, including ceiling and cell-envelope rounding. The continuous crossing t=(1-2N)/C=37/1040 lies inside cell 8; it does not replace these finite bounds. Discarding the cap envelope at the same C,k gives high minimum -150029/67500000. The new original-source hypothesis is essential.

Bins crossing .7 stay in the buffered low branch. Its smaller reserve 57/25000000 pays the O(buffer) loss. Density is used only when its lower edge is at least .7, with no enlargement of range.

For all-height recovery, finite Euler factors and their reciprocals and fixed derivatives cost U^epsilon on a fixed positive-real strip and are nonzero there. Natural zeros remain in the coefficient identities. Profiles separate on a common ambient logarithmic box before live labels. Euler derivatives of K(B product y_i^e_i) are uniform in B>0, so larger a_j gives no hidden power in a smooth seminorm. The weighted Fourier integral is taken in the direct-sum Hilbert space of rows and labels and charges their count once. Coprimality, valuation and zero-bin indicators are never differentiated.

The density's internal detector exponents precede its finite height order. Choose a distinct small external height exponent afterward to fit (1+T)^J in the same reserve. Internal smooth orders are chosen backward through the fixed transform graph; external Fourier-tail orders follow raw polynomial bounds. Arbitrarily larger input heights use absolute polynomial U-bounds absorbed by a sufficiently large fixed polynomial in those input heights. This retains independent plain, slot and witness heights without selecting a detector anew for each row.

## 6. Extracted errors, zero frequencies, exceptions and reopening limit

For the actual auxiliary prime, lambda=log_Z Npi>=a-log_Z2, hence lambda>=3a/4 eventually for all thirty pools. Both sharp pool endpoints remain literal. The extracted alternatives are (w,w_o)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda). Their old-radius defect is <=g+3a+w-w_o+small losses and allowance is >=w. Global squared slot cost 3/4 divided by 9/2 gives rate 1/6. After the same actual-width correction, reserves are a/4-g/6, 13a/4-g/6 and 4a-g/6.

| Branch | Minimum reserve divided by M |
|---|---:|
| First extracted error | 37791/20000000 |
| Sixth-power extracted error | 671859/20000000 |
| Seventh-power extracted error | 103797/2500000 |
| Second zero, 1-A_j-5a_j/M | 322949/5000000 |
| Main fixed-inducing, 1-A_j-4a_j/M | 18913/250000 |
| Error fixed-inducing, 1-A_j-9a_j/M | 20341/1000000 |

The normalized prime average has no second prime count. Moving valuations one and seven, natural zeros and scalars remain. The first zero frequency has its original powerful-product count. The artificially added zero Gauss row is unamplified and keeps -s0. The second zero excess is A-M-min(c,d)-B_c+5a+small losses, bounded by the table.

For fixed-inducing nonzero second rows keep the exact predicate, forced residues, masks and scalars. The actual main radius gives

    F1=(c+5d+R+E)/6+B_c-4a-5omega/6, if c>=d;
    F1=c+(R+E)/6+B_c-4a-5omega/6, if c<=d.

Therefore F1>=2c/3-4a-small losses and F2>=2b2/3. The exact coefficient is -4a. With v=c+min(c2,d2), L=M/4,

    max_(v>=0) [A-5M/6-2v/3-(L-v)_+]=A-M

at v=L. This pays main excess A-M+4a and original error excess A-M+9a. In particular the source Kphys^(5/6) cost is included. Leading lattice terms cancel for equal-product rectangles with the same whole character, mask, profiles and independent-height norm powers. Their amplifier index agrees.

All terminal terms have positive reserve. Choose aggregate losses below a fixed fraction of the table, 57/25000000 and 40919/337500000. Both joint side targets follow, and joint Cauchy plus comparison proves the local theorem. All descendants use old moments, so no recursion through C occurs.

The auxiliary joint-plane statement has a limited but correct interpretation. Write S=(n1+n2)/M, t=z/M. For positive raw old defect g/M=S+(9/2)t-1, the strict low condition is a/M>(7/3)(g/M). At that boundary the high reserve at delta=.7 is

    35/54-(7/10)(S+t)-(182/27)(S+(9/2)t-1).

Multiplying by 270 gives exactly 1995-2009S-8379t. Therefore the two scalar inequalities permit an open amplifier interval precisely when

    2009S+8379t<1995.

Its interval length is [1995-2009S-8379t]/780. This is a joint geometric condition, not an unconditional constant-capacity inequality.

Put b=1-2N. On S<=2N, S+Ct<=1, with t*=b/C inside [.034,.04], the plane 2009S+8379t is maximized at S=2N,t=t*. Before crossing its cap bound increases in t; afterward its slope is 8379-2009C<0. The lower bound S>=.82 leaves this witness admissible; every S in the permitted interval is realizable by n1=n2=SM/2. An independent exact check of all five polygon vertices confirms this maximum.

Ccrit=8379b/(2009b-14)=930069/212999, the denominator being positive. At equality tcrit=212999/5985000, rcrit=56853/425998 and acrit/M=6317/570000. The witness n1=n2=NM and t=tcrit is in the useful window, with positive raw defect. Both displayed reserves vanish. Raising a worsens high and lowering it worsens low. This obstructs simultaneous fixed strictly positive reserves at that point, not an epsilon-loss theorem, an epsilon-dependent construction or another analytic mechanism.

One explanatory qualification to the author's discussion: nonpositive raw defect means its positive part g is zero, but a positive outer amplifier still creates the 6a nominal defect. Its low deletion price is 14a/15 and net low reserve a/15, rather than a literally absent deletion cost. At a=0 the unamplified high reserve is positive throughout this region; choosing sufficiently small positive a gives both strict reserves. The auxiliary boundary observation survives. The explicit thirty-case proof already uses the correct g+6a formula, so this clarification changes no candidate, atlas or endpoint.

For C=546/125, C-Ccrit=38829/26624875 and the continuous plane margin at its crossing is 12943/130000. The actual k=.309, finite rounding and every terminal term are paid separately above. The largest terminal price 9a has same-cell reserve 20341/1000000 at case 9; even 1-A_max-9a_max/M=107/12500>0. Main exceptional and second-zero minima likewise occur at case 9; the three error and low minima occur at case 1. The same-cell reserve decreases up to case 8 and increases after case 9 because C-1-mk>0 for m=4,5,9.

The short-slot fallback with ceiling N permits a lower cutoff below (1-2N)/(9/2)=259/7500. The chosen .034 leaves 3/1250. This restricts this particular fallback envelope, not every geometry.

## 7. Physical endpoint, sharp shortening cutoffs and free shifts

Set

    theta=174973/200000, ell=11/3-4theta=25081/150000,
    h=3969737987/5000000000,
    x=1+ell-h=5598886039/15000000000,
    y=h-2ell=6893013961/15000000000,
    kappa_*=2theta-1=74973/100000.

Exactly x+y=1-ell, 0<ell<x<y<2x, y<1/2<h<2y, 1/6<ell<1/5, h>4ell, C<6kappa_* and theta>.87. Probe constraints are

    y-2x+ell=-598886039/5000000000<0,
    1+3ell-2(x+y)=-4919/30000<0.

For k_probe=5/6-x/3-ell/6, (5x+y)/12=theta-k_probe.

       -(3d/4)[(1-delta)J+delta P V/2].

The independent helper reconstructs every coefficient and matches every author leaf minimum/maximum. Exact rational cell coverage checks each interior cell once; boundaries follow by closure. Results:

## 9. Remaining fields and complete zero-exclusion return

Small nonprincipal rows below Z^d0, including fixed-conductor and finite-unit rows, keep the original global-line estimate with reserve

    -13h/75+y/2-63d0/50=21462387121/250000000000>1/20.

    y/20-(1+h)/1000-1/4000=313991484089/15000000000000>0,

With fixed zeta0=10^-10, choose a sufficiently large fixed positive line parameter v before the final threshold for the desired negative power. Constants may be large, but there is no new asymptotic loss or central-density assumption.

Off-height fields retain the three independent contour frequencies, complete original w-inversion, joining segments and separately extracted principal poles. The Gaussian controls its frequency; the other Mellin transforms have arbitrarily high fixed polynomial decay. Assign fixed fractions of each buffered height window. On joining segments reciprocals remain inside the zero-free buffer or on the global line. Raw unseparated numerator and conductor-height bounds have fixed polynomial Z-degree before external integration-by-parts order is chosen; then a sufficiently large fixed order pays Z^B T^-N. statement:
## T02. Direct completed selector and finite mean — PROVED CONDITIONAL REDUCTION

**Provenance:** BB R01, especially (R01.1)–(R01.4); inherited FD (1), (65)–(73). This valid reduction avoids even T01 for the specific common-completion transfer.

For the natural beta family set
\[
S_h(s)=F(s)D_h(s),\qquad x_a(s)=\xi(a)q_a^{1-3s}.
\]
Let `S_h^{(g)}` force squarefree `g` into the **whole completed column**, not only the squarefree core. Exact cube-selector algebra gives
\[
S_h^{(g)}(s)=
\sum_{d\mid g}x_{g/d}(s)\prod_{p\mid d}(1-x_p(s))
\beta(d)\vartheta_d(h)q_d^{-s}S_{dh}(s).
\tag{T02.1}
\]
**Proof.** At each prime dividing `g`, split its occurrence into two disjoint possibilities: it occurs in the cube label, contributing `x_p`; or it occurs in the squarefree core and does not occur in the cube label, contributing `1-x_p` times the core selector. Multiply these local alternatives and use (T0). A prime is allowed in both core and cube in the first alternative. The outside character vanishes if `(d,h)>1`. The identity holds initially in absolute convergence and then by independent continuation. ∎

Assume for every fixed required component and every `e,delta>0`,
\[
\sum_{0<q_h\le X}|S_h(1/2+e+it)|^2
\ll X^{1+\eta+\delta}T^A,\qquad 0\le\eta<1/4.
\tag{T02.2}
\]
The following estimate is then proved, but the hypothesis itself remains open:
\[
\sum_{q_g\le G}\sum_{q_h\le K}|S_h^{(g)}(s)|^2
\ll(KG)^\delta K^{1+\eta}\max\{1,G^{\eta-2e}\}T^A.
\tag{T02.3}
\]
To see this, first reindex the core part by `k=dh`. The condition `(d,h)=1` means `d|rad_{=1}(k)`. On `q_k` about `KE`, `1<=E<=G`, its divisor weight is at most `q_k^delta E^{-1-2e}`. The mean hypothesis gives `K^{1+eta}E^{eta-2e}` up to losses. The part `q_k<=K` and the dyadic sum give the claimed maximum, with endpoint logarithms absorbed. Divisor Cauchy in (T02.1) costs a subpower; so does the product of `1-x_p`. Write `a=g/d`; the remaining squared coefficient is `|x_a|^2=q_a^{-1-6e}`. Its ideal sum converges. Use cutoff `G/q_a` in the core estimate before majorizing by `G`. This proves (T02.3).

Mellin inversion of the original whole-column profile against `S_h^{(g)}` costs `D^{1+2e}` after squaring. Rapid Mellin decay absorbs polynomial height, and choosing `e` and preliminary losses sufficiently small pays the desired final loss. FD's independent large-divisor polynomial estimate and its common-profile argument therefore give
\[
|\mathfrak Q(D,K)|\ll(DK)^\rho\left[
DK^{1+\eta}G^\eta+DK+
D^2K^{1/3}/G+D^{5/3}K^{2/3}/G^{2/3}\right].
\tag{T02.4}
\]
No global reciprocal of `F` was used.

**Completion convention:** for the natural beta family `F` is common. A fixed multiplicative core twist adds its fixed factor at `d`. Individual sixth-order ray components can switch `nu` and have different natural completions. One can formally multiply an independently holomorphic vector by a single fixed common `F`, but matching those formal products to actual current periods is a separate obligation. Do not transport a mean for mismatched completed components through (T02.1) without explicitly restoring factors or fixing a common convention.

## G141. Every tail and cross term, including an actual arithmetic floor

For arbitrary |a_n|<=1, set N=X^b and write the complete energy kernel

    E(X)=sum_(n,m>=1) a_n conjugate(a_m) K_X(n,m),
    K_X(n,m)=integral_1^2 exp(-(n+m)/(N u^b))
                  exp(-i(n^k-m^k)/(X^k u^k))du/u.

Conjugate symmetry retains both ordered cross terms. With v=u^(-k),
the positive amplitude is exp(-A v^(b/k))/(kv), A=(n+m)/N. It decreases
on[2^-k,1]; endpoints plus total variation are at most2^(k+1)/k.
Integration by parts, with the damping differentiated, proves

    |K_X(n,m)| <<_(b,k) min(1,X^k/|n^k-m^k|), n!=m.

For n>m, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). All pairs outside the core n,m<=M
have max(n,m)>M, so both orientations sum absolutely to
O(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)), for every shell-fixed real M>=2. Hence exactly

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+D_>M(X)+O_(b,k)(X^k M^(2-k)log(2M)),
    D_>M=sum_(n>M)|a_n|^2 K_X(n,n)>=0,  D_>M<<_b X^b.

This includes the full core/tail strip, distant tail, real-cutoff
endpoints and both ordered crosses. Damping and the summable majorant
justify limits from finite squares. The same formula without E_<=M
holds for the tail's own energy. Only after this identity can positivity
of the remaining core or diagonal be used in a lower or reverse bound.

For the actual coefficients, elementary squared-divisor counting gives

    sum_(n<=y)|a_n|^2=d_q y+O_q(sqrt y),
    d_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

It counts the nonunit exclusions exactly and applies to every fixed
principal, nonprincipal or imprimitive character. With
C_(q,b)=d_q(2^b-1)/(2b), partial summation yields D_all=C_(q,b)X^b+O_q(X^(b/2)).
For b=3/2,k=6,M=X^(19/16), the complete identity becomes

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+C_(q,3/2)X^(3/2)+O_q(X^(5/4)log X).

Thus E(X)>=(C_(q,3/2)+o(1))X^(3/2). An every-epsilon L2 exponent
2gamma<3/2 is impossible for THIS source. The gamma=3/4 boundary,
weaker L1 bounds and different b remain eligible.

The review improves the actual tail by keeping its cutoff correction:

    Q_(q,b)(X,M)=(d_q X^b/2) integral_1^2
                         u^(b-1)exp(-2M/(X^b u^b))du,
    D_>M=Q_(q,b)(X,M)+O_(q,b)(X^(b/2)).

Stieltjes integration on(M,infinity) includes the boundary error
sqrt(M)exp(-lambda M) and the integral of lambda sqrt(t)exp(-lambda t),
both O(lambda^-1/2), uniformly in M. Therefore at M=X^(4/3), b=3/2,k=6,

    E(X)=E_<=M(X)+Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)),
    E_>M(X)=Q_(q,3/2)(X,M)+O_q(X^(3/4)).

The cross exponent2/3 has room to absorb its logarithm. Replacing Q
prematurely by C X^(3/2) would lose a correction of order X^(4/3).

There is also a log-free UPPER norm bound on the original sharp shell.
Let h(t)=0 for t<=0, h(t)=10t^3-15t^4+6t^5 for0<t<1 and h(t)=1 for
t>=1. Then phi(u)=h(2u-1)h((4-u)/2) is nonnegative C^2, supported
on[1/2,4] and equal1 on[1,2]. Majorize the COMPLETE squared tail by
its phi-weighted integral. Its transformed amplitude and first derivative
vanish at endpoints, and its L1/second-derivative L1 norms are uniform
in A>=0, since A-polynomials are multiplied by exp(-cA). Two integrations
by parts give |K_phi(n,m)|<< (1+|n^k-m^k|/X^k)^-2. With
delta_n=X^k/n^(k-1), sum_(h>=1)min(1,(delta_n/h)^2)<<delta_n.
Thus, with all coefficients and the original sharp shell still present,

    ||W_>M||_2^2 <<_(b,k) X^b+X^k M^(2-k).

This proves E(X)<<X^2+X^b generically by taking M=X. It removes the
logarithm from an upper norm, not from the earlier sharp signed identity.
The bounded array a_n=1 for n<=floor(X/2), zero otherwise, gives E>>X^2
at b=3/2,k=6. This shell-dependent array is a generic obstruction,
not a lower bound for actual Möbius coefficients.

## 6. Precise OPEN estimate and every-height zero return

The remaining sufficient input is the full signed L1 estimate for (R13): one common gamma<gamma11 chosen before chi and any candidate zero, such that for each fixed ordinary character chi and each of a fixed covering pair of unramified primes, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    int_X^(2X)|T_small,p,chi,tau_X(x)| dx/x
        <<_(p,chi,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).      (OPEN-LCG)

The choices tau_X may depend on epsilon, chi,p,X, but must satisfy (R11) and be fixed before live x. Constants and scale thresholds may depend on these fixed data. The pair of primes is chosen before the height and shell. A full L2 bound at the same exponent is stronger and sufficient. A fixed positive epsilon loss, selected block, sampled x, finite height band or character average is insufficient.

By (R14), this all-shell hypothesis is equivalent to the full L1 bound for the fixed source C. This norm equivalence is not arithmetic progress by itself and is not asserted to be an equivalence to zero exclusion.

The complete return can be reconstructed directly. Put

    H_p(z)=int_0^infinity C_p,chi(1/t)t^(z-1)dt.

Shell summation with epsilon smaller than Re z-gamma gives holomorphy on Re z>gamma, also after any fixed number of derivatives on every finite height compact set. Polynomial coefficient bounds and exp(-n/x^(3/2)) pay the other endpoint x near zero. Absolute Fubini initially requires Re z>3/2, with a sufficiently small divisor-exponent buffer.

For each coefficient integral, set v=nt and rotate clockwise through fixed 0<theta<min(pi/3,pi/12). On the sector, Re(v^(3/2))>0 and the oscillatory factor is nonincreasing in modulus; damping kills the large arc for each n and Re z>0 kills the small arc. On the ray exp(-iv^6) has exponential decay. The one-term Taylor remainder in exp(-n^(-1/2)v^(3/2)) is thus bounded by a compactly integrable constant times n^-1/2. It follows that

    I_n(z)=A0(z)n^-z+O_K(n^(-Re z-1/2)),
    A0(z)=Gamma(z/6)exp(-i pi z/12)/6.

Derivatives have only the corresponding logarithmic factors. Summing with |c(n)|<<_delta n^delta gives a normally holomorphic E_p on Re z>1/2. Hence

    H_p(z)=A0(z)P_p(z)J_p(z)L(2z,chi^2)^2/L(z,chi)+E_p(z). (R15)

The Mellin identity uses the original complete C, not the shell-dependent restricted core. That is why the paid transfer (R14) is indispensable.

A0 is finite and nonzero for Re z>0. J_p has zeros only on Re z=1/2. The Euler product makes L(2z,chi^2) finite and nonzero for Re z>1/2; its possible pole at 1/2 is outside the domain. P_p zeros lie on Re z=1. Two distinct fixed unramified primes have no common P zero at nonzero height, since such a zero would make log p1/log p2 rational using finite-order character values. For nonprincipal chi, choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1 to cover height zero; such a prime exists by factoring an integer with nontrivial character value. For principal chi the pole at one is the specified exception. Thus (R15) excludes each finite-height zero with Re z>gamma. No maximum zero height, rightmost attained zero or height-uniform constant is assumed. Natural imprimitive Euler factors remain present; no growing-conductor conclusion follows.

For general fixed b>1 and integer k, retain every term j<K:

    H_p(z)=sum_(j<K) A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j)+E_(p,K)(z),
    A_j(z)=(-1)^j Gamma((z+bj)/k)
                   exp(-i pi(z+bj)/(2k))/(k j!).

Choose fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. The remainder is normally holomorphic on Re z>max(0,1-(b-1)K). Start above one, where the Euler reciprocal is holomorphic, and descend by finitely many strips of width b-1. Every positive shift is already holomorphic before solving for the unshifted reciprocal, with the same two-prime cover. The factors L(2w,chi^2), J_p(w) and the principal pole retain exactly the preceding scope for w in this domain. No finite shift is omitted.

The inherited full architecture for each fixed gamma>1/2 chooses fixed 1<b<=2gamma and sufficiently large k with b>=2k/(2k-1), r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b and the old short corridor alpha<=(4gamma-b)/3. Then (R2) pays its new gcd complement because gamma>=b-1. For example gamma=3/5,b=11/10,k=12,K=5,r=27/25 is compatible. All of this is conditional on its complete signed core norm. There is no boundary gamma=1/2 or uniform limiting-parameter theorem.

statement:
### Exact periodic kernel and paid tails

Let

    H_chi(t)=sum_(n>=1)chi(n)e^(-nt)
            =[sum_(v=1)^q chi(v)e^(-vt)]/[1-e^(-qt)],
    f_(chi,r)(t)=(-d/dt)^r H_chi(t),
    g_(chi,r)(t)=f_(chi,r)(t)-m_q r! t^(-r-1).          (B4)

All these formulas hold for t>0, also for q=1. Convolution and the absolutely convergent reciprocal at r+1 yield the COMPLETE identity

    E_(chi,r)(X)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d)chi(d)g_(chi,r)(d/X).   (B5)

No cutoff was exchanged with a conditionally convergent series. Before subtracting the pole term, double sums converge absolutely for each X; after subtraction, the reciprocal sum is absolutely convergent since r+1>1.

The rational formula for H has only its possible simple pole m_q/t at zero. Its regular derivative in (B4) is analytic there. Reflection of residues v<->q-v gives H(-t)=-chi(-1)H(t), apart from the constant exception H_1(-t)=-1-H_1(t). The r>=2 derivative removes that exception. Since r has the parity of chi, f_r and its pole term are odd. Therefore

    g(t)=O_(chi,r)(t), g'(t)=O_(chi,r)(1)  as t down to 0.

At infinity, f_r and its derivative are O_(chi,r)(e^(-t)). Thus principal g(t)=-m_q r!t^(-r-1)+O(e^(-t)), with the differentiated tail retained; nonprincipal g decays exponentially. In particular

    |g(t)| <= C_(chi,r) min(t,t^(-r-1)),               (B6)
    |E(X)| <= C'_(chi,r) X  for X>=1.                 (B7)

The bound (B7) is unconditional but has exponent 1. For any target 0<gamma<1 and real cuts D=X^alpha, Y=X^beta, alpha<1<beta, (B5)-(B6) pay

    sum_(d<=D)|mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)| = O(X^(2alpha-1)),
    sum_(d>Y)|mu(d)chi(d)g(d/X)| = O(X^(r+1-r beta)).  (B8)

Endpoints are d<=D and d>Y. All real X are covered. Thus alpha=(1+gamma)/2 and beta=1+(1-gamma)/r pay both pieces at exponent gamma. The middle source D<d<=Y remains a full signed arithmetic obligation. For a nonprincipal chi, the upper cutoff can instead be C X log X and its full tail made any prescribed negative power by choosing fixed C large enough. Constants may depend on the fixed character.

## C. The wildcard boundary filter improves localization, not the exponent

Fix b>1 and integer m>=0, independently of X. Let T_b g(t)=g(bt) and

    K_m(t)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-b^(-(2j+1))T_b)g(t),
    E_m(X)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(I-b^(-(2j+1))D_b)E(X),
    D_b E(X)=E(X/b).                                  (C1)

The empty product is identity. The finite expansion, including every dilated main term, gives E_m(X)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n)K_m(n/X). Oddness and analyticity show K_m(t)=O(t^(2m+1)) at zero; each successive factor kills the indicated odd Taylor coefficient. At infinity the principal algebraic term is multiplied by the nonzero constant product_j(1-b^(-(r+2j+2))); nonprincipal tails remain exponential.

Hence, for D=X^alpha and Y=X^beta, the COMPLETE outer prices are

    O(X^((2m+2)alpha-(2m+1))) + O(X^(r+1-r beta)).     (C2)

Choose alpha=1-(1-gamma)/(2m+2), beta=1+(1-gamma)/r. For m=1, r=2 and gamma=.8748 the paid cuts become .9687 and 1.0626; for 5/6 they are 23/24 and 13/12; for 3/4 they are 15/16 and 9/8. This is actual endpoint cancellation with all complementary terms priced. It is a fixed finite filter; growing m or r needs new uniform estimates.

Its Mellin factor is

    F_m(s)=product_(j=0)^(m-1)(1-b^(-(s+2j+1))).       (C3)

All zeros have negative real part. Thus a complete every-epsilon bound for E_m at gamma>0 has the same direct zero-exclusion return as (B10), by repeating the split Mellin argument and retaining the modified main term. No inverse norm or missing dilation branch is silently dropped.

Nevertheless the same squarefree-density calculation gives

    sum_n |mu(n)chi(n)K_m(n/X)|
       =kappa_q X integral|K_m(t)|dt+O_(chi,r,m,b)(sqrt X), (C4)

with a strictly positive leading constant. Principal nonvanishing follows from the explicit far-tail multiplier. Nonprincipal nonvanishing follows also from (C3) times the nonzero Mellin transform, or from the slowest e^(-t) term in the finite sum. This is the decisive actual-source test for the proposed bootstrap: removing arbitrarily many FIXED endpoint Taylor terms does not lower its complete absolute exponent.

For clarity, an input bound |M_chi(t)|<=C t^beta, 0<beta<=1, only yields

    |E_m(X)| <= C X^beta integral_0^infinity t^beta |K_m'(t)|dt, (C5)

by full Abel summation. It preserves beta. A synthetic sharpness test is a(n)=n^beta-(n-1)^beta, 0<beta<1, whose summatory function is floor(x)^beta and whose coefficients are bounded by 1. For the principal kernel of modulus 1, a Riemann sum yields

    sum_n a(n)K_m(n/X)
      ~ beta Gamma(beta) zeta(beta-r)F_m(beta) X^beta.  (C6)

The coefficient is nonzero: beta-r lies between consecutive trivial zeros and F_m(beta)>0. Mellin integration of the pole-subtracted kernel gives Gamma(s)zeta(s-r) for -1<Re(s)<r+1; the same split/continuation argument as above proves it. This toy is not multiplicative Mobius and does not refute actual signed cancellation. It identifies exactly why the finite filter alone cannot be an exponent-improving operator.

Let V=1 on[0,1], V=0 on[2,infinity), as in the source, and

With Y=U^B the completed tail and its prefix/far split are

    P_R,u(s)=sum_(Nn>R)phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                                     e^(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L),
    F_R,u(s)=D_R,u(s)-P_R,u(s).                         (F6)

H is the same smooth function equal to one on[0,1], between zero and one, and zero beyond a fixed C. In particular the far coefficient is exactly multiplied by1-H(Nn/L). No sharp pair mask is substituted for it. Terminate genuinely at Nn<=U^(B+1), paying its exponentially small error before any pair expansion. This preserves every required derivative. The complete zero identity gives

                       [V(Nd/R0)-V(Nd/R1)].            (F8)

## 4. Exponent return and precise arithmetic gap

For fixed 0<theta<1 take H=floor(X^theta). For every fixed r, 2rH<=X eventually. The last term in (R1) is smaller than every negative power of X, since its logarithm has leading term

    -(1-theta)^2 (log X)^2/(2*tau).

The middle term is O(X^(1-r(1-theta))). Consequently the full hypothesis

    for every epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X:
    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) <<_epsilon X^(e+epsilon)             (OPEN-W)

gives the complete pointwise and dyadic L2 exponent

    gamma_r=max((1-theta+e)/2, 1-r(1-theta)).                 (R3)

The order r may be chosen after fixed theta and a fixed target exponent, then kept fixed as X tends to infinity. There is no theta=1 theorem or silent growing-order substitution. Endpoint equality has the usual every-epsilon interpretation. This is a sufficient return, not an asserted energy equivalence: oscillatory window-null directions can carry other information.

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character including its natural zeros,

    integral_0^infinity F_a(x) x^(-s) dx/x
        = exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi),       Re(s)>1.

The small-x tail is superpolynomial. The complete all-scale bound from (R3), or its dyadic L2 version followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, makes this Mellin transform holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma_r. Multiplying by L and analytic continuation excludes every zero there: the numerator is nonzero at every finite height and multiplicity. The principal pole of L produces a reciprocal zero, not a forbidden pole. No estimate for vertical reciprocal growth, Phragmen--Lindelof assumption, primitive replacement or conductor uniformity is needed for this forward implication.

The family statement needs a COMMON exponent for each fixed chi, with constants allowed to depend on chi. Neither Eisenstein/Hecke families nor a growing conductor nor a replacement f3 source has been proved by this argument.

To improve c6, both strict inequalities are necessary in this interface:

    e < 2*theta6-1+theta = .749722+theta,
    1-r(1-theta) < theta6=.874861.                           (R4)

The absolute energy bound is O(XH)=O(X^(1+theta)); its required arithmetic saving remains

    (1+theta)-(.749722+theta)=.250278=2*c6.

Only the old first-order approximation ceiling theta<theta6 is removed. For example theta=.9 and r=2 pay remainder exponent .8, but still require the unproved energy exponent e<1.649722. \[
 c_{\chi_{u,\lambda}}(I)
 =c_{\eta_\lambda}(I)\mathfrak s_{m_0^6u}(I),
 \qquad N\mathfrak q_{u,\lambda}\le K_\lambda N(u).
\]

The literal sextic character includes all ramified/nonunit zeros. The
modulus bound belongs to the natural representative, not the unrelated
existential `RowData.character`; coefficient equality transfers moments
between them. Whole-character conjugation reflects the height and keeps
the modulus; conjugating only `eta` is a different operation. Fixed
orientations may be handled label by label. The finite dictionary and
parent translate are fixed before the scale; unrelated translates are
never put into a single eligibility bin.

Set `K=max(1,max K_lambda)`, `U=KY`. This is fixed multiplicative padding,
not a power loss. Remove the union of fixed-inducing free rows for all
dictionary labels. Their primes lie in a fixed finite support and their
valuations are at most five, with finitely many units; the union is
finite. Every remaining natural character is nonprincipal. The removed
rows contribute `O(1)` to free-row density, without needing witnesses.

Use only the old no-slot inverse moment and PR15's established zero-slot
plain moment (P). The latter requires `m<=3/4`, not a restriction on the
zero bin. Its contradiction hypothesis `beta>=51/100` is automatic when
the current high-zero population is nonempty; if `beta<a`, that population
is empty. The plain source is obtained at the fixed modulus
`Q=q_eta(72)`, with its exact inclusion gates, a fixed small conductor
padding and width `max(1,2m)+padding<=2`. Its zero auxiliary slot has
identically zero profile and the selected product is empty; this does not
impose prime supply on the unmarked family. The omitted finite rows are
bounded absolutely by `|P_n|<=288A sqrt(D)`, uniformly in frequency.

Fix positive detector and moment errors `epsilon_det,epsilon_m`, with
`epsilon_det<=1/1000`. On a supported fiber
`m<=1/2+75 epsilon_det<=23/40<3/4` and `0<=r<=2`.
The inverse and plain inputs have a common fixed polynomial height degree
`J0`, uniform in the zero bin, dyadic choices, scale and actual witness
frequencies. One now chooses the detector auxiliaries and a small positive
`tau_det` AFTER this degree. It can satisfy the witness budget and make
`(J0+1)tau_det` arbitrarily small. There is no dependence of `J0` on the
later chosen witness frequency interval.

For `T<=U^tau_det`, use the actual buffered-bin theorem with
`I=ceil(49/(100e))`. Every nonempty part has

\[
  b>a-e>51/100,\qquad b\le7/8,
  \qquad \delta_b=2b-1\in(0,3/4].
\]

The last upper bound is the incumbent seven-eighths bound, applied to
the actual fixed dictionary. The mesh can put `delta_b` slightly below
`.65`; this is harmless because the actual count and witness gates are
strictly weaker. Set

\[
 t_*=\frac5{5-2\delta_b}
\]

for this bin before selecting witnesses. The cutoff is in `[1,3/2]`
throughout `0<=delta_b<=5/6`. At the proposed density endpoints it is
`50/37` and `10/7`. The source theorem is used at `Z=U,d_min=d_max=d=1`
with frequency allowance `U^(tau_det/2)` and
`H_i=2 pi U^(tau_det/2)+3iU^tau_det`.

Partition by the witness's independent character label and its two dyadic
indices. The cardinality of the latter is `O(log U)` each. Do not require
the witness label to equal a physical numerator/denominator label; the
finite union covers whichever label has the detecting zero.

Here is an independent derivation of the balanced exponent, including the
long inverse branch. With tolerance `gamma` and common moment loss `v`,
the two moment estimates give

\[
 |R|\ll U^{\max(1,(1+5r)/6)-\delta r+v},
 \qquad |R|\ll U^{1-2\delta m+v},
 \quad m\ge t_*-r-\gamma.
\]

For `r<=1`, the unperturbed bounds `1-delta r` and
`1-2delta(t_*-r)` cross at `r=2t_*/3`. The actual second bound adds
at most `2delta gamma`. Choose the inverse bound above the unperturbed
crossing and the plain bound below it, obtaining
`1-(2/3)delta t_*+2delta gamma`. For `r>=1`, the inverse exponent
is `1/6+(5/6-delta)r`; since `delta<=5/6` and `r<=t_*+gamma`, it is
at most `1/6+(5/6-delta)t_*+(5/6-delta)gamma`.
The choice `t_*=5/(5-2delta)` makes both main expressions equal to
`rho(delta)`. Bounding both error coefficients by two gives
`rho(delta)+v+2gamma`. No marked moment or amplitude theorem is used.

This is exactly the broader gate exposed by
`UnmarkedDensity.unmarked_count_bound` and
`count_from_unmarked_raw_moments`: `0<=delta<=5/6`. The concrete inverse
spike incurs `2 epsilon_det`; the squared plain-pair spike incurs
`4 epsilon_det`, while `max(1,2m)<=1+150 epsilon_det`.
Thus both source estimates fit `154 epsilon_det+epsilon_m`, and support
tolerance adds another `2 epsilon_det`, for the displayed
`rho(delta_b)+156 epsilon_det+epsilon_m`.

The source threshold precedes all live characters/height/bin/cutoff
variables in the supported theorem, and precedes those variables in the
count after the fixed source family is supplied. Taking finite maxima
over dictionary moment inputs is valid. Partition costs, the finite bin
count and `(1+H_i)^(J0+1)` consume arbitrarily small allotted powers.
Since

\[
 -\rho'(\delta)=\frac{50}{3(5-2\delta)^2}\le\frac{200}{147}
 \quad(\delta\le3/4),
\]

the rounding costs at most `(400/147)e<3e`. Choose the losses so that
`156 epsilon_det+epsilon_m+3e+dyadic_loss+(J0+1)tau_det<epsilon`.
Auxiliary choices exist in this order: select small detector/moment
errors; obtain their finite `J0`; select `e,kappa_aux,eta_aux` within the
detector budget; then decrease `tau_det` for both height and final loss.
All are fixed before `Y,a,T`.

For `T>U^tau_det`, the lattice bound `N<<U` suffices. Choose an integer
`J>=1/tau_det`; then `U<=T^J` and `rho>=2/7>0`. A single enlarged
constant covers bounded `Y`, uniformly in `a,T`. Consequently

\[
 N(Y,a,T)\ll_{\mathcal D,\epsilon}
 (1+T)^JY^{\rho(2a-1)+\epsilon}
 \quad(33/40\le a\le7/8)
\]

with one threshold before `a,T`. The weighted sixth-power lifting is
uniform because `rho>=2/7>1/6`; the sixth-root convolution converges.
After lifting, even the finite exceptional free cores are paid through
that convolution, not incorrectly declared a finite raw-row population.
Natural holes and orientation survive the lift. At a physical use
`T=Z^tau_out`, choose a DISTINCT `tau_out` after the final density degree
`J`; its polynomial height cost fits the physical loss. This proves the
enlarged source theorem within precisely the accepted fixed-family scope.

## 3. Reconstructing the stronger gain in actual source units

Write c_s,d_s for the genuine first-support widths, distinguishing them from the endpoint constant. On either consistent first-side orientation the literal row is

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-(c_s-d_s)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c=log_Z NF_c <=5(R-R0), R<=min(c_s,d_s).       (I1)

The actual enclosing radius is used before dropping its favorable extra -omega. The separate child width M'=M-(c_s-d_s)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2, with the original padding, is unchanged. Active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p modulo six remain distinct, including their zero-residue punctures. No equality of their F_c is assumed; the opposite first-side orientation is treated separately. Reflected second rows and whole-character conjugation remain within the fixed dictionary.

The actual joint high exponent relative to its target, from LA.13, is

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)+E1+E2+small,
    E1=(1-rho)(c_s-d_s)_+-delta c_s-(1+rho)R
       -E-Bc+rho L_c+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.                            (I2)

There is no additional square root to take after this formula. It has already combined the two normalized sides, the joint row count, the missing radical and the outside power.

For delta in [17/25,7/10], put

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    k=rho+delta-1=delta(5-6delta)/[3(5-2delta)].       (I3)

Here 5rho>1, 4rho-1>0, rho<2/5, and 0<k<delta. Let m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+, so c_s=m+T. Substituting L_c<=5(R-R0) into (I2) gives

    E1 <= -(rho+delta-1)T-delta m
          +(4rho-1)R+(1-5rho)R0-E-Bc
       <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-kT-E-Bc
       <= -k c_s.                                    (I4)

The last inequality is exactly delta-4rho+1-k=2-5rho>=0. This uses actual valuations and signs, not a finite residue-table enumeration. Since g2<=b2, also E2<=-delta b2-t2. Both coefficients are in the units of (I2).

For the full second projector, retain the B3.65 signed priority allocation. Extracting a selected plain n=d*l keeps psi_w(d), including its zero; l is unrestricted. Selecting a slot freezes that prime. No additional quotient puncture is inserted. For each of the four actual rectangle pairs put

    rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2,
    zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2.                                 (I5)

Every clipped reduction is nonnegative. B3.69 pays the divisor dyad by the two exact extraction scalars. Independently, the physical pointwise plain price contains -delta rbar. It is a shorter-plain saving, not an extraction scalar used a second time. The actual slot products stay inside the joint row sum; Cauchy and the accepted raw weighted bound replace their paired price delta zbar by gamma zbar. The gain there is eta zbar, where

    eta=4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta)=2k.               (I6)

For example, clearing 3(5-2delta) reduces both sides of eta=2k to 2delta(5-6delta). It is an identity throughout the interval, not a numerical endpoint coincidence.

The already reviewed coefficient reduction is essential: freeze the missing first radical before weighted summation; all other apparent moving holes are natural zeros of w. Residual fixed holes have divisor-many subsets, and the finite surviving slot lists retain their original relative characters. The second projector stays outside this row reconstruction. Its count is paid once by B3.69. Common Fourier majorants precede the labels and their diagonal contraction adds no label count. Thus the weighted bound has the actual fixed prime coefficients, natural conductor and same-parent zero maximum; it is not applied to arbitrary moving masks.

The surviving widths satisfy the already established literal incidence bound

    zbar >= z-c_s-b2-rbar-small.                       (I7)

Each genuine frozen incidence divides the relevant complete extracted column, with its multiplicity. The column widths are c_s+c2 and c_s+d2. Newly frozen second-projector slots are included in r_j, and clipping costs only the single aggregate endpoint tolerance. Both the support terms and (I7) refer to the same pair of rectangles.

Set s=c_s+b2+rbar. If s>=z, (I4), E2 and the retained plain reduction already save at least ks>=kz. This uses only the old density, with its supported-window completion; no positive surviving slot width or weighted-width premise is needed. In particular all-slot-exhaustion cases are covered.

If s<z, then c_s<z and (I1) gives W>=M-c_s-6a>M-z-6a. Under the strict condition

    M-6a>22z,                                        (I8)

one has W>21z. Each individual surviving z_j<=z is therefore admissible for the accepted raw weighted theorem. The gain is at least

    ks+eta(z-s)-small =ks+2k(z-s)-small >=kz-small.    (I9)

The weighted theorem's width condition is needed only here. No negative nominal width is put into a nonempty density count: outside this case the old supported-window rule applies, and in this case W is strictly positive. Since k decreases, its endpoint values are

    k(17/25)=391/6825,  k(7/10)=7/135.

This proves the sharper all-configuration gain **k(delta)z**, in paired units. The weaker uniform 7z/135 follows. Exceptional rows remain separate and contribute no part of (I9).

The internal supported-witness zero bin can still have a larger upper endpoint than the physical bin. The accepted weighted lemma supplies its inverse/prime witnesses using that larger bin, but its slot price uses the original physical upper bound. Buffered bins below .70 use their prescribed lower edge with an O(e) upper-price allowance. Bins above .70 can use the old high estimate. Bins crossing .68 use the original low-branch rounding rule. No transform or projector is applied to a zero-bin indicator.

## 1. Decision and exact limits

**Accept Theorems M and B as written mathematical results at their stated scope. Accept their combined quantitative obstruction. Do not credit an arithmetic energy improvement or any new zero-free constant.** The incumbent remains c6 = 125139/1000000, with b6 = 874861/1000000. The conditional returns to c = .13, 1/6 or 1/4 have a completely explicit missing hypothesis. They are not established endpoints.

I fully read the one frozen author packet: `report.md`, `check.py`, `receipt.json` and `freeze.json`. Its four byte bindings match the authorized handoff, and are independently recorded in `receipt.json` here. I did not execute or alter the author's helper. I reconstructed the arguments below rather than infer analysis from its finite arithmetic checks. No outside correlation theorem is needed for M or B.

The strongest relevant objection was simultaneous probability-one selection. An estimate uniform in a conditioned finite phase does not, by itself, license an uncountable intersection over every possible phase assignment. The stated theorem does not need such an intersection: finite prescriptions are fixed first; finite truncation sets, integer affine forms and ordinary character weights form countable collections. Section 3 below gives the complete selection argument, and a finite-basis strengthening if uniform finite-phase control is desired. Thus this is an explanation of the exact quantifier contract, not a fatal gap or a change to the theorem.

The model is genuinely multiplicative and has exactly the squarefree/coprime support. It permits complex phases. It does not have the actual global prime law a(p) = -chi(p), the prescribed global convolution inverse, or the real-valuedness of W27's model. Its fixed-H Cesaro energy limit is an averaged statement; it is not square-root cancellation in each individual interval. These distinctions are essential to the verdict.

statement:
# [research revision]: native translation costs and a fixed-source renewal obstruction

Accept G201-G203 at the scopes below, from the [W64 author](wild64/report.md)
and [independent review](wild64-review/report.md). The review corrects the
moving-stencil normalization and proves a stronger, single fixed synthetic
source obstruction. The [two selection-blind audits](wild64-review/independent-audits.md)
retain complete signed smooth prefixes and complete feedback forcing.
These results redirect particular norm-based attacks. They neither bound
the full signed arithmetic source nor increase c11=.1251459636.

## G201. Exact native carrier spectrum, with normalized stencil cost

Use the literal Eisenstein [JN source](../[research revision]/h-joint/report.md), not
an ordinary integer surrogate. Freeze the original long-prime pair of
distinct degree-one rational norms p,r, with Q=pr and phi=(p-1)(r-1).
The complete finite group has Q^2 elements and unitary Fourier factor 1/Q.
The row multiplier is m(h)=ell_p(h_p)ell_r(h_r), with quadratic characters
zero at zero. The mark factors vanish off exactly phi mark pairs and have
modulus one on them. The complete coefficient includes the original
b0=b(pi)conjugate(b(pi'))zeta_CRT, which may vanish.

For translation S_t f(h)=f(h+t), the row commutator is

    D_t=diag(m(h)-m(h+t)) S_t.

When t is nonzero in both residue fields, local autocorrelation is -1.
Indeed z^2=y(y+1) is equivalent, by an invertible change of variables over
an odd field, to (2y+1-2z)(2y+1+2z)=1. Counting its p-1 solutions proves
the local identity including the zero sites. CRT gives correlation 1.
There are B=(p-2)(r-2) positions where both row values are nonzero, two
where both vanish, and n1=2(p+r-3) where exactly one vanishes. Thus

    singular value 2: multiplicity n2=(B-1)/2;
    singular value 1: multiplicity n1;
    rank D_t=(Q+2p+2r-9)/2;
    ||D_t||_HS^2=2(phi-1),  ||D_t||_op=2.

For a shift nonzero only at p, replace these multiplicities by
n2=(p-1)(r-1)/2 and n1=2(r-1); the other case is symmetric. The full
carrier repeats each nonzero row singular value phi times and scales
it by |b0|. Unitary Fourier conjugation introduces no further saving.
For rank k<=n2 approximation the squared row Hilbert-Schmidt error is
at least 4(n2-k)+n1, and for k<n2 the operator error is at least 2.

Let P=sum c_j S_j for k distinct integer shifts 0<j<min(p,r). Distinct
matrix diagonals cannot cancel in Hilbert-Schmidt norm, so

    ||[M_m,P]||_HS^2=2(phi-1)||c||_2^2,
    sqrt(2(phi-1)/Q)||c||_2 <= ||[M_m,P]||_op
                             <=2 sqrt(k)||c||_2,
    rank[M_m,P] >= (phi-1)/(2k),  c!=0.

The lower operator bound uses rank<=Q. Moving coefficients require the
displayed normalization: c_1=Q^(-10) defeats the author's unnormalized
prose claim. The correct cost is relative to |b0| ||c||_2, or for stencils
whose normalized size does not vanish. The immutable author report is
retained with this explicit superseding correction.

These are ambient carrier facts. They do not identify the carrier with
the physical mark matrix, make the actual folded W an extremizer, or
bound its signed pairing below. All original projectors, ordered short
pairs including equality, complex gcd core, masks, roots, independent
heights and natural zeros remain. The raw H target is still

    Z^epsilon G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig,

followed by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. None of the .004 full-H deficit is
paid. A source-specific recurrence and its complete observation/residual
estimate remain legitimate targets.

## G202. Centered quotient norm and one fixed cumulative source

Now use a separate ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, with
a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a(1)=1 and literal natural zeros. Write M(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n),
psi_chi(y)=sum_(d<=y)Lambda(d)chi(d), and delta=1 for principal chi and
zero otherwise. The exact [[research revision] renewal identity](../[research revision]/wild55/report.md)
is prior credit:

    R(x)=sum_(d<=x)Lambda(d)chi(d)M(x/d)=-sum_(n<=x)a(n)log n,
    M(x)log x=int_1^x M(t)dt/t-R(x).

For integer N>=2 and floor-invariant f define the centered functional

    J_N(f)=sum_(d<=N)Lambda(d)chi(d)f_floor(N/d)
                     -delta int_1^N f_floor(N/u) du.

The pole-subtraction measure is du. The restored principal term is exactly
N sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n-M(N); it cannot be dropped. Merge equal quotient states
before taking absolute values:

    J_N(f)=sum_(1<=m<N)c_m f_m,
    c_m=psi_chi(N/m)-psi_chi(N/(m+1))-delta N/[m(m+1)].

The lower interval endpoint is strict. State m=N contributes neither a
nonzero discrete atom nor positive continuous length. The exact norm for
|f_m|<=m^beta and f_m=0 at m<=Y, with 0<beta<1, is

    C_(beta,Y)(N)=N^(-beta) sum_(Y<m<N)|c_m|m^beta.

Set D=floor(min(sqrt(N)/4,N/[4(Y+1)])). Each unramified prime power
2<=d<=D has a distinct cell m=floor(N/d)>Y of length
N/[m(m+1)]<=d^2/(N-d)<=1/8, containing d alone. Therefore

    C_(beta,Y)(N)>=2^(-beta-1)
                    sum_(d<=D,(d,q)=1)Lambda(d)d^(-beta)
                  >>_(q,beta) D^(1-beta).

The lower estimate needs only an elementary Chebyshev bound: prime
valuations of binomial(2n,n) give psi(2n)>=2n log 2-log(2n+1), and deleting
the finitely many q-prime-power rays costs O_q(log D). For Y=floor(N^theta),
0<=theta<1, even C/log N grows at least as
N^((1-beta)min(1/2,1-theta))/log N. This is a merged centered norm bound,
not a lower bound for J_N(M), R, or M.

The obstruction survives cumulative inputs with honest natural-zero
increments. For 1/2<beta<1 and 0<alpha<(1-beta)/(2-beta), let

    Q_q(t)=sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1)
          =kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt t),
    kappa_q=zeta(2)^(-1) product_(p|q)p/(p+1)>0.

For each unramified prime power d<=N^alpha, put m_d=floor(N/d),
H_d=floor(m_d^beta/8) and
B_d(n)=max(0,H_d-|Q_q(n)-Q_q(m_d)|). The squarefree density formula follows
by inserting sum_(e^2|n)mu(e), counting q-units, and paying every square-divisor
error and tail. It places each bump within m_d+O_q(H_d). The support-width
to nearest-center spacing ratio is O_q(N^(beta-1)d^(2-beta))=o(1).
Supports and increment boundaries are disjoint. Their inverse images
under u->floor(N/u) have width o(1), so each has exactly the integer
contact d; the floor error O(d^2/N) also tends uniformly to zero.

The compact synthetic sum G_N(n)=sum_d conjugate(chi(d))B_d(n) satisfies
|G_N(n)|<=n^beta and |G_N(n)-G_N(n-1)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1).
Every discrete atom contributes Lambda(d)H_d. For principal chi the full
continuous subtraction costs at most half this for sufficiently large N;
for nonprincipal chi it is absent. Thus

    J_N(G_N) >= c N^(beta+alpha(1-beta)) >0.

Independent strengthening: choose N_j increasingly so that each whole
bump block G_j, including its increment boundary, lies above N_(j-1)
and above the preceding support. If F_old is the earlier sum, choose
z_j=J_(N_j)(F_old)/|J_(N_j)(F_old)| when nonzero and z_j=1 otherwise.
Then |J_(N_j)(F_old+z_jG_j)|=|J_(N_j)(F_old)|+J_(N_j)(G_j).
Later blocks change no state sampled at N_j. Hence ONE locally finite
F=sum_j z_jG_j and b(n)=F(n)-F(n-1) satisfy

    |b(n)|<=mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1),  |F(n)|<=n^beta,
    |J_(N_j)(F)|>=c N_j^(beta+alpha(1-beta)).

Any fixed finite zero prefix can be prescribed. For principal chi, the
phases may be +/-1 and b(n) belongs to {-1,0,1}. A growing zero prefix
at infinitely many N_j would force F identically zero and is NOT claimed.
Only the cutoff-dependent construction retains that separate property.
Neither construction has the prescribed Möbius signs, multiplicativity,
or the actual inverse-convolution law. Those are the remaining structures
that a successful arithmetic argument must use.

## G203. A signed inner source does not rescue the outer positive budget

For fixed ordinary chi and y=x^eta, 0<eta<1, split each squarefree n uniquely
into its y-smooth part a and y-rough part b. With S_y the entire signed
smooth prefix, including its unit, exactly

    M_chi(x)=sum_(b<=x,Pminus(b)>y)mu(b)chi(b) S_y(x/b).

The proposed outer absolute budget retains all cancellation inside S_y.
Nevertheless each unramified prime p in (x/2,x] contributes exactly one
to that budget, because S_y(x/p)=1. It is therefore >>_q x/log x by the
ordinary [prime number theorem, DLMF27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
No arithmetic-progression or conductor-uniform theorem is imported.
On shells [X,2X], primes p in (X,3X/2] have the same unit inner prefix
through the common interval [3X/2,2X]. The sum of complete polymer L1 or
L2 norms also costs >>_q X/log X. This does not bound the signed sum or
its full Gram form below. Cross-polymer cancellation remains open.

## Complete feedback and arithmetic return remain explicit

The other blind audit retains a conditional feedback budget. For a fixed
compatible finite map T=[[a,b],[c,D]], let r>||D|| and
Delta=r-|a|-||b||||c||/(r-||D||)>0. The exact Schur denominator
s(w)=w-a-b(wI-D)^(-1)c has no zero at |w|>=r. Its full resolvent formula
gives C_r=K+(1+K||c||)(1+K||b||)/Delta, K=(r-||D||)^(-1), and

    ||T^j||<=C_r r^(j+1),
    ||z_j||<=C_r r^(j+1)||z_0||+C_r sum_(k<j)r^(j-k)||f_k||.

Every forcing term is retained. A contour-only denominator bound without
exterior zero exclusion is insufficient. Varying native Q^2 spaces require
compatible maps, physical observation and all discarded/forced complements;
the stationary lemma alone supplies none of these. G136/G151 retain ancestry.

For actual ordinary coefficients, [research revision]'s exact inverse
M(x)=1-R(x)/log x-int_2^x R(t)dt/[t(log t)^2] shows that a complete
all-real-x every-epsilon bound R=O(x^(gamma+epsilon)log x) is equivalent
to the corresponding Mertens exponent. Mellin continuation then excludes
regular L zeros at Re(s)>gamma, retaining the principal pole, imprimitive
factors and all finite heights for each fixed character. This entire
arithmetic estimate is still OPEN. A first gain requires gamma<.8748540364;
gamma=.8748,5/6,3/4 correspond to nearby c=.1252,1/6,1/4 targets.

## G112. Coalescence does not lower the independent-defect power cost

For each fixed ordinary character chi preserve all natural zeros and put
R(t,y)=sum_(n<=t,P^-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), with P^-(1)=infinity.
Its least-prime recurrence is R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p).
For a floor-invariant approximation F let Delta be its full recurrence
defect. G92 gives the exact root identity

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m) C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm),P^+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).    (77.1)

All coefficients are merged by the actual integer state BEFORE absolute
values. The strict lower/inclusive upper endpoints, v=1 and strict prime
ordering matter. For the exact integer collar m<=p^r, fixed integer r>=1,
the independent bounded-defect norm is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.        (77.2)

The earlier real-state exponent-one lower bound did not prove anything
comparable after signed coalescence. The actual cancellation at
(N,p,m)=(20196,17,18), v=65,66 remains valid. Here a new arithmetic
argument proves, for EVERY fixed principal character chi0 modulo q,

    lim_(N->infinity) log B_(r,chi0)(N)/log N=1.        (77.3)

The external input is Tenenbaum's fixed-order friable Mobius expansion,
combining Theorems2-3 in the [original source](headroom/Erdos-Alladi.pdf).
Write omega for the Buchstab function. For fixed K>=1 and a fixed compact
I contained in(K+1,infinity), uniformly for u=log x/log y in I,

    W(x,y)=sum_(n<=x,P^+(n)<=y)mu(n)
      =x sum_(j=1)^K a_j omega^(j)(u)/(log y)^(j+1)
        +O_(I,K)(x/(log y)^(K+2)),
    sum_(j>=1)a_j z^j=1/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)], a1=1.        (77.4)

The primary images confirm the sign, derivative index and logarithm power.
The source domain exp((log x)^(2/3+epsilon))<=y<=x holds for a fixed
epsilon in(0,1/3) and large y at each fixed compact u-range. That compact
is away from the first K+1 exceptional integers. Its extra error
Psi(x,y)/L_epsilon(y) is smaller than every needed fixed logarithmic
order. No uniform growing K or u estimate is imported. The published
theorem and ordinary PNT are mathematical premises, not consequences of
the local finite helper or a complete reproof of the twenty-page source.

The strict cutoff is exactly y=p-1. Its replacement by log p changes the
main expression by O(x/[p(log p)^2]), within the fixed-order remainder.
For principal q define A_q(s)=product_(ell|q)(1-ell^-s)^-1. Once p exceeds
every prime divisor of q, the complete convolution is

    W_q(x,p-)=sum_(d q-smooth) W(x/d,p-),
    sum_(j>=1)b_(j,q)z^j=A_q(1+z)/[(1+z)zeta(1+z)].    (77.5)

All powers of the primes dividing q occur. Truncating at D=(log p)^B
costs at most x D^-eta A_q(1-eta), for fixed0<eta<1. Fixed logarithmic
moments of d then justify the Taylor product on a slightly larger compact.
Thus (77.4) holds with b_(j,q) and b_(1,q)=q/phi(q). This retains the
principal character's natural zeros; it is not a nonprincipal extension.

For fixed p the intervals in(77.1), summed over m>p^r, cover exactly
(0,U_p], U_p=N/[p(p^r+1)]. Hence

    sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).          (77.6)

Choose a FIXED u>2 with omega'(u)!=0 and P=N^(1/(u+r+1)). Uniformly for
P<p<=2P, log U_p/log p=u+O(1/log P), and the K=1 expansion has a fixed
nonzero sign. PNT with partial summation gives

    sum_(P<p<=2P)sum_(m>p^r) C_(N,chi0)(m,p)
      ~ -(q/phi(q))omega'(u) kappa_r N P^-r/(log P)^3,
    kappa_r=(1-2^-r)/r>0.                              (77.7)

The plus one in U_p is exact; its later relative O(p^-r) replacement is
paid. Triangle inequality gives a lower bound for the actual merged norm,
with power theta(u,r)=(u+1)/(u+r+1). Expanding the merged coefficients
before the upper bound counts each squarefree q-unit d at most once,
so B<=N. There are admissible u arbitrarily large: an eventually zero
omega' would make omega constant on a tail, and
u omega'(u)=omega(u-1)-omega(u) propagates that constant backward to
(1,2), contradicting omega(u)=1/u. Taking successively larger FIXED u
in the liminf bound proves(77.3), without a growing-u asymptotic.

### 2.1 Exact disk theorem and strongest cheap counterexample

Let h be holomorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and h(0)=1. Define normalized circle measure dm=dtheta/(2pi),

    u(theta)=Re h(exp(i theta)),
    B(h)=integral max(-u(theta),0) dm.

Write u=u_+-u_-. The mean-value identity gives integral u_+=1+B and integral u_-=B. For |z|=rho<1 the Poisson kernel obeys

    (1-rho)/(1+rho) <= P_z(theta) <= (1+rho)/(1-rho).

Consequently, with k_rho=(1-rho)/(1+rho),

    Re h(z) >= k_rho(1+B)-B/k_rho.                 (W40.1)

This is the full complementary return: the negative part is paid against the largest Poisson weight and the positive part against the smallest. It follows that

    B(h) <= b(r):=(1-r)^2/(4r)
       ==> Re h(z)>0 for every |z|<r.              (W40.2)

At |z|=r a strict hypothesis gives strict positivity; equality only gives nonnegativity there. The open-disk conclusion with non-strict B<=b(r) is valid because b(rho) is strictly decreasing for 0<rho<1. In particular h has no zero in |z|<r. No positivity of the original arithmetic coefficients was used.

For completeness the signed representation is also exact:

    h(z)=integral (exp(i theta)+z)/(exp(i theta)-z)
                       *u(theta) dm.              (W40.3)

Expand the kernel into1+2 sum_(n>=1)z^n exp(-in theta). The Fourier coefficients of Re h give half the positive Taylor coefficients; the constant is h(0)=1. Uniform convergence on compact subdisks proves the identity. This avoids assuming a positive Herglotz measure or an analytic logarithm of h.

The generic budget is sharp in the signed-measure closure. Put B>0 and

    h_B(z)=(1+B)(1+z)/(1-z)-B(1-z)/(1+z).

Its representing measure is (1+B)delta_1-B delta_-1, and h_B(0)=1. It has a zero at

    z=-r_B,
    r_B=(sqrt(1+B)-sqrt B)/(sqrt(1+B)+sqrt B),
    B=(1-r_B)^2/(4r_B).                             (W40.4)

Thus arbitrarily small total negative mass can create a zero arbitrarily close to the boundary. A claim that a small unweighted defect gives the ENTIRE disk is false. A positive collar is essential. The rational h_B has boundary poles, so it is not an equality example in the smooth-boundary class. To verify sharpness there, take h_B(tz), t<1, and choose r_B=tr. It is analytic beyond the unit circle and has its zero at-r. Its boundary real part is the signed Poisson smoothing of the two atoms. Its negative mass tends to b(r) as t increases to1: the two Poisson kernels concentrate on disjoint arcs, and their overlap mass tends to0. For a proposed larger budget at fixed r, first choose r'<r with b(r') below that budget, then use this approximation at r'. Its zero is now INSIDE the target disk. Thus no larger uniform open-disk budget follows in the smooth class either.

This first test corrects the unpriced seed: total negative mass is useful only with the explicit radius-dependent return W40.2. It does not by itself prove any arithmetic bound.
title: 2.1 Exact disk theorem and strongest cheap counterexample

## 7. Uniform independent audit17: optimized contours retain the observed residues

The seed proposes signed endpoint states on a low-resolvent contour. The relevant test must use the actual reciprocal L-function, not an arbitrary rational transfer function.

For fixed ordinary chi define the first logarithmic Riesz sum

    R_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n)log(x/n)
           =integral_1^x M_chi(t)dt/t.                 (R15)

The n=x endpoint has weight0. On a fixed vertical line c>1, the elementary inverse Mellin kernel for log_+(y) is y^s/s^2. It follows by closing left for y>1 and right for y<1, with the double pole at0; at y=1 the vertical integral of1/s^2 is0. Its absolute vertical convergence and sum_n |a(n)|n^(-c)<=zeta(c) justify interchange. Thus the FULL identity is

    R_chi(x)=(1/(2pi i))integral_(c-i infinity)^(c+i infinity)
                         x^s/[s^2 L(s,chi)] ds.         (R16)

No character zero or source coefficient has changed.

Let 0<sigma<c and T>0, with the boundary of the finite rectangle avoiding zeros of L. Write I_(v,T) for the upward integral on Re(s)=v from -T to T, divided by2pi i, and K_x(s)=x^s/[s^2L(s,chi)]. The residue theorem gives EXACTLY

    R_chi(x)=I_(sigma,T)
          +sum_(rho inside rectangle) Res_(s=rho) K_x(s)
          +B_T(x)+E_(c,T)(x),                           (R17)
    B_T=-(1/(2pi i))[
          integral_(c+iT)^(sigma+iT) K_x(s)ds
          +integral_(sigma-iT)^(c-iT) K_x(s)ds],
    |E_(c,T)(x)|<=zeta(c)x^c/(pi T).

The last bound comes only from the omitted RIGHT-line tails and |1/L(c+it,chi)|<=zeta(c). It does not bound the horizontal pieces, the left side or any detours. Principal L's pole at1 is a zero of1/L, not a residue of K_x. The s=0 kernel pole is outside the sigma>0 rectangle. Ramified Euler factors have not been deleted.

If L has a zero rho of multiplicity m, with Re(rho)>0, its contribution has the exact form

    Res K_x(s)=x^rho P_(m-1)(log x),
    leading coefficient of P_(m-1)
       = m! / [L^(m)(rho) rho^2 (m-1)!] !=0.            (R18)

This follows by multiplying the leading Laurent term of1/L by the Taylor series of x^s/s^2. A closed local contour with winding1 around rho and0 around every other pole has integral2pi i times (R18), regardless of its optimized shape. For fixed rho its absolute value is asymptotic to a nonzero constant times x^Re(rho)(log x)^(m-1). Shrinking or moving that local detour cannot turn it into O(x^gamma) when gamma<Re(rho).

This is a scoped obstruction to discarding or underpricing a pole's local contour contribution. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete Mertens or Riesz sum: other residues and boundary integrals may interfere. Nor does it assert that a hypothetical arithmetic zero exists. It shows precisely what a source-correct contour-state construction would have to retain and estimate.

There is a complete conditional return. If, for every fixed chi and epsilon>0, the whole R_chi(x) is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(gamma+epsilon)) at all large real x, then

    integral_1^infinity R_chi(x)x^(-s)dx/x
       =1/[s^2 L(s,chi)]   initially Re(s)>1

continues holomorphically to Re(s)>gamma. The numerator1/s^2 is nonzero at every possible zero there, so all finite-height L zeros are excluded exactly as in section2. In particular (R3) implies this Riesz bound by Cauchy--Schwarz in (R15), with a harmless logarithm absorbed by every epsilon.

A contour proposal would therefore be sufficient if it proved a complete signed bound for ALL of (R17), including the right truncation, horizontal/endpoint states, left line, every enclosed residue and any induced numerator. An individual low-resolvent arc, a contour which simply avoids zeros, or a fixed-height check does not prove that assertion. Choosing T=T(x) to make the explicit right tail small still leaves all the other height-dependent costs.

This is standard Perron/Riesz/residue machinery applied to the exact source. F01/W27 weak detectors, W22's filter cautions and W39's all-height return are ancestry. More specifically, [research revision] G77 ALREADY retains the full Gaussian rectangle, nonzero multiplicity-residue polynomial, right tail, horizontals and a fixed finite-packet shell-norm lower bound. This audit changes to a Riesz kernel and its explicit polynomial right-tail bound; it does not improve that general gluing principle or its packet lower bound. The seed is promising only if it supplies the missing arithmetic signed boundary estimate; contour geometry or an observability toy does not replace it.

For j=1 fix a dyad P<=Np<2P, retaining the literal band endpoints in its arithmetic support. Then A/2<=P<=Y. Let E=D/P, y=Np/P and z=Nc/E. The first-power summand is exactly

                       (log Np/log D) V_D(yz),        (R3)

and P^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). There is no unpriced factor P^(1/2).

Apply the literal common-profile lemma B3.3 on an ambient compact box in y,z, with larger individual cutoffs equal to one on the entire current support. This box and its Fourier measure are fixed BEFORE a current row, prime, slot label or coloring is selected. The sharp band membership and every arithmetic hole remain in row-independent outer coefficients. The measure has a finite weighted L1 norm controlled by finitely many common seminorms; no prime-specific Fourier measure is chosen.

For clarity about heights, first write the original witness twist explicitly. If W_P(x)=W_0(x)x^(sigma+i gamma), then

    (yz)^(sigma+i gamma)=y^(sigma+i gamma)z^(sigma+i gamma).

Separate the remaining smooth kernel W_0(yz) log D/log(Dyz), with the bounded real power either retained there or factored as above. Thus high Fourier decay is a property of a kernel whose derivative constants do NOT grow as |gamma|^N. The original gamma appears explicitly in both output tests. A two-coordinate version of B3.3 has Fourier coordinates tau_1,tau_2; the plain upper bound is used at gamma+tau_2, and the new MI slot retains gamma+tau_1. Original slot heights stay independent. Nothing forces the new frequency to be a zero height.

Use only a fixed small fraction of the available retained height buffer for these frequencies. The actual witness lies at |gamma|<=3^i T_ht, while B_(i+1)<a+2e controls the larger box through 3^(i+1)T_ht. The original B0.14--15 contour padding therefore accommodates the retained frequency shift without changing i, a, beta, phi or the chosen zero. Here is an exact way to pay the ENTIRE Fourier complement. Use the source's internal floor T_ht>=U^kappa with fixed kappa>0. For |tau_2| above its reserved fraction of T_ht, absolute ideal counting gives |S_u(E;V)|<=C E^(1/2), uniformly in the imaginary twist. Since E<=C D is polynomially bounded, E^((1-beta)/2)<=U^C0 for a fixed C0. Choose a fixed J1>C0/kappa. Then

    E^(1/2) <=C E^(beta/2)(1+|tau_2|)^J1

on that complement. Bounded nonempty subunit E obey the same inequality by constants. On the retained frequencies use R1. The unconditioned MI already has polynomial cost in tau_1 and the original heights. The complete Fourier integral is therefore bounded by a weighted L1 norm of the SAME height-free kernel, with weight degree J1 plus the fixed MI degree. B3.3 makes this finite uniformly in U,D and the current labels. No Fourier piece or arithmetic term is discarded, and no tail is inferred merely from a large nominal height.

For the source height choices, first fix the MI/Sobolev degree J0 and the real/bin losses, then choose the internal small height range so its U^(J0*kappa) cost fits the allocated loss. The extra high derivatives just used belong to the height-free separation kernel; they do not increase this previously fixed MI height degree. Below the internal floor use the dictionary at that floor. Above the original small polynomial range a larger final external height degree pays the absolute source bound. The external physical height exponent is chosen after that degree. The original detector's contour tails retain their accepted B-before-N order. This full-integral implementation supplies the author's separation step without a circular height/decay choice or a new high-height theorem.
