# Accepted written extension: finite coupled amplifiers, c2 = 0.125128

Controller disposition, 11 October 2026: **accept the complete written
analytic extension to c2=15641/125000=.125128**, relative to the retained
PR9/PR15 analytic inputs. Its boundary is theta2=109359/125000=.874872.
The statement is the open half-plane Re(s)>theta2 for each finite-order
Hecke L-function of trivial infinite type over Q(sqrt(-3)), and every
ordinary Dirichlet L-function, including zeta. The principal pole at 1
is excluded. The statement adds no boundary-line, angular-family or
uniform moving-parent-conductor theorem.

This improves the accepted [research revision] c1=.12512 by exactly 1/125000=.000008,
and Gao's c_G=.1251134 by 73/5000000=.0000146. **Full endpoint
formalization, clean dependency replay and independent kernel verification
remain pending.** The old c0=.125113352960035869... retains its separate
[three-kernel receipt](../[research revision]/formal-evidence-update.md).

The [complete author proof](gao-coupled/report.md),
[independent mathematical review](gao-critic/report.md), and adjacent
arithmetic programs/receipts are preserved byte for byte. The controller
read both complete reports, checked the source bindings, reconstructed
the coupled geometry and endpoint returns, and replayed both exact
arithmetic implementations in owned copies. Each returned **8/6/1**
whole-rectangle certificates; the independent receipt reproduced
`abe39a6c4d0845ded15ce77834b9f3b76c60296de4e3e1c4ae3935c6094a7622`.
These finite checks support the written proof; they are not a kernel proof.

## Credit and preserved contracts

Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance, supplied the local construction and
bridges at PR15 `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, relative to
PR9 `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. OpenAI retains credit for
the initial 7/8 theorem and analytic/arithmetic framework; Hailey Collet
for the quartic, variable-moment, detector and source architecture; Akash
Levy for the weighted numerator. [research revision] supplies the larger-amplifier
specialization. [research revision] supplies a finite family of amplifiers coupled
to original slot width and its complete endpoint return. This is not a
claim of literature priority or upstream endorsement. Original sources
and licenses remain in the [preserved PR15 record](../external/gao-pr15-ca182b70/README.md).

The local theorem retains the fixed finite ray family, natural sextic
row, original prime pools and common annular profile, relative characters,
natural zeros, fixed original anchor Q_*, row-independent punctures and
non-FixedInducingRow eligibility. With U=Z^M, the window is

    .41M <= n1,n2 <= .44M,  .03M <= z <= .04M,
    n1+n2+(881/200)z <= M.

It gives the original paired squared moment O(Z^(M+epsilon) H_J),
including all four derivative-profile pairs. Descendants use only the
old 9/2 moment or unrestricted zero-slot input. Mesh, dictionary, finite
orders, constants and one eventual threshold precede the same live
scales, masks, subsets and independent heights as in the original source.

## Genuine new local input

Put C=881/200, r=9/2-C=19/200, k=9/40, and
b_j=.03+j/5000 for j=0,...,50. For t=z/M, take j=1 when t=.03 and
otherwise the unique j with b_(j-1)<t<=b_j. Choose the literal prime
amplifier exponent a_j/M=k b_j and sigma_j=3a_j. This is a ceiling
selection, including at the left endpoint. Within the same interval,

    A/M <= 1-(C-1)b_(j-1),   g/M <= r b_j.

Thus the proof does not combine incompatible full-window extrema. The
fifty choices are fixed before the target, rows, transforms or binning.
Both equal-product rectangles use the same j. Its dependence on original
slot width, rather than either plain scale, causes no derivative of a
selection boundary in plain-scale supremum recovery.

The exact PR9 amplification interfaces quantify original data and slot
widths after the eventual threshold, permit fixed positive sigma, and
require a sufficiently fine mesh. A finite maximum over the fifty
choices and four derivative pairs therefore gives the needed simultaneous
threshold. The representation multiplicity remains a fixed constant.
This is a source-level admissibility check, not an inference from the
older global theorem's separate small-sigma induction.

The enlarged actual main radius is K0+(d-c)_++6a_j+omega. Errors retain
their own radii and original canonical source. Exact interval checking
gives low reserve 151/22500000 >= 1/150000 and high reserve 1/43200,
including the actual rounding charge 13/100000. The high-branch
derivative is bounded below by 1548949/4860000>0 over its whole range.
The low/high transition at .7 is paid with the original mesh losses.

The three error reserves are at least 97/80000,1717/80000,1061/40000;
second-zero, main fixed-inducing and error fixed-inducing reserves are
2727/40000,7497/100000,8199/200000. The exact main exception retains
its -4a_j term. Joint row labels, missing radicals, valuations, projector
costs, natural zeros, moving holes, negative actual-width corrections,
both transforms and old-only descendants all remain in the argument.
Choose aggregate small losses below fixed fractions of the least reserve.

## Complete endpoint, not just local capacity

Use

    ell=15673/93750, h=3969737987/5000000000,
    x=5598466039/15000000000, y=6893853961/15000000000,
    kappa=46859/62500.

The actual shortening maxima are .422132747912 for each plain slot and
.036139510427 for the marked slot. Safe upper edges are **.423 and
.0365**; the older .036 edge cannot be reused. Short-slot and short-plain
complements have reserves 19/1000 and 11/4000. The coarse large
Euler-shift reserve is 2747/15858000>1/6000; its actual value is
37375232238487/188618444993538000. The earlier >1/4000 claim is not
reused. Coefficient mass and exhausted/empty-slot cases are retained.

On the complete delta,p rectangle, rational Bernstein subdivision proves
the local upper row, old junction and old lower row with respectively
8,6,1 leaves and savings 10^-6,10^-5,10^-3. The independent implementation
derives its polynomial separately, verifies every box, nonoverlap and
total coverage, and matches the author's exact extrema. No sampled
grid stands in for a continuous inequality.

The retained-row extension has saving 4999/5000000000; local and old
feedback coefficients are below 1/50 and 1/8. The proof also pays the
floor, finite-conductor and small-row cases, original free Euler shifts,
principal/eigenvalue terms, full height range and off-height fields.
Common reserves and the mesh are fixed before a near-extremal target;
the finite amplifier family adds no target-dependent saving. The final
strip iteration and the Eisenstein-to-ordinary-Dirichlet transfer are
part of the complete author and independent review, with the pole at 1
treated separately. No zero-times-pole inference is used.

## Exact limitation and useful next step

The inequality **C>3791/861** is the open range of the displayed
*strictly positive low/high reserve argument*. At equality the two
reserves cannot both be strictly positive. This does **not** prove the
epsilon-loss moment impossible at equality, and does not exclude an
epsilon-dependent construction or different argument there. Any stronger
wording in the frozen author discussion is qualified by this disposition.
The explicit C=4.405 theorem lies strictly inside the proved range and
does not rely on passage to equality.

A finer fixed family can test constants between this boundary and
4.405, with the complete endpoint repriced. A material further gain
requires a better low-bin deletion price, high-bin density loss, radius
increment or useful local window. Raising a lower slot edge must also
pay the enlarged short-slot complement. Neither such an improvement
nor a limiting endpoint is admitted here.

`V_P=exp(sum_(p<=P)p^-s) product_(p<=P)(1-p^-s)` has

These converge normally, with upper and lower modulus bounds on each `Re s>=rho>1/2`, since the first-prime channel was removed. Restoring it is not paid by bounding higher clusters. Under the separate open fixed-power prime-counting error, integration including the prime-2 atom gives

This matches W36 R36.20–22 verbatim in mathematical content, already credited to [research revision] A12/W21 there. Ordinary PNT is not the missing fixed-power bound. when

statement:
## 4. Common-filter arithmetic payment: full proof audit

For an integer t>=0 put f_t(n)=mu^2(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), using f_0=delta1. Fix p not dividing q and J>=2, independent of x. Let

    Q_p=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    v_(p,J)=Q_p^(*J), P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b_p=Q_p*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)).                       (4.1)

At p^a, the literal filter coefficient is binom(J,a)(-p chi(p))^a for 0<=a<=J. The actual b_p has period pq and mean zero. For nonprincipal chi both period sums vanish; for principal chi the p unrestricted copies cancel the p-multiple contribution, since chi(p)=1. Imprimitive and ramified natural zeros remain. Hence its partial sums are bounded by a constant depending on p,q.

### 4.1 Periodic hyperbola induction with every overlap

For any fixed bounded periodic mean-zero b, set B_t(x)=sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n). For every fixed integer t>=1,

    |B_t(x)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t), x>=1.                       (4.2)

For t=1 this is bounded periodic partial sums. For t>1 let Y=x^(1/t). Every admissible ordered t-tuple has at least one coordinate <=Y. Inclusion-exclusion over these t events is exact. In a term with j<t designated short coordinates, put m=t-j and beta=1-1/m. Their product is at most Y^j<=x, so the remaining summation threshold is >=1 and the induction hypothesis applies. Bounding ONLY the designated short coefficients costs

    C_m x^beta [sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^-beta]^j
       <=C_m(Dm)^j x^beta Y^(j/m)
       =C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t),                             (4.3)

where D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|). The exponent equality follows from m=t-j. For j=t the product cutoff is automatic and the term is exactly (sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t, bounded by D^t. This last cancellation must not be replaced by Y^t. Every sign and overlap remains; real floors and empty initial intervals cause no error.

The resulting recurrence is

    C_1<=D,
    C_t<=D^t+sum_(m=1)^(t-1)binom(t,m)C_m(Dm)^(t-m).

Induction gives C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2: after division by this proposed bound and j=t-m, each summand is <=2^-j/j!, since m!m^j<=t!. Their sum is <e^(1/2)-1, and the remaining D^t ratio leaves a strict margin for t>=2. This is a valid explicit upper bound, not an optimality claim.

### 4.2 Exact squarefree Euler correction and all p shifts

On Re s>1 the literal f_t has Euler product

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.       (4.4)

The product is over primes. Each local polynomial has constant one and zero linear term. Its coefficients g_t therefore satisfy

    Gabs_t(sigma):=sum_n|g_t(n)|n^-sigma<infinity
                                      for every sigma>1/2, (4.5)

for each fixed t. This follows from the absolutely convergent product of the finite local absolute polynomials; ramified local factors are one. No nonvanishing claim about G_t is needed or implied.

For 1<=t<=J the exact coefficient identity is

    v_(p,J)*f_t=b_p^(*t)*v_(p,J-t)*g_t.                   (4.6)

This retains a COMMON filter on the left. It follows from Q_p^t*chi^(*t)=b_p^(*t); it is not a subtraction of estimates obtained with different filters. For t=0 the source is the finite sequence v_(p,J).

Take sigma>1/2 with sigma>=beta_t:=1-1/t. On every real x, (4.2), (4.5) and (4.6) give

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*f_t)(n)|
      <= C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma.    (4.7)

To justify every endpoint, sum only over p^a d<=x, use the bound at y=x/(p^a d)>=1, and replace y^beta_t by y^sigma. The finite shifts have weights binom(J-t,a)p^a and arguments x/p^a, giving exactly the displayed factor. Terms whose argument is below one are empty, not approximated. At t>=3 choose sigma=beta_t>1/2; at t=1,2 choose sigma=1/2+epsilon. This proves the author's individual-color bound and preserves all dependence on fixed J,p,q.

Define a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu^2(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k), k>=1. Finite differences give

    a_k=sum_(t=0)^k(-1)^(k-t)binom(k,t)f_t.

Summing (-1)^k for k<=J gives the exact low-chain combination

    L_J:=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.              (4.8)

Equations (4.7)-(4.8) prove the author's complete common-filter estimate

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_(p,J)*L_J)(n)|
         <<_(p,q,J,epsilon)x^(max(1/2,1-1/J)+epsilon).     (4.9)

It includes every first-J chain sector and every compensator term for all real x. It is a genuine arithmetic estimate, including principal characters; it is not an estimate of an arbitrarily selected signed subsource.

### 4.3 Explicit growth is accounted for but gives no growing-J theorem

The local coefficient c_(t,a) of (1+tz)(1-z)^t obeys

    |c_(t,a)|<=t^a(1/a!+1/(a-1)!), a>=2.

For fixed 1/2<sigma<1, split primes at Y=t^(1/sigma). The tail local logarithm is O(t^2 l^-2sigma), with a universal constant because t l^-sigma<1. Summing over all integers beyond Y costs O_sigma(t^(1/sigma)). On l<=Y, the absolute local polynomial is bounded by (1+t l^-sigma)(1+l^-sigma)^t. Summing its logarithm over all integers up to Y proves

    log Gabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t).          (4.10)

Together with C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)^2 and (4.7), this confirms the author's explicit upper price, including all p shifts, all binomial coefficients in (4.8), and the t=0 bound (J+1)(1+p)^J. The condition sigma>=1-1/t must remain: a fixed target sigma cannot be used in (4.7) for arbitrarily large t. The factorial/Euler constants may also grow rapidly. These are failures of the available upper budget, not lower-bound impossibility theorems for a better growing-color argument.

## 3. The actual witness contract

PR9 Lemma1W, paper lines 298--342, chooses a cutoff `t_* in [1,3/2]`
before witnesses. For a nonfloor zero bin it produces one presentation,
one real power and a common height for the inverse/plain pair, and dyadic
length exponents satisfying

\[
 r\le t_*+O(\epsilon),\quad r+m\ge t_*-O(\epsilon),
 \quad 0\le m\le1/2+O(\epsilon),
\]
\[
 |M|^2\gg U^{\delta r-O(\epsilon)},\qquad
 |S|^2\gg U^{\delta m-O(\epsilon)}.
\]

The source's saturation step explicitly uses only `delta >= 1/50`, not
`delta >= .7`. The inverse cutoff is inserted before dyadic selection.
At an actual zero the unit contribution of the Gamma detector forces a
product spike; the two pointwise upper bounds then separately force both
spikes and `m<=1/2+O(epsilon)`. The smooth product separation and tails
are taken with fixed derivative orders, and the cutoff profile derivatives
are uniformly controlled on the same annulus. This is not a separate
row-dependent truncation inside a moment.

The actual theorem `actual_supported_witness_family`, lines 17--30 of
`DetectorSupportedWitness.lean`, is more precise. Fix

\[
 0<d_{min}\le d_{max},\quad 0<\tau<d_{min}/2,
 \quad4\tau<d_{min}\eta,
\]
\[
 \epsilon>0,\quad0<e<1/1000,\quad0<\kappa\le1,
 \quad\eta\ge0,
 \quad288e+8\kappa+2\eta\le\epsilon/2,
\]

and a finite bin bound `I`. It gives `Z0` BEFORE `Z`, every
`d in [d_min,d_max]`, the row type, finite label type, characters, `a`, bin
index and cutoff. The character family must be nonprincipal at every label;
every natural modulus must be at most `Z^d`. The remaining hypotheses are

\[
 i\le I,\quad51/100<a\le1,
\]
\[
 M(3(i+1)Z^\tau)<a+2e,
 \qquad a\le M(3iZ^\tau),\qquad1\le t_*\le3/2.
\]

The result is a supported witness for every row. For application one takes
the row type to be the nonexceptional rows under consideration (or their
subtype); one does not assert nonprincipality or witnesses on the removed
principal rows. The source allows arbitrary finite labels, independently
of later arithmetic source labels.

`WitnessRows.lean` gives, with `U=Z^d`, a chosen label, an actual zero
`L(chi_label,rho)=0`, `rho.re>=a`, `|rho.im|<=3i Z^tau`, two dyadic
indices, and `|nu|<=U^(tau/(2d_max))`. The common witness frequency is

\[
 h_u=2\pi\nu_u-\Im\rho_u,
 \qquad |h_u|\le2\pi U^{\tau/(2d_{max})}+3iZ^\tau.
\]

The two polynomials in a witness share this frequency and `rho.re`.
Different rows need not share either value; the moment count uses its
rowwise/Sobolev bounds. None of these frequencies is identified with an
independent physical source height.

The support theorem gives exact tolerances

\[
 t_*-r-\epsilon\le m,
 \quad r\le t_*+\epsilon,
 \quad0\le m\le1/2+75\epsilon,
 \quad r\ge t_*-1/2-76\epsilon,
\]

and each spike loses `2 epsilon`. Within fixed dyadic indices the base
profiles are common: the inverse profile is the fixed positive annular
profile times its fixed cutoff at `U^t_*`; the plain profile is fixed.
Their real powers remain in `[0,1]` since actual zeros have real part at
most one. The finite smooth orders and polynomial height degree are
available before the later live height and scale variables.

For clarity about paper versus formal coordinates: the paper's coarse bin
description uses geometric heights `3^i T`; the actual theorem and PR15
density assembly use `3iT` and `3(i+1)T`. The latter exact buffered-bin
theorem is what this reconstruction uses. Both give finitely many bins;
their notations should not be mixed in a claimed literal application.

`DetectorZeros.exists_actual_buffered_bin`, lines 134--156, requires
`T>2`, `e>0`, an integer `n>0` with `49/100<=ne`, and returns
`1<=i<=n`, `b=51/100+ek`, the two strict upper maxima, the lower
maximum, and the zero-free buffered disk for every family label. The
fallback is `51/100`. For a counted zero with real part at least
`a>=33/40`, monotonicity yields `b>a-e`; hence with `e<1/1000`
the fallback cannot be selected. Maximum attainment supplies a genuine
zero. No artificial zero or floor population is used as a witness.

The underlying saturation theorem still uses only `51/100<=b<=1`.
It requires `(3+(3i+2)Z^tau)^4 <= (Z^d)^eta` and enough Fourier
allowance; the strict inequalities above imply both beyond a common
threshold. The Gamma detector's terminal and frequency tails have fixed
polynomial growth paid by sufficiently large fixed decay orders. Lowering
`b` to above `.824` stays inside all these closed real-power/strip ranges.
The small auxiliary `kappa` here is not the physical endpoint's capacity
parameter or the proposed split `k`.

## 6. The complementary analytic term is really small

Although D11 is stated directly for the determinant field, D7 helps calibrate what is and is not gained. Write e_chi,delta for the Dirichlet coefficients of E_delta. For delta in I,

    |e_chi,delta(n)| <=4 d_3(n)n^(-delta),
    sum_n |e_chi,delta(n)| n^(-4/5-epsilon)
                                      <=4 zeta(1+epsilon)^3. (D12)

Each product in E has three factors, the least of its shifts is at least delta, and |mu chi|<=1; this proves the first bound, including its multiplicity 1+2+1. Since delta>=1/5, it proves the second uniformly. Therefore its Gaussian physical field obeys

    |E_chi,delta^g(x)| <<_(epsilon,tau) x^(4/5+epsilon)   (D13)

on all positive x after adjusting a fixed constant; the left tail is better. This uses g_tau(v)<=C_(tau,sigma) exp(-sigma v), with sigma=4/5+epsilon, and the D12 weighted coefficient norm. All three signed complementary fields are paid together, not deleted singly by an unproved cancellation.

The cofactor coefficients are absolutely summable with weight r^(-beta), uniformly for delta in I, whenever beta>3/5. D8 and its majorant prove this because beta+2delta>1. Thus the inherited Mertens calibration beta=.8749 gives

    H_chi,delta(x) <<_(chi,epsilon,tau) x^(beta+epsilon)  (D14)

if the corresponding accepted character Mertens bound is supplied. For zeta the current proof supplies that calibration explicitly. D14 is a comparison, not an improvement. The limiting accepted exponent is beta_0=1-c_G=.8748866 with any fixed positive buffer. The required arithmetic gain below remains genuine.

statement:
## G228. The sharp depth of a low-omega-completed inverse column

Fix 0<beta<1. For 1<=T<=beta N and an integer k>=0 define

    F_(T,k)(d)=1_(d<=T OR omega(d)<=k),
    z=E^-T (chi(d) F_(T,k)(d))_d.

The first row of E^-T is mu(d), and multiplying by A_chi cancels chi against
its conjugate. Using sum_(d|a)mu(d)=1_(a=1) gives the exact identities

    z1=sum_(d in S_N)mu(d)chi(d) F_(T,k)(d),
    r(a)=sum_(d|a,d>T,omega(d)>k)mu(d).                     (228.1)

If omega(a)=k+1 and a>T, all proper divisors are included, so r(a)=mu(a).
For a>N/2 its cofactor observation is exactly R_N(a)=chi(a).
Let b_k be the product of the first k primes not dividing q, b_0=1, and put
alpha=max(beta,1/2). Every prime p in (alpha N/b_k,N/b_k] not dividing b_k q
gives a distinct actual coordinate a=b_k p with |R_N(a)r(a)|=1. Thus

    B_N(z)<=W_N(z),
    B_N(z)>=#{alpha N/b_k<p<=N/b_k : p prime, p not|b_k q}. (228.2)

The second line is an exact finite inequality, possibly zero for small N.
For fixed k, the ordinary prime number theorem gives the lower asymptotic
(1-alpha)N/(b_k log N). Correcting primes, semiprimes or any other fixed number
of omega layers has not made this absolute residual small at any exponent<1.

There is also a matching upper bound for growing depth. Set h=k+1,
H_N=sum_(m<=N)1/m and A_N=sum_(p<=N)1/p, including conductor primes if desired.
Taking the absolute value in (228.1) and exchanging the finite divisor sums,

    W_N(z)<=N H_N sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)>=h)1/d
           <=N H_N sum_(j>=h) A_N^j/j!
           <=N H_N exp(A_N) A_N^h/h!.                     (228.3)

An unordered j-prime set occurs j! times in A_N^j. Admitting repeated primes
and products above N only enlarges the positive sum. The last inequality
uses (h+r)!>=h!r!. This pays EVERY residual coordinate and is uniform in T.

Ordinary PNT and partial summation give p_j~j log j and A_N=O(loglog N).
The [NIST reference](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records the prime asymptotics;
the consequences here are derived from them. Removing fixed q's finitely
many primes changes indices by a bounded amount, so log b_k~k log k as k grows.
If k~kappa log N/loglog N for fixed 0<kappa<1, then
b_k=N^(kappa+o(1)), while its largest prime is O(log N). The prime interval
in (228.2) lies above all these factors eventually; its endpoint is
N^(1-kappa+o(1)). PNT on a fixed-ratio interval, together with (228.3) and
log(h!)=h log h-h+O(log h), proves

    B_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)),  W_N(z)=N^(1-kappa+o(1)).      (228.4)

These are logarithmic exponents, uniform for 1<=T<=beta N, not fixed-k
logarithmic asymptotic formulas. If k=o(log N/loglog N), both exponents are1.

More generally fix ONE sequence k_N>=0 and ONE cutoff sequence
1<=T_N<=beta N for all sufficiently large N, independently of epsilon. For 0<gamma<1,

    B_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff W_N(z_N)<<_epsilon N^(gamma+epsilon) for EVERY epsilon>0
    iff liminf_N k_N loglog N/log N >= 1-gamma.             (228.5)

For sufficiency, bound the nonnegative tail in (228.3) at any smaller depth
a log N/loglog N with 0<a<1-gamma and then let a approach1-gamma according
to epsilon. For necessity, if the liminf is smaller, choose such an a above
it. Along infinitely many N the primorial is at most N^(a+o(1)), so (228.2)
has exponent at least1-a, contradicting a sufficiently small fixed epsilon.
No short-interval or growing-modulus prime theorem is used.

Equality in (228.5) is sufficient for the residual bill alone. It does not
pay z1. In fact, with D_N the number of omitted coefficients,

    z1=M_chi(N)-sum_(d in S_N,d>T,omega(d)>=h)mu(d)chi(d),
    D_N<=sum_(n<=N)binom(omega(n),h)
        =sum_(d<=N,d squarefree,omega(d)=h)floor(N/d)
        <=N A_N^h/h!.                                    (228.6)

Once (228.5) holds, the every-epsilon exponent-gamma estimate on z1 is
equivalent to that on M_chi(N). The retained coordinate still carries the
arithmetic problem. At the c11 benchmark the residual's threshold is
liminf k_N loglog N/log N >= .1251459636; the full certificate is still open.

The lower bounds concern COMPLETE ABSOLUTE bills of this SPECIFIC column
family. They do not lower-bound the complete signed residual, Mertens sum,
any arbitrary approximant or a Gaussian energy. Higher residual layers need
not have a common sign: for k=1,T=11,a=30, r(30)=mu(15)+mu(30)=0.

The ancestry is the first-unpaid-layer argument in W43/[research revision] and [research revision]'s
fixed-layer circle obstruction. W43's Newton defect includes prime powers
and factorial multiplicities; at T=1,k=1 its order-two defect at pq is2,
where (228.1) is1. G78/G83-G85 already paid their own growing-order Gaussian
restoration, so that older obligation is not reopened. The new scoped result
is the cofactor certificate's exact depth threshold and its remaining z1
obligation, rather than a new generic lesson about truncation.

statement:
### T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

Let \(P_r(y)\) be the exact [research revision] Z13–Z15 triple convolution, including equal-element projection, fixed good sectors, and all cube/core overlaps. For \(5/6<a<1\), suppose
\[
\int_Y^{2Y}\int_1^2|P_r(y)|^2\,dr\,\frac{dy}{y}
\ll_\epsilon Y^{\,2(3-2a)-\epsilon} \tag{T09.3}
\]
for every sufficiently small dyadic \(Y\) and every \(\epsilon>0\). Then \(\zeta_K^S\), and hence \(\zeta\), is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

Take \(H=L^2([1,2],dr)\) and \(P(y)=(P_r(y))_r\). Cauchy gives, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\),
\[
\left\|\int_Y^{2Y}P(y)y^{2s-3}\frac{dy}{y}\right\|_H
\ll Y^{2(\Re s-a)-\epsilon/2}.
\]
Choose \(\epsilon<4\delta\). The Bochner Mellin integral is holomorphic; large \(y\) decays exponentially uniformly on the compact \(r\)-interval. Initially its exact value is
\[
J_\bullet(s)
\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})}{\zeta_K^S(s)},
\quad
J_r(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{2s}K_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2
K_{1/3}(\kappa rt)\,dt.
\]
For fixed \(\Re s>0\), \(r\mapsto J_r(s)\) is analytic on \(r>0\). [research revision] Z16 proves a nonzero gamma-product limit for \(r^{1/3}J_r(s)\) as \(r\downarrow0\). Therefore \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on \([1,2]\); its \(H\)-norm is positive. The angular numerator is nonzero because \(3\Re s-3/2>1\). Continue the identity after multiplication by \((s-1)\zeta_K^S(s)\), and evaluate at a hypothetical zero. The right side is a nonzero vector, contradiction.

This removes the need for estimates uniform as \(r\to0\) or an individual zero-free kernel \(J_1\). It does not supply the arithmetic decay. At \(a=.87449\), the squared \(Y\)-exponent is \(2.50204\); \(N=Y^{-2}\) is a different scale.

**Sources:** BB R06–R07; [research revision] V1–V10; [research revision] Z13–Z18.
title: T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

statement:
## 4. Exact two-factor completion with alternating restoration

Fix kappa0>0 with eta+kappa0<1, and let

\[
 Y=\left\lfloor X^{(1-\eta-\kappa_0)/2}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad \mu_{\le Y}(n)=\mu(n)\mathbf1_{n\le Y}.
 \tag{DP20}
\]

The elementary convolution identity

\[
 \mu=2\mu_{\le Y}-\mu_{\le Y}*\mu_{\le Y}*\mathbf1
                         +\mu_{>Y}*\mu_{>Y}*\mathbf1
 \tag{DP21}
\]

follows by expanding (mu-mu_leY)^2*1 and using mu*1=e_1. Convolve with kappa. The new unrestricted factor is the exact periodic sequence

\[
 b=\kappa*\mathbf1,
 \qquad b(\ell)=1-2\mathbf1_{2\mid\ell}=(-1)^{\ell+1}.
 \tag{DP22}
\]

Thus no new random sign or arbitrary bounded coefficient has been inserted. Its period-two mean is zero.

Extend V_delta as a smooth compactly supported function on the real line by zero on nonpositive arguments. For any fixed integer B>=2,

\[
 |\widehat V_\delta(\xi)|
 \le C_B(1+\delta|\xi|)^{-B}.
 \tag{DP23}
\]

This follows from the L1 bound on V_delta and the bound C_B delta^{-B} on the L1 norm of its B-th derivative, with delta<=delta0. Alternating Poisson summation, with the zero extension causing no endpoint terms, gives for 0<t<=delta

\[
 \left|\sum_{\ell\ge1}b(\ell)V_\delta(\ell t)\right|
 \le C_Bt^{-1}(t/\delta)^B.
 \tag{DP24}
\]

There is no zero dual frequency: the dual frequencies are the half-integers divided by t. DP23 sums absolutely over them for B>=2. This is the precise removal of the Type I main term.

On x in [e^{-1}X,2eX], the term 2*kappa*mu_leY has support n<=2Y, eventually outside the narrow profile. For d,e<=Y, t=de/x satisfies t/delta_X<=C X^{-kappa0}. Consequently, for every fixed B,

\[
 \sum_{d,e\le Y}
 \left|\sum_{\ell\ge1}b(\ell)V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)\right|
 \le C_B X\left(CX^{-\kappa_0}\right)^B(\log(2Y))^2.
 \tag{DP25}
\]

Choose B after the requested error power, before X and all labels. Combining DP21--25 proves for every R>0

\[
 \boxed{F_{A,\delta_X}(x)
 =\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
       \sum_{\ell\ge1}(-1)^{\ell+1}
                       V_{\delta_X}(\ell de/x)
       +O_R(X^{-R}).}
 \tag{DP26}
\]

This holds uniformly across the entire enlarged shell at its single frozen width. All sums are finite on the kernel support. Their exact ranges imply

\[
 d,e\ll X/Y\asymp X^{(1+\eta+\kappa_0)/2},
 \qquad \ell\ll X/Y^2\asymp X^{\eta+\kappa_0}.
 \tag{DP27}
\]

The floors cause only fixed constants for large X. Both original ordered factor placements remain; neither d and e nor any restoration labels are identified. Repeated primes, shared primes, squarefree zeros and alternating signs remain exactly those of DP26. No conductor, height or primitive-character bound is invoked.

statement:
## 6. Signed Taylor completion; proof of the negative main term

Take W=delta L. For |w|<=W and r<=R, the arguments in ([research revision]) obey

    log x+w-log r >= (1-2delta)L > 2rho_1 L.

All derivatives up to order three of phi_t on this corridor satisfy

    |phi_t^(j)(a)|<=C_(rho_0,rho_1,j)L^(-1-j).       ([research revision])

This follows directly by scaling a=L u, t=L rho; the scaled compact
corridor stays a fixed positive distance above u=2rho. The original
cutoff definition phi=0 below 2t is not analytically continued across
its boundary.

Globally phi_t(a), defined by ([research revision]) and zero below 2t, is bounded by
C/t. Therefore the WHOLE discarded |w|>W portion of ([research revision]), even after
the absolute harmonic core sum, is bounded by a fixed power of X,L
times `exp(-c_(delta,tau)L^2)`. This pays both Gaussian ends before
the Taylor argument and does not extend a rational denominator across
a pole or a support boundary.

Set A=log x+w and v=log r in the retained integral. Write

    phi_t(A-v)=phi_t(A)-v phi_t'(A)
                  +(v^2/2)phi_t''(A)+e_A(v).

On 0<=v<=log R, Taylor's theorem and ([research revision]) give

    |e_A(v)|<=C v^3/L^4,
    |e_A'(v)|<=C v^2/L^4.                           ([research revision])

It would be WRONG to sum this error using `sum |f(r)|/r`; that would
erase the useful cancellation. Apply Abel summation instead:

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)e_A(log r)/r
      = A_f(R)e_A(log R)/R
        -integral_1^R A_f(u)
             [e_A'(log u)-e_A(log u)]du/u^2.         ([research revision])

Both the endpoint and the integral are `O_(beta)(L^(-4))`, since
`sup_(v>=0) exp(-(1-beta)v)v^3` and
`integral_0^infinity exp(-(1-beta)v)(v^2+v^3)dv` are finite.
This is uniform in w,rho in the retained corridor. This second signed
Abel step, not a positive Taylor estimate, is essential.

Complete the three polynomial moments before evaluating them. Equation
(C7) gives, for each fixed j=0,1,2,

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)(log r)^j/r|
       <= C_(beta,j) R^(beta-1)[1+(log R)^j].        ([research revision])

After multiplication by phi_t^(j), their combined error is at most
`C R^(beta-1)/L`. Inserting the exact moments ([research revision]), the j=0 and j=1
terms vanish and the surviving term is

    sum_(r<=R) f(r)/r phi_t(A-log r)
       = C_f phi_t''(A)+O(L^(-4)+R^(beta-1)/L).      ([research revision])

The positive 2C_f second moment meets the NEGATIVE curvature of the
actual two-prime density. There is no independent-sign premise and no
use of an unknown full energy in this cancellation.

Finally the tilted Gaussian has exact mass exp(tau/2) and finite first
absolute moment. Since log x=L+O(1) and phi_t''' is O(L^(-4)), ([research revision])
and the already paid tails imply

    integral_(-W)^W exp(w)g(w)phi_t''(log x+w)dw
       =exp(tau/2)phi_t''(L)+O_tau(L^(-4)).          ([research revision])

Direct differentiation gives

    phi_t''(A)=2log((A-t)/t)/A^3
                   -2/[A^2(A-t)]-1/[A(A-t)^2],
    phi_(rho L)''(L)=L^(-3)B(rho).                  ([research revision])

Equations ([research revision]), ([research revision])--([research revision]) prove (C3), with every core, prime power,
prime diagonal, sharp endpoint and Gaussian end accounted for.

Here is the complete error ledger, before convenient absorption:

| Source | Uniform field cost |
| --- | --- |
| Actual/completed source above U<z^3 | O_A(X^(-A)) for any fixed A |
| All signed cores r>R | O(X^(1-kappa)L) |
| Prime-pair p=q diagonal | O(X/z) |
| Both PNT replacements, N=8 fixed | O(X/L^6) |
| Full omitted tilted-Gaussian ends | O_A(X^(-A)) |
| Signed Taylor remainder | O(X/L^4) |
| Three signed moment completions | O(X^(1-kappa)/L) |
| Frozen-shell/tilted-Gaussian replacement | O(X/L^4) |

All constants are allowed to depend on the fixed compact rho interval,
tau,beta and the fixed accepted PNT constant. This ledger contains no
growing-order estimate or unsupported limit interchange.

## 8. Exact whole-rectangle proof and feedback

On the full closed rectangle 0<=delta<=3/4, 0<=p<=1/2 put

    D=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*), P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
    V=5/6-delta, J=VD+delta P,
    R=1-delta+delta P V/(2J), q=delta p.

V>=1/12, D>=D(1/2), P>=0 and J>=924595/5398056>1/10. The complete original w-inversion yields, for d>=1/2>y,

    G(d,c)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell delta p
      +d(1/4+3R/4-17/50)-delta p(2y-d)/(2c).

Below 1/2 the old term is -q min(d,2y-d)/(12kappa_*). Only the physical selection term changes with C; R stays the original detector.

For fixed d,c and saving v the positive-denominator numerator is

    N=J[theta-v-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2-ell delta p
          -d(1/4-17/50)+delta p(2y-d)/(2c)]
       -(3d/4)[(1-delta)J+delta P V/2].

J has degree <=(1,2), so N has degree <=(2,3) in (delta,p). On each rational rectangle its values at the 3 by 4 rational interpolation nodes uniquely determine it. Inverting the degree-2 and degree-3 Bernstein evaluation matrices reconstructs twelve coefficients exactly. Since that basis is nonnegative and sums to one, positive coefficients prove N>0 on the entire closed rectangle. This is an exact polynomial identity, not sampled positivity.

The independent helper reconstructs every coefficient and matches every author leaf minimum/maximum. Exact rational cell coverage checks each interior cell once; boundaries follow by closure. Results:

| Row d | Capacity | Saving | Leaves | Minimum Bernstein coefficient |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| h | 546/125 | 1/1000000 | 8 | 18050491532909813/30180747018240000000000 |
| h-.001 | 6kappa_* | 1/100000 | 6 | 373569162511014355403/1554080457553920000000000 |
| 1/2 | 6kappa_* | 1/1000 | 1 | 15701185574521824157763/303531339366000000000000 |

All 180 coefficients are strictly positive; all leaf boxes and exact bounds are in `receipt.json`. The denominator is positive, so these are bounds for the original G.

The old G is affine in d on [1/2,d_-], covered by its two certificates. At d_- the local G is no larger, since C<6kappa_* and 2y-d_->0. Local affinity covers [d_-,h]. A positive d-slope at most 2 pays the extension to d_+=h+10^-10, leaving saving 4999/5000000000. On [d0,1/2] the old G is convex because min(d,2y-d) is concave and its coefficient is nonpositive. Combine its half-row certificate with

    theta-[7/8-49h/150+7ell/8+33d0/50]
      =82211536363/750000000000>1/10.

Floor classes have saving theta-[.51+h/3+.51ell]=224106013/15000000000>1/100, with room for the extension; they need no detector zero above the floor sentinel.

For the contradiction set mu=beta_*-theta>0, kappa=2beta_*-1. Then kappa<=3/4 and kappa-kappa_*=2mu. The source derivative bounds partial_kappa c_kappa<=1/18 and partial_c R<=5/12 give

    partial_kappa G_C <=(3/4)d_+(5/12)(1/18)
      =317579039/23040000000<1/50.

Old rows also have changing reciprocal capacity. Its full derivative is

    partial_kappa G_old<=5/288+(3/8)(1/2)/(12(.7)^2)
      =695/14112<1/8.

Savings below beta_* therefore exceed the fixed certificates by at least 24mu/25 locally and 3mu/4 on old rows. The atlas is kappa-independent. This pays feedback through both capacities; kappa is not frozen at kappa_* in the actual contradiction argument.

statement:
## 6. Preserved failed draws28 and21

### 6.1 Complete rough feedback defeats this absolute small-gain proposal

Take y>=2, m_y(1)=1, m_y(n)=mu(n)chi(n)1_(Pplus(n)<=y), and l(n)=chi(n). Exact convolution gives

    e_y=delta1-l*m_y
       =-chi(n)1_(n>1,Pminus(n)>y).                    (28)

All valuations are included. For every finite y, its absolute coefficient norm diverges at sigma<=1, already on primes not dividing q. One elementary proof of sum_p1/p=infinity is that otherwise the finite Euler products product_(p<=y)(1-1/p)^-1 would remain bounded, although they eventually dominate every finite harmonic sum. Deleting finitely many primes does not change divergence. Therefore ||e_y||_sigma<1 cannot hold at sigma=.87486, even if y grows with a shell parameter: for each finite y, the complete norm still diverges. This rejects only this absolute convolution norm; the Gaussian readout itself converges and could enjoy signed cancellation.

Put u(n)=mu(n)chi(n), a pointwise product. For finite K>=1 the coefficient identity, with * denoting Dirichlet convolution, is

    u=m_y*(delta1+e_y+...+e_y^(*(K-1)))
                                          +u*e_y^(*K). (29)

Writing E_y(s)=1-L(s,chi)M_y(s), the first term has transform

    V_K(s)=M_y(s)sum_(j=0)^(K-1)E_y(s)^j
          =(1-E_y(s)^K)/L(s,chi).                     (30)

At a hypothetical L-zero rho, E_y(rho)=1. V_K is holomorphic there while E_y^K/L retains the reciprocal pole. A small approximant is not a smaller zero detector. These are the same exact rough-defect/finite-feedback obstructions already accepted in W44 and the earlier Newton work. The test is retained as a selected duplicate, not rerolled or credited as a fresh barrier.

### 6.2 The full Gaussian observable is not a positive-real impedance

The initially proposed direct impedance would need a positive-real observable, in particular a nonnegative real part on its intended right half-plane. The standard finite-dimensional rational positive-real definition and its realization conditions were checked against Timothy H. Hughes, *A theory of passive linear systems with no assumptions*, arXiv1611.06140v3, Section2/Lemma1. This citation fixes the meaning of the proposal; no rational realization theorem is being imported for an infinite Dirichlet series. [Primary source](https://arxiv.org/html/1611.06140v3#S2).

The literal untwisted canonical prime2 factor (1-2*2^-s)/(1-2^-s) is negative at real0<s<1. That alone rejects a factorwise claim that each source factor is positive-real on the target strip; it is not a statement about the full product there.

A decisive COMPLETE-field test needs no unproved zero-free premise. At Re(s)>1 let D(s)=sum_n f3(n)chi(n)n^-s, so Mellin(F)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)D(s). Because the coefficient of1 is1 and all coefficients have modulus<=1,

    Re D(4+it)>=1-sum_(n>=2)n^-4>=2/3.                (31)

The last bound follows by integral comparison from1 to infinity. Set t=pi/(4tau). Then the Gaussian phase is exp(i*tau*4*t)=-1, and

    Re Mellin(F)(4+i*pi/(4tau))
       <=-(2/3)exp(8tau-pi^2/(32tau))<0.              (32)

This holds for every fixed tau>0 and every ordinary character including its zeros. The same certificate applies to B and U. Thus none of these full fixed Gaussian Mellin transforms is positive-real on a half-plane containing that point, including any proposed Re(s)>gamma with gamma<1. A Laplacian/dissipation certificate for this literal direct observable cannot be obtained merely from a passive-network interpretation.

Stripping the Gaussian, changing the readout, using a vector impedance, or a different supply rate changes the proposal and needs its own quantitative return. Those alternatives are not disproved. The test gives no lower bound for the physical field and no statement that all passive approaches to L-functions are impossible. The full-field sign certificate is self-contained; the unsuccessful oversized MIT PDF fetch is retained only as retrieval history, not supporting evidence.

statement:
## 3. Development15: a growing inverse with uniform Gaussian restoration

This is the protected highest-reach development. It uses the formal inverse
and strict support gate already established by AH12/AH20 and [research revision]-W2. The
added statement is a uniform coefficient envelope for ALL depths, an
explicit moving-depth Gaussian tail, and a return to the SAME fixed U.
The finite absolute-strip contraction proposed in the original card fails.

### 3.1 The known absolute-norm failure

For any nonzero fixed finite Dirichlet polynomial M with least nonzero
coefficient m(d0), let r=delta-l_chi*m, where l_chi(n)=chi(n). If p exceeds
the support of m and p does not divide q, the only supported nonzero
divisor contribution to r(d0 p) is d0. Hence

    r(d0 p)=-m(d0)chi(p).

The absolute weighted residual norm diverges for sigma<=1. Indeed the
prime harmonic series diverges: if sum_p 1/p converged, the products
product_(p<=P)(1-1/p)^-1 would be bounded, although their positive
expansions eventually contain every finite harmonic partial sum. Removing
finitely many primes does not fix divergence, and p^-sigma>=p^-1 for
sigma<=1. This is the established W29 obstruction, now read in its exact
scope. It does not lower-bound a signed Gaussian output or prohibit
an algebra at a different exponent.

### 3.2 Fixed b>1 pays every growing-depth coefficient constant

Let `||a||_b=sum_n |a(n)|n^-b`. Dirichlet convolution is a Banach algebra
in this norm by absolutely convergent rearrangement. Fix ANY b>1. Choose
one fixed integer Y>=2 large enough that

    eta := zeta(b) Y^(1-b)/(b-1) < 1.                          (6)

This choice is independent of X, the depth, and chi. Define

    m_Y(n)=mu(n)chi(n)1_(n<=Y),
    d_Y=delta-l_chi*m_Y,
    Q_k=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^(*(k-1))), k>=1.                (7)

Because l_chi*(mu chi)=delta and the tail of mu chi starts above Y,

    d_Y=l_chi*((mu chi)1_(n>Y)),
    ||d_Y||_b <= zeta(b) sum_(n>Y)n^-b <= eta,
    ||Q_k||_b <= zeta(b)/(1-eta),                             (8)

uniformly in k. Every character zero, every multiplicity and every signed
Dirichlet convolution in (7) is literal. The estimate uses b>1 only;
it does not assert contraction at the prospective zero-free boundary.

Exact telescoping in the arithmetic-function ring gives

    delta-l_chi*Q_k=d_Y^(*k),
    mu chi-Q_k=(mu chi)*d_Y^(*k),
    d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y,
    (mu chi-Q_k)(n)=0 for n<(Y+1)^k.                          (9)

All coefficient operations at a fixed integer are finite. In particular

    ||mu chi-Q_k||_b <= zeta(b)(1+1/(1-eta)) =: B_b.          (10)

The stronger bound zeta(b)eta^k is also valid but is not needed. Keeping
the deliberately coarse constant (10) makes the tail argument independent
of how far a Newton depth overshoots its requested threshold.

### 3.3 Complete physical-shell restoration

Fix C>0 and set

    N_X=2X exp(C sqrt(log X)),
    k_X=floor(log(N_X)/log(Y+1))+1.                           (11)

Then `(Y+1)^k_X>N_X`, including exact-power endpoints. One may instead
take the least power of two k>=k_X; the same proof holds. The iterates

    P_0=m_Y, P_(r+1)=2P_r-l_chi*P_r*P_r

are exactly Q_(2^r), so only O(loglog X) algebraic stages are needed.
This is a stage count, not a bound on arithmetic computation cost.

Let

    V_X(y)=sum_n Q_(k_X)(n)g_tau(log n-y).                    (12)

This is a moving approximation, not a new fixed Mellin detector. From
(9)-(10), for x=exp(y) in [X,2X] and large X,

    |U(log x)-V_X(log x)|
      <= B_b sup_(n>=N_X) n^b g_tau(log(n/x))
      <= C_(b,tau,Y) X^b
         exp(-(C sqrt(log X)-b tau)^2/(2tau))
      = X^(b-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)).                              (13)

In the second line complete the square in `b v-v^2/(2tau)`; its maximum
over v>=C sqrt(log X) is at the endpoint once that endpoint exceeds b tau.
This pays the ENTIRE tail, not only the defect d_Y^k. The same supremum
argument proves local convergence of every field in (12). Constants do
not grow with depth. Shell L2 error costs only sqrt(log2).

Therefore for any fixed gamma>0, the hypothesis

    ||V_X||_(L2(log X,log(2X))) <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
    for EVERY sufficiently large dyadic X and EVERY epsilon>0,          (14)

with `b-C^2/(2tau)<gamma`, implies the identical complete-shell exponent
for the original fixed U. Its left Gaussian tail and reciprocal Mellin
identity then exclude all zeros of this fixed L(s,chi) with Re(s)>gamma
(in the target strip), exactly as for the supplied reciprocal detector.
No pole signal is assigned to an individual P_r or V_X. At an L-zero a
finite inverse polynomial is regular; this is fully consistent with the
argument, which restores U uniformly on all large physical shells first.

Conversely an original bound for U implies (14) under the same tail gate.
Thus this is an exponent-equivalent target, not a proof that finite inverse
depth improves cancellation. It is nevertheless a complete answer to the
uniform growing-depth/tail/zero-signal obligations for this particular
family. Fixed-k rough-sector lower bounds do not apply uniformly to this
growing k, nor are they contradicted by (13).

The coarsest sufficient tail budget approaches

    C^2/(2tau)>1-gamma,                                     (15)

by choosing fixed b>1 as close to1 as desired and then a sufficiently
large FIXED Y satisfying (6). It need not optimize eta or use the stronger
eta^k. For a concrete near gain gamma=.874860, b=1.001 and
`C^2/(2tau)=.127` give error exponent .874<gamma. The corresponding
complete arithmetic target (14) is OPEN. At gamma=5/6 or3/4, the same
b requires respectively tail ratios greater than .167666... or .251.
Those statements are conditional targets for c=1/6 and1/4, not results.

First decisive remaining action: estimate the entire SIGNED polynomial
output (12) at one of these exponents, keeping all inverse powers together.
No absolute sum of the k pieces, prime-only sector, or finite list of X
values supplies (14). Truncating (12) to its exact prefix simply recomputes
the original Mobius detector there; no algorithmic speedup is claimed.

A deliberately coarse concrete instance avoids any enormous initial
preconditioner: take b=2 and Y=4. Integral comparison gives zeta(2)<2,
so eta=zeta(2)/4<1/2, `||Q_k||_2<4`, and the coefficient-error norm in
(10) is <6 for ALL k and ALL ordinary chi. With C=sqrt(3tau), (13) is
`X^(1/2+o(1))`. Thus the single family generated from the literal four-term
Mobius prefix, at depths exceeding
`log(2X exp(sqrt(3tau log X)))/log5`, has a fully paid restoration to U
at every prospective gamma>1/2. The arithmetic hypothesis (14) for this
simple family remains exactly the unresolved part. This explicit uniform
instance is preferable to a claimed small-gain norm below1.

## G200. Complete weighted removal and the fourth paid class

For a fixed extracted ideal L,E=D/NL, the literal multiplier is theta(Lc).
Its exact plain expansion is

    S_(theta,L)(E)=ell_B(L)/log D S(E;V_D)
      +(1/log D)sum_(p,j>=1)log Np phi(p^j)(Np)^(-j/2)
                                      S(E/(Np)^j;V_D). (6)

When p|L the first term counts its existing valuations and the second counts
every additional valuation of c. Nonempty support gives NL<=CD. The complete
first-power absolute mass is Y^((1-beta)/2), and higher powers are smaller:

    |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|
      <<H_J U^epsilon(D/NL)^(beta/2)Y^((1-beta)/2).     (7)

This uniform bound on actual plain blocks is not an arbitrary coefficient
multiplier theorem. Insert it before [research revision]'s complete q,k,lcm convolution,
including every shared divisor and all inverse smooth-power restorations.
The old gcd/square pieces gain exactly one squared cost Y^(1-beta).
For G=Y=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), their weighted savings are(8beta-4)eta;
(5) saves2beta eta. Since beta>2/3 with reserved buffer, the latter is smaller.
The complete old weighted core therefore saves2beta eta, with its exact

More sharply, [research revision]'s coupled cut F(a,b)=N(gcd(a,b))Ns2(b)^2 has exact blocks
M^(q)(R/Nq)S(D/Nlcm(q,k^2)) and FULL positive mass T^(-beta/2)U^epsilon.
It satisfies the author's conditional interface exactly. Thus

    ||C_T^[theta]Q||^2
      <<H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                [A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]
      <<H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon),            (8)

at T=Y=U^(4eta). This is the complete weighted core, not a signed subset.
Keep [research revision]'s three paid classes FIRST. On their complement |C_T|>|MS|/2.
Define the new actual class there by |C_T^[theta]|>=|C_T|/2. Dividing (8)
by the original SAME-beta plain spike pays original inverse moment

    sum_newclass w_u |M(R)Q|^2
      <<H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).                 (9)

The preloss saving is at least(34/25)eta, reserve(9/25)eta above eta.
Q is never divided out. Every remaining row retains the exact signal

    |C_T^[1-theta]|>|MS|/4,
    1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb,            (10)
    N(abP/rad(abP))<T NP=U^(4eta)NP.

Band prime squares are absent from this core since p^2|b,Np>=A implies
F>=A^2=T. They were nonetheless fully paid in the preceding expansions.
The large-prime plain sector with squarefree coprime inverse has F=1 and
theta=0, so it survives. This is a coefficient example, not an actual
high-zero row or a lower bound for a signed norm.

The complete coarse norm from C_T^[1-theta]=C_T-C_T^[theta] is still
H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon). After the original plain division it is U^(1+epsilon).
The full signed outside-band estimate and whole-row cover remain OPEN.
No norm/class monotonicity follows from0<=theta<=1 or tuple inclusion.

All physical roots, projectors, positive children, original slots, labels,

The [manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves12 original files,7 author

statement:
### The exact full shift kernel and its affordable diagonal

Define
\[
 K_X(m,n)=\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\,\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
Absolute convergence, using the rapid decay of \(\phi\) at both ends, permits the exact regrouping
\[
 \int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2K_X(n,n)
 +2\Re\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\mu(n+h)K_X(n,n+h).
 \tag{T09.1a}
\]
The diagonal is \(O(X)\): uniformly for \(1\le t\le2\), integer counting gives \(\sum_n|\phi(n/(Xt))|^2\ll X\), and then integrate in \(t\). It is separately affordable for \(a\ge1/2\), including every intended numerical target. For \(a<1/2\), cancellation between this diagonal and the off-diagonal would still be required. More generally,
\[
 |K_X(m,n)|\ll_A (1+m/X)^{-A}(1+n/X)^{-A}.
\]
This bound follows directly from the upper-end Schwartz bounds for each factor; the lower-end decay only improves it. It justifies the regrouping and tail truncations with explicit losses, but gives no short-shift support. When \(m,n\asymp X\), differences of order \(X\) remain. Thus the next sufficient estimate is for the complete signed weighted off-diagonal in (T09.1a), including shared-prime and product coincidences. A fixed-shift theorem alone does not establish (T09.1). This exact decomposition and diagonal bound are an additional merger result used in portfolio F01.N1.

statement:
## 4. Pointwise cubic-sieve bound with the actual colors and slots

The unconditional input is Heath-Brown's squarefree cubic large sieve, stated in the pinned PR9 inputs and independently in [Dunn-Radziwill arXiv2109.07463v3](https://arxiv.org/html/2109.07463v3), equation(1.11)/Theorem9.1:

    sum_(d sf,q_d<<D) |sum_(e sf,q_e<<E) beta_e chi_e(d)^4|^2
      << (DE)^epsilon [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] sum_e |beta_e|^2. (4.1)

Replacing a cubic symbol by its conjugate changes nothing. Both variables are squarefree. beta can be any sequence independent of d. This is not an estimate for an arbitrary joint matrix beta_(d,e).

For separated coefficients of size bounded by fixed seminorm factors, Cauchy in d followed by (4.1) gives the normalized pointwise bound

    |(DE)^(-1/2) sum_(d,e sf) alpha_d beta_e chi_e(d)^4|^2
       << H_J [D+E+(DE)^(2/3)] (DE)^epsilon.             (4.2)

The coprimality (d,e)=1 is already present as the zero of the cubic symbol. Additional fixed punctures in either color, finite ray coefficients, angular Gauss phases, independent norm twists and natural zeros at ell are permissible separated coefficients. Conditioning on f,a,ell and on a slot tuple does not change this contract.

Here is how the original source, including slots, enters (4.2). Allocate each prime of extracted f to its actual inverse color or to an original slot; left and right copies allocate independently. The number of allocations is at most tau(f)^C for a fixed C depending on the eventual original slot count. Assigned slot primes divide f and retain their original coefficients. The remaining inverse lengths on a given side are D1'=D1/q_f1 and D2'=D2/q_f2. The remaining slot product has nominal length P'=P0/q_fP, and

    f=f1 f2 fP, (f1,f2,fP) pairwise coprime,
    D1' D2' P' = N0/q_f =: X_f.                         (4.3)

There is no arbitrary choice of these labels: each comes from an actual ordered tuple in(2.1). Empty support is omitted. A nonempty nominal subunit inverse window is clipped by a bounded dilation, as in PR9's convention. Each remaining slot retains its ORIGINAL pool and profile. P' differs from the product of their original nominal lengths only by bounded original annular ratios of the extracted slot primes; those ratios are kept in the profile. Unit residual colors are included in the elementary finite part of(4.2), with the same bound. H_J denotes one fixed polynomial height/seminorm envelope, enlarged finitely when bounding both copies.

For clarity, the four original inverse factors map as follows. In the first copy d1=f1*x and d2=f2*y, so the HB variables are x,y of lengths D1/q_f1,D2/q_f2. In the conjugate copy d1'=f1'*x' and d2'=f2'*y', with HB variables x',y' of lengths D1/q_f1',D2/q_f2'. The same common ideal satisfies f=f1*f2*fP=f1'*f2'*fP', but its two allocations need not agree. We bound each Gauss column separately and then their product. No HB variable is xx', yy', xy' or yx'. All same-color and opposite-color cross-copy coprimality conditions are supplied together by the COMPLETE mutual-gcd identity of Section3. Their artificial violations cancel in that full identity; no residual cross-copy coprimality is silently dropped from an individual norm. The within-copy x,y coprimality is instead the cubic-symbol zero in(4.4).

Freeze an actual surviving tuple P. In the remaining squarefree column m=d e P, the factors d,e,P are pairwise coprime, and twisted multiplicativity gives

    a0(deP)=a0(d)a0(e)a0(P) chi_e(d)^4 chi_(de)(P)^4.    (4.4)

The factors chi_d(P)^4 and chi_e(P)^4 retain the P-punctures and separate. The f-puncture, a-puncture, finite characters and chi_(de)(ell) likewise separate. The coefficient of d is now independent of e and vice versa. Thus (4.2) applies to these actual colors. A general joint coefficient would invalidate this step; none has been introduced.

The common-profile lemma PR9(B3.3) separates the coupled smooth norm factors before any live label is chosen. Dyadically localize a and the nonzero ell with fixed unit windows and nominal lengths A,H; the sharp condition q_ell<=Y remains an OUTER restriction. Use the full ambient box of the original inverse and individual slot norms on BOTH copies, together with q_a/A and q_ell/H. The kernel has the form K(C*y_ell/(y_a^6*product(y_columns))), C=UH/(A^6*N0^2), where C depends only on nominal sector lengths. Its Euler derivatives are uniformly bounded for every C>0 by the original Schwartz seminorms. The Fourier measure is therefore fixed before the actual a,f,ell or slot tuple. Substitute d_i=f_i*x_i only afterward. Extracted imaginary powers have modulus1, and the residual tests have the actual shortened scales. The O(log U)^2 nominal sectors have subpower total cost. Real inverse roots enter that profile once. This produces separated norm twists with finite weighted Fourier L1 mass and polynomial dependence on the original independent heights. No arithmetic pair mask is smoothed away.

For each fixed P, (4.2) bounds the centrally normalized two-inverse Gauss sum. Hilbert triangle (or pointwise triangle here) over the ORIGINAL remaining slot tuples costs at most

    (P')^(-1/2) sum_P |b(P)| << H_J (P')^(1/2+epsilon).

Ideal counting suffices; no prime theorem or slot independence is assumed. Consequently the entire normalized remaining column polynomial B_f(ell), for each allocation and each Fourier component, satisfies

    |B_f(ell)|^2
      << H_J P' [D1'+D2'+(D1'D2')^(2/3)] U^epsilon
      << H_J P0 [D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)] U^epsilon.         (4.5)

Both original height weights are still on their original colors. On the right side of a correlation, the whole column is conjugated. Equation(4.5) applies to either orientation separately; their product is bounded by the geometric mean. If ell shares any source, slot or f prime, its zero is retained as described in Section3 and the same inequality holds without a new gcd factor.

statement:
## B. Protected rare18: a kernel-adapted transport certificate

Fix a=f3 first, so each coefficient is exactly+1 or-1, including all prime powers and the literal prime2/3 rules. Let phi_n(v)=g_kappa(v)g_tau(log(n/X)-v), and use the H^-r norm A6. Define the exact nonnegative squared feature distance

    d_(r,X)(n,m)^2=J(n,n)+J(m,m)-2J(n,m).                (B1)

This is a Hilbert distance, not an arbitrary positive-entry matrix metric. It includes the radial weights b_X(n), which cannot be discarded in favor of only log(n/m).

Choose fixed A>0 and C,D with D>C and

    C^2>2 sigma(1+A), D^2>2 sigma(1+A).

Put N=floor(X exp(C sqrt(log X))) and a ghost label at real position x_*=X exp(D sqrt(log X)); its feature is defined by the same Gaussian formula, although x_* need not be an integer. This is an auxiliary balancing label, not an arithmetic coefficient. The omitted true field and the balancing ghost are each O(X^(-A+o(1))) in H^-r uniformly for all r>=0. For the tail use

    ||phi_n||_H^-r <= ||phi_n||_2
       =sqrt(g_(2nu)(0)) g_sigma(log(n/X)),
    sum_(n>N)g_sigma(log(n/X))
       <=X^(1-C^2/(2sigma)+o(1)).                        (B2)

Integral comparison on logarithmic dyads proves the last bound, including the exp(C sqrt(log X)) factor as subpower. The ghost mass is |sum_(n<=N)f3(n)|<=N; its feature norm is X^(-D^2/(2sigma)) times a constant. No conjectural Mertens estimate is needed for these two errors.

Add the ghost charge -sum_(n<=N)f3(n), so the resulting positive and negative measures have the same mass M<=N. Let pi be ANY nonnegative transport plan with these exact marginals, and set

    C_r(X)=sum_(positive n,negative m) pi(n,m)d_(r,X)(n,m)^2.

The signed feature identity is exact, and Hilbert Cauchy--Schwarz gives

    N_r(X) <= sqrt(M C_r(X)) + O(X^(-A+o(1))).           (B3)

Thus, since M<=X^(1+o(1)), a proved all-scale certificate

    C_(r_X)(X)<<_epsilon X^(q+epsilon)                   (B4)

returns the complete original moment exponent

    gamma=(1+q+d)/2,                                    (B5)

provided q>-1 and errors are chosen below it. The first-gain condition is

    q+d<2*.874864-1=.749728.                             (B6)

Quarter-strip arithmetic cost q=.5 tolerates d<.249728 for a first gain; q=2/3 tolerates d<.083061333... . With d=0, q=.74898 returns the old convenient target gamma=.87449. These statements include the full unmatched mass and both infinite tails, rather than silently treating equal sign counts as exact.

For a fixed complex ordinary character, split the literal coefficients into real and imaginary parts and transport each pair of positive/negative real measures with its own balancing ghost. Each mass is at most N, ramified zeros remain zero, and the triangle inequality adds two fixed constants. Both complete B4 hypotheses are then required. The scalar A13 itself already handles the complex source without this split.

### B2. Baseline construction is affordable but does not improve its exponent

Assume only the accepted buffered summatory bound

    S(t)=sum_(n<=t) f3(n)=O(t^beta), 1/2<beta<1.          (B7)

Credit G28 and the accepted buffered mu-Mertens premise for this fixed-source implication; beta may be any fixed value above.874864. Enumerate the positive locations p_k and negative locations m_k in increasing order. Since the two counting functions are t/2+O(t^beta), matching equal ranks gives, outside finitely many initial locations,

    p_k asymp m_k, |p_k-m_k|=O(p_k^beta).

This follows by solving k=t/2+O(t^beta) for each location; constants are uniform in k and in the cutoff N. Match as many ranks as possible below N, and send the excess last ranks to the ghost. There are O(N^beta) excess atoms, all in [N-O(N^beta),N], by the same two counting estimates. Finite initial locations have Gaussian norm O_A(X^-A) for every fixed A.

The product identity gives the exact derivative calculation

    ||d phi_w/dw||_2^2 = g_sigma(w)^2 g_(2nu)(0)
              *[w^2/sigma^2 + alpha^2/(2nu)].            (B8)

The cross term vanishes since integral g_nu*g_nu'=0. H^-r is at most L2. Hence the equal-rank pair costs are bounded by a constant times

    n^(2beta-2)(1+log(n/X)^2)exp(-log(n/X)^2/sigma),

with a harmless fixed widening of the Gaussian majorant for the small displacement. More precisely log(m/n)=O(n^(beta-1)); for n above a fixed threshold, comparing the derivative at w and at w+O(n^(beta-1)) multiplies it by exp(O(|w|n^(beta-1)+1)). The elementary inequality |w|n^(beta-1)<=epsilon*w^2+C_epsilon, with any fixed epsilon<1/(2sigma), yields a Gaussian of fixed larger variance. Summing on dyads gives O(X^(2beta-1)), because the substitution n=X exp(w) leaves the convergent integral exp((2beta-1)w) times that Gaussian. Its positive exponent2beta-1 is essential when absorbing fixed small-n terms.

The ghost pairs lie at w=C sqrt(log X)+o(1); by B2 their total cost is O(X^(beta-C^2/sigma+o(1))) plus O(X^(beta-D^2/sigma+o(1))). These are smaller than the main bound after the chosen tail constants are enlarged if necessary. Therefore this explicit monotone plan proves

    C_r(X) <<_beta,tau,kappa,A,C,D X^(2beta-1), ALL r>=0.(B9)

B3 returns beta when d=0. It supplies no exponent improvement, and d>0 can only worsen this baseline return. This is the existing monotone-transport mechanism of MM-D2, now paid for the new literal localized Gaussian feature metric and full f3 tail. Do not count it as a new broad transport discovery. W41's obstruction to single-prime edges is respected: these pairs use unrestricted near-one ratios, not edges n<->pn.

**New arithmetic action:** lower the cost exponent of a source-exact plan in THIS metric below .749728-d, retaining the ghost and all actual coefficients. A finite optimal-transport solve can discover structure but does not prove B4 uniformly. No such lowering is established here.
