# Independent review of the stronger support gain and tilted endpoint



## 1. Verdict and exact dependency boundary

**Approve the stronger paired high-bin gain, the tilted local plane, and the complete return to c=12514261/100000000=.12514261, relative to the same analytic source contracts as the accepted [research revision] result.** The increase over written c7=.12514 is 261/100000000. No substantive repair is required. The mathematical statement remains source-relative; this review does not establish a public record or external theorem admission.

The author froze before the controller accepted the [research revision] weighted-density/projector input at 07:18. Its repeated description of that input as pending is therefore accurate historical status. The exact input has now been independently reviewed in my frozen [research revision] packet. I reuse that completed audit and inspect the genuinely changed argument and return here. I do not treat the new arithmetic as proof of an unreviewed marked-density theorem.

The strongest objection is a factor of two, or repeated use of the second projector's scalars, in replacing the old z/56 reserve by k(delta)z. Actual PR15 LA.13 is already the final **paired joint exponent**. Its first-support term has coefficient at least k, and its second-support and clipped-plain terms have coefficient delta. The new weighted slot saving is also in those paired units. Sections 3--4 establish this directly. No exceptional or opposite-side reserve is transferred.

The unchanged F0/analytic-ancestry issue, old positive-slot uniformity contract, exact external root-LFunction comparison, and any external formalization/kernel duties remain open. The corrected first-transform phase, both signed active residues and the original physical exceptional costs are retained. The centered exceptional M/24 result is not an input.

## 2. Frozen evidence and independent method

All six files in `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/high-gain-optimization/` were read completely, including the preserved failed-search transcript. Main report: 20171 bytes, SHA256 `a0bc2fda10c48e27486a097dc3cf75abad593f149ac9f78cbfc881fca9c9d5a1`. Freeze: SHA256 `adf3a8028a57af36894bd4bf8cf3b8f3c2fa39309b72b217ae913053141b2876`, timestamp 07:17:11.375126 UTC. My helper verifies every frozen artifact and every supplied source pin; all match.

The decisive primary passages re-read here are:

* PR15 `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex`, LA.11--13 and the adjoining branch ledger, at commit `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef` (source lines 295--417). These fix the actual row width, paired normalization, support coefficients and missing-radical count.
* PR9 `paper.md`, B3.65--70 at commit `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b` (lines 2464--2526). These fix the complete signed projector, unrestricted quotients, retained natural scalars, four clipped rectangle pairs and exact payment of its divisor dyad.
* The retained forward `[restricted mathematical source]`, its source contracts and geometry/shortening/Euler sections, the complete rational and feedback argument, and the principal/small/upper-row/all-height/common-gap/continuation sections. These were also fully read in the preceding independent review.

The complete marked amplifier, supported-witness, raw lifting, fixed-dictionary, natural-zero, Fourier-mask and signed-reconstruction audit remains bound to my [research revision] report, SHA256 `c818274326a9a10bd172c8442a1ce8885688df13def8d09c8dff76f1c88176ed`. The supplement does not change those coefficient interfaces. Other source receipts bind exact bytes without claiming a new transitive proof. Header dates and receipt times remain distinct.

`independent-check.py` never executes or imports author code. It expands the physical expression as a sparse rational power polynomial, substitutes each rational box, and converts monomials to Bernstein coefficients. This differs from the author's interpolation-matrix calculation. It checks all 600 atlas cells, preserving each cell's A/a correlation; all 41 recorded margins; all 348 coefficients on 22/6/1 complete covers; the exact geometry; and the two final scoped failures. The entire coefficient arrays and power coefficients are retained in `receipt.json`, not only their minima. These calculations certify arithmetic, while the following argument establishes source applicability.

## 3. Reconstructing the stronger gain in actual source units

Write c_s,d_s for the genuine first-support widths, distinguishing them from the endpoint constant. On either consistent first-side orientation the literal row is

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-(c_s-d_s)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c=log_Z NF_c <=5(R-R0), R<=min(c_s,d_s).       (I1)

The actual enclosing radius is used before dropping its favorable extra -omega. The separate child width M'=M-(c_s-d_s)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2, with the original padding, is unchanged. Active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p modulo six remain distinct, including their zero-residue punctures. No equality of their F_c is assumed; the opposite first-side orientation is treated separately. Reflected second rows and whole-character conjugation remain within the fixed dictionary.

The actual joint high exponent relative to its target, from LA.13, is

    M(rho-1)+delta A+a(5-6rho)+E1+E2+small,
    E1=(1-rho)(c_s-d_s)_+-delta c_s-(1+rho)R
       -E-Bc+rho L_c+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.                            (I2)

There is no additional square root to take after this formula. It has already combined the two normalized sides, the joint row count, the missing radical and the outside power.

For delta in [17/25,7/10], put

    rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
    k=rho+delta-1=delta(5-6delta)/[3(5-2delta)].       (I3)

Here 5rho>1, 4rho-1>0, rho<2/5, and 0<k<delta. Let m=min(c_s,d_s), T=(c_s-d_s)_+, so c_s=m+T. Substituting L_c<=5(R-R0) into (I2) gives

    E1 <= -(rho+delta-1)T-delta m
          +(4rho-1)R+(1-5rho)R0-E-Bc
       <= -(delta-4rho+1)m-kT-E-Bc
       <= -k c_s.                                    (I4)

The last inequality is exactly delta-4rho+1-k=2-5rho>=0. This uses actual valuations and signs, not a finite residue-table enumeration. Since g2<=b2, also E2<=-delta b2-t2. Both coefficients are in the units of (I2).

For the full second projector, retain the B3.65 signed priority allocation. Extracting a selected plain n=d*l keeps psi_w(d), including its zero; l is unrestricted. Selecting a slot freezes that prime. No additional quotient puncture is inserted. For each of the four actual rectangle pairs put

    rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2,
    zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2.                                 (I5)

Every clipped reduction is nonnegative. B3.69 pays the divisor dyad by the two exact extraction scalars. Independently, the physical pointwise plain price contains -delta rbar. It is a shorter-plain saving, not an extraction scalar used a second time. The actual slot products stay inside the joint row sum; Cauchy and the accepted raw weighted bound replace their paired price delta zbar by gamma zbar. The gain there is eta zbar, where

    eta=4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta)=2k.               (I6)

For example, clearing 3(5-2delta) reduces both sides of eta=2k to 2delta(5-6delta). It is an identity throughout the interval, not a numerical endpoint coincidence.

The already reviewed coefficient reduction is essential: freeze the missing first radical before weighted summation; all other apparent moving holes are natural zeros of w. Residual fixed holes have divisor-many subsets, and the finite surviving slot lists retain their original relative characters. The second projector stays outside this row reconstruction. Its count is paid once by B3.69. Common Fourier majorants precede the labels and their diagonal contraction adds no label count. Thus the weighted bound has the actual fixed prime coefficients, natural conductor and same-parent zero maximum; it is not applied to arbitrary moving masks.

The surviving widths satisfy the already established literal incidence bound

    zbar >= z-c_s-b2-rbar-small.                       (I7)

Each genuine frozen incidence divides the relevant complete extracted column, with its multiplicity. The column widths are c_s+c2 and c_s+d2. Newly frozen second-projector slots are included in r_j, and clipping costs only the single aggregate endpoint tolerance. Both the support terms and (I7) refer to the same pair of rectangles.

Set s=c_s+b2+rbar. If s>=z, (I4), E2 and the retained plain reduction already save at least ks>=kz. This uses only the old density, with its supported-window completion; no positive surviving slot width or weighted-width premise is needed. In particular all-slot-exhaustion cases are covered.

If s<z, then c_s<z and (I1) gives W>=M-c_s-6a>M-z-6a. Under the strict condition

    M-6a>22z,                                        (I8)

one has W>21z. Each individual surviving z_j<=z is therefore admissible for the accepted raw weighted theorem. The gain is at least

    ks+eta(z-s)-small =ks+2k(z-s)-small >=kz-small.    (I9)

The weighted theorem's width condition is needed only here. No negative nominal width is put into a nonempty density count: outside this case the old supported-window rule applies, and in this case W is strictly positive. Since k decreases, its endpoint values are

    k(17/25)=391/6825,  k(7/10)=7/135.

This proves the sharper all-configuration gain **k(delta)z**, in paired units. The weaker uniform 7z/135 follows. Exceptional rows remain separate and contribute no part of (I9).

The internal supported-witness zero bin can still have a larger upper endpoint than the physical bin. The accepted weighted lemma supplies its inverse/prime witnesses using that larger bin, but its slot price uses the original physical upper bound. Buffered bins below .70 use their prescribed lower edge with an O(e) upper-price allowance. Bins above .70 can use the old high estimate. Bins crossing .68 use the original low-branch rounding rule. No transform or projector is applied to a zero-bin indicator.

## 4. Tilted plane, fixed atlas and every local branch

Put q=17/25, K_a=34/21, alpha=1/400000 and h_q=5-6rho(q). Then

    D=q+K_a h_q=81379/15925,
    B0=(1-rho(q)+K_a h_q)/D=14200/14361,
    Lambda=19312/4787-k(q)/D=57775/14361,
    B=B0-3/500000=7099956917/7180500000.              (I10)

This changes the slot coefficient, not just the intercept. The local window remains .41M<=n1,n2<=.44M and .034M<=z<=.04M, with new condition n1+n2+Lambda z<=BM.

For cell j=1,...,600, write l_j=.034+(j-1)/100000, b_j=l_j+1/100000. From the original slot system choose its ceiling cell and fix

    g_j=B-1+(9/2-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=K_a g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B-(Lambda-1)l_j.                              (I11)

These choices precede row summation, either Poisson transform, every live scale and all four derivative profiles. The auxiliary inverse amplifier in the weighted-density proof does not replace this physical Gauss amplifier. Mesh endpoints use either neighboring valid ceiling assignment; z=.034 can use the first cell. There is no live-scale choice of a_j.

The worst high reserve at q is

    H_j=1-rho(q)-q A_j-h_q a_j/M+k(q)l_j.            (I12)

Expanding shows its coefficient of l_j is

    q(Lambda-1)-K_a h_q(9/2-Lambda)+k(q)=0.

Thus every cell has exactly the same value. The rounding and alpha charge produce

    Bcap=B0-[q(Lambda-1)/100000+h_q alpha
                    +k(q)/100000]/D
        =6163068817207/6232980368000,
    B<Bcap,
    H_j=1230658453/457397850000000>0.                 (I13)

This is a strict sufficient ledger, not an impossibility theorem at Bcap or beyond. It is independently recomputed for all 600 cells, without separating A_j and a_j for the exceptional checks.

For delta in [.68,.70], the unweighted high derivative is

    50(1-6a_j/M)/[3(5-2delta)^2]-A_j.

Also k'=1-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]>=-139/486. Since 0<=z/M<=1/25, adding the variable gain k(delta)z/M subtracts at most 139/12150 from a derivative lower bound. Using the worst a and A separately here gives

    4456776045796133/16857397761750000>0.             (I14)

The scalar derivative is therefore positive throughout the interval, and (I12) suffices. The old high branch has reserve at .70 at least 2901555283/753952500000>0, with positive old derivative, covering [.70,.75] without the new weighted gain.

The actual width test (I8), using the largest physical amplifier and z/M<=1/25, has reserve

    1-6a_max/M-22/25=1461650461/33509000000>0.        (I15)

This uniform numerical margin is chosen before the family and all labels. It supplies compact positive free/raw width ratios to the weighted theorem; it is not merely an average over cells.

The low branch is unchanged in mechanism and uses only old 9/2 descendants and the unrestricted no-slot estimate. The exact amplifier choice cancels its g_j coefficient, leaving alpha(1-4q/3)=7/30000000. Retain its actual-width correction d_*+r(F-d_*)_+<=delta2+rF_+, including negative d_* and bounded supported scales.

Every other terminal reserve is positive. In this table ahat=a_j/M, A=A_j and g=g_j are normalized by the original M:

| Branch or gate | Minimum normalized reserve |
|---|---:|
| extracted valuation one: ahat/4-g/6 | 575224213/482529600000 |
| extracted valuation six: 13ahat/4-g/6 | 61536324389/2412648000000 |
| extracted valuation seven: 4ahat-g/6 | 3810068761/120632400000 |
| genuine second zero: 1-A-5ahat | 4587940223/67018000000 |
| main fixed-inducing: 1-A-4ahat | 510101569/6282937500 |
| error fixed-inducing: 1-A-9ahat | 3526102513/201054000000 |
| physical support: 1/4-7ahat | 4621070461/28722000000 |

The three errors keep their unamplified radii, squared scalars Np^-1, (1-Np^-1)^2, Np^-1 and extraction widths (lambda_p,lambda_p), (6lambda_p,0), (7lambda_p,lambda_p), with lambda_p>=3a/4 eventually. Their global slot price is 3/4, deletion rate 1/6, and normalized prime average is used once. They do not use high-bin heredity or a second amplifier. First zero keeps the powerful-product bound; artificial zero is unamplified and keeps its -s0 allowance. The comparison budget remains at most .93M+small.

Fixed-inducing rows retain the original paired predicate, forced residues, whole centered rectangle, physical K_phys^(5/6), both scalars and masks. Their substitutions F1>=2c_s/3-4a-small, F2>=2b2/3 and the maximum A-5M/6-2v/3-(M/4-v)_+<=A-M give precisely the old 4a and 9a costs. The same-cell A_j/a_j computations pay them; the stronger nonexceptional support gain is never used here.

Allocate all bin, mesh, annular and profile losses below fixed fractions of these positive numbers. The numerical mesh precedes the arithmetic family and slot count. After these are fixed, take common Fourier majorants before labels, internal smooth/height degrees before the returned density bound, a separate external height exponent after that degree, and raw polynomial bounds before tail orders. All descendant moments remain old inputs. Thus the new plane has the same fixed-family, natural-eligibility, independent-height and four-profile contract.

## 5. Changed geometry, shortenings and Euler shifts

The independently reconstructed parameters are

    c=12514261/100000000, theta=87485739/100000000,
    h=397683/500000=.795366,
    ell=11/3-4theta=12542783/75000000,
    x=1+ell-h=27890333/75000000,
    y=h-2ell=8641721/18750000,
    kappa_*=2theta-1=37485739/50000000.                (I16)

All original geometric inequalities remain strict: 0<ell<x<y<2x, y<1/2<h<2y, 1/6<ell<1/5, h>4ell, x+y=1-ell, y-2x+ell<0 and 1+3ell-2(x+y)<0. The exact physical-probe identity remains

    (5x+y)/12=theta-(5/6-x/3-ell/6).

Use d0=1/200, d_-=h-1/1000, d_+=h+10^-12 and t0=1/1000. With the retained coarse slope bound <2, this smaller extension leaves a positive certified reserve from the 10^-10 row saving; no necessity or maximality of this extension choice is asserted. On d in [d_-,d_+], t in [0,t0], the reflected plain scale n=1-y/d+t satisfies .41<n_min<=n<=n_max<N=264/625. The new capacity is

    z_A(t)=(B-2n)/Lambda,
    C_new(d)=d z_A(0)=[2y-(2-B)d]/Lambda.            (I17)

Its extrema satisfy .034<z_min<=z_A<=z_max<93/2500=.0372<.04. Exact enclosure gaps are

    N-n_max=10395285991321/11930490000015000,
    .0372-z_max=1348210220189/11473623912500000,
    z_min-.034=51069303382364420917/22976135325028887500000.

Thus replacing the old .037 cap is necessary and paid. The same whole-slot selector retains all widths, including error/zero-gain slots, in its amplitude denominator. If positive supply is exhausted, its gain is still at least the target q z_A. Every actual shortening is covered:

* Total selected width <=.034 uses 1-2N-(9/2).034=11/5000.
* A plain width <=.41 uses 1-.41-N-(9/2).0372=1/5000.
* Otherwise both plains and selected total are in the new local window, and n1+n2+Lambda z_I<=B.
* Empty selection uses the unrestricted bounded-plain no-slot estimate.

The same selected I and original ceiling cell work in all four derivative moments. A fixed parent width 1+nu is normalized before the atlas; the two old complements lose at most .153nu and .41nu. Choose nu below the now smaller short-plain reserve and the final endpoint tolerance. No old .037 shortening margin is reused.

Positive supply and detector capacity remain strict. In particular

    ell-d_+z_max>0,
    ell/d_+-4/21=330515239996/16702686000021>0,
    2ell-1/3=14261/12500000>0,
    4ell-y=650177/3125000>0,
    2y-d_+>0.

The physical detector's inverse capacity is at most 4/21 and plain capacity at most 1/12. For d<1/2 the literal selector has total width ell/d>=2ell>1/3>1/(6kappa); no wrapper requiring d>=1/2 is invoked. Small capacities still take their unmarked O(nu0) completion and strict MI decrements. Thresholds over d>=d0 are uniform after the fixed d0 choice.

The Euler expansion remains the original weighted one:

    sum |c_u(h0,hr)| h0^(delta/2) << U^epsilon,
    h0 hr << Y.

For t<=t0, capacity loss tq/Lambda is paid by delta t/2 since q<=delta/2 and Lambda>1. For t>=t0, put b=2y/d-1 and use

    S_b(t)=t/2-[(b-(1-B))/Lambda
                      -max(0,(b-2t)/(9/2))]/4.       (I18)

Its t-slopes are 7/18 before the kink and 1/2 afterward. For fixed t it is decreasing in b on both pieces, because 1/Lambda>2/9. Here b<=b_max=2y/d_--1, and

    .161-b_max=713029/1191549000>0,
    S_(.161)(t0)=8847749/346650000000>0.              (I19)

Also 2t0<b_max. Hence every larger shift is paid. This explicitly replaces the insufficient old coarse b<=.16. At clipped capacity zero the plain lengths are bounded by U^(1+o(1)), within the unrestricted old no-slot contract. For d<d_- retain old capacity and its original weighted shift argument. No squarefree-only simplification or unweighted Euler norm removes the large shifts.

## 6. Full rational certificate and all physical complements

The physical detector still uses the old count on 0<=delta<=3/4, 0<=p<=1/2. It is not replaced by the high-bin transformed-row formula. At kappa=kappa_* define

    Dp=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*),
    P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)), V=5/6-delta,
    J=V Dp+delta P,
    RJ=(1-delta)J+delta PV/2.

The cleared numerator, independently expanded from forward (4.2), is

    F=J[theta-v-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2
          -ell delta p-d(1/4-17/50)+delta p C_d/2]
         -(3d/4)RJ.                                  (I20)

For new rows C_d=C_new(d); for old rows C_d=min(d,2y-d)/(6kappa_*). The minimum is retained in the independent helper. At the three tested old/new rows it agrees with the source's appropriate affine branch. Since V>=1/12 and Dp>=Dp(1/2),

    J-1/10 >=961943821/13494866040>0.

The polynomial has degree at most (2,3). For each submitted box, the independent helper performs its affine power-basis substitution, then uses

    beta_ij=sum_(r<=i,s<=j) f_rs
                 binom(i,r)/binom(2,r)
                 binom(j,s)/binom(3,s).              (I21)

All resulting coefficients are strictly positive and each exact minimum matches the frozen author receipt:

| Row, capacity | Saving v | Boxes | Coefficients |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| d=h, new | 10^-10 | 22 | 264 |
| d=d_-, old | 10^-5 | 6 | 72 |
| d=1/2, old | 10^-3 | 1 | 12 |

Each collection covers the entire closed [0,3/4]x[0,1/2] rectangle. The helper checks disjoint interiors on the elementary grid induced by all box endpoints, covers every grid boundary/vertex, and verifies area 3/8. Nonnegative Bernstein bases sum to one, so these are full-domain proofs. The finer boxes near p=1/2 are not replaced by point samples. All 348 coefficients, including their maxima and the source power coefficients, remain in the independent receipt.

For row widths, the old exponent is affine on [1/2,d_-]. The new capacity exceeds the old at the junction by

    5512650433670972332961/4872911784131250000000000>0.

Consequently the old endpoint bound also bounds the new exponent there. The new exponent is affine on [d_-,h]. Its d-slope is at most 33/50+(3/8)(2-B)/(2Lambda)<2. Extending h by 10^-12 leaves

    10^-10-2*10^-12=49/500000000000>0.               (I22)

Below 1/2, min(d,2y-d) is concave and multiplied by a nonpositive coefficient in the old exponent; thus that exponent is convex even across d=y. Its d0 bound and the half-row certificate cover [d0,1/2]. The changed complements are independently recomputed:

|---|---:|
| floor: theta-.51-h/3-.51ell | 9027791/625000000 |
| far old: theta-7/8+49h/150-7ell/8-33d0/50 | 66026689/600000000 |
| nonprincipal small row: -13h/75+y/2-63d0/50 | 404449/4687500 |
| principal w contour: y/20-(1+h)/1000-1/4000 | 6299767/300000000 |
| principal z contour: h/600-1/1000-1/4000 | 7561/100000000 |

Floors require no nonfloor witness. Small nonprincipal rows include the finitely many nonprincipal units and use their separate ordinary convexity bound. The genuine principal row u=1 is separated first. Its double residue retains both positive residue constants, the exact radial normalization, and quotient-free compensator. The remaining principal terms save y/4, h/24 and mu_P>0. The changed h and y satisfy all their displayed contour inequalities.

The upper-row argument must use the **new** zeta=d_+-h=10^-12. The source estimate, valid for any fixed positive zeta and sufficiently large fixed v>2, is

    Z^[B_raw+(h+zeta)(1+epsilon)-zeta v+epsilon],
    B_raw=x/2+1+y.                                    (I23)

Choose v after this new zeta to make the exponent as negative as needed. Thus the smaller extension does not leave a gap between the central rows and an old h+10^-10 tail. It requires a larger finite decay order, with no change in the source identity. The author's reference to the unchanged upper-row method is valid with this explicit substitution.

All physical coefficients remain those of the forward argument: completed marked index cn^3, all collisions and both compensator branches, signed Gram identities, six-row local table, natural character zeros, complete w-inversion before reciprocal bounds, and independent imaginary coordinates Im(s+z), Im z, Im w. The new local gain does not alter any of them. Real contour strips and reciprocal buffers remain those already allowed by the old source. Fixed raw polynomial bounds precede the final height-tail order. Reflected profiles have their original summable annular decomposition and scale supremum before a moment is applied. No arithmetic indicator is differentiated.

## 7. Actual supremum, common gap and exact family return

In the contradiction branch let beta_*>theta and mu=beta_*-theta. The only initial global boundary is the imported beta_*<=7/8. For actual kappa=2beta_*-1, the unchanged detector inequalities give

    partial_kappa G_new <=5d_+/288<1/50,
    partial_kappa G_old <=695/14112<1/8.              (I24)

The independent margins below these bounds are 356633999999/57600000000000 and 1069/14112, respectively. Since kappa-kappa_*=2mu, exponent losses are at most mu/25 and mu/4 while the available boundary rises by mu. The old capacity decreases with kappa, preserving the new/old junction comparison. Thus all row estimates hold at the actual unknown supremum, rather than just at the numerical kappa_*.

The small new rational saving is still a fixed strictly positive number. First choose mu, the geometry and all numerical reserves, then a moment loss, amplitude mesh, capacity decrement and parent-width tolerance sufficiently small relative to (I13), (I22), and the shortening reserves. The moment mesh is uniform in the later family. Freeze a finite positive slot system of total width ell, fine enough on every d>=d0, and choose 0<mu_P<.87 times its smallest width. Then choose a common Delta>0 below fixed fractions of all reserves, y/4, h/24, mu_P and mu/4. In particular its choice can respect the 10^-10 central gap and 10^-12 row-extension scale before any target is selected.

Only afterward choose the primitive target, fixed excluded primes and dictionaries, profile orders and internal detector parameters. After the density theorem returns its polynomial height degree, choose the separate external height exponent so its loss fits the already fixed Delta. Tail orders follow fixed raw bounds; final thresholds may depend on the target. The larger v in (I23) is finite and fits the same order. No uniform constant over growing conductors is required. The old positive-slot uniformity premise is retained explicitly; numerical tuning cannot prove it.

The original physical estimate and all complements now give

    f_eta(Z) <<_eta Z^(beta_*-k_probe-Delta).

The small-Z estimate follows from moving the original line to any fixed A>2. Its Mellin integral is holomorphic on Re s>beta_*-Delta and, by the source's actual inversion, equals

    exp((s-5/6)^2) H_eta(s)/L_K^S(s,eta).

Since beta_*-Delta>theta>.87, the numerator is nonzero. The supremum supplies a primitive zero above beta_*-Delta/2; choose that target only after Delta, and apply its permitted constants and threshold. This contradicts the holomorphy without assuming that the supremum is attained. Hence beta_*<=theta relative to the imported analytic base.

The family is exactly the existing finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke family. Its imprimitive Euler factors are nonzero for Re s>0. The ordinary norm lift keeps ramified and imprimitive factors and yields L_K(s,eta_chi)=L(s,chi)L(s,chi chi_-3) on the relevant strip. Thus every complex Dirichlet character modulo each natural q!=0 has no zero for theta<Re s<1. Classical ordinary nonvanishing covers Re s>=1, including nonprincipal s=1; the principal pole is excepted, and modulus one is zeta. This is not a new infinite-type Hecke theorem. Exact comparison to an external root-LFunction definition and independent base imports remain explicit external obligations.

## 8. Failures, credit and final disposition

The final next-grid trial was independently reconstructed at c=6257131/50000000=.12514262, keeping this B, Lambda and h, and recomputing theta,kappa,ell,y. At delta=465841/1000000, p=1/2, with no requested saving, its exact cleared numerator is

    -2753608154520773498584558157099 /
      58474939849650000000000000000000000000 <0.

Increasing this plane's intercept by 10^-6 gives high-atlas margin -221341837/91479570000000<0. These establish failure of those specific sufficient inequalities and trials. They do not prove an upper bound on the true theorem, on other planes/geometries, or on stronger analytic estimates. Earlier floating searches in the author packet are preserved provenance, not proof or a global optimality claim.



**Final disposition:** approve the written source-relative c=.12514261 return, with all inherited base/admission obligations still open. No substantive amendment is required; the explicit new-zeta tail calculation above makes one inherited step concrete. No formalization, kernel or public verification claim. Full own-artifact readback, freeze, exact fresh-claim release and STOP conclude this lane.

## Two ordinary PNT substitutions with sharp endpoints

Restrict p,q to [z,B_X], B_X=X^(1/2+2delta); the portions excluded from
the central product range again have the full Gaussian/divisor tail.
Use the accepted fixed-order PNT pi(v)=li(v)+O_N(v/log^N v), with N=10
fixed before X. Throughout this rectangle logp,logq are comparable to L.

For fixed r,q, Stieltjes integration by parts replaces the p sum by
integral dp/logp with error bounded by

    C_tau,N * x/(r q L^N).                                    (CT4)

To verify CT4, the error measure's primitive is O(p/L^N). Multiplying
the weight derivative and integrating gives
integral p|d[g(log(rpq/x))]| <= C_tau x/(rq), since
integral e^u|g'(u)|du is finite. Endpoint terms obey the same bound from
sup_u e^u g(u)<infinity. A sharp central cutoff, if retained during this
step, has two atoms bounded identically. A prime exactly at z is excluded
according to p>z; its endpoint atom is included in this estimate.

Summing CT4 over the actual q primes and r<=X^delta uses only the integer
harmonic majorants sum_(q<=B_X)1/q=O(L), sum_(r<=X^delta)1/r=O(L).
The first total error is O(X/L^(N-2)). For the second PNT replacement,
apply the same integration-by-parts estimate inside the existing positive
p integral; bound dp/logp by dp and integrate1/p over the finite
rectangle. This again gives O(X/L^(N-2)). Coefficient signs are preserved
in the main term; absolute values are used only for these error bounds.

The resulting integral has factor1/2 from unordered primes. Extend its
limits to p,q>z and its core to all r>=1. The positive integrals with
divisor multiplicity and log denominators bounded by a constant have
Gaussian tails of the same arbitrary negative-power size. Thus

    R_z(x)=(1/2)sum_r f(r)
       integral_(p,q>z) g(log(rpq/x)) dp dq/(logp logq)
       + O_tau,kappa(X/L^4),                                 (CT5)

where the displayed error also absorbs the square-prime diagonal and
all Gaussian tails. No signed Mertens assertion was used to complete r.

# [research revision] joint-core independent review



## 1. Verdict and precise scope

Recommend acceptance of the prime-band product bound, the complete band-weighted gcd/square core estimate, and its disjoint actual-row saving. The proof uses the literal arbitrary-coefficient MI, one additional common-orientation slot, exact diagonal extraction and a normalized coloring identity. It does not use an arbitrary-mask MP theorem or a signed-subset norm inequality. The weighted intersection formula retains all prime powers shared with the extracted lcm.

The profile/height argument should be recorded with the explicit implementation in Section3: factor the original height twist before Fourier separation, then use the buffered estimate at small separation frequencies and a polynomial frequency majorant for the rest. This pays the complete Fourier integral. Only the ORIGINAL unshifted plain spike is divided out. A shifted shortened factor needs an upper bound, not a new zero witness.

The author left the old gcd/square removal as a pending dependency. This reviewer completed that source review, froze and normally released it before beginning this separate assignment. Root has since accepted its restricted estimates and joint-cut development for [research revision]. Those inputs can now be used at their exact source-relative scope. Section7 applies the author's stated absolute-block interface to that frozen joint cut. It gives the same band saving on a core with repeat factor <U^(4eta) NP, retaining the entire outside-band signed complement.

No full row cover or larger zero-free constant follows. The remaining signed source still admits large-prime plain columns; its complete coarse inverse norm remains U^(1+epsilon). The current written c11=.1251459636 and K=28114053/6250000 are unchanged, including the preceding-c10 SAME-family license, open F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and external admission obligations. No high-zero row or nonempty paid class is constructed. No proof-assistant, kernel, provider or child-agent work occurred.

## 2. Source contract and the exact logarithmic convolution

Fix delta in[17/25,7/10], 0<eta<=1/1000, v in[0,1/20], and the G137 common cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. Include the enlarged fixed MI system and its required orders in the initial source/height choices before selecting these witnesses. Work only in its original crossing window |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta, including the preallocated small endpoint padding. Let R=U^r and D=U^m. Here m is bounded away from zero, and the two witnesses have the SAME natural character, real power, height and retained zero. Fix the internal bin, label and dyads before each norm. Omega contains only the licensed nonprincipal supported-witness rows; principal, artificial and separate fixed-inducing branches retain their original treatment.

Write phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1), with one common orientation. Fixed finite phases need not have order dividing six. Retain the original S omission, primary/unit convention, all natural zeros and fixed holes. The actual normalized polynomials are

    M_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/E),
    S_u(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/E).

Q_u is the COMPLETE original product of disjoint prime slots of total width v. Its count is fixed before U, its individual heights remain independent, and its original coefficients, supports and holes stay literal. PR9 B0.3--4 and B3.31 permit arbitrary bounded row-independent prime coefficients in MI, with either common orientation and every subcollection. The additional band slot is in precisely that contract. Any licensed re-anchoring or whole conjugation is done to the whole system first; an unrelated moving character is not inserted into a prime coefficient.

Let beta=2a-1 be the selected INTERNAL buffered grade. It may exceed physical delta. The retained same-family upper bound keeps beta<=3/4, while beta>=delta-small. PR9 B0.13--20 and the already reviewed [research revision]/[research revision] interface give

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E;V)|^2 <= H_J U^epsilon_det E^beta,
                    0<E<=C D.                         (R1)

The direct line a+6e suffices for the second inequality. V ranges over the stated common smooth family and finite derivative profiles, at retained heights. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded dilations; scales below a fixed positive constant are empty. H_J is a polynomial in the height bounds, independent of the arithmetic thresholds below. Its fixed degree may increase between inequalities.

Keep beta in BOTH inequalities until D^beta cancels. Weakening the spike to D^delta earlier would leave an uncontrolled D^(beta-delta). No larger internal grade is used as a physical slot price.

Put A=U^(2eta), Y=U^(4eta), and let P_band be the fixed band of good prime IDEALS with A<=Np<=Y. Define

    ell_B(b)=sum_(p in P_band) v_p(b) log Np,
    theta(b)=ell_B(b)/log Nb, Nb>1; theta(1)=0.

The additive function is ell_B, not theta: ell_B(bc)=ell_B(b)+ell_B(c), with shared valuations counted. For example theta(p)=theta(p^2)=1 when p is in the band, so theta itself cannot be expanded additively. The original plain annulus has Nb>1 for sufficiently large U.

For any complete tuple polynomial, superscript[theta] means multiplying each original tuple coefficient by theta of its PLAIN ideal before signed merging. It is not a norm projection. With

    V_D(x)=W_P(x) log D/log(Dx),

the exact identity is

    S^[theta](D)
      =1/log D sum_(p in P_band,j>=1) log Np phi_u(p^j)
                  (Np)^(-j/2) S(D/(Np)^j;V_D).        (R2)

For every p, its j=1,...,v_p(b) terms contribute exactly v_p(b)log Np. Complete multiplicativity includes natural zero values, so no nonzero-character division is needed. The normalizations in R2 are exact. The denominator is log Nb, not an approximation by log D: V_D retains the exact ratio. On the fixed annulus log(Dx) is comparable to log D, and its finitely many Euler, real and log-scale derivatives are uniformly bounded in the given positive m range.

## 3. First powers: common profile, height buffer and one new slot

For j=1 fix a dyad P<=Np<2P, retaining the literal band endpoints in its arithmetic support. Then A/2<=P<=Y. Let E=D/P, y=Np/P and z=Nc/E. The first-power summand is exactly

    D^(-1/2) sum_(p,c) phi_u(p)phi_u(c)
                       (log Np/log D) V_D(yz),        (R3)

and P^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). There is no unpriced factor P^(1/2).

Apply the literal common-profile lemma B3.3 on an ambient compact box in y,z, with larger individual cutoffs equal to one on the entire current support. This box and its Fourier measure are fixed BEFORE a current row, prime, slot label or coloring is selected. The sharp band membership and every arithmetic hole remain in row-independent outer coefficients. The measure has a finite weighted L1 norm controlled by finitely many common seminorms; no prime-specific Fourier measure is chosen.

For clarity about heights, first write the original witness twist explicitly. If W_P(x)=W_0(x)x^(sigma+i gamma), then

    (yz)^(sigma+i gamma)=y^(sigma+i gamma)z^(sigma+i gamma).

Separate the remaining smooth kernel W_0(yz) log D/log(Dyz), with the bounded real power either retained there or factored as above. Thus high Fourier decay is a property of a kernel whose derivative constants do NOT grow as |gamma|^N. The original gamma appears explicitly in both output tests. A two-coordinate version of B3.3 has Fourier coordinates tau_1,tau_2; the plain upper bound is used at gamma+tau_2, and the new MI slot retains gamma+tau_1. Original slot heights stay independent. Nothing forces the new frequency to be a zero height.

Use only a fixed small fraction of the available retained height buffer for these frequencies. The actual witness lies at |gamma|<=3^i T_ht, while B_(i+1)<a+2e controls the larger box through 3^(i+1)T_ht. The original B0.14--15 contour padding therefore accommodates the retained frequency shift without changing i, a, beta, phi or the chosen zero. The loss, smooth orders and finite list of height coordinates are fixed beforehand.

Here is an exact way to pay the ENTIRE Fourier complement. Use the source's internal floor T_ht>=U^kappa with fixed kappa>0. For |tau_2| above its reserved fraction of T_ht, absolute ideal counting gives |S_u(E;V)|<=C E^(1/2), uniformly in the imaginary twist. Since E<=C D is polynomially bounded, E^((1-beta)/2)<=U^C0 for a fixed C0. Choose a fixed J1>C0/kappa. Then

    E^(1/2) <=C E^(beta/2)(1+|tau_2|)^J1

on that complement. Bounded nonempty subunit E obey the same inequality by constants. On the retained frequencies use R1. The unconditioned MI already has polynomial cost in tau_1 and the original heights. The complete Fourier integral is therefore bounded by a weighted L1 norm of the SAME height-free kernel, with weight degree J1 plus the fixed MI degree. B3.3 makes this finite uniformly in U,D and the current labels. No Fourier piece or arithmetic term is discarded, and no tail is inferred merely from a large nominal height.

For the source height choices, first fix the MI/Sobolev degree J0 and the real/bin losses, then choose the internal small height range so its U^(J0*kappa) cost fits the allocated loss. The extra high derivatives just used belong to the height-free separation kernel; they do not increase this previously fixed MI height degree. Below the internal floor use the dictionary at that floor. Above the original small polynomial range a larger final external height degree pays the absolute source bound. The external physical height exponent is chosen after that degree. The original detector's contour tails retain their accepted B-before-N order. This full-integral implementation supplies the author's separation step without a circular height/decay choice or a new high-height theorem.

For scale differentiation, use log Np/log U as the FIXED prime coefficient and place log U/log D=1/m outside the prime sum. Its derivatives are bounded because m stays in a fixed positive interval. Neither the band membership nor a live arithmetic prime coefficient is differentiated with D. Derivatives of V_D and the cutoff profiles remain in the finite smooth family. Any rowwise real/height/scale evaluation is dominated by tensor Sobolev on fixed rectangles, followed by MI on its derivative profiles. The dominance signal below is not asserted for derivatives; only the positive majorant is differentiated.

In each separated term, apply the shortened plain upper bound R1 FIRST. The remaining positive norm is the inverse times the full original Q and the new prime slot at scale P. Put lambda=log_U P<=4eta+small. The actual gates are

    r+2(v+lambda)
       <=1-1017/100000+8/1000+small
        =1-217/100000+small,
    2r+8(v+lambda)
       <=2-2(1017/100000)+4/20+32/1000+small
        =3-39417/50000+small.                         (R4)

Both margins are fixed and positive on the entire G137 window, including v=0 and the plain kink. Every further inverse shortening improves them. The added slot count is fixed, not a growing amplifier. No physical slot price U^lambda is substituted for MI.

When the slot supports are disjoint, MI and R1 yield

    ||M(R)Q * first-power dyad||_Omega^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta P^(-beta).          (R5)

The restricted row set is enlarged only inside the remaining positive MI norm. Every extracted row-dependent phase is a contraction there, not a new moving column coefficient. Section4 supplies the disjoint-support reduction needed for every actual dyad.

## 4. Every new/old collision, all higher powers and the full product

The original prime pools are pairwise disjoint. Partition the new dyadic pool into the part outside their union and its intersections with each original pool. There are only a fixed number of pieces. The outside piece meets the MI contract immediately. On an intersection with pool i, use the exact split p=q and p!=q, where p is the new prime and q the prime chosen by the old slot i.

For p=q, remove that old slot and extract its prime exactly. Write P_i0 for its original central scale. The coefficient mass after applying R1 to S(D/Np) is bounded by

    sum_(p in intersection) (P_i0 Np)^(-1/2)
                  * (D/Np)^(beta/2)
       <=C D^(beta/2) P^(-beta/2),                   (R6)

because the fixed annuli force P_i0 comparable to P and there are O(P) prime ideals, by the elementary ideal count. The remaining old slots satisfy MI with strictly easier gates. The exact phase phi_u(p)^2 is a contraction, including its zero value. An inverse term may contain p; this interaction is left to the literal original MI and is not declared coprime. Thus the diagonal satisfies R5.

For p!=q, independently color the prime IDEALS of the finite original pool i with two fair colors. For the resulting disjoint sets E0,E1,

    1_(p!=q)=4 E_color[1_(p in E0)1_(q in E1)].       (R7)

For p=q the right side is zero; for distinct ideals its event has probability1/4. Distinct prime ideals of equal norm remain distinct color labels. Coloring by norm would fail: two different ideals of norm7 would always have the same color, incorrectly giving zero for their off-diagonal pair.

For each coloring, the two supports are now disjoint; every other original pool remains disjoint from both. Each coefficient is bounded, fixed and row independent. The SAME uniform MI estimate applies to every coloring, by B0.4/B3.31's arbitrary-coefficient contract. Hilbert Minkowski under the normalized probability measure gives

    ||4 E_color F_color|| <=4 E_color ||F_color||,

so the norm cost is4, not 2 raised to the pool size. Squaring changes only a fixed constant. This is a finite coefficient identity followed by a uniform moment estimate; no independence or randomness of character values is asserted. All natural zeros, fixed holes, original slot coefficients and independent heights remain in the colored sums.

A new prime cannot collide with two old slots because the original pools are disjoint. The above pieces therefore exhaust every new/old collision. The construction is specified on each full finite pool before live primes are selected, and it costs only the fixed original slot count plus the scalar4.

For j>=2 in R2, first apply R1 to S(D/(Np)^j); only then take absolute values of the extracted prime sum. With the complete old Q retained inside MI, the dyadic coefficient mass is

    sum_(p in dyad) (Np)^(-j(1+beta)/2)
        <= C P^(1-j(1+beta)/2)
        <= C P^(-beta), j>=2.                        (R8)

The ratios of successive j bounds are at most a fixed negative power of P. The complete prime-power sum therefore converges geometrically; on actual support it is also a finite O_eta(1) list. Its squared norm costs at most H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta A^(-2beta), which is better than the first-power bound. Collisions of these extracted powers with Q or the inverse need no omission: phi_u(p^j) is removed only as a row contraction after the pointwise plain bound, while the original complete Q stays inside MI.

Summing dyads by Hilbert triangle costs logarithms absorbed in the prescribed loss. This proves the actual full-source estimate

    ||M S^[theta] Q||_Omega^2
        <=H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta A^(-beta).         (R9)

It is independent of the old gcd/square removal. No prime-number asymptotic, density of smooth numbers, canonical extra column, or unproved improved MI is needed.

## 5. Weighted extracted blocks and the complete old core

For a fixed extracted ideal L put E=D/NL. The remaining plain factor with the original multiplier is

    S_(theta,L)(E)=E^(-1/2) sum_c phi_u(c)
                                W_P(Nc/E)theta(Lc).

Let ell_B(L) denote its band logarithm. Then EXACTLY

    S_(theta,L)(E)
      =ell_B(L)/log D * S(E;V_D)
       +1/log D sum_(p in P_band,j>=1)log Np phi_u(p^j)
                       (Np)^(-j/2) S(E/(Np)^j;V_D).  (R10)

The denominator is correct since log(NL Nc)=log(D(Nc/E)). Even when p divides L, the first term counts its valuations already in L and the sum counts EVERY additional valuation in c. For L=p,c=p with a band prime, those two contributions are both log Np; omitting their intersection would incorrectly replace theta(p^2)=1 by1/2.

Nonempty support forces NL<=C D, so ell_B(L)/log D<=1+O(1/log D). Applying the SAME buffered upper bound R1 gives first-power dyadic mass at most P^((1-beta)/2); higher powers obey R8. Since beta<1 and is bounded away from1, their complete sum is at most a constant times Y^((1-beta)/2), with harmless logarithmic losses. Therefore uniformly in L,

    |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|
       <=H_J U^epsilon (D/NL)^(beta/2)
                              Y^((1-beta)/2).        (R11)

Nonempty subunit factors have only bounded columns and obey the same estimate; empty factors stay zero. The squared cost is Y^(1-beta), exactly once. This is a uniform estimate on the literal extracted plain blocks. It is NOT an operator-norm assertion for multiplying arbitrary signed coefficients by theta.

In the old exact source split B=M S=B_g+B_s+B_c, take G=U^(4eta), H=U^(2eta). The high-gcd part has N(a,b)>=G; the second part has N(a,b)<G and N s2(b)>=H. Their expansions use L=q, L=k^2 and L=lcm(q,k^2), respectively. The inverse mask is restored using every q-smooth power as in the prior frozen proof. Theta depends only on b and does not alter that restoration.

For the intersection, q is squarefree and

    L=lcm(q,k^2)=q k^2/(q,k),
    w_beta(q,k)=(Nq)^(-1/2)(NL)^(-(1+beta)/2).

The full common-prime correction is retained. The prior reviewed absolute sum gives norm mass G^(-beta/2)H^(-beta), including d=(q,k) with Nd>H. Insert R11 BEFORE its absolute convolution; its Y factor is uniform in q,k,L and can be extracted once. This proves

    ||B_g^[theta] Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta G^(-beta)Y^(1-beta),
    ||B_gs^[theta] Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                    G^(-beta)H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta),
    ||B_s^[theta] Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta H^(-2beta)Y^(1-beta). (R12)

The last line uses the complete signed identity between the weighted square-divisor term and weighted intersection. No assumption that the two divisibilities are independent is made. All shared primes from the band, the extracted L, the remaining plain ideal and the inverse mask are included in R10 and the exact lcm formula.

Now B_c^[theta]=B^[theta]-B_g^[theta]-B_s^[theta]. Hilbert triangle, R9 and R12 yield

    ||B_c^[theta]Q||^2 <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
       [A^(-beta)+(G^(-beta)+H^(-2beta))Y^(1-beta)].   (R13)

At the stated parameters, the squared savings are 2beta eta and (8beta-4)eta. Their difference is (6beta-4)eta, which is positive for beta>2/3. The allowed small internal-buffer error can be chosen below this fixed gap. At beta=17/25, the two coefficients are34/25 and36/25, with remaining reserve9/25 above the requested coefficient1. Hence

    ||B_c^[theta]Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*eta+epsilon).          (R14)

This pays the COMPLETE weighted core, not a selected subset of a previously bounded signed polynomial. Root's acceptance of the prior removal resolves the author's pending local dependency; the original analytic admissions remain source-relative.

## 6. Actual new rows and the exhaustive residual

Retain the old disjoint paid classes Omega_g,Omega_s first. On their complement Omega_c, the SAME chosen functions obey |B_c|>|B|/2. Define

    Omega_band={u in Omega_c: |B_c^[theta]|>=|B_c|/2}.

On this actual class, |M Q|<=4|B_c^[theta]Q|/|S(D)|. Divide only by the ORIGINAL unshifted lower bound in R1. The D^beta factor cancels before beta is weakened to physical delta. Thus

    sum_(Omega_band) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2
       <=H_J U^(1-2delta*eta+epsilon).               (R15)

The entire slot product stays in the inverse moment; Q is never divided out. This class is disjoint from the two prior paid classes by definition. The class predicate is about the original values, not derivative signals or reselected witnesses.

Every remaining row has the exact strict signal

    |B_c^[1-theta]|>|B_c|/2>|M S|/4,                 (R16)
    1-theta(b)=log N(b_outside_band)/log Nb.           (R17)

All old tuple cuts, masks, signs, real powers, heights and prime-slot tuples survive. It vanishes when b is supported entirely in the band. A band prime cannot occur twice in b within this original core: Np>=A=H and p^2|b would imply N s2(b)>=H. This fact does not remove the higher powers from R2 or R10; those complete source/intersection expansions were paid before subtraction.

The old repeat-factor bound remains N(n/rad n)<G H^2 NP. More importantly, a good prime plain ideal b at scale D has Nb>Y for sufficiently large U, since m>4eta. For a coprime squarefree inverse tuple it survives the core and has theta(b)=0. This is a surviving coefficient example, not a constructed high-zero row or lower bound for the signed norm.

The full coarse estimate is still paid: B_c^[1-theta]=B_c-B_c^[theta], the previous complete norm for B_c is H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon), and R14 is smaller. Triangle gives that same complete coarse bound for the residual. Its quarter-signal and R1 leave only U^(1+epsilon) for the original inverse moment. Therefore J_eta^all remains OPEN. The statement0<=theta<=1 gives no signed-subset norm monotonicity and cannot close R16.

## 7. Specialization to the frozen joint-cut proof

The prior review, now accepted by root, proves a coupled cut with

    F(a,b)=N(a,b)*(N s2(b))^2,
    B_T: F(a,b)>=T,   C_T: F(a,b)<T,
    B=B_T+C_T.

Here T is fixed before witnesses. Its exact coefficient is

    A_T(q,k)=sum_(d|q,e|k)mu(q/d)mu(k/e)
                                  1_(Nd*(Ne)^2>=T),

and B_T has the literal blocks M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/NL) with L=lcm(q,k^2), coefficient A_T(q,k)mu(q)phi_u(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL), and all q-smooth restorations. The prior full positive coefficient mass is U^epsilon T^(-beta/2). Its proof retains shared primes and beta<1; it does not use independent divisibility.

This EXACTLY meets the author's conditional interface. Apply R10--11 inside each block, then its already proved absolute convolution. Thus

    ||B_T^[theta]Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta).

The exact subtraction C_T^[theta]=B^[theta]-B_T^[theta] and R9 imply

    ||C_T^[theta]Q||^2
       <=H_J U^(1+epsilon)D^beta
                     [A^(-beta)+T^(-beta)Y^(1-beta)]. (R18)

At T=Y=U^(4eta), this again saves2beta eta. This corollary applies the frozen theorem and the author's new estimate; it neither reopens that frozen scope nor assumes a generic coefficient multiplier theorem.

Keep the prior three paid classes FIRST: the old gcd class, the disjoint old square class, and the additional joint-cut dominance class on their complement. On the remaining class the prior proof has |C_T|>|B|/2. Define the band class there by |C_T^[theta]|>=|C_T|/2. It saves2delta eta in the original inverse moment exactly as in R15. Every row outside all four paid classes retains

    |C_T^[1-theta]|>|M S|/4.                         (R19)

Its tuple coefficient has the SAME multiplier R17 and intrinsic necessary support

    N(n/rad n)<T NP=U^(4eta)NP.                      (R20)

Indeed the original bound N(ab/rad(ab))<=F(a,b) remains valid tuplewise. The slot product is squarefree, so multiplication by P adds at most NP to the repeat factor. ## 5. Other three selected tests and strongest scope restrictions

**S19.** A finite-prime inverse m_Y has m_Y*chi equal to chi(n) on Y-rough n and zero otherwise, with value1 at n=1. Thus delta-m_Y*chi is exactly -chi(n) for n>1, P^-(n)>Y. This retains prime powers and ramified zeros. Its absolute Dirichlet norm diverges at sigma<=1, already on the unramified primes. The known b>1 growing-depth inverse with a separately paid physical tail remains available; the trivial norm below1 fails. This is the [research revision]-W4/G78 boundary. The later G117 fixed-preconditioner theorem also covers this obstruction at its all-scale scope. No lower bound for the actual signed field follows.

**S14.** For T=[[rho,1],[0,rho]], d=1-rho^2, the reported positive P satisfies P-T*PT=I. Direct algebra gives det P=d^-2+d^-4 and trace P~2d^-3; hence lambda_max~2d^-3, lambda_min~(1/2)d^-1 and sqrt(cond P)~2/d as rho approaches1. The contraction inferred solely from this identity is sqrt(1-1/lambda_max). At rho=1 the eigenvalue1 forbids strict contraction in any positive metric. This prices a diagnostic's near-resonant conditioning; it is not a native-H transfer construction or an arithmetic lower bound. The exact checker used rho=1/3 and3/4, independently of the author's rho=1/2 case.

**S21.** The product-cutoff squarefree family IS a simplicial complex. For an unramified prime p, with T_p(x)=sum_(n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n), the full identity is

    M(x)=T_p(x)-chi(p)T_p(x/p)
        =sum_(x/p<n<=x,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)
           +(1-chi(p))T_p(x/p).

At q=5 with chi(2)=i, x=p=2, the value is1-i, the pure boundary is0 and the entire value lies in the twist bulk. The branch chi(p)=1 has no bulk term, but that does not transfer to all characters. For q=1,p=2 the unsigned boundary count is (2/pi^2)x+O(sqrt x), while its signed value is M(x). The classical complex/Betti correspondence is supported by [Bjorner, A Cell Complex in Number Theory, Theorem3.1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1101.5704). The result is already in A-SIMPLICIAL/W27, G94 and the frozen W54-X30 audit. No new topology theorem or all-topology impossibility follows. More global revisiting matchings stay eligible if their signed cost is actually proved.

## 5. Ordinary convexity and the separate I-HECKE improvement

Ordinary finite-order Hecke convexity gives
`h=(1-delta)/2` on `sigma=delta`, `0<delta<1`. It follows from the
ordinary functional equation in review [research revision] and absolute
convergence, with small boundary margins allocated to `epsilon`.
Equation (DC13) therefore proves (DC1). For
`K<=D^k0`, `C=D^gamma`, its exponent is
\[
\frac{11}{6}+\frac{7\gamma}{6}
 +\delta\left(k_0-\frac12-\frac\gamma2\right).
\]
At `k0=.87653`, the useful optimum is `delta` approaching zero,
giving `gamma=1/7` with arbitrary losses. For example,
`gamma=1/8`, `delta=1/32` give the strict exponent
`1.988980104166666...`.

For the stronger statement, invoke precisely the inherited I-HECKE
strip bound displayed in [research revision] T07:
\[
|L(\sigma+it,\eta)|
\ll q_{\mathfrak f_\eta}^{(b-\sigma)/2+\epsilon}(1+|t|)^A,
\qquad 1-b\le\sigma\le b,\quad b_0<b<1.
\]
Take the fixed positive line `sigma=1-b`, so `h=b-1/2`.
Equation (DC13) proves (DC2). The good conductor really is `ce`,
and all fixed factors affect only fixed constants on this strip.
This is a result relative to I-HECKE, not a consequence of ordinary
convexity or Riemann-zeta nonvanishing alone.

For `K<=D^k0`, `k0=.87653`, the limiting affordable cutoff is
\[
\boxed{
\gamma_*=
\frac{1/6+(1-k_0)c_0}{7/6-c_0}
=0.1748488627130781\ldots .
}
\tag{DC14}
\]
Choose `b>b0` close enough to `b0` in terms of the final loss,
allocate the other preliminary losses, and only then vary the scales.
This proves affordability at `C=D^gamma_*` with `D^(2+epsilon)`.
For the fixed rational buffer `b=7/8`, the exact cutoff is
`gamma=(7-3k0)/25=437041/2500000=.1748164`.

Within these available pointwise row bounds, the useful optimal line
is `1-b`: above it, the increased row-length cost dominates the
conductor saving at the relevant core ranges; below it, the
functional-equation conductor cost increases faster. The ordinary
convexity endpoint is similarly `delta` approaching zero. These are
limitations of the obtained upper budgets, not lower bounds for the
actual signed form.

statement:
## 4. D3 / S16: how much a small-prime syndrome can certify

Two elementary tests distinguish a probabilistic coding analogy from actual arithmetic.

First, on {0,1}^k let a syndrome be any linear map H over F2 whose row span does not contain the all-ones parity vector. Uniform measure on the even-parity hyperplane and uniform measure on the odd-parity hyperplane have exactly the SAME uniform syndrome distribution on im H; their parity biases are+1 and-1. Each syndrome fiber has equally many extensions of both parities before conditioning, because parity is independent of the rows of H. Their syndrome entropies and all statistics of that syndrome coincide. Thus entropy or a uniform syndrome alone does not control a missing parity character. This is a finite model obstruction, not an arithmetic lower bound.

For an ACTUAL arithmetic obstruction fix a principal character modulo q, let N grow, set y=sqrt(N), and partition S_N by the complete set of unramified prime divisors<=y. Let C0 be the cell with empty set. Since two primes>sqrt(N) have product>N,

    C0={1} union {p:sqrt(N)<p<=N,p not dividing q}.

Write L=#(C0 minus{1}), Q=#S_N. The signs in C0 are+1 at1 and-1 at each of its L primes, so its mass is L+1, signed sum1-L and conditional mean(1-L)/(L+1). Define the exact conditional square norm of any partition P by

    E(P)=sum_(C in P) |sum_(n in C)a(n)|^2/|C|,
    |M_chi(N)|<=sqrt(Q*E(P)).                          (15)

For this partition, and every REFINEMENT of it, conditional Cauchy gives

    E(P)>=(L-1)^2/(L+1)=L-3+4/(L+1).                  (16)

Refinement cannot reduce the conditional square norm. This allows all cancellation in every other cell; no unproved assumption about rough-number parity is made.

Elementary square-divisor counting gives Q=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q>0. An elementary prime-count lower bound suffices for L>>N/log N: binomial(2m,m)>=4^m/(2m+1), while each prime contributes at most2m to its factorization, so binomial(2m,m)<=(2m)^pi(2m). Use m=floor(N/2) and subtract pi(sqrt N)<=sqrt N plus finitely many ramified primes. No prime-distribution hypothesis is used. Therefore the NUMERIC RIGHT SIDE of the norm certificate(15) is at least

    sqrt(Q*E(P)) >>_q N/sqrt(log N).                   (17)

It cannot prove any fixed exponent gamma<1 by estimating E(P) from above. The target E(P)<<N^(2gamma-1+epsilon) is false for this observation, because(16) already has exponent1. For current gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 those putative E exponents are .74970,2/3,1/2. All fail for this particular positive conditional-square certificate.

This is NOT a lower bound for |M|. Coarsening cells so that terminal primes interact with other small-prime patterns, retaining cross-cell signed terms, or choosing an unrelated syndrome lies outside the obstruction. An arbitrary linear syndrome need not refine the small-prime pattern; the first toy and the second arithmetic test have distinct scopes. For every ordinary chi, a successful complete scalar reconstruction with |M_chi(N)|<<N^(gamma+epsilon) would have the full all-height reciprocal return already proved above; the principal case alone prevents this proposed universal norm route.

G103/G117/G145 own full energy, fiber/readout and positive diagonal-price warnings; G105 owns exact future-support merging. The narrow proposed addition is the explicit actual empty-syndrome cell after complete small-prime revelation, allowing arbitrary cancellation elsewhere and any further refinement. No literature novelty for the sieve parity problem or conditional expectation is claimed.
title: 4. D3 / S16: how much a small-prime syndrome can certify

# [research revision]: paid parts of the separated mixed moment

[research revision] accepts G155–G157 relative to the same PR9 source contracts and
[research revision] separated witnesses. It proves a large-common-divisor estimate,
pays three disjoint sectors of the remaining norm, and adds an intrinsic
restriction on its repeated-prime support. The signed high-conductor
remainder and its full physical return remain **OPEN**. The accepted
written value stays

\[
c_{11}=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636.
\]

The density input is still \(K=28114053/6250000\), licensed from the
preceding c10 same-family ancestry. No recalibration from c11, new
formalization, kernel result or external record admission is claimed.

The [author](separated-mixed/report.md) and
[independent development](separated-mixed-review/report.md) give the
complete calculations. [Retention](retention-manifest.json) binds fifteen
unchanged artifacts and fourteen review inputs: six author files, six
mathematical ancestry inputs and two assignment records. The original
review freeze is preserved alongside its corrected metadata receipt.

## Fixed object and quantifiers

Use the original Eisenstein field, primary/unit convention, fixed excluded
set and finite dictionary. Write
\(\phi_u(n)=\nu(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1}\), retaining natural zeros. The fixed
factor \(\nu\) need not have order six; it remains in column coefficients
when the row character is summed. For fixed smooth profiles put

\[
M_u(D;W)=D^{-1/2}\sum_n\mu(n)\phi_u(n)W(Nn/D).
\]

Let Q be the actual product of the original prime slots. Their pools are
pairwise disjoint, their coefficients and natural zeros are unchanged,
and \(P_0=\prod_iP_i=U^v\), \(0\le v\le1/20\).
The slot pools may intersect either inverse. The elementary bound is
\(\sup_u|Q_u|^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\). If inverse orientation is reversed,
align the **entire** slot product at the positive norm, including its
coefficients, zeros and heights; individual slot switching is unavailable.

The norm sums nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed nonnegative smooth
enclosing ball of scale U, with the licensed fixed ray/unit sectors. A
row divisor weight is dominated before expansion and Poisson. An
arbitrary row selector, zero predicate or signed physical projector is
not admitted into that free-row Poisson identity.

The physical box supplied by [G147–G148](../[research revision]/far-complement-integration.md)
is

\[
17/25\le\delta\le7/10,\quad17/20<r<47/50,\quad
33/25<s<141/100,\quad s-r>3/8,\qquad D_1=U^r,D_2=U^s.
\]

Both inverse heights are independent. Their same-zero, same-annulus and
plain-complement restrictions remain those of the actual G147 witness;
enlarging its exponent set to this box is only for bounding the norm.
The internal buffer \(\delta_b\) may exceed .70; extract the signal there
before weakening to physical \(\delta\). Slot pricing uses physical
\(\delta\), not that internal buffer.

Use the existing common mesh and buffer **before** eventual arithmetic
family and slot choices. Then fix the allowed dictionary/slot data,
profiles, derivative orders, auxiliary losses and height choices before
the eventual large-U threshold. This is the reviewer's corrected order;
the author's abbreviated list is not permission to tune mesh after
seeing a family. Every implied constant has exactly this fixed-data
dependence. The UM slack is chosen before applying the original moment.

Tensor Sobolev covers the common bounded real parameter, both independent
inverse heights, the original slot heights and logarithmic scales. Scale
derivatives replace W by -W/2-yW'; other derivatives retain the original
twists and add fixed logarithmic factors. The tuple gcd threshold is
fixed at U and is not differentiated. Write q/h sums over a fixed global
support bound and use Hilbert Minkowski before the rowwise supremum.
For a common product profile, B3.3 fixes its Fourier measure on the whole
ambient box before any row or q label; keep both Fourier coordinates
distinct. Choose derivative orders backward through the bounded
dependency graph, and Fourier decay only after the raw polynomial label
count and all height orders are known. G147 already pays the genuine
detector tails and both frozen profile families; no completed divisor
identity is silently truncated here.

For reference, with \(h=5-2\delta\), put

\[
\rho=1-\frac{10\delta}{3h},\quad k=\rho+\delta-1,\quad
D_K=15K-10-6K\delta,
\]
\[
a_K=\frac{\delta(5-6\delta)^2}{3hD_K},\quad
b_K=\frac{2\delta(5-6\delta)(K-1)}{D_K},\quad
E_K=\rho+\delta v-\min(3kv,a_K+b_Kv),\quad
T=\delta(r+s)+E_K.
\]

Here \(E_K\ge\rho\ge19/54\), because
\(\delta-3k=4\delta^2/(5-2\delta)>0\). Consequently
\(T\ge123353/67500\). H_J denotes the fixed Sobolev/height envelope.

## G155. Actual large-common-divisor saving

Set \(B=M(D_1)M(D_2)\). Cut its original ordered tuples by
\(N\gcd(d_1,d_2)\ge G\), **before** merging coefficients. This is not a
slot cut or a row selector. Define

\[
a_G(q)=\sum_{d\mid q,\,Nd\ge G}\mu(q/d).
\]

Divisor inversion gives \(\sum_{q\mid g}a_G(q)=1_{Ng\ge G}\),
\(a_G(q)=0\) for \(Nq<G\), and \(|a_G(q)|\le d(q)\).
Only squarefree q survive the two original Möbius factors. With
\(d_1=qx,d_2=qy\), their product is
\(\mu(x)\mu(y)1_{(x,q)=1}1_{(y,q)=1}\); no condition \((x,y)=1\) is
inserted. Thus the exact centrally normalized identity is

\[
B_{\ge G}(u)=\sum_{\substack{q\ \mathrm{squarefree}\\Nq\ge G}}
\frac{a_G(q)\phi_u(q)^2}{Nq}
M_u^{(q)}(D_1/Nq)M_u^{(q)}(D_2/Nq),                 \tag{G155.1}
\]

where superscript q means the literal coprimality mask. Fixed profile
support bounds \(Nq\ll D_1\). Natural zeros are kept, never divided out.

Restore each mask exactly:

\[
M_u^{(q)}(E;W)=
\sum_{h\ q\text{-smooth}}\frac{\phi_u(h)}{\sqrt{Nh}}
M_u(E/Nh;W).                                        \tag{G155.2}
\]

Primewise this is \(\mu*(1,1,\ldots)=(1,0,\ldots)\). It restores the
original Möbius coefficients, so the invoked moment is PR9 B0.9, not a
new moment for \(\mu*\mu\). All h shorten the scales. The finitely
supported sums may be dominated using
\(\prod_{\mathfrak p\mid q}(1-N\mathfrak p^{-1/2})^{-1}\ll(Nq)^\epsilon\).
A retained polynomially bounded puncture R0 is handled by qR0, within
the already frozen family. Nonempty subunit scales are bounded away
from zero by fixed profile support; smaller scales are empty.

Minkowski over q and both h, the trivial first-inverse bound and
\(\|M(E)\|_U^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon[U+U^{1/6}E^{5/6}]\) give

\[
\|B_{\ge G}Q\|_U^2\ll H_JU^{v+\epsilon}\frac{D_1}{G}
\left[U+U^{1/6}(D_2/G)^{5/6}\right].                 \tag{G155.3}
\]

The q-shell mass \(\sum|a_G(q)|/Nq\) is subpower; the shortened-scale
factors decrease geometrically. With \(G=U^{1/5}\), the second bracket
term dominates throughout the box and the exponent is
\(v+r+5s/6-1/5\). The target gap is at least

\[
\rho+(47/20)\delta-393/200\ge2809/273000>1/100.
\]

The derivative is \(47/20-50/[3(5-2\delta)^2]>0\). An independent exact
Bernstein certificate verifies this on the whole interval. Reserving
1/1000 for geometric pads and 1/500 for all auxiliary losses still
leaves a retained norm margin 1/200 and spare \(5/2184\).

On actual witnesses, where \(|B|^2\ge U^{\delta(r+s)-\eta}\), rows with
\(|B_{\ge G}|\ge|B|/2\) have the paid slot mass exponent
\(E_K-1/200+\epsilon\), after choosing the losses. Otherwise
\(|B_{<G}|\ge|B|/2\). The full norm also satisfies
\(\|BQ\|^2\le2\|B_{<G}Q\|^2+2\|B_{\ge G}Q\|^2\), which pays every
large/small cross once the remaining norm is bounded. A cross-term
estimate alone is not that remaining norm bound.

## G156. Complete diagonal and two off-diagonal sectors

Merge only after the tuple cut:

\[
B_{<G}(u)Q_u=\sum_n c(n)\psi_u(n)^{\pm1},\qquad
n=d_1d_2\prod_ip_i,\quad N_0=D_1D_2P_0.
\]

The coefficient c contains every Möbius sign, fixed character, pool,
profile, independent height, normalization and original tuple gcd cut.
Each prime valuation of n is 0,1,2 or3, including all collisions. Hence
\(n/n'\) is a sixth power as an ideal only when \(n=n'\): the valuation
difference lies in [-3,3]. Finite unit/root phases remain in their fixed
sectors. This fact does not apply to older completions with unbounded
prime powers. Divisor bounds give
\(|c(n)|\ll H_JN_0^{-1/2}U^\epsilon\) and
\(\sum_n|c(n)|^2\ll H_JU^\epsilon\). The **complete** paired diagonal is
therefore \(O(H_JU^{1+\epsilon})\); this is not a lower bound for the full
norm.

For an off-diagonal pair let \(e_{\mathfrak p}=v_{\mathfrak p}(n)-
v_{\mathfrak p}(n')\), let q_j be the radical of primes with
\(|e_{\mathfrak p}|=j\), and write

\[
Q_j=Nq_j,\quad Q=Q_1Q_2Q_3,\quad V=Q_1Q_2^2Q_3^3.
\]

Retain the full oriented integer vector. Although signs +3 and -3 have
the same sextic phase, their integer ratios differ; the finite allocation
cost must not be discarded. Every nonzero exponent has nonprincipal
primitive local phase at a good prime. The fixed factor \(\nu\) stays
in c and is not falsely treated as order six.

Write \(n=ga,n'=gb,(a,b)=1\). Then \(NaNb=V\) and
\(Ng\ll N_0/\sqrt V\), so for one full relative vector

\[
\sum_{(n,n')\text{ inducing it}}|c(n)c(n')|
\ll H_JU^\epsilon V^{-1/2}.
\]

This includes all shared slot/inverse collisions. Counting vectors in
fixed dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 boxes gives mass
\(\ll H_JU^\epsilon(Q_1/Q_3)^{1/2}\). Empty subunit gcd ranges remain
empty, with fixed endpoint constants retained.

The row kernel includes **all** natural-zero holes E from shared primes
whose character phases cancel, and all retained frozen punctures not
already in the primitive conductor. Cancellation of phase does not
remove a hole. Here NE is polynomial in U. Applying the existing masked
Poisson formula, whose primitive prefactor is X/\(\sqrt Q\) and dual
scale XNh/Q, gives \(\min(X,\sqrt Q)\), with zero dual term absent.
Expand sixth-power-freeness and full holes by
\(b^6\mid u\) and \(d\mid\operatorname{rad}E\), respectively, putting
\(X=U/((Nb)^6Nd)\). Splitting at
\(Nb=(U/(Nd\sqrt Q))^{1/6}\) yields

\[
|\mathcal K(n,n')|\ll H_JU^\epsilon
\min(U,U^{1/6}Q^{5/12}).                              \tag{G156.1}
\]

The hole Euler product with exponent -1/6 is subpower. Thresholds below
one use the complete tail; conductor-sharing natural zeros and fixed
excluded/ray sectors are retained. Finitely many inducing free-row
deletions cost O(1) per kernel, already absorbed. This is not a blanket
deletion license for the raw physical row set.

Separate the paired sum disjointly: full diagonal; then Q≤\(U^{9/5}\);
then the remaining pairs with \(Q_1/Q_3\le U^{8/5}\). The low-Q sum uses
V≥Q and the divisor count to sum \(Q^{-1/12+\epsilon}\); its total is
\(\ll H_JU^{109/60+\epsilon}\). The ratio sector uses the U branch of
(G156.1) and costs \(\ll H_JU^{9/5+\epsilon}\), with every Q2 and all
holes included. Polynomial conductor ranges cost only logarithmic boxes.

| Paid part | Exponent | Minimum gap below T | Spare after .001+.002+.005 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete diagonal | 1 | 55853/67500 | 55313/67500 |
| Total conductor Q≤U^(9/5) | 109/60 | 182/16875 | 47/16875 |
| Remaining ratio Q1/Q3≤U^(8/5) | 9/5 | 1853/67500 | 1313/67500 |

Each raw gap exceeds 1/100 and pays the retained 1/200 margin. These are
upper bounds for paid sectors, using absolute values there; no sign or
positivity is asserted for the residual. Masked Poisson and relative-mass
machinery are reused from the exact PR9/[research revision] sources, rather than
counted as newly proved general theorems.

## G157. Repeated-prime support and the exact remaining estimate

The independent reviewer strengthens the actual small-gcd support.
For a surviving original tuple write \(d_1=gx,d_2=gy\), with g,x,y
pairwise coprime squarefree, and let \(p=\prod_ip_i\), squarefree by
disjoint original pools. Set

\[
A=(g,p),\quad b=(xy,p),\quad g=Ag_0,\quad xy=bz,
\quad p=Abp_0,\quad B=g_0b,\quad C=zp_0.
\]

Then A,B,C are pairwise coprime squarefree and

\[
n=A^3B^2C,\qquad n/\operatorname{rad}n=A^2B=gAb,
\qquad Ab\mid p.
\]

These radicals are intrinsic to the merged n, even when many tuples
contribute to c(n). Thus \(N(n/\operatorname{rad}n)<CGP_0\). Comparing
two such columns, the local valuation table gives
\(q_2q_3^2\mid(n/\operatorname{rad}n)(n'/\operatorname{rad}n')\) and
\(q_3\mid A(n)A(n')\). Consequently

\[
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\qquad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.           \tag{G157.1}
\]

At maximal v the exponents are 1/2 and1/10. Fixed profile constants
require arbitrarily small geometric pads, rather than literal unpadded
finite-U cutoffs. Profile derivatives, independent heights and the
fixed positive common-profile integrals preserve this support. This is
an exact new support fact, not a signed norm saving by itself.

Let \(\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\) be the real ordered off-diagonal paired sum
remaining after G156, with the actual coefficients c(n)\(\overline{c(n')}\)
and full kernels. It has

\[
n\ne n',\quad Q>U^{9/5},\quad Q_1/Q_3>U^{8/5},\quad
Q_2Q_3^2<CU^{2/5+2v},\quad Q_3\le CU^{2v}.
\]

The same definition includes the fixed finite derivative sum and positive
common-profile measure needed for the Sobolev envelope. The necessary
open hypothesis is the **one-sided** estimate

\[
\mathcal R_{\rm mix}\le H_JU^{T-\xi+\epsilon}
\quad\text{for some fixed }\xi>0,                    \tag{OPEN-MIX-RES}
\]

uniformly over the licensed fixed data and both independent heights.
Absolute value would be a stronger optional target, not a proved or
necessary replacement. The residual need not be positive.

This estimate would complete G148 OPEN-MIX with a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200)\). Combining the actual separated witness and G147
counted prefix then requires a margin below
\(\min(\xi,1/200,1/2000)\), with every witness, height and buffer loss
chosen from that strict slack. It still does not pay the full raw or
positive-child physical return: both signed coprimality projectors,
family reconstruction, root/slot holes, fixed inducing and exceptional
rows, physical radii/amplifier, clipped rectangles, shifted/shortened
Euler families, principal terms and the actual supremum/common mesh
all retain their previous obligations. The centered reserve is unspent.

## Strongest surviving obstruction and the next attack

With zero slots and squarefree n, the actual coefficient already contains

\[
c(n)=(D_1D_2)^{-1/2}\mu(n)\nu(n)
\sum_{d\mid n}W_1(Nd/D_1)W_2(N(n/d)/D_2),
\]

with the two independent twists on their respective divisors. This
divisor-profile coefficient is outside the original canonical B3.6
Möbius moment. Squarefree coprime pairs can have \(Q_1\asymp N_0^2\),
Q2=Q3=1 and tuple gcd1; none of (G157.1) removes them. The available
absolute envelope UN0 is too large. That is an obstruction to this
upper-bound method, not an actual lower bound for the whole signed norm
or a realized high-zero configuration. Same-zero coupling supplies no
probabilistic independence.

The next useful step is an identity or correlation estimate for this
signed divisor-profile source, possibly after extracting the now-short
repeated-prime part. Further clean Poisson bounds or cutoff optimization
alone do not address this squarefree sector. A replacement source is
also admissible if it brings its own complete bridge and pays its terms.

Root read both complete reports, both helpers and receipts, checked exact
input hashes, and reviewed the literal moment/Poisson source slices.
Finite diagnostics retain independent nonconstant profiles and natural
zeros, plus all eight local valuation configurations and64 paired cases.
They check algebra and budgets; the written argument supplies the
analytic content. Inherited F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot
uniformity and external admission remain open. The original29 families,
109 children and all later mechanisms remain preserved.
