Natural unmasked conductor is <=K Nw with K fixed. Polynomial holes are paid by FM, not put inside K. For .7<=delta<=.75, the unchanged density

If W is nominally negative, an unsupported range is empty; bounded nonempty end windows use support padding. There is no bound of a nonempty population by a number less than one.

Relative to target (7), the paid second-projector allocation and paired pointwise estimate give exact excess

\[
 M(\rho-1)+\delta A+a(5-6\rho)

Use min(c,d)>=p>=R, rho+delta>1, 5rho>1 and L_c<=5(R-R0). Its middle line is at most (4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c, with coefficient <=-79/270. Its last terms are <=-delta*b2-t2 since g2<=b2. For case j, the remaining saving divided by M is

\]

\]

Its least value, at j=1, is **1/43200**. The explicit rounding charge (13/20)h_s=13/100000 is retained. No unrounded variable-amplifier estimate is substituted for this smaller reserve. Bins straddling .7 use the low branch at .7+O(e); density is used only above its supported lower endpoint. There is no gap between branches. ## 6. Extracted errors, zero rows and fixed-inducing return

An original extracted error has defect <=g+3a+w-w_o+eta and allowance >=w. Use the GLOBAL old removal price (3/4)/(9/2)=1/6, the same exact-width correction, original characters/holes and unrestricted zero-slot complement. With lambda>=3a/4, its reserves are a/4-g/6, 13a/4-g/6, 4a-g/6. Since a>=kz and g<=rz, conservative bounds are:

|---|---:|

| 6, w=6lambda,w_o=0 | 1717/80000 |
| 7, w=7lambda,w_o=lambda | 1061/40000 |

The zero-power hole and valuation-one/seven moving prime characters stay in the old source. The prime average remains normalized; no second count or improved moment is used.

The first zero frequency uses the original powerful-product count. The added zero Gauss row is unamplified with its -s0 allowance. Second zero excess is <=A-M+5a+O(eta). For the paired fixed-inducing children retain the exceptional predicate, masks, forced congruences, raw scalars and whole-product norm power. At the ACTUAL radius (6), B3.75 is

\[
 F_1=\begin{cases}
 (c+5d+R+E)/6+B_c-4a-5\omega/6,&c\ge d,\\

Thus F1>=2c/3-4a-O(eta) and F2>=2b2/3. For v=c+min(c2,d2) and comparison length M/4,

\[
 \max_{v\ge0}\{A-5M/6-2v/3-(M/4-v)_+\}=A-M.
\]

The maximum is attained at v=M/4. The main fixed-inducing cost is therefore A-M+4a; the error-radius cost is A-M+9a. The exact main coefficient is -4a, not -5a. Leading terms cancel because the comparison retains identical total product, profiles, holes, whole character and norm power, including independent heights.

For m=4,5,9, the interval reserve satisfies

\[

These expressions increase with j and give:

|---|---:|

| Main fixed-inducing (m=4) | 7497/100000 |
| Error fixed-inducing (m=9) | 8199/200000 |

All terminal a costs are fixed and explicitly paid. Original exceptional-energy hypotheses require positive physical radius and polynomial caps; both hold in all fifty cases. None is absorbed in an arbitrary epsilon.

## 7. Uniform closure and the exact remaining barrier of this mechanism

The smallest displayed reserve is 1/150000. Choose total exponent loss below a strict fraction of it and the requested epsilon. Choose the original slot mesh, low/high bin buffers, radius/support pads and Fourier buffers from this common budget before the target dictionary. Finite original slot count affects constants and eventual threshold; aggregate annular tolerance tends to zero and is not an unpriced permanent loss per slot.

After a target family supplies the final density degree J, choose the DISTINCT external tau_out small enough for its polynomial height factors. The internal density tau_det is unchanged. Choose derivative and height orders backward through the finite graph, Fourier orders afterward, and one threshold last. FM supplies one integrable majorant for label-dependent scale parameters and a diagonal contraction of norm <=1. Very large independent input heights use a fixed sufficiently large polynomial height allowance to absorb the common bounded-geometry raw power. There is no extra height or label multiplicity.

Finally maximize constants/orders/thresholds over j=1,...,50 and the four derivative pairs. Both Cauchy steps average exponents; they do not double the already priced loss. Minkowski pays the original coefficient mass. Two-variable scale-supremum recovery proves (3). Since j depends on z/M rather than either plain scale, supremum differentiation never differentiates an atlas boundary. In the endpoint, varying the outer dyad or selected subset merely chooses another member of this same finite list; all constants are already simultaneous. For d>=d0 a common U-threshold becomes a common Z-threshold by U=Z^d.

There is also an exact useful limitation. Let C=9/2-r and consider the admissible geometric point z=.03M, n1=n2=(M-Cz)/2. At this point A/M=1-(C-1)*.03 and g/M=.03r. Any amplifier in the unchanged low/high ledger must have

\[
 a/M>7r/100,
 \qquad35/54-(7/10)[1-(C-1)3/100]-(26/9)(a/M)>0.
\]

Eliminating a gives

\[
 r<167/1722,\qquad C>3791/861
       =4.403019744\ldots.                     \tag{13}
\]

At equality both budgets cannot be strictly positive. This is a sharp barrier of these two reserve inequalities with the unchanged low cutoff and full local window; it is NOT a lower bound on the actual moment. The point lies inside the stated plain-length range for the relevant C.

## 5. Remaining frozen first tests

### 5.1 W40-11 — the proposed full operator bound fails for the actual critical split

For a Hermitian block M=[[a,z],[conj(z),d]],

    M<=lambda I iff lambda>=a,d and
                    |z|^2<=(lambda-a)(lambda-d).    (W40.17)

This follows directly from the two principal minors of lambda I-M, including equality cases. Its largest eigenvalue is(a+d+sqrt((a-d)^2+4|z|^2))/2. Improving only the a-sector cannot pay d or the cross block.

Use the canonical actual split F=T_z+R_z of [research revision], with z=kappa sqrt X, fixed tau and kappa^2>=2exp(3tau). The accepted critical profile gives ||R_z||_[X,2X] comparable to X/(log X)^2. The actual two-vector Gram matrix has d=||R_z||^2, so its largest eigenvalue is at least d, of order X^2/(log X)^4. A whole-matrix bound O(X^(2gamma)) for any gamma<1 is impossible for this actual matrix, even though the particular direction(1,1) can be much smaller. This conclusion uses the canonical unmasked profile, not the unintegrated gcd-one result or a hereditary mask transfer.

The surviving source target is precisely the directional cancellation already retained in [research revision]: both ordered TR and RT terms and the amplitude mismatch. The frozen f3 A29b further diagnoses the all-g hard mask, but is evidence for independent review and is not newly accepted here. Repackaging the full matrix as a Schur complement does not lower its norm. This is a useful rejection of this stronger implementation, not a new obstruction to every directional dual certificate.

### 5.2 W40-29 — fixed phase-list occupancy cannot save a power

Give total positive weight V/2 to each phase+pi/3 and-pi/3. Every half-open arc of length pi/3 contains at most V/2, but the complex sum is V/2. Replicate or rescale all weights by any power of X: the same exponent survives. A fixed occupancy cap is thus at most a constant-factor input, not a power-saving theorem.

A precise stronger target is available. For a positive phase measure mu of total V let

    Delta=sup_(connected half-open circle arcs I)
          |mu(I)-V*length(I)/(2pi)|.

Then

    |integral exp(i theta)dmu|<=2 Delta.            (W40.18)

Proof: subtract uniform measure, write its cumulative function F on a cut circle, and note that the oscillation of F is at most Delta, since every interval difference is an arc discrepancy. Subtract the midpoint of its range, giving |F|<=Delta/2. Rotate so the desired integral is real. Stieltjes integration by parts against cos has no boundary term (total signed mass is0), and integral|sin|=4. This gives2Delta; atom endpoints are retained by half-open conventions or a limit of cuts avoiding them. The required arithmetic improvement is a POWER-small complete weighted discrepancy. No distribution law for actual H phases, including their signs/projectors, is proved.

### 5.3 W40-28 — an exact collision defect blocks the naive chain complex

Let epsilon be the proposed scalar arithmetic evaluation on the multiplicative semigroup. The first bar-type maps are

    d1[a]=epsilon(a)-1,
    d2[a|b]=epsilon(a)[b]-[ab]+[a].

Direct substitution gives

    d1 d2[a|b]=epsilon(a)epsilon(b)-epsilon(ab).     (W40.19)

For epsilon=mu and a=b=p prime, this is1 because mu(p^2)=0. For epsilon=f3 and p!=3 it is2 because f3(p^2)=-1. Thus replacing collision terms by an abstract d^2=0 complex changes the actual coefficients and natural zeros. Coprime pairs give0, but that does not dispose of the original all-gcd sum.

The requested three-label test gives the same obstruction without changing multiplicity. Define d3[a|b|c]=epsilon(a)[b|c]-[ab|c]+[a|bc]-[a|b]. The four displayed terms cancel in d2 d3 except for [epsilon(a)epsilon(b)-epsilon(ab)][c]. At[a|b|c]=[p|p|q] the defect is[q] for mu and2[q] for f3 with p!=3. Abstract homological cancellation therefore fails already on this exact repeated-prime triple.

For the actual f3 sign the defect has an exact full formula:

    f3(ab)=f3(a)f3(b)f3(gcd(a,b)),
    defect=f3(a)f3(b)(1-f3(gcd(a,b))).              (W40.20)

It retains every valuation and the exceptional sign+1 at prime3. The resulting sign cocycle c(a,b)=f3(gcd(a,b)) obeys

    c(a,b)c(ab,d)=c(b,d)c(a,bd),

but is a coboundary: c(a,b)=f3(a)f3(b)/f3(ab). Twisting the semigroup product by it makes f3 multiplicative on that new algebra, at the price of a diagonal sign change. This identity alone creates no arithmetic cancellation and does not justify keeping the old right module or bar differential unchanged. A useful homological construction must retain and estimate W40.19/20's collision terms before claiming exactness. This is related to W03 seed02 and prime-insertion braids; the actual mu/f3 defect is the scoped calculation here.

## 5. W47-19: the sharp exterior criterion and its native limits

For a finite matrix T, let (A=T^*T\succeq0), d be its full input dimension, (t=\operatorname{tr}A), and
\[
 e_2={t^2-\operatorname{tr}A^2\over2}=\|\wedge^2T\|_{HS}^2.
\]
For d≥2 and t>0, Cauchy on the other d−1 eigenvalues gives
\[
 \lambda_{\max}(A)\le{t+\sqrt{(d-1)((d-1)t^2-2de_2)}\over d}. \tag{R11}
\]
Equality holds when all other eigenvalues coincide. The d=1 and t=0 cases must be handled separately. For (t/d\le B^2\le t), the sharp sufficient condition based only on these two moments is
\[
 e_2\ge {t^2-B^4-(t-B^2)^2/(d-1)\over2}. \tag{R12}
\]
If (p=\operatorname{tr}A^2/t^2), δ=B²/t, this is (p\le\delta^2+(1-\delta)^2/(d-1)). B²≥t needs only the trace; B²<t/d is impossible for a nonzero matrix with that trace. A constant area fraction is not a power saving: diag(M,1) already has large e₂ while its top eigenvalue grows like M. The dimension floor cannot be suppressed.

For the intended application, (T_H) must be the coefficient matrix of the **entire original form** after all the contractions and masks in R4, with (v_i(P)=u_i(P)/\sqrt{q_P}). Then \(\|v_i\|^2=\Omega_i\). The desired raw norm is
\[
 B\ll Z^\epsilon GK[\,N+L+(NL)^{2/3}\,]P_{\rm orig}, \tag{R13}
\]
with the actual profile/height factor and its paid family sum. Afterward the outside scalar (N^{-1}G^{-2}) is applied once. A single u,v/core child, a fixed height, a dense arbitrary-mode matrix or an extra unsigned deletion does not establish R13. Neither the required trace nor the fourth contraction/e₂ of this exact (T_H) is bounded here.

The far-mask clarification matters. Entrywise multiplication by a 0/1 mask is an idempotent self-adjoint operator on matrix entries. It **does not generally take PSD matrices to PSD matrices**. The mask's Hermitian matrix has zero diagonal; if nonzero, its zero trace forces both signs. A synthetic (J-I) mask has norm d−1 even when initial feature vectors are orthogonal; this illustrates the direction problem but is not a native-H lower bound. The general all-g pressure .004 is not automatically a saving relative to a Frobenius norm. The author's hypothetical purity calibration can be used only after an actual matching normalization is established.

## Status and exact claim

The new arithmetic step is to retain the actual prime-slot product inside a marked inverse detector moment. The argument below gives a candidate source-relative weighted density estimate, its complete physical high-branch transfer, and an exact rational return to

    c_candidate = 6257/50000 = .12514,
    theta_candidate = 43743/50000 = .87486.

This exceeds written c6=.125139 by 1/1000000. It is submitted for independent mathematical review and controller decision; it is not an accepted increased constant. All claims are relative to the same pinned analytic base as c6. In particular the prior unresolved F0/analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity and exact comparison-root-definition binding remain unresolved. No formalization, proof-assistant or kernel work was performed.

The report proves a proposed new restricted analytic lemma, rather than assuming a better numerical density exponent. Its restrictions are material: fine original slot mesh, an actual eligible parent dictionary, a pointwise bound on those actual slots in the physical buffered bin, and delta in [17/25,7/10]. The far high bins use the old bound. No claim is made for arbitrary bounded prime coefficients in the pointwise step, although the marked inverse moment itself permits them.

The mechanism does not presently supply an approach to c near 1/6 or 1/4 with complete costs. This continuation prioritizes the first concrete gain within the existing architecture.

## 1. Sources, ancestry and the binding configuration

Primary mathematical evidence is the local pinned PR9 paper at head 58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b, especially B0.7--9, B0.17--20, B3.31--39, B3.58--70, and PR15 at ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef, especially PhysicalLocalAssembly (LA.9--13), SignedReconstruction and PlainUnmarkedDensity. The current forward statement is [restricted mathematical source] sections 1--5. Exact paths, hashes and read locations are in source-receipts.json. Its source-map creation time is 2026-10-12T03:08:26.474035+00:00; this is a receipt time, not an inferred theorem date.

Credit remains with OpenAI for the initial framework; Hailey Collet for the PR9 architecture, quartic and subsequent detector/source development; Akash Levy for weighted-numerator work; and Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance, for PR15's local density split and signed-row reconstruction. The older coupled-amplifier/affine developments and [research revision] density-range extension are used as recorded in the project index. This report's claimed new contribution within the inspected record is the slot-weighted detector, its marked inverse amplification and its transport through the actual physical high norm. This is not a literature-priority claim.

The first-transform convention uses the literal centrally normalized reconstruction already frozen in [research revision]: CRT contributes +xi_r(ab), so the old D.10 C-side coefficient is tau(a)chi_a(er)xi_r(a), with the corresponding conjugate on the other side. The printed inverse-xi convention in PR9 B3.52 requires this repair. Gao's SignedReconstruction independently retains both residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p; the endpoint accounting covers either signed class without a numerical cost change. Root's independent-review intake of 2026-10-12 confirms this narrow convention boundary. That review's M/24 exceptional gain is only for a centered equal-product difference with L=M/4 and an independently established joint opposite-side bound. It is not a per-label high bound, an uncentered reserve, or an input to this report.

The forward high excess, before favorable support terms, is

    (rho(delta)-1)M + delta A + a(5-6rho(delta)),
    rho(delta)=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)].                    (1)

The support terms vanish in the allowed nonexceptional sector with both genuine common supports empty: c=d=p=R=E=Bc=b2=g2=t2=0, and residual projector t=1. This is exactly the sector already identified in [research revision], not a new counterexample. In the same child the low comparison costs (2delta/9)(g+6a), where g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+. At q0=17/25,

    a=(34/21)g  =>  a-(2q0/9)(g+6a)=0.

The high slot slope also vanishes at Lambda=19312/4787. Thus a correction supported only on genuine common primes or exceptional rows cannot alter this binding comparison. The earlier exceptional valuation reserve remains separate and is not spent here. Positive summands with different row predicates cannot exchange exponent reserves merely by addition.

## 2. Marked inverse amplification with the actual slots

Let free mean sixth-power-free with all six source units retained. Fix natural rows u with 0<Nu<=Z^W, a finite fixed ray dictionary, and a product Q_u of the source's centrally normalized prime slots of total logarithmic width z. A polynomial-size row-independent puncture is permitted. For this section only, their prime coefficients may be arbitrary bounded row-independent coefficients, exactly as in B3.31. Let M_u(Z^r) be the actual inverse detector polynomial, including its common smooth cutoff and bounded real power. All lengths are in fixed bounded ranges, with W bounded away from zero.

For every epsilon>0 there is a sufficiently fine mesh, chosen before the eventual character family, slot list, profiles and heights, for which

    sum_free u |M_u(Z^r) Q_u|^2
      << Z^[E_MI(W,r,z)+epsilon] H_J,
    E_MI(W,r,z)=W/6+(5/6)max(W,r+2z,(2r+8z)/3).          (2)

Here H_J denotes the same kind of finite seminorm and polynomial-height cost as the sources. The bound is uniform in fixed polynomial-size punctures in the slot coefficients. The witness inverse has its natural row character; no arbitrary moving coefficient is inserted into it.

Proof. Put H0=max(W,r+2z,(2r+8z)/3), choose a small fixed xi>0, and set H=H0+xi W, alpha=(H-W)/6. Take a fixed prime-ideal pool Z^alpha/2<Np<=Z^alpha, prime to the fixed bad set, with the source's chosen primary generators. It has Z^[alpha+o(1)] primes by the same fixed-field prime ideal theorem used in B3.7. Choose every slot length below xi W/12. Since alpha>=xi W/6, the pool is disjoint from every slot support once Z exceeds the fixed endpoint threshold. This is why the new lemma retains a fine-mesh hypothesis.

For every pool prime, the literal zero-extended identity B0.7 reads

    M_u(D)=M_(up^6)(D)-mu_unit(u,p) (Np)^(-1/2) M_(up^6)(D/Np),
    mu_unit(u,p)=varphi_u(p),                            (3)

where the minus sign is mu(p)=-1. The displayed scalar has modulus at most one and is zero when the natural character requires it. There is no coprimality requirement between u and p. Because the pool misses all slots,

    Q_u=Q_(up^6)

exactly, including their original zeros, fixed masks, signs and relative characters. Apply the two-term squared triangle bound to (3), multiply by |Q_u|^2, and average with the literal normalized prime measure. The map (u,p)->up^6 is injective on free u: valuations modulo six recover u, and the quotient recovers p; the chosen prime generator preserves the unit of u. Thus the positive enlarged sum is at most

    Z^[-alpha+o(1)] sum_(Nv<=Z^H)
        sup_(0<E<=D) |M_v(E) Q_v|^2.                   (4)

Both exact restoration terms have been retained; the second's factor (Np)^(-1) can be bounded by one. Its p-dependent scale is handled by the common logarithmic-scale supremum, not by turning p into an inverse arithmetic coefficient. Differentiate the inverse profile using -W/2-yW', as in B0.8, and integrate over unit logarithmic boxes. Subunit scales are empty below a fixed scale and otherwise contribute only boundedly many boxes. B3.31 applies at row width H to every E<=D, since H-r-2z>=xi W and 3H-2r-8z>=3xi W. Its exponent is H; (4) has exponent H-alpha=W/6+5H/6. Taking xi and the source power losses small proves (2).

The same argument handles the actual cutoff W(y)V_le(Z^r y/Z^t), its scale derivatives, rowwise bounded real powers and frequencies by the source's Sobolev argument. In (3)--(4) all inverse polynomials keep this same frozen profile: at the shortened scale D/Np one must not reset the original truncation parameter from D to D/Np. Its dilation, real-power and frequency seminorms are uniform, and the scale supremum differentiates that fixed profile. The slot heights remain independent. A detector label differing from a slot's parent fixed character is absorbed into that slot's fixed relative coefficient; B3.31 explicitly allows such bounded coefficients. Whole orientation is kept throughout, or wholly conjugated using its allowed second orientation.

## 3. The weighted free-row detector

Fix delta in [17/25,7/10]. Consider free rows of width W in an actual eligible parent translate, with a nonprincipal member of its fixed dictionary having a zero of real part at least (1+delta)/2 at height <=T. In addition require the physical-bin slot bound

    |Q_u|^2 << Z^[delta z+epsilon] H_J                 (5)

on these rows. The product must be the actual source prime slots with their original smooth/ray coefficients and holes, for which the existing buffered-bin prime estimate gives (5). A bounded bin padding in delta is absorbed in epsilon. The family is not enlarged to characters on which a slot becomes principal. For z<=W/20, the claimed weighted estimate is

    sum_these_free_rows |Q_u|^2
      << (1+T)^J Z^[rho(delta)W+gamma(delta)z+epsilon],
    gamma(delta)=delta(5/3+2delta)/(5-2delta),
    eta(delta)=delta-gamma(delta)
              =4delta(5/6-delta)/(5-2delta).             (6)

In particular eta(17/25)=782/6825 and eta(7/10)=14/135. This saves a fixed positive multiple of the actual slot width compared with applying unmarked density and (5) separately.

Proof. Normalize W=1 and write v=z/W<=1/20. Choose

    t=(5-4delta v)/(5-2delta),                          (7)

before selecting witnesses. It lies in [1,3/2]. Apply the existing supported-witness construction and partition by its finite label and two dyads. Up to arbitrarily small source tolerances it gives

    r+m>=t, r<=t, 0<=m<=1/2,
    |M_u(Z^r)|^2>=Z^(delta r),
    |P_u(Z^m)|^2>=Z^(delta m).                         (8)

The inverse and plain factors have the source's common real part/frequency and common profile. Their rowwise real part/frequency is paid by its usual polynomial Sobolev factor.

An important height/bin issue is explicit here. The density proof may build a new internal buffered bin whose zero maximum exceeds the original physical maximum or .85. Its actual witness lower exponent delta_b is at least the prescribed delta-O(e). Use the weaker inequalities (8), and keep the cutoff (7) fixed at the prescribed delta. Do not substitute delta_b into (5). Lemma 1W allows any cutoff chosen before witnesses; its saturation m<=1/2 follows using the actual delta_b and the incumbent 7/8 upper bound. Thus no unsupported upper zero bound at the larger internal height is required.

Divide (2) by the inverse witness, or divide the old unmarked inverse/plain moments by their witnesses and then apply (5). The weighted count exponent is bounded by the minimum of

    U(r)=max(1,(1+5r)/6)-delta r+delta v,
    A(r)=1/6+(5/6)max(1,r+2v,(2r+8v)/3)-delta r,
    P(r)=1-2delta(t-r)+delta v.                         (9)

Using m>=t-r is favorable in the third bound. The source bound max(1,2m) differs from one only by its prescribed small witness tolerance. All such tolerances, dyadic partitions and finite dictionary factors are charged before the final epsilon.

Here is the full r-range calculation. Supported r>=t-1/2>4/5, so r>=2v. Hence (2r+8v)/3<=r+2v. Set R=1-2v.

* For r<=R, A=1-delta r. It crosses P at r_b=(2t-v)/3. The better of them is at most S=1-(2/3)delta t+(1/3)delta v. The crossing is before R: 2t+5v<=3 is equivalent to (5-6delta)-(25-18delta)v>=0, bounded below on the full rectangle by 81/500.
* For R<=r<=1, A=1/6+(5/6-delta)r+5v/3 increases, whereas U=1-delta r+delta v decreases. Their crossing r_c=1-(2-6delta/5)v has value C=1-delta+delta(3-6delta/5)v. The quantity rho+gamma v-C, after multiplication by the positive 3(5-2delta)/delta, is

      (5-6delta)-(40-42delta+36delta^2/5)v.

  This is at least 1923/31250>0 on delta in [.68,.70], v<=.05. Thus this transition, which cannot be omitted, lies below the claimed envelope.
* For r>=1, use U. It increases since delta<=.70<5/6, and its maximum at r=t is L=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+delta v.

The chosen t makes S=L=rho+gamma v. This proves all detector lengths, including boundaries and v=0. The interval lower bounds just given are algebraic bounds on continuous rectangles; critical-point checks in check.py are supplementary.

Fix moment/seminorm degrees before the internal detector exponent tau_d, just as in PR15. If T is at most the internal power threshold, the buffered construction, height Sobolev bounds and finite dyadic partition fit the final power loss. If T exceeds it, ideal counting and the absolute bound |Q|^2<<Z^(z+epsilon) are absorbed by increasing the final polynomial degree J (take a degree at least 2/tau_d on these compact ratios). This yields a common threshold before T. The separate physical height exponent is chosen only after that returned J. Fixed conductor multipliers change constants; they are not growing powers.

## 4. Raw rows, natural holes and uniformity

The raw version of (6) holds for z<=W/21. Write w=u v0^6 with u free and retain the unit in u. The natural slots are exactly the slots for u punctured at primes dividing v0. Their primitive positive-real zeros are unchanged. At each fixed v0 this is an allowed row-independent polynomial-size puncture; (2) is uniform because it uses arbitrary bounded slot coefficients, and (5) is the original natural character's bound. Finite removed prime sums cost only the existing arbitrarily small power after central normalization. No natural sixth-power hole is discarded.

Dyadically put s=log_Z Nv0, V=W-6s. In the range V>=20W/21, one has z/V<=1/20, and the free weighted estimate gives exponent rho V+gamma z. The root count contributes s, so the summation has exponent

    rho W+gamma z-(6rho-1)s.

It converges with an arbitrarily small dyadic loss, since rho>=19/54>1/6 on the used delta range. This range keeps V bounded away from zero uniformly relative to W.

For V<20W/21, use the old unmarked free density together with (5). Then s>W/126, and the exponent is at most

    rho W+delta z-(rho-1/6)W/21
      <=rho W+gamma z.                                (10)

Indeed z<=W/21 and rho-1/6>=5/27>1/8>eta(delta). The strict inequality 5/27-1/8=13/216 leaves room for the dyadic and bounded-window costs. Bounded free windows and the finite free fixed-inducing cores are bounded directly by Z^[W/6+delta z+epsilon], also below (6). They are not incorrectly called a finite raw population. Where canonical eligibility excludes them, the exclusion is preserved.

This proves the raw estimate uniformly for the actual fixed parent translate, both whole orientations, fixed finite unit/ray sectors and every prescribed polynomial-size common puncture. Arbitrary variable masks depending on the live row have not been admitted. The application below reduces all such apparent variation to natural row zeros plus fixed missing-radical masks before invoking this statement.

## 5. Transfer through the literal signed high norm

Retain the complete centered rectangle, both transforms and both coprimality projectors from PR9. They are not reapplied to a zero-bin indicator. Positivity is used only after the exact identities and complete projectors, as in the source. The first common-support side has the actual signed effective row

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-(c-d)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c=log_Z N(F_c)<=5(R-R0).                          (11)

The favorable radius padding is omitted only after using the actual enclosing ball. For the other first side exchange C,D in this calculation and retain its own signed residue; no equality of the two F_c is assumed. Keep both first active residues 1+t_p and 1-t_p, their zero-residue punctures, all scalars, the genuine second common-frequency partition and all natural holes. No phase or conductor is replaced by its absolute value before it has supplied the row identity. The actual child width remains M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2, plus the stated enclosing delta2; it is not shortened by this new estimate.

At fixed missing first radical, all first genuine labels, the first projector s and genuine second labels have divisor-bounded reconstruction from w. The missing radical has width at most p-R-E+R0 and is still counted once. A missing radical is now frozen before the weighted estimate. Its primes supply a fixed common slot puncture. Every other genuine common prime divides w and is already a natural zero. If a subset of the frozen missing radical is enough for a particular label, sum over its divisor-many subsets; this changes only the existing small-power allowance. Thus the weighted slot polynomials, after fixing their finite surviving subsets and parent dictionary, do not acquire a new moving arithmetic coefficient as w varies.

The second residual projector t is different and is not declared a divisor of w. Freeze it and perform the complete signed priority allocation B3.65--69. Keep each scalar psi_w(d), even when zero; do not puncture the quotient again. Let rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2 and zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2, where z_j is the total width of surviving live slots on the two sides after that allocation. The two exact normalization scalars pay the divisor-dyad count as in B3.69. The clipped reductions are nonnegative. Whole products and both independent heights remain intact.

Use the original pointwise plain bound on each side, but leave its Q_{I_j} in the row sum. The squared plain price on side j is delta(A_clip,j-z_j); the paired price is therefore delta(A-c-b2-rbar-zbar), up to the single aggregate endpoint tolerance. At fixed t, missing radical and finite allocation, apply Cauchy in w to the two actual live slot products, then the raw weighted estimate (6). The resulting paired slot exponent is rho W+gamma zbar, in place of rho W+delta zbar. The outside factors and pointwise plain lengths are unchanged. Consequently the full old high excess gains

    eta(delta) zbar + delta rbar                      (12)

relative to the version in which the clipped-reduction term was discarded. The second term was already present before that discard; it is not a new extra normalization factor. No second independent count of the first labels or s is added. The count of t is still paid by its two scalars, and the weighted bound is uniform in its fixed allocations. There are four rectangle pairs, a fixed finite cost.

For completeness, the genuine support terms from LA.13 are

    E1=(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-Bc+rho L_c+R0,
    E2=g2-t2-(1+delta)b2.

On [.68,.75], write m=min(c,d), T=(c-d)_+ and use L_c<=5(R-R0), R<=m, 5rho>1 and 4rho-1>0. Then

    E1<=-(delta-4rho+1)m-(rho+delta-1)T-E-Bc<=-c/28,
    E2<=-delta b2-t2.                                  (13)

Here delta-4rho+1>=1166/6825>1/28 and rho+delta-1>=1/28. This uses the actual signs and multiplicities, not a squarefree substitute.

The frozen-slot widths obey, with one aggregate endpoint tolerance,

    zbar >= z-c-b2-rbar-small.                         (14)

Indeed the products of genuinely frozen slot primes divide the extracted first C-side and the appropriate second common product. Their total logarithmic norms are bounded by c+c2 or c+d2. Newly frozen t-slots are part of r_j, and r_j-r_clip,j is at most the one aggregate clipping tolerance. Repeated slot incidences are counted with their actual multiplicities. There is no error charged once per slot.

Now restrict delta to [.68,.70]. If c+b2+rbar>=z/2, equations (13) and the retained projector term already save at least z/56. If c+b2+rbar<z/2, (14) gives zbar>=z/2-small. Moreover

    W>=M-c-6a>=M-z/2-6a.                              (15)

For the new atlas below, z<=M/25 and a<=a_max, and the exact reserve

    1-1/50-6a_max-21/25=269586511/4021080000>0

ensures W>21z. Hence each z_j<=z fits the raw weighted estimate. Equation (12) saves at least eta z/2>=7z/135>z/56, up to the preallocated small losses. Thus every configuration, not merely the empty-support case, has the new uniform high reserve z/56. Slots exhausted by allocation are covered by the first alternative. No exceptional-row reserve is used.

For delta>=.70 use the old high estimate; its monotonicity and the exact reserve below suffice. Bins crossing .70 can be assigned by their lower endpoint; a weighted bin with lower endpoint <=.70 uses its upper prime price only as the already reserved O(e) error. Low bins at .68 retain the original rule. All bin predicates enter after both transforms on positive child energies.

## 6. New local affine moment, with every other branch paid

Use the old plain and slot ranges .41M<=n1,n2<=.44M and .034M<=z<=.04M, but replace the affine intercept by

    B_new=1420129249/1436100000 = B_c6+1/10000,
    Lambda=19312/4787, q0=17/25, Ka=34/21,
    alpha=1/400000, cell width=1/100000.

For the same 600 original-slot cells, with b_j=.034+j/100000, set

    g_j=B_new-1+(9/2-Lambda)b_j,
    a_j/M=Ka g_j+alpha,
    A_j=B_new-(Lambda-1)b_(j-1).                        (16)

The amplifier is fixed by the original slot cell before live scales, derivatives, children or profiles. Its pool, normalized average, three extraction errors and actual radius increment 6a+omega remain exactly those of the c6 proof. The new detector amplifier of section 2 is an auxiliary inverse-moment proof; it does not replace that physical Gauss amplifier or mix their normalizations.

All low bins use only the old 9/2 positive-slot moment and unrestricted zero-slot moment, with the exact actual-width inequality d_*+r(F-d_*)_+<=delta2+rF_+. Their reserve is unchanged, 7/30000000. At q0 the new high reserve, including .034/56, is

    3651758247/30493190000000 > 0.                     (17)

Every high-cell expression is affine in its endpoint. The derivative of the unweighted high reserve is bounded below by 35015082398263/124869613050000>0. On [.68,.70] the added z/56 is independent of delta; for [.70,.75] the old reserve is already at least 15589229923/2714229000000>0.

The exact minima of the remaining normalized terminal reserves are:

| Branch | Reserve |
|---|---:|
| first extracted error | 542448581/482529600000 |
| sixth extracted error | 11605866353/482529600000 |
| seventh extracted error | 3592930199/120632400000 |
| genuine second zero | 8644965559/120632400000 |
| original main fixed-inducing | 252468929/3015810000 |
| original error fixed-inducing | 925890593/40210800000 |

The amplifier-size reserve 1/4-7a_max is 568295311/3446640000. Comparison reflection still costs at most .93M. First zero uses the original powerful-product bound; artificial zero remains unamplified with its -s0 allowance. The three extracted Gauss errors keep squared scalars Np^-1, (1-Np^-1)^2, Np^-1 and widths (lambda_p,lambda_p), (6lambda_p,0), (7lambda_p,lambda_p); their normalized prime average is not counted twice. They keep the unamplified radii, global slot price 3/4 and deletion rate 1/6. The original exceptional lattice cancellation, full rectangle, both projectors and physical costs 4a/9a suffice. The [research revision] exceptional improvement is not an input.

Choose one numerical power-loss budget below fixed fractions of these reserves. Choose the physical slot mesh to satisfy both the old moment and section 2's prime-pool separation, before the character family and slot list. Aggregate annular errors vanish as Z grows after that list is fixed. Choose common Fourier majorants before live labels; fixed-family moment/profile degrees next, separate external bin height exponent afterward, and raw polynomial bounds before tail orders. These are the existing c6 quantifiers, with one additional numerical mesh restriction.

Subject to the source inputs and the new arguments above, this proves the same local moment with n1+n2+Lambda z<=B_new M, all four plain derivative pairs and the original canonical eligibility.

## 7. Complete quantitative return tested at c=.12514

Keep h=3969737987/5000000000 and use

    theta=43743/50000, kappa_*=18743/25000,
    ell=11/3-4theta=6271/37500,
    x=1+ell-h=5599186039/15000000000,
    y=h-2ell=6892413961/15000000000.

All definitions and original physical coefficients are those of the forward c6 manuscript, with only this geometry and B_new changed. The same d0=1/200, d_-=h-1/1000, d_+=h+10^-10, t0=1/1000, plain cutoff 264/625 and slot cutoff .037 work. Capacity is

    C_new(d)=[2y-(2-B_new)d]/Lambda,
    C_old(d)=min(d,2y-d)/(6kappa_*).                    (18)

The whole-slot selector still retains all widths in its amplitude denominator, including zero-gain/error slots. Every shortening is paid: total selected width <=.034 uses the old reserve 11/5000; a plain <=.41 uses the old reserve 11/10000; otherwise the new local moment applies. Empty selection uses the unrestricted old no-slot moment. The same selected subset works in the four scale-derivative profiles. Actual positive supply and the old detector's selected inverse/plain capacities remain strict, as recorded in arithmetic.json.

The exact physical Euler coefficients retain their old weighted norm sum with h0^(delta/2), h0<=Y, conductor damping and repeated-power deficit. For t<=t0, capacity shrinkage tq/Lambda is paid by delta t/2. For t>=t0 the piecewise-linear paid-shift function has the same slopes 7/18 and 1/2; its new coarse lower value is 3605053/69523200000>0. Thus no large Euler-shift tail is omitted.

For the full physical detector rectangle 0<=delta<=3/4, 0<=p<=1/2, retain the old marked count R_kappa, not the transformed high-bin formula. Put

    D=3-p-2p/(3kappa_*), P=2(1-p)(1-p/(3kappa_*)),
    V=5/6-delta, J=VD+delta P,
    JR=(1-delta)J+delta P V/2.

The tested polynomial is exactly

    F=J[theta-v-(1+delta)/2-13h/75+y/2+ell/2
        -ell delta p-d(1/4-17/50)+delta p C_d/2]
      -(3d/4)[(1-delta)J+delta P V/2].                 (19)

It equals J(theta-v-G_kappa*) with J>1/10. The degree-(2,3) tensor Bernstein calculation in check.py is exact rational arithmetic, transcribed from the pinned written source; no project code or proof assistant is imported. It proves (19) on whole closed rectangles with disjoint-interior cover, not sampled points:

* d=h, new capacity, v=10^-6: eight boxes, all 96 coefficients positive.
* d=d_-, old capacity, v=10^-5: six boxes, all 72 coefficients positive.
* d=1/2, old capacity, v=10^-3: one box, all 12 coefficients positive.

arithmetic.json records every box and its exact coefficient minimum and maximum; check.py reconstructs all coefficients and verifies an independent interior polynomial evaluation for each box. The local affine atlas needs only its two endpoint cells, since all displayed branch quantities are affine in b_j. There are 40 recorded positive rational checks.

The unchanged affine/convex row-width argument extends these three endpoint bounds over their original intervals. The old/new junction capacity gap is 1689487545955437451727/1628841672000000000000000>0; row extension keeps 4999/5000000000. Floor, far-old, small-row and both principal contour reserves remain positive in the receipt. The old/new feedback derivatives remain below 1/8 and 1/50, respectively. Consequently replacing kappa_* by the actual kappa=2beta_*-1 costs less than the usual fraction of beta_*-theta, with the same fixed supremum-gap choice before the target character.

Finally use the unchanged full physical inversion, principal residues, nonprincipal small rows, upper-row integration tail, all independent Fourier heights, reciprocal-contour gluing, numerator nonvanishing on Re>=.87, and norm lift stated in manuscript section 5. No new estimate is asserted for any of those objects. All their changed numerical margins are positive in the receipt; the probe identity (5x+y)/12=theta-(5/6-x/3-ell/6) is exact. Thus, if this report's new weighted lemma and physical transfer are accepted relative to those imports, the original zero-exclusion argument returns the candidate c=.12514 in exactly the c6 character/height/normalization scope. This conditional written conclusion does not resolve any broader base or external-root binding obligation.

## 8. Strongest objections and remaining review boundary

The high count cannot be improved by simply dropping the slot maximum from the old unmarked theorem. Equation (2), proved with exact Euler restoration and a slot-disjoint prime pool, is the necessary new estimate. Its middle r interval and long-inverse complement are retained in (9); omitting them would give an unjustified larger saving. The internally reconstructed zero bin need not have the physical bin's upper endpoint: section 3 explicitly weakens its witnesses to the prescribed lower delta while retaining the physical slot bound separately.

A weighted estimate cannot be applied to arbitrary row-varying punctures or a changing character dictionary. Section 5 freezes the genuinely missing radical, uses natural zeros for all support already in w, handles its divisor-many subsets, and leaves the second projector outside the row reconstruction. That reduction, and the exact width/frozen-slot inequality (14), are the highest-priority independent review targets. If either fails at the actual coefficients, the candidate endpoint is not established; the free/raw weighted-density result remains a separately useful proposed lemma.

The briefly tested smaller-power Gauss amplifier did not provide a free shortcut. For p coprime to a column, G(u,hp^k)=overline(chi_u(p))^k G(u,h); compensating with chi_u(p)^k changes the column character. For 1<=k<=5 these p-dependent polynomials cannot be merged into the single positive norm that supplies the source's Z^-a density factor. After second Poisson their row contains p^k j with its natural hole, restoring the apparent radius change. This diagnoses that attempted modification only; it is not a general impossibility theorem for correlated amplifiers.

No full transitive audit is claimed. The oldest analytic contracts remain the explicit source-relative imports of the forward proof. The independent reviewer must inspect the new inverse amplification, the all-range weighted witness argument, the raw lifting and literal projector transfer before using the numerical return. The numerical check alone cannot supply any of those analytic statements.

## 6. Uniform parked audit25: rescue the checksum and price its return

The author's card was untested and called incoherent as stated. An exact
realization exists. For sequences on1,...,N define the additive prefix and
divisor incidence transforms by

    (A v)(n)=sum_(k<=n)v(k),
    (D v)(n)=sum_(d|n)v(d),
    C_N=A D-D A.

They preserve all integer labels. Counting the same divisibility relation
in the two orders gives the explicit signed commutator

    C_N(n,k)=floor(n/k)-#{d:d|n, d>=k}.                  (R41-C1)

Let mu have its literal squarefree zero extension and M(n)=sum_(k<=n)mu(k).
Since D mu=delta1, A D mu is the constant sequence1. The actual checksum
q(n)=(C_N mu)(n), independent of N once N>=n, therefore satisfies

    q(n)=1-sum_(d|n)M(d),
    M(n)=1_(n=1)-sum_(d|n)mu(d)q(n/d).                 (R41-C2)

The second line is exact divisor inversion of the first. No absolute
values or endpoint terms were removed. The first is a genuine common
integer identity linking additive and multiplicative summation; the second
reconstructs the signed partial sum from the mismatch. The first values
of q are0,0,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,3,2,5. These were independently checked by the
full integer matrix and by inversion, not inferred from a few samples.

For every fixed gamma>0, the all-n, every-epsilon statements

    |q(n)| <<_epsilon n^(gamma+epsilon)
       iff |M(n)| <<_epsilon n^(gamma+epsilon)           (R41-C3)

are equivalent. In either direction, R41-C2 and the divisor count bound
d(n)<<_eta n^eta prove the implication after dividing epsilon between
the input and divisor loss; the constant1 is harmless. For completeness
the divisor bound follows by bounding k+1 by p^(eta k) uniformly for
sufficiently large primes p, and absorbing each of the finitely many
small-prime ratios into its finite maximum. This proof includes every
sign, nonsquarefree zero, divisor and outer n. The checksum is thus a
precise reorganization, with no cheaper exponent hypothesis established.

Its original-source zero return is complete. Under either side of R41-C3,
with0<gamma<1, the integral

    H(s)=s integral_1^infinity M(x)x^(-s-1)dx

is holomorphic for Re s>gamma by the every-epsilon bound, locally uniformly
also after derivatives. For Re s>1, partial summation identifies H=1/zeta.
The identity zeta(s)H(s)=1 continues meromorphically and is holomorphic
at every proposed zero away from the pole at1. A zero in Re s>gamma would
give0=1. All fixed heights are covered; no independent reciprocal-growth
estimate is assumed. This is the ordinary Möbius source, not f3 and not an
unproved transfer to the capped H/SP source. In fact the current accepted
buffered Mertens calibration and R41-C2 already imply
q(n)<<_epsilon n^(.874864+epsilon). This recovers the c5 baseline, with
no further gain. The useful new hypothesis would require gamma<.874864;
that actual checksum estimate remains open. The author's historical
gamma=.874864 example is no longer an improving target.

A finite checksum alone is also incomplete in a sharply visible way.
For k>N/2 and every n<=N, R41-C1 is zero: when n>=k, floor(n/k)=1 and
the only divisor of n at least k is n itself; otherwise both terms vanish.
Thus C_N has at least ceil(N/2) independent invisible coordinate directions.
Given distinct k,l>N/2 and real .5<rho<1, the Dirichlet polynomial

    P(s)=[k^(rho-s)-l^(rho-s)]/[k^(rho-2)-l^(rho-2)]      (R41-C4)

is supported in that kernel, has P(2)=1 and P(rho)=0. Its explicit
coefficients need not be bounded or Möbius; this is a finite checksum
countermodel for unrestricted inputs only. It does not contradict R41-C3,
which requires the actual mu input and a coherent estimate for every n,
not one finite kernel condition. To reconstruct individual coefficients
one may then take mu(n)=M(n)-M(n-1), with M(0)=0; this supplies no new
norm contraction either.

Credit the classical divisor-inversion/floor-sum identity and the existing
A-FLOORDUAL/signed-incidence portfolio. The recorded new review action is
to make this particular parked proposal coherent and expose its exact
arithmetic return and finite blindness. It is not a claim of a newly
discovered general Möbius theorem. Preserve the rare seed as useful-set-aside
with R41-C1–3, rather than equating “author untested” with “impossible”.

statement: # Independent W59 review **Verdict.** Retain the exact finite cutoff identities, the least-active-prime multiplicity theorem F10, and the complete conditional ordinary-character returns. F10 is a useful extension of the recorded cone calculation to arbitrary complex weights, including smaller zero weights and a moving least active prime. Retain R5's original-source correction and its coarse absolute budget as a scoped failed route. There is no new arithmetic estimate, native-H transfer or increase in c. The graph, gluing, observability, coupling and constructive matching mechanisms remain eligible beyond the specific shortcuts tested here. Current calibration is root-accepted c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 and theta11=.8748540364. A first gain requires a common ordinary-character exponent gamma0, D=Pi d Pi, B=(I-Pi)d Pi and E=B*B. Divisor closure gives (I-Pi)d*Pi=0 and Pi d(I-Pi)=0. Expanding the full CAR identity gives D^2=0, D*D+DD*=W Pi-E, 0<=E<=W Pi. (1) E includes signed overlaps of distinct insertions reaching the same outside state. Replacing it by its diagonal would be a different operator. With Gamma=(-1)^omega, Str(A)=Tr(Gamma A), and T_chi diagonal chi(n), cyclicity gives exactly W M_chi(N)=Str(T_chi E)+Str([T_chi,D*]D). (2) The corresponding diagonal expression is sum_p |w_p|^2 { sum_(N/pN, is valid. Treat the finitely many p<4/kappa_q by (3). For larger p, begin with the squarefree q-units in (N/2,N] and remove at most N/p multiples of p. For all sufficiently large N depending only on q, this leaves at least kappa_q N/8. Thus kappa_q WN/8 <= Tr E = sum_p |w_p|^2 C_p(N) <= WN. (4) This uses no PNT and no uniformity in a growing q. It obstructs a normalized positive-trace certificate of exponent below one. It is not an arithmetic lower bound on (2), a Gaussian field or native H. Let p_* be the least prime with nonzero weight; smaller primes may remain in the basis with zero weights. Set h_N=C_(p_*)(N). The claim that E has eigenvalue W with **exact multiplicity h_N** is correct. Here is the quotient argument with the truncation issue made explicit. Let U be the span of p_*-free states with n>N/p_*. Every active creation has prime at least p_*, so D kills U. In the quotient, each p_*-free n<=N/p_* is paired with p_*n; the corresponding coefficient w_(p_*) is invertible. The homotopy w_(p_*)^(-1)c_(p_*)* is well defined modulo U. Anticommutation cancels other active creations. If truncation spoils one of these cancellations, its remaining p_*-free state lies above N/p_* and hence is zero in the quotient. The quotient is therefore contractible. The long exact sequence for 0→U→range Pi→range Pi/U→0 identifies cohomology with the graded vector space U. Finite-dimensional Hodge decomposition identifies its dimension with ker D intersect ker D*. By (1), this is exactly ker(W Pi-E). If p_*>N, D=0, U is the whole state space and the same formula holds. Arbitrarily small nonzero w_(p_*) causes no problem for the finite homology statement, but the argument does not supply a uniform homotopy norm as that weight tends to zero. The identification of cohomology with U is **not** the assertion that each displayed critical basis vector is harmonic or an eigenvector of E. For example, at q=1,N=12 with all weights nonzero, the critical states 7 and 11 have nonzero D* images. They count two harmonic classes, whose harmonic representatives need not be those basis vectors. The author's dimensional proof does not require the stronger, false identification. This interpretation should accompany integration. Combining (4) with h_N>=kappa_q N/8 gives a linear-dimensional full-loss eigenspace and ||E||=W for all sufficiently large N, uniformly over the moving weights and active primes. This blocks an ambient gap below W, not cancellation of the two signed traces in (2). For q=1,p_*=2, the count is the classical odd-squarefree critical count in Björner's Theorem 3.1. The reviewed primary statement identifies reduced Betti numbers by odd squarefree integers in (N/2,N]. [A cell complex in number theory](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704). [research revision] G144 already owns the q-unit least-prime cone/rank and filtration cost. The increment here is the explicit arbitrary-zero-weight, least-ACTIVE-prime version and its exact boundary-Gram eigenvalue. No new general topology theorem or arithmetic gain is claimed. **3. Complete return, with exact quantifiers.** Suppose for every fixed presented ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integers N, one specified allowed sequence of nonzero weight vectors satisfies the COMPLETE right side of (2) bounded by C_(chi,epsilon) W N^(gamma+epsilon), with one common gamma>0. Dividing by W gives the actual Mertens estimate; moving weights and W tending to zero are harmless only because the hypothesis is normalized by the same W. Absolute positive trace bounds do not supply this hypothesis. For each compact subset of Re s>gamma, choose epsilon below its distance from gamma. Abel's integral s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1)dx then converges normally and is holomorphic. It agrees with 1/L(s,chi) for Re s>1. Multiplication by the actual meromorphic L and analytic continuation excludes a zero anywhere in Re s>gamma. No fixed height ceiling was introduced; constants may depend on the fixed character and compact set. A principal pole at 1 is not a zero, and the finite imprimitive Euler factors have no zeros in Re s>0. This is a complete conditional ordinary-family return. It provides neither the signed estimate nor an Eisenstein or growing-conductor extension. **4. R1–R7: source-exact but substantially ancestral.** With finite unramified B, write a_B(n)=a(n)1_((n,P_B)=1), e_B(d)=mu(d)chi(d)1_(d|P_B), and r_B(m)=chi(m) on all B-smooth integers, zero elsewhere. The unit and every prime power in r_B matter. Local Euler factors give e_B*r_B=delta_1, a=e_B*a_B and a_B=r_B*a. For overlapping blocks, e_A*e_B=e_(A union B)*e_(A intersection B), and the analogous identity holds for a_A*a_B. No squarefree-only convolution or independent-block assumption is used. The finite factors E_B(s)=product_(p in B)(1-chi(p)p^-s) are nonzero in Re s>0. The channel F_B=1/(L E_B) retains the same reciprocal-L factor. Multiplying every channel by a common meromorphic scalar preserves the overlap determinant. Thus that determinant alone supplies no pole exclusion; this does not rule out additional source information about joint channels. For gamma>0, the exact absolute coefficient sums are product(1+p^-gamma) and product(1-p^-gamma)^(-1). Minkowski gives the corresponding upper bounds on the global all-real-shell norm sup_(T>0)T^-gamma ||U||_(L2([T,2T],dx/x)). Calling these exact absolute sums is justified; it should not be read as a sharp operator norm on every restricted arithmetic source. Fixed blocks preserve exponents with positive buffers. A growing block must pay the products and every shifted shell, not merely a favorable estimate at its parent X. The explicit Mellin examples are exp(-n/x) and exp(-(n/x)^2), the latter an ordinary Gaussian in n/x rather than the log-Gaussian used in other lanes. Their transforms are Gamma(s)/(L E_B) and Gamma(s/2)/(2 L E_B). Small x gives the genuine exponentially decaying tail. Every-epsilon, all-large-shell L2 bounds give normal convergence in Re s>gamma by Cauchy–Schwarz and dyadic summation, and the gamma factors never vanish there. The same meromorphic identity excludes zeros at every finite height. The source convolution identities can be applied to other fixed kernels, but their Mellin multipliers must then be retained separately. If min B>sqrt N, every squarefree divisor of P_B with two primes exceeds N. For each real 1<=x<=N this gives M(x)=M_B(x)-sum_(p in B,p<=x) chi(p) M(x/p). (5) The inner function is the original M, because x/p. All shared-prime interactions and phases remain. R1/R3/R4 are classical finite Euler removal and already have G28, G81, G92 and G108 ancestry. R2 records the proposed overlap invariant; R5/R6 give a useful explicit short-original-source accounting, not a new inverse family. [research revision] G146–G148 now also stresses that exact overlap dependence cannot justify multiplication of marginal rarities. Its actual native simultaneous-witness estimate OPEN-MIX has not been supplied by these ordinary Euler identities. **5. The other first tests and the native source boundary.** S17's chosen conditional expectations preserve the constant vector. Their commutator annihilates it and is also invisible to its dual mean. The actual principal-modulo-3 source at N=12 has M=-2, while the stated residue and two-interval projections commute. This refutes a mean bound based solely on that commutator. The finite equal-bin example is not a theorem that all logarithmic filtrations commute, and it does not close a complete gluing identity with the common mode retained. S11's real/imaginary transport must retain all ghost/unmatched mass. In logarithmic coordinates exp(-n/x) has Lipschitz constant at most 1/e. Balanced one-dimensional W1 is the integral of the absolute cumulative imbalance; it is not free arithmetic input. The feature-Cauchy version has the previously recorded G65 mass/displacement price. No improved actual matching was constructed. This leaves source-specific couplings eligible. S23 correctly recovers the native tensor before discussing a generic dilation. It retains ideal coefficients a=alpha eta chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2, the multiplicative chi_d(e)^4 interaction with common-prime zero extensions, xi=alpha^3 eta^3, and chi_R(ng)^3 chi_P(n)^4 1_((P,Rg)=1) u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P). Both rooted arrays/projectors, perpendicular masks and independently chosen heights remain, with the original h((g,g')) core, gap |q_n-q_n'|>floor(Z^.05), both equal-norm exclusions, original profiles/JPS3 domain, and the once-only outside factor N^(-1)G^(-2). The source family is not replaced by the ordinary vector used above. For a literal source matrix T and a proved r>=||T||, K=T/r has its Julia unitary dilation. The identity ||Kv||^2+||(I-K*K)^(1/2)v||^2=||v||^2 is exact. A small channel norm requires nearly full source observation by the loss channel; unitarity alone supplies no such estimate and r is not free. The diagonal toy tests only that implication, not every two-observer mechanism. No native-H saving or adapter has been proved. S07's two-prime cutoff at 2,3,N=5 genuinely removes the 6-cell from the complete cube. Applying separate masks would restore a coefficient that is absent in the actual source. The joint cutoff in (1) is the valid repair and retains its entire boundary Gram. This is consistent with old tensor/cutoff ancestry, including G121; it supplies no signed saving. **6. Protected independent audit S18: an actual source kernel for the natural graph.** This audit starts from the frozen high-reach seed, not the author's selected result. Let V_N be all squarefree q-unit integers n<=N, including 1. For every internal edge n→pn with p not dividing n, pn<=N and p unramified, define the natural covariant incidence (nabla_chi f)(n,p)=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n). (6) The actual source a satisfies nabla_chi a=0 on every edge. More precisely, write f(n)=a(n)g(n), possible because |a(n)|=1 on V_N. Since a(pn)=-chi(p)a(n), (6) equals chi(p)a(n)[g(n)-g(pn)]. This is a unitary vertex/edge gauge of the ordinary incidence. The full prime-divisor graph is connected to 1 by deletions, so its internal kernel is exactly span{a}. It is the source itself, not merely an unrelated constant mode, which evades internal dissipation. Extend f by zero outside V_N and include outgoing edges. On a boundary edge pn>N, the defect becomes chi(p)a(n), of modulus one. With arbitrary edge-prime weights w_p, its positive edge energy is exactly sum_p |w_p|^2 C_p(N), subject to the linear price (4). This graph energy keeps edges as separate observations; it is not identified with the coherent CAR boundary Gram E, whose off-diagonal overlaps remain different. Either construction requires a source-sensitive signed observation to recover an improvement. Embed a in all N integer coordinates with the true squareful/nonunit zeros and apply the unitary additive discrete Fourier transform. The zero-frequency coordinate is M_chi(N)/sqrt N, and the other coordinates are all retained. Fourier conjugation transports the source kernel; it does not eliminate it. On the actual quartic character modulo 5, chi(2)=i, at N=7, V_N={1,2,3,6,7} and the coefficients are {1,-i,i,1,-i}. Every internal flux in (6) is zero while M=2-i. Thus no estimate of the scalar solely by this internal dissipation can hold, regardless of its constant. This is a decisive first test of a natural incidence implementation of S18. It is not a refutation of the seed's advertised absorbing-boundary/scattering observation, which could add a new exact coupling. To make that broader route useful, specify an observation of the full actual boundary whose norm controls |hat a(0)|, pay its reconstruction and all frequency/scale complements, and prove that norm below N^(gamma-1/2+epsilon). If it directly yields |M(N)|<N cases. The same helper verifies the actual S18/S12 example, all graph edges and acyclicity, three R5 families over 197 real half-integer endpoints, all thirty literal probabilities, each full author pool/draw, and the critic's original factoradic permutation/choices. ## G137. A restricted inverse moment can pay both witness branches

Use the exact [[research revision]](../[research revision]/density-integration.md) family and
[[research revision]](../[research revision]/joint-density-integration.md) same-character,
same-zero witness contract. Freeze K=28114053/6250000=4.49824848 from
the accepted c10 SAME-family input; it is not the physical kappa and
is not recalibrated from c11. Keep the original labels, natural holes
and coefficient zeros, independent slot heights, derivative profiles,
positive grades, finite dictionary and common thresholds. A signed
projector does not automatically preserve a joint-witness restriction.

Normalize the free width to 1, write d=delta in[.68,.70], v=z/W, and
retain r<=t, r+m>=t, m<=1/2 from the original witnesses. Their bounds are

    I(r)=1-d r+d[v-(1-r)/2]_+,
    P(m)=1-2d m+d[v-(1-2m)/K]_+,
    L(t)=1/6+(5/6-d)t+d v.

The long inverse branch is bounded by L(t). Put

    u=2d(K-1)/K, alpha=u/(d+u)=2(K-1)/(3K-2),
    D=15K-10-6Kd,
    t_A=(5-6dv)/(5-2d),
    t_B=[15K-10-6d-12d(K-1)v]/D,
    t_*=max(t_A,t_B),
    r_*(t)=min(2t/3,[u t+d(1/K-v)]/(d+u)).

These are the old complete separate-moment cutoff and short crossing.
The minimum of the crossing locations is required because P is the
maximum of its two affine pieces. Near the crossing I is in its
full-fit piece 1-dr. The old short maximum Q_*(t)=1-d r_*(t) is the
maximum of decreasing affine functions with slope magnitudes 2d/3
and d alpha. At t_* it agrees with the long bound E0(1,v).

Fix 0<eta<=.001 and the SAME cutoff t=t_*-eta BEFORE witnesses.
The new hypothesis J_eta^all is a saving eta in the ORIGINAL inverse
moment restricted to actual rows that also carry the large plain
witness of that SAME character and zero, only when

    |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta,   0<=v<=1/20.

After dividing by the inverse spike this gives I(r)-eta. Require it
uniformly in every original source parameter and every actual live
positive child list where it is used. It is not supplied by separate
moments, witness independence, a changed prime pool or the rank-one
shared-zero signal in G115. This hypothesis is OPEN.

Here is its paid implication. Across the plain kink the increasing
function P(t-r) has slopes between u and 2d. If the new crossing moves
left by h, then eta=(d+b_eff)h for b_eff in[u,2d]. Its value falls by
b_eff h>=alpha eta, and h<2eta. Outside the window, the old minimum
has already fallen by at least 2d eta>=alpha eta. This remains valid
beyond adjacent pieces by monotonicity. Thus the entire short maximum
is at most Q_*(t)-alpha eta. Moving t down by eta increases Q_* by at
most (2d/3)eta, while it decreases the long branch by (5/6-d)eta.
On the full d interval,

    alpha-2d/3>=2/15,   5/6-d>=2/15.

Therefore the COMPLETE free-row envelope improves by (2/15)eta W.
Keeping the old cutoff would leave the long branch unchanged and
would not prove this conclusion.

The independent 20-by-25 exact rational interval enclosure covers
d in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], eta in[0,.001], including both sides of
the plain kink and zero slot width. It verifies the entire length
window has r>1/2, 0<m<1/2, 1<t<3/2 and r+2v<1. The last gate and
r>1/2 also imply 2r+8v<3. Its full-fit reserve exceeds .01017.
The original fine mesh and all finite losses are fixed below positive
reserves before witnesses. Since m>=t-r>t-1>0 in the short regime,
bounded/zero-length plain witnesses cannot create an omitted short
branch; long and unrestricted exceptional cases keep their source bounds.

For raw w=u_core b^6, freeze b, preserve its holes and set
s=log_Z Nb, V=W-6s. Define

    rho=1-10d/[3(5-2d)], k=rho+d-1,
    a_K=d(5-6d)^2/[3(5-2d)D],
    b_K=2d(5-6d)(K-1)/D,
    E0(W,z)=rho W+d z-min(3kz,a_K W+b_K z).

For V>=20W/21 and 0<=z/W<=1/21 the free ratio z/V<=1/20.
The two W-slopes of E0 are rho and rho-a_K, so

    E0(W-6s,z)<=E0(W,z)-6(rho-a_K)s.

Counting all roots costs Z^s. The conditional exponent is therefore

    E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W
      -[6(rho-a_K-(2/15)eta)-1]s.

The bracket exceeds 1.10376 on the complete box. In the remaining
V<20W/21 range, s>W/126 and the OLD unmarked tail pays the gain with
reserve [(rho-1/6-3k)/21-(2/15)eta]W>.00109398W. Original bounded
free windows and fixed-inducing free cores retain their actual raw
populations and fit this reserve; they are not declared finite raw sets.
Consequently J_eta^all implies the complete source-relative bound

    Z^[E0(W,z)-(2/15)eta W+epsilon] H_J,
    0<=z/W<=1/21.

At eta=.001 the conditional saving is W/7500. A sharper version on
.034<=z/W<=.05 retunes t=t_B-12(K-1)eta/D and gives
C_J eta W, C_J=2(5-6d)(K-1)/D>=7/50. Its narrower hypothesis does
not imply J_eta^all. Both versions and their checks are preserved.

No numerical endpoint is assigned. Every child saving uses its actual
width. Support loss, signed reconstruction, extraction scalars,
amplifiers, local plane, complete physical rectangle, Euler shifts
including zero capacity, principal residues and actual-supremum
feedback still need integration. The unchanged architecture's c<2/15
barrier cannot reach 1/6 or 1/4 by this envelope alone. The decisive
next estimate is the actual inverse moment on this same-zero,
large-plain subset, not another optimization of the old separate bounds.

## [research revision]-S3. The determinant repair keeps the original hard energy

For a positive definite finite Gram M, the determinant lemma gives

    det(M+lambda cc*)/det(M)=1+lambda c*M^-1 c.

This is dual energy, not the desired primal energy c*Mc. Replacing c by
v=Mc repairs the identity to1+lambda c*Mc, so it keeps the entire original
moment obligation. Infinite limits also owe conditioning and tails. This
rules out the proposed shortcut, not every determinant architecture.

The seven other first tests preserve their exact failure scopes, including
unitary gauges, the proposed log2/log3 resultant, convolution-inverse
uniqueness, mu versus mu chi, trace-zero commutators with nonzero quadratic
form, and unjustified algebraicity at general complexs. The reports retain
each tested identity and broader variants that were not tested.

### C. The coefficient is sharp even for a one-sided arbitrary-input form

This checks the strongest affordable objection: perhaps the absolute estimate wastes the sign so badly that a generic one-sided operator argument could pay a much larger range. For the principal character that hope fails at this level.

Let T->infinity, L_T=sqrt T, Y_T=a(1+T)^b, t_T=pi/log Y_T, and take the test function

    f_T(y)=e^(i t_T y) 1_[T,T+L_T](y).

This is an arbitrary-input test, not the actual z. Delays for admitted primes are O(log T), so only O(log T) of the interval is lost at its left edge. On the rest, conjugate(f_T(y))f_T(y-log p)=p^(-i t_T). Under the positive weights log p p^(-gamma), the mass with p<=Y_T^(1-epsilon) is negligible compared with S_gamma(Y_T). For all the remaining mass, t_T log p lies between (1-epsilon)pi and pi+o(1). First let T grow, then epsilon decrease. Therefore

    -Re int conjugate(f_T)K_small f_T
       /int y|f_T|^2 -> kappa(a,gamma).                     (C8)

The finite q-exclusions do not change the limit. Uniformly across the window Y_a(y)/Y_T->1, and the edge loss is O(log T/sqrt T), so neither alters it. This attains the same leading one-sided coefficient as(C4). If the cutoff power b'>1/(1-gamma), the same test gives a ratio asymptotic to a^(1-gamma)T^(b'(1-gamma)-1)/(1-gamma), which diverges. Consequently no bounded one-sided relative-form certificate on arbitrary inputs can pay such a supercritical power. This does not lower-bound the actual source's Q_small or H_a,R; it leaves arithmetic source-specific cancellation open.

The attempted weakest coarse estimate of the FULL hard part still fails: granting only |U(y)|<=C e^(beta y), gamma<beta<1, absolute prime summation produces scale exponent 1+beta-2gamma, versus 2beta-2gamma for I_R. The gap1-beta remains, as G173 already records. The exact logarithmic equation and the new critical interface do not supply the missing signed saving. Treating its inverse resolvent as bounded across a possible L-zero would merely assume the conclusion.

statement:
## 6. A stable first-shell inverse and its unpaid future tail

This is a distinct non-character test of agenda D1--D7. Set t=2sigma,
0<sigma<1, p_k=k^(-t)-(k+1)^(-t), and use
||F||_sigma^2=t^(-1) sum_k p_k |F(k)|^2. Let h_N be the agenda's
exact finite-prefix interpolant and r_N=1-h_N. For N<=n<2N put
b_n=n f_n-2N f_(2N). On N<=k<2N,

\[
b_n(k)=-n1_{k\ge n},\qquad
a_n=-\frac{r(n)-r(n-1)}n,\quad r(N-1)=0.
\]

This is the unique exact first-shell inverse; including n=N is
necessary. It satisfies sum|n a_n|^2<=4 sum|r(k)|^2. The weighted
version has a sigma-dependent constant since p_k is comparable
on the shell. This does not bound the correction's future repetitions.
For the actual residual,

\[
a_N=-S_{N-1}-\mu(N)/N,\qquad a_n=-\mu(n)/n\ (n>N),
\quad\boxed{c_N:=\sum a_n b_n=h_{2N}-h_N.} \tag{R6}
\]

Thus exact refitting produces the old interpolant at twice the scale.
One component is completely stable: B_N=2f_(2N)-f_N is the indicator
of alternating integer blocks [(2j+1)N,(2j+2)N). If
eta_alt(t)=sum_(j>=1)(-1)^(j-1)j^(-t), then
||B_N||_sigma^2=N^(-t)eta_alt(t)/t. Its first-shell mass is
N^(-t)(1-2^(-t))/t and its future mass is their difference.
The initial correction (N S_(N-1)+mu(N))B_N consequently has
controlled future-to-shell cost. The remaining increments are
the source of the unproved analytic estimate.

The complete future correction has the exact floor representation

\[
c_N(k)=\sum_{N\le n<2N}\mu(n)\lfloor k/n\rfloor
+NS_{N-1}\lfloor k/N\rfloor
-2NS_{2N-1}\lfloor k/(2N)\rfloor. \tag{R7}
\]

Let F_N be the squared residual norm restricted to N<=k<2N,
T_N the squared correction norm on k>=2N, and J_N the inner product
of r_N with c_N on k>=2N, all with weight p_k/t. Then

\[
\boxed{\|r_N\|_\sigma^2-\|r_{2N}\|_\sigma^2
       =F_N+2\Re J_N-T_N.} \tag{R8}
\]

Interpolation removes the first shell but need not decrease the
total norm. An independent exact expression for its future cost is

\[
\begin{gathered}
A_N(s)=\sum_{N\le n<2N}\mu(n)n^{-s}
       +N^{1-s}S_{N-1}-(2N)^{1-s}S_{2N-1},\\
T_N=\frac1{2\pi}\int_{\mathbb R}
\frac{|\zeta(\sigma+iu)A_N(\sigma+iu)|^2}{\sigma^2+u^2}\,du-F_N .
\end{gathered} \tag{R9}
\]

This follows directly from the Mellin transform
Mf_n(s)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s and Plancherel. It uses no new
reciprocal bound. For b=b0+epsilon<1, the accepted Mertens estimate
and partial summation give S_(N-1)<<N^(b-1) and F_N<<N^(2b-2sigma).
The fractional-part expression gives |c_N(k)|<<N. Expanding the
floors in (R7) instead gives |c_N(k)|<<k N^(b-1). Splitting the
weighted tail at N^(2-b) proves

\[
T_N\ll_{\sigma,\epsilon}N^{\,2-2\sigma(2-b)}. \tag{R10}
\]

At sigma=0.8745 the limiting first-shell and future-tail exponents
are +0.000773294079928262 and +0.032176745672897265... .
These are insufficient upper-bound certificates, not lower bounds
or divergence results. The crude full-tail bound decays only for
sigma>1/(2-b0), approximately 0.8887993351.

A sufficient next lemma is the SIGNED capture inequality
F_(2^j)+2 Re J_(2^j)-T_(2^j)>=delta_j ||r_(2^j)||_sigma^2,
where 0<=delta_j<1 and sum_j delta_j diverges. No such inequality
is proved. Even first-shell convergence requires an improved
square-integral estimate for
N S_(N-1)+M(k)-M(N-1); good finite interpolation alone does not
provide it.

### 3a. Formation and every tail are paid from periodicity

From (3)-(5), let

    H0=sqrt(2a) C_q/(a-gamma),
    K=1+2a/(a-gamma).

Then |h(t)|<=H0 exp(-gamma t), and induction gives
|Q^j h(t)|<=H0 K^j exp(-gamma t). For the truncated Gram G_N^(T),

    |(G_N-G_N^(T))_(j,k)|
       <=H0^2 K^(j+k) exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma),
    0<=G_N-G_N^(T)<=eta_N(T) I,
    eta_N(T)=(N+1)H0^2 K^(2N)exp(-2gamma T)/(2gamma). (12)

The second inequality follows from the first entrywise bound and the PSD tail Gram. It exposes the growing-degree cost instead of calling a finite matrix the full source. To bound the actual error without any inverse-condition-number assumption, take a specific p with p0=1, put C_p=sum_(j=0)^N |p_j|K^j, and use

    ||pF-F0||^2 <= integral_0^T |p(Q)h-F0 ell0|^2dt
       +H0^2 C_p^2 exp(-2gamma T)/gamma
       +2|F0|^2 exp(-2a T).                           (13)

This is the squared triangle inequality only on the tail. On a finite interval, b(t)=A(n)-r exp(t) for log n<=t<log(n+1); (3) and (5) are elementary exponential integrals. Thus a finite witness has a fully specified ordinary arithmetic source and certifiable tails. It still must make the complete interior integral small. Taking T large while leaving the interior unchanged does not advance (8).

The coarsest sufficient new input is an actual sequence of polynomials p_m and truncations T_m for which the complete right side of (13) tends to zero, for each fixed chi at a common gamma below theta11. No such sequence is constructed here. The apparent replacement of a power bound by an o(1) limit changes the representation, not the established arithmetic difficulty.

## 3. W56-26: integral persistence and its complete source return

**Accept the full filtered decomposition.** Use augmented degree omega(n) for squarefree basis vector e_n, including e_1 in degree0, and ordered-prime deletion boundary. For every odd squarefree m define b_m=e_(2m), z_m=d b_m. Then

    z_m=e_m-e_2 wedge d(e_m),    d b_m=z_m,    d z_m=0.

All correction terms have indices2m/p<m because every p|m is odd. Replacing each odd e_m by z_m and retaining each even e_(2m) is therefore an integral unitriangular change of basis at EVERY real cutoff. No denominator or field change is involved. z_m enters exactly at m and b_m at2m. This directly splits the whole filtered chain complex into elementary two-term complexes and its homology persistence module into [m,2m), in degree omega(m). At death2m the class is already a boundary. The m=1 interval is included; reduced homological degree is shifted by one. Every inclusion is identity on a still-live class and zero after its death. Finite rank checks do not replace this proof.

All logarithmic lifetimes are log2. In particular H(C(x))->H(C(2x)) is zero although M(3)=-1. Thus observing only long-lived classes deletes the desired signed trace. This is a source-level observation, not a lower bound on the best possible use of a different filtration. Static squarefree topology and its prime2 contraction are already W27/Björner ancestry; the full integral filtered splitting and paid observation are the increment relative to this portfolio. No claim of literature novelty is established.

For fixed lambda in[1,2), alpha=lambda/2, the surviving classes of C(x)->C(lambda*x) are exactly alpha*x<m<=x, m odd squarefree. With actual ordinary chi, define

    O_chi(x)=sum_(m<=x, m odd) mu(m)chi(m),
    R_(alpha,chi)(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(alpha*x).

This is a weighted arithmetic barcode readout. It is not a trace of a character-twisted chain map: the prime deletion boundary is generally not equivariant for such a scalar multiplication. The distinction matters and the author retains it.

The exact odd/even reconstruction is

    M_chi(x)=O_chi(x)-chi(2)O_chi(x/2).

It includes the ramified case chi(2)=0 and all ordinary imprimitive characters. For Re s>1, termwise integration gives

    integral_0^infinity R_(alpha,chi)(x)x^(-s) dx/x
      =(1-alpha^s)/[s(1-chi(2)2^(-s))L(s,chi)].

The numerator has no zero in Re s>0; neither does1-chi(2)2^(-s). The source vanishes below1. An every-epsilon complete dyadic L2 bound at squared exponent2gamma extends the integral holomorphically to Re s>gamma by dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz and locally uniform convergence. It excludes every L-zero in that half-plane, at every height. At a principal pole,1/L vanishes, so no spurious pole is asserted. The zero exclusion is for each fixed chi with allowed chi-dependent constants/thresholds and common gamma. No conductor-uniform theorem is imported.

For pointwise bounds, the finite exact telescoping O(x)=sum_(j>=0)R(alpha^j x), with terms zero below1, costs(1-alpha^gamma)^(-1) at gamma>0. The fixed-lag unsigned rank is (4/pi^2)(1-alpha)x+O(sqrt(x)), so positivity alone does not supply the required signed cancellation.

**Accept the moving-window eta loss, with its stated scope.** For0<eta<1 put T(x)=x-x^(1-eta), x>=2. The corresponding arithmetic difference has the trivial O(x^(1-eta)) bound. Its interpretation as an inclusion image requires lambda(x)=2-2x^(-eta)>=1, which holds only for x>=2^(1/eta); the finite initial range must be paid separately. Iterate x_(j+1)=T(x_j) until below2. In a dyadic band[2^k,2^(k+1)), each step removes at least2^(k(1-eta)), so there are at most2+2^(k eta) steps. For gamma>=0 a bound R_eta(x)=O(x^gamma) consequently gives O_chi(x)=O(x^(gamma+eta)) after summing bands and the terminal bounded range. There is no free fixed-width Mellin inversion when alpha depends on x.

The loss is sharp for this generic recovery: an odd constant comparison source has O(x)~x/2 and R_eta(x)~x^(1-eta)/2. It is not an actual Möbius lower bound. At eta=1/4 a first gain needs gamma<.6248540364; the trivial gamma=3/4 is inadequate. A new signed window estimate or genuinely different filtered source is still needed.

## 4. W56-01: exact finite bank and its limits

Let U be the SAME complete ordinary-character Möbius Gaussian, S U(x)=U(x/2), a=15/8, b=31/16. ## 5. W56-28: conditional same-zero density gain

### Complete common-cutoff calculation

Write d=delta in[.68,.70], v=z/W. The short branches have

    I(r)=1-d*r+d[v-(1-r)/2]_+,
    P(m)=1-2d*m+d[v-(1-2m)/K]_+,

    r_*(t)=min(2t/3,[u*t+d(1/K-v)]/(d+u)).

The maximum/minimum orientations are correct: P is the maximum of its two pieces, so its increasing graph crosses the decreasing I at the smaller of their individual r-crossings. For J_eta^all,0<eta<=.001,0<=v<=.05, choose the SAME t=t_*-eta before witnesses. Suppose I improves to I-eta only for actual simultaneous large-plain rows with |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta. At its new crossing write d_r for displacement to the left. Integrating the increasing piecewise affine graph gives eta=(delta+b_eff)d_r, b_eff in[u,2delta]. Therefore the entire short maximum falls by at least alpha*eta relative to its old value at the new cutoff.

Reducing t by eta can increase the old short maximum by at most(2delta/3)eta, since its two slopes have magnitudes2delta/3 and delta*alpha. The long branch falls by(5/6-delta)eta. On the entire delta interval,

    alpha-2delta/3 >=2/15,

Consequently the complete free-row gain is h*eta*W, h=2/15. Equality in the second inequality at delta=.70 is permitted; no strict margin is invented there. At eta=.001 the gain is W/7500.     rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)],
