# [research revision] independent headroom branch B — one-grid arithmetic-wavelet obstruction

Status: PROVED RESTRICTED OBSTRUCTION, pending independent review. No new c. Deadline 2026-10-11T23:40:00Z. Draft writer [research revision]-headroom-b owns only this directory; canonical research, tracker and Git are untouched.

## Frozen objective and discovery

The accepted written analytic endpoint is c4=25027/200000=.125135, relative to pinned Gao PR15/PR9. Its full new-endpoint formal/kernel replay remains pending. A new claim must beat sigma4=1-c4=.874865. The targets 5/6 and 3/4 for the zero-free boundary remain. Historical c2/c3 examples are not new gains.

Five independent seeds and their scope are frozen in seed-checkpoint.md: additive short windows; completely multiplicative Liouville/gcd collapse; higher rough convolutions; arithmetic residue-wavelet/source-resolvent revival; and joint incommensurable grids. The chosen lane is the fourth, with a precise fifth-seed repair gate. This rotates to F08.N1/N2 and F19 rather than another refinement of recent f3/Gaussian small-value work.

A square-root short-window estimate at H=X^theta has nominal c=theta/2, hence c=1/4 at theta=1/2, but needs a complete moving-window transfer and actual power cancellation. Liouville has reciprocal zeta signal through zeta(2s)/zeta(s) above 1/2, but its primitive-pair energy is not supplied. Higher rough convolutions retain all alternating complements and only relocate the signed correlation. None of these observations is admitted as a theorem or gain.

## 1. Exact source and its quantitative return

Use the literal F08 arithmetic source

  H_sigma=L2((0,1),x^(2sigma-1) dx),   0<sigma<1,
  f_n(x)={1/(n x)}-(1/n){1/x},   n>=1,   f_1=0.

On 1/(k+1)<x<=1/k its value is (k mod n)/n. All cell endpoints are measure-zero and every later reciprocal cell is retained. The exact norm of a cell-constant F is

  ||F||_sigma^2=(1/(2sigma)) sum_(k>=1)
                  [k^(-2sigma)-(k+1)^(-2sigma)] |F(k)|^2.       (B1)

The Mellin functional E_s(F)=integral_0^1 F(x)x^(s-1)dx is continuous for Re(s)>sigma, with norm [2(Re(s)-sigma)]^(-1/2). Direct integration, initially Re(s)>1 and then continuation, gives

  E_s(f_n)=zeta(s)(n^(-1)-n^(-s))/s.                           (B2)

At s=1 the removable value is log(n)/n. No pole is discarded. If 1 is approximable by finite original f_n combinations in H_sigma, then a zero rho with Re(rho)>sigma and rho!=1 would give E_rho(F)=0 for every approximant but E_rho(1)=1/rho, a contradiction. This is the sufficient zero-exclusion return used here; no stronger converse or ordinary-character transfer is claimed.

The actual dormant dyadic extension SW34 in [restricted mathematical source] uses

  w_(2,n)=2 f_(2n)-f_n.

More generally for an integer q>=2 set

  w_(q,n)=q f_(qn)-f_n = floor(k/n) mod q on reciprocal cell k.

It vanishes on all k<n. Directly from B2,

  E_s(w_(q,n))=eta_q(s)n^(-s)/s,
  eta_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))zeta(s).                               (B3)

For k!=0 let s_(q,k)=1+2 pi i k/log q. These are artificial common zeros: eta_q(s_(q,k))=0, because zeta is holomorphic at those nonreal points. In contrast eta_q(1)=log q. Thus the pole cancellation at the real point does not cancel the nonreal lattice.

## 2. The full signed one-grid span has a positive error floor

Let W_q be the H_sigma-closed span of all w_(q,n), n>=1. For any finite or norm-limit W in W_q, B3 and continuity give E_(s_(q,k))(W)=0. Cauchy-Schwarz therefore proves

  ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= 2(1-sigma)/(1+(2 pi k/log q)^2),  k!=0.    (B4)

This is a lower bound on the complete signed source norm, including every future repetition and cross term. It is not a failure of termwise absolute summation. It allows arbitrary complex coefficients, arbitrary choice/order of indices, refitting, and arbitrary finite linear combinations of the exact source wavelets.

In particular the exact operators SW34-SW35 cannot alone form a compatible capture chain converging to 1 in H_sigma at any sigma<1. Their valid second-shell leakage identity SW38 remains valid. What is ruled out is promoting these fixed-dyadic extensions, even with perfectly signed tail estimates, to full closure of the target.

For q=2, log2>2/3 and pi<22/7 give the deliberately coarse rigorous floor

  ||1-W||_sigma^2 > (98/4405)(1-sigma).                       (B5)

Thus even the target sigma=.874864 (c=.125136, only .000001 beyond c4) has a fixed positive floor. Exact rational values are recorded by check_exact.py. The same obstruction persists at sigma=5/6 and sigma=3/4. It already fails at the present endpoint; no rebudgeting of a finite tail can make it a first gain.

## 3. Finite arithmetic seeds cannot repair the fixed grid

THEOREM. For every finite E subset of positive integers,

  dist_(H_sigma)(1, W_q + span{f_n:n in E}) > 0.              (B6)

Proof. First suppose a fixed S=sum_(n in E)c_n f_n satisfies 1-S in W_q. Evaluating at every nonzero s_k=s_(q,k) implies

  zeta(s_k) P(s_k)=1,
  P(s)=sum_(n in E)c_n(n^(-1)-n^(-s)).                       (B7)

Put alpha_n=log n/log q. Simultaneous Dirichlet approximation supplies, for every integer Q>=2, an integer 1<=k<=Q^r with max_n ||k alpha_n||<=1/Q, where r=|E| (terms n=1 may be removed; if no terms remain B4 applies). To prove this directly, put Q^r+1 orbit points j*(alpha_n)_n mod1 into Q^r equal coordinate boxes and subtract two in the same box. If such k remain bounded along Q->infinity, one nonzero k has all phases exactly integral, so P(s_k)=0 and B7 fails. Otherwise choose k->infinity. Since k<=Q^r, the phase bound gives

  |P(s_k)| <= (2pi/Q) sum_(n in E)|c_n|/n.

The elementary bound |zeta(1+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)) then makes zeta(s_k)P(s_k)->0, since log(k)/Q<=r log(Q)/Q->0. This contradicts B7.

For completeness the zeta bound follows without an unproved zero-free input: for integer N>=1 and Re(s)>0, s!=1,

 zeta(s)=sum_(n<=N)n^(-s)+N^(1-s)/(s-1)
              -s integral_N^infinity {u}u^(-s-1)du.

At s=1+it choose N=max(1,ceil |t|); the finite sum is O(log(2+|t|)) and both remaining terms are O(1) for |t|>=1.

Finally W_q is closed and adding a finite-dimensional space gives a closed subspace. If the distance in B6 were zero, a fixed S of the preceding form would exist. This proves strict positivity uniformly over all varying seed coefficients, even if those coefficients diverge before projection. No numerical conditioning assumption is used. The empty seed case is B4.

For a specified fixed S there is the explicit evaluable lower bound

 dist(1-S,W_q)^2 >= sup_(k!=0)
  2(1-sigma)|1-zeta(s_k)P(s_k)|^2/|s_k|^2.                  (B8)

B6 does not supply a useful numerical lower bound uniform over every finite E. Its strict positivity is enough to disprove convergence for any fixed finite patch.

## 4. Why this changes the live source contract

The old SW41 obstruction showed that absolute summation of all future repetitions diverges for sigma<=1; its text explicitly left signed arithmetic-wavelet capture open. B4-B6 go further for the exact fixed-q Haar frame: even optimal signed combinations cannot approximate the target, and a fixed finite arithmetic starting fit cannot repair it. This is a restriction of the broader F08.N1 proposal, which permits arbitrary balanced n f_n-m f_m. Those larger families and the full original f_n space are NOT ruled out.

Any finite family of dilation ratios that are powers of one integer base shares a nonreal lattice and has the same obstruction (replace q by that base in the annihilating lattice). Merely adding more dyadic widths or smoothing coefficients within the same frame does not help.

The weakest plausible repair is to introduce genuinely incommensurable integer dilation ratios at unbounded stages, for example 2 and 3. Their factors 1-2^(1-s) and 1-3^(1-s) have no common nonreal zero: a common zero would force 2^a=3^b for positive integers a,b. At s=1 the canceled factors have values eta_2(1)=log2 and eta_3(1)=log3. Zeta zeros remain common as required. Absence of artificial common zeros is only a necessary repair; it is not arithmetic closure. Adding only finitely many q=3 wavelets is still a finite arithmetic seed and is ruled out by B6, so the second family must grow.

The literal repaired extension is

 (W_(q,N)R)(k)=sum_(j>=1) b_q(j) R(floor(k/j)),
 b_q(j)=1-q 1_(q divides j),                                (B9)

obtained by replacing SW34 with sum_(n=N)^(2N) [R(n)-R(n-1)] w_(q,n). It retains every later repetition, including all q=2 versus q=3 mixed products in a combined energy. Prefix preservation and the first-shell equality still hold because b_q(1)=1. No common-grid tail or mixed Gram term is silently inherited.

OPEN REPAIR: prove a full signed compatible capture or source-resolvent estimate for such a genuinely enlarged arithmetic frame at a fixed sigma<.874865. In the capture formulation, exact successive orthogonal projections give d_(j+1)^2=d_j^2-g_j; a sufficient complete estimate is g_j>=delta_j d_j^2 with sum delta_j=infinity. No positive decay rate is intrinsically required, but every full-tail norm, every cross-grid interaction, and every step of the fixed arithmetic span must be included. The one-grid theorem proves that this condition cannot hold indefinitely for the unpatched fixed-q source.

## 5. Strongest objection and scope

Objection: the first fitted arithmetic block might remove the artificial resonance, or the signed future tails might do so. B6 addresses a fixed finite block, while B3-B4 already include fully signed tails and arbitrary refitting. A starting correction from an infinite enlarged family is a materially different mechanism, not a finite patch. Two incommensurable grids are a legitimate surviving candidate but their complete arithmetic capture remains unproved.

This report proves an obstruction for the actual zeta fractional-part source. It does not prove a Gaussian/f3 bound, an H covariance estimate, a Dirichlet/Hecke transfer, any claim about growing conductors or angular characters, or a better zero-free constant. Existing coefficients/masks/projectors in the Gaussian and H architectures are not replaced. The current written c4 and all accepted restricted results remain intact.

## 6. Ancestry, evidence and handoff

Direct ancestry: F08.A/N1/N2, F19, the [research revision] merged portfolio section9, and [research revision]-continuation/scale-wavelets.md SW33-SW41. Nearby N28 common-dilation small-divisor ideas are acknowledged; this result concerns the exact arithmetic Haar span and its finite-seed obstruction, rather than merely a generic exponential countermodel. Initial discovery did not read the independent peer output.

Primary outside source consulted directly: Michel Balazard and Eric Saias, The Nyman-Beurling equivalent form for the Riemann hypothesis (1998), https://www.esi.ac.at/preprints/esi623.pdf, especially its Mellin identity/orthogonal formulation. It supplies context, not the new wavelet theorem: B2-B8 are derived in full above, and the weighted norm and finite-seed argument are not imported from a citation.

Independent review is required before controller acceptance. Useful next work is the paired q=2,3 full arithmetic Gram/capture, with an explicit complete first-gain estimate; another one-grid signed-tail optimization is ruled out by this source obstruction.

## 7. A stronger exact floor and the literal interpolating coefficients

The whole resonance lattice gives a useful sharper bound. Put a=1-sigma, h=log q, and

  I_q(u)=(q^u-1)/u for u!=0,   I_q(0)=log q.

Then every W in W_q obeys

 ||1-W||_sigma^2 >= J_(q,sigma),
 J_(q,sigma)=(1-q^(-2a))/(1-q^(-1))^2
       *[ I_q(-2sigma)-I_q(1-2sigma)^2/I_q(2a) ] >0.         (B10)

Proof. The isometry U F(y)=exp(-sigma*y)F(exp(-y)) sends H_sigma to L2(0,infinity). The evaluation vectors for the nonreal lattice are exp(-a*y)exp(2pi i k y/h), k!=0. Their closed span consists exactly of exp(-a*y)phi(y mod h), where phi has zero unweighted mean on [0,h]. This follows because the induced weight

  W(r)=exp(-2a*r)/(1-exp(-2a*h))

is bounded above and below by positive constants on that compact interval. The target U1=exp(-sigma*y) pairs with phi through

  H(r)=exp(-r)/(1-exp(-h)).

Its projected squared norm onto this annihilating subspace is

  integral H^2/W -(integral H/W)^2/(integral 1/W),            (B11)

all integrals over [0,h]. The orthogonal complement of the zero-mean phi space in L2(W dr) is span{1/W}; this proves B11. Evaluating the three elementary integrals gives B10. Strict Cauchy-Schwarz gives positivity because H(r) is not constant. Every q-wavelet is orthogonal to every vector in this closed span by B3. No unproved characterization of the full annihilator is needed: B10 is a lower bound, not an assertion of the exact distance to W_q.

For the first-gain example sigma=.874864, the displayed all-mode value is approximately .0098719719458. This decimal is illustrative; B10's formula and strict positivity are proved, and the deliberately coarser exact certificate remains

   ||1-W||^2 > 383229/137656250.                            (B12)

The current c4 floor is 1226323/440500000; the corresponding floors at 1/6 and 1/4 are 49/13215 and 49/8810. These positive constants are complete norm obstructions, not error exponents to be added to the separate Gaussian or H budgets.

There is also an exact arithmetic explanation for the tail escaping every fitted prefix. Define

  a_q(n)=sum_(j>=0:q^j divides n) q^j mu(n/q^j),
  b_q(n)=1-q 1_(q divides n).

Their finite Dirichlet convolution is a_q*b_q=delta_1. Consequently

  H_(q,N)(k)=sum_(n<=N)a_q(n) w_(q,n)(k)=1 for k<=N.         (B13)

These coefficients are uniquely forced if only w_(q,1),...,w_(q,N) are used to fit all first N cells, by the triangular diagonal w_(q,n)(n)=1. For q=2 and odd m,

  a_2(m)=mu(m),
  a_2(2^r m)=2^(r-1)mu(m), r>=1.                           (B14)

Thus original squarefree zeros in mu(m) are retained literally. Despite pointwise prefix convergence, B10 gives ||1-H_(q,N)||^2>=J_(q,sigma) for every N. Since its error is supported on reciprocal cells k>N, whose H_sigma measure is (N+1)^(-2sigma)/(2sigma), the conditional RMS of that complete future error is at least

  sqrt(2sigma J_(q,sigma)) (N+1)^sigma.                     (B15)

This is an actual-source tail growth statement. It does not presume a conjecture about Mertens sums. It shows why finite prefix agreement and an attractive first leakage shell cannot certify the proposed infinite signed scheme.

## 8. A coarse paid conditioning lemma for the surviving two-grid option

This analytic lemma is restricted to the paired multiplier; it supplies no arithmetic capture. Define the entire normalized factors

  B_q(s)=(1-q^(1-s))/(s-1),    B_q(1)=log q.

For every T>=1 and |t|<=T,

  |B_2(1+it)|^2+|B_3(1+it)|^2
        >= exp(-2T)/[4(1+T)^2].                           (B16)

Here is a direct coarse proof, avoiding an ineffective irrationality assertion. For |t|>=1 let delta=max(|1-exp(-it log2)|,|1-exp(-it log3)|). Choose the nearest integers m,n to t log2/(2pi), t log3/(2pi). By replacing t by |t|, assume t>0. Their phase errors are at most pi delta/2. If delta<1/2, m,n cannot both vanish, since that would imply t log3<=pi/4<log3, contrary to t>=1. Unique factorization gives 3^m!=2^n. Hence

  |m log3-n log2| >= 1/max(3^m,2^n)
       >= 3^(-1/2) exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi)).

On the other hand the phase-error relation bounds this logarithm by delta log6/4. Thus delta>=(4/(sqrt3 log6))exp(-t log2 log3/(2pi))>=exp(-t)/2. If delta>=1/2, the last bound also holds. Dividing by t proves max|B_q|>=exp(-t)/(2t). For |t|<=1, the elementary sine chord bound gives |B_2|>=2log2/pi>1/4. These bounds imply B16.

For any measurable V(t) and W_q(t)=B_q(1+it)V(t), the exact recovery is

  V(t)=sum_(q=2,3) conjugate(B_q) W_q / (|B_2|^2+|B_3|^2).

On |t|<=T this has spectral L2 norm cost at most 2(1+T)exp(T). A local physical square expansion must retain the four ordered grid pairs and the two independent heights; this recovery does not justify replacing that local square by its t=t' diagonal or by separate source pieces.

The complete-height Gaussian version is also paid: for every fixed tau>tau'>0,

 integral_R |exp(tau*(1+it)^2/2)V(t)|^2 dt
 <= C_(tau,tau') sum_(q=2,3)
       integral_R |exp(tau'*(1+it)^2/2)W_q(t)|^2 dt.         (B17)

Indeed the squared inverse cost is at most 4(1+|t|)^2 exp(2|t|) (for |t|<=1 the same chord bound gives |B_3|>=2log3/pi>1/2), and multiplying it by exp(-(tau-tau')t^2) is uniformly bounded. The harmless real Gaussian factor exp(tau-tau') is absorbed in the fixed constant. This proves the whole-height comparison, not merely a truncated statement with an unpaid tail.

At the current Gaussian height scale T=D sqrt(log X), the finite-height inverse coefficient cost and its two-height squared coefficient cost are X^o(1); this is not itself a local-energy inequality. Thus deliberately coarse elementary conditioning does not itself impose a fixed positive exponent loss for this paired multiplier. The missing theorem is still the exact original-source arithmetic approximation/capture with a coefficient construction and all cross-grid terms. B16-B17 alone do not transfer arbitrary local Gaussian energies, prove membership in the required half-plane Hardy space, or prove the open repair.

## 9. Verification and operational record

check_exact.py and evidence.json verify the literal reciprocal-cell formula, all restoration signs, Dirichlet inverse identities, exact prefix fits, the q=2 natural-zero formula, and the rational first-gain/current/1/6/1/4 floors. The finite arithmetic checks are supporting evidence; proofs of B4, B6, B10 and B16-B17 are the displayed analytic arguments. Approximate decimal displays do not enter a rigorous inequality.

The report is below 32 KiB. Source hashes identify the exact local mathematical contracts read. The live canonical checkpoint remains root-owned. The original deadline survives the definite stream interruption and root's saved-prefix reconciliation; the same exact claim and source reasoning were retained.


## 10. Direct source-resolvent consequence

This also rules out a purely reweighted Schur/resolvent repair of the same dictionary. For any positive summable weights v_n and any fixed finite arithmetic seed set E with positive weights u_n, define

 K= sum_(n>=1) v_n (w_(q,n) tensor w_(q,n))
           +sum_(n in E) u_n(f_n tensor f_n).

Because |w_(q,n)|<=q-1, K is positive trace class and

 ker K=(W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^perp.

For the actual target 1 the spectral theorem, exactly as in A08.2, gives

 lim_(lambda down to0) <1,lambda(K+lambda I)^(-1)1>
   = ||P_(ker K)1||^2
   = dist(1,W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^2 >0.                    (B18)

For no seeds this limit is at least J_(q,sigma), and the same lower bound holds for the resolvent at every lambda>0. The failure survives polynomial, exponential or predetermined dyadic-block reweighting, arbitrary finite truncation strategies, and arbitrarily slow proposed o(1) rates. It is the target's genuine positive zero atom for this exact arithmetic dictionary; compactness is not being used as a surrogate for an arithmetic theorem. Adding unbounded genuinely new arithmetic directions is the surviving repair.

This recombines the proved A08 spectral identity with the exact SW34 wavelet source, giving the weakest complete first-gain test a decisive negative answer: even o(1), without a specified power or contraction rate, is impossible for this fixed grid. The larger A08 operator using all original f_n, the variable-ratio A09 correction, and arbitrary-ratio F08 remain open and are not subject to B18's dictionary restriction.

statement:
## T09. Scale-\(L^2\) direct detectors

### T09a. One fixed Möbius profile

Let
\[
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\quad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))',\quad
S_\phi(x)=\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\phi(n/x).
\]
For \(0<a<1\), suppose for every \(\epsilon>0\) and every sufficiently large dyadic \(X\),
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\,\frac{dx}{x}
\ll_\epsilon X^{2a+\epsilon}. \tag{T09.1}
\]
Then \(\zeta\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>a\).

Indeed, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\), Cauchy bounds the Mellin contribution of one shell by \(X^{-\delta+\epsilon/2}\). Taking \(\epsilon<2\delta\) makes the dyadic sum and every fixed complex derivative converge locally uniformly. At zero the function is exponentially small. Thus
\[
F(s)=\int_0^\infty S_\phi(x)x^{-s}\frac{dx}{x}
\]
is holomorphic for \(\Re s>a\). Initially \(F(s)=\Phi(s)/\zeta(s)\), where [research revision] proves
\[
\Phi(s)=2(1-s)K_s(2).
\]
For completeness, a zero \(K_s(2)=0\) would give \(f(t)=K_s(2e^t)\), \(t\ge0\), with Dirichlet boundary and
\[
\int_0^\infty(|f'|^2+4e^{2t}|f|^2)\,dt
=-s^2\int_0^\infty|f|^2\,dt>0.
\]
Hence such \(s\) is purely imaginary. Therefore \(\Phi\) has no zeros in \(\Re s>0\) except \(1\). Continue
\[
(s-1)\zeta(s)F(s)=(s-1)\Phi(s).
\]
Any proposed zeta zero in \(\Re s>a\) contradicts the nonzero right side. No uniform lower bound for \(\Phi(\sigma+it)\) is used.

The exact positive scale kernel is
\[
\int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
=\sum_{m,n}\mu(m)\mu(n)
\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
The arithmetic coefficients retain signs and all shared primes.

### The exact full shift kernel and its affordable diagonal

Define
\[
 K_X(m,n)=\int_1^2\phi(m/(Xt))\overline{\phi(n/(Xt))}\,\frac{dt}{t}.
\]
Absolute convergence, using the rapid decay of \(\phi\) at both ends, permits the exact regrouping
\[
 \int_X^{2X}|S_\phi(x)|^2\frac{dx}{x}
 =\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)^2K_X(n,n)
 +2\Re\sum_{h\ge1}\sum_{n\ge1}\mu(n)\mu(n+h)K_X(n,n+h).
 \tag{T09.1a}
\]
The diagonal is \(O(X)\): uniformly for \(1\le t\le2\), integer counting gives \(\sum_n|\phi(n/(Xt))|^2\ll X\), and then integrate in \(t\). It is separately affordable for \(a\ge1/2\), including every intended numerical target. For \(a<1/2\), cancellation between this diagonal and the off-diagonal would still be required. More generally,
\[
 |K_X(m,n)|\ll_A (1+m/X)^{-A}(1+n/X)^{-A}.
\]
This bound follows directly from the upper-end Schwartz bounds for each factor; the lower-end decay only improves it. It justifies the regrouping and tail truncations with explicit losses, but gives no short-shift support. When \(m,n\asymp X\), differences of order \(X\) remain. Thus the next sufficient estimate is for the complete signed weighted off-diagonal in (T09.1a), including shared-prime and product coincidences. A fixed-shift theorem alone does not establish (T09.1). This exact decomposition and diagonal bound are an additional merger result used in portfolio F01.N1.

### Frozen-dyad balanced finite form

Set, for large \(X\),
\[
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil.
\]
Use [research revision]'s fixed smooth cutoffs \(\rho,\chi\), and define on \(x\in[X,2X]\)
\[
\mathcal B_X(x)=
\sum_{d,e>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)
\rho(de/T_l)\chi(de/T_u)
\sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell de/x).
\]
For every \(A>0\) and fixed Euler derivative order \(r\),
\[
(x\partial_x)^r\{S_\phi(x)-\mathcal B_X(x)\}
=O_{A,r}(X^{-A}). \tag{T09.2}
\]
This is a bounded extension of [research revision] V7–V8, not a new cancellation estimate.

To prove it, apply the exact Möbius convolution identity with the same arithmetic cutoff \(Y\) throughout the dyad. The short Möbius term is exponentially small. In the Type-I term \(de/x\le L^{-4}\); lower removed Type-II products have \(de/x\le2L^{-4}\). [research revision] V6's complete Poisson cancellation bounds these by \(e^{-cL^2}\) before truncating the \(\ell\)-sum. The infinite upper product tail has \(de/x\ge L^2/2\) and is likewise superpolynomially small after divisor counting. On the retained support \(Jde/x\ge4L^2\), so truncating \(\ell>J\) costs the same. There are \(O(XL^3)\) retained pairs, all with
\[
\sqrt X/L^2<d,e<2\sqrt X L^4.
\]
Every arithmetic cutoff is fixed on the dyad; differentiating only changes the smooth profile. The same endpoint estimates hold for each fixed Euler derivative. Replacing \(S_\phi\) by \(\mathcal B_X\) in (T09.1) changes energy by \(O_A(X^{-A})\) after reserving a larger preliminary \(A\).

At \(a=.87449\), the target squared-energy exponent is \(1.74898\). The gain over the inherited baseline squared-energy bound is \(0.000793294079928262\ldots\). The energy estimate remains open; averaging does not erase a hypothetical \(x^\rho\) mode.

### T09b. Compact-profile triple-convolution criterion

Let \(P_r(y)\) be the exact [research revision] Z13–Z15 triple convolution, including equal-element projection, fixed good sectors, and all cube/core overlaps. For \(5/6<a<1\), suppose
\[
\int_Y^{2Y}\int_1^2|P_r(y)|^2\,dr\,\frac{dy}{y}
\ll_\epsilon Y^{\,2(3-2a)-\epsilon} \tag{T09.3}
\]
for every sufficiently small dyadic \(Y\) and every \(\epsilon>0\). Then \(\zeta_K^S\), and hence \(\zeta\), is zero-free in \(\Re s>a\).

Take \(H=L^2([1,2],dr)\) and \(P(y)=(P_r(y))_r\). Cauchy gives, on \(\Re s\ge a+\delta\),
\[
\left\|\int_Y^{2Y}P(y)y^{2s-3}\frac{dy}{y}\right\|_H
\ll Y^{2(\Re s-a)-\epsilon/2}.
\]
Choose \(\epsilon<4\delta\). The Bochner Mellin integral is holomorphic; large \(y\) decays exponentially uniformly on the compact \(r\)-interval. Initially its exact value is
\[
J_\bullet(s)
\frac{L^S(3s-3/2,\xi_{\rm ang})}{\zeta_K^S(s)},
\quad
J_r(s)=\int_0^\infty t^{2s}K_{1/3}(\kappa t)^2
K_{1/3}(\kappa rt)\,dt.
\]
For fixed \(\Re s>0\), \(r\mapsto J_r(s)\) is analytic on \(r>0\). [research revision] Z16 proves a nonzero gamma-product limit for \(r^{1/3}J_r(s)\) as \(r\downarrow0\). Therefore \(J_r(s)\) cannot vanish almost everywhere on \([1,2]\); its \(H\)-norm is positive. The angular numerator is nonzero because \(3\Re s-3/2>1\). Continue the identity after multiplication by \((s-1)\zeta_K^S(s)\), and evaluate at a hypothetical zero. The right side is a nonzero vector, contradiction.

This removes the need for estimates uniform as \(r\to0\) or an individual zero-free kernel \(J_1\). It does not supply the arithmetic decay. At \(a=.87449\), the squared \(Y\)-exponent is \(2.50204\); \(N=Y^{-2}\) is a different scale.

**Sources:** BB R06–R07; [research revision] V1–V10; [research revision] Z13–Z18.
title: T09. Scale-\(L^2\) direct detectors

## G97. Exact local diagnostics and a growing filter's reconstruction cost

On the first cell, the source often simplifies drastically. For even chi,
r=2 and m_chi=q^-1 sum_(j mod q)chi(j),

    Phi(x)=2L(2,chi)-2pi^2 m_chi x+2pi^2 chi(0)x^2.

For q1 use chi(0)=1. For every even nonprincipal character both extra
coefficients vanish. On the complete shrinking arc,

    R_N(x)=2L(2,chi)T_N+2cos(2pi x)-2,
    abs(sqrt(E_arc)-sqrt(h)*abs(2L(2,chi)T_N)) << h^(5/2).

Thus in this class the proposed arc estimate is explicitly a single
weighted tail estimate. For odd chi and r3,
Phi(x)=2L(3,chi)-4pi^2L(1,chi)x^2 on the first cell. The finite Bernoulli
formula justifies the endpoint differentiation; convergence of L(1,chi)
suffices, with no assumed left-half-plane nonvanishing.

Localized squarefree averaging preserves the signs and phases on reduced
quotients u,v. For the signed sector u,v<=H<=N the author proves

    E_(N,H)=N^-2r D_H
       +O_(q,r,epsilon)(N^(-2r-1/2)H^(3/2+epsilon)), |D_H|<<H.

The localized derivative bound lacks the extra(uv)^-r from complete-period
orthogonality. At H~N the accumulated error has no power saving, and
quotients>N are still omitted. H=N^(1-2c-kappa) pays only a sector already
inside the large-gcd complement. Neither limitation is an arithmetic
lower bound; better signed summation remains eligible.

The critic develops a genuine shrinking-spacing filter:

    F_(N,H)=R_N-R_(N+H), 1<=H<=N,
    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2<<H N^-2r.

For unequal n,m in the block, (n,m)<=H. The exact global Gram and at most
4H^2/g^2 distinct pairs of multiples yield the bound. More precisely,

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)d_q H N^-2r
       +O(N^(1/2-2r)+H^2N^(-2r-1)+H^(2r+1)N^-4r).

For H=N^alpha,1/2<alpha<1 this is a positive leading asymptotic. Choosing
H=N^(1-2c) has the desired formal energy gain for0<c<1/4; at c1/4 the
upper bound survives but the elementary asymptotic error is not smaller.

Recovering the original signal remains essential. Use a common arc of
length1/(2qN), partition(N,2N] into aboutN/H blocks, and pay the actual
endpoint observer on each. Separate norms and triangle reassembly give

    |sum_(N<n<=2N)a(n)n^-r|<<N^(3/2-r)H^-1/2.

At H=N^(1-2c) this is N^(1+c-r), weaker than the elementary full-tail
bound. Cauchy-Schwarz on block labels alone does not improve that cost.
The small filtered norm is valid but cannot also pay an unproved signed
reconstruction. A coupled growing filter or genuinely new observation
remains open; its complete reconstruction is the next decisive test.

### Polynomial-height consequence

Suppose `F` is fixed and entire, has polynomial growth on every fixed vertical strip, and has a positive uniform lower bound on one fixed right-hand vertical line. For `s0=sigma+it` in a buffered strip, take a fixed small disk about `s0` and a larger fixed-radius disk anchored on that right-hand line. In (T01.1), `m` is bounded below and `M<<T^B`, `T=2+|t|`. Consequently
\[
\|U(s_0)\|^2\ll T^C\sup_{|s-s_0|\le r}\|F(s)U(s)\|^2.
\tag{T01.2}
\]
A completed vector estimate with arithmetic exponent `X^rho` therefore retains that exponent after extraction. The larger disk need only be a domain for `F`; only the smaller disk requires holomorphy and bounds for `U`.

Take `F(s)=L^S(3s-1,xi)`, where `xi` is the fixed nontrivial angular Hecke character. Entire continuation, fixed-strip polynomial growth, and the fixed-conductor functional equation are among the source inputs. The absolutely convergent Euler product gives the required lower bound on a right-hand line. For moving finite deletions,
\[
L^{(Sh)}(3s-1,\xi)=F(s)E_h(s),\qquad
E_h(s)=\prod_{p\mid h,\,p\notin S}(1-\xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}).
\]
On `Re s>=a>1/2`, for every `delta>0`,
\[
|E_h(s)|+|E_h(s)|^{-1}\ll_{a,S,\delta}q_h^\delta.
\tag{T01.3}
\]
Indeed `|xi(p)Q_p^{1-3s}|<=Q_p^{-(3a-1)}<1`. For sufficiently large prime norms each local factor or inverse is at most `Q_p^delta`; the finitely many smaller primes contribute a fixed constant. Multiply over distinct primes only. This costs a subpower of the physical row norm as well because the conductor radical divides the row.

If the completed estimate is given on every fixed vertical line, obtain the local strip bound by choosing two fixed neighboring lines, scalarizing the finite row vector against an arbitrary unit functional, and applying three-lines after division by a sufficiently high power of `C+s`. FD (59) permits the strip maximum principle with no uncontrolled height growth. Recover the vector norm by taking the supremum over unit functionals. This does not introduce a dimension factor or replace a sum by a sum of rowwise suprema. Cauchy estimates give any fixed number of spectral derivatives on a smaller strip.

Thus completed and uncompleted means, with arbitrary positive exponent losses and every fixed buffer, have the same arithmetic exponent. A Lipschitz dependence of that exponent on `Re s` is handled by choosing the local radius inside the allocated loss.

**Limits:** separate holomorphy is essential; the lemma cannot prove holomorphy of `1/zeta` from a holomorphic product. It does not create a missing period realization, extend a primitive-current estimate to a missing ray component, handle a moving angular character without uniform hypotheses, or remove a gamma factor with exponential height behavior. [research revision]'s gamma removal remains a necessary inherited step.
title: Polynomial-height consequence

## 3. Development 2: no finite preconditioner in the full sup norm (W52-02)

For gamma>0 let B_gamma contain all functions f on [1,infinity), extended by zero below1, with norm sup_(x>=1)x^-gamma|f(x)|. For a sequence c define the locally finite dilation operator

    (T_c f)(x)=sum_(n<=x)c(n)f(x/n).

Its extended operator norm, allowing infinity, is exactly

    ||T_c||_(B_gamma->B_gamma)=sum_(n>=1)|c(n)|n^-gamma.        (W5)

The upper bound is the triangle inequality. For the lower bound, fix K, take x=K and assign f(K/n)=(K/n)^gamma conjugate(c(n))/|c(n)| for nonzero c(n), n<=K, and zero elsewhere. The arguments K/n are distinct, ||f||<=1, and x^-gamma T_cf(x)=sum_(n<=K)|c(n)|n^-gamma. Let K increase.

The same infinite-space lower bound holds if f must be constant on each integer interval [j,j+1). For a fixed finite prefix n<=K, take a separate integer X tending to infinity with X>K(K+1). The values floor(X/n), n<=K, are distinct and each has no other integer n' in its quotient fiber. Put f on those intervals equal to floor(X/n)^gamma times the aligning phase, and zero elsewhere. The resulting ratio tends to the finite prefix in W5. This does **not** identify any single finite-X floor-merged norm with the unmerged price. It shows that arbitrary floor-invariant inputs over all scales still attain every fixed coefficient prefix.

Let b be any fixed finitely supported complex sequence, with support at most B, and set

    r=delta-b*chi.

**Finite-preconditioner obstruction.** At every 0<gamma<=1, T_r cannot have norm less than1 on B_gamma. If b(1)=0, r(1)=1 and W5 gives norm at least1. If b(1)!=0, then for every prime p>B not dividing q,

    r(p)=-b(1)chi(p).

Its prime contribution to W5 is infinite. Indeed sum_p 1/p diverges: otherwise the finite products product_(p<=Y)(1-1/p)^-1 would stay bounded, whereas each dominates the harmonic sum through Y. Removing finitely many ramified primes does not change divergence, and p^-gamma>=p^-1. Thus ||T_r||=infinity in this case. Natural zeros are kept, never divided out.

The certificate would have a genuine complete return if it existed. Since a*chi=delta,

    T_chi M_chi=1,     M_chi=T_b 1+T_r M_chi.                  (W6)

If ||T_r||=kappa<1 and T_b1 in B_gamma, the Banach inverse supplies U=(I-T_r)^-1T_b1 and ||U||<=||T_b1||/(1-kappa). This identifies U with the actual M_chi **without assuming M_chi is already in B_gamma**: kappa<1 forces b(1)!=0, and W6 determines the function successively on integer intervals from its smaller x/n arguments. The small interval [1,2) gives U=1, and induction gives U=M_chi. The zero-exclusion return is in section5.

The negative theorem is only for a fixed finite b and the full arbitrary-input weighted supremum norm. It does not forbid an infinite cancellation-sensitive inverse, a changing preconditioner with a completely paid return, or an invariant space restricted by real arithmetic constraints. Nor does it follow merely from a finite matrix being triangular. Checks with b(n)=mu(n)chi(n), n<=30, verify r(p)=-chi(p) for all36 primes in(30,210] and q=1,4,5; they do not replace the divergence proof.

statement:
## DQ9. The complementary classes force the opposite pole

For any finite collection `F` of cube-free classes, define its continued
complement by subtraction from the whole dual L-function. Exactly,

\[
L_{F^c}(1-z,\bar\eta)
=L(1-z,\bar\eta)-Z_{ce}(3-3z)
 \sum_{d\in F}\overline\eta(d)q_d^{z-1}.
\]

The whole nonprincipal L-function is entire at `z=2/3`; hence

\[
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=2/3}L_{F^c}(1-z,\bar\eta)
=\frac{\kappa_K}{3}
 \prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-1})
 \sum_{d\in F}\overline\eta(d)q_d^{-1/3}.
\tag{DQ9}
\]

This is precisely the opposite of the selected classes' residue. The pole is
introduced by the class projection, not a pole of whole CC. Its complementary
CC addback is compulsory and cannot be reassigned to II. In particular, one
cannot sum infinitely many class residues term by term or declare the
fixed-class polar estimate to be the full signed remainder.

statement:
### A1. The actual multiplicative Hankel is compact for an elementary reason

Fix sigma>1/2. On l2(N) set

    T_sigma(m,n)=f(mn)(mn)^(-sigma).

It is a real self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt operator, since

    ||T_sigma||_HS^2=sum_(m,n)(mn)^(-2sigma)=zeta(2sigma)^2.       (A1)

This uses |f|=1 exactly, including all prime powers. It gives no cancellation estimate. Under prime-exponent coordinates, for p!=3 put

    q_p=p^(-2sigma), R_p=q_p/(1-q_p),
    v_p=(p^(-sigma k))_(k>=1), ||v_p||^2=R_p.

The local matrix, on e0 and v_p/sqrt(R_p), is

    H_p=[[1,-sqrt(R_p)],[-sqrt(R_p),-R_p]],                     (A2)

and it vanishes on the orthogonal complement. At p=3 it is w_3 w_3^T, w_3(k)=3^(-sigma k), k>=0, of rank1. This is DIFFERENT from W29's squarefree/prime-two source: its odd block has lower-right0 and its prime-two block is3 by3. Replacing those blocks by A2 would be invalid; A2 is derived afresh for f3.

Let

    D_p=sqrt(1+6R_p+R_p^2),
    lambda_p^+=(1-R_p+D_p)/2,
    lambda_p^-=(1-R_p-D_p)/2,
    c_p=1/(lambda_p^++R_p).

Then lambda_p^+>1, lambda_p^-<0, 0<c_p<1, and

    lambda_p^+=1+c_p R_p,
    1-c_p=c_p(1+c_p)R_p<=2R_p.                              (A3)

The unit positive eigenvector has coordinates

    u_p(0)=(1+c_p^2 R_p)^(-1/2),
    u_p(k)=-c_p p^(-sigma k)u_p(0), k>=1.                    (A4)

All these are immediate two by two identities. Since sum_p R_p<infinity, the products of lambda_p^+ and u_p(0) converge to finite nonzero constants. The actual infinite vector with these local coordinates exists in l2: its squared norm is the convergent product of 1+c_p^2R_p times the square of the normalizing product. Finite-prime compressions of T converge in Hilbert–Schmidt norm by the absolutely convergent sum in A1; this justifies the tensor limit without an unproved infinite Euler continuation.
title: A1. The actual multiplicative Hankel is compact for an elementary reason

### Exact contact with the original far H form

At fixed original scales, finite ray components and BOTH independent
height variables, normalize original mark arrays by v_i(P)=u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P).
The complete finite far-packet form is a bilinear matrix pairing
`v_2^* T_H v_1`, with each entry DEFINED as its coefficient in the original
form. In constructing that entry retain the complete original g,g' and
row sums, bounded true-core weight, phases a(pi),xi(g), both projectors,
natural zeros, original sharp caps, and exact far mask
`q_pi!=q_pi'`, `|q_pi-q_pi'|>floor(Z^.05)`. There is no altered coefficient,
new positive submask, or renamed prime statistic in this definition.

Then `||v_i||_2^2=Omega_i`. Taking T=T_H in (22), with
`B=Z^epsilon G K S(N,L) P_orig` and the actual original profile factors,
would pay this raw packet. Multiplying once by the original physical

statement:
### 8.1 One fixed bounded-coefficient Gaussian field defeats fixed geometric samples

Fix L>0, 1/2<beta<1, omega=pi/L and the original tau. Define the SINGLE real sequence

    a(n)=n^(beta-1) sin(omega log n - tau*beta*omega).

It satisfies |a(n)|<=1. For its complete original Gaussian field,

    F_a(x)=exp(tau*(beta^2-omega^2)/2) x^beta sin(omega log x)
                                      +O_(beta,omega,tau)(x^(beta-1)).   (A06.1)

Proof: replace the sum by the integral of

    phi_x(t)=t^(beta-1) sin(omega log t-tau*beta*omega) g(log(t/x)).

With t=x exp(v), the integral is the imaginary part of

    exp(-i*tau*beta*omega) x^(beta+i*omega)
                            exp(tau*(beta+i*omega)^2/2),

which is the displayed main term. The function is flat at zero and decays at infinity. Differentiating and making the same substitution gives integral |phi_x'(t)|dt=O(x^(beta-1)); all remaining v-dependent factors are a fixed exponential times a Gaussian and polynomial/trigonometric factors. Comparing phi_x(n) with its integral over [n-1,n] bounds the complete sum-integral error by that derivative integral. Both tails are included.

At x_j=exp(jL) the main term vanishes, so these samples are only O(x_j^(beta-1)). At the intervening half-period they have size comparable to x^beta, and the L2 energy on each logarithmic interval of length L has exponent beta with a fixed positive constant. Thus very small values on this fixed geometric grid do not imply a full-field improved exponent, even for a single fixed bounded sequence and exactly the original Gaussian.

One may take beta<theta6 to fit a buffered baseline. This is not mu*chi, integer coefficients or a multiplicative construction. W43 seed12 already contains the log-periodic invisibility mechanism; W38/[research revision] contains different and stronger coefficient-class observation failures. The present calculation supplies an explicit bounded-coefficient fixed-Gaussian realization and does not erase those results or claim a new general countermodel family.

## R4. Kernel normalization, support and exact projected complement

For the rest of the review choose the least unramified p and fix

    h=1/(4p^2), omega=2 log p,
    K_h(theta)=3h/(8 pi) sinc(h theta/4)^4.                  (R4.1)

Here sinc(0)=1. This is a nonnegative integrable weight. To check every Fourier constant, let f_4 be the density of the sum of four independent uniforms on [-1,1]. Its characteristic function is sinc(t)^4, it is supported on [-4,4], and

    f_4(0)=[4^3-4(2^3)]/(2^4 3!)=1/3.

Fourier inversion applies because sinc(t)^4 is integrable. It gives integral_R sinc(t)^4 dt=2 pi/3. Changing variable t=h theta/4 yields integral K_h=1. In the convention hat K(xi)=integral K(theta)e^(i xi theta)dtheta,

    hat K_h(xi)=3 f_4(4xi/h),

using the evenness of f_4. Its support is [-h,h], and hat K_h(0)=1. For every other positive integer r,

    |log(r/p^2)| >= log(1+1/p^2)
       >1/(p^2+1)>1/(4p^2)=h.                              (R4.2)

The lower neighbor has a larger logarithmic gap, so it causes no exception. The scalar coefficient functional

    P_p U(x)=integral_R K_h(theta)e^(i omega theta)U(theta,x)dtheta

is bounded on L2(K_h dtheta), with norm 1. Equations R2.4 and R4.2 give

    P_p H(x)=p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x),
    M(x)=a(p)^(-1)p^(2delta)P_p H(px)
                           +g(log(1/x))+a(p)g(log(p/x)).   (R4.3)

Since a(p)=-chi(p) has modulus 1, scalar inversion has no exceptional zero. The kernel is positive; the phase-weighted scalar functional is not a pointwise positivity-preserving average. Its associated rank-one map U -> e^(-i omega theta)P_p U is an orthogonal projection in L2(K_h dtheta), which is the precise positivity relevant to the norm argument.

For A(x)=p^(-2delta)B_(p^2)(x), direct expansion therefore gives

    integral K_h |H|^2
      =|A(x)|^2+integral K_h |H-A(x)e^(-i omega theta)|^2.   (R4.4)

The cross term vanishes because P_p(H-Ae^(-i omega theta))=0. This extracts a lower bound containing the ENTIRE signed square of M minus its two atoms. In that square every ordered c,d pair has phase a(c)conjugate(a(d)); both free labels have theta exponent zero. Theta frequency diagonalization cannot distinguish those output correlations. At fixed x, a Bohr mean also gives sum_r r^(-2delta)|B_r(x)|^2 by absolute convergence. It supplies no quantitative finite-window diagonalization for the remaining frequency pairs.

Every p^2-frequency tuple has median <=p. Its complement consequently satisfies the exact FULL-LINE statement

    P_p(H-H_(median<=p))=0.                                (R4.5)

For least p the retained live field is exactly

    J(theta,x)=a(p)sum_(c>p) a(c)V_(delta+i theta)(1,p,c)^2
                                             g(log(pc/x)),
    P_p J=P_p H.                                           (R4.6)

No part of the unbounded free-label tail or a common-prime case is excepted. The zero is a statement about this linear functional. It does not state that the median complement has zero energy, that its cross terms with J vanish in the original energy, or that a signed norm bound on H controls a norm bound on J.

statement:
## 8. Developing the remaining growing-filter possibility

Fixed-filter coercivity leaves colliding scales open. A concrete test is the adjacent difference

    F_(N,H)=R_N-R_(N+H)=sum_(N<n<=N+H)a(n)n^(-r)Phi(nx),
    1<=H<=N, N,H integers.

This has an actual unconditional small global norm:

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2 <<_(q,r) H N^(-2r).                 (R15)

Proof: the complete-period Gram has diagonal at most 2L(2r,chi0)H N^(-2r). For distinct n,m in the block, g=gcd(n,m) divides |n-m| and hence g<=H. For each g, the number of ordered distinct pairs of multiples in the block is at most 4H^2/g^2. Consequently the absolute off-diagonal contribution is

    <<N^(-4r)H^2 sum_(g<=H)g^(2r-2)
      <<H^(2r+1)N^(-4r),

which is at most O(H N^(-2r)). This uses the actual signed arithmetic field; positivity is only used for the upper bound on the off-diagonal error.

More precisely the squarefree count and variation of n^(-2r) give

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)delta(q)H N^(-2r)
      +O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)+H^2N^(-2r-1)
                         +H^(2r+1)N^(-4r)).             (R16)

Thus if H=N^alpha with fixed 1/2<alpha<1, the leading constant is positive and the relative error tends to zero. Floors change no power. In particular H=N^(1-2c) gives the SAME formal energy saving N^(-2c) needed by (R6) for every 0<c<1/4. At c=1/4 the elementary density error is as large as the main term, so (R16) does not by itself give an asymptotic there; the upper bound (R15) still holds. This is a genuine favorable calculation for a growing filter, not a reason to stop at the fixed-filter theorem.

Its return fails in a precisely priced place. On a common arc of length 1/(2qN), partition (N,2N] into J~N/H adjacent blocks. The endpoint observation of each filtered field recovers beta times its short weighted sum, and costs O(sqrt(N)) in L2. Applying (R15) separately gives a bound O(sqrt(H)N^(1/2-r)) for each such sum. Reassembling the dyadic weighted tail by the triangle inequality costs J, leaving

    |sum_(N<n<=2N)a(n)n^(-r)|
       << N^(3/2-r) H^(-1/2).                         (R17)

If H=N^(1-2c), this is N^(1+c-r): after Abel inversion it would give gamma=1+c, not the target 1-c. It is weaker than the elementary bound for the whole tail. Estimating the joined field directly with its global norm restores gamma=1, still without a gain. Cauchy-Schwarz over block indices alone gives the same reassembly factor and does not supply signed cancellation. The small norm in (R15) is therefore real but cannot be spent twice while recovering the original signal.

This result rules out only this specified adjacent-difference reconstruction using separate norm bounds. It does not rule out a coupled growing filter, a signed reconstruction, or a better observation. Such a survivor must state its complete original-signal reconstruction and control its coefficient/conditioning cost before claiming the energy gain. The first affordable decisive calculation for another filter is this reconstruction cost, rather than another finite Gram norm optimization.

statement:
## 4. A18: one full factor, all original masks, all divisors

The accepted input here is the fixed buffered Mertens estimate
M(t)<<_beta t^beta, .874872<beta<1. It is the accepted zero-free
baseline, not an inference from a Gaussian norm bound. Define

    f_d(n)=product_(p|n, p not dividing 3d)(-1).

For every positive integer d,n, including repeated primes,

    f(dn)=f(d)f_d(n),    f_d=h_d*mu.                         (R13)

The local h_d generating factors, with w=p^-s, are

    (1-w)^(-2),                        p|3d,
    (1-2w)/(1-w)^2 = 1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)w^j,   p not dividing 3d.

For fixed beta>1/2 the absolute coefficient sum satisfies

    B_d(beta):=sum_a |h_d(a)|a^-beta
       <= C_beta product_(p|d)(1-p^-beta)^(-2)
       <<_(beta,delta) d^delta,                            any delta>0. (R14)

The product over unexceptional primes converges because its first
nonconstant term is O(p^-2beta). The final bound absorbs finitely
many small primes in the constant and bounds each remaining factor
by p^delta. No reciprocal of the prime-two zero is taken.

Convolution with M gives

    sum_(n<=t)f_d(n) <<_beta B_d t^beta,    t>=1,

and this partial sum is zero below one. Abel summation over the whole
positive half-line, with vanishing Gaussian endpoint terms, yields

    F_d(y):=sum_n f_d(n)g(log(n/y))
       <<_(beta,tau) B_d y^beta,                            all y>0. (R15)

The controlling integral is
y^beta integral exp(beta v)|g'(v)|dv. Extending below t=1 only
enlarges this bound. Thus d>X, where y=x/d may be less than one,
is explicitly covered.

Now fix ANY original one-variable mask A_X(n) with 0<=A_X(n)<=1.
It may depend on X arbitrarily, have discontinuities, and fail to be
multiplicative. It remains frozen as a coefficient sequence while x
varies in the shell. Define its induced divisor field with the exact
argument

    G_(d,A)(y)=sum_n f_d(n)A_X(dn)g(log(n/y)).

Only the positive estimate |G_(d,A)(y)|<=C_tau y is used. Insert the
Möbius formula for coprimality before estimating either factor.
By R13, the two occurrences of f(d) multiply to one, giving exactly

    C_1(F,f A_X)=sum_(d>=1)mu(d) integral_X^(2X)
                     F_d(x/d)G_(d,A)(x/d) dx/x.            (R16)

Fubini is already justified before cancellation by the positive bound
sum_d [sum_n g(log(dn/x))]^2<=C x^2 sum_d d^-2. After applying
R14--R15, the absolute sum in R16 is at most

    C X^(1+beta) sum_d B_d/d^(1+beta) << X^(1+beta),         (R17)

choosing delta<beta. This proves A18 uniformly over the stated
original masks, with constants independent of their choice. Every
divisor, every valuation and the exact induced moving threshold
A_X(dn) remains in the restored scalar.

These quantifiers are necessary. The statement needs one unmasked
factor. It proves no cancellation estimate for two arbitrary masks,
for a general pair mask, or for a masked field by itself. Replacing
A_X(dn) by a mask defined at scale X/d changes the source. Similarly,
arbitrary independent d-dependent masks would no longer restore the
same original scalar, even if their individual absolute estimates
remained available. In the present rough application the correct
threshold is always the original z=kappa sqrt(X).

Taking A_X=1 and using R15 on BOTH full factors gives separately

    C_1(F,F)=sum_d mu(d) integral F_d(x/d)^2 dx/x
                  =O(X^(2beta)),                          (R18)

because sum_d B_d^2/d^(2beta) converges after choosing
2delta<2beta-1. Its only coprime diagonal K_X(1,1) is superpower
small. This is A19 at the accepted baseline only.

Apply R17 with A_X=A_R and pay the short-shift/window removal by
R11--R12. Exact F=T+R at the same pair mask gives

    C_1^H(F,R)=O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(T,R)=-C_1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C_1^H(R,T)=C_1^H(T,R).                                (R19)

For H=X/L^6 the error is o(X^2/L^4), since beta<1 is fixed.
This proves A5, including its opposite sign. The fourth ordered
piece is also fixed by the exact identity:

    C_1^H(F,F)=C_1^H(T,T)+C_1^H(T,R)+C_1^H(R,T)+C_1^H(R,R),
    C_1^H(T,T)=C_1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).            (R20)

For R20 use R18, its removed negligible diagonal, and the positive
short-shift payment. Since 2beta<1+beta, that full-factor error is
absorbed. The algebra uses no PSD property of the coprime scalar.
All four ordered pieces remain; replacing the two mixed pieces by
one, or taking their absolute values, would destroy the full return.

The primitive coprime form is exactly

    C_1^H(R,R)=2 sum_(h>H)sum_((a,h)=1)
       f(a(a+h))A_R(a)A_R(a+h)1_(a,a+h in I_X)K_X(a,a+h).

Here gcd(a,a+h)=1 justifies f(a)f(a+h)=f(a(a+h)). The ordered TR
scalar instead uses the bracket
A_T(a)A_R(a+h)+A_T(a+h)A_R(a), without an extra factor two.
This is the full actual g=1 obstruction, not a prime-dilation ray.

## Uniform independent audit28: fractional regularity pays the boundary

This audit concerns the specific B22 sorted-Fock source (A30.1), not an unspecified fractional space. The sharp cutoff evaluator has ordinary Hilbert norm

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||^2 = sum_(n in S,n<=N)n^(2sigma)
      ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/(2sigma+1).

The source norm is finite and independent of N. Generic Cauchy therefore gives exponent sigma+1/2>1; letting fixed sigma approach1/2 reaches the exponent1 boundary, not theta11. This existing B22 obstacle is retained rather than rediscovered as a new result.

Define the natural fractional logarithmic graph scale for fixed real s by

    ||u||_s^2=sum_n (1+log n)^(2s)|u_n|^2.

The actual v_sigma belongs to every such fixed space because2sigma>1. The exact evaluator norm is

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||_(s,dual)^2
      =sum_(n in S,n<=N) n^(2sigma)/(1+log n)^(2s)
      ~ kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/((2sigma+1)(log N)^(2s)).   (A28.1)

Partial summation against Q_q(x)=kappa_q x+O_q(sqrt x) proves this for every fixed real s; the error is lower by a positive power of N, up to logarithms. Fractional logarithmic order changes a logarithm, not the power needed. Similarly the infinite Dirichlet evaluator on this graph space still requires Re z>sigma+1/2 for convergence away from the boundary; logarithms can affect equality at that boundary but cannot move the strict power threshold below1.

There is a stronger exact diagonal-weight statement. For arbitrary positive weights w_(n,N), even chosen separately at each cutoff, whenever the indicated norms are finite,

    (sum_(n in S,n<=N)w_(n,N)|v_sigma(n)|^2)^(1/2)
    * (sum_(n in S,n<=N)n^(2sigma)/w_(n,N))^(1/2)
       >= sum_(n in S,n<=N)|v_sigma(n)|n^sigma
        = #S ~ kappa_q N.                              (A28.2)

A full infinite source norm is at least its truncated value, so it cannot evade this floor. Complex phases and ramified zeros are explicitly accounted for by S and |chi|=1 there. This is a source adaptation of G117's positive Cauchy price, not a lower bound on the actual signed evaluation. Non-diagonal correlations, new boundary conditions or a source-specific signed estimate are outside this obstruction.

The complete missing input can be stated as |Lambda_(N,sigma)(v_sigma)|=O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(gamma+epsilon)) at all N, equivalently the M bound. In the ordinary Hilbert normalization it requires a source/evaluator alignment of size N^(gamma-sigma-1/2+epsilon), which is a power rather than a logarithmic improvement. For sigma approaching1/2 and gamma<theta11, the needed decay exceeds c11. No Gaussian, Eisenstein, angular, growing-conductor or native H transfer is proved by this audit.

statement:
### 2.2 Complete Poisson expansion and every nonstationary frequency

Fix a high output scale N=2^j X and a row block I_M=[M,2M) intersect[1,D], with dyadic M. Put T=(N/X)^6>=1 and define

 beta_h=Q^(-1)sum_(r mod Q)b(r)exp(-2pi i hr/Q), h in Z.

It is periodic, |beta_h|<=||b||inf and beta_h=0 for h divisible by Q. Poisson on the smooth compactly supported positive-variable function, extended by zero, gives exactly

 sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)
   =(1/m)sum_(h in Z) beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
 I_r(x)=integral_0^infinity w(n/N)exp(-n/x^(3/2))
              exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.                       (4)

This includes both signs and every integer alias, not just one period. The h=0 term is exactly zero. For r>0 there is one positive critical point,

 n_r(x)=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
 Phi_r(n_r)=kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
 kappa_Q=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5), Phi_r''(n_r)=-30n_r^4/x^6.            (5)

Choose fixed positive c_Q,C_Q so that r in R_N=[c_Q T/N,C_Q T/N] includes every critical point that can meet[1,4]N for every x in[X,2X], and leaves a fixed derivative gap outside it. One explicit choice is c_Q=3Q/(128pi), C_Q=6Q*4^5/pi. This frequency range is chosen BEFORE x and BEFORE individual live labels. In rescaled variable n=Nt, the positive near phases form a compact smooth family with one nondegenerate stationary point in a fixed positive compact interval. The derivative of order2 at that point is bounded away from zero. All derivatives of the damped amplitude of any fixed needed order are O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), after absorbing fixed polynomial factors.

The uniform first stationary term is therefore

 I_r(x)=Z_r(x)exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4)
            +O_Q((N/T)exp(-cN/X^(3/2))), r in R_N,              (6)
 Z_r(x)=sqrt(pi/15) x^3 n_r(x)^(-2)
                     w(n_r(x)/N)exp(-n_r(x)/x^(3/2)).

The deliberately weak O(T^-1) remainder is sufficient. To justify its uniformity, localize near the unique critical point with one fixed-width smooth partition; the Morse change y=sgn(t-t0)sqrt(|Phi(t)-Phi(t0)|/T) has uniformly bounded inverse derivatives on this compact family. The Gaussian/Fresnel leading integral gives (6); subtract its value at zero and integrate the residual, or use one further Taylor term, to get O(T^-1). Away from that neighborhood two integrations by parts suffice. When t0 is outside the support of w the main coefficient is zero; its approach to the smooth support edge is covered by the same uniform estimate. No sharp edge is present. This is the standard one-dimensional nondegenerate stationary-phase calculation, with all varying parameters restricted as stated.

For completeness, let H_m=mT/N. The number of positive near aliases is O(1+H_m). If any such integer h exists, H_m>=c>0, so their combined remainder after the prefactor1/m is

 O((N/(mT))(1+H_m)exp(-cN/X^(3/2)))=O(exp(-cN/X^(3/2))).         (7)

Outside R_N, negative and small positive aliases with |h|=O(H_m) have derivative of size T after n-scaling. Two integrations by parts give O((N/m)T^-2) per alias, with damping. There are O(H_m) such nonzero integers when present, hence total O(T^-1). For |h|>C H_m the derivative has size |h|N/m; two integrations by parts give O((m/N)h^-2). Its entire two-sided tail is O(T^-1) if H_m>=c, and O(m/N) if H_m<c. Since m<=X^alpha0 and N>=X, all these costs are O(1), with damping retained. Enlarging fixed constants covers intermediate finitely sized ranges. Thus the whole transformed row equals the stationary bank in (6) plus a uniform damped O(1) error. After summing the block, the error is O(AM exp(-cN/X^(3/2))). There is no unpaid frequency tail or endpoint.

statement:
# [research revision]: short rational cofactors and separated products

**Status: proved relative to the stated rational Mertens premise; independently reviewed by the triple-source lane.** SP1–SP34 retain all original signs, masks and frozen endpoints. The positive-coefficient countermodel tests only the limitations of the stated generic prefix bounds. OPEN-MG and a larger zero-free constant remain unproved.

## 1. Exact imported dependencies and frozen form

The imported arithmetic premise is

\[
M(U)=\sum_{n\le U}\mu(n)\ll_\delta U^{b_0+\delta},\qquad
b_0=.874886647039964131\ldots .
\tag{SP1}
\]

This is [MG1](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#1-imported-inputs-and-the-actual-finite-form).
Consequently one may fix any \(b\in(b_0,1)\) and use
\(M(U)\ll_b U^b\). The numerical choice is
\(b=8749/10000=.8749\), strictly above \(b_0\).

Keep exactly [MG2--MG8](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#1-imported-inputs-and-the-actual-finite-form):

\[
\begin{gathered}
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil,\\
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\qquad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))'=(1-u+u^{-1})e^{-u-u^{-1}},\\
\Xi(q;x)=\rho(q/T_l)\chi(q/T_u)
               \sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell q/x),\qquad X\le x\le2X.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SP2}
\]

The fixed smooth cutoffs obey \(0\le\rho,\chi\le1\),
\(\rho=0\) on \((0,1]\), \(\rho=1\) on \([2,\infty)\),
\(\chi=1\) on \((0,1]\), and \(\chi=0\) on \([2,\infty)\).
Every arithmetic parameter is frozen as \(x\) varies. The exact
approximation of the original detector, with arbitrary power errors and
each fixed Euler derivative, is imported from
[T09.2](../[research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#frozen-dyad-balanced-finite-form).
No cutoff or third-factor endpoint in that theorem is changed here.

In particular,

\[
\Xi(q;x)=0\quad\hbox{unless }T_l<q<2T_u,
\qquad
\sup_{q,x}|(q\partial_q)^r\Xi(q;x)|\ll_r L^6.
\tag{SP3}
\]

The latter bound follows by bounding the \(J\) individual summands and
the fixed cutoff derivatives; no additional Poisson estimate is needed.
Every nonzero individual factor lies in

\[
Y<d_i<U_{\max}:=2T_u/Y\ll\sqrt X L^4.
\tag{SP4}
\]

There are \(O(1+\log L)\) dyadic intervals in this range. All mixed Euler
derivatives using each variable at most once of
\(\Xi(de;x)\overline{\Xi(fh;x)}\) are \(O(L^{12})\).

Put \((d_1,d_2,d_3,d_4)=(d,e,f,h)\), and retain the original mask

\[
\mathfrak m=1_{(d,e)<H}1_{(f,h)<H}
\prod_{ij\in\{13,14,23,24\}}1_{(d_i,d_j)<R},\qquad
H=X^{1/1400},\quad R=X^{1/700}.
\tag{SP5}
\]

For an additional tuple mask \(\mathfrak n\), define

\[
Q[\mathfrak n]=\int_X^{2X}
\sum_{d,e,f,h>Y}\mu(d)\mu(e)\mu(f)\mu(h)
\mathfrak m\mathfrak n\,
\Xi(de;x)\overline{\Xi(fh;x)}\,\frac{dx}{x}.
\tag{SP6}
\]

Thus \(Q[1]=Q_{\rm good}\) of
[MG35--MG36 and OPEN-MG](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#7-exact-target-reduction-and-the-remaining-arithmetic-estimate).
The target remains \(|Q[1]|\ll_\epsilon X^{1.74898+\epsilon}\).
Earlier internal-gcd removal uses the \(L^2\) triangle inequality,
not an additive energy error. The signed sector estimates below are
different statements, proved directly for their quartic forms.

## 2. Uniform divisor masks in one and two Möbius sums

Let \(D\) be squarefree, let \(F\) be any function on its divisors with
\(|F|\le1\), and let \(c\ge1\). Write
\(A_c=(c,D)\), \(D_c=D/A_c\). Since \((D_c,c)=1\),
partitioning by \(r=(u,D_c)\) gives the exact identity

\[
\sum_{\substack{u\le U\\(u,c)=1}}\mu(u)F((cu,D))
=\sum_{r\mid D_c}\mu(r)F(A_cr)\,M_{cD_c}(U/r),
\quad
M_v(T)=\sum_{\substack{n\le T\\(n,v)=1}}\mu(n).
\tag{SP7}
\]

Indeed, for a nonzero Möbius term, writing \(u=rv\) imposes
\((v,cD_c)=1\), and \((cu,D)=A_cr\). Natural squarefree zeros supply
the required coprimality with \(r\).

The uniform coprime estimate in
[MG9--MG10](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#2-uniform-coprime-mertens-sums-and-weighted-rectangles)
is
\(M_v(T)\ll_{b,\eta}T^b v^\eta\).
The additional divisor factor satisfies
\(\sum_{r\mid D_c}r^{-b}=\prod_{p\mid D_c}(1+p^{-b})\ll_\eta D_c^\eta\).
Apportioning the arbitrary small losses proves, for every \(\eta>0\),

\[
\left|\sum_{\substack{u\le U\\(u,c)=1}}
\mu(u)F((cu,D))\right|
\ll_{b,\eta}U^b(cD)^\eta.
\tag{SP8}
\]

Subtraction includes arbitrary sharp interval endpoints.

**Two-variable lemma.** Let \(I\subset[E,2E]\),
\(I'\subset[V,2V]\) be intervals, let \(F,G\) be bounded by one on
the divisors of a squarefree \(D\), and let \(|a_g|\le1\). For a smooth
weight \(W\), set

\[
\mathcal S(W)=\max_{i,j\in\{0,1\}}\sup
|(e\partial_e)^i(h\partial_h)^jW(e,h)|.
\]

Then

\[
\left|\sum_{\substack{e\in I\\h\in I'}}
\mu(e)\mu(h)F((e,D))G((h,D))a_{(e,h)}W(e,h)\right|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}\mathcal S(W)D^\epsilon(EV)^b.
\tag{SP9}
\]

**Proof.** First freeze the original gcd \(g=(e,h)\). Nonzero terms
have squarefree \(g\). Expand the coprimality of the two remaining
factors by an auxiliary divisor \(q\). With \(c=gq\), the exact sum is

\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{g\ge1}\mu(g)^2a_g
\sum_{\substack{q\ge1\\(q,g)=1}}\mu(q)
\sum_{\substack{cu\in I,\ cv\in I'\\(uv,c)=1}}
&\mu(u)\mu(v)F((cu,D))G((cv,D))\\
&\hspace{6mm}\cdot W(cu,cv).
\end{split}
\tag{SP10}
\]

There is no residual condition \((u,v)=1\). The coefficient \(a_g\)
is attached to the original exact gcd; it must not be recomputed from
the variables in an auxiliary summand. The other masks depend on the
actual individual values \(cu,cv\), so remain as displayed.

Apply (SP8) in each variable, followed by two-dimensional Abel summation
on \(I/c\) and \(I'/c\). This gives

\[
\ll\mathcal S(W)(EV)^bD^{2\eta}c^{-2b+2\eta}.
\tag{SP11}
\]

The scaled Euler seminorm does not change. All faces and corners are
included by interval partial sums; a nonempty scaled interval has upper
endpoint at least one. Choose \(\eta>0\) with \(2b-2\eta>1\) and
\(2\eta\le\epsilon\). The two sums in \(g,q\) converge absolutely,
which proves (SP9). \(\square\)

## 3. Short rational cofactor relations are affordable

For \(ij\in\{13,14,23,24\}\), define

\[
A_{ij}(K)=\{\exists\ 1\le r,s\le J:
 |r d_i-s d_j|\le K\},\qquad
A(K)=\bigcup_{ij}A_{ij}(K).
\tag{SP12}
\]

**Proposition.** Uniformly for \(0\le K\le Y/2\),

\[
|Q[1_{A(K)}]|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}
X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(K+1)
+X^{1+\epsilon}(K+1)^2.
\tag{SP13}
\]

The proof is uniform in the two original gcd thresholds. In particular,
it also holds on the fully pairwise-coprime stratum by setting both
thresholds to \(2\).

**Proof for one edge.** Freeze squarefree \(d,f\), retaining
\((d,f)<R\). Put \(D=\operatorname{rad}(df)\) and, for \(r\mid D\),

\[
F(r)=1_{(r,d)<H}1_{(r,f)<R},\qquad
G(r)=1_{(r,f)<H}1_{(r,d)<R},\qquad a_g=1_{g<R}.
\tag{SP14}
\]

These encode exactly the five remaining original gcd restrictions.
Apply (SP9) with
\(W(e,h)=\Xi(de;x)\overline{\Xi(fh;x)}\). On every nonempty dyadic
rectangle, the support gives \(EV\ll X^2L^4/(df)\), and
\(\mathcal S(W)\ll L^{12}\). As \(D\ll XL^8\), the divisor-mask
loss is absorbed into \(X^\epsilon\). Summing the
\(O((1+\log L)^2)\) rectangles yields

\[
\left|\sum_{e,h}\text{the complete remaining summand}\right|
\ll_{b,\epsilon}X^{2b+\epsilon}(df)^{-b},
\tag{SP15}
\]

uniformly in \(d,f,x\), with the sharp endpoints kept.

If \(|rd-sf|\le K\), \(1\le r,s\le J\), and \(K\le Y/2\), then
\(sf\ge rd/2\), hence \(f\ge d/(2J)\). For fixed \(d,r,s\), there
are at most \(2K+1\) possible integers \(f\). Taking absolute values
only after the two-variable cancellation therefore gives

\[
\begin{split}
\sum_{\substack{d,f>Y\\A_{13}(K)}}(df)^{-b}
&\ll J^{2+b}(K+1)\sum_{d>Y}d^{-2b}\\
&\ll_b J^{2+b}(K+1)Y^{1-2b}.
\end{split}
\tag{SP16}
\]

Combining (SP15)--(SP16), and integrating over an interval of
\(dx/x\)-length \(\log2\), proves

\[
|Q[1_{A_{13}(K)}]|
\ll X^{b+1/2+\epsilon}(K+1).
\tag{SP17}
\]

The same argument applies to each cross edge.

**Signed union.** Let \(k\) count the four events holding at a tuple.
The pointwise identity has error bounded by

\[
\left|1_{\{k\ge1\}}-k\right|\le {k\choose2}.
\tag{SP18}
\]

Any two distinct cross edges form a two-edge forest on four vertices.
For fixed multipliers, choose the two root variables freely; each other
variable then lies in an interval of length at most \(2K\). Taking the
positive union bound over at most \(J^4\) multiplier choices shows that
each pairwise intersection contains at most

\[
O(J^4U_{\max}^2(K+1)^2)
=O(XL^{32}(K+1)^2)
\tag{SP19}
\]

tuples. Bound the coefficients by one and the weight by \(O(L^{12})\)
only for this overlap error. Equations (SP17)--(SP19) prove (SP13).
No positivity of a signed localized covariance is asserted. \(\square\)

## 4. Nearby expanded products, with arbitrary further masks

Expand the two original finite sums in \(\Xi(de;x)\) and
\(\Xi(fh;x)\). For \(0\le P\le X\), the total absolute contribution
of

\[
|\ell de-mfh|\le P,\qquad 1\le\ell,m\le J,
\tag{SP20}
\]

is

\[
\ll_\epsilon X^{1+\epsilon}(P+1).
\tag{SP21}
\]

The bound holds after any additional bounded tuple mask, in particular
after excluding \(A(K)\).

**Proof.** Put \(n=\ell de\), \(n'=mfh\). Support gives
\(n,n'\le Z=2JT_u\ll XL^8\). The numbers of representations are
at most \(d_3(n)\) and \(d_3(n')\). Each individual profile factor
is bounded and the cutoffs have modulus at most one. Thus the absolute
contribution, including integration, is bounded by a constant times

\[
\sum_{\substack{n,n'\le Z\\|n-n'|\le P}}d_3(n)d_3(n')
\ll(P+1)\sum_{n\le Z+P}d_3(n)^2
\ll(P+1)(Z+P)\log^8(2Z+2P).
\tag{SP22}
\]

The first inequality is Cauchy--Schwarz for each difference. The second
uses \(d_3(n)^2\le d_9(n)\) and the elementary mean bound for \(d_9\),
the precise positive majorant already proved in
[AD3](../review-cycle-20.md#exact-coalescence-of-all-product-coincidences).
This proves (SP21) without extending either short third-factor range.
\(\square\)

**Exact coincidences are already absent.** For nonzero Möbius terms the
four factors are squarefree, and prime by prime

\[
(de,fh)\le(d,f)(d,h)(e,f)(e,h)<R^4.
\tag{SP23}
\]

Indeed, if a prime occurs \(a\) times in \((d,e)\) and \(b\) times
in \((f,h)\), with \(a,b\in\{0,1,2\}\), its exponent on the left
is \(\min(a,b)\le ab\), the exponent on the right. If
\(\ell de=mfh\), put \(g=(de,fh)\). The relatively prime factors
\(de/g\), \(fh/g\) force \(de/g\mid m\), so

\[
g\ge de/J>T_l/J\gg X/L^{10}.
\tag{SP24}
\]

This contradicts \(g<R^4=X^{1/175}\) for sufficiently large \(X\).
Thus (SP21) adds a sector of nonzero product differences to the existing
reduction; its center is already empty under the cross-gcd cuts.

## 5. Exact exponents and the residual signed form

Take

\[
b=\frac{8749}{10000},\qquad
K=X^{187/500}=X^{.374},\qquad
P=X^{7489/10000}=X^{.7489}.
\tag{SP25}
\]

These choices satisfy \(K\le Y/2\) for large \(X\). The single-edge
and nearby-product costs both have exponent

\[
b+\frac12+.374=1+.7489
=\frac{17489}{10000}=1.7489,
\qquad
1.74898-1.7489=\frac1{12500}.
\tag{SP26}
\]

The overlap cost has exponent \(1+2(.374)=1.748\), with margin
\(49/50000\). All arbitrary small losses can be chosen below the
displayed fixed margins. For general \(K=X^\kappa\), a fixed margin
is available when

\[
\kappa<\min\{1.24898-b,\ .37449\}.
\tag{SP27}
\]

Optimizing over the accepted \(b>b_0\) therefore permits every
\(\kappa<.374093352960035869\ldots\). No improvement of the accepted
Mertens exponent is used in this optimization.

Define \(Q_{\rm far}\) by retaining all original conditions in the
expanded quartic form and additionally imposing

\[
|rd_i-sd_j|>X^{.374}
\quad(ij\in\{13,14,23,24\},\ 1\le r,s\le J),
\qquad
|\ell de-mfh|>X^{.7489}.
\tag{SP28}
\]

First remove \(A(K)\) by (SP13). Then apply (SP21) to the nearby
product band on its complement. This is the signed identity with
controlled remainder

\[
Q_{\rm good}=Q_{\rm far}
+O_\epsilon(X^{1.7489+\epsilon}).
\tag{SP29}
\]

Both removed sectors are directly bounded signed quartic forms. This
does not change the distinction between squared-energy subtraction and
the \(L^2\) triangle step in MG34. The previous gcd costs retain their
already established exponent \(4897/2800\); the present bounds do not
reprove or weaken them.

## 6. A precise limit of the profile-moment argument

The following countermodel concerns a proposed inference from bounded
one-variable sums, squarefree support, and the actual derivative profile.
It is not a counterexample for the Möbius function.

Let

\[
D_j=2^{2^j},\qquad
a(n)=\mu(n)^2n^{b-1}
1_{\{n\in\bigcup_j[2D_j,\frac72D_j]\}}.
\tag{SP30}
\]

Then \(|a(n)|\le1\), the support is squarefree, and for every modulus
and every bounded divisor mask,

\[
\left|\sum_{n\le U}a(n)(\text{mask})\right|
\le\sum_{n\le U}n^{b-1}\ll_b U^b.
\tag{SP31}
\]

These bounds are uniform even without modulus losses. At
\(X_j=D_j^2\), the frozen individual range (SP4) contains nonzero
coefficients from only the \(j\)-th block, for all large \(j\): the
previous block ends at \((7/2)\sqrt{D_j}\ll Y_j\), while the next
starts at \(2D_j^2\gg U_{\max,j}\).

All contributing individual factors are therefore at least \(2D_j\),
so \(de/x,fh/x\ge2\). Since \(\phi(u)<0\) for
\(u>(1+\sqrt5)/2\), every summand in each finite profile is negative.
Every expanded quartic summand with coefficients \(a\) is nonnegative,
including after the masks (SP5), (SP28).

Restrict to squarefree, pairwise-coprime tuples in

\[
d,e\in[2D_j,\tfrac52D_j],\qquad
f,h\in[3D_j,\tfrac72D_j].
\tag{SP32}
\]

There are \(\gg D_j^4\) such tuples. Here is an elementary justification
of that density assertion. At a prime \(p\), the permitted residues
modulo \(p^2\) have relative density
\((1-p^{-1})^4(1+4p^{-1})\): either no coordinate is divisible by
\(p\), or exactly one is divisible by \(p\) but not by \(p^2\).
The product over primes is positive because each factor is positive and
equals \(1+O(p^{-2})\). Finite CRT counting gives the finite-prime
density in the four fixed proportional intervals. After cutting at
\(p>B\), square-divisibility failures have total
\(O(D_j^4/B+D_j^{7/2})\), while shared-prime failures have total
\(O(D_j^4/B+D_j^3\log D_j)\). First choose \(B\) large, then
\(j\) large. A positive proportion survives.

The union of the rational near-cofactor strips excludes at most

\[
O(J^2D_j^3(K+1))=o(D_j^4)
\tag{SP33}
\]

of these tuples, by fixing one factor on an edge and then the other two
unconstrained factors. Thus \(\gg D_j^4\) tuples still satisfy the
first part of (SP28). For \(\ell=m=1\), their products satisfy
\(fh-de\ge(11/4)X_j>P\). All original gcd cuts hold, since the
tuples are pairwise coprime.

On these boxes the cutoffs are one for large \(j\), and the arguments
of the two \(\ell=m=1\) profile factors lie in the compact interval
\([2,49/4]\). Their absolute values are bounded below by a positive
constant. Each coefficient product is
\(\gg_bD_j^{4b-4}\). Positivity of all the other model summands
therefore gives

\[
Q_{{\rm far},a}(X_j)\gg_b D_j^{4b}=X_j^{2b}.
\tag{SP34}
\]

Thus a universal saving over \(X^{2b}\) cannot follow solely from
(SP31), squarefree support, the retained gcd restrictions, and the
actual profile's zero moment. The sequence (SP30) is not Möbius and
does not preserve every Möbius convolution identity; that is exactly
the scope limitation of the countermodel.

## 7. Open remainder and review gate

The new paid sectors satisfy the target with the exact margins in
(SP26). The fully pairwise-coprime portion of \(Q_{\rm far}\) survives.
The still-missing estimate is cancellation using the actual four
Möbius signs across the far rational-cofactor and far-product tuples;
the generic one-variable bounds and profile moment do not supply it.

No finite calculation is promoted to an infinite estimate, and no new
uniform height statement or reciprocal-zeta bound is claimed. The
original T09 detector and all its fixed-profile and height qualifications
remain imported unchanged. Independent mathematical review accepted
SP1–SP34 with the rational Mertens input and the scopes recorded above.

statement:
### R39-F. f3 keeps its actual Euler factors and full signed return

The source f3 is multiplicative with f3(p^k)=-1 for every k>=1
and p!=3, and f3(3^k)=1. Thus its local Dirichlet factors are
(1-2z)/(1-z) for p!=3 and (1-z)^(-1) at 3. Dividing by the local
factor of 1/zeta gives exactly

    D3(s)=B(s)/zeta(s), B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^(-2)(1-3^-s)^(-2)
             product_(p>=5) (1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.        (R39.10)

For p>=5 the linear term cancels. On Re s>=b>1/2, both local
logarithmic series have summable O_b(p^-2b) tails; 2*5^-b<1
excludes every numerator zero. H and its inverse are consequently
analytic, bounded and nonzero on that half-plane. The separate
factors at 2 and 3 are essential. B has its retained zeros on
Re s=1 and no zeros in 1/2<Re s<1.

For the complete F3(z)=sum_n f3(n)g_tau(log n-z), the actual Mellin
identity is exp(tau*s^2/2)B(s)/zeta(s). Holomorphy of this transform
above h excludes zeta zeros in h<Re s<1. The known zero-free right
edge, already available in the project, completes the conclusion;
one must not pretend B is nonvanishing on that edge. Replenishment
uses the independently established reciprocal bound for zeta and
the bounded actual B. R39-A--D therefore prove the f3 criterion for
every fixed gamma>1/2 and kappa<1/2.

This criterion is equivalent, with epsilon buffers, to the full
pointwise Gaussian exponent. The reverse direction simply takes
E_j to be the whole interval. It is also equivalent to the complete
Gaussian square-moment target in the stated range: pointwise bounds
give that moment; conversely, dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz gives holomorphy
of the Mellin transform, then zero exclusion and R39.7 give the
pointwise bound again. Thus equivalence is proved through the
actual meromorphic multiplier, not a generic L2-to-supremum claim.

Current-proof G28 separately gives A=k*f3, f3=h*A, with the
weighted absolute convolution norms finite for each sigma>1/2.
Their fixed-field identities transfer the complete moment; G27
and G29--31 price the moving cutoffs only in their stated order.
The original A(1),A(2),A(4)=1,-3,2 remain. The f3 moment expands
with its true O(X) diagonal and every signed ordered off-diagonal
term. No absolute value may be moved inside that scalar, no negative
term deleted, and no arbitrary submask inherits the valley theorem.

The resulting **OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa)** is an arithmetic
estimate on a measurable subset of **every** fixed log interval,
for the complete f3 sum and gamma<.874867, kappa<1/2. It is not
established by the accepted leading signed-band asymptotics,
independent-prime models, finite sampling, or density-one good
intervals. The f3 corollary supplies zeta's return; ordinary chi and
the Hecke family have their own separate full-field hypotheses.
