# [research revision]: paid detector composition and actual prime matching

**Accept G73–G77 below at their stated scopes. The source-relative written
endpoint remains c6=125139/1000000; no new arithmetic saving is proved.**
The [author](wild46/report.md) and [independent critic](wild46-review/report.md)
retain all 30 seeds, six author tests and two independent audit developments.
The critic's matching and contour results are additions to the author's
three developments, not generator claims. Root read both complete arguments.

Throughout, fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and tau>0.
Let g(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)). F is the complete Gaussian
field of f3(n)chi(n), where f3 counts distinct primes other than 3 and
**includes 2**. B uses b(n)=(-1)^(number of distinct primes >=5 dividing n),
and U uses mu(n)chi(n). Zero extension on nonunits is retained. Shell norms
are L2(dx/x) on [X,2X]; global sigma norms are sup_(x>0) x^(-sigma)|F(x)|.
All character-dependent constants and inherited growth bounds stay fixed
before X tends to infinity. Changing finite sources return to a fixed
complete field before any Mellin continuation.

## G73. Exact detector composition with both complements paid

For z=chi(p)p^(-s), the Dirichlet series of b(n)chi(n) is H(s)/L(s,chi):

    H_2=H_3=(1-z)^(-2),   H_p=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2 (p>=5),
    K=H^(-1), K_2=K_3=(1-z)^2, K_p=1+z^2/(1-2z).

Ramified local factors are 1. The full products H,K and their absolute
coefficient sums converge for Re(s)>1/2. For p>=5 and j>=2,
h(p^j)=-(j-1), k(p^j)=2^(j-2); both first-prime coefficients vanish.
Thus U=T_k B and B=T_h U are bounded global sigma-norm transfers.
The missing prime-2 correction is

    F(x)=B(x)-2 chi(2) B(x/2).

If chi(2) is nonzero, the future inverse is

    B(x)=-sum_(j>=1) (2 chi(2))^(-j) F(2^j x).

Its boundary term vanishes by the accepted buffered growth exponent
beta in (.874861,1), not by assuming a new bound at the proposed gamma.
For a fixed character, buffered zero-free holomorphy plus standard
polynomial L-growth and Borel–Caratheodory give polynomial reciprocal
growth on that beta line; Gaussian decay then permits the full contour
shift. When chi(2)=0, F=B directly. This is the G28/G70/RCC3 inverse
mechanism with an explicit source correction, not a new independent route.

For R=floor(X^b0), J=ceil(a log_2 X), define the complete-field combination

    Q_X(x)=-sum_(r<=R) k(r)chi(r)
                   sum_(1<=j<=J)(2 chi(2))^(-j) F(2^j x/r).

For chi(2)=0 use sum_(r<=R)k(r)chi(r)F(x/r). Then U-Q_X=E2+EK with
shell exponents beta-a(1-beta) and beta-b0(beta-sigma0), sigma0<beta.
The dyadic floor and fixed constants are paid; at sigma0=3/4,
K_sigma0<70 and H_sigma0<264. Squared norms retain the cross error
2||Q_X||||U-Q_X||+||U-Q_X||^2, rather than deleting either complement.

| Conditional target gamma | beta | a,b0 | E2 exponent | EK exponent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| .87486 (c=.12514) | .874862 | 1/50000,1/50000 | .87485949724 | .87485950276 |
| 5/6 (c=1/6) | .874862 | 1/3,1/3 | 312431/375000 | 624931/750000 |
| 3/4 (c=1/4) | .874862 | 1,101/100 | 187431/250000 | 37437569/50000000 |

At the first target the strict minimum margin is 12431/25000000000.
The support of k is powerful away from 2,3, giving O(sqrt R) nonzero
r's and O(X^.00001 log X) shifted complete fields at that target. This
is a representation count, not an evaluation algorithm or cancellation.
For 1/2<gamma<1, the every-epsilon bounds for Q_X and fixed U are
equivalent. The proposed signed Q_X estimate remains OPEN. Its Mellin
return treats all heights, all fixed ordinary characters and the
principal pole as the removable zero of 1/L.

## G74. A spectral gap can leave the entire arithmetic sign harmonic

For each distinct p|n,p!=3, take C0 with one even basis vector and C1
with two odd vectors, both mapped to the even vector. Its Laplacian has
eigenvalues 2,2,0, one odd harmonic state and supertrace -1. Tensoring
over distinct primes gives one harmonic state of parity omega_(p!=3)(n),
uniform positive gap 2 and a complement homotopy of norm <=1/sqrt(2).
Repeated powers add no cube; p=3 contributes a trivial factor.

With the actual chi(n)g(log(n/x)) weights, complete trace convergence
follows from 3^omega(n/3^v3(n))<=n^2. For every t>=0,

    F=Tr(Gamma W exp(-t Delta))=Tr(Gamma W P_harmonic).

The inverse/homotopy only acts on I-P, so the gap gives no bound on F.
Its absolute harmonic price is (phi(q)/q) exp(tau/2)x+O_(q,tau)(1),
an upper-certificate obstruction, not a lower bound on the signed field.
Different-integer matching requires a separate weighted readout estimate.

The direct complete Gaussian scalar is also not positive-real on its
proposed right half-plane: at s=4+it, Re D(s)>=2/3 for each of F,B,U,
since the coefficient of 1 is 1 and the remaining absolute mass is <=1/3.
At t=pi/(4 tau), exp(tau s^2/2) has negative real phase, so the real part
of the Mellin observable is strictly negative. This excludes this literal
scalar realization only; a different/vector readout must prove its return.

## G75. The native H operator must retain phases and the full Gram sum

For a frozen finite native packet, keep complete h(g,g'), rooted marks,
original masks/projectors, natural zeros, independent heights, endpoints
and the literal phases, including the two cubic h factors, s powers
2 and 4, b_pi conjugate(b_pi') and the CRT phase. Group Fourier inversion
has its 1/Q normalization; unitarity alone is no saving. With the actual
scalar convention sum v_P K_PP' conjugate(w_P'), H=w* K^T v.
Conjugating an input without transporting the kernel would change H.

For T=K^T, a sufficient bound is

    ||T||^2 <= max_j [sum_i |T_ij|^2
                     +sum_(k!=j)|sum_i conjugate(T_ij)T_ik|].

The inner signed sum must include all cores, masks and heights. The raw
target is G K0 [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, with original
K0; apply the outside N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once afterward. A norm deficit
Z^delta needs a square-level gain Z^(-2delta) in this strategy. No such
native bound or complementary-branch estimate is supplied here.
Gauge changes preserve the full operator norm. A real zonotope does not
contain arbitrary complex phases; independent discs lose cancellation.
The complex rank-one bilinear convex relaxation is the nuclear-norm
ball, whose dual is spectral norm, subject to the actual input restrictions.

## G76. Exact first-eligible-prime matching, with a uniform critical bill

Choose any finite ordered list P=(p1,...,pr) of distinct primes excluding
3 and primes dividing q; 2 remains eligible. Put Q=product P. At the
first j with v_pj(n)<=1, toggle that valuation between 0 and 1. Earlier
pi^2 still divide both endpoints, so this is a disjoint involution. Its
unmatched set is exactly Q^2|n. Define the complete lower-endpoint field

    A_j(x)=sum_(p_j not dividing m, p_i^2|m for i<j)
                 f3(m)chi(m)g(log(m/x)).

The exact decomposition is

    F(x)=S_P(x)+C_P(x),
    S_P(x)=sum_j [A_j(x)-chi(p_j)A_j(x/p_j)],
    C_P(x)=sum_(Q^2|n) f3(n)chi(n)g(log(n/x)).

Every power and natural zero is present. On writing n=Q^2 m, the
coefficient equals (-1)^r chi(Q^2) times the character-weighted sign
which ignores P, and therefore has modulus <=1. Uniformly for every y>0,

    sum_(k>=1)g(log(k/y)) <= C_tau y,
    C_tau=max(exp(tau/2)+2g(0), 2g(0)exp(2tau)).

For y>=1 use bounded variation; for y<=1 complete the square and sum
k^(-2)<=2. Consequently

    ||C_P||_[X,2X] <= 2 C_tau sqrt(log 2) X/Q^2.

For moving P_X and Q_X^2>=X^(1-gamma+eta), eta>0, a complete signed
S_(P_X) bound with every-epsilon exponent gamma is equivalent to the
same fixed-F bound, in both directions. For gamma=.87486,5/6,3/4 the
required Q exponent is respectively .06257,1/12,1/8 plus eta/2.
All cross terms stay inside ||S_P||. Making Q huge alone does not simplify
this arithmetic target. No Mellin transform is taken of a moving source.

**The absolute edge certificate costs order X, uniformly in moving P.**
For a fixed first prime p, c=chi(p),

    J_p(c)=integral exp(v)|g(v)-c g(v+log p)|dv
            >= exp(tau/2)|1-c/p| >= exp(tau/2)(1-1/p).

For fixed P the jth edge price has leading constant
(phi(q)/q) Q_<j^(-2)(1-1/p_j)J_pj(chi(p_j))x.
To cover a changing first prime, let Z_q(y) be the positive coprime
Gaussian sum and B_p(y)=Z_q(y)-Z_q(y/p). The first edge price is at least
B_p(x)-B_p(x/p)>=Z_q(x)-2 C_tau x/p. For all sufficiently large p this
is uniformly a positive multiple of x; finitely many smaller p have a
positive minimum from the fixed-prime formula. Thus every nonempty
moving list has positive certificate cost Omega_(q,tau)(X). This is
not a lower bound on F or S_P. The signed cancellation is precisely
the remaining input. Derivative rewriting retains (1-c)g and the full
integral of g'; it cannot erase chi(p) or its price.

This develops U-PRIME-CHAIN/U-TRANSPORT and W43/W44 ancestry into an
all-power canonical matching with a uniform moving residual estimate.
It does not claim the basic prime-toggle idea as new.

## G77. Full contour gluing includes the horizontal and residue terms

For fixed U, M(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi). Start at b>1, choose a in
(1/2,1) avoiding zero real parts and a finite height T avoiding boundary
zeros. No zero-free interior is assumed. The rectangle identity is

    U=V_(a,T)+H_top-minus-bottom+Z_residues+R_(b,T).

A zero rho of multiplicity m contributes x^rho times a polynomial in
log x of degree m-1 with nonzero leading coefficient
m exp(tau rho^2/2)/L^(m)(rho). The principal pole at 1 instead gives a
zero of 1/L. The F numerator has no zeros in this open strip.
The complete right-tail shell norm is

    ||R_(b,T)|| <= C X^b T^(-1) exp(-tau T^2/2).

Choose a boundary-admissible T_X within one unit above
sqrt(2(b-gamma+delta)log X/tau). The error is
O(X^(gamma-delta)/sqrt(log X)); the truncated ORIGINAL b-line band
is thus exponent-equivalent to U. Moving to a requires the full prices

    C X^a integral_(-T)^T exp(-tau t^2/2)|1/L(a+it)|dt,
    C X^b exp(-tau T^2/2) integral_a^b
                      (|1/L(sigma+iT)|+|1/L(sigma-iT)|)d sigma,

and all residues. No proximity-to-zero bound is assumed away.
A fixed finite nonempty residue packet whose maximal real part is
sigma*>gamma has shell norm >=c X^sigma* (log X)^d for all large X,
by positive definiteness of the fixed distinct-frequency Gram matrix.
This is conditional on such zeros existing. Its constant is not uniform
in growing T, zero count or separation, and it supplies no lower bound
for the growing packet. Complete contour gluing remains an open
arithmetic estimate, not automatic flux cancellation.

## Retention, admission and next decisive work

G76 is the substantive new source decomposition and uniform obstruction;
G77 pays the exact contour alternative. G73 prices a composition of valid
recent and older components, permitting mixed detector attacks without
pretending that changing representation improves an exponent. G74/G75
retire precise spectral-gap and phase-convention shortcuts.

The duplicate finite Euler inverse failure is retained: an absolute rough
inverse diverges at sigma<=1, while finite polynomial pole erasure leaves
the full reciprocal pole in the omitted residual. Reopen only with a
controlled complete inverse or a changed detector with a proved return.

Author reservations03/16/28, rare11/21 and wildcard15 are immutable.
The implementation used <=.10/<=.01 instead of strict thresholds, but
there are no endpoint ties and the actual eligible pools coincide. No
binary partition was used. Independent protected20 and uniform29 were
chosen from outcome-free frozen orders; 22 cards remain untested. Full
29-family/109-child history remains.

Twenty-two evidence files retain original bytes. The unchanged reviewer
manifest also names a host-local claim receipt: that receipt remains

No sentinel, claim or tracker database is in this research export.
The author is mathematical STOP with its old claim retained after binding
drift; the independent reviewer stopped and released its own new claim.

The decisive targets are the signed moving S_P or Q_X estimate, an actual
different-integer weighted cancellation theorem, or the full native H
Gram plus complementary branches. The growing-order actual-source pass
continues separately. The proof packet is complete as a delivery task;

# [research revision]: chaining, simultaneous detection, and recombination in one proof

Yes: the two approaches can be used in the same proof, including repeated
alternation. The [independent construction](hybrid-detector-review/report.md)
gives exact operators and their costs. It also gives a way to harvest bounds
proved in different representations for different fixed pieces of one source.
The remaining task is to prove a new arithmetic estimate in one of those
representations. This construction alone changes no accepted c.

Attribution: choosing the easier detector for different results or pieces,
transferring them and merging them was the user's FIRST proposal. H17 below
formalizes that original mix-and-match idea. The later question adds
interleaving this approach with simultaneous detection. The controller's
initial whole-detector interpretation was narrower than the user's request;
the harvesting idea is not a later controller-originated suggestion.

This extends the [consultation integration](detector-and-consultation-integration.md).
The current written endpoint remains c5=.125136 from the separate affine
argument, relative to pinned PR9/Gao and its original fixed-family scope;
full new-endpoint formalization and independent kernel replay remain pending.

## 1. Keep the simultaneous family while changing the smoother

Let H=L2(I), where I is a fixed bounded interval of positive length. For the
unprojected Q(i) family, write each good ideal uniquely as m=c d² with c
squarefree, allowing c,d to overlap, and put

    B_m(t)=mu_K(c)chi2(d)Nd^(1+it),
    F_k(x)(t)=sum_m B_m(t)k(log(Nm/x)).

The coefficients are fixed before x. Elementary ideal counting gives
sum_(Nm<=Y)||B_m||_H=O_I(Y log(2Y)). This pays the infinite sums, compact
left tails and Gaussian tails. The already proved scalar smoothing maps
therefore act on the whole H-valued family:

    F_new=S_no F_old,       F_G=S_gn F_new.

For every fixed a>0, their norm costs are the finite quantities
C_h(a)=integral |h(v)|exp(av)dv. Smoothing changes the scale profile and acts
as the identity on the retained phase coordinate. The phase family's
complementary numerator information survives.

The exact square-dilation formation of F_t from F_K also commutes with
smoothing on the absolute convergence domain. That identity supplies no
bounded square-dilation map at the desired exponent: its unattenuated
absolute cost still loses the gain, as the preceding integration explains.
The rational A(n), Gaussian ideal family and Eisenstein family remain
different sources; this theorem does not identify them.

## 2. Split into a bank and reconstruct without undoing smoothing

Fix beta below the desired growth exponent, with a fixed positive gap, and
set

    D_lambda F(x)=F(x)-lambda^beta F(x/lambda), lambda=2,3.
    A_beta F=(D_2 F,D_3 F).

On a weighted Mellin line Re(s)=a>beta, write
r_lambda=lambda^(beta-a), q_lambda=1-r_lambda and

    A=q_2²+q_3² >0.

The bank has sharp global weighted-L2 lower bound
||A_beta F||²>=A||F||². An explicit analytic, causal left inverse is

    E_lambda G(x)=sum_(j>=0)lambda^(j beta)G(x/lambda^j),
    w_lambda=q_lambda²/A,
    R_a(G_2,G_3)=w_2 E_2G_2+w_3 E_3G_3,
    R_a A_beta=I.

It uses only past scales; the compact/Gaussian left tails pay the telescoping
boundary. Its exact global weighted-L2 norm is A^(-1/2). For the all-shell
norm N_a(F)=sup_(X>0)X^(-a)||F||_[X,2X], the joint-bank bound is at most
sqrt(2/A), with the extra factor accounting for component suprema occurring
on different shells. Every operator acts as the identity on H.

An every-epsilon growth statement does not imply global weighted integrability
at its limiting exponent. Use N_a directly, or choose a strictly buffered
line and a smaller epsilon before invoking the global frame bound.

This reconstruction is not Gaussian deconvolution. The forbidden reverse
smoothing maps remain unbounded. At beta=a the simple inverse and positive
frame bound fail. Near that boundary the bank inverse costs order
(a-beta)^(-1); a serial product of both filters costs order(a-beta)^(-2).
This is a conditioning advantage of the bank, not an arithmetic power gain.

## 3. A concrete alternating construction

The following chain is legitimate:

    old compact family
      -> new compact family
      -> simultaneous 2/3 bank
      -> Gaussian bank
      -> common Gaussian family by R_a
      -> another simultaneous bank.

A two-level version has four channels

    G_ij=D_i S_gn D_j S_no F_old=D_iD_j F_G, i,j in{2,3}.

Applying R_a in each index recovers F_G with global cost A^(-1), or all-shell
cost at most2/A. At depth m the corresponding costs are A^(-m/2) and
(sqrt(2/A))^m. Multiply in every smoothing/shift cost as well. Fixed finite
depth costs a constant. Scale-dependent depth must have total cost X^o(1),
or debit its explicit power from the proposed saving. With a uniform stage
bound C>1, depth o(log X) suffices for a subpower product. Source and profile
choices must remain consistent throughout the reconstruction.

These particular scalar scale operators commute. Merely reordering them
cannot improve the exponent. Their value is that a different representation
may expose an arithmetic estimate that is hard to prove directly.

## 4. Harvest different estimates and merge them rigorously

Choose fixed bounded ideal masks p_1,p_2,p_3 with sum_j p_j=1. Let F_k^(j)
be the field with coefficients p_j(m)B_m. Their individual Dirichlet series
need not detect zeros. Suppose different methods can estimate:

- the old compact field F_old^(1);
- the simultaneous bank A_beta F_new^(2);
- the four-channel Gaussian bank G^(3).

Then the exact complete field is

    F_G=S_gn S_no F_old^(1)
        +S_gn R_a(A_beta F_new^(2))
        +(R_a in both indices)G^(3).

The all-shell bound is the sum of the three proved bounds multiplied by
C_gn C_no, C_gn sqrt(2/A), and2/A respectively. This is a concrete realization
of the user's proposed mixture of chaining, simultaneous analysis and
parallel merging. The fixed pieces sum back to the original detecting field.
It is a sufficient route; the needed piece estimates have not been proved.

An X-dependent completed list C_X is not a fixed mask in this theorem. Its
coefficients at every shifted scale, and every mismatch and remainder, must
be paid separately. Growing partitions also pay their size and mass. If the
only available estimates depend on cancellation between different pieces,
the triangle inequality above may lose precisely what is needed; retain and
estimate the full cross terms instead.

## 5. The complete arithmetic target and zero signal

For the four-channel phase family a sufficient new target is

    [sum_(i,j) integral_I integral_X^(2X)
       |sum_(c,d)mu_K(c)chi2(d)Nd^(1+it)
          kappa_ij(log(Nc Nd²/x))|² dx/x dt]^(1/2)
      <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),

where 1/2<gamma<.874864, beta<gamma, and

    kappa_ij(z)=g_tau(z)-i^beta g_tau(z+log i)
               -j^beta g_tau(z+log j)
               +(ij)^beta g_tau(z+log(ij)).

All repeated-square towers, Gaussian tails, signs and ordered profile/source
cross terms remain. If using the quartic relative period, require uniform
finite-source approximation bounds and both actual orbit cells; local
Fourier symmetry or an ambient Hilbert norm is insufficient.

The Mellin numerator is the tensor product of the nonzero smoothing factor,
the filter-symbol bank and t->L_K^S(2s-1-it,chi2). The last vector is nonzero
at every fixed s by the identity theorem. Hence the complete bound gives a
zero contradiction in Re(s)>gamma without dividing by one possibly vanishing
scalar numerator. This proves a conditional ordinary-zeta conclusion via
zeta_K=zeta L(s,chi_-4); other fixed families need their own constructions.

The phase interval must survive the proof. A scalar phase average or the
specific rank-one compact projection can erase the signal. A small fixed
interval is sufficient qualitatively, but if it shrinks around a numerator
zero of order r its squared signal is of order h^(2r+1), with derivative
constants. Shrinking intervals and growing height windows require new
quantitative capture estimates.

For fixed operators the complete bank bound is equivalent, up to the paid
constants and epsilon buffers, to the complete Gaussian phase-family bound.
There is no weaker exponent merely because more channels are present. The
bank can still be useful as a proof tool if its signed cross terms, or the
harvesting decomposition above, admit a better arithmetic argument.

statement:
### A1. Source, fixed localization and exact Fourier formula

Let a(n) be a fixed complex coefficient sequence with

    C_B=sum_(n>=1)|a(n)| n^(-B)<infinity                    (A1)

for some fixed B>0. Fix tau,kappa>0 independently of X. Put

    F(x)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)), h=log2,
    W_X(v)=g_kappa(v) F(X exp(v)),
    sigma=tau+kappa, nu=tau*kappa/sigma, alpha=kappa/sigma,
    w_n=log(n/X), b_X(n)=g_sigma(w_n).                     (A2)

Here g_t is the normalized Gaussian of variance t. This is the COMPLETE original field; no prime, pair, height, cutoff or sign is discarded. The Gaussian product identity is exactly

    g_kappa(v)g_tau(w-v)=g_sigma(w)g_nu(v-alpha*w).        (A3)

With hat f(t)=integral_R f(v)exp(-itv)dv, absolute Fubini gives

    hat W_X(t)=exp(-nu*t^2/2)
               sum_n a(n)b_X(n)exp(-i alpha*t*w_n).       (A4)

Indeed sum |a(n)|b_X(n)<=C_B X^B sup_w[e^(Bw)g_sigma(w)]
=C_B X^B exp(sigma B^2/2)/sqrt(2pi sigma). Thus for a constant C,

    |hat W_X(t)|<=C X^B exp(-nu*t^2/2), X>=1.            (A5)

This source-only bound is uniform at every real height. No continued Dirichlet series is interchanged on a nonabsolute line. All fixed derivatives and all displayed field series converge normally on compact real windows. For the half-open shell I=[X,2X), every nonidentity integer dilation carries I past its right endpoint. Thus P_I E P_I=I. Splitting the complement into past and future, the past receives no shell input and the shell receives no future input. The proposed Schur feedback is zero, while past-to-shell injection carries the entire arithmetic coefficient problem. A closed shell adds only its genuine endpoint atom where applicable. This is the coefficient version of G69's already proved causal output identity; no new contraction follows. The finite diagnostic at N=64, I=[16,32) checks the block identities exactly. No fixed-source or physical-shell norm is inferred from an unrestricted operator bound.

**W49-22, fixed-pair phase holonomy.** The actual JN9 kernel for one long-prime pair is

    kappa(h,s,s')=b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi')
        chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4. (T22)

On its literal nonzero set U={(h,pi*pi')=1,s!=0,s'!=0}, it factors as a constant times H(h)S(s)T(s'). For a fixed s', any mixed rectangular holonomy is exactly

    kappa(h,s,s')kappa(h',s1,s') /
       [kappa(h,s1,s')kappa(h',s,s')] =1.                 (T23)

The constant CRT/ray phase cancels in this calculation; it was not set to1 in T22. Zero vertices cannot be divided by and do not define an alternate nontrivial holonomy. Removing vertices by actual projectors leaves T23 true on every surviving rectangle, while all missing terms remain in the source. The complete short sum W_hat is generally pair-dependent and complex. Gauging away this factorized phase merely moves it into W_hat; it does not make the arithmetic positive or reduce a norm. Nor does T23 assert flatness across changing long-prime pairs with different residue spaces. Thus the seed's inexpensive optical-loop cancellation is unavailable at its first fixed-pair test; a cross-pair construction with a canonical identification remains open.     w*Q_w T Q_v v=(B_w w)*
        [B_w L_w^+ T L_v^+ B_v*](B_v v).                 (T24)

### All ten exact first tests

**S04: small-prime conditioning.** For finite P contained in primes>=5, let f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))) and f_P(n)=f(n)1_(gcd(n,product P)=1). The exact Dirichlet-convolution multiplier that reconstructs f from f_P has local series 1-z-z^2-z^3-..., not 1-z. Thus every eliminated prime power is retained. Its positive reconstruction price is product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)^-1. A moving P is affordable in a strict subpower range, but its source estimate must keep the parent cutoff frozen on cofactor shells. **Pass as a source-specific conditional bridge; developed D04.**

**S15: central covariance plus absolute complement.** Current-proof G23 already proves the full actual-f3 far-pair bound X^(2-r^2/(4tau)+o(1)) outside |log(n/m)|<=r sqrt(log X). To pay this below a target 2gamma-eta, choose r^2>=4tau(2-2gamma+eta). The true diagonal is O(X). This merely specializes G23; central signed energy is still open, and no H saving can be added. **Duplicate quantitative split, not a new survivor.**

**S45: weak negative Sobolev proposal.** For the finite actual coefficient measure nu=sum c(n)delta_(log(n/X)), r>1/2 gives

    ||g_tau*nu||_(L2(R))^2
       <= M_(tau,r) ||nu||_(H^-r(R))^2,
    M_(tau,r)=sup_t exp(-tau*t^2)(1+t^2)^r < infinity.

This follows directly from Fourier multipliers. The proposed rational frequency weight is a *stronger sufficient all-height estimate* than the Gaussian weight; it is not a weakening of the needed arithmetic cancellation. It also controls the full line, whereas the original energy is shell-local. A fixed smoothing or primitive multiplier nonzero at s=rho does not change the growth exponent of an e^(rho u) mode. **Valid conditional organization, existing D-GREEN/A-GRAPH ancestry; no new arithmetic norm or relaxed input. Parked after first test.**

**S51: Koszul detector.** Contraction d by the all-one covector and exterior multiplication h by a chosen generator obey dh+hd=I: the augmented complex is acyclic. A sharp mask introduces [d,P]. W37 T15/D28 already supply this obstruction and a paid-boundary repair; finite Euler zeros cannot replace the infinite reciprocal limit. **Duplicate failure.**

**S31: divisor Stokes boundary.** For n=pq with distinct primes p,q<=Y<pq, sum_(d|n,d<=Y)mu(d)=1-1-1=-1. The full Boolean rectangle adds mu(pq)=+1 and sums to zero. Truncation leaves exactly the omitted top face. For the actual Gaussian d,e,ell source W37 D28 supplies the stronger fixed-total-product boundary identity, including the masks. **Exact boundary failure duplicates U-PRIME-CHAIN/W37; no new saving.**

**S33: finite marginal LP.** Retain the actual local sign (-1)^(1_(p|n)), including p=2 and excluding p=3. Chinese-remainder independence on one complete period gives exact pair correlations, but the single-field average is identically zero because of prime 2. Gaussian smoothing makes that periodic field rapidly small. The full f3 field is not that finite local model. **Pass as a restricted source-specific calculation and failure diagnosis; developed D33.**

**S37: complex saddle contour.** For 0<r<1, averaging log|1-r exp(it log p)| over its full height period gives zero, by the absolutely convergent logarithmic series. A fixed imaginary shift leaves this average unchanged. Thus avoiding the finite Euler factor's zeros alone cannot provide a strictly smaller modulus at all heights, even in the one-prime test. An adaptive contour would still need its exact source integral, Jacobian, growth and residue payments. **Scoped failed free-contour gain; broader arithmetic saddle estimates remain untested.**

**S06: contour index.** B_a(z)=(z-a)/(1-a z), 0<a<1, has a zero, B_a(1)=1 and |B_a|=1 on the whole circle. Winding one coexists with the constant function's boundary L2 norm. ### 3.2 Full integer projection and exact dilation realization

Let Z(u)=sum_n g_tau(log n-u), and let mu_u(n)=g_tau(log n-u)/Z(u). Under the already proved full-pattern CRT theorem (W41 B2), for a moving P=P_X with Q<=X^(1-delta), fixed delta>0, the occupancy law under mu_u has L1 distance epsilon_X=O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) from pi, uniformly for u in[log X,log(2X)]. All patterns, including rare ones, are included. Z(u)=exp(tau/2)e^u+O_A(X^-A).

The pointwise identity sum_S Z_S(B)^2=1/pi(B)<=Q and Cauchy give |q_D(B)|<=sqrt Q. Hence |a_P-q_D|^2<=4Q and the actual-law discarded energy is at most rho_D^2+4Q epsilon_X. Cauchy with |r_P chi|<=1 therefore proves the uniform, COMPLETE field comparison

    |F_chi(u)-F_(P,D,chi)(u)|
      <=Z(u)[rho_D+2sqrt(Q epsilon_X)],
    F_(P,D,chi)(u)=sum_n q_D(B(n))r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u). (C4)

The source is constructive and retains all rough-tail signs. Define the exact dilation D_p V(u)=V(u-log p). Since r_P(pn)=r_P(n), divisibility gives

    sum_(p|n) r_P(n)chi(n)g_tau(log n-u)=chi(p)D_p R_(P,chi)(u).

Substitute this into C1 to obtain

    F_(P,D,chi)
      =sum_(|S|<=D) (-2)^|S| product_(p notin S)m_p
          product_(p in S)(chi(p)D_p-q_p I) R_(P,chi). (C5)

At D=|P| the polynomial factors exactly as product_(p in P)(I-2chi(p)D_p), and C5 equals the original F_chi. No prime power, character zero, Gaussian tail, shifted scale or negative cross term is deleted. At smaller D, C4 pays the full reconstruction error. Because every surviving S contains2, the coded field retains the exact factor I-2chi(2)D_2. Its P and D may move with X, so the zero return is through C4 and the ORIGINAL fixed F_chi, not a Mellin transform of a moving detector.

# Growing-order completion, paid arithmetic sectors and a direct return

[research revision] accepts G83-G85 as written mathematical progress. A uniform
growing-order completion pays its discarded faces, while genuine diagonal
and large-gcd sectors of its arithmetic moment are bounded. The stronger
all-real-scale moment contract returns directly to Mertens cancellation
without a prior subunit-growth hypothesis. Its remaining signed estimate
is open. **The accepted source-relative endpoint stays c6=.125139.**

The complete [author proof](headroom-next/report.md), [freeze](headroom-next/freeze.json),
[independent review](headroom-next-review/report.md) and [review freeze](headroom-next-review/freeze.json)
are retained byte-for-byte. The [controller observation](full-cutoff-moment-return.md)
is credited separately; the reviewer extends it to eta=0 and the shorter
order band. No formalization or kernel execution was performed.

## G83. Actual balanced completion at growing order

Fix an ordinary, possibly imprimitive complex Dirichlet character chi and
tau>0. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), m_Y=a 1_(n<=Y), u_Y=a-m_Y, and
g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). All convolutions below are
Dirichlet convolutions. Since a*chi=delta, for every integer K>=2,

    u_Y^(*K)*chi^(*(K-1))
      =a+sum_(j=1)^K (-1)^j choose(K,j)m_Y^(*j)*chi^(*(j-1)).

Write L=log X. In band I take L^(1/3)/2<=K<=2L^(1/3); in band II take
(2/5)sqrt(L)/log L<=K<=2sqrt(L)/log L. Define

    Y=floor exp(L/(K-1/2)), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2, r=K-1,
    F(x)=sum a(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    F_r=(1-x d/dx)^r F,
    phi_r(v)=(1+d/dv)^r g_tau(v).

Let C be (-1)^(K+1) times the sum of

    a(d1)...a(dK) chi(ell1)...chi(ell_(K-1))
      phi_r(log(d1...dK ell1...ell_(K-1)/x))

over every d_i<=Y and every ell_i>=1. Let C_bal impose only
Xe^(-W)<=d1...dK<=2Xe^W. Shared primes and squareful products remain.
Every d_i in that balanced sum lies between e^W and e^(2V). Uniformly
for X<=x<=2X and for all integers K in either band, for every A>0,

    |F_r(x)-C_bal(x)| <<_(A,chi,tau) X^(-A).

The proof separately pays C-F_r and C-C_bal. The derivative estimate is
|phi_r(v)|<=exp(O_tau((r+1)log(r+2))) exp(-v^2/(4tau)). For a completed
j-face its Mellin integrand contains
exp(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^(K-1)L(s,chi)^(j-1); the possible principal pole at
1 is canceled, including j=K. Functional equation, reflection and
duplication give on Re(s)=-B the uniform bound

    |L(-B+it,chi)| <= C_q^(B+1) Gamma(B+1) exp(pi|t|/2).

The resulting face cost is bounded by

    exp[-BZ+tau B^2/2
      +O(K(B+1)log(B+2)+K^2+Klog(K+2))],

with Z at least V or W as appropriate. Taking B=Z/tau gives a negative
term of order L^(4/3) in band I and L(log L)^2 in band II. It dominates
the full tuple and multiplicity costs. The all-large remainder starts at
(Y+1)^K>Xe^V and is paid with its d_(2K-1) coefficient envelope and a
Gaussian tail. Neither side of the product cutoff is dropped. A sufficient
general order regime is K growing with K^2 log L=o(L), with separately
compatible future-order bands; optimality is not claimed.

The dyadic balanced-source return keeps its exact premise. If
M_chi(z)=sum_(n<=z)a(n)<<z^b for fixed b<1, then the future-Gamma identity

    F(e^u)=1/Gamma(r) integral_0^infinity e^(-t)t^(r-1)F_r(e^(u+t))dt

holds. K is chosen at the base scale and held fixed throughout this
integral. The band margins keep it admissible through t<=4log X. An
every-dyadic C_bal norm bound at exponent gamma gives the desired main
term, while the future tail costs X^(5b-4+o(1)). Thus 5b-4<=gamma is
sufficient, with every positive epsilon retained. The source-relative
b=7/8 input gives 3/8. This route does not erase its growth premise.

## G84. Exact moment and genuine paid sectors

For 1/2<sigma<1 and even K=2m, put

    M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)a(n)n^(-s),
    Q(X,K)=integral_R exp(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt.

The full Mellin majorant H for C satisfies

    H=integral exp(-tau t^2/2)|1-sigma-it|^(K-1)
          |L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt,
    ||C||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x)) << X^sigma H,
    H <= exp(O_(chi,tau,sigma)(Klog(K+2))) Q.

Consequently Q<<X^(eta+epsilon) supplies gamma=sigma+eta, with no
square root of Q. The full |t|>3sqrt(L)/tau tail of H is O(X^(-3));
the central part remains an arithmetic problem.

The coefficient of M_Y^m is exactly lambda(n)chi(n)N_(m,Y)(n), where
N_(m,Y) counts ordered factorizations into m squarefree positive integers
at most Y. Unit factors, repeated primes across factors and squareful
outputs remain. With N=Y^m=X^(1/2+o(1)),

    Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_(n,k<=N) lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)conj(chi(k))
        N_(m,Y)(n)N_(m,Y)(k)(nk)^(-sigma)
        exp(-(log(n/k))^2/tau).

This is the complete double sum. Its total is nonnegative, but its signed
sectors need not be. The independent proof bounds:

- Diagonal: at most a fixed Gaussian constant times zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)
  =X^o(1), by N_(m,Y)<=d_m and d_m(p^j)^2<=d_(m^2)(p^j).
- Large gcd: its coefficientwise absolute price, for 1<=G<=N, is
  <<_epsilon X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G. Divisor submultiplicativity and
  Rankin summation retain the costs zeta(1+delta)^m and
  zeta(1+delta)^(m^2); both are X^o(1) in the stated bands.
- Large ratio: |log(n/k)|>=L^(2/3) has price O_A(X^(-A)) for every A.

Set gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, choose
0<kappa<gamma-1/2 and G=X^(c+kappa). Let Core be the same signed
double sum, including its Gaussian constant, with n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G
and |log(n/k)|<L^(2/3). Then

    Core <= X^(eta+epsilon)  for every epsilon>0

is equivalent at the exponent level to the Q bound: the discarded gcd
sector costs X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), the diagonal X^o(1), and the ratio
tail decays faster than any power. The inequality is one-sided.

Taking termwise absolute values cannot prove it. A positive-density
squarefree unit-phase class in [B/2,B], B=floor X^(1/K), yields a
positive subcollection with price X^(1-sigma-o(1)). Grouping products
in logarithmic windows of length1 pays the Gaussian. Removing the
diagonal and large gcd sector leaves this exponent unchanged. These
products lie inside the balanced product window because W/K tends to
infinity. This is an actual coefficientwise-price obstruction, not a
lower bound for signed Core, Q or the physical norm; cancellation between
different actual phases can still pay the desired estimate.

## G85. Full-scale moment return without the baseline

For fixed 1/2<sigma<=gamma<1 and eta=gamma-sigma>=0, the Q hypothesis
for every sufficiently large **real** X and every admissible even K in
either band is equivalent to M_chi(Y)<<_delta Y^(gamma+delta), for every
delta>0. The full-X one-sided Core hypothesis is equivalent too.

For every large integer Y, put u=log Y and choose

    band I:  K=2ceil(sqrt(u)/2),
    band II: K=2ceil(u/(8(log u)^2)),
    X=Y^(K-1/2).

Each choice is admissible in its respective band, tends to infinity and
hits the integer cutoff exactly. Write A=|M_Y(sigma)| and choose
D_Y=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma)log Y>=1. The elementary derivative bound
|d M_Y(sigma+it)/dt|<=D_Y shows, when A>=1,

    Q >= c_tau (A/2)^K / D_Y.

Indeed an interval inside [-1,1] of length at least 1/D_Y has amplitude
at least A/2. Thus the assumed Q bound gives

    A <= 2(C_epsilon D_Y/c_tau)^(1/K)
          Y^((1-1/(2K))(eta+epsilon)).

Fix epsilon before sending Y to infinity. The derivative-width cost is
Y^o(1), so the weighted partial sums are O_delta(Y^(eta+delta)), also
at eta=0. Abel inversion recovers Mertens with exponent gamma. The
converse follows by Abel summation, giving
|M_Y(sigma+it)|<<_delta(1+|t|)Y^(eta+delta), and the Gaussian integral
cost exp(O_delta(Klog(K+2))). No initial subunit Mertens bound is used.

The recovered Dirichlet series sum a(n)n^(-s) is holomorphic on
Re(s)>gamma and agrees with 1/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>1. Analytic continuation
therefore excludes zeros throughout Re(s)>gamma, retaining the principal
pole exception and including nonprincipal s=1. A common exponent must
hold for every fixed ordinary character before its own threshold; no
uniform growing-conductor or automatic Hecke statement follows.

**Do not substitute dyadic X for full real X in this equivalence.**
Dyadic cutoff gaps can have size Y/K and cannot be filled by a trivial
power-saving interpolation. The weaker dyadic balanced-source route
above retains its future-growth premise. This distinction is essential.

At sigma=3/4, the open eta targets are .124861 for the incumbent
boundary, .124860 for c=.125140, 1/12 for c=1/6, and0 for c=1/4.
Existing Mertens exponent b yields only Q<=X^(b-sigma+o(1)); raising
the order does not divide this exponent by K. No target bound is proved.

## Admission, ancestry and next action

W01 supplied fixed-order completion with a different profile. W47/G78
already supplied uniform geometric/Newton restoration with a fixed
b>1 absolute envelope. The new contribution is the actual growing-order
balanced family with paid faces, the arithmetic sector estimates and
the direct full-cutoff return. Neither prior mechanism bounds the new
signed Core. This is not a new inverse algebra or an easier equivalent
statement merely because its notation changed.

The next decisive step is a cancellation estimate for the actual small-gcd
Core, or a replacement mechanism that avoids its proved absolute price.
The near endpoint and1/6,1/4 remain separate open targets. Original
29-family/109-child history, PR9/Gao credits, old-c0 kernel evidence and
external root-definition/import obligations remain unchanged.

Read the stable prefix, frozen [research revision] problem and assignment in that order; their hashes matched the controller packet. The primary preprint is Alexandre de Faveri, *Optimal large sieve for fixed order characters*, arXiv:2610.04045v1, submitted 2 October 2026, [versioned primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1). The local HTML SHA256 is 7639be04b4023701377a4a339f2392994afdada8624b8f39e863fab7cbae91d4. Theorem1.1, Sections2.3–2.5 and the root-coupling discussion were read. The old source is PR9 commit58344df, local paper SHA256 2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8. The literal B0.3–5, B2.1, B2.4–6, B3.1–8 and B3.40 contracts, current attempt index, [research revision]/G99 and [research revision]/G110–111 were inspected. ## 6. Coarse attempts on the actual hard remainder

The first deliberately coarse estimate uses only |coeff R|<=p*d_3.
Split its physical integer at X, use the divisor bound on the prefix
and (3.1) on the tail. It proves

    ||R||_1+||R||_2 <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(1+epsilon)

when b<=2. The same bound for T follows from the paid complements.
It misses the first-gain L1 threshold gamma<.8748540364 by at least
.1251459636 in power. It is a complete estimate, not a dropped-tail
or point-sampling estimate, and it fails to give a new c.

The previously imported fixed-degree Green--Tao polynomial theorem also
applies to C_p. Indeed C_p is the sum of the two literal mu*chi series
with weights f_x(n) and -p*chi(p)*f_x(pn). A constant dilation changes
only fixed phase/damping constants; the accepted truncated-polynomial
bound and full bounded-coefficient tail proof work with those constants.
For every FIXED D>0 this gives, for b=3/2,k=6,

    ||C_p||_1 <<_(chi,p,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^(-D),
    ||T_p,chi,X||_1 << X^(gamma+epsilon)+X(log X)^(-D).  (6.1)

The latter is actual arithmetic control of the remaining sum, but only
with a logarithmic improvement on exponent1. D may not grow with X.
No uniform constant for growing degree, conductor, compensator or
logarithmic strength is imported. This is reuse of G142, not a second
novel arithmetic saving credited to this pass.

The stronger claim that every dyadic factor block is already affordable
fails for an ACTUAL principal-character block. Let chi be principal
modulo fixed q and select in (5.1) l=1 and distinct prime d,e in

    sqrt(X)/2 < d,e <= sqrt(X/2).

For large X these primes are unramified, exceed U,V and have
X/4<de<=X/2, inside (L,M]. Their coefficient is exactly +1 in EACH
compensated source: mu(d)mu(e)=1, chi(de)=1, b_p(1)=1. The ordered
prime-pair count is J(X)(J(X)-1), where the prime number theorem gives
J(X)~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X. The exclusion d=e ensures no
squareful original product is smuggled into this selected component.

For every x in [X,2X], the phase satisfies (de/x)^k<=2^(-k), and the
damping is at least exp(-X^(1-b)/2). The REAL PART of this selected
component B_p(x) is consequently at least

    exp(-X^(1-b)/2) cos(2^(-k)) J(X)(J(X)-1)
                       >>_q X/(log X)^2.               (6.2)

Thus both its L1 and L2 norm have exponent1. This is an actual signed
arithmetic component, with its sign proved, rather than a shell-dependent
arbitrary-array countermodel. Any estimate that partitions the exact sum
into cells and pays this cell's norm separately by a positive triangle
budget cannot achieve X^(gamma+epsilon) for ANY fixed gamma<1. The
same obstruction survives the two-prime detector bank, whose l=1 cells
are identical. It is only an obstruction to this separated budget.
It is NOT a lower bound for the full R,T,C_p, nor a no-gain theorem for
signed cross-cancellation or nonprincipal characters.

Accordingly the next surviving route has to couple this prime-prime
cell with other exact factorization/cofactor cells before taking an
absolute value or squared norm. The mean-zero free cofactor helps on
small products de; it cannot cancel the l=1 cell by itself when de~X.
This is the strongest source-specific failed coarse test in this pass.

statement:
# [research revision]: a complete repetition-layer sieve estimate

The completed [research revision] high-ceiling pass gives a useful bound for the actual
labelled canonical Gauss and completed theta sources. Taking the better
estimate on each exact sixth-power repetition layer, before counting all
layers, lowers the required label exponent from M/6 to M/7 when N>=8M/7.
This is a source-relative analytic deduction from the named sieve inputs.
It does not improve the zero-free constant or repair the unfinished Gao
weighted source theorem. At label exponent V=0 it gives exactly the older
all-row sieve price, which misses the current physical source.

The conditional benchmark remains c11=312864909/2500000000. Its source
status is the [PR15 author clarification](../imports/qrtracker-20261013/pr15-status-clarification.md).
The independent author and reviewer reports are retained as
[author/report.md](author/report.md) and [review/report.md](review/report.md).
Their historical endpoint language predates that clarification; the
conditional qualification here controls current use.

## G212. Fixed-family binding and complete row/column lifts

Let K=Q(omega), q_a=N(a), with the original primary convention, fixed
excluded set S containing the primes above6 and fixed conductors, and the
original finite ray dictionary. Every character power, including a
cancelled phase, retains its zero at a nonunit. Write
psi_u(b)=chi_b(u) and phi_u=nu psi_u^(+/-1), with nu fixed; nu need not
have order dividing6. All coefficients below are independent of the row
being summed. A moving but fixed puncture is a zero column coefficient,
not a new fixed character datum.

The external input is de Faveri, *Optimal large sieve for fixed order
characters*, [arXiv2610.04045v1, Theorem1.1 and Sections2.3–2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/2610.04045v1).
It is the operator bound for sixth-power-free S-coprime ideal rows AND
columns, with arbitrary column coefficients:

    sum_(q_a<=A)^(6) |sum_(q_b<=B)^(6) lambda_b chi_a(b)|^2
      << (AB)^epsilon T6(A,B) sum_b |lambda_b|^2,
    T6(A,B)=A+B+A^(5/6)B^(1/3)+A^(1/3)B^(5/6).       (1)

The constants depend on the fixed construction data. This manuscript
already cited that theorem in Appendix S.1; its reuse is not a new
discovery of the external result. Its analytic proof and external
definition/import/admission remain named inputs, not newly verified here.

Here is the actual family binding. In the class-number-one Eisenstein
field choose the source's representative generators m_E to be global
primary generators. In its decomposition a=(x)E g^6, x=1 modulo the fixed
ray modulus, take a primary generator g0 of the fractional ideal g.
Then x m_E g0^6 and the primary a0 generate the same ideal and are both1
modulo3. Their quotient is a unit congruent to1 modulo3 and hence equals1.
Thus the source's symbol equals (a0/b)_6 on coprime ideals; its prescribed
zero extension also agrees. Other permissible generator conventions split
into finitely many S-unit classes modulo sixth powers, giving fixed column
twists. Split element units and S-valuations modulo6, then count their
S-supported sixth powers with a logarithmic loss. Absorb nu into the
column coefficients. For the opposite orientation conjugate the WHOLE
inner sum. Reverse residue-symbol orientation, when used, retains the
original finite modulo36 reciprocity sectors. No row-column coefficient
array or moving-conductor character license is inferred.

For a product of J fixed normalized polynomials of lengths X_j, put
B=product X_j. Exact ordered convolution, including all collisions, has

    F_u=sum_b lambda_b psi_u(b),  q_b<<B,
    |lambda_b| << B^(-1/2) d_J(b).                    (2)

Signs, phases, independent heights, original slot coefficients and the
fixed nu remain in lambda. Disjoint slot pools do not imply a slot is
coprime to a plain factor. Write b=d h^6 uniquely with d sixth-power-free,
allowing (d,h)>1. Then

    psi_u(d h^6)=psi_u(d) 1_((u,h)=1),
    sum_d |lambda_(d h^6)|^2 << B^epsilon q_h^(-6).

For each fixed h apply (1) and remove the h restriction only from its
positive outer norm. Hilbert Minkowski sums q_h^(-3), a convergent ideal
series. This gives T6(U,B) on sixth-power-free rows. For ALL rows write
u=a e^6, with all units and S-parts as above. The extra factor
1_((b,e)=1) is a fixed column mask for each e. Applying (1) at U/q_e^6
and summing every e yields

    sum_(0<q_u<<U) |F_u|^2 << (UB)^epsilon Tall(U,B),
    Tall(U,B)=U+B U^(1/6)+U^(5/6)B^(1/3)
                         +U^(1/3)B^(5/6).           (3)

The term B U^(1/6) counts the sixth-power repetitions; they are not a
finite dictionary. No principal or fixed-inducing row is discarded.
The normalized short gate is B<=U^(1/2). In particular S(U^m)^2 Q has
B=U^(2m+v), and two independent plains have B=U^(n1+n2+v). The failed
proposal m+v<=1/2 for a fourth moment lost a factor of2. The correct
2m+v<=1/2 and inverse r+v<=1/2 were already in equation (S.4) of Appendix S.1.

Now take the literal PR9 B3.6 canonical energy, writing X=Z^N,
U=Z^M, F=Z^V:

    E=F^(-1) sum_(q_f~F)^(sf) w(f)
       sum_(0<q_k<<U)
       |X^(-1/2) sum_n^(sf) a0(n)nu(n)rho(n)
           chi_n(k)chi_n(f)^4 d_I(n) W(q_n/X)|^2.    (4)

Here a0=bar(alpha)gamma_2 has modulus1 on good squarefree indices;
w is nonnegative divisor-bounded; rho is the fixed puncture; d_I is
the original product-form mark from fixed disjoint slot pools. Pools,
coefficients and punctures are independent of the live f,k. A fixed
polynomial-size puncture can move between instances. The coefficient
mass for each fixed f is Z^epsilon, uniformly in its natural holes;
F^(-1) cancels the count of f. Thus (3) gives exponent

    Eall(M,N)=max(M,N+M/6,5M/6+N/3,M/3+5N/6)
       = M                    for 0<=N<=M/2,
         5M/6+N/3             for M/2<=N<=M,
         N+M/6                for N>=M.              (5)

This bound alone remains valid for column coefficients depending on the
fixed f, provided the coefficient mass is uniformly controlled. That
extra freedom is NOT available in the label-average argument below.

The full completed theta source has index A=c b^3, c squarefree, and
coefficient

    a0(c)nu(c) bar(alpha(b))^3 nu(b)^3
      chi_A(f)^4 rho(A)d_I(A)V(q_A/X)/(sqrt(q_c)q_b). (6)

Its character is psi_k(A), with all common c,b primes permitted. Each
A has at most one such representation. Writing A=d h^6 gives
d=c b0^3, b=b0 h^2, with c,b0 squarefree and possibly overlapping.
The exponents of d are0,1,3,4. At fixed h the squared coefficient mass
is at most

    X^epsilon q_h^(-4)
       sum_(b0 sf) q_b0^(-2) sum_(q_c<<X/q_h^6) q_c^(-1)
      << X^epsilon q_h^(-4).                        (7)

All whole-index marks, phases and f/puncture/row holes stay in (6).
Minkowski now sums q_h^(-2), again convergent. Both T6 and Tall therefore
apply to the COMPLETE theta source with X as column length. This is not
a restriction to its b=1 or coprime c,b part.

The profile contract is annular support or rapid decay at both endpoints,
with prescribed finite derivative orders. Original common product
profiles use the Fourier measure fixed on the whole ambient box before
the live labels, as in PR9 B3.3. Minkowski and dyadic decomposition sum
these tails; subunit scales are treated at the original profile. Tensor
Sobolev restores the independent heights and the bounded profile/scale
suprema at a fixed polynomial cost H_J. Derivative orders and Fourier
decay precede the final large-scale threshold. This argument does not
grant a new small-x decay bound for an arbitrary sharply reflected
profile. Genuine detector tails keep their own prior payment.

When f=1 and rho=1, the old unmarked completed bound B2.43 may be
combined with (5). The resulting exponent is M, then5M/6+N/3, then
2M-N, thenM on the consecutive intervals
[0,M/2],[M/2,7M/8],[7M/8,M],[M,infinity). Its maximum is9M/8.
For the old marked S.5 scope, z<=M/2, take the minimum with
M+max(0,(N+2z-2M)/4,M+2z-N); e.g. N=.7M,z=.04M improves
1.38M to16M/15. These old-theorem comparisons are not extended to
new labels or punctures without their own proof.

## G213. Average the true cubic label before counting repetitions

In (4) fix k and use the order-three character chi_n(f)^4 in the actual
squarefree f,n variables. The old squarefree cubic sieve B2.25 gives,
after dividing by F and counting all k,

    Elabel=M+L,  L=max(0,N-V,(2N-V)/3).              (8)

For (6), fix b first:
chi_(c b^3)(f)^4=chi_c(f)^4 1_((b,f)=1).
The b phase has modulus at most1. Remove its natural f-hole only after
taking the fixed-b positive norm. Its coefficient mass is bounded by
q_b^(-2) times logarithms, and its c-length is X/q_b^3.
Minkowski sums q_b^(-1) for the constant-in-length term (a logarithm);
the positive column-length terms converge. Thus (8) holds for the full
theta source as well. This requires the coefficients, marks, puncture
and common profile to be independent of f. Arbitrarily conditioning them
on the label would invalidate the cubic sieve.

The whole-norm minimum of (5),(8) does not enlarge the boundary for the
canonical target exponent N+V. The label-only gate is
V>=max(M-N,M/2,(3M-N)/4), which is at least the old all-row gate.
There is nevertheless a stronger estimate BEFORE counting repetitions.

For each exact e in k=a e^6, both estimates apply to the SAME complete
positive joint norm in f and sixth-power-free a. The column mask
1_((A,e)=1) is fixed through both averages. Put Arow=U/q_e^6. Its bound
is the minimum of T6(Arow,X) and Arow Z^L, up to the same small loss
and height cost. The two methods do not select incompatible sources.
Counting EVERY e dyad q_e~Z^y, including both endpoints, with t=M-6y
therefore proves

    E << H_J Z^(Emix+epsilon),
    Emix(M,N,V)=sup_(0<=t<=M)
        [(M-t)/6+min(C(t,N),t+L)],
    C(t,N)=max(t,N,5t/6+N/3,t/3+5N/6).              (9)

This is valid for (4) and the complete (6). The dyadic count Z^y is
essential. No signed subsource monotonicity, invented f-average or
discarded principal layer occurs.

For completeness, a continuous evaluation of (9) gives

    E0=min(C(M,N),M+L),  P=(M+5N+L)/6,
    Emix=E0, except that
    Emix=max(E0,P) if L>=N/2 and N-L<=M.             (10)

Indeed C(t,N) has successive affine pieces
N,t/3+5N/6,5t/6+N/3,t, with breakpoints N/2,N,2N.
On the first piece its contribution after subtracting t/6 decreases,
whereas the label contribution increases. Their sole crossing is
t=N-L. Because0<=L<=N, it lies in the first piece and in[0,M]
exactly under the condition in (10). The value there is P.
On each later piece both branches increase: their respective slopes
after counting are1/6,2/3,5/6 and5/6. Their minimum increases as well.
Thus the endpoint t=M and that one crossing give the entire maximum.
This also covers a truncated first interval; M=0 or N=0 is immediate.

For M>0, the precise boundary of THIS proved upper envelope is

    Emix<=N+V iff V>=g(M,N),
    g(M,N)= M-N                   (0<=N<=M/2),
             5M/6-2N/3            (M/2<=N<=M),
             (2M-N)/6             (M<=N<=8M/7),
             M/7                  (N>=8M/7).        (11)

Here is the proof of necessity as well as sufficiency for the envelope.
For N<=M, (9)<=Eall proves sufficiency at the first two thresholds.
At t=M, the sieve branch reaches the target only at that threshold,
while the label branch requires the stronger gate following (8).
For N>=M the proposed threshold is at most M/6. In0<=V<=M/6,
L=N-V and the crossing t=V is present. Its price is
N+(M-V)/6, so it is paid exactly when V>=M/7.
The t=M label price exceeds N+V throughout this interval; the sieve
branch requires V>=(2M-N)_+/6. Their maximum switches at N=8M/7.
These conditions suffice by (10). Larger V decreases Emix and increases
the target; a smaller V fails a displayed envelope branch.
Equality has the usual Z^epsilon loss. Applications needing a strict
reserve must choose a padded inequality. This is no lower bound on the
true arithmetic energy.

At (M,N,V)=(1,8/7,1/7), the new price9/7 equals N+V, while Eall=55/42
and Elabel=2. At (1,2,1/7), they are15/7,13/6,20/7.
The gain over Eall is1/42 in each example. Polynomial-size common
punctures remain uniform; the improvement need not satisfy PR9 B3.7's
older sufficient Q gate. Conversely at V=0, L=N and C(t,N)<=t+N.
Equation (9) becomes EXACTLY Eall. In particular Emix>N for every
M>0. The complete unlabelled canonical target remains unpaid.

## G214. Counted sectors and the full physical obstruction

Useful lower-order subfamilies remain available with their counts.
For sixth-power-free u=t a^2, t squarefree, a cube-free, permit shared
primes and retain q_t<=D. In the completed source,

    chi_(c b^3)(t a^2)
      =chi_(c b^3)(t) chi_c(a)^2 1_((a,b)=1).

Fix b before the positive a norm and use the CUBE-FREE cubic input,
not a silent enlargement of squarefree B2.25. This input is explicit
in the retained [research revision] MQ1 (or de Faveri's n=3 theorem with its binding).
Counting each t at length(U/q_t)^(1/2) gives

    (UD)^(1/2)+XD+U^(1/3)X^(2/3)D^(2/3).            (12)

For u=t a^3, t cube-free, a squarefree, the squarefree quadratic sieve
and counts instead give U^(1/3)D^(2/3)+XD. All coefficients, zeros
and b sums are treated as in the fixed-b proof above. [research revision]'s MQ4 already
contains the counted cubic mechanism for its own original source.
These are useful actual-sector extensions, not a new universal sieve.
A generic squarefree row has t=u in both decompositions, so a small D
does not cover it. Non-S sixth-power repetitions require their own
counted lift; [research revision] MQ5 additionally uses a named all-character reciprocal
strip. Neither that assumption nor a missing complement is free.

The physical failure can be quantified over the entire relevant range.
At [research revision]'s conditional geometry set
ell=313594727/1875000000, M=1-ell; then1/6<ell<1/5.
Every compensator subset of width d in[0,ell] has

    M'=M-2d, z'=ell-d, N'=1+ell-d,
    N'-M'=2ell+d>0, N'-(M'+2z')=3d>=0.

PR9 B0.26 costs Eold=M'+max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4. Equation (5) costs
N'+M'/6, whose excess is

    (1+11ell)/6+2d/3-max(0,-1+5ell+d)/4 >19/45.     (13)

The first term exceeds17/36 and the subtracted term is less than1/20.
This pays the comparison on the whole subset interval, including the
empty subset. The exact signs, outside coefficients and tuple counts
in B0.25, and the old -d saving in B0.27, are retained on both sides.
These sources have f=1,V=0, so (9) cannot alter (13).

The actual two-plain window .41M<=n_i<=.44M with .034M<=v<=.04M
has merged length at least .854M. Equation (5) then costs at least
1.118M, instead of the required M. Even v=0 leaves length at least
.82M and misses the short gate. The literal Euler restoration B0.41–44
has h=h0 h_r, repeated-row allocation q_u/q_rad(u), reflected scale
at most(U/Y)h0 and weighted mass sum|c_u(h0,h_r)|h0^(delta/2)<<U^epsilon.
The critical h0=1 case already fails; increasing h0 cannot repair it.
Shortened cases do not pay their longer complements. Independent heights,
four clipped profile pairs, shortage and empty-selection alternatives,
zero capacity, fixed-inducing/principal branches, and the original
Euler/detector tails retain their old proofs. No label signal is inserted.

Nor does the imported density corollary fix the active density gate.
De Faveri Corollary1.5 at n=6, delta=2sigma-1 in[1/3,5/6], saves

    D6=3delta(6delta-1)/(60delta-36delta^2-10).

For delta in[17/25,7/10] its row exponent1-D6 exceeds the retained
rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)] by

    delta(312delta-252delta^2-55) /
      [3(5-2delta)(60delta-36delta^2-10)] >17/100.    (14)

The concave numerator quadratic is at least998/25, delta>=17/25,
and the positive denominator is at most98007/625. The resulting
16966/98007 is greater than17/100. Since delta v<=.035 and
E_K<=rho+delta v, the new corollary is weaker even on the uncontested
untwisted subfamily. It is a zero-count bound, not zero exclusion;
arbitrary fixed-nu extensions are not asserted.

Finally, the separated inverse source in [research revision] has r+s>217/100,
delta in[17/25,7/10], v<=1/20 and target T=delta(r+s)+E_K.
Its merged length b=r+s+v exceeds2.17. Even the sixth-free sieve
cost b exceeds T by at least

    (1-delta)(r+s+v)-rho >=8077/27000.               (15)

The minimum is at v=0,r+s=217/100,delta=7/10: the delta derivative
is negative on the whole interval. The all-row cost is larger.
This is a failure of the proposed sufficient price, not a norm lower
bound or impossibility theorem for the signed arithmetic.
The current [research revision] residual is R_U,hard+R_N,hard, replacing the older
[research revision] R_nonunique+R_middle wording in these raw reports. Its one-sided
saving and physical return remain open.

The field-source targets gamma<.8748540364 (energy<1.7497080728),
gamma=.87485 at c=.12515, gamma=5/6 at c=1/6 and gamma=3/4 at c=1/4
remain target conversions with their actual transfers required.
The old ell<1/5 limit c<2/15 and ell<x<=y, x+y=1-ell limit c<1/6
are restrictions of that architecture, not universal barriers.

## Evidence, potential and next mathematical action

Root read the full author and independent-review arguments, original
PR9 source formulas, current Appendix S.1–S.2, [research revision]'s cube-free/counting
contract, [research revision]'s literal geometry/Euler return and [research revision]/[research revision]'s signed
source. The primary external theorem and family construction were
checked against the versioned text. Root independently reconstructed
(9)–(11), both endpoint cases and the quantitative comparisons above.

Retained diagnostics check442368 sixth-power identities,4096 completed
indices,1369 whole-norm parameter pairs, and the review's1849 exact
layer-envelope pairs. They support finite arithmetic and algebra only;
they are not proofs of an asymptotic sieve or the Gao source theorem.
Root did not rerun unchanged helpers. The original factor-of-two failed
proposal, source-print failure, capacity delays and deadline history
remain in their original records. The retention manifest binds the
mathematical bytes; operational claim receipts stay host-local.

Potential: moderate for a genuinely labelled child source, low for
direct substitution into the current unlabelled physical source, and
unproved for an upstream detector redesign. The strongest objection is
the V=0 complement, resolved here as a quantitative negative comparison,
not by an invented averaging variable. The next useful action is to
derive a detector/induction source with a genuine paid label average
whose full return uses (11), or develop cancellation that removes the
unlabelled obstruction itself. PR26's source reconstruction is a
separate active lane. F0/ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity,
