### 3.3 A large actual isolated set exists on every sufficiently large shell

Fix q, C>0, an integer d>=1, and 0<=theta<1. Precisely, every graph edge {n,m} must satisfy the displayed distance bound and delete at most d prime factors from EACH squarefree endpoint when passing to the other endpoint. This condition is independent of a flow's orientation; an incoming edge cannot bypass the source-side budget. Squarefree Hamming radius<=d satisfies it, and optional zero-mass integer vertices are allowed subject to the same endpoint rule. Choose an integer

    k > d/(1-theta),   y=(2X)^(1/k).                            (C6)

Let V_X contain all products of k DISTINCT primes in

    (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)].

Each n in V_X is squarefree, X<n<=2X, and for large X is coprime to the fixed q. All its primes are<=y. Since1-theta-d/k>0, inequality C5 holds for every n in V_X once X is sufficiently large. Hence every such vertex is isolated in the entire short-move graph, including possible neighbors outside this shell or cutoff.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this FIXED k,

    t_X=#primes in the displayed interval
       ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization counts distinct vertices exactly as binomial(t_X,k). Therefore

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.                                (C7)

Only fixed-relative-width intervals are used, not a primes-in-short-interval theorem or a growing-k substitution. For the external input, the published PNT was checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12, equations4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12). All deductions C3-C7 are given here. The constants can be tiny and the onset large; both are permitted and neither changes the power obstruction.

It follows that ANY disjoint matching in this graph leaves at least A_k X/(2(log X)^k) actual unit-modulus source coefficients unmatched on [X,2X], for every sufficiently large X. The absolute unmatched mass cannot be O(X^delta) for ANY delta<1. Thus the fixed-radius candidate cannot meet M2, at a near gain,1/6,1/4, or any other power-saving target.

This extends beyond integral matching. For an arbitrary complex edge flow F supported on the same graph, let div F(n) be its net outgoing mass, whenever defined. In any exact source decomposition a=div F+r, an isolated vertex satisfies r(n)=a(n). Hence

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.                               (C8)

No choice of complex flow weights, linear combinations of codewords, or repeated local steps removes an isolated vertex. Chaining cannot start there. The result still holds for any uniformly bounded family of radii and for subpower inflation of C, by first replacing theta by a fixed slightly larger number below1. It does NOT cover growing radii, genuinely long edges, nonlocal auxiliary states with a different exact transfer, or a bound retaining signed cancellation among the isolated states.

| Intended exponent theta | Fixed radius d | k used | Strict isolation exponent1-theta-d/k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|17497/20000=.87485|3|24|3/20000|
|5/6|3|19|1/114|
|3/4|3|13|1/52|

The first row has about X/(log X)^24 isolated24-prime products, all with principal coefficient+1. The next two rows use19- and13-prime products, with principal coefficient-1. This is a lower bound for the absolute residual and for those particular signed subcollections. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete signed residual or M_chi: different prime-count layers can cancel, and that cancellation remains an eligible arithmetic input.

## 3. Full physical covariance after the new core and gcd results

### F04.C — The new hard sector

Use the actual fully compensated field \(S_c\) containing every completed column \(A=cn^3\) with squarefree core \(c\), all descendants, marks and embeddings. With
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad L=Z^\ell,
\quad \mathcal F_A=1+P_a^{1/6}+LP_a^2/Y,
\]
T06 proves
\[
\mathcal D_{\rm core}=\sum_c\|S_c\|_2^2
\ll (Z^\epsilon/Y)\mathcal F_A.
\]
This is the actual square function, not a bound on \(\|\sum_cS_c\|_2^2\). For a smooth true-gcd dyad,
\[
\mathcal C(G)=\sum_{c\ne c'}w(q_{(c,c')}/G)\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle,
\]
T07 gives, relative to the stronger inherited finite-order Hecke inputs,
\[
|\mathcal C(G)|\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A
 {Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{1+3b_0/2}\over G^2}.
\]
The actual product-slot structure is essential. Thus dyads above
\[
G_0=Z^{1/2+b_0/4}L^{1/2+3b_0/4}
\]
are affordable; at the saved .12551 geometry \(\log_ZG_0=.91621058\ldots\). A rigorous proof works first at a fixed \(b>b_0\), then allocates the final small loss. Rational \(b=7/8\) gives \(G_0=Z^{23/32}L^{37/32}\). The result does not follow from rational-zeta nonvanishing alone.

The exact remaining target is a one-sided upper bound, or the stronger absolute bound,
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_{G<G_0}\mathcal C(G)
\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A\ }
\tag{CORE}
\]
with a smooth complete partition and all inherited uniformities. At the saved geometry \(LP_a^2/Y\) is harmless and \(\mathcal F_A\asymp P_a^{1/6}\) up to allowed losses. This leaves a large arithmetic sector; the tail exponent .9162 is a useful reduction, not evidence that only a negligible set remains.

For \(c=gu,c'=gv\) and embedded products \(D=G_*d,E=G_*e\), the live common-core character is
\[
\psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}.
\]
The exact collision masks \((u,e)=(v,d)=1\), together with the two gcd decompositions, make every surviving off-core good character nonprincipal. A marked prime enters the squarefree Euler identity through
\[
f_s(p)={t_p\over1+t_p},\qquad t_p=\psi(p)q_p^{-s};
\]
a same-slot coincidence contributes \(f_s-f_s^2\). The first two powers carry nonprincipal cubic characters; the first possible principal power is paid by its cubic decay. This is the mechanism already exploited in the large-gcd tail. A small-gcd proof must improve its averaging order or its use of the remaining cofactors.

### F04.N1 — New pass 1: switch the averaging order where the tail stops

The proposed object is the exact gcd-one kernel obtained from \(\langle S_u,S_v\rangle\), with \((u,v)=1\), before absolute values in the row, prime slots or cube descendants. Fix dyads for the *relative character conductor*, distinct from \(q_uq_v\) and the full additive period. Expand mask-only primes as divisibility conditions; preserve the actual \(f_s\) factors at live slots. Try row completion for small relative conductors and column/slot averaging first for large ones. The switching inequality must include the original two product profiles and quotient-square embeddings.

The first missing lemma is a coefficient-specific bound on this switched sum giving the CORE budget after its conductor dyads are summed. The cheapest decisive test is one coprime pair with two unequal embedded products and one genuine marked slot. Print its minimal arithmetic period and transformed phase. If the proposed transform becomes a long individual character sum, it has not exploited the new reduction. A fallback is a thin band of small \(g\) for which a true relative-conductor saving can be summed; record the uncovered region explicitly.

### F04.N2 — New pass 1: core-frame calibration and exact mark cumulants

T06 supplies a useful normalization absent from the earlier raw-Gram proposals. On a finite truncation let \(d_c=\|S_c\|_2\) and
\(\Gamma_{c,c'}=\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle/(d_cd_{c'})\) for nonzero entries. The full target is a bound on the **actual weighted direction** \(d^*\Gamma d\), not an arbitrary-vector spectral bound. Pairing the physical field with the theta witness may require still less than this energy. Compute an independently defined residual subspace of \(\Gamma\) only after its coefficient vectors and principal calibration are explicit.

A complementary arithmetic test centers two actual mark slots *inside* the common Euler identity. The second cumulant must retain \(f_s-f_s^2\), cross-slot collisions and all addback terms. One may seek cancellation in the centered block while pricing its lower moments by T06/T07. An apparent saving that simply drops an addback carrying the original signal fails. This differs from the supplied primewise tail proof: the proposed averaging is across two slots and the remaining small-gcd cofactors simultaneously. First output: a two-slot identity and its full norm/principal terms, then an aggregate estimate. Neither the normalized frame nor the cumulant identity supplies cancellation by itself.

### F04.N3 — New pass 1: merge paid sectors only through an exact common partition

There are two legal decompositions:

- Core decomposition: full physical energy = same-core square function + large-gcd off-core covariance + small-gcd off-core covariance.
- Frequency decomposition: full physical energy = complete zero mode + coherent-unembedded pairwise zero-subtracted remainder + all other pairwise zero-subtracted remainders.

These cannot be combined by declaring their overlapping “paid pieces” positive. A01 controls the coherent principal-good-character pair condition \(aA'/(bA)\in\mathcal I^6\), after subtracting each pair's zero contribution. It does not control a nonprincipal character evaluated on a sixth-power frequency. A15 shows that gcd masks need not preserve positive semidefiniteness, even on a two-column Gram.

The concrete new bookkeeping/lemma task is to express both decompositions on one finite pair index set, enumerate intersections, and price the resulting addbacks before removing truncation. A useful extension would transport the coherent divisibility-discrepancy proof to one mixed embedding: derive coherence after substituting the true rows \(e^2r,d^2r\), then prove the CRT/Jacobian/profile statement. Merely reusing the unembedded ratio is wrong. This is an enabling theorem worth a bounded attempt because it could remove an additional portion of CORE; it is not H or a full saving.

# [research revision]: local small-value sets recover a complete Gaussian exponent

The W39 [author](../[research revision]/wild39/report.md) and
[independent critic](../[research revision]/wild39-review/report.md) prove a conditional
analytic return for actual complete arithmetic Gaussian fields. Root
read both complete arguments and independently replayed the finite
identity checks. The hypothesis is open: no new zero-free constant,
arithmetic small-value bound or kernel verification is claimed.

## 1. The local-set theorem

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character, let

    F(z)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n) g_tau(log n-z),   tau>0 fixed.

All natural zeros remain. The complete series is entire and satisfies
|F(u+iv)|<=C exp(u+v^2/(2tau)) for u>=0, with a Gaussian real left tail.
Fix 0<gamma<1 and 0<=kappa<1/2. Suppose for EVERY epsilon>0 there are
constants c_epsilon,C_epsilon>0 such that for EVERY sufficiently large
integer j a measurable E_j subset [j,j+1] satisfies

    |E_j|>=c_epsilon j^-kappa,
    ess sup_(y in E_j)|F(y)|<=C_epsilon exp((gamma+epsilon)j). ([research revision]-V1)

Then the full field is O_epsilon(exp((gamma+epsilon)y)) on the real
axis and L(s,chi) has no zero in Re(s)>gamma. The converse follows
from the full-field bound; this is an equivalent observation criterion,
not a proof that the arithmetic hypothesis holds. Fixed positive-length
intervals also work. Arbitrarily shrinking intervals need another proof.
No missing logarithmic intervals, density-one substitute, finite sample
or selected signed subfield is permitted.

Here is the mechanism, including the errors. A complex polynomial of
degree N on a unit interval obeys

    sup_I |P| <= (4e/delta)^N ess sup_E |P|,  |E|>=delta.

Quantile Lagrange interpolation proves this for complex values. Given
a prior complex bound C(1+|v|)^K exp(bu+v^2/(2tau)), expand to
N=ceil(2(b-gamma)j/log j) on Cauchy radius sqrt(tau(N+1)). Both Taylor
remainders are multiplied by the interpolation factor. The resulting
single-step exponent is h=gamma+2kappa(b-gamma), with subexponential
loss. The calculation at kappa>=1/2 gives no improvement by THIS
method; it is not an impossibility theorem for other sampling arguments.

The bilateral Mellin identity

    integral_R F(y)exp(-sy)dy = exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi)

first excludes zeros to the right of h. Only AFTER this exclusion is
the improved complex bound replenished. Ordinary character summation
gives polynomial growth of L on fixed positive half-planes. Regularize
the principal pole by (s-1)L, choose a zero-free logarithm on a disk
centered at2+it, and use Borel--Caratheodory with a positive fixed disk
gap. This proves polynomial reciprocal growth on every fixed line
b>h. Gaussian Mellin inversion then restores the complex bound at b.
Thus h_m=gamma+(2kappa)^m(B-gamma). For each output epsilon choose a
FINITE m and positive intermediate buffers; no infinite limiting
constant or circular reciprocal assumption is used.

## 2. Exact fixed-family and f3 extensions

For each fixed finite-order Eisenstein Hecke character of trivial
infinity type, use the ideal Gaussian with its presented ray modulus
and fixed omitted primes. The Euclidean lattice count is

    sum_(Na<=X) psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1).

The Eisenstein covering radius1/sqrt3 and six units give the required
count with the actual periodic residue weights. Nonprincipal c_psi=0;
the principal density has factor pi/(3sqrt3). The ideal count O(X)
pays the entire Gaussian estimate, while the error gives the required
polynomial continuation in Re(s)>1/2. The same theorem follows for
gamma>1/2, separately for EACH fixed member. No angular or growing-
conductor uniformity and no unsupported ordinary-to-Hecke transfer
is asserted.

For the literal f3 field, its actual Dirichlet series is B(s)/zeta(s),
where

    B(s)=(1-2^(1-s))H(s),
    H(s)=(1-2^-s)^-2(1-3^-s)^-2
          product_(p>=5)(1-2p^-s)/(1-p^-s)^2.

H and its inverse are bounded on each Re(s)>=b>1/2. The zeros of B
on Re(s)=1 are retained. The Mellin return excludes zeta zeros in
gamma<Re(s)<1; the known zero-free edge completes that return. The
zeta reciprocal and B replenish the complex bound in the required
order. This f3 conclusion concerns zeta; the ordinary and Hecke fields
need their OWN hypotheses.

The complete f3 square moment, full pointwise field and local-set
condition have the same exponent through Mellin continuation and
dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz with the paid left tail. This is not an arbitrary
L2-to-supremum estimate. The new exact target is

    OPEN-F3-VALLEY(gamma,kappa): [research revision]-V1 for the complete f3 field,
    1/2<gamma<.874865 and fixed 0<=kappa<1/2.                 ([research revision]-V2)

The strict numerical boundary here is CURRENT c4. Historical .874872
examples in the frozen W39 source are not represented as current gains.
Near gains, gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 remain possible conditional targets.
The W21 smooth-bump countermodel lacks this entire-Gaussian structure;
the W38 sparse-bad-interval countermodel fails the EVERY-interval
hypothesis. Both older failures remain correct in their stated scopes.

## 3. Other reviewed W39 developments

The selected C04 one-path importance sampler has optimum variance
V^2-|Z|^2, attained by probabilities proportional to the absolute
weights. For the actual ordinary Gaussian,
V=d_q exp(tau/2)exp(y)+O(exp(y/2)), where
d_q=zeta(2)^-1 product_(p|q)p/(p+1). Conditional on a desired small
mean of exponent gamma<1, an independent sample mean needs order
exp(2(1-gamma)y) samples for comparable RMS error. This is limited to
that estimator, not all algorithms, arithmetic grouping or control variates.

C01 preserves the signed tensor boundary. The exact rank is the number
of distinct nonzero row-prefix counts; distinct Gaussian logs give full
exponential-matrix rank. The analytic rank-r approximation has paid
error C(w)exp(Z)Z^r/r! times BOTH weighted coefficient l1 masses,
Z=UV/tau, with the corresponding operator l2 bound. On O(sqrt(log X))
bins, r=C3 log X can pay any prescribed fixed negative power for the
stated finite exponential masses. Actual signed growing-degree
contractions and the complete cross-Gram remain open. Sol wave01 A34
and W35 ancestry are credited; this adds no paid arithmetic sector.

F05's natural divisor normal operator squares conditioning; it does
not rule out every Hodge construction. D02's translated Gram determinant
misses a rank-one dangerous exponential; the two-mode/coalescing formula
requires nonzero amplitudes, distinct shifts and positive weighted
variance. B05's mask defect is 2Re(U,V)+||V||^2 and needs a LOWER bound
to inherit an upper estimate; its two-label Gaussian test is scoped.
The independent C05 heat audit preserves boundary flux; the raw kernel
adds E/tau to the normalized energy identity. A dangerous exponential
restores the old growth term. These are precise reopening conditions,
not blanket rejections of related methods.

## 4. Sampling, scope and evidence

All30 seeds froze at21:34:55UTC before portfolio history at21:35:01.
Pools froze AFTER history/deduplication, before draws and development.
Six first tests were A02,C04,F05,D02,C01,B05. Literal all-group rarity
eligibility was preserved, with base pool sizes23 and14. The critic's
protected E03 and uniform C05 were frozen before outcomes. E03 overlaps
the A02 proof; it is not a seventh author test or an extra discovery.
The [[research revision] index](../[restricted mathematical source] research revision].md) retains every card and its
individual independent disposition. Both author and critic froze,
read back and stopped; only their own claims were released.

| Author report | 38739 | df8115dede9dd0f06fcf5d3146ef71823800008f99d77450713fe9fdeb1ebab9 |
| Author manifest | 2823 | c838ac105f9a7f793b407834f387c0e4a7b9e966fb08d1b069e5b7dd6e8d7ce6 |
| Independent report | 39606 | 2065f4f1495b7dba146392b340673424e66e1187bdb758489616aed0ac482ef7 |
| Independent freeze | 4183 | 2b151382cf16029d66f55e539ebc5120ac3eb00b5052ac3f2b100ec4d1ca2ba6 |

Immutable mathematical source bindings matched. Mutable proof/index
observations changed as c4 and H were integrated, and are explicitly
identified in the controller receipt. The independent finite evidence
replay matches after removing only timestamps and those source
observations; full-byte equality of changing evidence is not claimed.
Analytic acceptance comes from the complete written arguments. No

## 3. Trying a signed repair that annihilates the leading mean

Taking absolute values was the proposed norm improvement; theoremA defeats
it even after exact integer coalescence. A more plausible repair gives the
residual a signed quotient profile chosen to cancel the leading mean.
Here that construction can be tested completely rather than guessed.

Let g(v)=(v-1)^3*(2-v)^3 on [1,2] and0 elsewhere, and set

    h(v)=v^2*g'(v),
    m0=integral_1^2 h(v)/v^2 dv=0,
    m1=integral_1^2 h(v)*log(v)/v^2 dv
         =-integral_1^2 g(v)/v dv <0.                    (6)

The extension g is C^2; h is C^1 with h(1)=h(2)=0 and |h|<=3/4.
This is an actual signed profile with its complete leading mean removed.
At each integer N prescribe the residual

    Delta_N(m,p)=1_(P<p<=2P)*h(m/p^r),
    Delta_N(N,1)=0,

and zero at all other states. It vanishes on the entire exact collar
m<=p^r. The finite recurrence

    F_N(m,y)=1-sum_(y<ell<=m,ell prime)
                    chi0(ell)F_N(floor(m/ell),ell)+Delta_N(m,y)          (7)

constructs the approximation and its defect, with all child states smaller
than m. Set Delta=0 unless y is a prime or the root as above. This defines
F_N without using an unknown value of M in its construction. Its exact
collar values are the genuine rough sums, not an imposed constant1.
The root error is the full G92 scalar, with no complementary residual.

THEOREM B. Fix u>3 with omega''(u)!=0, P=N^(1/(u+r+1)), and fixed q,r.
For (7), the exact signed root error satisfies

    F_N(N,1)-M_chi0(N)
      ~ (q/phi(q))*m1*omega''(u)*kappa_r
                         *N*P^(-r)/(log P)^4.            (8)

Thus the leading cancellation in (6) earns one logarithm but no fixed
power. For any gamma<1 choose a sufficiently large fixed u with omega''(u)
nonzero and (u+1)/(u+r+1)>gamma. Then this bounded, signed, exact-collar
residual has root error larger than N^gamma. This is a fully induced
defect calculation, not just a formal subtraction from a bound.

Proof. Put L=log p, A=N/p^(r+1), u_p=log A/log p, and v_m=m/p^r.
Let S_m=W_q(N/(pm),p-). Exactly C_m=-(S_m-S_(m+1)). Because h vanishes
at the endpoints and outside [1,2], discrete summation by parts gives

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=-sum_m S_m*(h(v_m)-h(v_(m-1))).     (9)

There are no omitted terms at either sharp support endpoint. Apply (2)
with K=2 uniformly on v in [1,2], using a fixed compact near u>3:

    S_m=A/v_m*[ b1*omega'(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^2
                +b2*omega''(u_p-log(v_m)/L)/L^3]
                          +O_(q,r,u)(A/L^4).

The total variation of the fixed h is bounded, so the remainder stays
O(A/L^4) in (9), rather than being multiplied by the number of m. Replacing
the main smooth sum by its integral has error O(A/(p^r*L^2)), which is
smaller. Taylor expansion and integration by parts give

    integral h'(v)/v dv=m0=0,
    integral h'(v)*log(v)/v dv=m1-m0=m1.

Hence the COMPLETE prime block is

    sum_m C_m*h(v_m)=b1*m1*omega''(u_p)*A/L^3
                 +O(A/L^4+A/(p^r*L^2)).                 (10)

The b2 term also vanishes by m0=0; no value or sign of b2 is needed.
Now u_p=u+O(1/log P), and PNT sums (10) over the entire prime band to
give (8). The principal natural zeros were already included in (2).

To justify arbitrarily large u with omega''(u)!=0, if omega'' vanished
on a tail then omega would be affine there. Substitution into
u*omega'=omega(u-1)-omega(u) forces its slope to vanish. The constant-tail
contradiction from theoremA applies. Thus the theorem is nonvacuous beyond
every prescribed target threshold, without a floating-point derivative
test or a conjecture about oscillations.

This construction is root-adapted through P and N, as the independent
error-norm question allows. It is an obstruction for a fixed-shape
annihilation certificate, not a claim that all source residuals are free
to vary this way. Its recurrence is finite but no economy of computing
the exact collar is asserted.

## 3. B1–6: actual occupations and the complete unexposed covariance

Let P be any finite prime set containing2 and excluding3, Q=product P,
a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)), and r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n).
The identity f=a_P r_P is pointwise. Both factors retain all valuations;
r_P consists of exactly the primes outside P other than3. The complete
period mean of a_P is product(1-2/p)=0. No squarefree probability law
is used.

For any Q-periodic a of mean0 and |a|<=1, let its discrete Fourier
coefficients be b_k, k=1,...,Q-1. They satisfy |b_k|<=1. With
h(t)=g_tau(log t), zero-extended to t<=0, ordinary Poisson and m>=2
integrations by parts give

    |sum_n a(n)h(n/x)|
       <=2 zeta(m)(Q/(2pi))^m x^(1-m)||h^(m)||_1.       (R41-B1)

Indeed the reindexing r=Qj-k is one-to-one over nonzero integers not
divisible by Q. Its absolute m-series is bounded by2zeta(m); there is
no lost extra factor Q. Flatness of h at0 pays every boundary term.
This is a direct periodic-source calculation, not a masked application
of a completed alternating field.

For fixed0<delta<1 and Q<=X^(1-delta), even one fixed sufficiently large
m proves any prescribed negative power uniformly on [X,2X]. The stronger
displayed bound with m=2+floor(delta log X/tau) is also valid, because
the *explicit* G7 contract bounds its growing derivative order:

    ||h^(m)||_1<=K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau(m-1)^2/2).

Substitution bounds the logarithm by
-delta^2(log X)^2/(2tau)+O_(delta,tau)(log X loglog X).
Constants are independent of the actual list P, but depend on the fixed
delta and tau. Thus F_P=sum a_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x)) is O_A(X^-A) for every
fixed A. Shrinking delta with X or changing tau is not part of the theorem.

Put Z=sum g_tau(log(n/x))=exp(tau/2)x+O_A(x^-A), by period1 Poisson,
and use the actual positive all-integer measure mu_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/x))/Z.
Each prime-occupation pattern indicator is Q-periodic, with CRT mean

    pi_P(s)=product_(s_p=1)1/p *product_(s_p=0)(1-1/p).

Apply R41-B1 to indicator-minus-mean, of absolute size at most1. The
normalization is exact: its Gaussian sum divided by Z is the difference
between actual pattern probability and pi_P(s). Summing over all patterns
costs at most2^|P|<=Q<=X. Increasing the prescribed negative power once
pays this factor, so the full L1 pattern error is O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A),
uniformly over the full shell and every permitted P. No rare pattern was
discarded and no division by a possibly tiny individual pi_P(s) was used.
This is an absolute joint-law error, not a relative conditional-law estimate.

W38 used a squarefree Gaussian measure, giving occupation1/(p+1) and a
logarithmic partial-parity bias. W41's measure is on all integers, giving
1/p and the prime-two zero mean. Both statements are valid at their
different sources; W41 does not repair or disprove W38's result.

Define the explicit bilinear covariance

    C_P=E[a_P r_P]-E[a_P]E[r_P].

Then, without approximation,

    F=Z C_P+F_P E[r_P].                                  (R41-B2)

Since |E r_P|<=1 and Z is comparable to X throughout the shell, for any
chosen permitted family P_X the complete field estimate is equivalent to

    integral_X^(2X)|C_(P_X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                       <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon). (R41-B3)

Both directions follow from the norm triangle with the uniform rapidly
small F_P error; the gamma>.5 restriction is needed for the existing
zero return, not for this elementary covariance identity. Keeping P={2}
already yields the equivalence. For example, with p_j=Pr(1_(2|n)=j) and
m_j=E[r_{2}|1_(2|n)=j], direct expansion gives
C_{2}=2p0p1(m0-m1). The exposed even/odd probabilities are close to1/2;
their *conditional rough means* still carry the full problem.

More generally, m_P(s)=E[r_P|s] satisfies

    C_P=sum_s Pr(s)(a_P(s)-E[a_P])m_P(s).                (R41-B4)

All these conditional means and signed interactions remain. The accurate
unconditional product law bounds none of their needed cancellation.
For a fixed ordinary chi replace r_P by chi r_P, including zero values.
The positive law stays unchanged, the explicitly bilinear formula stays
valid, |r|<=1 still pays the error, and R41-A9 supplies the exact return.
No character independence, pair-mask domination or ideal-norm transfer
is implied. The covariance target uses the fixed F for Mellin continuation,
not the moving periodic field.

**Attribution correction:** [research revision] gaussian-signed S24–29 already derives
the all-valuation prime-divisibility product, its mean zero at2, and rapidly
small periodic Gaussian remainder in a priced radical/ray range. More
directly, post52 Sol D33.1–5 has the same finite-prime f3 field, the same
Fourier reindexing, a growing period, and the exact full rough correction
whose exponent bound is equivalent to F's. That independent batch and
its Sol/Astra reviews were frozen before this W41 final review. D33's
formula R41-B1 already implies arbitrary Q<=X^(1-delta), even though its
worked sieve is z_X=a log X/loglog X. Therefore general-Q cancellation is
an explicit extension of presentation, not a new analytic mechanism.
W41's all-pattern L1 statement and normalized conditional covariance are
useful refinements of that same source contract. The covariance is a
reorganization of the full rough correction, not a weaker estimate.

The author correctly credits W34/W35 Poisson and W38's different law, but
its phrase “distinct f3 consequence” needs the [research revision]/D33 qualification.
This is a record-relative mathematical deduplication. It does not assert
that the author saw an unavailable contemporary packet, copied it, or
violated fresh generation. External literature priority is not assessed.

Fix a bounded-overlap dyadic partition q_a~A before live labels, and write L_A=A^6N0^2/U. Each copy has at most O(H_J N0 U^epsilon) original inverse/slot tuples by ideal counting. The two central roots and the primitive Poisson factor together are O(U/(q_a^6 N0^2)) on their original supports. Primitive Gauss factors have modulus one; masks can only reduce this absolute bound. Thus the genuine coprime sector, for q_ell~H, satisfies

    |R_(A,H)| <= sum |genuine source terms in that dyad|
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) A^(-5) H
                    [1+H/L_A]^(-B).                  (R20)

This uses O(A) possible a and O(H) frequencies. It keeps the full kernel, every original mask and both heights; no mutual-gcd extension or common Fourier separation is used in this tail bound. All derivative orders and raw-factor powers are fixed before choosing B.

For fixed tau>0, summing the dyadic frequencies H>U^tau L_A in (R20) costs at most

    H_J U^epsilon A N0^2 U^(-tau(B-1)).               (R21)

Here L_A>>1 throughout the actual box, so no small-radius lattice term is missing. Summing A<<U^(1/6), and using r+s<47/20 and v<=1/20, bounds all these tails by

    H_J U^(149/30+epsilon-tau(B-1)).                   (R22)

## 2. Independent development: cofactor-resolved residual transfer

For squarefree a,b in S put g=(a,b), l=[a,b], and define the literal cofactor sum

    M_{chi,lq}(y)=sum_{m<=y,(m,lq)=1} mu(m)chi(m).

Writing d=lm in (1), squarefreeness forces (m,l)=1. Since mu(a)mu(b)mu(l)=mu(g), exact complete entries are

    (A_chi^{-1})_ab = mu(g)chi(l) M_{chi,lq}(N/l).             (3)

The right side is zero when l>N. In particular the entire first row is

    R_chi,N(a)=chi(a) M_{chi,aq}(N/a),     |R_chi,N(a)|<=N/a.  (4)

This is an identity for finite coprimality masks, not a claim of uniform estimates for growing-conductor L-functions. Large labels are short cofactor sums; small labels can retain the original hard arithmetic.

For any proposed approximate column z on S, with its COMPLETE residual r=e_1-A_chi z, the exact reconstruction is

    M_chi(N)=z_1 + sum_{a in S} R_chi,N(a) r_a,
    |M_chi(N)-z_1| <= N sum_{a in S} |r_a|/a.                 (5)

No projection or residual coordinate can be omitted. If r is supported on a>N/H, H>=1, (5) is at most H||r||_1. Thus a full global inverse norm is an unnecessarily expensive default bill for residuals concentrated at large labels. The stronger exact signed residual sum in (5) remains available; its absolute majorant is only a sufficient certificate.

A precise sufficient open input is: for every fixed ordinary chi, every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large integer N, construct z=z_{chi,N,epsilon} on the ACTUAL S such that

    |z_1| + N sum_{a in S} |(e_1-A_chi z)_a|/a
       <<_{chi,epsilon} N^{gamma+epsilon}.                  OPEN-RES

This implies the pointwise Mertens bound and the same all-height zero exclusion as above. First improvement requires gamma<.8748540364; gamma=5/6 and gamma=3/4 are the conditional 1/6 and 1/4 targets. No vector satisfying this budget is constructed. An algorithm computing the exact inverse is not evidence that its observed coordinate is small. The criterion remains hard even though its residual payment is more precise.

The cheapest candidate demonstrates the danger. Set

    z_T=E^{-T}(chi(d) 1_{d<=T})_{d in S},   1<=T<=N.

Then z_T,1=M_chi(T) and

    r_T(a)=1_{a=1}-sum_{d|a,d<=T}mu(d)
          =sum_{d|a,d>T}mu(d).                               (6)

Residual support is indeed confined to a>T. But for T<=N/2 and primes p in (N/2,N] not dividing q, r_T(p)=-1 and R_chi,N(p)=chi(p). Therefore

    sum_a |R_chi,N(a)r_T(a)| >= #{N/2<p<=N : p does not divide q}
                               ~ N/(2 log N).               (7)

The weaker explicit budget in (5) is at least as large. The ordinary prime number theorem suffices; only finitely many excluded primes divide fixed q. [DLMF 27.12.4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12) records this classical asymptotic. The same conclusion holds for a cutoff <=beta N with any fixed beta<1 after shortening the prime interval. Equation (7) is an absolute-price obstruction for this specified truncation, NOT a lower bound for the signed residual, M_chi, or a general certificate. This preserves the real opportunity: construct a residual aligned with the actual signs, or eliminate the prime residual through a new complete arithmetic correction while paying every new coordinate.

Six finite exact matrix cases, q=1 and the quartic character modulo 5 at N=2,12,24, independently verify the literal displayed convention, (3), and (6)'s reconstruction for T=1,floor(N/2),N. Arithmetic values are small Gaussian integers, exactly represented; the algebra above supplies the general proof. No unchanged author diagnostic was rerun.

This is an analytic source review, not certification by that finite helper. The secondary G90 numeric example and all older ancestry arguments are retained as scoped author evidence rather than represented as freshly re-proved in this short turn.

## Exact coefficient and valuation audit

For J=[U^eta,U^(2eta)), the ordered pair weight is sum_{p,q in J,pq|b} logNp logNq/(logNb)^2. At p=q it requires v_p(b)>=2 and counts that pair ONCE, regardless of higher valuation. Expanding the square of the radical logarithm removes precisely the v_p(b)=1 diagonal. Hence the author's (8) is exact. Since J is disjoint from the old closed band, omega<=ell_J(b)^2/(logNb)^2<=(1-theta)^2<=1-theta. This is a coefficient inequality only.

For every extracted L and d=pq, put h=d/gcd(d,L). At each prime the remaining divisibility requirement is max(v_p(d)-v_p(L),0), so d|Lc iff h|c. Substituting c=h c' preserves all remaining valuations and gives the exact phase phi(h), normalization (Nh)^(-1/2), and length E/Nh. It does not divide by a character. If p=q, h=p^2,p,1 for v_p(L)=0,1,>=2. If p!=q, h contains exactly the missing primes. Natural zeros are multiplicative through this substitution, even when primes occur simultaneously in L, the inverse puncture and the cofactor. The logarithmic profile is exact: NL*Nc=D*(Nc/E). This verifies author (15), including the most dangerous middle valuation.

A useful independent refinement is available without any new analytic input. Write s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=logNp/logD, I=sum_{p|L}w_p, V=sum_{p not|L}w_p(Np)^(-s). The EXACT positive pair mass after the shortened plain estimate is

  A_L=sum_{p,q in J} w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
     =(I+V)^2-sum_{p in J,v_p(L)=1}w_p^2[1-(Np)^(-s)].

Proof: all distinct pairs factor as products of the single-prime weights; their diagonal removal is restored by p^(-2s) when v_p(L)=0, p^(-s) when v_p(L)=1, and1 when v_p(L)>=2. Thus only valuation1 differs from the diagonal of (I+V)^2. This identity includes p=q and every shared-prime equality. In particular A_L<= (I+V)^2; no extra diagonal loss is needed. It is a sharper label-specific absolute block mass, not a signed norm contraction or a new global power saving.

Nonempty support gives NL<=CD, so I<=1+O(1/logD). Ideal counting gives V<<U^epsilon A^((1-beta)/2), A=U^(2eta). Therefore A_L<<U^epsilon A^(1-beta). The original whole profile contributes only its declared common derivative/height envelope. This re-proves the author's uniform (16), and clarifies that its SQUARED cost is A^(2(1-beta))=Y^(1-beta), once.

## Full product, collisions and both gates

For p!=q, dyadic lengths lambda_i<=2eta give total added width<=4eta. The exact product normalization is P1^(-1/2)P2^(-1/2)E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2). Common profile separation precedes live primes or colors; the arithmetic coefficients logNp/logU stay fixed when D is differentiated. G137 gives r+2v<=1-.01017 before losses. Thus r+2(v+lambda1+lambda2)<=1-.00217 at eta=.001. From 2r+8v<=2-.02034+4v, the second enlarged gate has margin at least .78834=39417/50000. Both margins hold throughout the stated window, including v=0; inverse shortening helps. The enlarged fixed slot count and finite derivative orders must be selected before witnesses, exactly as stated. Neither MP nor arbitrary merged-column coefficients are substituted.

When a distinct new prime equals an old slot prime, that old slot is removed and its actual normalizers have bounded absolute dyadic mass: the two prime scales are comparable and there are O(P) ideals at scale P against normalization O(P^-1). The plain shortening still yields the full (P1P2)^(-beta/2). Two new distinct primes cannot both equal the same old prime, since the old slots have disjoint supports. All remaining equality exclusions can be imposed in the row-independent pools at each fixed extracted term. The extracted phi(p)^2 is a positive-norm contraction, with zeros retained; the inverse is not declared coprime to p.

On the surviving all-distinct variables, h^h times the NORMALIZED random-color expectation is exactly the indicator that all h prime IDEALS differ. Thus the coloring cost is a fixed constant, not a growing count. The zero-slot case uses the empty product directly. Equal-norm distinct ideals must remain distinct labels; the helper checks this particular issue.

For p=q, retaining the complete old Q and inverse before extracting the phase gives norm mass sum_p (Np)^(-1-beta) times bounded logarithmic coefficients. Its dyadic sum is O(P^-beta). Squaring yields Z^-2beta, including p=q equal to an old slot prime. The off-diagonal gives (P1P2)^-beta<=Z^-2beta as well. Summing finite patterns and logarithmically many dyads by Hilbert triangle proves the full product estimate (14), without signed subset monotonicity.

## Full removed source and complementary signal

G198's complete blocks have L=lcm(q0,k^2), not q0*k^2 when primes overlap. Their absolute coefficient mass after the shortened plain bound and every q0-smooth inverse restoration is T^-beta/2 U^epsilon. Band prime squares remain excluded; lower-band squares are included and were paid above. Pure large-prime plain columns paired with coprime squarefree inverse tuples still have F=1 and theta=omega=0. This is an actual coefficient example, not evidence of any high-zero row or lower bound. The three-coordinate separation factors the original witness twist first, leaving a height-free smooth kernel. Its Fourier measure is fixed before rows, extracted primes or coloring. ## 5. Moving finite twists, natural zeros, and masked Möbius sums

Insert the finite unit-neutral projector. For each dual ideal
`mathfrak n` and unit component `u0`,
\[
\eta(\lambda u_0)\bar\eta(\mathfrak n)
=\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
 \overline{\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(e)},
\qquad
\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(c)
=\vartheta_c(\lambda u_0)
 \overline{\vartheta_c(\mathfrak n)}.
\tag{BC12}
\]
Cubic reciprocity makes this a finite-order character in the good core
variable. Its primitive good conductor consists of the primes for
which `v_p(mathfrak n)` is nonzero modulo three, hence has norm at
most `q_mathfrak_n`.

**Primes dividing `mathfrak n` to a multiple of three still impose
natural zeros.** They remain finite deletions even when absent from
the primitive conductor. The supplementary twist at `lambda u0` has
fixed conductor. Arbitrary fixed-S valuations of the dual ideal do
not create a moving good conductor.

Let `h=1/2-z`. I-HECKE gives
\[
\sum_{\substack{m\\(m,M)=1}}
\mu(m)\chi_{\mathfrak n,u_0}(m)q_m^hF(q_m/U)
\ll
(q_{\mathfrak n}q_M)^\delta T^A
U^{b+\Re h+\delta}\mathcal S(F).
\tag{BC13}
\]
Here `S(F)` uses finitely many Euler derivatives on a fixed norm
annulus. The reciprocal series is `1/L^S(s,chi*)` with the additional
deleted Euler factors required by `M` and the natural zeros at
`rad(mathfrak n)`. Unramified deleted primes contribute factors
`(1-chi*(p)q_p^(-s))^(-1)`, bounded by a subpower of the deletion
norm on the fixed line `b>0`. The primitive reciprocal costs a
subpower of its actual conductor and height by I-HECKE. Buffered
Perron bounds and partial summation also permit a sharp interval
endpoint. All preliminary losses can be decreased independently.

No subpower bound for a moving angular L-function is used. The only
moving reciprocal functions in (BC13) have finite order.

## 2. New exact conductor geometry

Fix an original ordered long-prime pair. Set M=pi*pi', Q=q_M asy N^2. Fold the ENTIRE actual short-source sum and its complete bounded core into W(R,P,P'). It includes both projector indicators and all retained profile/component coefficients; it may depend on the prime pair. Its row support is inside the original O(K)-point disk, and the two mark supports have O(L) points. The original support injects modulo each long prime for sufficiently large Z in the pressure box. These properties survive the signed short-source recombination.

The accepted exact JN4--JN9 transform, with both character inversions and their Gauss factors, has native kernel

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4

times b(pi) conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi'), where b retains alpha and fixed ray data and the exact CRT root zeta is not set to one. The finite group is (O/M) x (O/pi) x (O/pi'), with Q^2 elements; its unitary transform has factor 1/Q and phases -Rh/M -Ps/pi +P's'/pi'. This already accounts for the two local 1/q factors. No new physical factor arises.

The kernel is zero unless

    U = {(h,M)=1, s nonzero mod pi, s' nonzero mod pi'}.

Choose integral representatives in bounded fundamental parallelograms, so q_h<=C Q and q_s,q_s'<=C N. For each nonzero h let a2(h) be the product of GOOD prime ideals at which v(h) is odd. For nonzero s let a3(s) be the product of good prime ideals at which v(s) is nonzero modulo 3. These are ideal products; neither integer squarefree kernels nor rational norms are factored in their place.

By JN17/JNR5 the first prime-variable good local exponent is 3v(h)+2v(s) modulo 6 and the second is 3v(h)+4v(s') modulo 6. The exact elementary equivalences are

    3A+2B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3),
    3A+4B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3).

Consequently the two GOOD primitive finite conductor ideals are exactly

    f1_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)),
    f2_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')).                         ([research revision].1)

In particular a2(h) divides both. A cubic mark factor cannot cancel the quadratic row factor, even at a shared good prime. At canceled conductor primes the original natural zero of the imprimitive character remains; ([research revision].1) does not turn it into an unrestricted constant. Fixed bad-place and angular data are retained separately. This is not an ordinary-Hecke prime-sum estimate.

Each conductor declaration freezes the chosen integral indices and takes the reciprocal finite-kernel character in that prime variable. The pair-dependent Fourier coefficient still samples h/(pi*pi'), s/pi and s'/pi'. Nothing here supplies a common prime-independent weight after regrouping by conductor; the original angular alpha factor also remains.

Let a frequency selector, allowed to depend on h,s,s', the prime pair and all coefficients, retain only points of U where AT LEAST ONE of q_f1_good or q_f2_good is <=D. It is pointwise contained in

    E_D x (O/pi) x (O/pi'),
    E_D={h !=0: q_a2(h)<=D}.                          ([research revision].2)

This containment, rather than commutation of the adaptive selector itself, is what permits the row-only uncertainty bound.

Here D denotes a conductor cutoff only; it is not the mark-collision divisor D in JSR11, or the Type I factor length D in SF2. No D*Omega factor from those different variables has been dropped. Their roots and complete projectors are inside the actual tensor before this Fourier statement is applied.

For 1<=D<=C Q, write the ideal of a chosen h as a_S*a*b^2, where a is good squarefree, q_a<=D, and a_S ranges over the finitely many squarefree products of fixed bad primes. The ideal class number is one and each principal ideal has six generators, so there are only a fixed number of possible representatives for each factorization. Elementary Eisenstein ideal counting gives

    #E_D <= C_S sum_(q_a<=D) sqrt(Q/q_a)
          <= C_S sqrt(QD).                            ([research revision].3)

The last inequality follows by partial summation from #ideals(q<=x)<=C x. Arbitrary powers at bad primes are already in b^2; their parity contributes only the finite a_S choice. For D beyond the stated range one uses #E_D<=Q. This estimate is uniform in the orientation of the chosen fundamental cell.

The reviewer sharpens the uniform block calculation. Write

    s=(1+beta)/2, w_p=log N(p)/log D,
    I=sum_(p in J,p|L)w_p,

    A_L=sum_(p,q in J)w_p w_q N(pq/gcd(pq,L))^(-s)
       =(I+V)^2-sum_(p in J,v_p(L)=1)w_p^2[1-N(p)^(-s)]
       <=(I+V)^2.                                  (3)

Distinct pairs factor. On the diagonal, valuation0 contributes p^(-2s),
valuation1 contributes p^(-s), and valuation at least2 contributes1.

(3), including all p=q and shared-prime cases, with no extra diagonal loss.

positive mass, not a new global power saving or signed contraction.

## 4. Development23: full large-prime complement and sharp diameter

Let sqrt(X)<=y<=X, fix low-prime unit phases and zeros at p|q0, and put a_z(n)=mu(n)z(n). Every squarefree n<=X with a prime factor p>y has exactly one such factor, with n=pm and m<=X/p<p. Thus

    M_z(X)=S_y(X)-sum_(y<p<=X,p not dividing q0)z_p A(X/p),
    S_y(X)=sum_(n<=X,P^+(n)<=y)a_z(n),
    A(t)=sum_(m<=t)a_z(m), t<=X/y<=y.                 (R7)

The cofactor is determined entirely by the low phases. There is no missing gcd(m,p) restriction, because m<p, and repeated-prime contributions vanish by mu. Natural zeros remain in A and in the outer exclusion.

Set R_y(X)=sum_p |A(X/p)|. Choosing each independent z_p to align its whole cofactor gives maximum distance R_y from S_y and diameter2R_y between two compatible sums. These are a radius and a diameter, not a claim that every point of the intervening disk is attainable. If low phases are real signs, A is real; opposite sign choices attain S_y+R_y and S_y-R_y. The preceding CRT proof realizes both by actual real characters, with the same low data and zeros through X.

Grouping by the EXACT integer m=floor(X/p) gives

    R_y(X)=sum_(1<=m<=floor(X/y))|A(m)|
       [pi_q0(X/m)-pi_q0(max(y,X/(m+1)))].            (R8)

The lower endpoint is strict and the upper inclusive; a terminal empty interval contributes zero. When y<=X/2, A(1)=1 gives R_y>=pi_q0(X)-pi_q0(X/2). For fixed q0, ordinary PNT makes this (1/2+o(1))X/log X. I checked the ordinary prime asymptotic in [NIST DLMF 27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no progression uniformity or improved zero-free input is used. The exact identities and prime-count inequality require no PNT.

This is a genuine obstruction to a CONDUCTOR-INDEPENDENT, phase-blind small-prime certificate that claims a uniformly sublinear complement. It is not an obstruction for one fixed chi as X tends to infinity.

The reported fixed-modulus escape is proved: characters modulo a fixed q that agree on every unramified prime<=q agree on every unit residue. Factor its least positive representative r<=q into such primes; nonunit values are already zero. Hence y>=q removes the apparent freedom in the tail. For y=sqrt X this holds once X>=q^2. The adversarial pair uses changing, generally different moduli, precisely where that argument is unavailable.

The whole smooth complement, every cofactor and all pairwise interactions in a later energy remain. The geometric radius is no estimate of the actual fixed-character signed sum. The useful next input must exploit the fixed modulus's global linkage, rather than treat its large-prime values as independent phases.

## 2. Independent reconstruction of the author's deletion and parity claims

Let D_X={n<=X:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}, including1, for fixed q and real X>=1. Let k(n)=omega(n), K_X=max_D k(n), 0<rho<=1, lambda=1-rho and R=(2-rho)/rho. Retain zero outside D_X. The channel and inverse, with ROW d and COLUMN n, are

 B(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^k(d) lambda^(k(n)-k(d)),
 C(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).                 (1)

For C B, the intermediate e contributes rho^(-k(e))*rho^k(e); the remaining sum over e/d is (lambda-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)). For B C the analogous cancellation has the remaining rho^(k(d)-k(n)), which equals1 on the diagonal. Every intermediate divisor belongs to D_X. Thus BOTH products are the identity, with the endpoint rho=1 interpreted by0^0=1. Column sums give exactly ||B||_1=1 and ||C||_1=R^K_X.

Since the product of k distinct primes is at least(k+1)!, K_X<=(1+o(1))log X/loglog X. Fixed rho therefore costs X^o(1). This is the actual size-downset operator, not a full prime cube of dimension2^pi(X); charging exp(c*pi(X)) would be wrong. Conversely rho_X=(log X)^(-b), b>0, has R^K_X=X^(b+o(1)), using K_X~log X/loglog X from primorials and ordinary PNT. The asymptotic prime facts are verified in [DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12), specifically27.12.1 and27.12.4-5. No progression, GRH or growing-q estimate is imported.

The actual input is nu(n)=chi(n) on D_X, not mu(n)chi(n). Its output is

 b_X(d)=rho^k(d)chi(d) sum_(m<=X/d,(m,dq)=1) mu(m)^2 chi(m)lambda^k(m).              (2)

The erased character phase and coprimality are forced, not optional. The observer h(d)=(-R)^k(d) satisfies sum_(d|n)h(d)B(d,n)=(-1)^k(n), since lambda-rho R=-1 at every prime. Hence <h,b_X>=M_chi(X), with ordinary bilinear evaluation, NO conjugation. The complete residual inequality is

 |M_chi(X)| <= |<h,btilde_X>| + R^K_X ||b_X-btilde_X||_1.                          (3)

Every-epsilon bounds on both terms at a common gamma give the full Mertens exponent for all real X and each fixed chi. A selected label set, nonprincipal phase deletion, or omitted approximation error invalidates this return. The construction supplies no such approximation.

Compressing by k(d) gives P_X(z)=Z_X(lambda+rho z), Z_X(z)=sum_D chi(n)z^k(n). This is an EXACT cutoff polynomial; the unrestricted finite Euler product contains products exceeding X and needs its size projection. Evaluation P_X(-R)=M_chi(X) and circle Parseval give |P_X(-R)|<=sqrt(sum_(j<=K)R^(2j)) ||P_X||_circle. At fixed rho the evaluation cost is subpower, but the required whole-circle estimate fails for the actual principal source.

Indeed principal coefficients beta_j are nonnegative and primes contribute lambda+rho z, so beta_0+beta_1>=pi_q(X) for every retention schedule. Thus ||P_X||_circle>=pi_q(X)/sqrt2. Removing all original degrees<=r, fixed integer r>=0, still leaves at least c_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1) products of r+1 distinct primes in((X/2)^(1/(r+1)),X^(1/(r+1))]. Each contributes a nonnegative degree-(r+1) coefficient vector of total mass1. Their sum has l2 norm at least its mass/sqrt(r+2). Remaining original layers add nonnegative coefficients. This verifies the author's lower bound uniformly even for X-dependent rho. It is a norm lower bound, NOT a lower bound for its alternating evaluation, not a rejection of growing signed deflation, and not a refutation of G106's exact quotient.

For fixed0<rho<1, cofactor primes give b_X(d)>>X/log X at every fixed label d. This particular lower bound excludes rho=1; the full observer norm is still due there.

### F04.N2 — New pass 1: core-frame calibration and exact mark cumulants

T06 supplies a useful normalization absent from the earlier raw-Gram proposals. On a finite truncation let \(d_c=\|S_c\|_2\) and
\(\Gamma_{c,c'}=\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle/(d_cd_{c'})\) for nonzero entries. The full target is a bound on the **actual weighted direction** \(d^*\Gamma d\), not an arbitrary-vector spectral bound. Pairing the physical field with the theta witness may require still less than this energy. Compute an independently defined residual subspace of \(\Gamma\) only after its coefficient vectors and principal calibration are explicit.

A complementary arithmetic test centers two actual mark slots *inside* the common Euler identity. The second cumulant must retain \(f_s-f_s^2\), cross-slot collisions and all addback terms. One may seek cancellation in the centered block while pricing its lower moments by T06/T07. An apparent saving that simply drops an addback carrying the original signal fails. This differs from the supplied primewise tail proof: the proposed averaging is across two slots and the remaining small-gcd cofactors simultaneously. First output: a two-slot identity and its full norm/principal terms, then an aggregate estimate. Neither the normalized frame nor the cumulant identity supplies cancellation by itself.

## 5. The changed unconditioned density

With q=delta and K fixed as above, replace only the plain line by

    P_K(m)=1-2delta m+delta[v-(1-2m)/K]_+.

On the full-fit branch the short crossing is r=2t/3 and t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta). On the partial branch, solving I=P_K gives

    r=[(2K-2)t+1-Kv]/(3K-2).

Balancing against L(t) yields

    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    t=[15K-10-6delta-12delta(K-1)v]/D_K.

The seven source gates cover all delta in [.68,.70], K in [Knew,9/2] and v in [0,1/20]. The full-fit cutoff is also within the witness range, and its kink inequality is the q=delta case already checked. The exact switch is e/[3K(5-2delta)-12delta]. These facts prove, without a sampled extrapolation,

    sum_high |Q_u|^2 << Z^[rho W+delta z-G_K(W,z)+epsilon] H_J,
    G_K(W,z)=min(3kz,a_K W+b_K z),
    a_K=delta e^2/[3(5-2delta)D_K],
    b_K=2delta e(K-1)/D_K,
    k=rho+delta-1.

At K=9/2 these are exactly the accepted coefficients. Clearing both denominators gives the independently verified identity, when the affine branches are active,

    G_K(W,z)-G_(9/2)(W,z)
      =delta e^2(9/2-K)(W-2z)/(D_K D_(9/2)).

It is positive in the relevant empty-support range. No strict gain is asserted when the min instead selects 3kz. The same raw-root proof applies because a_K<1/500 and G_K<=3kz. The theorem is unconditioned on amplitude deficits and therefore independent of the unresolved part of Section 4.

### 1.3 Signed large-core tail, including its lower boundary

Put R=floor(X^delta). For any y>0, integration by parts using (R1.2)
gives

    |sum_(r>R) f(r)g(log(r/y))|
      <= C_beta y^beta Q_beta(log(R/y)),
    Q_beta(v)=exp(beta v)g(v)
                 +integral_v^infinity exp(beta w)|g'(w)|dw. (R1.6)

The first term pays the actual boundary -A_f(R)g(log(R/y)). Q_beta
is bounded for v<=0 and decays faster than every exp(-Bv) for v>=0.
For Y>=1, splitting integers k at Y and then into dyadic intervals,
using sum_(k<=V)d(k)<=C V log(2V), yields

    sum_k d(k)k^(-beta)Q_beta(log(k/Y))
       <= C_beta Y^(1-beta)log(2Y).                   (R1.7)

Apply this with y=x/(pq), k=pq and Y=x/R. Summing (R1.6) over every
actual p<q, and only then majorizing by d(k), bounds the entire removed
core by

    C x R^(beta-1)log(2x/R)=O(X^(1-eta)L).            (R1.8)

This is cancellation of the actual unrestricted f(r) core furnished by
(R1.4)--(R1.5). It is not a bound for an arbitrary smooth or masked core.

## 1. Exact sources and input contract

Internal sources:

- [Main manuscript B0.21--B0.25](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md#b03-the-physical-probe-signed-gram-bound-and-compensator): the actual probe, the \(Y^{-3/2}\) additive source, the outside \(Q^{-1/2}\), the original profiles and the exact finite compensator.
- [T06.1--T06.3 and T06.6](../[research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#t06-the-complete-same-core-sextic-square-function): every embedded branch, the completed coefficient \(q_c^{-1/2}q_n^{-1}\), actual marked weight \(K_D\), and its uniform rapid envelope.
- [PC1--PC5](../[research revision]-continuation/physical-covariance.md): exact prime-power Gauss support, natural zeros, fixed-place factors and primitive character completion.
- [FR3, FR6--FR10 and FR19](../[research revision]/physical-forced-rows.md): interpolation with the actual forced divisor, including principal multiples of six. The current FR file records independent review; this record proves its separate linear application.

External provenance is pinned throughout to CrossNox commit
\[
\texttt{f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db}.
\]

- [gram_mixed.tex, lines 17--31](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): raw source and completed-coefficient conventions.
- [Lines 145--240](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the active/passive split and compact row profile.
- [Lines 287--373](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/[restricted mathematical source]): the all-source Ramanujan identity and the nonsummable sixth-power tail in the unweighted refined count.
- [GramMixedArithmetic.lean](https://github.com/CrossNox/quasi-riemann-hypothesis-extension/blob/f677cc0a820bb2aff86bb4cbe783d076f5c097db/lean/GramMixedArithmetic.lean): the local transform and calibrated complete-mean identities. Its declarations do not assert the analytic block theorem proved below. No Lean rebuild is claimed.

The external identities are used as evidence and are derived in the local calculation below. The new estimate is the combination of that exact single-source reduction with a forced-row weight and its summable squareful-source Euler series.

**I-SEXTIC-XM.** Work over \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\), with the original fixed excluded prime set \(S\), one primary generator for every good ideal, and the original finite unit/ray sectors. Write \(q_a=Na\). At each good prime the residue character has exact order six. Natural zero extensions, including those for positive exponents divisible by six, are retained. The fixed calibration \(\xi\) has fixed conductor, is nonprincipal, and is coprime to every good moving modulus. The original finite ray split puts source/completed reciprocity phases in row-independent coefficients; the only moving row character is \(\chi_A(m)\). All such coefficients have the inherited unit or fixed bounded size.

The source profiles \(W_0,W_1\) are the original smooth positive-annulus profiles; the completed profile is
\[
V(x)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt\pi}\exp(-(\log x)^2/4).
\]
The fixed slot count, fixed profile supports and fixed arithmetic data do not grow with \(Z\). The prime-slot weights are the actual bounded smooth weights, or their inherited divisor-bounded majorants.

**I-POISSON-XM.** Ordinary Poisson summation on the Eisenstein lattice is available for a primitive character of good conductor \(\mathfrak h\), multiplied by this fixed calibration. Its complete zero frequency is zero and its Gauss transform has modulus \(O_S(\sqrt{q_{\mathfrak h}})\). Section 3 gives the resulting row estimate, including subunit row scales. No I-HECKE, I-ZETA, Dedekind nonvanishing or higher moment estimate is used.

All scale parameters in the final probe application are in fixed polynomial ranges, with \(Q_D,Y_D\ge1\). Estimates for individual completed dyads are stated with their own small factors \((YCTNH_0Q)^\eta\), before summing the original infinite profile tails. This avoids treating infinite completed labels as polynomially bounded.

## 6. The already accepted family bound improves the source MP

The dependency is explicit and acyclic:

    original PR9/Gao inputs -> accepted c10 family theorem
      -> original PR9 B3.40 at fixed kappa10
      -> stronger weighted density below -> proposed c11.

PR9 B3.40 assumes 7/10<=kappa<=3/4, beta_*>=51/100 and 2beta_*-1<=kappa. It is uniform over that kappa interval with the original mesh/height/fixed-family order. In the contradiction for c11, accepted c10 gives beta_*<=theta10; hence kappa10=2theta10-1 is allowed. The lower beta_* condition follows whenever a high-bin zero exists. The density coefficient is fixed at kappa10 before any target or witness, not set to the desired unproved c11 value. If one had accepted only an ordinary-character statement without the same Hecke-family supremum bound, this bridge would be unavailable. The accepted frozen review explicitly retains that family return.

Use the original MP with its reduced capacity K=6kappa10 only in the free density proof. Keep inverse amplification, all physical descendant budgets and low/fallback capacity 9/2 unchanged. For general fixed K in [28114053/6250000,9/2], replace the plain line by

    P_K(m)=1-2delta m+delta[v-(1-2m)/K]_+.

Set D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta and

    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)D_K],
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K.

The same inverse and plain crossing argument gives

    G_K(W,z)=min(3k(delta)z, a_K W+b_K z),
    sum_high |Q|^2 << Z^[rho W+delta z-G_K(W,z)+epsilon] H_J. (D6)

The full-mark branch still uses t=(5-6delta v)/(5-2delta), r_b=2t/3. Otherwise

    t=[15K-10-6delta-12delta(K-1)v]/D_K,
    r_b=[(2K-2)t+1-Kv]/(3K-2).

The switch is v=(5-6delta)/[3K(5-2delta)-12delta]. The seven cleared source gates are positive over the FULL box delta in [.68,.70], K in [K_new,4.5], v in [0,.05], certified by 64 rational Bernstein coefficients. In particular t is within [1,3/2], the plain witness is in [0,1/2], the short crossing precedes 1-2v, and a_K<1/500. Four exact polynomial identities check balance, switch and the following gain change. This is not an extrapolation from the endpoint K value.

When both affine branches apply, the gain change is particularly transparent:

    G_K(W,z)-G_(9/2)(W,z)
     =delta(5-6delta)^2 (9/2-K)(W-2z)/(D_K D_(9/2)).     (D7)

It is positive for W>2z and also in the allowed empty-common-support sector W=M-6a. Thus this is a real source improvement there, independent of any conjectural failure of high-bin saturation. Where the min chooses 3kz, there is no gain, and no strict inequality is asserted there. The full nonlinear envelope is always used before deciding its active branch.

The actual threshold, label, anchor, pool, raw-root, height and puncture arguments from Sections 2 and 4 are unchanged; D6 is unconditioned on slot amplitudes. The raw root tail still pays because G_K<=3kz; the main root sum still decays since a_K<1/500. This proves the raw z<=W/21 version required by the actual source.

## A shorter-factor corollary and the actual limits of the estimates

The order (log X)^(1/3) is a convenient first instance, not a structural boundary. The same proof gives the following stronger source-compression corollary. Put f(L)=sqrt(L)/log L and allow all integers

  (2/5) f(L)<=K<=2 f(L), K>=2,                           (N30)

with the identical definitions Y=floor(exp(L/(K-1/2))), V=L/(2K-1), W=V/2. Then the source theorem(N4) and the sector estimates(N25)--(N29) still hold uniformly. Now every balanced Möbius factor lies between exp(c sqrt(L)log L) and exp(C sqrt(L)log L), which are shorter than the first displayed exp(Theta(L^(2/3))) scale.

To verify every changed asymptotic: V,W are comparable to sqrt(L)log L; the leading negative term in(N9) is of order -L(log L)^2, while K V log V=O(L log L), K^2=O(L/(log L)^2), and all tuple counts cost exp(O(L)). Thus the faces and product tails are still smaller than every inverse power. The same holds for(N10). The diagonal and gcd constants cost exp(O_delta(K^2))=X^o(1), derivative and height constants cost exp(O(Klog L))=X^o(1), log N=(1/2+o(1))L, and W/K is comparable to(log L)^2, validating the balanced positive cone. These checks are uniform over the band(N30).

For the future inverse choose K=2ceil(f(log X)/2). Up to t=4log X, the ratio of f(log X) to f(log Z) tends uniformly to at least1/sqrt5>2/5, and the upper band also has a strict margin. Thus the SAME fixed order remains admissible on every future shell, with(N16) unchanged. All later implications hold with(N30) replacing the first band. This is a genuine uniform source theorem with shorter actual factors, but it still does not prove(N28).

The proof used a comfortable gap between L^2/K^2 and L log L. Its general sufficient asymptotic condition is K going to infinity with K^2 log L=o(L), together with a future-compatible order family. Equality or the failure of this sufficient comparison is NOT an impossibility theorem. No claim is made that this rate is optimal, or that an epsilon-loss moment cannot hold at a vanishing reserve. This is separate from every old local-window coefficient boundary.

statement:
## 2. A shift lemma that pays a genuine Type I operator

Suppose a restoration sequence b has bounded partial sums

    B(y)=sum_(ell<=y)b(ell),  B(y)=0 for y<1,
    sup_(y>=0)|B(y)| <= C_b.

Extend h_b(v)=exp(-av)B(exp(v)) by zero for v<0. Then

    ||h_b||_L1(R) <= C_b/a.                            (H2)

For each integer k>=1 the kernel exp(-a(t+u))B(exp(t+u)/k) equals k^-a h_b(t+u-log k). Reflect and zero-extend one input to R, then apply the ordinary L1--L2 convolution inequality. Translation on R costs no norm. Thus its FULL L2(0,L) Hankel norm is at most C_b k^-a/a, independently of L and k. This argument retains all off-diagonal rectangles and uses no derivative or smoothness norm of the test functions.

For A_Y(a)=sum_(d<=Y)|mu(d)chi(d)|d^-a <= C_a Y^(1-a), H2 gives

    ||Gamma[a0*a0*b]_(a,L)|| <= (C_b/a) A_Y(a)^2
                              <<_(a,b) Y^(2(1-a)).   (H3)

This is an actual restricted arithmetic estimate: cancellation in the complete restoration partial sum B precedes absolute summation over the short factors. It is not obtained by replacing b(ell) with its magnitude.

For nonprincipal chi, finite-period orthogonality gives |sum_(n<=y)chi(n)|<=q. Take b=1_chi in H1. A finite atom z(n) contributes a shifted kernel with L1 norm |z(n)|n^-a/a, so

    | ||Gamma[a]_(a,L)|| - ||Gamma[a1*a1*1_chi]_(a,L)|| |
      <= (2/a)A_Y(a)+(q/a)A_Y(a)^2
      <<_(a,q) Y^(2(1-a)).                            (H4)

This directly concerns G149's ORIGINAL mu(n)chi(n) source for every fixed nonprincipal character. It does not assume cancellation in either long factor.

### The actual principal obstruction

Principal characters cannot simply inherit H4. At Y=1 their removed coefficient sequence is 2delta_1-1_chi, with partial sum 2-C_chi(x). Since C_chi(x)=(phi(q)/q)x+O(q), its Hankel operator contains a nonzero rank-one kernel -(phi(q)/q)exp((1-a)(t+u)), plus a uniformly bounded remainder. Its norm is therefore

    (phi(q)/q)(exp(2(1-a)L)-1)/(2(1-a))+O_(a,q)(1).

This is an ACTUAL source term of H1, not a toy kernel imported from elsewhere. A positive budget for that term misses every gamma<1. The full long-factor term may cancel it, so this is not a lower bound on M_chi or the complete source.
title: 2. A shift lemma that pays a genuine Type I operator
