statement:
# [research revision] direct joint-window lane: current worklog



Objective: an actual arithmetic estimate for the original inverse moment on
same-zero large-plain rows near G137's crossing, or a useful proved subcase with
its complement. Current written c11=.1251459636 and licensed density
K=28114053/6250000 remain unchanged; F0, positive-slot uniformity and external
admission remain open. No formalization, new packet, children or provider work.

Completed source intake: [research revision] density and [research revision] same-character/same-zero contract,
G137 and its full joint-window source, literal PR9 B0.17--20 and B3.39--40,
PR15 PlainUnmarkedDensity, and relevant [research revision]/[research revision] duplicate boundaries.
The dyadic witnesses have common character, real power and height; slot heights
remain independent. Full cutoff cancellation does not hold on each dyadic pair.
The mixed convolution is outside the original canonical column contract.

Current survivor: a complete large-gcd inverse/plain estimate uses the SAME
buffered plain bound on every shortened scale, then the fully marked original
MI. A second square-divisor removal pays all its intersections with that gcd
part. This proves the desired inverse saving on an actual proper row subclass;
the complementary near-coprime, nearly squarefree plain source remains open.
Completed: complementary source/failed shortcuts, one exact identity check run,
source pins and full artifact readbacks. Remaining: final freeze, own release
and the reserved independent handoff. No c gain is claimed.

## 1. Literal source and statement

Write U=Z^W and use the original Eisenstein ideals, primary/unit convention,
excluded set S and finite natural character dictionary. One whole orientation
is fixed, phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+/-1), with its actual zeros. The fixed nu
need not have order six. Put R=U^r, D=U^m and

    M_u(R)=R^(-1/2) sum_a mu(a)phi_u(a)W_I(Na/R),
    S_u(D)=D^(-1/2) sum_b phi_u(b)W_P(Nb/D),
    B_u=M_u(R)S_u(D).

The profiles include the original common real power and common witness height.
The original slot product Q_u retains its independent heights, all canonical
pools, every individual coefficient, root/puncture hole and natural zero.
Its total normalized width is v. No pool or profile is changed here.

Fix the physical bin delta in[.68,.70], v in[0,.05], 0<eta<=.001 and the
G137 cutoff t=t_*(delta,v)-eta BEFORE witnesses. After their original
construction, partition by label, internal bin and dyads, and retain the
parts with |r-r_*(t)|<=2eta. The dyads are common within each ensuing norm;
the original moment thresholds are uniform before that partition. G137's certificate
supplies r>1/2, 0<m<=1/2 up to its small allocated tolerances, and

    r+2v <= 1-c_1,       2r+8v <= 3-c_2,                 (1)

with fixed positive reserves (the first exceeds .01017 before fine losses).
We reuse these gates, not another optimization or scalar certificate. The
following estimate in fact holds in any fixed length box satisfying(1).

Omega contains only the original NONPRINCIPAL supported-witness rows. Principal,
artificial and fixed-inducing exceptions are not reclassified into it.
Partition the original rows by their actual internal buffered zero bin and
fixed witness label/dyads. Call one part Omega and its lower squared grade beta.
Here beta>=delta-small, beta<=3/4; the internal maximum can exceed the physical
bin. At the selected common real part/height the literal B0.15/B0.18 bounds give

    |S_u(D)|^2 >= D^beta U^(-epsilon_det),
    |S_u(E)|^2 <= E^beta U^(epsilon_det) H_J,
          0<E<=C D, u in Omega.                         (2)

The second bound uses the direct (unreflected) line in B0.15, so it is valid
even when a small endpoint tolerance makes m slightly exceed1/2. Every E
below is an ACTUAL shortened scale with the SAME character, real power, height
and plain profile. Bounded nonempty subunit E are comparable to a fixed positive
constant and satisfy(2) with a fixed multiplier; smaller E have empty support.
The source buffer/derivative losses may be chosen arbitrarily small BEFORE U.
They will be absorbed in the displayed final epsilon. We never put beta in
place of delta in a physical slot upper price.

Throughout H_J means a finite polynomial (1+T)^J in all retained heights;
the separate symbol H below denotes a square-divisor threshold, not that height.
For a nonnegative original radial weight (or its paid U^epsilon majorant),
write ||F||_Omega^2=sum_(u in Omega) w_u |F_u|^2. Enlarging this set is allowed
only AFTER a pointwise use of(2), inside a positive original MI norm. No
zero-conditioned Poisson formula is asserted. The literal PR9 B0.4/B3.31 gives

    ||M_u(E) Q_u||_(all original rows)^2
          << H_J U^(1+epsilon),        0<E<=C R,          (3)

uniformly over the shortened scales and the required rowwise witness parameters.
Section5 below pays its profile, mask, height and small-scale interfaces.

For ideals b define the integral ideal

    s_2(b)=prod_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2).

Let G,H>=1 be fixed functions of U, chosen before witnesses. Split the literal
ordered (a,b) coefficient sum of B disjointly into

    B_g:       N(a,b)>=G;
    B_s:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)>=H;
    B_c:       N(a,b)<G and N s_2(b)<H.                   (4)

Thus B=B_g+B_s+B_c exactly, with equality placed on the first two sides as
written. These are signed source polynomials, not positive projections.

**Restricted arithmetic theorem.** For fixed positive g,h and G=U^g,H=U^h,
within all the preceding source hypotheses,

    ||B_g Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-beta*g+epsilon),
    ||B_s Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m-2beta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (5)

The common buffer grade is used before weakening to physical delta. Define
the disjoint actual row classes

    Omega_g={u in Omega: |B_g(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_s={u in Omega\Omega_g: |B_s(u)|>=|B(u)|/4},
    Omega_c=Omega\(Omega_g union Omega_s).

Then(2),(5) prove bounds for the ORIGINAL inverse moment, not a substituted
coefficient family:

 sum_(Omega_g) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-delta*g+epsilon),
 sum_(Omega_s) w_u |M_u(R)Q_u|^2 << H_J U^(1-2delta*h+epsilon).
                                                               (6)

On the entire complement,

    |B_c(u)|>|B(u)|/2, u in Omega_c.                     (7)

In particular choose g=4eta,h=2eta. Both proper classes save at least
(68/25)eta before freely chosen losses, hence imply the requested saving eta
there with substantial reserve. This is a genuine source-relative arithmetic
estimate on defined actual rows. It does NOT prove that all rows lie in their
union, or supply J_eta^all on Omega_c. No actual high-zero row or nonempty
dominance class is constructed. Empty common support is allowed, including
v=0. No c increase or complete new physical return is asserted.

## 2. Large common divisor: exact signs, all holes, and the bin saving

For an ideal q define

    A_G(q)=sum_(d|q, Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Ideal divisor inversion gives the exact identity

    1_(Nk>=G)=sum_(q|k) A_G(q),
    A_G(q)=0 if Nq<G,       |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).             (8)

Because a is squarefree, every contributing q|a is squarefree. With a=qc,
mu(qc)=mu(q)mu(c)1_(c,q)=1. There is no coprimality condition on b/q. Thus

 B_g(u)=sum_(q sf,Nq>=G) A_G(q)mu(q)phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
           M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/Nq),                    (9)

where M^(q) has the extra column condition (c,q)=1. Every q up to the literal
profile endpoint remains; q can meet a slot, the row or a fixed hole. Character
zeros are retained in phi_u(q)^2; no phase is divided out or reduced to a unit.

To avoid an illicit moving-mask MI input, restore the inverse exactly:

    M_u^(q)(E)=sum_(k supported on primes of q)
                   phi_u(k)/(Nk)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nk).       (10)

At each p|q the local convolution mu*1 is1 at exponent0 and0 otherwise.
Consequently(10) includes ALL k=p^j and preserves natural zeros even at shared
row primes. It is finite on an actual annulus. Its absolute mass is

    prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
                                                               (11)

Small primes supply a fixed constant and each sufficiently large prime factor
is at most (Np)^epsilon. A fixed polynomial extra inverse puncture, if not
already part of the licensed natural character, is restored by the same formula
over q times that puncture; its complete mass is again U^epsilon. Actual slot
holes remain in their fixed bounded coefficients, as permitted by MI. This is
the existing [research revision] restoration device, here used on ONE inverse and an unchanged
plain factor; it is not claimed as a new general divisor identity.

Apply Hilbert Minkowski to(9),(10), then use the SAME-bin plain bound(2) and
the fully marked moment(3). The outside phases are contractions. This gives

 ||B_g Q||_Omega
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2)
          sum_(Nq>=G) tau(q)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1-beta/2)
   << H_J U^(1/2+epsilon) D^(beta/2) G^(-beta/2).
                                                               (12)

The last estimate follows from ideal counting on dyadic shells, uniformly for
beta in a fixed positive compact interval. Every q-shell count is present: the
factor(Nq)^(-1) in(9) alone would only yield logarithmic mass; the additional
power comes precisely from the shortened plain sum at the same buffered zero.
Squaring proves the first part of(5). A mere trivial plain bound would give
U D/G instead and need a much larger G. This use of(2) is the substantive
same-zero improvement of the [research revision]-style decomposition.

## 3. Large plain square divisors, including their complete intersection

Define A_H(k) by(8) with H in place of G. Since k|s_2(b) iff k^2|b,

    1_(N s_2(b)>=H)=sum_(k^2|b) A_H(k).                 (13)

Unlike the gcd divisor q, k need NOT be squarefree. Define the actual plain
part S_bad(D) with this indicator. Multiplicativity gives

 S_bad(D)=sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi_u(k^2)/(Nk)
                         S_u(D/(Nk)^2).

Using(2) BEFORE triangle and ideal counting afterwards yields the uniform
pointwise bound on the same buffered rows

    |S_bad(D)| << H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2) H^(-beta).
                                                               (14)

All prime powers, equality at H, terminal nonempty scales and fixed holes remain.
Consequently ||M S_bad Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta).
This alone does NOT license deleting the intersection with B_g from a signed
source. We pay that intersection next.

Let B_gs restrict to BOTH N(a,b)>=G and N s_2(b)>=H. Expand(8),(13) simultaneously.
For squarefree q, put L=[q,k^2]=q k^2/(q,k). Then a=qc,b=Ld, and EXACTLY

 B_gs(u)=sum_(q sf,k;Nq>=G,Nk>=H)
    A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi_u(qL)/(Nq NL)^(1/2)
                    M_u^(q)(R/Nq) S_u(D/NL).           (15)

This formula includes q/k intersections of every valuation. It is not obtained
by incorrectly replacing lcm(q,k^2) by qk^2. Restore M^(q) by(10). The coefficient
mass left after(2),(3) is

 sum_(q,k) tau(qk)^(O(1)) (Nq)^(-1/2)(NL)^(-(1+beta)/2).

Primewise, put i=v_p(q) in{0,1}, j=v_p(k)>=0. Then
v_p(L)=max(i,2j)=i+2j-min(i,j). Thus its non-divisor weight equals
q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2) in norm notation.
For i=1,j>=1 its local factor is exactly
(Np)^(-1/2-j(1+beta)); the shared prime is not counted twice.
For i=1,j=0 it is (Np)^(-1-beta/2), and for i=0 it is
(Np)^(-j(1+beta)). These exhaust all valuation cases, including holes.

Writing d=(q,k), k=de, and dropping only positive coprimality restrictions gives

 sum_(Nk>=H) (Nk)^(-1-beta) N(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) (Nd)^((beta-1)/2)
       << U^epsilon H^(-beta) tau(q).                  (16)

For Nd<=H, sum the e tail from H/Nd. For Nd>H, its complete sum is bounded;
(Nd)^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)(Nd)^((beta-1)/2). Thus BOTH ranges satisfy(16).
The strict compact upper bound beta<1 is used, and all divisor losses fit the
arbitrarily small U^epsilon. Summing q then proves

    ||B_gs Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).
                                                               (17)

Finally B_s=M S_bad-B_gs. Hilbert triangle and G>=1 prove the second part of(5).
No signed subset monotonicity or independent signs have entered. The three
pieces in(4) are exhaustive, and every low/high cross term is paid by the
same Hilbert triangle when a complete norm is needed.

## 4. The original inverse moment and the exact surviving source

On Omega_g, |M S|<=4|B_g|. Divide by the actual lower plain bound in(2),
retaining its error and common beta, then sum with w_u|Q_u|^2. Equation(12)
gives U^(1-beta*g+small). The same argument using(17) and(14) gives
U^(1-2beta*h+small) on Omega_s. Since beta>=delta-small and all ranges are fixed,
the freely allocated losses give(6). At no point is the inverse witness divided
out; the conclusion is the original restricted inverse MOMENT. A subsequent
division by its usual inverse spike is legal, but is not needed to state(6).

On Omega_c the strict inequalities in the two preceding class definitions and
B=B_g+B_s+B_c prove(7) by triangle. The whole original common-zero product lower
bound B0.20 is therefore retained by B_c, up to the fixed factor1/2 and the old
small errors. No witness is chosen afresh and no new cutoff is selected.

The surviving literal coefficient has the two tuple restrictions

    N(a,b)<G,   N s_2(b)<H,
    mu(a)phi_u(ab)W_I(Na/R)W_P(Nb/D)/(RD)^(1/2).        (18)

After including one prime from each original disjoint slot pool, equal ideal
products may be merged WITH their signs. All their original tuple restrictions,
labels, independent slot heights and zeros stay in that merged coefficient.
The following intrinsic fact survives all coincidences. Since a is squarefree,

    (ab)/rad(ab)=(a,b) b/rad(b),
    N((ab)/rad(ab)) < G H^2.                            (19)

Indeed b/rad(b) divides s_2(b)^2 primewise. The original slot product P is
squarefree; multiplying it changes the repeat factor by (P,ab), whose norm
is at most NP. Thus the full merged column n=abP obeys

    N(n/rad(n)) < G H^2 NP.                             (20)

These are support statements, not signed norm bounds. The small repeated-prime
part can be frozen for a later legitimate source analysis; doing so does not
make the squarefree remainder canonical automatically. With g=4eta,h=2eta,
the unmarked repeat factor has width<8eta, and the full one width<8eta+v.

## 5. Admissibility, profiles, every shortening and the physical complement

The input gates are literal PR9 B0.3--4/B3.31 and B0.13--20, together with the
accepted [research revision]/[research revision] fixed-dictionary and same-zero selection bridges. In particular:

1. The physical delta and cutoff t are fixed first; the actual label and internal
   buffered bin are selected by the original finite procedure. Lemma1W permits
   ANY t in[1,3/2] fixed before its witnesses. Its proof supplies the spike at the
   actual internal beta BEFORE weakening it to physical delta. Using the weaker
   physical spike but the larger internal beta only in the shortened upper bound
   would lose an unwanted factor D^(beta-delta). That invalid shortcut is avoided
   in(2),(6). No upper slot price is replaced by an internal maximum.
2. In(9) the new inverse scale is R/(Nq Nk); in(15) it is the SAME scale after
   restoration. The plain scale is D/Nq or D/NL. These all decrease. If r' is
   the logarithmic inverse scale, then r'<=r; hence BOTH gates(1) improve.
   When r'<0 but the support is nonempty, replace its scale by1 and make a
   bounded dilation of the common profile. This still has r'=0<=r and gives
   2v<=1/10<1 and 8v<=2/5<3. No artificial amplifier, added slot, enlarged
   prime pool, or new derivative index is introduced. The same original Q
   is inside each MI application; there is no unpriced U^v slot factor.
3. The inverse source profile includes the old cutoff
   V_le(R y/U^t). After a=qkc and E=R/(Nq Nk), its argument is still
   V_le(R(c/E)/U^t), so this is exactly the SAME function of its normalized
   variable. It is not a moving arithmetic coefficient or a new cutoff chosen
   after q,k. The plain normalized variable has the identical property.
   Character phases from q,L,k keep their zero values; every exponent, including
   a multiple of six, remains a literal character power with its natural hole.
4. The source's finite Sobolev orders give (3) for rowwise real powers/heights
   and for the finite derivative-profile list. Scale derivatives replace W by
   -W/2-yW', and real/height derivatives add the original logarithmic weights.
   The gcd/square-divisor thresholds are frozen at U BEFORE this operation and
   are not differentiated. Smooth scale suprema use the original logarithmic
   boxes, not a row-dependent coefficient choice. Independent slot heights are
   never equated to the witness height. A fixed global polynomial support bound
   may be used for q,k and restoration variables before these norms; individual
   terms vanish outside their real profile support. This avoids differentiating
   a moving summation endpoint.
5. The plain bound(2) is used only on the retained buffered rows. Its direct
   Mellin shift is uniform for the common shortened profiles and heights by
   B0.14--15. Explicitly the fixed finite conjugation-stable dictionary Theta
   gives X(u)={nu psi_u^(+/-1)}; the good-prime rows have conductor O_S(U).
   With fixed buffer e>0 and I=ceil(1/e)+2, the selected i<I obeys
   a<=B_i<a+e and B_(i+1)<a+2e. Here B_j is the maximum of51/100 and
   real zero parts in that dictionary up to height3^j T. The nonfloor zero
   has a<=Re(rho)<a+e and |Im(rho)|<=3^i T. Put beta=2a-1. On the retained
   height segments the direct line Re(s)=a+6e gives the E^beta bound, with
   its original small U loss, common smooth seminorms and deleted Euler zeros.
   Shortening E changes neither this bin nor its zero-free region, character,
   profile or selected heights. It does not request a new bin at scale E.
   The finitely many independent coordinates use fixed fractions of T;
   discarded tails are U^B T^(-N), with B including polynomial divisor counts
   fixed before N, in the source range U^tau_minus<=T<=U^tau_plus.
   At large heights retain the source's polynomial factor. Choose
   the finite profile orders, bin/mesh and epsilon shares before the internal
   small polynomial height exponent, and the raw tail powers before their decay
   order and final threshold. Above that internal height range, the original
   trivial row count and absolute polynomial bounds on M,Q and the source parts
   are paid by a larger fixed height degree. This final degree may depend on the
   already chosen internal height exponent. The external physical height
   exponent is chosen AFTER that degree, to fit its cost below the eta reserve;
   it is not identified with the internal exponent. No growing-conductor
   uniformity or new growing-height theorem is imported.
6. All sums over q,k in the proof use actual nonempty polynomial support. A
   positive convergent extension was used only AFTER absolute values to bound
   their mass. Every root/puncture hole is retained in the original factor or
   explicitly restored as in(10). Extra slot holes are fixed coefficients
   permitted by MI; MP with arbitrary coefficients is never invoked. Disjoint
   original slot pools can meet inverse/plain factors or q/k freely. None of
   these intersections is replaced by an independence assumption.

The physical meaning of(6) is deliberately limited. It can be applied on an
ACTUAL positive child norm only after the original signed reconstruction has
produced that norm, its complete character and its live slot list. One must
test the defined dominance class with that child's own R,D,Q and actual zero.
It cannot be attached to a parent and pushed through a signed projector.
Keep both projectors, missing radicals, joint-label counting, every original
clipped rectangle, all extraction scalars and masks unchanged. A Cauchy pair
averages its two actual child savings; a gain on one side is not doubled.

For a raw decomposition w=u b^6 the old root holes remain frozen before free
summation. This report proves the local free-row lemma and its exact source
complement, not a uniformly improved raw envelope: Omega_c still has the old
bound. All other raw roots, low/high and fixed-inducing branches, bounded free
windows, first/second/artificial zero, old-only descendants, actual6a/9a radii,
physical K_phys^(5/6), empty/short slot supply, shortened plain alternatives,
weighted Euler shifts including zero capacity, principal residues and common
Delta-before-target supremum return therefore retain their OLD paid estimates.
No new physical comparison is performed and the centered M/24 reserve is unspent.

Since no uniform gain on Omega_c is proved, neither G137's conditional raw
gain nor a changed local plane or endpoint follows. The SAME-family license
for K remains its accepted c10 ancestry. The present MI-based proper-sector
lemma does not alter K, physical kappa, the accepted c11 or its open admissions.

## 6. Actual next obstruction and a deliberately coarse complete test

Two potentially attractive shortcuts were tested and fail at identifiable
source steps, not by an abstract nonexistence theorem.

First, applying the complete mu*1 cancellation to an individual selected
inverse/plain dyad is false. On the unmarked, fully coprime squarefree part of
(18), merge n=ab and extract the row factor psi_u(n)^(+/-1).
Then mu(a)=mu(n)mu(b), so the literal coefficient is

 c(n)=mu(n)nu(n)/(RD)^(1/2)
       sum_(b|n) mu(b)W_I(N(n/b)/R)W_P(Nb/D),           (21)

with the original tuple cuts and zeros. At a common height and real power,
the two norm twists DO combine into one function of Nn/(RD). This pays their
normalization exactly, but the divisor-profile sum in(21) remains arithmetic.
It is not a smooth profile of Nn, a fixed ray character or a coprimality mask.
An additional original prime-slot tuple contributes its own literal factors
and product coincidences; it does not change this conclusion.

For a transparent actual coefficient test, take two distinct unramified prime
ideals p,l with Np on the inverse annulus, Nl on the much shorter plain annulus,
and choose nonnegative smooth profiles nonzero at these two points with small
fixed relative supports. At n=pl, only a=p,b=l lies in those two annuli; a=l,
a=1 and a=pl do not. The coefficient is -nu(pl) times their nonzero normalized
weights, before any natural row zero. It lies in N(a,b)=1, s_2(b)=1 and hence
survives every G,H>1. This is a literal coefficient failure of dyadic divisor
cancellation, not an example of a high zero or saturation of a whole norm.
No density, positive lower bound for the complete moment or independence of
such rows is asserted. The completed cutoff identity G115 still holds only
after all its required divisor/dyadic pieces have been reconstructed.

Second, the original canonical energy B3.6 expressly permits NO further
coefficient on its squarefree column. The divisor-profile factor in(21) is
outside that contract. Divisor boundedness, the common height, empty support
and the tiny repeated-prime bound(20) do not license its removal. The usual
unmarked inverse theorem B3.39 also has actual mu(n) coefficients; it cannot
be applied to(21) just by writing a new symbol for this factor. Such an
extension would require a new proof using the displayed signed divisor law.

The complete coarse test makes the remaining deficit explicit. On Omega,
the SAME-bin bound(2), followed by marked MI, gives

    ||B Q||_Omega^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon).

Using B_c=B-B_g-B_s and the already proved estimates gives the same upper
power for ||B_c Q||_Omega^2, with every mixed term paid by Hilbert triangle.
On Omega_c the only available comparison back to the original inverse is

    |M_u(R)| <= 2|B_c(u)|/|S_u(D)|.

The plain lower bound therefore yields U^(1+epsilon), precisely the old
inverse moment. It supplies NO positive eta saving. Replacing this triangle
by an unsupported comparison with a signed subset would be the missing proof.

This pinpoints the next arithmetic repair without a scalar re-optimization:
estimate the signed divisor-profile source(18)/(21), with its near-coprime
inverse/plain factors and small repeated-prime part, on the same buffered
large-plain rows. An estimate only for a different canonical coefficient,
for averaged unrelated heights, or for selected q/k terms is insufficient.
The full core with its actual product signal(7) is now the only unpaid source
inside this crossing window. It is not known to be easier merely because it
has been renamed. The substantive new progress is(5)--(6) and the exact,
overlap-paid support reduction(18)--(20), not a claimed solution of that core.

## 7. Evidence, provenance and disposition

The primary input inspected here is PR9 commit
58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b, local paper.md, B0.3--4,
B0.7--20, B3.3, B3.6, B3.31 and B3.39--40. Its exact hash and the pinned
PR15 PlainUnmarkedDensity.tex are retained in source-evidence.json. No
proof-assistant file or kernel was opened or executed. [research revision]/[research revision] supply the
accepted fixed-data, internal-bin and physical source interpretation; G137
supplies the existing whole crossing window. These are source premises,
not re-certified by the finite helper in this pass.

[research revision]'s two-inverse divisor inversion and smooth-number mask restoration are
explicitly reused. The difference here is an inverse/plain pair, the actual
same-bin shortened PLAIN estimate in(12), all original slots retained inside
MI, the additional large-square-divisor removal and its lcm intersection.
This is not the parallel R4 primitive low/middle-dual sector calculation.
The original 29-family/109-child library is preserved. Credit remains with
the PR9/Gao and [research revision]/[research revision]/[research revision]/[research revision] authors and reviewers, OpenAI, Hailey Collet,
Akash Levy and Zhongpai Gao with AI assistance. No literature priority is
claimed for elementary divisor or lattice-counting ingredients.

One lean exact helper, check.py, was fully read before its only execution.
Native receipt1b2869 passed five groups: 2,400 ideal-monoid-model divisor/square
identities; full signed polynomial identities in12 character/hole/threshold
cases, including all q/k overlaps and two disjoint original-style slot pools;
2,560 higher-power mask restoration cases; repeat-factor support identities;
and the exact eta budget. Integer Gaussian pairs retain quartic phases and
natural ramified zeros; no floating-point comparison is used. These integer
monoid cases test the universal divisor algebra, not actual Hecke high rows,
MI uniformity, B0.15, source admissions or an asymptotic theorem. The written
argument is the proof of the displayed estimates relative to their sources.

Outcome pending independent review: a proved proper-subclass inverse-moment
saving, a second overlap-paid arithmetic restriction, and an exact unpaid

## R4. The prefix is paid over the whole slot interval

Let N0(P) be the complete sum over free rows of squared tensor Sobolev norms on [a,1] times the enlarged height interval, with derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in {0,1}, and the original nonnegative row majorant. The real width is at least 3/20. The previous prefix proof applies with this fixed t>1 and gives

    N0(P)<<H_J U^(J_t+epsilon),
    J_t=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.              (R7)

Here is the exponent reconstruction. R2 restricts the complementary cofactor to Nm<C_H L/R. For fixed m, the inner inverse dyads satisfy R<<D<<L/Nm. The centrally normalized free inverse moment is U^(1/6)D^(5/6+epsilon); d^(-s) supplies D^(-delta) in its square. Apply common-profile separation before fixing the live cofactor, and keep the profile containing the original R unchanged under every shortened inverse scale in B0.7. Hilbert triangle over inverse dyads is dominated by D~L/Nm because 5/6-delta>0. Multiplication by phi_u(m) is a contraction, even with common primes and zeros. The resulting norm is bounded by

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon)L^[(5/6-delta)/2]
                   sum_(Nm<C_H L/R)(Nm)^(-11/12).

Indeed a+(5/6-delta)/2=11/12 exactly. The ideal count, with its unit, gives (L/R)^(1/12). Squaring gives U^(1/6)L^(5/6-delta)(L/R)^(1/6), exactly R7. The same argument treats the finite tensor derivatives by logarithmic factors. No cancellation between different cofactors is assumed.

Only after positive evaluation at an actual zero multiply its exceptional-set count by the physical slot price. Thus

    sum_(|P(rho_u)|>=1/4)|Q_u|^2
        <<H_J U^(J_t+delta v+epsilon).                (R8)

No zero selector has been inserted in Poisson or in the inverse moment. This is not the full marked norm estimate with cost 5v/3.

For the current density envelope put

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    a_K=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3hD_K),
    b_K=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/D_K,
    G=min(3kv,a_K+b_K v), E_K=rho+delta v-G.

On the full rectangle, E_K-J_t-delta v>eta. A sufficient lower bound uses G<=a_K+b_K/20. Multiplying its excess above eta by Den=3hD_K gives a cubic whose four Bernstein coefficients are positive; the least is 31963522910683/488281250000000. The review reconstructed this from the rational functions, not from the author's coefficient array. Consequently the previous t=4/3 failure at v=.05 is not being ignored: this t=33/25 detector pays the complete prefix over v<=.05. ### Fixed-ray squarefree selector estimate

For one of these fixed characters `chi`, squarefree `R`, and a moving deleted set `M1`, define
\[
U_\chi(X;M_1,R)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf},\,(c,M_1)=1,\,R\mid c}
\chi(c)\sqrt{q_c}W_0(q_c/X).
\]
If `R` meets the deletion set or the character conductor, this is zero. Otherwise, for every fixed `sigma>1/2`,
\[
|U_\chi(X;M_1,R)|
\ll(q_{M_1}q_R)^\epsilon q_R^{-\sigma}X^{\sigma+1/2}.
\tag{T05.3}
\]
Indeed `sqrt(q_c)W0(q_c/X)=sqrt(X)W(q_c/X)`. Its squarefree forced-divisor Dirichlet series is
\[
\chi(R)q_R^{-s}{L^S(s,\chi)\over L^S(2s,\chi^2)}
\prod_{p\mid M_1R}(1+\chi(p)Q_p^{-s})^{-1},
\]
with repeated primes counted once and conductor/excluded primes omitted. The denominator reciprocal converges absolutely for `Re s>1/2`; a principal numerator pole at one is canceled by the original root `W-hat(1)=0`. Moving local factors cost a subpower by the same elementary argument as T01. Shift Mellin to `Re s=sigma`; fixed-character height growth is absorbed by rapid Mellin decay. This proves (T05.3), including small `X`. No new zero-free input is used here.

**Profile qualification:** this is the original root-preserving profile, its conjugate, and permitted Euler derivatives retaining that root. An arbitrary multiplicative norm twist moves the root and is not covered by this argument without a corrected residue calculation. Do not advertise T05 for such a family merely because another theorem uses Mellin twists.

## G142. Actual logarithmic improvement and the remaining complete core

Use Green–Tao's [published Theorem1.1, pp.542–543](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v175-n2-p03-p.pdf):
fixed-degree polynomial nilsequences have every fixed logarithmic Möbius
saving, uniform in the polynomial coefficients, with ineffective constants.
A fixed torus with the degree-k abelian filtration and fixed sine/cosine
functions gives sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)e(P(n))<<_A Y(log(2Y))^-A. A dummy torus
coordinate is available to satisfy the stated dimension convention.
The GRH power-decay remark is unused. The separately inspected
[Gao–Zhao v2 Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2212.09241v2) assumes GRH
and is not an unconditional input.

Expand the actual periodic chi in its finite additive Fourier series,
retaining zeros and coefficient absolute sum<=q. Apply the polynomial
bound to ell n/q-n^k/(2*pi*x^k). Splitting prefix lengths at sqrt M
and Abel summing the decreasing damping proves
|W_<=M(x)|<<_(q,A) M(log M)^-A, uniformly in real x. For k=6,b=3/2,
take M=X(log X)^B, B=(D+2)/4, A=B+(D+2)/2. The core log exponent
is -D-2, the complete off-diagonal log exponent -D-1, so

    E(X)<<_(q,D) X^(3/2)+X^2(log X)^-D,
    ||W||_1<<_(q,D) X^(3/4)+X(log X)^-D

for every fixed D>0. This is actual arithmetic progress for this new
source. It still misses the first-gain energy threshold1.7497080728
by .2502919272 in power; logarithmic strength cannot grow with X.

For 0<c<=1/4 put gamma=1-c and r=1+c/2. Freeze L=X^gamma,M=X^r
before x varies over[X,2X]. The prefix n<=L costs O(X^gamma), while
G141 gives ||W_>M||_2^2<<X^(3/2)+X^(6-4r)<<X^(2gamma).
Both complementary L1 and L2 norms are therefore O(X^gamma). The
SINGLE complete core target is

    integral_X^(2X)|sum_(X^gamma<n<=X^r) mu(n)chi(n)
              exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6)|dx/x
                   <<_(chi,c,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon).  (CORE1)

By the norm triangle inequality in both directions this is equivalent
to the full source L1 input. The same holds for L2, which is sufficient
but stronger. The complements also permit exact big-O equivalence.
No omitted cross is hidden: the full tail function was first bounded
in L2, and only then used in the L1 triangle inequality.

| Conditional c | gamma | Upper cutoff exponent r | L2 target |
|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | .8748 | 1.0626 | 1.7496 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 5/3 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/2 |

Every row is OPEN. The first would exceed c11 by135091/2500000000.

The review also proves a fixed-parameter larger conditional architecture.
For ANY fixed 1/2<gamma<1 choose 1<b<=2gamma, integer k>2 with
r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2)<b, and integer K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Low prefix
and complete tail still cost O(X^gamma); CORE1 on X^gamma<n<=X^r
is sufficient. Use ALL the shifts in G140. Starting with 1/L holomorphic
on Re s>1, solve for the unshifted reciprocal on
Re s>max(gamma,a-(b-1)) whenever it is known on Re s>a. Each j>=1
term is already holomorphic. A finite number of steps reaches gamma;
the nonzero A0, principal pole and actual Euler holes are paid throughout.

For example gamma=3/5, b=11/10, k=12, K=5 gives r=27/25, remainder

statement:
## 4. The complete short-arc observation and zero-exclusion return

Here is the weakest full source estimate used by this replacement. Fix 0<c<1/2 and gamma=1-c. For every fixed ordinary chi modulo q, use the fixed parity-compatible r above, put h=1/(qN), and require, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large integers N,

    E_arc(N):=integral_0^h |R_N(x)|^2 dx
       <<_(chi,r,epsilon) N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon).        (10)

The positive epsilon loss is chosen after c; thresholds may depend on the fixed character and epsilon. No average over characters or exceptional scale set is allowed. In fact(10) is equivalent, up to arbitrary epsilon losses, to M_chi(X)=sum_(n<=X)mu(n)chi(n)<<X^(gamma+epsilon). This equivalence is stated explicitly: the new source estimate is not called easier merely because its notation differs.

Proof of the forward direction, including the observation cost: discrete Fourier inversion modulo q writes chi(k)=sum_(a=0)^(q-1) c_a e(ak/q). The Fourier formula for the periodic Bernoulli polynomial gives

    Phi(x)=-(2pi i)^r/r! sum_a c_a B_r({x+a/q}).

Thus on 0<x<1/q, Phi is one fixed polynomial P(x) of degree at most r. It is continuous at0 since r>=2, and its constant term is

    beta=Phi(0)=2L(r,chi)!=0.

The nonvanishing here is the absolutely convergent Euler product on r>1; no zero-free assertion to the left of1 is used. In particular principal and imprimitive characters are covered with their original zeros. Let p_r be the endpoint reproducing polynomial on [0,1]:

    p_r(u)=sum_(j=0)^r (2j+1)(-1)^j P_j(2u-1),

where P_j is the Legendre polynomial. Orthogonality, or integration against monomials, proves

    integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0) (0<=j<=r),
    integral_0^1 |p_r(u)|^2du=(r+1)^2.               (11)

For the first identity it suffices to test the shifted Legendre basis: the integral selects its j-th coefficient with value (-1)^j, exactly the value of that basis polynomial at0. The norm is sum_(j=0)^r(2j+1). The Bernoulli Fourier formula used above follows by repeated integration by parts from B_j'=j B_(j-1), mean zero and B_1(x)=x-1/2; it has no additional analytic input. In particular B_2=x^2-x+1/6 and B_3=x^3-3x^2/2+x/2 cover the two orders needed here.

Define O_N f=integral_0^1 p_r(u)f(hu)du. Every n<=N has nhu<=1/q, so the same local polynomial applies to every original term, without a moving choice of a cell. It follows exactly that

    O_N D_N=beta sum_(n<=N)a(n)/n^r.

Writing eta_N=O_N E-2, Taylor's theorem and(11) give |eta_N|<=C_r h^(r+1). Since sum a(n)/n^r=1/L(r,chi),

    beta sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r = O_N R_N-eta_N.          (12)

Cauchy-Schwarz pays the full observation cost:

    |O_N R_N| <=(r+1) sqrt(qN) E_arc(N)^(1/2).       (13)

Equations(10)-(13) give T_N:=sum_(n>N)a(n)/n^r<<N^(gamma-r+epsilon). For integer N, ordinary partial summation, with T(t)=T_floor(t), gives the exact inverse formula

    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^r T_N
                 +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T(t)dt.     (14)

It yields M_chi(N)<<N^(gamma+epsilon), and real X follows by taking its integer part. All integer N are required; a sparse scale family is not silently interpolated.

For completeness, the reverse direction is equally paid. Phi is bounded and globally Lipschitz: this follows from its finite Bernoulli representation, including r=2 and the finitely many derivative jumps. Abel summation in(1), using |M_chi(t)|<<t^(gamma+epsilon) with gamma+epsilon<1, gives

    |R_N(x)| << N^(gamma-r+epsilon)
                      +|x|N^(gamma-r+1+epsilon)

for 0<=x<=h. The derivative integral converges since r>=2>gamma+1+epsilon. Integrating its square proves(10), after relabelling epsilon. This uses the actual full tail and not a pointwise Fourier series summation shortcut.

The zero return has no hidden height truncation. The Mertens estimate makes

    A(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(t)t^(-s-1)dt

holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma and equal to 1/L(s,chi) on Re(s)>1. For nonprincipal chi, bounded period sums give L(s,chi) holomorphic on Re(s)>0. For principal chi modulo q, the floor integral for zeta together with product_(p|q)(1-p^(-s)) gives the usual meromorphic continuation, with its only pole in that half-plane at1. The identity A(s)L(s,chi)=1 then continues throughout the connected half-plane with that pole removed. Hence L has no zero with Re(s)>gamma, at any imaginary height. At the principal pole the excluded point remains a pole, not a zero. Finite imprimitive Euler factors have zeros only on Re(s)=0. This is an ordinary-character conditional theorem. It neither supplies the open estimate(10) nor resolves the separate pinned PR9 source/K-scope issue in the incumbent proof.

## G145. Full-word and sorted-creation commutators have different returns

In the full free-word lift, all k! orders of an integer's distinct primes
have the same phase. Abelianization maps each word to that integer.
Adjacent-transposition differences span its zero-sum kernel: the
permutation graph is connected, and a spanning tree has k!-1 independent
differences. The hard product cutoff retains entire fibers, so integer
evaluation annihilates every such within-fiber commutator. For positive
word weights w_v, beta_n=sum_(v in fiber n)1/w_v, the least squared lift
norm is sum_n|a_n|^2/beta_n and evaluator norm squared is sum_n beta_n.
Their product is at least(#S)^2. This is the existing G117 price;
cross-integer correlations remain eligible.

The existing B22 sorted-prime space has a different, nonzero commutator.
For fixed sigma>1/2 define on increasing unramified prime words

    A_p e_n=chi(p)p^-sigma e_(np) if p>P+(n), else0,
    T=sum_(p not dividing q)A_p,  P+(1)=1.

Different parents have disjoint r-step descendants, so
||T^r||^2<=S_sigma^r/r!, S_sigma=sum_(p not dividing q)p^-2sigma<infinity.
Hence the norm-convergent Neumann inverse gives
v_sigma=(I+T)^-1 e_1, with coordinate mu(n)chi(n)n^-sigma.
For p<r, A_p A_r=0. Thus, with[A,B]=AB-BA,

    C=sum_(p<r)[A_r,A_p]=T^2.

The infinite sum is defined through finite prime cutoffs: their C_P=T_P^2
converges in norm since ||T-T_P||^2<=sum_(p>P)p^-2sigma. Compression
to n<=N preserves the same identity because intermediate products never
exceed the final product. With Lambda_(N,sigma)u=sum_(n<=N)n^sigma u_n,

    M_chi(N)=1-sum_(p<=N)chi(p)+Lambda_(N,sigma)(C v_sigma). (88.4)

The final term is exactly the contribution with at least two prime
factors. It must cancel the prime term; a small norm of C alone does
not do so. Only an estimate for the complete scalar(88.4) gives the
all-scale M return. The source/operator construction is credited to B22;
the complete commutator/source accounting is the present adaptation.

Fixed fractional logarithmic regularity cannot pay the arithmetic gap.
For ||u||_s^2=sum_n(1+log n)^(2s)|u_n|^2 and fixed real s, v_sigma
belongs to every such space, while partial summation against Q_q gives

    ||Lambda_(N,sigma)||_(s,dual)^2
      ~kappa_q N^(2sigma+1)/((2sigma+1)(log N)^(2s)).

Its limiting power is still sigma+1/2>1. More generally every positive
diagonal weight w_(n,N), even chosen separately for each N, obeys

    sqrt(sum_(n in S)w_(n,N)|v_sigma(n)|^2)
      sqrt(sum_(n in S)n^(2sigma)/w_(n,N))>=#S.

This is a price for a product of norms, not a signed M lower bound.
Non-diagonal correlations and source-specific boundary estimates remain
open, with their complete return to be proved.

## 4. The other first tests and source attribution

T03's geometric compact multiplier product_j sinh(2^(-j)s)/(2^(-j)s) is nonzero for Re s>0: each zero lies on the imaginary axis and the tail is1+O_K(4^(-j)). [research revision]/G49 already supplies the smooth compact kernel and complete transfer. A bank of copies is not new numerator coverage.

T16's sign convention is sound. With empty face retained and degree|S|, Str(I)=sum mu(n)=M(x). Since d,h are odd and W even,

    Str(W(dh+hd))=Str((Wd-dW)h).

Thus dh+hd=I-P gives the stated weighted identity. Character weights generally do not commute with d. The source's linear total reduced Betti mass,2x/pi^2+O(x^theta) for theta>17/54, is confirmed directly in [Bjorner's original paper, Theorem3.4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1101.5704), with the reduced-Euler sign in equations1.1-1.2. This is an unsigned certificate obstruction, not a lower bound on signed M or a refutation of all topology. W27 owns the relevant prior mechanism.

T21's principal finite-product obstruction is correct. Were the zero-free P_y(s)=product_(p<=y)(1-p^(-s)) locally bounded on Re s>a for0<a<1, Montel gives a holomorphic subsequential limit agreeing with1/zeta on Re s>1. Meromorphic identity forces a zero at1. Hurwitz forbids it in a nonzero limit of zero-free functions. W41 already gives the wrong-sign real-limit obstruction, and W36 proves a stronger actual low-height norm divergence. D1 explicitly changes P_y by the continuous vacuum and does not erase either old failure.

T30's diag(s-rho,I_N) is a valid rank-one bad-block countertest. It is not arithmetic data. T24's four-root multiplier preserves conjugation/reflection symmetry and changes zero counts by at most4, so statistics invariant under O(1) perturbations cannot exclude that outlier. It preserves neither the Euler product nor every possible fine rigidity statistic. Their failures remain restricted to the stated insufficient inputs.

T25's pair expansion includes -(z+w)+zw. The quadratic and higher logarithmic terms are affordable above1/2; the singleton is not automatically removed. The arbitrary-finite-block principal-real argument also works: if A_B=1-product_(p in B)(1-p^(-sigma)), then0<A_B<1, and summability of A_B would make the product over blocks positive. Exhausting all unramified primes instead gives zero for0<sigma<=1, by prime harmonic divergence. This does not reject signed complex blocks or the explicitly different D2 nonprincipal construction.

W33's singleton/higher-power separation and W36 R36.21-R36.22 are the closest analytic ancestry. G76 is an actual source-specific prime-toggle matching, not a proof of PB. G108 is a hard-cutoff Mobius marginal with signed cofactor intervals, not an Euler-logarithm pairing. These distinctions are necessary for fair credit. D1's one-sided subpower interface and D2's complete structural block contract are retained additions within those families, with no literature-priority assertion and no arithmetic-saving credit.

## G197. Two paid classes with complete shared-prime cost

For an ideal q define A_G(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=G) mu(q/d). Then
sum_(q|g)A_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G), A_G(q)=0 below G and |A_G(q)|<=tau(q).
Since a is squarefree, the high-gcd piece is exactly

    B_g=sum_(q sf) A_G(q)mu(q)phi(q)^2/(Nq)
                      M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/Nq).                (3)

The extra inverse mask is restored by the COMPLETE q-smooth series

    M^(q)(E)=sum_(h q-smooth) phi(h)/sqrt(Nh) M(E/Nh).

All powers and natural zeros remain. Its absolute mass is at most
product_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1) <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.
Polynomial fixed inverse punctures are handled in the same way. Extracted
row phases are contractions after taking a positive norm, never new MI
column coefficients. Minkowski, (1)-(2) and ideal counting give

    ||B_g Q||^2_Omega << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta). (4)

Let s2(b)=product_p p^floor(v_p(b)/2). The high-square plain part is
sum_(Nk>=H) A_H(k)phi(k^2)/(Nk) S(D/(Nk)^2), with k unrestricted.
Its pointwise absolute bound is H_J U^epsilon D^(beta/2)H^(-beta).
The intersection with the high-gcd part uses L=lcm(q,k^2)=q k^2/(q,k):

    B_gs=sum_(q sf,k) A_G(q)A_H(k)mu(q)phi(qL)/sqrt(Nq NL)
                         M^(q)(R/Nq) S(D/NL).             (5)

Norm notation suppresses N only in the following positive mass:

    w_beta(q,k)=q^(-1-beta/2) k^(-1-beta) (q,k)^((1+beta)/2).

At q=k=p the local weight is p^(-3/2-beta); falsely independent divisibility
would miss p^((1+beta)/2). Put d=(q,k),k=de. The complete k-tail satisfies

    sum_(Nk>=H) k^(-1-beta)(q,k)^((1+beta)/2)
      << H^(-beta) sum_(d|q) d^((beta-1)/2)
      <= H^(-beta) tau(q).                               (6)

For d<=H use the e-tail; for d>H use the complete e-sum and
d^(-(1+beta)/2)<=H^(-beta)d^((beta-1)/2). Thus every large common divisor
is paid. The q-tail supplies G^(-beta/2), including all divisor/restoration
losses on the polynomial support. Squaring yields

    ||B_gs Q||^2 << H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon) G^(-beta)H^(-2beta).

Define B_s=M S_bad-B_gs and B_c=B-B_g-B_s. Hilbert triangle proves
||B_sQ||^2<<H_J U^(1+beta*m+epsilon)H^(-2beta). No signed-subset
monotonicity is asserted. Partition actual rows by |B_g|>=|B|/4, then
|B_s|>=|B|/4 outside the first class, then the remainder. Dividing (4)
and its B_s counterpart by the SAME lower bound (1) gives original inverse
moment savings delta*log_U(G) and 2delta*log_U(H), after losses.

At G=U^(4eta),H=U^(2eta), each pre-loss saving is at least(68/25)eta.
The remaining B_c has magnitude>|B|/2 and unmarked repeat factor<GH^2.
Every original slot remains, so the full repeat factor is<GH^2 NP.

# Merged [research revision] integration

## Actual outcome

**The best established zero-free constant remains**
\[
 c_0=0.125113352960035869\ldots,\qquad
 \zeta(s)\ne0\quad(\Re s>1-c_0,\ s\ne1).
\]
It is the accepted research premise at revision **c06e952f6512f78a15016c97533c104551acaef8**. No larger-\(c\) theorem survives the combined work. This package nevertheless contains substantial proved forward progress and a separately developed, expanded research portfolio.

The original cycle19_handoff_results.zip was a raw **combined** collection of independent solve and brainstorming submissions. This ZIP is its **merged** mathematical integration, including further original work performed after auditing those submissions. It contains no repeated baseline snapshot or agent manuscript.

## Both tracks are mandatory

| Track | Files | Product |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Forward mathematical progress** | [[restricted mathematical source]]([restricted mathematical source]), [[restricted mathematical source]]([restricted mathematical source]) | One coherent proof update with ten main result groups and eighteen auxiliary groups; full new proofs relative to precisely identified inherited inputs |
| **B — Merged and newly augmented brainstorming** | [03_MERGED_AND_AUGMENTED_RESEARCH_PORTFOLIO.md](03_MERGED_AND_AUGMENTED_RESEARCH_PORTFOLIO.md), [04_HIERARCHICAL_IDEA_LEDGER.md](04_HIERARCHICAL_IDEA_LEDGER.md) | All 26 original families, three additional families, 109 stable child IDs, six fresh pass-1 attacks and five fresh pass-2 constructions, with quantitative gates and stop rules |

| **Continuation** | [07_CODEX_NEXT_CYCLE_BRIEF.md](07_CODEX_NEXT_CYCLE_BRIEF.md) | Immediate proof tasks, threshold budgets, invariants and reconciliation instructions |

The proofs and the research portfolio are independently useful. Integrating only the theorem updates or only the top three suggestions leaves half the task undone. The checks directory contains portable finite checks, the corrected conditional interval certificate and machine-readable provenance; it is not a substitute for the proofs.

## What is newly available

- **Completed cubic interface:** T01 removes a fixed angular completion with polynomial height loss and no new arithmetic exponent; T02 alternatively transfers a common completed ordinary mean directly. The uncompleted family's separate holomorphy and actual component matching remain explicit.
- **Physical row reduction:** T03 lifts cube-free physical rows to all rows without changing an exponent above \(1/3\). T04 pays the actual inverse-prime-square sector with its physical \(Q^2\) scale.
- **Signed cubic restriction:** T05 proves the physical cube-row Type I bound \(D^{4/3}K^{2/3}Y^4\), retaining completion densities and the original Mellin root.
- **Full sextic localization:** T06 pays the complete same-core square function. T07 bounds a large **true-gcd** covariance tail with all embeddings and actual prime marks. The strongest version uses the separately imported I-HECKE package and leaves the full small-gcd covariance open.
- **More economical sufficient estimates:** T08 proves the two-exponent finite-incidence transfer and a new exact sufficient divisor corridor; T09 uses scale \(L^2\) Möbius/triple energies; T10 adds a new continuum-dilation criterion and quantitative calibration.
- **Supporting advances:** A01 pays a distinct coherent unembedded aggregate; A07/A08/A09 clarify source norm and approximation costs; A11 merges the corrected prime criteria and optimizes their height sensitivity; A14 verifies five conditional full-probe-saving geometries.

The small numerical gains still require genuine arithmetic cancellation. For example:
\[
 \mathcal T(K,G)\ll K^{9/8}G^{1/32}(KG)^\epsilon T^A
 \quad\text{for all }1\le G\le CK^{28/65}
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad c=\frac{14}{111},
\]
under T08's complete family and strip hypotheses. The implication and corridor are proved; the displayed incidence estimate is open.

## First research actions

1. **Full small-gcd sextic covariance:** derive the gcd-one two-core kernel with unequal embeddings and a real prime slot; seek cancellation in the remaining columns/rows/marks.
2. **Coefficient-specific short-divisor H:** derive and bound the actual short-column restriction, beginning with \(e=1,b=1\), then close every required branch. Keep this separate from the full physical covariance.
3. **Frozen-dyad Möbius energy:** retain the complete weighted off-diagonal after the paid \(O(X)\) diagonal. At \(a=.87449\), the target squared exponent is \(1.74898\).

The next-cycle brief also gives completed-mean/finite-incidence, triple-energy and full signed-cubic alternatives. The ledger preserves quadratic, approximation, operator and geometric branches beyond those immediate tasks.

## Corrections that must survive integration

Physical norm, primitive conductor and Fourier index are different. A cube label may share primes with its core. A finite incidence is not an infinite trace. A signed or gcd-localized covariance is not automatically positive. A pair-dependent sixth-power Gram label does not define a vector projection. A restricted branch does not establish the full H or probe hypothesis. T05's original profile root cannot be moved without a new residue calculation.

Gemini's prime-square Jacobi identity is false; its trace-function saving is unsupported. Grok's full-probe numerical transfer survives with corrected directed inequalities, while its projection and detached-window interpretations do not. A convergent source does not by itself bound its continued period. These corrections preserve useful changed constructions rather than closing entire families.

## Read and integrate

Read this page, then document 07 for the operational state. Integrate documents 01–02 into the proof record, and independently integrate documents 03–04 into the research agenda and persistent ledger. Use documents 05–06 to resolve conflicting statements and source aliases. Exact inherited proofs remain in the original packet at the frozen revision.

If Codex has newer work, compare claims and scopes before replacing anything. Preserve stronger validated newer results, avoid duplicate proofs, and mark the incorporated parallel work as **[research revision]**. Continue directly toward a genuine \(c>c_0\), including a modest first gain. The accepted baseline should not become another lengthy revalidation task.

## Forced valuation count and centered return

Let T1 sum the least residues (-1-i+j) mod6 on C-side first active common
primes, and5 on its first mask primes, weighted by log_Z of prime norm.
Let T2 sum the forced second-common residues (-v_P(G_c V)) mod6. Natural
zeros ensure that the two genuine common supports are disjoint. Frozen
scalars that vanish stay zero; artificial terms of the residual projector
do not become genuine common primes or frequency divisors.

Within a fixed outer row presentation and fixed unit/ray sector, an
exceptional frequency has (h')=h0 v^6, with h0 fixed and
N(h0)>=Z^(T1+T2). In the actual enclosing ball
N(h')<=Z^(m'+delta2), the count is

    #h' << Z^((m'+delta2-T1-T2)/6+o(1)),

and it is empty if the fixed initial norm exceeds that ball. Do not add
an unjustified1 or identify the enclosing ball width with a possibly
smaller canonical child width. Nonexceptional imports keep their original
width correction.

The all-multiplicity proofs establish

    F2_sharp >= b2,
    F1_sharp+S >= c+w-3sigma-5delta1/6,
    S=c+d-2p-R-Bc-Bd >=0.

For example, the four F2 local values are i+ceil(i/6), i+floor(i/6),
7k-1 when i=6k, and i+k-1 for i>j0=6k. Each is at least its actual
b2 value. These are proofs for every multiplicity, not finite tests.

The centered equal-product input has each original plain length at least
L=M/4. Its two rectangles have identical whole-product characters,
natural masks and norm powers. Set x=min(c2,d2) and r_*=(L-c-w-x)_+.
The leading lattice term cancels. Both projectors and extraction scalars
are retained, with their exact cost bounded using

    t_- -r1-r2-(r_*-r1)_+
      =(t_--r2)-max(r_*,r1) <= omega2-r_*.

Since b2>=x, this yields F1_sharp+F2_sharp+r_*+S>=M/4-loss.
The refined exceptional excess is therefore at most
A-13M/12+S+loss, alongside the old A-M+loss bound. Pair the better
joint bound with the independently established opposite-side target.
The original first-label Cauchy outside exponent M-S/2 gives

    M-S/2+(A-M+loss)/2+min(0,S-M/12)/2
      <= M-M/24+(A-M+loss)/2.

S is spent exactly once. Terms with both sides exceptional may use the
refinement on one side and the full target on the other. This describes
a positive Cauchy upper bound, not an orthogonal decomposition of the
original signed row norm.

The actual physical main retains loss4a and its radius
K_main=K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega, density ell=a. Extracted errors retain
loss9a, their original radius, squared extraction coefficients, normalized
prime average and phases including sixth-power punctures. Accordingly
the main/error parent exponents gain M/24 with their old4a/9a costs.
The first zero frequency, added zero Gauss row and genuine second diagonal
are separate; none obtains a new saving here.

## 4. Literal degree12 source and all complements

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension, and a fixed unramified prime p. Let a(n)=lambda(n)chi(n), pointwise. Put h0=chi and s(r^2)=chi(r)^2, zero off squares. With Dirichlet convolution *, define

    q1=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    q2=delta1-p chi(p)^2 delta_(p^2), v=q1*q2,
    b0=v*h0, c=a*a*b0=v*a*s,
    b0(l)=chi(l)[1-p1_(p|l)-p1_(p^2|l)+p^2 1_(p^3|l)].

In particular the q2 coefficient is -p, not -p^2. The identities follow from a*h0=s and preserve shared primes, all ordered factors and natural character zeros. The actual b0 is bounded, periodic of period p^3q, and mean zero. Also v*s=q1*(q2*s), explaining the exact two square-root rows in Section3.

Use b=3/2,k=12,gamma=5/6 and freeze

    L=X^(5/6), U=V=X^(5/12), G=X^(1/6), M=X^(31/30).

Write a_U=a 1_(n<=U) and similarly for V. The complete ordered identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_U*(v*s), Q_V=a_V*(v*s),
    S=a_U*a_V*b0, R=(a-a_U)*(a-a_V)*b0.                  (4.1)

The entire S has frozen coefficients A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e), supported m<=UV=L and bounded by d2(m). Apply (H), choosing its fixed divisor loss after epsilon: S costs X^(5/6+epsilon). This is a complete source estimate; no output mask is inserted into H. Section3 pays both complete Q faces.

Every R tuple has de>UV=L, hence n=del>L. The low output prefix n<=L is identically empty, even for nonintegral real cutoffs. Coefficients of R are bounded by a fixed multiple of d3(n), uniformly in X,U,V. The FULL divisor-bounded tail, proved by the smooth-shell kernel and all integer gaps, gives

    ||sum_(n>M) R(n) f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_epsilon X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^12 M^(-10+epsilon)
      <<_epsilon X^(5/3+epsilon).                        (4.2)

This import is [research revision]'s fixed b>1,k>2 theorem, not its obsolete small-product cap. Its kernel is exp(-c(n+m)/X^b)min(1,[X^k/|n^k-m^k|]^2), with diagonal, both orientations and complete infinite damping. A sufficiently small divisor exponent chosen after epsilon pays the displayed losses. It needs no M<X^b assumption.

Next use [research revision] G182 with the literal bounded mask d>U,e>V,L<del<=M. Its fixed b>1,k>=4 theorem pays all tuples with gcd(d,e)>G by

    X^epsilon[X/G+X^(b/2)/sqrt(G)]
      =X^epsilon[X^(5/6)+X^(2/3)].                       (4.3)

This theorem allows the exact joint mask; no mean-zero estimate is applied after gcd restriction. Strict gcd>G and closed retained gcd<=G are complementary for every real G. There is no extra coprimality with l.

Define the COMPLETE retained core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) f_x(n)
       sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G) a(d)a(e)b0(l),
    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c(n)f_x(n).

Then for every epsilon>0,

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_1+||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_2
                         <<_(chi,p,epsilon) X^(5/6+epsilon). (4.4)

Norm triangle applied to (4.1)-(4.3) pays every cross term, including both tail/core orientations. All physical output endpoints and ordered tuples survive. Since de>L and n<=M, each retained l satisfies l<M/L=X^(1/5), strictly. Within this fixed degree12 detector, (4.4) makes its every-epsilon full core norm hypothesis equivalent to the corresponding full C_p norm hypothesis. It is not asserted equivalent to zero exclusion or to a different phase detector's norm.

statement:
## 10. Geometric and operator fronts, retained with quantitative gates

### F21 — Repaired Hardy discs and a changed known-zero test

In the Hardy half-plane \(\Re s>a_H\), take \(E_t(s)=(s+b_H-it)^{-1}\) and \(G_{n,t}=\zeta(s)(n^{-s}-n^{-1})E_t\). A certified squared residual \(q_t\) excludes
\[
q_t|s+b_H-it|^2<2(\Re s-a_H).
\]
At \(a_H=3/5,b_H=-3/8\), an all-height bound \(q_t\le32/15\), four percent below \(20/9\), gives the overlapping strip \(3/4<\Re s<15/16\). The first practical result could be a rigorously covered finite-height interval. A height net requires derivative control and certified overlaps; average or sampled heights do not cover the bad heights.

**F21.N1 — New pass 2, finite known-zero deflation as a deliberate escape test.** The old \(a_H<1/2\) strict uniform-gain construction is blocked by critical-line zero clusters. Change its **target**, not just its coefficients: for a finite inner Blaschke product B formed from known critical-line zeros in the Hardy domain, approximate \(BE_t\) by the original zeta span. The residual evaluation at an off-line zero is now
\(q_t\ge2(\beta-a_H)|B(\rho)|^2/|\rho+b_H-it|^2\). Multiplication by B is an isometry, but the factor \(|B(\rho)|\) moves into the detector. Thus deflation does not remove the difficulty for free.

The first lemma should compare the improved residual and this evaluation penalty on a prescribed off-line band, with explicit zero-count/tail bounds as the finite product grows. If its gain is entirely canceled by the Blaschke factor, stop. A global version would need an independently controlled infinite inner factor and an arithmetic approximation theorem for the quotient; defining that quotient through unknown off-line zeros is circular. This preserves a changed geometric construction without reviving the refuted uniform-gain claim.

### F22/F24 — Band counts and two-sided phases

Poincaré–Lelong gives
\((2\pi)^{-1}\int\log|\xi|\Delta\varphi_T=\sum_\rho m_\rho\varphi_T(\rho)\).
A nonnegative bump at least one on a translated rectangle excludes its zeros if the pairing is uniformly below one. Its Laplacian changes sign. A useful new estimate must use arithmetic information, include boundary/truncation costs and survive an off-line zero quartet countermodel. Merely bounding \(|\xi|\), applying the functional equation or naming an attractive boundary is insufficient.

Grok's signed test negative on the critical line has a surviving idea—subtract known zero contributions—but loses the simple positive-count implication. Its child must price all negative contributions explicitly before deducing that a far-right rectangle is empty. Zero density alone can leave an isolated offending zero. An actual prime-side formula for the chosen signed kernel is the first test; a logarithmic-width result does not raise the fixed c.

The two-sided theta integral for \(\xi\) supplies another exact object. Rotate or split its \(x^{s/2}\) and \(x^{(1-s)/2}\) pieces together, retaining boundary terms and exponential height costs. The missing lemma is a phase-sensitive coupled bound stronger than separate absolute values. Left-first arguments are useful if that estimate is easier, even though the conclusion reflects to the right. Ordinary reflected half-planes, horizontal gaps, density-selected rectangles and finite-height discs remain valid lower-priority geometry, not new all-height improvements.

### F23/F26.H/F26.J — Strict positivity, heat and Jensen

For \(E_h(z)=\xi(1/2+h-iz)\), the actual shifted Hermite–Biehler diagonal is
\[
K_h(z,z)={|E_h(z)|^2-|E_h^\#(z)|^2\over4\pi\Im z}.
\]
Strict positivity in the upper half-plane implies \(c=1/2-h\). PSD alone is insufficient: a common nonreal factor can leave a PSD kernel and an upper zero; A10 gives \((z^2+1)e^{-iz}\). At h=0 the reflected functions coincide, so the endpoint requires all h>0, not strict positivity at h=0. First construct an arithmetic representation of this exact kernel with a controlled negative remainder and common-zero treatment.

The actual de Bruijn–Newman heat flow and Jensen polynomials are retained explicit families. Generic backward heat stability fails: positive even Fourier measures, even smooth densities, can produce nonreal zeros that become real under forward flow. An actual-zeta reverse-stability/coercivity theorem would need Euler/theta arithmetic, especially near collisions. Eventual Jensen hyperbolicity at each fixed degree leaves an unbounded degree/shift region; a useful root-confinement theorem must quantify that region and its transfer. These are structural high-upside projects, not consequences of positivity or finite experiments.

### N29 — Merge the prime-coefficient criteria; then vary the height geometry

A's density-subtracted log criterion and B's completed Laguerre criterion encode the same zero obstruction after a known analytic factor. Let \(Z(s)=(s-1)\zeta(s)\), \(s(z)=b+r(1+z)/(1-z)\), \(b>0\), \(b+r>1\). If \(\ell_n\) are the Taylor coefficients of \(\log Z(s(z))\), and \(a_n\) those of \(s'(z)\xi'/\xi(s(z))\), then
\[
a_n=(n+1)\ell_{n+1}+h_n,
\]
where \(h_n\) comes explicitly from the nonvanishing factor
\(\xi(s)/Z(s)=(s/2)\pi^{-s/2}\Gamma(s/2)\). A11 supplies the exact formulas. They are complementary arithmetic representations, not independent zero-free criteria.

Subexponential coefficient growth is equivalent to zero-freeness in \(\Re s>b\). The prime-side objects are explicit density-subtracted polynomial/Laguerre integrals. The known pole at one produces an exponential raw-prime contribution canceled by completion; demanding a subexponential **raw** prime sum is false even under RH. The first analytic task is a complete principal-subtracted saddle/log-scale estimate with complementary ranges and gamma terms intact. A zero of height \(\gamma\) can require very large degree; finite coefficients do not prove the limiting growth bound.

**N29.N1 — New pass 2: height-adaptive Cayley anchoring.** For \(\rho=b+\delta+i\gamma\), \(\delta>0\), its disk image has
\[
\log|z_\rho|^{-1}
={1\over2}\log{(r+\delta)^2+\gamma^2\over(r-\delta)^2+\gamma^2}.
\]
At fixed r and large height this is \(2r\delta/\gamma^2+O(\gamma^{-4})\). For the intended high-height bands the unconstrained optimizer \(r=\sqrt{\delta^2+\gamma^2}\) satisfies the Euler-anchor requirement \(r>1-b\), and gives \(\operatorname{artanh}(\delta/r)\sim\delta/|\gamma|\). A height-band-adapted anchor \(r\asymp T\) therefore changes the degree needed for **order-one single-zero modulus amplification** from \(T^2/(r\delta)\) at fixed r to \(T/\delta\).

This is not a finite-degree detection theorem: zero contributions can cancel, and the coefficients now require two-parameter control in degree and r. The price is explicit: prime weights \(m^{-b-r}\), Laguerre argument \(2r\log m\), gamma contribution and endpoint costs all move. If the unconstrained optimizer lies below \(1-b\), the admissible supremum is instead at that boundary; the real-axis singular case is not an admissible Euler anchor at a prospective zero. The new missing lemma is a uniform principal-subtracted coefficient bound in a coupled degree/height regime, followed by a rigorous band-to-all-height transfer. Test the known pole cancellation and one off-line quartet first. If changing r merely moves the same exponential loss into the prime/gamma cancellation, keep the optimization as a diagnostic and stop the analytic claim.

### F26.O — Fredholm models with every compensator retained

The prime diagonal \(T_s=\mathrm{diag}(p^{-s})\) has \(\det(I-T_s)=1/\zeta(s)\) in \(\Re s>1\). Its Hilbert–Schmidt regularization extends farther, but
\(1/\zeta(s)=\det_2(I-T_s)e^{-P(s)}\): the omitted prime compensator carries the unresolved continuation. Bounded similarity does not repair the trace-class failure. A non-diagonal arithmetic operator remains a permissible new construction only after an exact determinant identity, prime-power coefficients and every factor where a zero can hide are supplied. The arithmetic residue resolvent in §9 is a different valid operator, with its own unproved source-specific estimate.
