statement:
# Cubic dual cube classes, their polar addback, and the remaining moment

**Status: independently reviewed by c21_all_branch_h within the stated inputs and scopes.** DQ1--DQ12 give fixed-class continuation and a precise remaining moment obstruction. No larger c is proved.

## Inputs and exact scope

Write `q_a=N(a)`, `b0=1-c0`, and work over `K=Q(omega)`. Column labels are
the original good primary ideal representatives, with the fixed excluded set
`S` containing the primes above 6. Row elements include all units and all
fixed-prime valuations. No moving prime is put in `S`.

The inputs are the source coefficient and original kernel in M (2.14)--(2.15),
the ordinary finite-order Hecke functional equation and exact root cancellation
in review-cycle-9 section 1, the cube-free cubic sieve M (5.15), and, where
explicitly stated, **I-HECKE** from the [research revision] input ledger. I-HECKE is the
inherited all-finite-order Hecke package on fixed buffered lines to the right
of `b0`; it is stronger than zeta nonvanishing alone. Fixed angular entire
continuation is a different, fixed-conductor input. No new uniform Hecke moment
is assumed here.

The balanced sector has independent smooth core norm selectors `q_c~D` and
`q_e~D`, possibly with separable interval endpoints. Both cores are squarefree
and nonunit. Its columns are `N1=c B^3`, `N2=e E^3`, and the full condition is

`(c,e)=(c,E)=(e,B)=(B,E)=1`.

The restrictions `(c,B)=1` and `(e,E)=1` are not imposed. The original profile
is `W0(x)=x^(-1/2)W(x)`, rapid with its required Euler derivatives at both
endpoints. Its original Mellin roots remain unchanged. Let `R` be the original
radial Fourier row kernel and `R_tilde` its Mellin transform, holomorphic on
`Re z>0` and rapidly decreasing on each fixed positive line. For

`xi=bar(alpha)^3`, `beta(c)=mu(c) overline(G(c))`,

the actual coefficient is

`C_k(cB^3)=beta(c) theta_c(k) xi(B) q_B`.

In particular there is no `(B,k)` mask in `C`. Put
`eta=theta_c overline(theta_e)`. Unit summation kills a pair unless
`eta|_{mu6}=1`; in a surviving pair the full row series is `6 L_K(z,eta)`.
Since `c,e` are nonunit, squarefree and coprime, this character is nonprincipal,
with primitive good conductor exactly `ce`.

All stated constants may depend on fixed buffers, fixed component data and
finitely many original profile seminorms. Heights have polynomial cost, absorbed
by the original rapid Mellin decay. Small contour parameters are fixed in terms
of the final epsilon before any scale varies. Nothing is asserted uniformly as
such a parameter tends to zero. Products on Mellin lines use the same complex
`z`, never an unjustified absolute square.

## DQ1--DQ2. Exact cube classes and their natural zeros

Every dual ideal has a unique factorization

\[
 n=d\kappa^3,\qquad d\text{ cube-free}.
 \tag{DQ1}
\]

There is no condition `(d,kappa)=1`. Writing `d=d1 d2^2`, the two `di` are
squarefree and coprime. The primitive good conductor of the cubic character
induced by `d` is `rad(d)=d1 d2`, not generally `d`.

The root-cancelled core character is
`psi_n(c)=theta_c(lambda) overline(theta_c(n))`. Thus

`psi_(d kappa^3)(c)=psi_d(c) 1_(c,kappa)=1`.

The first factor retains every natural zero from `d`, including a prime whose
exponent in `d` is two; the second retains all cube-factor zeros. For one
surviving pair `(c,e)` and fixed `d`,

\[
 \sum_\kappa\overline\eta(d\kappa^3)q_{d\kappa^3}^{z-1}
 =\overline\eta(d)q_d^{z-1}Z_{ce}(3-3z),\qquad
 Z_{ce}(s)=\zeta_K(s)\prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-s}).
 \tag{DQ2}
\]

This fixed-class series converges absolutely for `Re z<2/3`. It includes the
fixed-prime row factors. One can first derive the full dual-series identity
on `Re z<0` and then continue each fixed class. The sum of all continued
classes is not asserted to converge normally on a positive `z` line.

## DQ3--DQ5. Exact Type-I addback and a coefficient obstruction

Use the actual source decomposition

`I_Y=-m_Y*m_Y*1`, `m_Y=mu 1_(q<=Y)`, `C=J[mu]`.

The CP21 source identity is

\[
 J[v]_k(cB^3)=q_B\xi(B)\overline{G(c)}\theta_c(k)
 \sum_{t\mid B}w_t v(ct^3)1_{(t,k)=1},
 \qquad w_t=q_t^{-1/2}\overline\xi(t).
\]

For `t|B,u|E` define

`r(t,u)=product_(p|tu,p not dividing ce) p`,
`Delta_r(z;eta)=product_(p|r)(1-eta(p)q_p^(-z))`.

The exact Mellin coefficient for the II addback is

\[
 \mathcal I_Y(c,e;B,E;z)=
 \sum_{t\mid B,\ u\mid E}
 w_t\overline{w_u}\,I_Y(ct^3)I_Y(eu^3)
 \Delta_{r(t,u)}(z;\eta).
 \tag{DQ3}
\]

Primes of `tu` dividing `ce` already have natural zero and do not require a
second deletion. Own-column overlaps remain allowed. These factors are
`Delta_r(z;eta)` on the original row line, not guessed factors at `1-z`.

Let `W_D(c,e;B,E)` be the two balanced core selectors times
`bar(W0(q_c q_B^3/D)) W0(q_e q_E^3/D)`. The ordinary FE is

`L(z,eta)=A(z)(q_c q_e)^(1/2-z) epsilon(eta)L(1-z,bar eta)`,

where

`A(z)=3^(1/2-z)(2 pi)^(2z-1) Gamma(1-z)/Gamma(z)`.

The exact Gauss cancellation is
`beta(c) bar(beta(e)) epsilon(eta)=mu(c)mu(e)eta(lambda)`.
Consequently the fixed-class projection of the original signed CC-minus-II
kernel, on `0<a<2/3`, is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac6{2\pi i}\int_{(a)}&\widetilde R(z)A(z)(K/D^2)^z q_d^{z-1}\!
\sum_{\substack{c,e>1\ {\rm sf},\ (cB^3,eE^3)=1\\
                 \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
\sqrt{q_cq_e}(q_Bq_E)^{1+3z}\xi(B)\overline\xi(E)\,
W_D(c,e;B,E)\\
&\qquad\times\psi_d(c)\overline{\psi_d(e)}Z_{ce}(3-3z)
\left[\mu(c)\mu(e)-\mathcal I_Y(c,e;B,E;z)\right]\,dz.
\end{aligned}
\tag{DQ4}
\]

The core powers follow exactly from
`(ce)^(1/2-z)(c B^3/D)^z(e E^3/D)^z
=sqrt(ce)D^(-2z)(B E)^(3z)`.
There is one row Mellin variable. This formula applies the same class
projector to both signed terms. It does not import the whole-II bound into a
restricted dual-class theorem, nor identify this analytic class with a physical
cube-row projection.

There is an immediate coefficient counterexample to universal CC--II
identification. Take `B=E=1`, `c=pq`, `e=r`, with distinct primes all beyond
the Type-I cutoff, in permitted unit-neutral ray sectors. Then

\[
 I_Y(c)=I_Y(e)=-1,\qquad
 \mu(c)\mu(e)-I_Y(c)I_Y(e)=-2.
 \tag{DQ5}
\]

Such columns can be taken in balanced norm ranges whenever the cutoff permits
two rough factors in one column, as in the intended application. More generally
the local coefficient identity already holds independently of a range choice.
For `d=lambda`, `psi_d(c)=1` on good cores, so the same discrepancy occurs in
the principal fixed-ray class. It persists in the class pole coefficient.
This disproves a termwise or universal coefficient/pole equality with II. It
does not disprove a separate aggregate signed cancellation theorem.

## DQ6--DQ8. A fixed-class polar asymptotic relative to I-HECKE

Define the original balanced polar form

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathscr A_d(D)=
\sum_{\substack{c,e>1\ {\rm sf},\ (cB^3,eE^3)=1\\
                 \eta|_{\mu_6}=1}}
&\mu(c)\mu(e)\psi_d(c)\overline{\psi_d(e)}
\sqrt{q_cq_e}(q_Bq_E)^3\xi(B)\overline\xi(E)\,
W_D(c,e;B,E)\\
&\times\prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-1}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{DQ6}
\]

Let `kappa_K=Res_(s=1) zeta_K(s)` and
`C_R=2 kappa_K A(2/3) R_tilde(2/3)`. This actual row-profile constant may
vanish; it is not replaced by a generic nonzero constant. For fixed
`b0<b<1` and `2/3<z1<(2+b)/3`, the candidate asymptotic is

\[
\boxed{
Q^{[d]}_{CC,\mathrm{bal}}
=C_R q_d^{-1/3}K^{2/3}D^{-4/3}\mathscr A_d(D)
 +O_\epsilon\!\left(
D^{2b+1+\epsilon}(K/D^2)^{z_1}q_d^{z_1-1+\epsilon}
\right).}
\tag{DQ7}
\]

This is a fixed-class statement; displayed conductor factors describe its
uniformity in `d`. It is not a normally convergent sum over all `d`.

Here is the density-weighted core continuation needed for the error. For a
finite-order core character `chi`, with all natural zeros and finite deletions
retained, write `s=3-3z`. Its Euler series factors as

\[
\prod_p\left(1-\chi(p)(1-q_p^{-s})q_p^{-w}\right)
=\frac1{L^S(w,\chi)}
\prod_p\left(1+
 \frac{\chi(p)q_p^{-w-s}}{1-\chi(p)q_p^{-w}}
\right).
\tag{DQ8}
\]

The second product is absolutely convergent when `Re w+Re s>1`, with
`Re w>0`. Fixed buffered core lines `Re w=b>b0` are therefore permitted
while `Re z<(2+b)/3`. I-HECKE bounds the reciprocal factor with subpower
actual finite conductor and height cost. The finite factors required by the
original column restrictions are retained before their subpower bounds; they
cannot be silently absorbed in fixed `S`. For good primes `q_p>=7`, their
local denominators stay uniformly away from zero on the fixed contours used
here. Fixed small-prime factors are kept separately.

Insert the complete `(c,e)=1` projector before separating the two core sums.
After `c=g c',e=g e'`, the Möbius/density weights and squarefree constraints
are exact; the positive majorant has a convergent `g^(-2b+epsilon)` sum.
For fixed `B,E`, the two masks `(c,E)=(e,B)=1` are finite core deletions.
Core Mellin inversion and (DQ8) give a bound
`D^(2b+1+epsilon) q_d^epsilon` with polynomial height. Because `q_c,q_e~D`,
the original rapid profile at `q_c q_B^3/D` and `q_e q_E^3/D` pays arbitrary
powers of `q_B,q_E`; all outside cube sums and their deletion costs converge.
Separable hard core endpoints follow from partial summation with the same
buffered bounds. Only finite-order core characters are asserted here.

In the fixed-class formula shift the row contour right from `a<2/3` to `z1`.
The only pole crossed is the zeta pole in `Z_ce(3-3z)`, whose residue is

`-(kappa_K/3) product_(p|ce)(1-q_p^(-1))`.

The right-shift identity is `I_a=I_z1 minus residues`, giving the positive
factor `6/3=2` in `C_R`. The gamma pole at `z=1` is not crossed, and the
original row transform is holomorphic throughout. The last-line bound is
exactly the error in (DQ7).

For `b=.8749`, `z1=.95`, and `K<=D^.87653`, the error for fixed `d` has
exponent `1.6825035`. The available estimate
`A_d(D)<<D^(2b+1+epsilon)q_d^epsilon` gives a leading exponent approaching
`2.000793294079928...`. Paying that fixed-class main term at this geometry
requires `A_d(D)<<D^(10/3)K^(-2/3)`, exponent `2.74898`, whereas
`2b0+1=2.749773294079928...`. This small gap belongs only to a fixed-class
polar estimate; the noncube aggregate is still unpaid.

For the prescribed fixed finite-row component `rho`, the class density becomes

`L_K(3-3z,bar(rho)^3)
 product_(p|ce)(1-bar(rho(p))^3 q_p^(-3+3z))`,



## DQ9. The complementary classes force the opposite pole

For any finite collection `F` of cube-free classes, define its continued
complement by subtraction from the whole dual L-function. Exactly,

\[
L_{F^c}(1-z,\bar\eta)
=L(1-z,\bar\eta)-Z_{ce}(3-3z)
 \sum_{d\in F}\overline\eta(d)q_d^{z-1}.
\]

The whole nonprincipal L-function is entire at `z=2/3`; hence

\[
\operatorname*{Res}_{z=2/3}L_{F^c}(1-z,\bar\eta)
=\frac{\kappa_K}{3}
 \prod_{p\mid ce}(1-q_p^{-1})
 \sum_{d\in F}\overline\eta(d)q_d^{-1/3}.
\tag{DQ9}
\]

This is precisely the opposite of the selected classes' residue. The pole is
introduced by the class projection, not a pole of whole CC. Its complementary
CC addback is compulsory and cannot be reassigned to II. In particular, one
cannot sum infinitely many class residues term by term or declare the
fixed-class polar estimate to be the full signed remainder.

## DQ10--DQ11. The legitimate weighted cubic-sieve estimate

Retain the BC polynomial smoothing

`V(x)=(2 pi i)^(-1) integral exp(w^2)x^(-w) dw/w`,
`N=D^4 T^4`, `T=2+|Im z|`, `z=a+it`.

BC9--BC10 justify
`L(1-z,bar eta)=sum_n bar eta(n) q_n^(z-1)V(q_n/N)+error`.
The original finite-order FE, not an absolutely convergent series at `1-a`,
pays the error. After the outside FE its bound is
`O_J(D^(-2J)T^(-2J))`, harmless after absolute core counting and the original
profile. On dyads `q_n~M`, `q_d~U`, there are
`O_epsilon((M/U)^(1/3+epsilon))` possible cube factors `kappa`.

For each fixed `kappa` and common-core projector divisor `g`, retain
`(c,kappa g)=1` in the coefficients and `(d,g)=1` on the rows. Cubic reciprocity
separates the permitted fixed ray sectors. The normalized core energy is
`O((D/g)^(1+epsilon))`, so M (5.15) gives

`(D/g) [U+D/g+(UD/g)^(2/3)]`

up to arbitrarily small powers. The full common-core projector is inserted
before Cauchy--Schwarz. Its first contribution costs only a logarithm; the
other two `g` sums converge. Original outside cubes have rapid decay in this
balanced sector; their support masks remain in the coefficients before
positive estimates. Using the actual dual weight `M^(a-1)` gives

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal B^{\mathrm{dual}}_{M,U}(a+it)|
\ll T^A D^{2-2a+\epsilon}M^{a-2/3}
\left[U^{2/3}+DU^{-1/3}+D^{2/3}U^{1/3}\right].}
\tag{DQ10}
\]

The factor `D^(1-2a)` is the outside FE, another `D` is core energy, and
`(M/U)^(1/3)` counts cube factors. Thus the cube multiplicity is not omitted.
For a row `d=d1d2^2`, its actual primitive conductor is `rad(d)`, and every
natural zero at `d kappa` stays present. The cube-free sieve is applied on
its stated cube-free ideal index set, without replacing this conductor by
`q_d` in a separate Hecke bound or introducing `(d,kappa)=1`.

Summing `M>=U>=G` and using rapid decay beyond `N` yields, with fixed `a`
chosen inside the final epsilon budget,

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal B^{\mathrm{dual}}_{q_d\ge G}|
\ll T^A D^{2+\epsilon}
\left(1+\frac D G+\frac{D^{2/3}}{G^{1/3}}\right).}
\tag{DQ11}
\]

The harmless factors `N^a` and `K^a` are charged by this fixed choice for
`K<=D^B` with fixed `B`. The bound pays `q_d>=D^2` in this smoothed analytic
decomposition. It is not a physical-row sector theorem or an improvement of
the full original remainder. In particular, the long artificial smoothing
length by itself is not the dominant obstruction; `q_d<D^2` remains.

## DQ12. The dominant primitive band remains after removing cubes

The natural reflected row length in the balanced bare-cube sector is
`H=D^2/K`. Applying all three terms of the legitimate all-row sieve yields

\[
D^2+D^3H^{-2/3}+D^{8/3}H^{-1/3}
=D^2+D^{5/3}K^{2/3}+D^2K^{1/3}.
\tag{DQ12}
\]

At `K=D^.87653` the two loss exponents are `2.25102` and
`2.292176666666...`. The last term is already present for `kappa=1` and
squarefree `d~H`, so these rows have primitive conductor `q_d~H`. Removing
perfect cubes, or any fixed finite collection of cube classes, does not
remove this large-sieve loss.

The precise remaining task is a coefficient-specific primitive-row estimate
for the original two coprime Möbius columns, all their opposite-column masks,
fixed components, same-complex-variable profiles, and original signed II
subtraction. In the primitive band `d~H` the needed covariance budget before
the physical `H^(-1)` normalization is `H D^2`. The current cross-sieve
term loses

`D^(2/3) H^(-1/3)=K^(1/3)`.

This is an upper-bound obstruction, not a lower bound for the actual moment.
The fixed-class polar calculation proves neither that loss is necessary nor
that II cancels it. The actual residual remains the double-large-core CC
contribution minus the original whole II term. T05 pays its physical cube-row
II sector only and cannot replace this residual by a transformed class.

## Source anchors and review boundary

- [M](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md): conventions at lines 65--79;
  (2.14)--(2.15), the source coefficient and original kernel; section 4.1,
  definitions of `I_Y,J[v]`; (5.15)--(5.16), cube-free/all-row cubic sieve,
  near lines 913--924. Original profiles, full row set and fixed components
  remain part of the theorem, not disposable notation.
- [Ordinary row FE and exact root cancellation](../review-cycle-9.md):
  section 1, especially the FE near line 66 and (R1).
- [Cubic packet definitions](../cubic-packets.md): CP21--CP27,
  starting near line 385, exact completed `J[v]` coefficient, full masks,
  principal densities and original physical kernel; CP31--CP32 for the
  existing all-row sieve budget.
- [BC proof](cubic-mobius-core-moment.md): BC5, exact moment;
  BC7--BC10, positive row contour, FE and Gaussian dual approximation;
  BC12--BC13, natural zeros, moving finite twists and interval Möbius bounds.
  Its accepted reviewed bytes have SHA256
  `BD30C4EE717D3ABD6001D72BE1C115D5C420DDFCD1006F32F90961A3C68C41CB`.
- [[research revision] input ledger](../[research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]):
  I-HECKE near line 27; T01, distinct fixed angular continuation; T05,
  physical cube-row II with the original root-preserving profile.

Independent review accepted the density-weighted continuation, exact local deletions, right-shift residue sign, mandatory complement pole and weighted cube multiplicity/common-core projector. The whole signed estimate remains open.

Reviewed source SHA-256: `0d46f396d276659c8581d6fe81bf3a1f661a4940e7d9c93f4a4e1b1afc82ab56`. Review owner: `c21_all_branch_h`.

# [research revision]: adaptive conductor exclusion and an arbitrary-graph transport adapter for native H



## Compact worklog

Objective: obtain a useful estimate for the complete original-prime interaction in H, or a new actual-source obstruction which redirects a live signed strategy. Preserve both mark projectors and roots, all short pairs, original masks, both heights and physical normalization. During this lane the controller independently integrated c3=.125133; the live current-proof/index/scorecard now record it, with endpoint kernel replay pending. This lane does not contribute to that increase.

Read: [research revision] hard-upstream controller review and hard-covariance report, current attempt-index and H scorecard, [research revision] native joint coefficient identity JN/JNR, signed return JS/JSR, [research revision] prime/divisor interface JPS, [research revision] original-prime covariance, and the actual manuscript B1/B2 interfaces. Adjacent exact-receipt.json binds the actual bytes of fifteen source files; Section6 gives their exact equation return map.

Completed mathematical derivation: a common quadratic core of the row frequency divides BOTH good primitive prime-variable conductors. This places even mark-adaptive low-conductor selections inside a row-only set of size O(N sqrt(D)). Applying the accepted native tensor uncertainty estimate gives a squared-mass fraction O(K sqrt(D)/N). At the physical pressure point this excludes fixed-fraction norm compression to conductor D=Z^d when d<.006. It is not a lower bound on the signed H pairing.

Second, materially distinct route completed: extend the accepted radial bounded-degree signed covariance estimate to its transported/centered version for arbitrary row/mark-independent prime graphs. A deliberately coarse absolute transport difference is O(G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)); its return fits the physical budget throughout the accepted graph-degree gate. This removes the prior norm-gap-only transport restriction for this sparse-graph range. The raw graph estimate was already proved in JSR19; the new claim is its transport/centering compatibility, not a newly paid raw H sector. It does not cover all far pairs.

Final handoff protocol: exact evidence, full final readback, hash-bound freeze, STOP and release only this claim; the freeze record and final tool receipt certify those operational steps separately. Mathematical residual: complete signed original-prime covariance outside the sparse graphs, and the other H branches; no whole-H saving is claimed.

## 1. Exact source and normalization

The field is the Eisenstein field, with q the ideal norm and the original primary, fixed-ray, six-unit and fixed bad-place conventions. No squarefree-integer-norm substitute is made. In the original hard block the distinct long prime ideals pi,pi' have distinct rational norms in the original windows q_pi,q_pi' asy N; their opposite equal-norm orientations are also excluded. Original short sources g,g' are good squarefree rationally primitive ideals of norms asy G. Both ordered short sources are retained, including g=g'. The ideal core is the actual bounded complex h((g,g')), and the rational gcd screen is evaluated on q_g,q_g'. The hard range has N>C_orig(K+L+G^2), C_orig G<A0 and L<=sqrt(N), so the original long/short collision screens simplify exactly as in JSR17--18; no row or mark opposite-coprimality screen is added.

The source coefficient and mark masses are

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P.

The two arrays are independent original arrays. Each actual term retains u_1(P)/sqrt(q_P), conjugate(u_2(P'))/sqrt(q_P'), both projectors 1_(P,Rg)=1 and 1_(P',Rg')=1, native phases and the two original separating-height factors. The complete common core can be left as its bounded h or fully inverted and then recombined; no individual positive divisor child replaces it.

Write S(N,L)=N+L+(NL)^(2/3). The target RAW covariance is

    G K S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.

P_orig denotes the actual original component coefficients, kernel scalars and weighted profile seminorms, not a replacement by one. The physical outside scalar is N^(-1) G^(-2), applied exactly once. Its target is K S(N,L)/(NG) times the same masses and profiles.

The physical pressure exponents are k=.835507578307735986..., nu=k+.003, gamma=.001 and ell=.170813789153867993..., with K=Z^k, N=Z^nu, G=Z^gamma and L=Z^ell. Here S asy N. The full all-branch deficit remains .004. The known .6738809116 positive-method calculation is neither used nor interpreted as an H lower bound.

## 2. New exact conductor geometry

Fix an original ordered long-prime pair. Set M=pi*pi', Q=q_M asy N^2. Fold the ENTIRE actual short-source sum and its complete bounded core into W(R,P,P'). It includes both projector indicators and all retained profile/component coefficients; it may depend on the prime pair. Its row support is inside the original O(K)-point disk, and the two mark supports have O(L) points. The original support injects modulo each long prime for sufficiently large Z in the pressure box. These properties survive the signed short-source recombination.

The accepted exact JN4--JN9 transform, with both character inversions and their Gauss factors, has native kernel

    chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4

times b(pi) conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_(pi,pi'), where b retains alpha and fixed ray data and the exact CRT root zeta is not set to one. The finite group is (O/M) x (O/pi) x (O/pi'), with Q^2 elements; its unitary transform has factor 1/Q and phases -Rh/M -Ps/pi +P's'/pi'. This already accounts for the two local 1/q factors. No new physical factor arises.

The kernel is zero unless

    U = {(h,M)=1, s nonzero mod pi, s' nonzero mod pi'}.

Choose integral representatives in bounded fundamental parallelograms, so q_h<=C Q and q_s,q_s'<=C N. For each nonzero h let a2(h) be the product of GOOD prime ideals at which v(h) is odd. For nonzero s let a3(s) be the product of good prime ideals at which v(s) is nonzero modulo 3. These are ideal products; neither integer squarefree kernels nor rational norms are factored in their place.

By JN17/JNR5 the first prime-variable good local exponent is 3v(h)+2v(s) modulo 6 and the second is 3v(h)+4v(s') modulo 6. The exact elementary equivalences are

    3A+2B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3),
    3A+4B=0 (mod 6) iff A=0 (mod 2) and B=0 (mod 3).

Consequently the two GOOD primitive finite conductor ideals are exactly

    f1_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s)),
    f2_good=lcm(a2(h),a3(s')).                         ([research revision].1)

In particular a2(h) divides both. A cubic mark factor cannot cancel the quadratic row factor, even at a shared good prime. At canceled conductor primes the original natural zero of the imprimitive character remains; ([research revision].1) does not turn it into an unrestricted constant. Fixed bad-place and angular data are retained separately. This is not an ordinary-Hecke prime-sum estimate.

Each conductor declaration freezes the chosen integral indices and takes the reciprocal finite-kernel character in that prime variable. The pair-dependent Fourier coefficient still samples h/(pi*pi'), s/pi and s'/pi'. Nothing here supplies a common prime-independent weight after regrouping by conductor; the original angular alpha factor also remains.

Let a frequency selector, allowed to depend on h,s,s', the prime pair and all coefficients, retain only points of U where AT LEAST ONE of q_f1_good or q_f2_good is <=D. It is pointwise contained in

    E_D x (O/pi) x (O/pi'),
    E_D={h !=0: q_a2(h)<=D}.                          ([research revision].2)

This containment, rather than commutation of the adaptive selector itself, is what permits the row-only uncertainty bound.

Here D denotes a conductor cutoff only; it is not the mark-collision divisor D in JSR11, or the Type I factor length D in SF2. No D*Omega factor from those different variables has been dropped. Their roots and complete projectors are inside the actual tensor before this Fourier statement is applied.

For 1<=D<=C Q, write the ideal of a chosen h as a_S*a*b^2, where a is good squarefree, q_a<=D, and a_S ranges over the finitely many squarefree products of fixed bad primes. The ideal class number is one and each principal ideal has six generators, so there are only a fixed number of possible representatives for each factorization. Elementary Eisenstein ideal counting gives

    #E_D <= C_S sum_(q_a<=D) sqrt(Q/q_a)
          <= C_S sqrt(QD).                            ([research revision].3)

The last inequality follows by partial summation from #ideals(q<=x)<=C x. Arbitrary powers at bad primes are already in b^2; their parity contributes only the finite a_S choice. For D beyond the stated range one uses #E_D<=Q. This estimate is uniform in the orientation of the chosen fundamental cell.

For every fixed physical mark pair, Cauchy on the O(K) rows gives squared Fourier mass <=C K #E_D/Q times its physical squared norm. Plancherel in both mark variables preserves this inequality because E_D is independent of those variables. The original signed short sum remains inside W throughout. Therefore ([research revision].2)--([research revision].3) imply

    ||1_U 1_{min(q_f1_good,q_f2_good)<=D} W_hat||_2^2
       <= C_orig K sqrt(D)/N ||W||_2^2.               ([research revision].4)

This holds for arbitrary further adaptive sub-selection. Accepted JNR5 independently gives

    ||1_U W_hat||_2^2
       >= [1-O_orig((1+L)/N)] ||W||_2^2.              ([research revision].5)

Thus, when the denominator is nonzero, the eligible-mass fraction in ([research revision].4) is at most C K sqrt(D)/N divided by the bracket in ([research revision].5). If W is zero, no nonvanishing is claimed.

At the pressure point D=Z^d, the upper fraction is O(Z^(-.003+d/2)). In particular D=Z^.004 captures O(Z^(-.001)), and the good-finite-principal choices D=1 capture O(Z^(-.003)). A fixed positive fraction in this coordinatewise norm-approximation strategy requires D at least a constant multiple of (N/K)^2=Z^.006. These are squared-mass statements about the exact native tensor, not size statements about its signed pairing with the character kernel.

The sample cutoff D=Z^.004 is a concrete frequency threshold only. The .004 H pressure deficit does not by itself impose that conductor budget, and no such identification is used in a return estimate.

The joint product-conductor version is also useful: q_f1_good*q_f2_good<=Y forces q_a2(h)<=sqrt(Y), hence its squared-mass fraction is at most C K Y^(1/4)/N divided by the same eligible bracket. A fixed fraction therefore requires Y at least a constant multiple of (N/K)^4=Z^.012. A pair-product budget Z^.008 still captures only O(Z^(-.001)). Thus the common quadratic conductor cannot be allocated independently between the two cubic marks to evade the count. For Y>C Q^2 the trivial fraction bound is used.

The representative convention is material: the result is for bounded integral lifts, which are exactly what makes a proposed small-conductor reciprocity argument quantitative. Adding arbitrary modulus multiples is not a permitted way to preserve the claimed conductor budget. The original Fourier value itself is independent of that presentation; a route using unbounded alternative lifts would have to charge its new support, conductor and moving weights separately.

## 3. Second route: arbitrary-graph transport and centering

JSR19 proves for an arbitrary original row/mark-independent directed graph E with both degrees <=B (possibly frozen separately with each short pair) that

    |C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359)
             N^(103/359) S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.

It is already an all-short-pair bound and keeps both mark projectors via their complete signed divisor expansion and lcm Schur sum. At the pressure point its sufficient degree exponent is .056035346678811698... with a fixed small power buffer. The accepted transported/centered theorem, however, was proved only for the specified norm-gap graph; it cannot be inherited for arbitrary masks.

A new elementary adapter suffices. The row transport moves only its smooth profile rho(R/sqrt K) to rho((R+P+P')/sqrt K), keeping the original sharp R support. The smooth compact-annulus extension is the actual one in RH/JS; its global mean-value bound is C sqrt(L/K)||grad rho||_infinity. Since |P|,|P'|<=C sqrt(L), this applies even when the segment between the two arguments crosses the edge of the original smooth support. No sharp indicator is differentiated.

For each frozen ordered short pair there are O(NB) long-prime edges. There are O(G^2) such short pairs and O(K) actual rows. Native a(pi), xi(g), all characters and their natural zeros have modulus at most one, and the complete original core has modulus at most one. The two absolute mark sums satisfy, with their roots intact,

    (sum_P |u_1(P)|/sqrt(q_P))
    (sum_P' |u_2(P')|/sqrt(q_P'))
       <= C L sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2).

This charges BOTH mark counts explicitly, rather than importing an unproved submask version of a signed sieve norm. The source and short profiles are charged to their original seminorms. Thus the full transport error is bounded by

    |C_E^tr-C_E|
       <= C_orig G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
             sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.             ([research revision].6)

At S>=N the ratio to the target is <=C G B L sqrt(L/K); its pressure exponent is gamma+b+3ell/2-k/2, negative for the entire accepted degree gate. This does not appeal to signed-mask monotonicity or to a row character estimate after an additive twist. All projector deletions occur only inside this explicit absolute error bound, after the exact full difference has been written.

For completeness, the genuine common-unit Jacobi correction is also paid on every such graph. Its local numerator and denominator are exactly JSR28:

    C1(T)=J_+(pi) J_-(pi') chi_pi(T) chi_pi'(T)^(-1),
    h1(T)=product_(p|pi*pi') (q_p^2-3q_p+3-1_(p|T)).

The two local convolution minus signs cancel. Both Jacobi sums have square-root modulus, giving |C1(T)/h1(T)|<=C N^-3, uniformly even at an exceptional total T divisible by one of the primes. An absent third local character is initially the unrestricted constant; replacing it by a unit indicator is justified only because the actual marks lie below both primes. Its induced subtraction is exactly the displayed Jacobi term, not a zero or a supposed principal-character average.

The remaining folded weight retains chi_R(uv)^3, the common-short-divisor puncture, all projectors and all profiles. Absolute summation over the actual graph as above gives

    |M_E^(J,tr)|
       <= C_orig G^2 K B L/N^2
               sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.          ([research revision].7)

This is the full mean including all mark off-diagonals. The N^-2 comes from O(NB) prime pairs times N^-3, not from an additional Fourier normalization. The sharp row support remains on R=T-P-P', and supported totals inject modulo pi*pi' because Q>C_orig(K+L). Thus the smooth transported factor is genuinely constant on each supported residue-total fibre. All original unit/ray components are folded with their own coefficients; there is no division by six.

Writing R_E^(J,tr)=C_E^tr-M_E^(J,tr), the elementary triangle inequality, ([research revision].6)--([research revision].7) and the inherited JSR19 prove the explicit all-short-pair return

    |R_E^(J,tr)| <= Z^epsilon sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig *
       [ G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359) N^(103/359) S(N,L)
         + G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K)
         + G^2 K B L/N^2 ].                           ([research revision].8)

The same formula without the last term controls the uncentered transported covariance. It holds for every graph with both degrees <=B, independent of live marks and rows; the graph and its bounded complex edge weight may be frozen with each original short pair. Empty graphs, bounded B and bounded source windows cause no exception. One may replace the degree condition by the corresponding two absolute Schur row-sum bounds if the edge count in ([research revision].6)--([research revision].7) is interpreted with absolute edge weights.

Three sufficient conditions for payment by the ORIGINAL target, with a fixed small power buffer, are

    B <= K^(128/359) N^(-103/359) G^(-462/359),
    G B L sqrt(L/K) <= 1,
    G B L/N^3 <= 1.                                  ([research revision].9)

The first is exactly the old raw-graph gate. The second and third are new explicit adapter gates, obtained using S>=N and therefore sufficient without an unproved S asymptotic. At the physical pressure point set B=floor(Z^(11/200)). The three relative exponents are respectively

    -.001035346678811698...,
    -.105533105423066003...,
    -2.288708945769339965....                         ([research revision].10)

Choose the total epsilon allowance smaller than one quarter of the first displayed margin, and distribute it through the finitely many inherited divisor and conductor losses. Heights are treated by the actual profile integrals, not by this epsilon budget. Multiplying ([research revision].8) by N^-1 G^-2 yields the complete physical bound

    N^-1 G^-2 |R_E^(J,tr)|
       <= Z^epsilon K S(N,L)/(NG)
               sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,          ([research revision].11)

for this graph range. Every term of the triangle is paid separately before that conclusion.

This adapter was unavailable in the prior stated theorem: JSR1/JSR25--30 explicitly restrict their sharper filtered transport argument to the norm-gap graph. The deliberately cruder estimate above is adequate for sparse graphs and requires no separability or small Fourier mass of their edge mask. Its radial raw covariance bound is inherited; calling ([research revision].11) a newly paid raw-H sector would overstate the result.

## 4. Source-specific far masks and full return details

One eligible new transported mask uses the ACTUAL primary generators, with any frozen lattice displacement z0, and Y>=1:

    E_geo(pi,pi') = 1_(q_(pi'-pi-z0)<=Y)
                   1_(|q_pi-q_pi'|>floor(Z^.05)),     ([research revision].12)

intersected with every original long-prime window and screen. A disk of radius sqrt(Y) contains O(Y+1) Eisenstein lattice points uniformly in its centre, so both degrees are O(Y+1), without invoking any primes-in-short-regions estimate. Take Y=Z^.055 times a fixed sufficiently small constant, or leave its harmless original constant in the buffered gate. This pays the transported/centered form on the displayed strict-far set. No assertion that every disk contains primes is necessary. For z0=0 its possible norm gaps extend to O(sqrt(NY)+Y), vastly larger than the existing Z^.05 near band, although no claim of populated endpoints is used.

A second entirely finite illustration avoids geometric support assumptions. From two actual ordered prime lists with all cross norm gaps >floor(Z^.05), take equally sized sublists pi_0,...,pi_(m-1) and pi'_0,...,pi'_(m-1), and retain edges j-i modulo m in {0,...,B-1}, where B<=m. This is a B-regular directed bipartite graph with mB literal far edges. Its definition is independent of rows, marks and heights. The theorem applies to the actual available lists; it is not an unproved asymptotic assertion about their cardinality. All native coefficient signs survive. A small finite graph check below tests only this support statement.

The following items delimit the original return, including the cases which would invalidate a whole-H claim:

1. Both original preprojection corrections vanish on the distinct-rational-norm prime packet by SUPPORT, before any bound. Equality pi*g=pi'*g' is impossible because a long prime cannot divide the opposite short source. Equality P*pi*g^3=P'*pi'*g'^3 is also impossible because the opposite mark and short source are both smaller than the long prime. Their intersection is empty. The same argument applies to every subgraph above. It makes no assertion about these corrections in nonprime or other source branches.

2. After g,g' are fixed, put d=(g,g'), u=g/d, v=g'/d. The exact row character is chi_R(pi*pi'*u*v)^3 times 1_(R,d)=1. Opposite ideal orientations in u,v do not cancel, and both distinct long primes survive in the good primitive row conductor. There is consequently no newly omitted principal row in the inherited JSR19 row estimate. The original mark projectors expand into every D,D' with genuine q_D^-1/2 and q_D'^-1/2 roots and the full [D,D'] kernel; the JSR14--15 lcm Schur sum includes all their cross terms. The original core h(d) is never replaced by the d=1 child or a positive mean.

3. The tensor estimate ([research revision].4) retains ALL short-pair signs before its norm is taken, all original marks and all prime-pair phases. The graph bound takes the permitted absolute sum over O(G^2) ordered short pairs only after each inherited raw signed row estimate; the new transport and mean estimates explicitly charge G^2. Neither result presumes a coherent G saving. g=g', shared short primes, opposite short orientations and the exceptional short-row mode are included.

4. Write the original common row factor of a pair of separated components as rho_(theta,theta'). It is a smooth compact-annulus function with the actual norm-height difference and the original two scalar kernel factors outside. Its global gradient costs at most a fixed polynomial in BOTH original height vectors. The inherited row estimate costs (3+|t-t'|)^(2delta+epsilon) and a fixed radial-variation seminorm, with delta=103/718. Both costs are bounded by a fixed product polynomial in t and t', and are integrated against the PRODUCT of the two actual common logarithmic densities from M B2.22. That density has all required fixed weighted L1 moments by M B2.21--22. Fix its differentiation order above these powers once, before integration. Finite source components and their mixed covariances are included with their actual coefficients. There is no row-dependent density, equality of heights, zero-height specialization or assertion that unbounded heights are Z^epsilon.

5. Both orientations of the strict-far mask are kept literally in ([research revision].12), and graph edges are ordered. For unequal arrays their reverse is not automatically a conjugate or twice a real part. Equal-rational-norm orientations remain absent by the ORIGINAL gcd screen. All actual sharp row/source/short/mark cutoffs remain on their original variables and at their literal endpoints. Only the smooth row factor is transported. Subtracting a graph from the far set is an exact signed partition, with the complement left as its own unestimated form.

6. Apply the original full-series tail bound M B2.23/B2.37 BEFORE common separation or transport. The original discarded argument is at least Z^(tau_ref/2); the source/root envelope and all original counts have a fixed polynomial majorant Z^Btail independent of the Schwartz order. Taking that order above 1+2(Btail+A)/tau_ref gives an arbitrary-power linear remainder. Each mixed retained/discarded pair is bounded absolutely by this remainder times a fixed absolute polynomial majorant for the complete opposite side; enlarge A once for both mixed terms and the double tail. Every graph selector has modulus <=1, so this absolute tail proof applies to it. Define the transported object using the same retained components and leave the original discarded tail unchanged, or include its exact correction. A shifted tail is not assigned its old argument without proof.

7. These claims are uniform for all original finite component pairs and all heights in the stated SAME-SCALE prime block, and for other literal blocks satisfying all displayed endpoint, injection and payment gates. They do not sum an independently widened scale range, give arbitrary unequal-block interactions, estimate original composite/prime-composite Type II covariances, or transfer a squarefree-prime auxiliary bound to all H. The already accepted prime-completion and von Mangoldt identities remain exact tools, but are not invoked to pretend that this sparse prime graph pays their other ordered branches. There is no new small-prime, exceptional-character or inert contribution silently deleted: those are outside this theorem's specified original degree-one prime packet and remain obligations of the full H return.

## 5. Strongest objections and decisive limitations

**Does adaptive mark dependence defeat ([research revision].4)?** It defeats the older argument if one merely asserts that a selected set commutes with mark Fourier transform. Here the selector need not commute: its support is contained in the proven row-only set E_D by ([research revision].1). Positive squared Fourier masses can first be enlarged to that set. Only then are the two mark Plancherel identities used. This is precisely the previously unproved conductor-count adapter mentioned at JN immediately before its second-mean discussion and excluded from JNR6's mark-independent scope.

**Do primitive-conductor cancellations, squares or natural zeros defeat it?** Squares are the reason for the sqrt(QD) count: they are all included, not discarded. Odd row valuations force exponent 1,3 or5 modulo6, so neither cubic mark exponent can cancel them. Canceled factors keep their original natural zero. The zero representative and h divisible by either long prime are absent from U; JNR5 proves that those zero-kernel frequencies cannot hold the missing tensor mass in this box. A good finite principal character is included at D=1. Its small NATIVE TENSOR NORM FRACTION does not mean that its signed contribution to H is paid.

**Does this prohibit a signed orbit reduction?** No. JN22--24/JNR9 already provide an exact kernel-invariant orbit projection which can discard tensor norm while preserving its kernel pairing. ([research revision].4) is a restriction on coordinatewise low-conductor NORM approximation of the actual unprojected tensor, even with mark-adaptive coordinates. It does not apply to a new orbit-weighted tensor, an unbounded-lift reparameterization, or an argument that directly controls a small signed pairing without approximating the tensor. These are the legitimate directions to pursue; their moving weights and return costs must still be proved. The live residual after the first approach is signed averaging allowing conductor at least on the Z^(.006-o(1)) scale, or a controlled orbit recombination, not a missing bound on a few principal frequencies.

To test the tempting but invalid inference that a small low-conductor norm fraction already buys the .004 physical saving, a coarse complete Cauchy calculation can be made. For the fully recombined all-g tensor, |W(R,P,P')| is bounded by O(G^2) times the original two rooted mark coefficients and original profile norms, so ||W||_2<=C G^2 sqrt(K) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2). The set in ([research revision].4) has at most O(N^3 sqrt(D)) eligible coordinates by ([research revision].3). Kernel Cauchy and ([research revision].4) give the following deliberately coarse certificate

    |C_low| <= C G^2 K N^3 sqrt(D)
                       sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,  ([research revision].13)

after summing O(N^2) original prime pairs. Its ratio to GKN is G N^2 sqrt(D). Even D=1 is not paid by this crude procedure. This is solely an UPPER-BOUND METHOD calculation; no lower bound for C_low or H follows. A smaller set from the cubic conductor restrictions might improve it, but ([research revision].13) is enough to reject the claimed automatic .004 return. We do not substitute this certificate for a new analytic result.

**Can sparse-graph coverage finish the far set?** The new adapter supplies no saving in B beyond JSR20. For a complete bipartite prime set with m,m' vertices, any cover by graphs of maximum degree B requires at least max(m,m')/B layers, simply by counting all neighbours of one vertex. Summing ([research revision].8) in absolute value across such a cover reproduces the full degree price; it does not recover the cancellations between layers. This exact combinatorial obstruction is not an H lower bound. The remaining original-prime form is C_far-C_E on every frozen short pair, with the same heights, roots, projectors and core; it has not been estimated by the present work.

## 6. Candidate comparison and actual source map

| Mechanism tested | What was genuinely proved here | Decision / residual |
|---|---|---|
| Adaptive low-conductor selection after the EXACT native joint transform | Common quadratic conductor factor, ideal-frequency count and ([research revision].4) for mark-adaptive selectors; exponent threshold .006 | Redirect norm-compression route to high-conductor signed averaging or a priced orbit reduction. Does not estimate H. |
| Transport the inherited arbitrary bounded-degree signed graph theorem | Absolute transported-profile error, complete graph Jacobi count, all-height/tail return ([research revision].8)--([research revision].11) | New prerequisite removal at b=.055. Raw graph bound inherited; full graph and cross-branch return unpaid. |

No third generic reformulation was pursued. Neither approach imports a new Kloosterman, trace, metaplectic or moving-conductor theorem. The second uses the ALREADY reviewed all-height Hecke row bound only through JSR19; it does not strengthen or re-verify its published input.



Final mathematical verdict, pending independent review: ([research revision].1)--([research revision].5) supply a new actual-source adaptive-conductor obstruction, and ([research revision].6)--([research revision].11) remove a specific transport prerequisite for already-paid sparse raw graphs. They do not prove the complete original-prime H covariance, close any of its .004 pressure deficit, or establish a new c or kernel theorem. The strongest useful next target is a signed estimate for the exact native high-conductor/orbit aggregate, with its moving prime-pair Fourier weights and full small-gcd interaction retained. Repeating the separate positive sieve or covering the far set by absolute graph layers cannot furnish that estimate.

## 7. Evidence and STOP

The adjacent exact_checks.py uses only standard-library exact fractions and finite integer arithmetic. It verifies all216 local exponent triples, including108 odd-row cases which force both good conductor factors and12 cases with both good local factors principal; the three pressure-return exponents and all four corners of a conservative rounding box; and a six-edge strict-far graph on actual primary generators of split prime norms7,13,19 and31,37,43. That finite graph is a support illustration, not an instance proving the asymptotic H theorem. No numerical Fourier experiment is substituted for the Hilbert-space or ideal-counting proofs above.

## 6. What is actually paid; the unit and low-gcd complement

For w=1, r_w(t)=1_(t=1), so R25 returns exactly the ordered
all-prime pair scalar. For w_U(s)=1_(q_s>=U), r_w(t)=0 below U.
If U>1, R26 has only composite long products with a common core
of norm at least U and two distinct-norm prime cofactors. The core
itself can be prime or composite. There is no original prime-pair
coefficient.

This restricted form is not vacuous as an arithmetic expression:
if s is a good prime with q_s>=U and the other original factors
are eligible, r_w(s)=1 and R26 is nonzero. The review uses no
prime-counting asymptotic or covariance lower bound to establish
its analytic estimate.

For w_coprime(s)=1_(s=1), r_w(t)=mu(t). In particular the full
coefficient at n=r p, n'=r p' with r prime is the NEGATIVE of
R29 with w(r)=1. Coprime EXTRACTED labels therefore still create
shared composite long cores after full allocation summation.
The signs cannot be replaced by an independence heuristic.

The exact low complement w_<U=1-w_U has transform

    r_<U(t)=1_(t=1)-r_U(t).                         (R30)

For U>1 this is one at the unit, zero at 1<q_t<U and -r_U(t)
at q_t>=U. Consequently, after summing all label cells,

    C_all-prime = C_<U + C_>=U,
    C_<U = C_all-prime - C_>=U.                     (R31)

These are partitions of ordered AUXILIARY PAIRS, not a high/low
decomposition of a linear source. There is no invented additional
Cauchy cross term between the two pair masks. Every ordered
D,D' interaction already belongs to one of them.

Every pair with v=1 or v'=1 belongs to C_<U for U>1, including
unit/nonunit interactions. The unit self cell is not itself a pure
prime source: it contains the original long composite extensions
as well, as R29's preceding example shows. Actual primes have only
the v=1 nonzero allocation, so their full coefficient stays one
in the low complement. Both facts are needed for an honest return.

At the frozen pressure point

    K=Z^k, k=.835507578307735986...,
    N=K Z^.003, G=Z^.001,
    L=Z^.170813789153867993..., S(N,L) comparable to N,

the bound R5 divided by the original raw target G K S(N,L) is

    Z^epsilon [1 + Z^(.004-u)], U=Z^u.             (R32)

Thus U0=NG/K=Z^.004 pays the WHOLE high-gcd auxiliary pair
form at target size. The outside N^(-1)G^(-2) is unchanged
and cancels from this comparison. Away from this pressure point
one can use U0=max(1,NG/K); if NG/K<=1 the incumbent bound is
already target-sized. This convention introduces no new H scope.

However, R31 shows that at U0 an estimate for the full low form
at any proposed budget at least target size is equivalent, up to
an already target-sized additive error, to the same estimate for
the original all-prime form. In particular B's NEXT or A's HA27
is not yet an independently easier global theorem. This is the
strongest relevance limitation on the otherwise valid bound.

At present the low form has only the incumbent budget
Z^epsilon G(K+NG)S(N,L) times the original masses, obtained by
the EXACT identity R31, JPS24 and R5, not by signed-submask
inheritance. Its pressure exponent deficit remains .004.
No target-sized high-sector estimate justifies reducing that
incumbent bound or a unit/nonunit cross budget.

A cellwise continuation such as A's HA26 can still be a useful
research question. It must estimate the actual coupled truncated
coefficient R27, and return every other small-gcd cell, the unit
self term and all ordered unit/nonunit interactions. Even completing
the retained prime packet would leave the other original H branches
and quantitative zero-exclusion return. The accepted c0 remains
0.125113352960035869... without promotion.

# W60: prime-factor turnover is the missing cost in local coding

No arithmetic power saving or increase in c is proved. The two developed outputs are a source-specific obstruction to **every fixed-radius, short-displacement prime code/flow** (W60-12), and a cut obstruction to **all disjoint divisibility matchings**, including adaptive character-one pivots (W60-23). The first identifies a precise remaining arithmetic sector, beyond the previous fixed-pivot and unsigned homology calculations. The other four selected cards received the concrete first tests below; their proposed shortcuts fail at their stated scopes. No formalization, proof packet, or public claim is supplied.

The current written value stays c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636, gamma11=.8748540364. Its inherited analytic ancestry, positive-slot uniformity, and external definition/import/admission remain open. The accepted baseline is a research premise. Statements called proved below are author derivations submitted for independent review, not automatic project acceptance.

## 1. Frozen selection and evidence

The complete thirty-card seeds.md was written and read before detailed history/current-proof/index intake: SHA-256 **8d7f8088bcfa5b092f3aa457977361467dd57b3be242fd43d475de678a48cc5b**. All six groups and four recipes are retained. Literal p values are subjective generation typicality, not success probabilities. Recipe, frozen problem, stable prefix, and sampler hashes matched the assignment. An administrative search for the prefix exposed only coordination snippets before the seed freeze; that exposure is disclosed in the deck.

After source inspection, selection.json froze W60-28 (strongest bridge), W60-23 (protected high reach), and W60-12 (different mechanism), SHA-256 **8f8bcd2b7f4e9f0cae565fd46b0e0e888fc79d898e797d5bc9398fbb5f0c8fcb**. No complete mechanism was excluded; broad ancestors were not treated as family-wide failures. Three fresh independent OS-entropy stages used all remaining qualifying cards across every group. Each complete ordered pool was written, flushed, read back, and hashed before its own entropy was read. Rejection mapping is unbiased; all three first samples were accepted, so no rejection or redraw occurred.

| Stage | Complete pool size | Zero-based index | Card | Draw SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| p<.10 | 25 | 21 | 26 | bb88a9448eaa327c27a604238622df2224c05f0f15e8662640affda78b7c00f6 |
| p<.01 | 15 | 11 | 25 | f332a9e3627e0122890a69b794e792972540cc46f5a314217c8f36745cfebf61 |
| remaining wildcard | 25 | 24 | 30 | 47176f2c65bcedd2eb3ea4b684386ae4e6034c1aa3d42716765eaf438bbe2609 |

The six actual first tests are therefore 28,23,12,26,25,30. Only 12 and23 receive extended development. The rare/wildcard selections were not replaced by more convenient cards. Their exact failed realizations and viable but unpaid variants are preserved in Sections5-7. The other24 cards are untested, not disproved.

checks.py ran once and wrote checks-result.json, SHA-256 **b7483aa3f10da4532045ed4a6b764437cd33cbf37706478cda390525b46845d2**. It checks finite matching, actual quartic-character phases, 4,211 exact turnover incidences, rational thresholds, torsion determinants, and a Krylov determinant. Infinite and uniform conclusions depend on the written proofs, not those finite checks. The native H source inspection is documentary, not a synthetic native H evaluation.

## 2. A complete direct return, and the proposed code graph

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q and retain a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including every squareful/nonunit zero. Let S_q be the squarefree q-units, including1. No ideal/arithmetic-H source is substituted for this rational source. Write M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x)a(n).

**Matching return.** Suppose there is a disjoint pairing of some members of S_q, with each pair (u,v) satisfying

    a(u)=-a(v),  |u-v|<=C_chi min(u,v)^theta,  0<=theta<1.       (M1)

Finitely many exceptional pairs may be charged separately. Suppose the unmatched count through x is O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0, with delta<1. All pairs are in one global pairing; separate unrelated finite-cutoff matchings are not being silently glued.

Every pair wholly below x cancels exactly. A pair crossing x has its lower endpoint in [x-C_chi x^theta,x], so at most C_chi x^theta+1 distinct pairs cross. Coefficient moduli are1. Consequently

    |M_chi(x)| <= C_chi x^theta + O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).
                                                                  (M2)

Thus a common gamma=max(theta,delta)>0 gives the every-epsilon M bound. For Re(s)>gamma the integral

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx              (M3)

converges locally uniformly with all derivatives: choose the epsilon below the compact's distance to gamma, and absorb powers of log x. On Re(s)>1 it is exactly1/L(s,chi). The identity L F=1 continues meromorphically to the whole half-plane. A regular zero of L there is impossible. A principal pole at1 forces the reciprocal zero and causes no zero-exclusion exception. This covers every finite height and every imprimitive character directly, with its actual Euler-factor zeros retained. Constants/onsets may depend on each fixed chi. No growing-conductor estimate is asserted.

For simultaneous characters modulo a fixed q, sufficient edge conditions are mu(u)=-mu(v) and u=v mod q. They imply a(u)=-a(v) for every character; squareful and nonunit states still have zero mass. The matching hypothesis is OPEN at every improved exponent.

A plausible coded realization uses small symmetric differences of prime sets. For distinct unramified primes p,r,s and a squarefree m coprime to prs,

    u=mp, v=mrs, p=rs mod q
    => mu(u)chi(u)=-mu(v)chi(v).                              (M4)

These are three-coordinate exchanges between incomparable integers. For example6 and11 cancel for all characters modulo5. One-prime toggles are divisibility edges; two-coordinate exchanges preserve mu's sign and cannot cancel the principal source. A three-coordinate exchange is the first possible nondivisibility cancellation of this kind. Its geometric bill is m|p-rs|, not merely the Hamming length3. A complete matching must retain the common-cofactor and coprimality conditions, all unmatched states, and every cutoff crossing.

For targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4, M1-M2 with theta,delta<=gamma would give respectively c=.12515,1/6,1/4. The first would exceed c11 by10091/2500000000. These are conditional numerical returns; no matching input is supplied. The point of the next result is that **fixed code radius cannot supply the required absolute unmatched budget**, even if the codewords and flow coefficients are otherwise arbitrary.

## 3. Developed W60-12: exact phase compatibility and arithmetic isolation

### 3.1 A binary checksum does not automatically preserve a complex character

For a finite unramified prime set P and subset S, write w(S)=(-1)^|S| chi(product S). For a fixed nonempty toggle C,

    w(S symmetric_difference C)/w(S)
      =(-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                    product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).       (C1)

Therefore w(S xor C)=-w(S) for EVERY S if and only if

    chi(p)^2=1 for every p in C,
    (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)=-1.                            (C2)

Necessity follows by comparing S empty with each singleton in C; sufficiency is substitution. The hypothesis product_C chi(p)=1 alone is insufficient for an odd toggle when nonreal phases occur.

Actual counterexample: take the primitive quartic character mod5 with chi(2)=i, chi(3)=-i, chi(11)=1 and C={2,3,11}. The empty subset pairs1 with66 with opposite coefficients. But {2} pairs2 with33, whose actual coefficients are BOTH -i. All four integers are squarefree5-units. The exact script checks all eight states. The restricted edge6<->11 is valid; a code must track the state as well as its syndrome.

For a binary matrix A and principal chi, if the parity vector1 lies in the row space of A, parity is constant on every syndrome class and there is no within-class sign cancellation. If it does not, the full uncut cube has balanced parity in every class: translate by an odd element of ker A. The multiplicative cutoff need not respect that translation. This is elementary code duality, not a new theorem about arithmetic cancellation. C1-C2 identify the extra phase failure for the actual complex coefficients.

### 3.2 Turnover lemma: a short move must replace a large factor

For distinct positive integers n,m, put g=gcd(n,m). Then

    g divides n-m, so g<=|n-m|.                                 (C3)

If C>0, 0<=theta<1, and |n-m|<=C min(n,m)^theta, it follows exactly that

    n/g >= C^(-1) n^(1-theta).                                  (C4)

When n is squarefree, n/g is the product of the prime factors deleted from n. If all those primes are <=y and at most d are deleted, then n/g<=y^d. Thus n has NO such neighbor whenever

    n^(1-theta)>C y^d.                                         (C5)

This argument allows m to be squareful or nonunit: adding zero-mass auxiliary integer states does not help when an edge may delete at most d of n's prime factors. In particular it applies to the usual squarefree Boolean Hamming radius<=d, whose number of deleted coordinates is<=d. No coefficient estimate or character-distribution assumption is used.

### 3.3 A large actual isolated set exists on every sufficiently large shell

Fix q, C>0, an integer d>=1, and 0<=theta<1. Precisely, every graph edge {n,m} must satisfy the displayed distance bound and delete at most d prime factors from EACH squarefree endpoint when passing to the other endpoint. This condition is independent of a flow's orientation; an incoming edge cannot bypass the source-side budget. Squarefree Hamming radius<=d satisfies it, and optional zero-mass integer vertices are allowed subject to the same endpoint rule. Choose an integer

    k > d/(1-theta),   y=(2X)^(1/k).                            (C6)

Let V_X contain all products of k DISTINCT primes in

    (X^(1/k),(2X)^(1/k)].

Each n in V_X is squarefree, X<n<=2X, and for large X is coprime to the fixed q. All its primes are<=y. Since1-theta-d/k>0, inequality C5 holds for every n in V_X once X is sufficiently large. Hence every such vertex is isolated in the entire short-move graph, including possible neighbors outside this shell or cutoff.

The ordinary prime number theorem gives, for this FIXED k,

    t_X=#primes in the displayed interval
       ~ k(2^(1/k)-1) X^(1/k)/log X.

Unique factorization counts distinct vertices exactly as binomial(t_X,k). Therefore

    |V_X| ~ A_k X/(log X)^k,
    A_k=[k(2^(1/k)-1)]^k/k! >0.                                (C7)

Only fixed-relative-width intervals are used, not a primes-in-short-interval theorem or a growing-k substitution. For the external input, the published PNT was checked in the official [NIST DLMF27.12, equations4-5](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12). All deductions C3-C7 are given here. The constants can be tiny and the onset large; both are permitted and neither changes the power obstruction.

It follows that ANY disjoint matching in this graph leaves at least A_k X/(2(log X)^k) actual unit-modulus source coefficients unmatched on [X,2X], for every sufficiently large X. The absolute unmatched mass cannot be O(X^delta) for ANY delta<1. Thus the fixed-radius candidate cannot meet M2, at a near gain,1/6,1/4, or any other power-saving target.

This extends beyond integral matching. For an arbitrary complex edge flow F supported on the same graph, let div F(n) be its net outgoing mass, whenever defined. In any exact source decomposition a=div F+r, an isolated vertex satisfies r(n)=a(n). Hence

    sum_(X<n<=2X)|r(n)| >= |V_X|.                               (C8)

No choice of complex flow weights, linear combinations of codewords, or repeated local steps removes an isolated vertex. Chaining cannot start there. The result still holds for any uniformly bounded family of radii and for subpower inflation of C, by first replacing theta by a fixed slightly larger number below1. It does NOT cover growing radii, genuinely long edges, nonlocal auxiliary states with a different exact transfer, or a bound retaining signed cancellation among the isolated states.

| Intended exponent theta | Fixed radius d | k used | Strict isolation exponent1-theta-d/k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
|17497/20000=.87485|3|24|3/20000|
|5/6|3|19|1/114|
|3/4|3|13|1/52|

The first row has about X/(log X)^24 isolated24-prime products, all with principal coefficient+1. The next two rows use19- and13-prime products, with principal coefficient-1. This is a lower bound for the absolute residual and for those particular signed subcollections. It is NOT a lower bound for the complete signed residual or M_chi: different prime-count layers can cancel, and that cancellation remains an eligible arithmetic input.

### 3.4 What survives and what has changed

The remaining high-ceiling target is an exact phase-compatible interaction with enough **prime-factor turnover**, or a signed estimate for the smooth isolated complement coupled to other prime-count layers. At a vertex n with largest allowed deleted prime y, C4 requires at least

    ((1-theta)log n-log C)/log y

deleted prime factors. This is the quantity a growing code or multiscale construction must pay; a small Hamming distance by itself is the wrong budget. The concrete three-prime exchange M4 repairs the large-prime failure of deletion matchings but leaves the proved high-degree smooth obstruction. A future combined construction must estimate both parts and their signed interaction. No favorable coding distance or representation count pays that term.

Functional signature: actual squarefree mu-chi source; additive-near, bounded prime-turnover graph; exact coefficient cancellation/flow; C3 forces isolated high-degree products; complete unmatched-count return M1-M3. The new claimed record delta is C6-C8 for all fixed-radius local flows, plus the source-phase criterion C2 and explicit reopening condition. The general pairing return is existing transport ancestry. No literature priority is claimed.

## 4. Developed W60-23: all divisibility matchings have a prime cut

The exact deletion/contraction identity is retained, not claimed as new. For unramified p, put A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not|n)mu(n)chi(n) and B_p(X)=A_p(X)-A_p(X/p). Splitting according to p|n gives

    M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)
            =B_p(X)+(1-chi(p))A_p(X/p).                        (D1)

This is the full character defect, including squareful zeros. Choosing chi(p)=1 removes the interior twist but leaves B_p. W57's topology development already proves this identity, the weighted commutator, and the linear absolute bill for its canonical least-prime cone. This round tests whether an ADAPTIVE decision tree or arbitrary comparable-face matching could evade that specific cone.

## New quantitative theorem

For every required fixed finite ray, every nonzero integral h, and
each fixed buffered strip 1/2+epsilon<=sigma<=B, write T=1+|t|.
The full sixth-order family and each norm sector satisfy

\[
|\Psi_{\nu,d}(h,\sigma+it)|+|\Psi_\nu(h,\sigma+it)|
\ll Tq_h^4+T^3q_h^{6-2\sigma}.
\]

All original fixed-prime valuations are allowed. The constants depend
on the fixed level, S, rays and strip, not h or t. Finite squarefree
extraction transfers this with an arbitrarily small q_h^delta loss.
The exact forced-divisor identities give explicit polynomial g,h
growth, with all outside collision zeros retained.

Combined with [research revision] holomorphy, this justifies pole-free buffered
Mellin shifts for every finite row/divisor truncation. Summing the
coarse row powers over unbounded divisors is not justified. The
incidence mean, original product-kernel transfer and both moment
zero-frequency terms remain open.

The proof is in sixth-forced-divisors.md Sections 16--17, (50)--(59).
The controller derived fixed-argument Whittaker inversion;
review_cubic independently checked it. sixth_order supplied
the elliptic cutoff-resolvent construction. The controller supplied
the spinor spectral lower bound that makes the argument uniform at
all t; sixth_order and independent review_sixth checked that
identification and its constants. review_sixth then reviewed the
integrated theorem, including arithmetic powers and truncation limits.

At y_h=x/(2pi R_h), R_h=2q_h^2/sqrt(3), the exact local vector has
norm comparable to T^(-1)q_h^(2sigma-3). The large-order K expansion
has a dominant Gamma(w) term; its exponential size cancels the
Gamma(w+1) denominator. Compactness and whole-vector nonvanishing
handle bounded t. The x=2 leading constant is an asymptotic, not an
exact finite-height formula.

On the fixed arithmetic quotient the standard SU(2) type gives a
rank-two spinor bundle, with a flat unitary genuine twist. For
D=-(Omega1+Omega2),

\[
D=2\nabla^*\nabla-\tfrac32
=2\mathscr D_{\mathrm{spin}}^2+\tfrac32,\qquad
\lambda(w)=\tfrac32-2(w-\tfrac12)^2.
\]

Essential self-adjointness and compact-support form positivity imply
spec(D) is contained in [3/2,infinity). For v=sigma-1/2,
the distance of lambda(w) to this half-line is 2(v^2+t^2) if
|t|<=v and 4v|t| otherwise. It is at least v(v+|t|), giving
a resolvent bound O_epsilon(T^(-1)) for all t.
An initially suggested extra factor two in that lower bound was
withdrawn: t=v/2 disproves it. The stated weaker inequality suffices.

Subtract ALL incoming cusp terms with fixed cutoffs. The forcing
is compactly supported and O(T); the remaining outgoing and
nonconstant terms are L2 for each fixed parameter. The resolvent
therefore gives an O(1) L2 norm and O(T^2) covariant H2 norm.
Scaled Sobolev evaluation costs H^(3/2) at reduced cusp height H.
Adding the incoming part proves

\[
|E(g,w)|\ll H(g)^{\sigma+1/2}+T^2H(g)^{3/2}.
\]

The elementary bound H(n(z)a_y)<<1+y+y^(-1), uniform over the
finite components of the adelic Fourier integral, then gives the
displayed arithmetic estimate through Whittaker inversion.

Primary inputs:
[DLMF Bessel connection formula](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.27.E4),
[I-series](https://dlmf.nist.gov/10.25.E2),
[Gamma asymptotics](https://dlmf.nist.gov/5.11),
[Melrose, twisted Lichnerowicz formula, Section 3.2](https://math.mit.edu/~rbm/18.199-S06/18.199-S06.pdf),
and [Braverman--Milatovic--Shubin, Theorem 2.3 and Corollaries 2.9--2.10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0201231v3).
The cycle-6 KP realization supplies the actual Eisenstein family.

The earlier alternative Q=(Omega1-Omega2)/i was not used: formal
symmetry and centrality did not establish its proposed self-adjoint
domain and strong commutation. A separate compact-t cusp-propagation
argument also became unnecessary once the spinor lower bound was
proved. Neither alternative remains an active proof dependency.

## 4. Square-core middle estimate: unrestricted cubic outer variable

Factor the integral frequency ideal as ell=kappa*b^2, kappa squarefree, allowing (kappa,b)>1; the fixed Delta/unit factors are understood literally as above. On every unit and nonunit,

    chi_m(ell)^eta=chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(b)^(2eta).     (4.1)

For fixed kappa the second factor is cubic. Absorb the first into the actual inner coefficient. Its squared mass still satisfies (2.3), independent of b. The common (f,ell)=1 restricts outer b and/or kills the fiber; source/slot intersections with b are exactly the natural zeros of the cubic symbol.

The precise unconditional input is [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Theorem4.1/Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3): with squarefree primary inner m of length X and an arbitrary inner sequence, the unrestricted outer variable b of length B has energy bounded by

    (BX)^epsilon B^(1/3)(B+X) * inner squared mass.      (4.2)

Cubic reciprocity/conjugation supplies the orientation in (4.1), after the fixed ray handling just stated. This is Section4's large sieve, NOT the paper's cuspidal bilinear theorem. Neither squarefreeness of b nor an arbitrary joint matrix is assumed.

In an a-dyad the outer length is B<~(H_A/Nkappa)^(1/2). For a core cap C>=1, sum kappa by ideal counting. Using sum_(Nkappa<=C)Nkappa^(-2/3)<<C^(1/3) and sum Nkappa^(-1/6)<<C^(5/6), the complete positive fiber price is

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3)
                              +X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)].  (4.3)

Sharp middle restrictions and the core selector are allowed by Section3. Empty B<1 fibers contribute nothing; fixed bounded clipping costs are harmless. Both scalar sides satisfy (4.3), so Cauchy pays their product at this same price, not its square.

Restore (2.1), both allocation multiplicities, and O(A) original a labels. The exact dyad/f prices are

    U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^(-1) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-1) C^(1/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^(-4) N0^(1/3) (Nf)^(-2) C^(5/6).

The A sums are geometric and bounded. The f^-1 sum with tau(f)^C is harmonic up to an arbitrarily small power; the f^-2 sum converges after such a loss. Therefore the literal signed selected middle obeys

    |R_sq(C)| << H_J U^epsilon [
        U^(1/3+2tau/3) N0^(1/3) C^(1/3)
       +U^(5/6+tau/6) N0^(1/3) C^(5/6)].              (SQ)

All roots, original slots and both f allocations have been paid. This is an actual joint frequency/source estimate; replacing every frequency by (2.4) would give a larger price.

## G138. Full integral persistence and fixed versus moving readouts

Use the augmented squarefree complex with deg(e_n)=omega(n),
ordered prime-deletion differential and C(x)=0 for x<1. For each odd
squarefree m set b_m=e_(2m), z_m=d b_m=e_m-e_2 wedge d e_m.
Every correction has index 2m/p<m. This gives an integral
unitriangular basis at EVERY real cutoff, with d b_m=z_m and d z_m=0.
Thus the entire persistence module splits into intervals [m,2m) in
augmented degree omega(m), including [1,2) in degree 0 (reduced -1).
Inclusions are identity while an interval survives and zero at death.
This is a direct filtered-basis proof, not an imported barcode theorem.
Classical static topology retains its Björner/W27 attribution.

All logarithmic lifetimes equal log2. The map H(C(x))->H(C(2x)) is
zero, although M(3)=-1. A selection of longer-lived classes deletes
the signal. For fixed alpha in[1/2,1), write

    O_chi(x)=sum_(odd n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),
    R_alpha,chi(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(alpha x),
    M_chi(x)=O_chi(x)-chi(2)O_chi(x/2).

Character weighting is an arithmetic readout, not a commuting chain
map. Include chi(2)=0, every natural zero and the n=1 atom. On Re s>1,

    Mellin R=(1-alpha^s)/[s(1-chi(2)2^-s)L(s,chi)].

Both extra factors are nonzero on Re s>0. A COMPLETE every-epsilon
dyadic L2 bound at exponent 2gamma therefore excludes zeros Re s>gamma
for every fixed ordinary character at every height, with common gamma
and character-dependent constants. The left tail vanishes below 1;
dyadic Cauchy–Schwarz pays holomorphy and its derivatives. The principal
pole is a meromorphic point and actual imprimitive factors remain.
Pointwise reconstruction is the finite-for-each-x sum
O_chi(x)=sum_j R_alpha,chi(alpha^j x), costing (1-alpha^gamma)^-1.
Unsigned rank remains [4(1-alpha)/pi^2]x+O(sqrt x).

For T(x)=x-x^(1-eta), 0<eta<1, the arithmetic difference
R_eta(x)=O_chi(x)-O_chi(T(x)) is bounded trivially by x^(1-eta)+1.
Its persistence interpretation starts at x>=2^(1/eta); the initial
bounded interval is paid separately. Iteration until x<2 takes at
most 2+2^(k eta) steps in the dyadic band [2^k,2^(k+1)). Thus a
uniform pointwise R_eta=O(x^gamma), gamma>=0, only gives
O_chi=O(x^(gamma+eta)). The odd constant comparison source proves
this black-box loss can be sharp; it is not a Möbius lower bound.

readout does not supply it. Keep the signed-window target OPEN.

# Signed readouts, paid prime cutoffs and actual positive Gram prices

13 October2026. The controller reconstructed the complete frozen W66
[author](wild66/report.md), [independent review](wild66-review/report.md),
[two pre-outcome audits](wild66-review/audits.md), and the independently
