# [research revision] author candidate: cap both original plain lengths and obtain c4 = 0.125135



## 1. Candidate and exact dependency boundary

The original local proof can retain a useful initial constraint which previous capacity ledgers discarded: each original plain length is at most a fixed N. Set

```
N=4223/10000=.4223, C=546/125=4.368,
.41M<=n1,n2<=NM, .034M<=z<=.04M,
n1+n2+Cz<=M.
```

The resulting source-relative local theorem is the original paired squared moment `O(Z^(M+epsilon) H_J)` for the same fixed arithmetic family, natural coefficients and masks, all independent heights, original prime pools and four derivative-profile pairs. The new input is the bound

`A/M <= min(2N+t,1-(C-1)t)`, `t=z/M`,

rather than the capacity envelope alone. Thirty fixed amplifier choices, depending only on original selected-slot width, suffice. Every descendant uses the completed old `9/2` moment or unrestricted zero-slot theorem. No amplifier is selected after inspecting live plain scales.

The complete written endpoint candidate is

```
theta4=174973/200000=.874865,
c4=25027/200000=.125135.
```

It improves the accepted written [research revision] `c2=.125128` by `7/1000000=.000007`, and the controller-accepted [research revision] `c3=.125133` by `1/500000=.000002`. The latter comparison does not make the [research revision] theorem a proof dependency. Against Gao's `c_G=.1251134`, the increase is `27/1250000=.0000216`.

The proposed statement is the open half-plane `Re(s)>theta4` for each finite-order Hecke L-function of trivial infinite type over the Eisenstein field, and each ordinary Dirichlet L-function, including zeta, excluding the principal pole at 1. It adds no boundary-line, angular-family or uniform growing-parent-conductor result. The arithmetic is certified by **8/6/1** whole-rectangle Bernstein leaves with savings `10^-6,10^-5,10^-3`. Independent review, full endpoint formalization, clean dependency replay and independent kernel verification remain pending. The older c0 theorem retains its separate three-kernel receipt.

This is a genuine use of the tighter original plain window. At these exact C and k, discarding the plain cap gives high-envelope minimum `-150029/67500000<0`; retaining both envelopes gives `40919/337500000>0`. The grid has the same thirty cells as [research revision]. No limiting scalar optimum is being promoted to a theorem.

Credit remains with Zhongpai Gao, with AI assistance, for the PR15 local construction and bridges; OpenAI for the initial 7/8 theorem and analytic/arithmetic framework; Hailey Collet for the quartic, variable-moment, detector and source architecture; and Akash Levy for the weighted numerator. [research revision] supplies the enlarged-amplifier specialization and [research revision] its finite coupled construction. The frozen [research revision] argument supplies reusable work on the narrowed slot window; the present proof rederives its needed composition directly from the accepted source. The controller identified the discarded plain cap and joint-plane algebra. This lane supplies the explicit capped-window candidate and its complete repriced endpoint. These provenance statements make no literature-priority or upstream-endorsement claim.

## 2. Source interfaces and the strongest applicability objection

At lane startup the maintained research index identified [research revision] c2. The controller subsequently reported acceptance of [research revision] c3 after its separate review and exact replay. No changing current-proof file was reread as a dependency; this argument uses the frozen source bundles below. Full endpoint/kernel replay remains pending. The accepted `[restricted mathematical source]`, frozen [research revision] review and frozen [research revision] report/helper/receipt were read and reused. No evolving draft was inspected. No provider or child agent was contacted.

PR15 is pinned at `ca182b70ac2aee2d053d679b4ddf1233883f9eef`, PR9 at `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. Below LA, RC, SS and EA mean `PhysicalLocalAssembly.tex`, `RestrictedCanonicalSource.tex`, `PhysicalScaleShortening.tex` and `EndpointAssembly.tex` in `[restricted mathematical source]`. The signed reconstruction, fixed dictionary, unmarked density and Fourier transport supplements remain accepted companion inputs. `arithmetic.json` binds the four principal files, accepted integration, frozen review and three [research revision] artifacts by exact local hashes.

The new upper plain edge N<.44 is a restriction of LA.1. The lower marked-slot edge .034>.03 is likewise a restriction. The stronger coefficient C is proved anew below, not obtained by invoking LA verbatim. All source uses of the original scalar bounds are still valid where unchanged: `A/M>=.854>.85`, the comparison length M/4 lies below each original plain length, total original geometry stays inside the old compact ranges, and slot width remains at most .04M. The new total-width upper bound is .8802, smaller than .9. The local proof is not called at daughter states, so no daughter is incorrectly assumed to retain either plain cap or the useful slot window.

The main objection is that the useful cap could be lost when centering or reflecting, or that selecting an amplifier from actual varying plains would invalidate four-profile recovery. Neither is needed. N bounds only the original pair entering the local theorem, and hence its original A. The equal-product comparison may have a longer second factor; it is paid by the old moment after reflection. The transformed and extracted children use their literal original allocation and the old unrestricted source. The amplifier index depends only on original z/M and fixed N,C, not on either differentiated plain scale. The proof does not impose N on comparison or daughter pairs.

The arithmetic family remains a fixed finite ray character times the natural extended sextic row, with no positive-width moving parent; ray modulus and anchor are fixed. Keep `Q_*=internalQ(Q,eta0)`, proper, nonzero and contained in (72), and its literal non-FixedInducingRow exclusion. Original canonical pools, one common annular profile, relative characters, natural nonunit zeros, and row-independent polynomial-size punctures remain intact. A puncture may depend on frozen outer labels, with one Fourier majorant before their sum. Initialization remains `51/100<=beta_*<=7/8` in the nontrivial branch.

The unchanged source admissibility was already settled in the frozen reviews. Its decisive exact interfaces are retained here, without rerunning those audits:

* PR9 `Moments/FirstAmplificationChoice.lean`, blob `1e7a23d2f1319bd7a025a0ee8148a577c685b52d`, lines 712-740, requires sigma>0, loss>0, nonnegative polynomial bounds and `eta<sigma/6`; no upper smallness hypothesis on sigma occurs. The eventual threshold at line 718 precedes universal original data and slot exponents at lines 725-730.
* `Moments/AmplifiedRetainedRadius.lean`, blob `f6d0c98a4212c85ac9de0c0ce7de35f519383d89`, lines 220-255, has the same order, with `Csec>=1`, `xi>=0`, positive support reserve, and actual main/error radii. The Poisson interface permits every positive physical radius.
* `Moments/SecondExceptionalFixedQSource.lean`, blob `286754d49563f233397d28b24f5e5138ef1027f2`, uses proper fixed Q, fixed polynomial caps/profiles and positive `Kphys`, explicitly charging `Kphys^(5/6)`. The new price is included in Section 5.

Original actual-width, moving-error, old physical fourth-moment, unrestricted zero-slot and continuation interfaces remain precisely those recorded in the frozen [research revision]/54 source reviews. The argument below uses their actual formulas directly. It does not assume the [research revision] theorem, and a reference to its frozen arithmetic is provenance rather than an additional hypothesis. No fresh foundational or formal replay of the accepted framework is claimed.

## 3. Two compatible envelopes and fixed finite choices

Normalize to U=Z^M, hence M=1 for choosing fixed numerical data; retain M in ledgers. Put

```
r=9/2-C=33/250, k=309/1000,
b_j=17/500+j/5000, j=0,...,30.
```

For t=z/M use j=1 at t=.034 and otherwise the unique j with `b_(j-1)<t<=b_j`. Set `a_j/M=k b_j`, `sigma_j=3a_j`. The literal pool is `(Z^a_j/2,Z^a_j]` and the map is the source map h to h*p^6.

Writing S=(n1+n2)/M, one has `S<=2N` and `S<=1-Ct`. Therefore both pointwise bounds for A/M=S+t hold simultaneously. On the fixed cell use

```
A/M <= A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1)),
g/M <= g_j=r b_j,
g=(n1+n2+(9/2)z-M)_+.
```

The opposite endpoint choices are intentional: the first envelope increases in t, while the second decreases. The minimum of these two cellwise upper bounds is still a valid upper bound for every point of the cell. There is no inference that min of endpoint values equals the true cell maximum. We use the conservative displayed envelope and price its real rounding. Also g/M<=r t, including when the actual old-capacity defect is zero, so g_j is a valid conservative bound.

The exact family satisfies

```
52839/5000000 <= a_j/M <= 309/25000,
max_j A_j=4401/5000=.8802,
max_j g_j=33/6250=.00528,
7 max_j(a_j/M)=2163/25000=.08652<1/4.
```

The actual continuous crossing is `t*=(1-2N)/C=37/1040=.035576923...`, inside cell 8. The conservative envelopes switch between cells 8 and 9. This explains why the worst high and terminal cases move away from the first cell. The proof checks them all rather than transferring [research revision]'s monotonicity conclusion.

The larger k does not change the source conditions: all sigma_j are fixed positive numbers; a common mesh below `min_j(a_j/M)/10` implies the required sigma gap, and it can be reduced to fit the least reserve. Prime-cardinality and deleted-prime bounds work with the smallest positive a_j and common polynomial envelopes. Removing row/mask/projector primes costs O(log Z); the finite representation factor `(Mmax+2sigma_j)/(sigma_j/6)` has a common finite bound. The prime average stays normalized. The internal small amplifier used to prove the old global theorem is separate from this fixed outer family.

Choose the thirty numerical cases first, then common small budgets and mesh from the requested loss and fixed compact geometry. Fix the finite original slot system and arithmetic family. The original source quantifiers put all live original data, widths, masks and scales after their eventual threshold; a maximum over thirty choices and four derivative pairs is finite. Orders and constants may depend on the fixed family but the real reserves and mesh do not depend on a later target dictionary.

The classwise endpoint selector fixes I before summing its amplitude class. Its original width and thus j stay fixed during the moment and both plain-scale derivatives. Both centered rectangles use that same j. Different outer d, subsets and shifts choose among already simultaneous estimates and introduce no extra growing label. In particular no amplifier is chosen from S after inspecting the plains. For U=Z^d with d>=d0=.005, a common U-threshold is reached by `Z>=U0^(1/d0)`; choosing a correspondingly small U-loss works for every d<=h+10^-10.

Common Fourier measures and the Euler derivative bounds for `K(B product y_i^e_i)` are taken before live labels and are uniform for B>0. Hilbert direct sums keep those labels inside Cauchy; the diagonal restriction is a contraction. Radial scaling changes neither the normalized seminorm nor a Z exponent. Internal density height parameters precede the finite degree, then a distinct external height exponent fits the numerical reserves. Choose derivative orders backward through the finite two-transform graph, Fourier orders afterward, and the threshold last. Large input heights use a fixed polynomial allowance and the same bounded raw envelope. All four profile pairs remain covered.

## 4. Actual transforms and main low/high branches

Here c,d,p,R,E and the second-stage labels are the original extraction widths, unrelated to the endpoint constant c4. The equal-product comparison has lengths M/4 and n1+n2-M/4. Exact mask deletion, reflection, conductor restoration and bounded scale recovery give old capacity at most

`M/4+M/2+(9/2)(M/25)+xi=93M/100+xi`.

Thus its reserve is `7M/100`. Products, whole characters, profiles, independent heights and common punctures agree. Nonempty subunit scales are clipped using the bounded annular rule; empty slots use the unrestricted old theorem.

The first-transform outside exponent is `M-A-R/2-E`. Its common labels, including the first projector, remain inside Hilbert Cauchy. With `B_c=(3c-5d-R)_+/6`, it suffices to prove

`sum_lambda N_(C,lambda) << Z^(p+A-c+R+E+B_c+eta)`,

and the exchanged assertion. Since `B_c+B_d<=c+d-2p-R`, the averaged exponent with the outside factor is at most M+eta. Per-label branches keep the original `-s0` allowance and pay the `Z^(p+s0+eta)` first-label count once. The high branch counts the joint labels directly. No multiplicity is appended afterward.

The actual main radius is

```
K_main=K0+(d-c)_+ +6a_j+omega,
K0=2A-c-d+R+E-M,
omega=delta_1+supportreserve,  2<=Z^supportreserve.
```

RC lines 130-139 and the exact common-radius interface provide genuine smooth domination at this ball. The three errors retain their own radius

`K0+max(d-c-2w+w_o,0)+3a_j+delta_1+supportreserve`.

They are not enlarged to the main radius. The physical scale stays positive even if its logarithmic exponent is negative; unsupported negative row windows are empty and supported bounded end windows receive the fixed padding. The second Poisson formula is applied at the actual radius. Fixed polynomial envelopes cover all thirty cases.

The exact main child identities remain

```
M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a_j-omega-g2+t2,
(A-c-c2-M')-(A-M)
  =6a_j+omega-min(c,d)-(c2-g2)-t2 <=6a_j+omega,
Delta=b2-p2+B_c+a_j >= a_j.
```

Keep the full second projector and original source allocation. The moving child character is not inserted into the fixed anchor Q_*. Canonical kept rows retain each required natural nonprincipal presentation. Original relative-character dictionaries, parent-translate separation, reciprocity/unit sectors, whole-product conjugation and height reflection are unchanged. Moving holes preserve literal eligibility and positive-real zero maxima. Principal rows are treated separately, not inserted into the nonprincipal density.

Low-bin indicators are attached only to positive allocated child energy after both transforms. Slot removal has squared price `.7+O(e)` per width, hence old-capacity-defect price `7/45+O(e)`. After paying it, drop the indicator and use only the old canonical moment. Exhausted slots use unrestricted zero-slot input, with no plain-length-sum hypothesis. No Poisson formula or differentiation is applied to an indicator.

The actual canonical width can be smaller than M'. If `d_*=M_actual-M'<=delta2`, then for `0<=s<=1`,

`d_*+s(F-d_*)_+ <= delta2+sF_+`.

This pays negative width differences as well as positive padding. Nominal low defect is at most `g+6a_j+eta`; the greedy removal overshoots by one mesh increment. Therefore the reserve before small losses is

```
a_j-(7/45)(g+6a_j)
 >= M b_j(k/15-7r/45)
 = M b_j/15000 >= 57M/25000000.
```

The strict reserve is **.00000228 M**. Choose aggregate padding, support, bin rounding, divisor and mesh costs from a sufficiently small fixed fraction of it and of epsilon. For a fixed finite slot list, per-slot losses are assigned from one aggregate budget. They are not multiplied by an uncontrolled slot count.

For the main high bins the signed reconstruction gives the actual nonzero row

`w=u0 e F_c G_c V h'`, `L_c=log_Z NF_c<=5(R-R0)`,

with formal-side residues `1+t_p` or `1-t_p` modulo six. Zero residue remains an Euler hole. The first projector and genuine second common primes divide w. Missing first-common primes have radical width at most `p-R-E+R0`; fixed-row valuations and first-projector choices are divisor-many. The second projector need not divide w; its dyadic count is paid by the original two extraction scalars. Natural conductor is at most K Nw for fixed K, with moving Euler holes separate.

The actual support has

`log_Z Nw<=W+O(eta)`, `W=M-R-(c-d)_+ +L_c-6a_j`.

For `.7<=delta<=.75`, let `rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)]`. The original unmarked density counts joint rows and labels by

`Z^(rho W+p-R-E+R0+eta)(1+T_h)^J`.

Sixth-power stripping is summable since `rho>=2/7>1/6`; removed primes stay holes. Bounded supported windows are padded, so a nonempty population is not spuriously bounded by a negative power. Parent translates remain separated in the fixed dictionary. The exact high excess relative to the joint target is

```
M(rho-1)+delta A+a_j(5-6rho)
 +(1-rho)(c-d)_+-delta c-(1+rho)R-E-B_c
 +rho L_c+R0+g2-t2-(1+delta)b2+O(eta).
```

Using `min(c,d)>=p>=R`, the L_c bound, `rho+delta>1` and `5rho>1`, the middle terms are at most `(4rho-1-delta)p-E-B_c<=-79p/270-E-B_c`. The final terms are at most `-delta b2-t2`. Every label cost is already present.

The remaining normalized saving is

`H_j(delta)=1-rho-delta A_j-k b_j(5-6rho)`,

where **both** original constraints are retained:

`A_j=min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1))`.

Its derivative is `50(1-6k b_j)/(3(5-2delta)^2)-A_j`. With `A_j<=4401/5000` and `a_j/M<=309/25000`, a common lower bound on the whole interval is

`50(1-6*(309/25000))/(3*(18/5)^2)-4401/5000=188591/607500>0`.

Thus the minimum occurs at delta=.7, where

`H_j(.7)=35/54-(7/10)min(2N+b_j,1-(C-1)b_(j-1))-(26/9)k b_j`.

For j=1,...,8 the first envelope is smaller. For j=9,...,30 the second is smaller. On the first segment the high reserve decreases by `(7/10+(26/9)k)/5000` per step. On the second it increases by `[(7/10)(C-1)-(26/9)k]/5000`, which is positive. The two adjacent cases are

```
j=8: A_8=4401/5000,      H_8(.7)=967/4218750,
j=9: A_9=275031/312500,  H_9(.7)=40919/337500000.
```

Consequently the exact minimum is **40919/337500000 M** in case 9. This includes both the ceiling-amplifier charge and the actual interval-envelope rounding; no continuous crossing optimum substitutes for a finite case. Bins crossing .7 go to the buffered low branch; density is used only at or above .7. The low branch's O(e) payment is allocated from its smaller positive reserve.

## 5. Every error, zero and fixed-inducing contribution

The original three errors have `(w,w_o)=(lambda,lambda),(6lambda,0),(7lambda,lambda)`. From the literal pool, eventually `lambda>=3a_j/4`; this follows already when `log_Z 2<=a_j/4`, uniformly for the finite family. Their nominal defect is at most `g+3a_j+w-w_o+eta`, allowance at least w. Use only the old global deletion price `1/6`, with the same actual-width correction. The three reserves are

`a_j/4-g/6`, `13a_j/4-g/6`, `4a_j-g/6`.

Moving-prime characters at valuations one and seven, natural zero coefficients and extraction scalars stay literal. The average over amplifier primes stays normalized; no second prime count or improved density is introduced.

The first zero frequency keeps the original powerful-product estimate. The artificially added zero Gauss row remains unamplified and retains its `-s0` allowance. The second zero costs at most `A-M+5a_j+O(eta)`. For paired fixed-inducing rows, the exact main F1 has `-4a_j-5omega/6`, giving `F1>=2c/3-4a_j-O(eta)`; `F2>=2b2/3`. With `v=c+min(c2,d2)` the exact maximum

`max_(v>=0)[A-5M/6-2v/3-(M/4-v)_+]=A-M`

occurs at v=M/4. Thus the main fixed-inducing excess is at most `A-M+4a_j+O(eta)` and the error excess at most `A-M+9a_j+O(eta)`. These include the exceptional source's actual `Kphys^(5/6)` cost. Equal-product lattice leading terms cancel with the same profiles, whole character, masks and independent-height norm powers; both rectangles use the same j.

The exact minima over all thirty interval envelopes are:

| Branch | Normalized reserve | Attaining case |
|---|---:|---:|
| Comparison | `7/100` | all |
| Low | `57/25000000` | 1 |
| High | `40919/337500000` | 9 |
| Error 1 | `37791/20000000` | 1 |
| Error 6 | `671859/20000000` | 1 |
| Error 7 | `103797/2500000` | 1 |
| Second zero | `322949/5000000` | 9 |
| Main fixed-inducing | `18913/250000` | 9 |
| Error fixed-inducing | `20341/1000000` | 9 |

For the last three, the reserve is `1-A_j-mk b_j`, with m=5,4,9. It decreases on the first-envelope segment and increases on the second, since `C-1-mk>0`; checking cases 8 and 9 gives the displayed minimum. In particular the largest terminal price, **9a_j**, is paid; it is not hidden in epsilon. Even the coarser unrelated extrema satisfy `1-max A_j-9 max(a_j/M)=107/12500>0`, though the argument uses the sharper same-cell reserve.

The program checks every cell, recording each minimum's attaining indices. The three error reserves increase with b_j and are smallest at case 1. All fixed amplifier costs, natural zeros and exceptional radii are therefore priced. Two transforms and old-only descendants complete the local source composition without a recursive call to this stronger theorem. Common Fourier integration and four-profile recovery follow with the orders already specified.

## 6. The joint plane and its precise strict-ledger limitation

Let S=(n1+n2)/M and t=z/M. When the actual old-capacity defect `g/M=S+(9/2)t-1` is positive, eliminating the amplifier at the low-reserve boundary `a/M=(7/3)(g/M)` turns the high reserve at delta=.7 into

`35/54-(7/10)(S+t)-(182/27)(S+(9/2)t-1)`.

Multiplying by 270 gives exactly

**`1995-2009S-8379t`**.

Thus the underlying necessary joint condition for these two strictly positive reserves is `2009S+8379t<1995`, in the positive-defect regime. This is not intrinsically a constant-capacity inequality. It is an actual geometric constraint, not a mixture of incompatible extrema.

For the cap S<=2N and capacity S+Ct<=1, write b=1-2N. Suppose the crossing t*=b/C lies inside the useful slot window. At that crossing, S=2N and g/M=(9/2-C)t*>0 for C<9/2. The strict plane is equivalent to

`C > 8379b/(2009b-14)`,

provided 2009b-14>0. For N=4223/10000 this gives

```
Ccrit=930069/212999=4.366541626955995...,
rcrit=56853/425998,
tcrit=212999/5985000=.0355888053467...,
(a/M)crit=6317/570000.
```

The point n1=n2=NM is literally permitted and tcrit lies between .034 and .04. At equality both low and high reserves vanish; increasing a makes high negative, decreasing it makes low negative. This obstructs simultaneous **fixed strictly positive reserves at that point**, not an epsilon-loss theorem or an epsilon-dependent construction. Equality is unproved by this argument, not declared mathematically impossible.

For completeness this crossing is the maximum of the eliminated plane over the relevant capped-capacity polygon: before the crossing S<=2N makes `2009S+8379t` increase in t; afterward S<=1-Ct gives slope `8379-2009C<0` for these C. In the region g<=0 the low deletion cost is absent, and the original high term at zero amplifier is already positive. Thus the crossing identifies the genuine strict-ledger bottleneck, subject to the stated geometry, rather than just one arbitrary test point.

This boundary is not used as a theorem. The explicit C=546/125 has

`C-Ccrit=38829/26624875>0`,

and the continuous joint-plane margin at its own crossing is `12943/130000>0`. Its actual fixed k=.309 and thirty ceiling cells are paid in Sections 3-5, including rounding and every terminal branch. The equality idealization does not replace any finite check.

At the tighter safe plain edge the old short-slot fallback permits a lower cutoff strictly below

`(1-2N)/(9/2)=259/7500=.034533333...`.

The retained .034 edge therefore leaves reserve .0024. This is a limit of that fallback envelope, not an impossibility result. No attempt to optimize to either strict boundary is part of this candidate.

## 7. Complete endpoint geometry and all shortening cases

Define from theta4

```
ell=11/3-4theta4=25081/150000,
h=3969737987/5000000000,
x=1+ell-h=5598886039/15000000000,
y=h-2ell=6893013961/15000000000,
kappa_*=2theta4-1=74973/100000.
```

Exact arithmetic gives `x+y=1-ell`, `0<ell<x<y<2x`, `y<1/2<h<2y`, `1/6<ell<1/5`, `h>4ell`, `C<6kappa_*` and theta4>.87. The compensated-probe arguments are

`y-2x+ell=-598886039/5000000000<0`,

`1+3ell-2(x+y)=-4919/30000<0`.

Its exact identity remains `(5x+y)/12=theta4-k_probe`, `k_probe=5/6-x/3-ell/6`.

Put `d_-=h-.001`, `d_+=h+10^-10`, `t0=.001`, `d0=.005`. On `d_-<=d<=d_+`, `0<=t<=t0`, the upper reflected plain length is `n=1-y/d+t`; nominal capacity is `z_A=(1-2n)/C`, slightly decremented to pay fixed annular and scale-box errors. Both monotonicities are explicit. The extrema before that decrement are:

| Quantity | Exact value | Approximation |
|---|---:|---:|
| n minimum | `5001200000/11894213961` | .420473350858 |
| n maximum | `402248737237/952737117000` | .422203281534 |
| z_A minimum | `74119821263/2080777863528` | .035621208089 |
| z_A maximum | `236476745125/6494240822706` | .036413300889 |

# [research revision]: original-prime row covariance, bounded attack


Sole owned tree: `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/hard-covariance/`.
The controller owns canonical integration, tracker and Git. No children,
provider changes or publication. This draft is not an accepted theorem.

## Current checkpoint

Completed bounded attack: SF2 is a simultaneous marked bilinear square
function over disjoint ORIGINAL product-norm intervals. SF8--11 return
the entire exact strict far mask at logarithmic cost, eliminating D6's
separate near-band term without factoring an additive product phase.
SF12--15 give the decisive failure: the leading balanced certificate
still has deficit .6738809116, and actual primes remain in the unpaid
unit Type I vector. No original prime interaction, full H estimate, or
constant increase is newly paid. Independent controller review is
required before even the restricted SF lemma is promoted.

Current accepted written analytic target is Gao's c_G=.1251134; its
endpoint/kernel replay remains separate from old c0 verification.
The initial row-dual opening matched the existing JN/RH obstruction
and was not repeated or counted as progress. The source files and
shared repository state remained read-only. The exact structured
host-local claim uses this task UUID and the sole assigned tree.

Constraints: preserve the original q_P^(-1/2) mark roots and
Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P, each Delta root/mass, physical outside
N^(-1)G^(-2), both independent heights, every ordered source/component
pair, original masks and actual norm near/far bands. The paid high
extracted-gcd composite correction does not pay original prime pairs.
Two-cutoff Lambda identities and their semiprime 1,-1,-1,1 cancellation
are already established; repeating them is not new output.

Mathematical development, original return, source bindings and the
endpoint calculation are complete. Remaining handoff steps: final
whole-file readback/hash, STOP and own-claim release.

## 1. Bounded direction and novelty boundary

The row-dual opening was stopped at the first source comparison:
JN3--9 already give the exact simultaneous row/mark transform, and
JN10--18 keep its necessary moving frequencies. RH26/FG18--19 already
record the unmatched reflected character and the unpaid prime
complement. Those are inputs, not results of this attack. I do not
repeat a completion formula and call it a new covariance estimate.

The concrete remaining test is different. [research revision] D2 is a marked
bilinear estimate for one original product interval. Its D5 correctly
rejects separation of the additive product phase used for the far cut.
D6 therefore subtracts the entire near band at an extra cost.
Here I keep the signed covariance until an EXACT interval-rectangle
decomposition, and prove a simultaneous square-function version of D2.
The result removes that separate near-band cost for every ordered
bilinear interaction. It will then be tested on the actual unit Type I
source and the signed I/II return. An interface improvement is not a
payment for the original prime covariance.

## 2. A marked product-interval square function

The exact source is `[restricted mathematical source]`,
D1--6; M is `zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md`, B1.9--11 and
B2.21--30. JPS is `[restricted mathematical source]`.
The native coefficients remain

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4 on coprime d,e.

All ideal labels retain their original good primary squarefree and
finite-ray conventions; no squarefree integer-norm hypothesis is used.
The source has its original zero extension at shared d,e. The mark
array u(P) is the original one, independent of live n,g,R.

Notation and domain are exactly [research revision] D1. Fix the original R,g and
one original separated profile component. The original n is de, with
q_d in a D dyad and q_e in an E dyad, DE comparable to N. The source
coefficients c(d),b(e) are source-only and divisor-bounded, with all
their actual cutoff and prime supports. The masks (de,g)=(de,bar(g))=1,
the squarefree product, all fixed finite-ray conditions and the
projector 1_(P,Rg)=1 remain. Let

    V_I(R,g) = sum_(d,e,P; q_de in I)
       c(d)b(e)a(d)a(e) chi_d(e)^4 chi_R(de)^3
       [u(P)/sqrt(q_P)] chi_P(de)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1
       C(de) 1_(de,g bar(g))=1.                       (SF1)

Intervals I are intervals of REAL NORM VALUES with arbitrary strict
or non-strict endpoints. Their evaluation is on the original integer
norm q_de. The original long-source support is intersected with I;
it is never replaced by an interval on a quotient. The physical short
factor xi(g)A(g)chi_R(g)^3 is still on the outside, including its zero.

**Claim SF (proved below, relative to M B2.25).** For every finite
family of pairwise disjoint norm intervals I_j,

    sum_j |V_(I_j)(R,g)|^2
       <<_(epsilon,orig) Z^epsilon
          N T(D,E;L) Omega P_lin^2,
    T(D,E;L)=min{S(E,LD), S(D,LE)},
    S(X,Y)=X+Y+(XY)^(2/3),
    Omega=sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P.                        (SF2)

There is NO factor for the number of intervals. The bound is uniform
in their endpoints, R,g and the original independent norm height.
P_lin denotes the original linear profile mass; in a normalized
single separated component it is one. This is a simultaneous estimate,
not an inference from separate applications of D2. The allowed masks
are the ones displayed in SF1 and the inherited fixed supports. No
arbitrary extra bounded function of de is asserted.

### 2.1 Proof before profile integration

First take a product profile C(de)=C_d(d)C_e(e); its factors have the
original bounded envelopes. Include C_d in c and C_e in b. The exact
characters on d and the mark are put in

    A_(R,g,J)(t)
      = sum_(P d=t; q_d in J)
          [u(P)/sqrt(q_P)] c(d)a(d) chi_R(d)^3
          chi_P(d)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1 1_(d,g bar(g))=1.  (SF3)

Here J is a norm interval on the ORIGINAL d dyad. All P and d
supports, their finite phases, and squarefree conditions are retained.
The zero chi_P(d)^4 forces (P,d)=1, so t=Pd is squarefree.
All e-dependent characters then have exactly the product
chi_t(e)^4. In particular the zero at (e,t)>1 supplies BOTH the
original (e,P)>1 and (e,d)>1 zeros. The remaining coefficient is

    B_(R,g)(e)=b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1.   (SF4)

Its squared mass is O(Z^epsilon E). No inverse character is used at
a collision. P has NOT been replaced by t in the physical mark root.

Build a fixed binary interval tree on the attainable integer norm
values in the D dyad (zero coefficients may fill missing values).
Pad to the next power of two if necessary. Let J range over all its
nodes, and let ell_D=O(log(2D)) be its depth plus one. Any interval of
d norms is a disjoint union of at most 2 ell_D tree nodes. For fixed
e, the intervals I_j/q_e are disjoint. Their canonical tree covers
are therefore disjoint as sets of d norms, so any fixed node J occurs
at most once among all these covers at that e.

Apply Cauchy in e to each SF1, then sum j. Apply the just-described
tree cover and Cauchy over its at most 2 ell_D nodes. This gives

    sum_j |V_(I_j)|^2
      << Z^epsilon E ell_D
         sum_J sum_(e original)
             |sum_t A_(R,g,J)(t) chi_t(e)^4|^2.     (SF5)

This step retains the actual product endpoint. There is no claim that
e(a q_d q_e) separates. The set of d norms selected at fixed e is an
interval simply because q_e>0 and q_(de)=q_d q_e.

For each J the coefficients SF3 are independent of live e. The cubic
sieve M B2.25, with the original zero extension, gives

    sum_e |sum_t A_(R,g,J)(t) chi_t(e)^4|^2
      << Z^epsilon S(E,LD) sum_t |A_(R,g,J)(t)|^2.  (SF6)

The orientation uses the even reciprocity already admitted in D2.
The t length is LD, not a new source length or a new physical mark.
For each t there are at most tau(t) factorizations t=Pd. Therefore

    sum_J sum_t |A_(R,g,J)(t)|^2
      <= Z^epsilon sum_J sum_(P,d; q_d in J)
                    |u(P)|^2/q_P |c(d)|^2
      << Z^epsilon ell_D D Omega.                  (SF7)

Each d occurs in exactly one node at each tree level. That is why
the total cost is ell_D, not the total number of nodes or intervals.
The full root q_P^(-1/2) is essential: changing it to q_t^(-1/2)
without q_d^(1/2) would incorrectly remove the D in SF7.

Equations SF5--7 give N S(E,LD) Omega times logarithms. Reversing d
and e, keeping their actual source coefficients and both original
supports, gives N S(D,LE) Omega. Taking the smaller proves SF2.
The unit dyad is included by using a one-node tree; no factorization
of a prime into two nonunits has been introduced.

### 2.2 Actual profile and endpoint return

For the actual smooth C(de), use its common Mellin/logarithmic Fourier
separation ONCE and apply Minkowski in the Hilbert space of all interval
outputs j. A norm height factors exactly as q_d^(it)q_e^(it), with
unchanged modulus; the coefficients SF3 remain independent of e.
The original two sides later have their own independent heights.
All original sharp product endpoints can be intersected with the
I_j and kept in the tree; they need no new smooth approximation.
Fixed finite-ray restrictions on de are separated by the original
finite character resolution, with its fixed coefficient mass.

Thus the common profile seminorm and root envelope are exactly the
ones already permitted in JPS/[research revision]. If a particular profile factor
has already been separated into d,e factors, it is not separated a
second time. Source-only angular and Gauss factors stay in a(d),a(e).
The proof does not extend arbitrary row-dependent or n-dependent
selectors beyond the stated original contract.

The D/D' in this lemma are factor lengths, not the mark/row collision
divisor Delta. That projector stays literal in SF3. If it is instead
expanded before this lemma, EVERY Delta term and intersection must be
restored: its root is q_Delta^(-1/2), its mark squared mass is at most
q_Delta Omega_Delta, and their cancellation is the original one. This
lemma provides no extra division of N or D by q_Delta.

## 3. Exact far-mask return without an additive product phase

Let A_i(m;R,g) denote the complete coefficient of the ORIGINAL norm
q_n=m in one SF1 block on side i, including all ideals of that norm.
This is notation for regrouping, not a replacement of ideals by integer
factorization. The intervals used below select m, so both distinct ideal
orientations with equal rational norm always stay together.

Fix an integer H>=0. Choose a power-of-two integer interval containing
all possible values of x=m and y=m'+H. Its width is O(N) when H is below
the original norm range; if H exceeds that range the far mask is empty.
For each binary-tree node J let J_L,J_R be its left and right children.
The exact integer identity is

    1_(m>m'+H)
      = sum_(all internal J)
          1_(m in J_R) 1_(m' in J_L-H).             (SF8)

Every strict ordered pair is separated at its unique lowest common
ancestor. Equality m=m'+H contributes zero. At EACH fixed tree level,
the J_R intervals are disjoint, as are all translated J_L-H intervals.
All endpoints in SF8 are integer membership conventions, so there is
no smoothing or missing boundary strip. The reverse strict orientation
has the same identity with m,m' interchanged. Adding them gives exactly
1_(|m-m'|>H), without either equality orientation.

For any original bounded complex true-core weight h,

    h((g,g')) = sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f),
    r_h(f)=sum_(a|f) mu(f/a)h(a), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f). (SF9)

This is the entire original core inversion, with g=f b,g'=f b'.
It is not a recomputed core of de,d'e'. All source and short masks,
the original squarefree/primitive conditions, and both original g
windows remain in the summands. In particular chi_R(f)^3 keeps its
zero until a positive bound permits dropping its modulus.

Apply SF8 before any inequality. At one fixed level and f the ordered
covariance is a sum over disjoint interval pairs. Cauchy in the JOINT
coordinates (tree node,R), followed on each side by triangle over the
actual O(G/q_f) short sources, and then SF2, gives

    << Z^epsilon K (G/q_f)^2 N
           sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))
           sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.            (SF10)

For different source coefficients the two SF2 estimates are applied
to their own arrays, profiles and independent heights. The bounded
paired row factor is retained until its absolute value enters this
Cauchy measure. The O(K) row count is displayed; no new row theorem
is hidden here. All signs of r_h and every ordered bilinear interaction
were present in the exact expression before this bound.

There are O(log(2N)) levels. Sum the entire f inversion using
sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2<infinity, or the admitted subpower allowance. This
proves the following replacement for [research revision] D6:

**SF-far theorem (restricted, proved).** Under the original D1/JPS
contract, with DE,D'E' comparable to the same original N,

    |C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h]|
      <<_(epsilon,orig) Z^epsilon K G^2 N
             sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))
             sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.          (SF11)

The sharp threshold may be the actual H0=floor(Z^.05), including its
strict endpoint. The estimate also holds uniformly for any integer H
at this same scope. There is no +(H0+1)L term. The same proof works for
the near mask by subtracting the two strict far orientations from the
complete product; that is an EXACT identity, not signed-submask
inheritance. The sharper preexisting near-prime theorem remains a
different input and is not invoked for auxiliary composites.

SF11 does not require and does not assert that exp(i a q_d q_e)
factors into d and e phases. It uses interval selection and a proven
simultaneous square function instead. It also does not infer SF11 by
taking a difference of two independently unproved norms. Each tree
rectangle is bounded in a common positive (node,R) measure.

The proof gives a useful abstract interface: a simultaneous bound for
all disjoint original norm intervals controls any single threshold
staircase m>m'+H at logarithmic cost. The sign of H and reversed order
are handled by the same exact finite identity. Arbitrary pair masks
are not covered merely because their values are bounded.

## 4. Decisive pressure test and the remaining original-prime term

SF11 is stronger than D6 as an interface, but its leading arithmetic
certificate has NOT improved. At the frozen hard dyad write

    k=.835507578307735986...,
    nu=k+.003, gamma=.001,
    ell=.170813789153867993...,
    K=Z^k, N=Z^nu, G=Z^gamma, L=Z^ell,
    S(N,L) comparable to N.

Every factor split DE=N satisfies

    S(E,LD) >= (NL)^(2/3),
    S(D,LE) >= (NL)^(2/3).                           (SF12)

The balanced split E=LD, hence D=sqrt(N/L), E=sqrt(NL), attains this
order because NL>=1. The best balanced certificate SF11, divided by
the required raw G K S(N,L), therefore still has size

    G (NL)^(2/3) = Z^(.673880911641069319333...).     (SF13)

The separate near-band term with old exponent .221813789153867993...
has disappeared; it was not the leading obstruction. Compared with
the incumbent's .004 deficit, the remaining surplus is
.669880911641069319333.... The cycle's new interval argument has
therefore not paid an original prime interaction at the required scale.
SF12--13 are lower bounds on this positive CERTIFICATE, not lower
bounds on the original covariance.

Even replacing the cubic sieve by its hypothetical two-linear-term
version would leave

    min(E+LD,D+LE) >= 2 sqrt(NL),
    target-relative scale at least G sqrt(NL),
    exponent .5056606837308019895....               (SF14)

Thus neither free removal of the entire near band nor removing only
the mixed cubic term repairs this fixed-row argument. A proposed new
row average that replaces K in SF11 by K Z^(-sigma) would need
sigma>=.673880911641069319333... just to pay this balanced packet.
Even a hypothetical K^(1/2) row cost would leave a positive certificate
deficit .256127122487201326333... . These are diagnostic requirements
for THIS ordering of inequalities, not universal necessities for H.

### 4.1 Signed I/II return through the interval tree

Let F_I and F_II denote the two exact normalized linear terms of
[research revision] B1--2, with all their original n,R,P,g factors. Restriction to
any tree interval J is multiplication by 1_(q_n in J), hence commutes
with the pointwise identity:

    (F_I+F_II)_J = F_(all-prime),J.                  (SF15)

The strict far covariance is consequently the exact sum of its four
ordered (I,I),(I,II),(II,I),(II,II) tree expressions. On every eligible
semiprime above both cutoffs the interval coefficient is still 1,-1
on the two linear pieces, giving 1,-1,-1,1 in the ordered covariance
whenever the original pair is in that rectangle. Thus the two ordered
mixed terms remain necessary. They cancel BEFORE the prime projection,
not as a post hoc cancellation between positive bounds.

On an original prime n, the coefficient in F_I is one and that in
F_II is zero. It stays in the unit factor cell D=1,E~N at every tree
level. In this cell

    T(1,N;L)=min{S(N,L),S(1,NL)} comparable to N,

so SF11 gives K G^2 N^2, of target-relative size G N, with exponent
.839507578307735986.... This is weaker than the existing joint
quadratic/cubic bound and is not promoted. Combining all signed
allocations FIRST restores the original prime source at original
length N; applying the established joint sieve to it restores
G(K+NG)S(N,L), still with deficit .004. No shortened unit source is
created by SF15.

This is the decisive obstruction to this attempted route. The exact
product-interval adapter fixes an analytic masking loss, but the
first positive fixed-row estimate still discards the covariance that
the unit prime source needs. The signed small-gcd complement remains
the original-prime form minus the already paid common-core composite
counterterm. No new equality identifies that counterterm with primes.

The next useful target is therefore an estimate on SF15's JOINT
original-row interval vectors before the fixed-R cubic Cauchy step,
or a signed Type-I/Type-II estimate in that same joint norm. A theorem
with the square-function scope of SF2 would now return the full sharp
far mask by SF8 at logarithmic cost. Proving such a row estimate is
still the arithmetic work; SF2/SF11 do not assume it.

## 5. Complete original return and unchanged unpaid scope

All statements above are first made with finite ORIGINAL cutoffs in
the accepted JPS domain

    N>C_orig(K+L+G^2), C_orig G<A_0,
    1<=L<=sqrt(N), G>=1.                            (SF16)

The source remains the evaluated perpendicular auxiliary extension
used in JPS Sections 3--4: the masks depend on n=de and original g,
the coefficient is the native a(n), the original short core is
(g,g'), and the outside squared scalar is N^(-1)G^(-2). It is not a
new physical H source with e in place of n or with d absorbed into g.
The mark is the original P, and its root remains q_P^(-1/2).
Every ordered pair of bilinear blocks is retained, including unit/
nonunit and the two distinct I/II cross orientations. Selecting a
binary interval node does not change any of those coefficients.

Consequently SF11's physical bound is exactly

    Z^epsilon K sqrt(T T')
        sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig,                (SF17)

against the desired K S(N,L)/(N G) with the same masses. There is no
extra d-, t-, interval-, or Fourier-normalization root to divide out.
In particular the D Omega in SF7 cannot be replaced by Omega.

Before returning to the original degree-one prime packet, recombine
all cutoff terms to the all-prime source by SF15 and [research revision] B1--3.
Only then invoke the accepted JPS11 all-prime-minus-inert identity.
Its inert square and BOTH ordered inert cross terms retain their
existing raw budget

    Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)
      [sqrt(N)L + {S(N,L)sqrt(N)L}^(1/2)]
      sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.                  (SF18)

The original completion gates JPS12 apply on each eligible dyad;
one pressure calculation is not substituted for them. The already
accepted transport and complete-unit Jacobi subtraction return once,
with their existing budgets

    Z^epsilon G^2(K+N)S(N,L)sqrt(L/K),
    Z^epsilon G^2 K L/N,                             (SF19)

times the same original profile and array masses. Neither these
payments nor SF18 estimates the new signed small-gcd arithmetic
residual. No true core, matching correction, total-index selector,
or paid-source complement is recomputed on an auxiliary composite.

For full profiles use M B2.22's one common separation before positive
row enlargement. Its linear envelope
min(Y^(1/4),(1+Y)^(-A)) stays on EACH side. Both independent height
variables are integrated against their original rapid densities, with
the original finite component and six-unit weights. SF2 adds at most
fixed powers of logarithms and divisor functions; these are absorbed
by allocated subpower losses, not by deleting a physical scalar.

The full discarded lattice tail and original source/root ends are
handled by M B2.23 and B2.37--40 with their original absolute
polynomial majorants. First pair one complete tail with the full
other side and then choose the available Schwartz order larger than
that polynomial. This pays BOTH ordered mixed tails and the squared
tail. The tree construction never differentiates a sharp annulus.
For the noncompact originals, form the finite retained cut first and
restore the original tail by this argument; an auxiliary tree cutoff
does not authorize silently dropping it. No uniformity over a single
weak seminorm or a fixed finite height interval has been added.

Other original H branches, mixed dyads outside SF16, nonprime source
interactions outside this evaluated extension, the other two cusp
coefficient systems and their cube sources, and all original global
correction returns remain as before. This report does not identify
their coefficients with a(de), nor infer their estimates from SF11.
No branch or ordered cross term has been declared paid by an analogy.
The full all-branch H statement and an improvement beyond c_G remain
open. This is not a theorem-validation claim about Gao or the old
kernel certificates, which were not re-audited here.

## 6. Verification, limits and handoff

The proof of SF2 is the explicit order SF3--7: fixed R,g, Cauchy in
e, disjoint interval tree, cubic sieve with e-independent coefficients,
then the divisor multiplicity at the ORIGINAL root. The proof of
SF11 is the exact two-orientation identity SF8, common (node,R)
Cauchy, full short-core inversion and its convergent f sum. These
derivations, not the finite script, are the claimed mathematical
evidence. There was no new external theorem, provider call or prime
equidistribution hypothesis.

The small `check_interval_identity.py` calculation checks only SF8's
integer endpoint identity and disjoint level intervals. It covered
30 (maximum norm,gap) cases and 15,148 ordered norm pairs, including
zero gap, endpoint equality, gaps exceeding the norm range and
non-power-of-two original supports. All exact integer assertions
passed. It also evaluated SF12--14 from the displayed truncated
decimal pressure inputs. These are combinatorial/arithmetic receipts,
not a native Gauss-sum experiment or a proof of an analytic bound.
The output and current source hashes are in `interval-evidence.json`.

The strongest objections were checked as follows:

1. A separate D2 bound for each interval would lose their number.
   SF5--7 sum a single fixed tree and count each d once per level.
2. Absorbing P into t changes the cubic sieve length, but not its
   physical root; SF3 and SF7 retain q_P^(-1/2) and D Omega.
3. An additive product phase is not separable. None enters this proof;
   SF8 selects original norm intervals with exact shifted endpoints.
4. The two far orientations and both equal-norm exclusions matter.
   SF8 treats both strict inequalities and excludes equality exactly.
5. Signed I/II covariance cannot be estimated by deleting cross terms.
   SF15 is imposed before any bound and retains 1,-1,-1,1 on composites.
6. A new mask adapter does not improve the main arithmetic estimate.
   SF12 is split-independent, and the unit prime calculation is explicit.
7. A full-source or one-cusp identity does not cover all H branches.
   SF16--19 state the retained restricted return and remaining scope.

Within the inspected record, SF2 and its SF8--11 application are the
additional mathematical output. The binary-tree method, Cauchy and
the cubic sieve themselves are standard; no literature-priority claim
is made. [research revision] already contains the scalar D2 estimate, the original
two-cutoff prime identity, the unit obstruction and the failed leading
exponents. Here the change is the PROVED simultaneous interval scope
and full far-mask return without the old auxiliary near-band term.
The pressure calculation is its decisive failure test, not a new
numerical optimization or another baseline audit.

For independent review, the consequential checks are SF5's count of
tree nodes after summing disjoint output intervals; SF7's same-level
factorization mass with common marks; the preservation of all natural
zeros in SF3--4; and the common-node Cauchy step in SF10. If any of
those fails, SF11 must not be promoted. Even a favorable review will
not pay an original prime interaction or establish a larger c.



The final entire report and both small evidence files will be read
back; exact byte counts and SHA-256 values will be returned with the
handoff. After that readback this worker will STOP writing, release
only its exact owned claim, and leave integration to the controller.

The generic tail uses r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2). This is conditional reach, not arithmetic progress or a theorem at gamma=1/2.

The full general Mellin return retains all K shifted terms, with fixed K satisfying1-(b-1)K<gamma:

    H_p(z)=sum_(j<K) A_j(z)D_c(z+(b-1)j)+E_K(z),

statement:
## 3. Independent proof of H

Let b be fixed, bounded and Q-periodic with mean zero. Let |A_m|<=A, frozen before live x. First take 1<=D<=X^alpha0 for a fixed alpha0<1. All sums are absolutely convergent by damping. The theorem is

    ||sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml)||_1
      +||sum_(m<=D) A_m sum_(l>=1)b(l)f_x(ml)||_2
        <<_(Q,alpha0,||b||inf) A(D+X^(3/4))log^4(2X).         (R3)

The stronger arbitrary-D version is proved in Section4 without using any further arithmetic hypothesis.

### 3.1 Exact output partition and low source

Choose smooth nonincreasing phi, equal to1 on[0,1], zero on[2,infinity), and w(t)=phi(t/2)-phi(t). Then

    1=phi(n/X)+sum_(j>=0)w(n/(2^j X)), n>0.                  (R4)

This is an exact telescoping identity, with w supported on[1,4]. No original sharp mask is replaced. For the low term ml<=2X, the nonlinear phase derivative in l, after division by2pi, is -3m(ml)^5/(pi x^6). Its magnitude is O(m/X), including the final discrete increment. For m<=X^alpha0 this is eventually less than1/(4Q). Each nonzero Fourier mode j/Q therefore stays a fixed distance from every integer, and has monotone derivative. Discrete first-derivative summation bounds every prefix by O_Q(1). The product phi(ml/X)exp(-ml/x^(3/2)) has bounded total variation. Abel summation gives O_Q(1) per row, hence O(AD) for the full low source. Bounded initial X values are covered by the fixed constant.

The last-increment issue is real: it suffices to use ml<=3X for that increment since m=o(X). Section4 gives a version with an explicit small multiple of X, which also avoids this asymptotic qualification.

### 3.2 Exact Poisson formula and its signs

For a high output scale N=2^jX, set T=(N/X)^6>=1. Decompose m into dyadic intervals I_M=[M,2M) intersect[1,D]. Define

    beta_h=(1/Q)sum_(r mod Q)b(r)exp(-2pi i hr/Q), h in Z.

Then beta is Q-periodic, bounded by ||b||inf, and beta_h=0 whenever Q divides h. Applying Poisson after extending the smooth positive-support function by zero gives

    sum_l b(l)w(ml/N)f_x(ml)=(1/m)sum_(h in Z)beta_h I_(h/m)(x),
    I_r(x)=integral w(n/N)exp(-n/x^(3/2))
                         exp(i[2pi r n/Q-(n/x)^6])dn.        (R5)

The sign is correct. A Fourier mode exp(2pi i j l/Q), paired with the Poisson integer k, has frequency (j-kQ)/m; it is exactly h/m with h congruent to j modulo Q. Negative aliases and all repeats are present. The h=0 mode vanishes, rather than being estimated away. For each finite row the transformed sum converges absolutely after two integrations by parts in the large-|h| tail.

Write rho=N/(X^(3/2)) and x=Xz,1<=z<=2. The rescaled phase is

    T[2pi (rN/T)t/Q-t^6/z^6], n=Nt.

Choose a fixed positive frequency interval c_Q T/N<=r<=C_Q T/N which contains every possible stationary point on t in[1,4], with a fixed gap outside. The author's explicit constants work: c_Q=3Q/(128pi), C_Q=6Q*4^5/pi. At the lower outside boundary the linear derivative is at most half the minimum nonlinear derivative; at the upper outside boundary it is at least twice the maximum. These strict margins hold uniformly in z.

For a near positive r the unique critical point and phase are

    n_r=(pi r/(3Q))^(1/5)x^(6/5),
    Phi_r(n_r)=5(pi/(3Q))^(6/5)r^(6/5)x^(6/5),
    Phi_r''(n_r)=-30n_r^4/x^6.                               (R6)

In rescaled variables the critical point remains in a fixed positive compact interval and the second derivative is bounded away from zero. The amplitude and each fixed needed derivative are O(e^(-c rho)): derivative factors are powers of rho, absorbed into a weaker exponential. Uniform smooth stationary phase therefore gives

    I_r=Z_r exp(i kappa_Q r^(6/5)x^(6/5)-i pi/4)
                  +O_Q((N/T)e^(-c rho)),
    Z_r=sqrt(pi/15)x^3 n_r^(-2) w(n_r/N)exp(-n_r/x^(3/2)).    (R7)

The normalization and negative Fresnel sign follow directly from (R6). The deliberately weak T^-1 error is valid; a smooth nondegenerate expansion gives a stronger remainder. Support-edge crossings do not introduce a sharp endpoint: w and its derivatives extend smoothly by zero. The uniform proof and constants are detailed in support.md. No stationary expansion with a discarded sharp cofactor cutoff is used.

### 3.3 The full transformed-row error

Put H_m=mT/N. The number of positive near aliases is O(1+H_m). If any exists, its positive integer h forces H_m>=c_Q'>0. Consequently their remainders, INCLUDING1/m, sum to

    O(e^(-c rho)(N/(mT))(1+H_m))=O(e^(-c rho)).              (R8)

Outside the near window, nonzero |h|<=C H_m have scaled derivative separated from zero by cT. Two integrations by parts give (N/m)T^-2 e^(-c rho) per alias. Their count is O(H_m) whenever nonempty, so they cost O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)). This includes all negative aliases in that range.

For |h|>C H_m the derivative has size |h|N/m and dominates every higher phase derivative. Two integrations by parts give (m/N)|h|^-2 e^(-c rho). Summing BOTH signs costs O(T^-1 e^(-c rho)) if H_m is bounded below, and O((m/N)e^(-c rho)) otherwise. Here m<=X^alpha0<=N, so this is O(e^(-c rho)). The transition ranges have fixed constants and cause no loss. Thus every complete row equals its full stationary bank plus a uniform damped O(1). No infinite alias bill remains. Summing the block errors costs O(AMe^(-c rho)) pointwise and in both shell norms.

### 3.4 Coincident frequencies must be grouped before taking energy

For a reduced positive rational r=u/v write h=uj,m=vj. The WHOLE amplitude Z_r, including its support and damping, depends only on r,N,x. The exact coefficient is

    C_(u/v)=sum_(j: vj in I_M) A_(vj)beta_(uj)/(vj).          (R9)

Every natural zero and every nonconstant phase beta_(uj) remains. No averaging along j is assumed. The dyadic interval gives |C_(u/v)|<=C A||b||inf/v. Since u>=1 and r<=C_Q T/N, every active denominator obeys

    v>=N/(C_Q T).                                           (R10)

Counting numerators only in an upper bound yields

    sum_r |C_r|^2
      <<A^2||b||inf^2 sum_(max(1,N/(C_QT))<=v<=2M)
                                          [(T/N)v+1]/v^2
      <<A^2||b||inf^2 (T/N)log(2M).                         (R11)

Indeed sum v^-2 from the lower limit is O(min(1,T/N)), hence O(T/N). The empty range gives zero. This is the decisive calculation: deleting (R10) would leave a false N^2/T term after energy formation. Shared rational frequencies cannot be treated as orthogonal original aliases; (R9) pays their exact coherent sum first.

### 3.5 Complete shell Gram and damping

For j=0,1,

    |(d/dz)^j Z_r(Xz)| << (N/sqrt T)e^(-c rho).              (R12)

On the support of w or its derivative n_r is comparable to N and dn_r/dz=(6/5)n_r/z. All damping derivatives are absorbed by a weaker exponential. This also holds through the smooth support boundaries. For r!=s in the near window the phase difference has first derivative comparable to N|r-s|, since

    X^(6/5)(T/N)^(1/5)=N.

Its second derivative is a bounded multiple of the first. One integration by parts on the ACTUAL interval1<=z<=2, retaining both shell endpoint terms and the derivative of1/z, gives the Gram bound

    C (N^2/T)e^(-c rho) min(1,1/(N|r-s|)),                  (R13)

and the same scale with minimum1 on the diagonal. All distinct reduced fractions with denominators<=2M have spacing at least1/(4M^2). Ordering them gives the full row sum

    O(1+(M^2/N)log(2+J)), J<<M+M^2T/N.                     (R14)

Apply 2|C_r C_s|<=|C_r|^2+|C_s|^2 to the complete double sum, both orientations included. Combining (R11)-(R14), using log(2+J)<<_Q log(2N), gives

    ||whole stationary bank||_2^2
        <<A^2 e^(-c rho)(N+M^2)log^2(2N).                  (R15)

Add the full row error by norm triangle. Sum the whole blocks in norm over M and N, never by a signed-subset norm comparison. The M contributions sum geometrically to D, then acquire O(log X) from output scales below damping. The sqrt N contributions sum to O(X^(3/4)log X) and have at most O(log(2D)) row blocks. The infinite N tail converges with the actual exponential, even after all logarithmic factors. The low part is O(AD). Log^4(2X) is a safe total allowance. Finite-measure Cauchy supplies L1 from L2. This proves (R3), including all low/high and inter-block crosses.

## HCR4. All-dyad norm return and complete pole accounting

The following is the exact sufficient theorem, expressed relative to the
updated accepted premise. Fix tau,A>0, 1/2<a<b_*, and a certified fixed
T>=1-a such that every nontrivial off-critical-line zero has |Im rho|>T.
Trivial zeros are outside the candidate region. Put

    d=A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2),      gamma_crit=a-d.

Assume d<c_* and gamma<=gamma_crit. If, for every epsilon>0 and every
sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_(log X)^(log(2X)) |D_A f(u)|du
          <= C_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),                 (HCR4.1)

then zeta has no zero with Re s>a. All of tau,A,a,T,gamma are fixed before
epsilon and X. The bound is required on every sufficiently large dyad,
not on a selected sequence of favorable shells. Its threshold X_0 and
constant may depend on epsilon and the fixed parameters. The stronger
bound with |D_A f|^2 and exponent 2gamma+epsilon suffices by
Cauchy--Schwarz on the constant-length logarithmic shell.

Proof: shells [k log 2,(k+1)log 2] tile the tail. On any compact subset
Re w>=gamma+eta, choose epsilon<eta. Summing HCR4.1 with exp(-Re w*u)
gives a convergent geometric series. Inserting any fixed power u^j does
not affect convergence. Therefore H and all its fixed w-derivatives are
holomorphic in Re w>gamma. The initial bounded u interval gives an entire
function. By HCR3.2 and the meromorphic identity theorem, H agrees there
with R and R has no pole in this half-plane.

Suppose a<Re rho<=b_* and set delta=1-Re rho. Then
c_*<=delta<1-a and |Im rho|>T. The other preimage of phi_A(rho) is

    rho^*=1-A/(1-rho).

Because delta/(delta^2+T^2) is increasing for 0<=delta<=T,

    Re rho^* = 1-A*delta/(delta^2+(Im rho)^2)
              >= 1-d > b_*.

F is regular at rho^*. Moreover

    phi_A'(rho)=1-A/(1-rho)^2 != 0,
    (1-rho)/(rho^*-rho)=1/phi_A'(rho).

Nonvanishing follows already from delta>0 and Im rho!=0: (delta-i Im rho)^2
cannot be the positive real number A. Near w_0=phi_A(rho), a pole of F of
order m with leading coefficient C gives a pole of R of the same order
with leading coefficient C*phi_A'(rho)^(m-1). Thus simple-zero assumptions
are unnecessary; the simple-pole residue is unchanged. There cannot be
cancellation from another nontrivial or trivial zero, because the only
other root is in the accepted zero-free half-plane.

Finally, for |t|>=T>=1-a the function
1-delta-A*delta/(delta^2+t^2) decreases strictly in delta on this interval.
Since delta<1-a,

    Re phi_A(rho) > a-A*(1-a)/(T^2+(1-a)^2) >= gamma.

This contradicts holomorphy of H. Zeros to the right of b_* were already
excluded by the baseline; zeros at height <=T are handled by the stated
finite-height input. The conclusion concerns the open region Re s>a;
gamma=gamma_crit is allowed because the candidate zero has Re rho>a.
This proves the conditional return, not its hypothesis.

## G151. An actual two-variable repair and two fully priced detector interfaces

### The squarefree lift and its principal branch obstruction

Define, initially Re(s),Re(t)>1,

    F_chi(s,t) = sum_(m,n>=1) c(m,n)m^(-s)n^(-t),
    c(m,n) = mu(mn)chi(mn)2^(-omega(mn)),

with zero coefficient when mn is not squarefree. Natural ramified zeros,
the prime two when unramified, and c(1,1)=1 all remain. Unique allocation
of every prime to one of the two coordinates gives

    F_chi(s,t) = product_p [1-chi(p)(p^(-s)+p^(-t))/2],
    F_chi(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi).

On every finite hard product cutoff, the complete diagonal coefficient of
k is exactly mu(k)chi(k), since a squarefree k has 2^omega(k) allocations.
This is an actual source identity. Its absolute convergence cone is exactly
Re(s)>1 and Re(t)>1: the prime terms on either coordinate axis force the
two prime series, and their convergence suffices. Finite ramification
does not alter this cone.

For x=chi(p)p^(-s),y=chi(p)p^(-t), on both real parts greater than1/2 put

    log G(s,t) = sum_p [log(1-(x+y)/2)
                       - (1/2)log(1-x) - (1/2)log(1-y)].

Power-series logarithms are legitimate since |x|,|y|<1. The linear terms
cancel and the quadratic term is (x-y)^2/8; compactly uniform bounds by
a constant times |x| squared+|y| squared give normal convergence.
Thus G is holomorphic and nowhere zero there, G(s,s)=1, and initially

    F_chi(s,t)^2 L(s,chi)L(t,chi) = G(s,t)^2.                (G151.1)

For principal chi fix a safe real t0>1. Since L(s,chi) has a simple pole
at1, the right side of F(s,t0)^2=G(s,t0)^2/[L(s)L(t0)] has a zero of order
one at s=1. A square of a holomorphic function has even vanishing order.
Hence this particular F cannot be holomorphic near (1,t0), and cannot
extend to the whole product half-plane Re(s),Re(t)>gamma for
1/2<gamma<1, even if zero exclusion is already known. The diagonal itself
is consistent: both reciprocal factors there have the same zero.

This actual obstruction redirects the lift, rather than rejecting all
two-variable detectors. A sloping tube, different source or explicit pole
normalization remains possible. The exact simple repair B=F squared keeps
its genuine two-variable convolution coefficients

    b(m,n) = sum_(d|m,e|n) c(d,e)c(m/d,n/e),
    B(s,t) = G(s,t)^2/[L(s,chi)L(t,chi)],
    B(s,s) = 1/L(s,chi)^2.

These b are not the original c. For fixed1/2<gamma<1, holomorphy of B on
the whole product half-plane is equivalent to zero exclusion for L in
Re(s)>gamma. Fixing t0 and nonvanishing G proves the forward implication;
holomorphic1/L, including its principal-pole zero, proves the converse.
No growth estimate or coefficient cancellation follows from this equivalence.
This is a corrected exact return, not an independent gain or a claimed
literature priority.

### Fixed native H packets: commuting operations still have a mixed bill

Use the exact Eisenstein source in
[[research revision] h-joint Sections1–2](../[research revision]/h-joint/report.md), including long
prime ideals pi,pi' of distinct rational norms, original orientations and
bad-place data, complete ordered short g,g' including equality, the complex
core, rational gcd screen, both rooted mark weights, both projectors and
independent heights. The coefficient systems remain
a(n)=alpha(n)eta(n)chi_n(lambda)^(-2)gamma_2(n) and
xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3. Nothing is replaced by an integer-norm or
positive-divisor surrogate.

For M=pi*pi',Q=q_M the finite group
(O/M) times(O/pi) times(O/pi') has size Q squared. Its unitary transform
F has factor1/Q and phases -Rh/M-Ps/pi+P's'/pi'. The literal dual kernel is

    K = b(pi)conjugate(b(pi')) zeta_CRT
        chi_pi(h)^3 chi_pi'(h)^3 chi_pi(s)^2 chi_pi'(s')^4,

with all natural zeros. Put kappa=conjugate(K) and take inner product linear
in the first argument. The complete raw packet is <F W,kappa>.

Freeze this packet except a designated smooth row profile rho_i and cap A_j.
Write W_ij=rho_i 1_(A_j)W0, where W0 is the source formula with that factor
omitted, retaining the full union of the caps. No division by a profile or
removal of its zeros occurs. Then exactly

    Delta H = <F[(rho1-rho0)(1_A1-1_A0)W0],kappa>,
    |Delta H| <= ||(rho1-rho0)1_(A1 symmetric-difference A0)W0||_2 ||kappa||_2.

The multiplication operations commute, but their four-corner finite
difference need not vanish. A zero operator commutator is not a small
rectangle-flux estimate. A true row translation V_delta instead satisfies

    [P_A,V_delta]W(R,...) = (1_A(R)-1_A(R-delta))W(R-delta,...),

and changes both rooted-projector arguments. This is distinct from the
accepted [research revision] adapter, which moves only the smooth profile from R/sqrt(K)
to (R+P+P')/sqrt(K), leaving sharp support and projectors in place. No
inter-scale map between varying prime-pair groups has yet been constructed.
The finite corner example is algebraic evidence, not an arithmetic lower bound.

The return still requires the entire raw target
G K [N+L+(NL)^(2/3)] sqrt(Omega1 Omega2) P_orig, then physical multiplication
by N^(-1)G^(-2) exactly once. Every corner, commutator and outside complement
must be paid. No .004 H gain follows. The genuine inter-scale idea remains
open, with [G89](../[research revision]/wild48-integration.md) and
[G136](../[research revision]/wild55-integration.md) ancestry retained.

### Two delay channels: local division versus a finite-height floor

For the complete fixed Gaussian field with Mellin transform
exp(tau s squared/2)/L(s,chi), physical dilation
D_lambda U(x)=U(x)-lambda^beta U(x/lambda) has multiplier
m_lambda(s)=1-lambda^(beta-s). Complete every-epsilon shell L2 bounds
of exponent gamma on lambda=2,3 give holomorphic channel transforms to
Re(s)>gamma, retaining the complete source and Gaussian left tail.

The multipliers have just one common zero, s=beta, simple for each.
Consequently these bounds exclude zeros in the target half-plane except
possibly a simple real zero at beta. A multiple zero still leaves a pole.
Independently excluding beta or adding another paid channel closes that
exception. Local division away from beta needs no global positive floor.
This retains the [principal Gaussian return](../[research revision]/principal-gaussian-integration.md)
and [G109 bank analysis, including its G47 exception](../[research revision]/sol04-integration.md).

Simultaneous recurrence prevents any all-height positive floor for a fixed
positive weighted sum of the squared multipliers. A finite-height replacement
is available. With kappa=log(2)log(3)/(2pi), 0<t0<=|t|<=T,

    max(|m_2(beta+it)|,|m_3(beta+it)|)
      >= min(2t0 log(3)/pi,
             4exp(-kappa T)/((log(2)+log(3))sqrt(3))).

For t>0 choose nearest nonnegative integers k,l to t log(2)/(2pi),
t log(3)/(2pi). If both vanish, the larger phase error is at least
t0 log(3). Otherwise 3^k and2^l are distinct integers, so the logarithmic
gap is at least exp(-kappa T)/sqrt(3). Combining the two phase errors and
2|sin(e/2)|>=2|e|/pi for |e|<=pi proves the bound; symmetry covers t<0.
The exponential price is deliberately coarse and yields no arithmetic
channel bound or uniform limit as T increases.

The retained weighted-degree and hidden-tail examples are narrowly scoped:
exp(i sin(t)) with weight A(1+epsilon cos(t)) has weighted crossing total
2A epsilon despite degree zero; exp(rho v)1_(v>=A) has Laplace transform
exp(-(s-rho)A)/(s-rho). Neither is a counterexample for actual native H or
an all-scale Möbius invariant. They identify unpaid weighted amplitude
and tail-continuation assumptions only.

## 3. Why the changed lower window is a legal original input

## 6. Extracted errors, zero frequencies, exceptions and reopening limit

For the actual auxiliary prime, lambda=log_Z Npi>=a-log_Z2, hence lambda>=3a/4 eventually for all thirty pools. Both sharp pool endpoints remain literal. Therefore F1>=2c/3-4a-small losses and F2>=2b2/3. The exact coefficient is -4a. With v=c+min(c2,d2), L=M/4,

at v=L. This pays main excess A-M+4a and original error excess A-M+9a. In particular the source Kphys^(5/6) cost is included. Leading lattice terms cancel for equal-product rectangles with the same whole character, mask, profiles and independent-height norm powers. Their amplifier index agrees.

All terminal terms have positive reserve. Choose aggregate losses below a fixed fraction of the table, 57/5000000 and 5861/13500000. Both joint side targets follow, and joint Cauchy plus comparison proves the local theorem. All descendants use old moments, so no recursion through C occurs.

The author's scalar reopening calculation is also correct with a limited interpretation. At a generic fixed lower edge s and C=9/2-r, take t=s and n1=n2=(1-Cs)M/2. Strict low reserve requires a/M>(7/3)rs. At that lower boundary the high reserve at delta=.7 is

    G(d,c)=(1+delta)/2+13h/75-y/2-ell/2+ell delta p

## 9. Remaining fields and complete zero-exclusion return

Small nonprincipal rows below Z^d0, including fixed-conductor and finite-unit rows, keep the original global-line estimate with reserve

    -13h/75+y/2-63d0/50=21464387121/250000000000>1/20.

With fixed zeta0=10^-10, choose a sufficiently large fixed positive line parameter v before the final threshold for the desired negative power. Constants may be large, but there is no new asymptotic loss or central-density assumption.

Off-height fields retain the three independent contour frequencies, complete original w-inversion, joining segments and separately extracted principal poles. The Gaussian controls its frequency; the other Mellin transforms have arbitrarily high fixed polynomial decay. Assign fixed fractions of each buffered height window. On joining segments reciprocals remain inside the zero-free buffer or on the global line. Raw unseparated numerator and conductor-height bounds have fixed polynomial Z-degree before external integration-by-parts order is chosen; then a sufficiently large fixed order pays Z^B T^-N. For each fixed target only afterward choose its exclusion set S, anchor/dictionary and finite internal moment, profile and Sobolev orders. The density's internal detector exponent was already fixed. The original compensated probe and numerator assembly give

The fixed target cutoff gives |H_eta-1|<=1/2 on Re(s)>=.87 and the Gaussian is nonzero. Since beta_*-Delta>theta>.87, a target zero there cannot be canceled by the numerator. No zero-times-pole inference at s=1 is used. The ordinary and zeta conclusions follow in the stated scope.

The changed-window objection is resolved by original-data quantifiers and the explicit old-moment complements; polynomial slack alone would not suffice. No mathematical repair is requested. Preserve the fixed original-family/common-profile restrictions, the accepted upstream framework as a dependency, the limited strict-boundary interpretation, and pending full formalization/kernel replay. Hash checks and exact arithmetic are not a new Lean proof.

## 6. Source-resolvent consequence, including the atom at zero

For fixed q, a fixed finite E, positive weights v_n with sum v_n<infinity,
and positive u_n on E, define the exact operator

    K=sum_(n>=1) v_n(w_(q,n) tensor w_(q,n))
         +sum_(n in E)u_n(f_n tensor f_n).

It is positive trace class because ||w_(q,n)||^2<=(q-1)^2/(2sigma). Its
quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative weighted squared inner products, so

    ker K=(W_q+span{f_n:n in E})^perp.

For the spectral measure of the actual target 1, dominated convergence gives

    <1,lambda(K+lambda I)^(-1)1>
       =integral_[0,infinity) lambda/(t+lambda) dmu_1(t)
       ->mu_1({0})
       =||P_(ker K)1||^2>0.                              (R14)

The integrand is exactly 1 at t=0 and tends to 0 at positive t. Hence every
lambda>0 resolvent value is already at least that atom. With no seeds, the atom
is at least J. With seeds it is still positive by R9, but J is not automatically
a lower bound for the patched source.

Changing positive summable weights cannot change this kernel. Polynomial,
exponential or predetermined block weights are covered when they satisfy the
stated positivity and summability. Every finite truncation from the same fixed
dictionary has span inside the full one and inherits the distance floor. This
does not cover a growing finite seed set that introduces infinitely many new
directions. The full original f_n resolvent remains open.

This uses the generic A08.2 spectral identity, already paid in the old record.
The new deduction is the strictly positive atom for the literal fixed-ratio
wavelet source. It is neither a generic compactness obstruction nor a failure
of an upper-budget estimate.

## 5. A further conditional transfer of the nonlinear marked-plain gain

This section is separate from the accepted-density route. It assumes the NEW [research revision] marked-plain source lemma and its all-regime/raw-lifting proof, independently approved according to the controller but still pending root intake at this writing. It does not mistake the accepted marked-INVERSE theorem for that marked-PLAIN theorem.

The stronger [research revision] raw theorem has gain

    G_delta(W,v)=min(3k v, A_delta W+B_delta v),
    A_delta=2delta(5-6delta)^2/[3(5-2delta)(115-54delta)],
    B_delta=14delta(5-6delta)/(115-54delta).           (12)

Its range is 0<=v<=W/21. [research revision] proves the free estimate for v/W<=1/20 by a partially marked plain fourth moment and the accepted marked inverse estimate; the short, middle and long inverse regimes are all included. Its raw sixth-power sum uses the original holes, decay 6(rho-A_delta)-1>0 in the near range, and tail reserve rho-1/6-3k>0 in the complementary range, including bounded or fixed-inducing free cores. Those source assumptions and their fixed-dictionary/height quantifiers remain necessary here.

It would be WRONG to replace [G(W,z_1)+G(W,z_2)]/2 by G(W,zbar): G is concave. Instead fix the ORIGINAL z. For 0<=v<=z, G(W,v)/v is decreasing in v, so

    G(W,v)>=(v/z)G(W,z).                            (13)

The zero endpoint follows directly. G is nondecreasing and A_delta-Lipschitz in W. Write V=M-6a. In the case s0<z of Section 4, W>=V-c>21z. Consequently, after the actual Cauchy average,

    [G(W,z_1)+G(W,z_2)]/2
      >= [G(V,z)/z]zbar-A_delta c,                 (14)

because zbar<=z. This uses each slot product at its actual width and charges the possible row-width reduction c once.

Throughout the atlas z/M in [17/500,1/25]. Both A_delta and B_delta decrease on [.68,.70]. For A, its logarithmic derivative is

    1/delta-12/(5-6delta)+2/(5-2delta)+54/(115-54delta)<0;

bound the three positive terms at their interval maxima and the negative term at -12/(.92)=-300/23. For B, the derivative numerator is 14(575-1380delta+324delta^2)<0; that quadratic decreases throughout this interval. At q,

    A_q=17986/13356525, B_q=5474/48925,
    Kmax=A_q/(17/500)+B_q=2023402/13356525.

In particular

    Hval(q)-A_q-Kmax=6166/342475>0.                 (15)

Since V<=M and delta>=q>Kmax, all support/projector/plain costs in (14) are paid: (6), (9) and zbar>=z-s0 give a total saving at least G(V,z). If s0>=z, Hval(q)z alone is greater than G(V,z)<=Kmax z. Thus, in EVERY support configuration, including empty common support,

    final paired gain >= G_delta(M-6a,z)-small.     (16)

Also Kmax<3k(.70), so the affine branch in (12) is active at V,z for this whole atlas. The gain in (16) is therefore exactly

### D26.1 Exact local repair

The naive tail of h_p-1 contains the prime coefficient tD and costs P^-sigma. Remove it by the exact, absolutely bounded factor

    E(s)=L_K^S(s+1,eta),
    H_eta(s)=C_S E(s) Rcal(s),
    r_p(s)=(1-tD) h_p(s).                               (3.1)

This E is not assumed small: its coefficient mass at sigma is sum_a Na^(-1-sigma), and its inverse has the same positive majorant. Both are finite for sigma>0. Every power and phase remains in

    r_p-1=(1-t)[tD^2+R(1-(1+t)D)]/[(1-D)(1-R)].          (3.2)

In particular the coefficient at p is zero, and that at p^2 is t(1-t)a^2. The original p^6 contribution remains; it is not converted to an arbitrary Gaussian kernel error.

For sigma>2/3,

    ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <= (1-t)[t d^2+r(1+(1+t)d)]/[(1-d)(1-r)]
       = O_sigma(Q^(-1-2sigma)+Q^(3-6sigma)).             (3.3)

The inverse r_p^-1=h_p^-1/(1-tD) has a corresponding summable local bound; hence finite products and their inverses have coefficient norms bounded uniformly in their prime cutoff. This follows either from the direct product or from (2.6) and the E factor. No randomness, conditional independence or martingale drift estimate is used.

Let Rcal_<=P and Rcal_>P be the literal products over Q<=P and Q>P, respectively. ALL valuations at retained primes are included. By ideal counting and partial summation,

    sum_(Q>P) ||r_p-1||_sigma
       <<_sigma P^(-2sigma)+P^(4-6sigma).

For 2/3<sigma<1 the second term dominates, and the product estimate yields

    ||r_>P-delta_1||_sigma <<_sigma P^(4-6sigma).          (3.4)

For bounded P enlarge the fixed constant. For large P use product(1+b_p)-1<=exp(sum b_p)-1. All omitted interactions among large primes are included in that product; (3.4) is not a sum retaining only one missing prime.
