statement:
# [research revision] independent review: separated inverse products



## 1. Verdict and unchanged boundary

**R1. The new large-within-column-gcd estimate survives independent review.** Its signed divisor inversion and Euler convolution are exact. After the moving masks are removed, the only analytic inverse input is the original B0.9 moment on its original Mobius coefficient. The central factor is exactly `1/Nq`; all q labels and both q-smooth restoration sums are paid. The complete norm bound is

    ||B_{>=G} Qslots||_U^2
      << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/G)
                         [U+U^(1/6)(D2/G)^(5/6)].                 (R1)

At `G=U^(1/5)` this supplies a conservative squared-norm/counting margin `1/200` against the actual separated mixed target, after the stated loss allocation. It removes a real portion of the paired coefficient; it does not assert that actual high rows must obtain their signal from that portion.

**R2. The proposed complete diagonal and two relative-conductor payments also survive**, using the retained whole orientation, disjoint original slot pools, full natural holes, and positive norm before majorization. The coefficients have prime valuations at most three, so the whole same-sixth-power ideal class is `n=n'`. The paid absolute off-diagonal sectors are first `Q<=U^(9/5)` and then `Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5)`. They do not assert a sign for the surviving contribution.

**R3. An additional exact support restriction is proved in Section 8.** The small-gcd merged coefficient vanishes unless

    N(n/rad n) < C U^(1/5+v).

Consequently its relative conductors obey

    Q2 Q3^2 < C U^(2/5+2v),       Q3 <= C U^(2v).                  (R2)

The constant depends on the fixed annulus endpoints and slot system. These are genuine coefficient-support restrictions, not an extra estimate or a gain in c. They expose the short repeated-prime part of the still-uncontrolled source.

**R4. OPEN-MIX and the full zero-exclusion return remain open.** The remaining one-sided signed sum is still unproved. Current accepted source-relative values remain

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    theta11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364,
    K=28114053/6250000.

K retains its preceding-family ancestry; it is not recalibrated using c11. F0/base ancestry, the old positive-slot uniformity obligations, and exact external root-definition/import/admission bindings remain open. No exceptional centered reserve, new raw/positive-child theorem, or physical endpoint is spent here.

## 2. Evidence and precise source contract

The author report, helper, receipt, source manifest, worklog and freeze were read completely. The full accepted G146--G148 integration and root's bounded assignment were read. The relevant literal primary source was inspected again: PR9 B0.3, B0.7--9 and B3.3--6, including the actual zero extension, free-row amplification, moving-coefficient prohibition, common-profile quantifiers and full masked primitive Poisson. [research revision] review Sections 5--7 were checked for the relative mass and complete-hole derivation. Exact byte hashes, including the frozen author's report SHA256 `3c9634551f202495b426d18f0162118e10d75376d8feb0a82bfd86c171d4854c`, are retained in `inputs.json`.

The primary file is `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`, 198343 bytes, SHA256 `2b4c67c3e817d7854ee57e451cea1789c8a4a1d03a72ddb83b980421167096d8`, pinned to PR9 commit `58344dfdbe756cf2f743da1908ffe0582418cf5b`. The accepted reduction is `[restricted mathematical source]`, SHA256 `1457ca010ba659fd302e865796823249bad02350f64cb7471d2d1b39609c3ce0`. Source-relative acceptance of these inputs is the premise; the current pass does not repair their retained upstream obligations. The balanced-residue/Poisson mechanism already occurs in external RM-A/RM7 and the [research revision] record. No literature-priority claim is made for this review's support observation.

Fix the original field, primary-generator/unit convention, fixed excluded set S, fixed finite character dictionary, and one whole orientation. Set

    phi_u(n)=nu(n)psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1),
    M_u(D;W)=D^(-1/2) sum_n mu(n)phi_u(n)W(Nn/D).

All natural zero values are part of complete multiplicativity. Fixed nu need not have order six; it remains in column coefficients when rows are summed. Columns retain the source's S restriction. Original slots are the actual product

    Qslots_u=prod_i P_i^(-1/2)
        sum_(p in original pool i) a_i(p)phi_u(p)Wi(Np/P_i),
    P_i=U^(z_i), P0=prod_i P_i=U^v, 0<=v<=1/20.

The pools are disjoint across slots, but may meet either inverse index. Their relative characters, coefficients, height twists and zero extensions are unchanged. The slot count is fixed before the asymptotic threshold. Absolute prime/ideal counting gives `sup|Qslots|^2<<H_J U^(v+epsilon)`.

If the common inverse presentation has opposite orientation to the slots, align the **entire** slot product only at the positive norm stage, using `|Qslots|=|conjugate(Qslots)|`, with all its coefficients, heights and zero extensions conjugated. The retained fixed dictionary/relative reanchoring then gives the above convention. This does not justify independently orienting selected slots. The diagonal argument below requires the aligned common orientation or the equivalent whole-conjugated positive norm.

The ambient norm sums nonzero sixth-power-free rows in a fixed smooth enclosing ball of scale U, with the licensed fixed ray/unit sectors. The smooth majorant is nonnegative. Any original nonnegative divisor-bounded row weight is bounded by its subpower cost **before** pair expansion. No high-bin selector, amplitude selector, moving dictionary, or signed physical projector is introduced into its Poisson kernel. Fixed inducing free rows can be retained; deleting the already licensed finite list is separately priced below.

Physical parameters are

    17/25<=delta<=7/10, 17/20<r<47/50,
    33/25<s<141/100, s-r>3/8, D1=U^r, D2=U^s.

The actual G147 witness keeps its compatible plain lengths, same product annulus, same character and same zero real part. Its two inverse Fourier heights are independent. The internal buffered zero parameter can exceed .70: its stronger inverse signals are first obtained there and then weakened to physical delta. Original slot prices and E_K use physical delta. Both pre-frozen G147 profile families and their noncircular re-extraction remain required.

Write

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    DK=15K-10-6Kdelta,
    aK=delta(5-6delta)^2/(3h DK),
    bK=2delta(5-6delta)(K-1)/DK,
    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,aK+bKv),
    T=delta(r+s)+E_K.                                           (R3)

Only `E_K>=rho>=19/54` is used: `min(...)<=3kv` and `delta-3k=4delta^2/(5-2delta)>0`. The moment imported from literal B0.9 is

    ||M(E;W)||_U^2 << H_J U^epsilon[U+U^(1/6)E^(5/6)].           (R4)

It is uniform over the required bounded polynomial scales and original smooth profiles, after choosing UM's small slack first. Dyadic row annuli give the ball estimate. Nonempty subunit windows have bounded support and scales bounded away from zero by a fixed profile constant; smaller windows are empty. Those branches do not require a new coefficient theorem.

## 3. Independent reconstruction of the large-gcd identity

Let `B=M(D1;W1)M(D2;W2)`. The projection `B_{>=G}` imposes `N gcd(d1,d2)>=G` on its two inverse indices before merging. It does not constrain the slot indices or select rows. Define

    a_G(q)=sum_(d|q,Nd>=G) mu(q/d).

Interchanging `d|q|g` gives

    sum_(q|g)a_G(q)=1_(Ng>=G),
    a_G(q)=0 for Nq<G, |a_G(q)|<=d(q).                            (R5)

All q actually dividing both nonzero Mobius terms are squarefree. For `d1=qx,d2=qy`, squarefreeness yields

    mu(qx)mu(qy)=mu(x)mu(y)1_((x,q)=1)1_((y,q)=1).

There is no condition `(x,y)=1` here. The two q factors in the natural character give `phi_u(q)^2`; they are zero, not invertible phases, when a natural zero applies. If `M^(q)` includes the displayed extra column coprimality, central normalization gives exactly

    B_{>=G,u}=sum_(q sf,Nq>=G)
       a_G(q)phi_u(q)^2/(Nq)
       M_u^(q)(D1/Nq;W1)M_u^(q)(D2/Nq;W2).                       (R6)

The sum ends at a fixed multiple of D1. Indeed `(Nq)^(-1)(D1/Nq)^(-1/2)(D2/Nq)^(-1/2)=(D1D2)^(-1/2)`. Omitting the `1/Nq` would lose the entire q-label count and invalidate the claimed result.

B0.9 cannot be applied directly to the new moving q-mask. The exact repair is

    M_u^(q)(E;W)=sum_(h q-smooth)
             phi_u(h)/(Nh)^(1/2) M_u(E/Nh;W).                    (R7)

For `p|q`, convolution of the local Mobius sequence `(1,-1,0,...)` with `(1,1,1,...)` is `(1,0,0,...)`. At other primes it stays Mobius. This proves the coefficient identity on ideals; complete multiplicativity carries it through natural zero values. The normalization is exact because `h^(-1/2)(E/h)^(-1/2)=E^(-1/2)`. At every actual profile support the h sum is finite. It can safely be absolutely bounded by

    sum_(h q-smooth)(Nh)^(-1/2)
       =prod_(p|q)(1-(Np)^(-1/2))^(-1)
       <<_epsilon (Nq)^epsilon.                                (R8)

Separate finitely many small primes; each remaining factor is at most `(Np)^epsilon`. For an already retained polynomial-size puncture R0, use primes dividing qR0. This extension is explicit and has the same subpower cost; it does not license an arbitrary growing source dictionary. Neither a q-mask nor a `mu*mu` coefficient is hidden in a smooth test.

## 4. Complete norm proof and continuous margin

Multiplication by `phi_u(q)^2`, or by either h phase, is a contraction of the positive row Hilbert norm. Apply Minkowski first to R6 and then to both exact R7 expansions. Bound the first ordinary inverse trivially and the second by R4:

    |M_u(E1;W1)|<<H_J E1^(1/2),
    ||M^(q)(D1/x)M^(q)(D2/x)Qslots||_U
      <<H_J U^(v/2+epsilon)(D1/x)^(1/2)
                         [U+U^(1/6)(D2/x)^(5/6)]^(1/2).         (R9)

The trivial bound holds uniformly on nonempty subunit scales by their fixed lower support bound. The restored scales only decrease, so R8 bounds both h sums. The q-sum has its full cost:

    sum_(Nq in [X,2X]) |a_G(q)|/(Nq) << X^epsilon.

This follows from linear ideal counting and the divisor bound. The shortened factors in R9 then decrease by fixed positive powers of X. The dyadic tail from G is geometric, proving R1 including every q and every slot collision. It is not an unpriced normalized average over q or h, and no joint arithmetic independence is used.

At `G=U^(1/5)`, `s-1/5>=28/25>1`, so the long-inverse branch dominates. Its exponent is

    Egcd=v+r+5s/6-1/5.

On the whole closed coarse box,

    T-Egcd >=rho+(delta-1)r+(delta-5/6)s+1/5-v
            >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200
            >=2809/273000 >1/100.                              (R10)

Both width coefficients are negative, so upper r,s and upper v are the worst case. The derivative of the middle expression is `47/20-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]`, positive on the entire delta interval; hence its minimum is at 17/25. Independently, `60(5-2delta)^2` times that derivative is the polynomial `2525-2820delta+564delta^2`. Its exact Bernstein coefficients on `[17/25,7/10]` are

    542621/625, 105958/125, 20684/25,

all strictly positive. This is a continuous certificate, not a sample grid. The excess over 1/100 is `79/273000`.

For an explicit conservative loss ledger, reserve at most 1/1000 for the cumulative exponent change from fixed geometric pads, and at most 1/500 for all new subpower, internal-height, fixed-derivative and witness-signal losses combined. After retaining margin 1/200, R10 still has reserve `5/2184>0`. Endpoint pads are chosen small enough for the first aggregate bound by continuity on a compact box. The number of auxiliary losses is fixed; choose their individual epsilons and the internal height power after their finite orders are known. This ledger applies to this new source estimate. G147's smaller existing counting margin 1/2000 retains its own separately chosen loss allocation.

On an actual witness, `|B|^2>=U^[delta(r+s)-eta]`. Where `|B_{>=G}|>=|B|/2`, positivity, R1 and the above allocation bound the original weighted slot mass by `U^[E_K-1/200+epsilon]`. No division by a possibly zero slot product occurs. On the other rows, `|B_{<G}|>=|B|/2` by the triangle inequality. Alternatively

    ||BQslots||^2<=2||B_{<G}Qslots||^2+2||B_{>=G}Qslots||^2.     (R11)

This latter implication handles all low/high cross terms once the complete small-gcd norm is bounded. It does not independently save each cross term before that missing bound exists.

## 5. The whole paired diagonal

Merge the actual low-gcd tuple into

    n=d1 d2 prod_i p_i, N0=D1D2 P0,
    B_{<G,u}Qslots_u=sum_n c(n)psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1).               (R12)

The coefficient c includes `(D1D2P0)^(-1/2)`, both Mobius signs, both independent inverse profiles, all fixed nu and relative slot phases, all original pool restrictions, and `N gcd(d1,d2)<G`. Every factorization contributing to c must obey that tuple condition. It is not replaced by a condition on a gcd of two merged columns. The source B3.6 does not admit this extra c as a canonical coefficient, and is not invoked on it.

Each inverse contributes exponent 0 or 1 at a prime; the disjoint slot pools contribute at most one further appearance. Thus `v_p(n) in {0,1,2,3}` including every collision. For n,n', the difference is in `[-3,3]`; it is zero modulo six exactly when it is zero. The complete ideal sixth-power class is therefore `n=n'`. The fixed generator/unit sectors retain their finite phases. No unequal-root sum has been discarded: unequal ideal sixth-power roots cannot occur in this finite paired source. This observation would be false for the older completed Mobius-convolution source with unbounded prime powers.

Tuple multiplicity is divisor bounded. Linear ideal counting on the fixed product annulus, or Cauchy inside each factorization sum, gives

    |c(n)|<<H_J N0^(-1/2)U^epsilon,
    sum_n|c(n)|^2<<H_J U^epsilon.                               (R13)

It holds for all fixed derivatives, with larger finite seminorm orders. Dropping the small-gcd restriction only after taking this absolute majorant is legitimate. The entire diagonal, with its natural zeros and retained holes, is at most `H_J U^(1+epsilon)`. This is an upper bound for the diagonal contribution, not a lower bound for the full norm.

## 6. Relative conductor, coefficient mass and natural holes

For n!=n', let `e_p=v_p(n)-v_p(n')`. Define pairwise coprime radicals qj by `|e_p|=j`, j=1,2,3, and

    Qj=Nqj, Q=Q1Q2Q3, V=Q1Q2^2Q3^3.

The full oriented integer valuation vector specifies the pair ratio. Signs of 3 agree as sextic characters but give different integer ratios; the finite multiplicity is paid. Each nonzero good local exponent has conductor that prime. Fixed S-data cannot cancel it. Thus every off-diagonal vector is nonprincipal on its good conductor. Fixed nu remains in c rather than being incorrectly assigned order six.

Write `n=g a,n'=g b,(a,b)=1`. For a fixed oriented vector, `Na Nb=V`. Since both columns have norm comparable to N0, `Ng<=C N0/sqrt(V)`. With R13 and the linear ideal count,

    sum_(pairs with that vector)|c(n)c(n')|
       <<H_J U^epsilon V^(-1/2).                               (R14)

If the upper bound for Ng is below one, there are no pairs. The bounded endpoint case has the same estimate. Allowing every g is an overcount; it cannot remove a natural restriction. Summing vectors in dyadic Q1,Q2,Q3 ranges yields

    mass <<H_J U^epsilon (Q1/Q3)^(1/2).                         (R15)

This is the old balanced-residue mechanism, derived here for the finite actual paired coefficient rather than imported as an arbitrary-coefficient inverse moment.

The kernel is exactly

    K_(n,n')=sum_(free u)Phi(Nu/U)
                   xi_e(u)1_((u,E_(n,n'))=1),                 (R16)

with the licensed fixed ray/unit sectors. E contains every shared prime whose phase canceled and every retained frozen hole not already enforced by the primitive conductor. Equal prime powers cancel a phase but not its natural zero. Polynomial column support makes NE polynomial in U.

Literal B3.5 at a primitive nonprincipal modulus of norm Q has prefactor `X/sqrt(Q)`, normalized Gauss amplitude one, dual argument `X Nh/Q`, and zero dual coefficient zero. Schwartz decay bounds the nonzero dual sum by `O(sqrt(Q))`; direct counting gives `O(X)`. Expand the sixth-free indicator by `sum_(b^6|u)mu(b)` and the complete hole by `sum_(d|rad E)mu(d)`. Their actual inner scale is `X=U/[(Nb)^6 Nd]`. The b split at `[U/(Nd sqrt(Q))]^(1/6)` gives

    U^(1/6) Q^(5/12) prod_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6))
       <<U^(1/6+epsilon) Q^(5/12).

If the split is below one, use the full convergent sixth-power tail, bounded by `U/Nd`, which is smaller than the displayed expression. Bounded/subunit windows use the fixed support convention; the nonzero row sum is empty when the scale is too small. Shared primes with the conductor give zero phases and can be dropped only after absolute values. Fixed ray conductors cost a fixed factor. Combining the trivial row count proves

    |K_(n,n')|<<H_J U^epsilon min(U,U^(1/6)Q^(5/12)).            (R17)

This is the [research revision] complete-hole proof on this actual source. It is not merely a clean coprime transform. Deleting the already licensed finite inducing free rows costs O_fixed(1) per kernel, absorbed in R17; they can instead be retained throughout. Zero rows remain excluded. No direct negative-power zero exclusion or arbitrary raw-family deletion is inferred from this finite-row fact.

## 7. Paid small-gcd sectors and full margins

Assign sectors disjointly: diagonal first; then `Q<=U^(9/5)`; then its complement with `Q1/Q3<=U^(8/5)`. For the first off-diagonal sector, R14 and `V>=Q` give

    absolute sum <<H_J U^(1/6+epsilon)
                          sum_(Nq<=U^(9/5))(Nq)^(-1/12+epsilon)
                 <<H_J U^(109/60+epsilon).                     (R18)

The number of oriented vectors over a radical is divisor bounded. This is the full vector count, not one pair per conductor. For the second sector use R15 with the trivial U branch of R17, obtaining `H_J U^(9/5+epsilon)`. All Q2 values, canceled-prime holes, shared inverse factors and slot collisions are included. There are only logarithmically many dyadic ranges on the finite polynomial support.

The uniform target floor is

    T>= (17/25)(217/100)+19/54=123353/67500.

Its exact margins above the three paid exponents are

    diagonal 1:       55853/67500,
    total-conductor:    182/16875,
    ratio:             1853/67500.                              (R19)

Each exceeds 1/100. The same 1/1000 geometric and 1/500 auxiliary loss allocation leaves margin 1/200, with positive residual reserves `55313/67500`, `47/16875`, and `1313/67500` respectively. No small equality endpoint is spent. These sectors are controlled by absolute majorants; the unassigned signed sector can still be positive or negative.

## 8. Additional survivor: the repeated-prime part is short

**R20. Exact support lemma.** For any tuple contributing to c(n), put `g=gcd(d1,d2)`, `d1=gx,d2=gy`, and `p=prod_i p_i`. The ideals g,x,y are pairwise coprime and squarefree; p is squarefree by disjoint original pools. Let

    A=gcd(g,p), b=gcd(xy,p), g=A g0,
    xy=b z, p=A b p0.

These factorizations use actual ideal gcds and retain the original tuple labels. The ideals

    A, B=g0 b, C=z p0

are pairwise coprime and squarefree, and

    n=A^3 B^2 C,
    n/rad n=A^2B=g A b,     A b divides p.                      (R20)

Hence `N(n/rad n)<=Ng Np<G Np`. Because `Np<=C P0` on the fixed slot annuli, every contributing tuple satisfies

    W(n):=N(n/rad n)<C G P0,
    N A<=min(Ng,Np).                                           (R21)

The ideals A,B,C are also the intrinsic valuation-3, valuation-2, and valuation-1 radicals of n; the normal form is unique once n is given. Different admissible tuple factorizations change their allocation to the original factors, not these radicals. Thus c(n) is identically zero outside R21. Cancellation between coefficients is not needed. With zero slots, p=1, A=1, and `n/rad n=g` exactly.

For a pair of supported columns, the local inequality

    (|v_p(n)-v_p(n')|-1)_+
       <=(v_p(n)-1)_+ +(v_p(n')-1)_+

shows that the ideal `q2 q3^2` divides `(n/rad n)(n'/rad n')`. A valuation difference of three also requires a cubic prime in one column, so q3 divides `A(n)A(n')`. Therefore

    Q2 Q3^2 <=W(n)W(n')<C G^2 P0^2,
    Q3<=C P0^2,

proving R2. One may also retain the bound `Q3<G^2`; the slot bound is stronger on the current v range. At its largest v, `Q2Q3^2<<U^(1/2)` and `Q3<<U^(1/10)`. These fixed-constant inequalities convert to exponent support with arbitrarily small pads, without claiming false exact powers at finite U.

This is not an estimate on the gcd of two merged columns. It follows separately from every small-within-column-gcd tuple in each coefficient. It survives fixed profile derivatives, independent heights and common-profile integration because those operations change weights, not the arithmetic support. It does not replace c by an arbitrary coefficient having this support.

The lemma narrows the genuine target: its hard conductor comes primarily from the valuation-difference-one radical, while its squared/cubic components have the displayed short budgets. It does not remove the generic coprime squarefree sector, where `W(n)=W(n')=1`, `Q2=Q3=1`. No extra norm saving, literature novelty, or arithmetic impossibility follows merely from this structural restriction.

## 9. Exact remaining target and quantitative return

Let Rmix be the real ordered off-diagonal contribution from R12/R16 with

    n!=n', Q>U^(9/5), Q1/Q3>U^(8/5),
    Q2Q3^2<C U^(2/5+2v), Q3<=C U^(2v),                        (R22)

and with the actual coefficients c(n),c(n') separately restricted by their original tuple gcd cutoff. The final two conditions are automatic support from R20--R21; imposing them does not change the remainder. Retain every canceled-prime hole, fixed phase, original slot allocation and both independent heights. On the tensor Sobolev norm, sum the actual derivative coefficient products over its fixed finite derivative list and integrate with its fixed positive parameter measure.

The open estimate is a one-sided bound

    Rmix <= H_J U^[T-xi+epsilon], xi>0,                         (R23)

uniformly for the prescribed data and profiles. It does not assert nonnegativity or bound every pair absolutely. R18--R19 plus R23 would control the entire small-gcd positive norm. R11 and R1 would then give OPEN-MIX with a margin less than `min(xi,1/200)`. Evaluating on both actual inverse witnesses yields the original weighted separated-row count; no slot denominator is used. Combining with G147's paid complement gives a density margin less than `min(xi,1/200,1/2000)`, after separately allocating the witness, height and buffer losses. For example choose half this minimum and choose all auxiliary losses before the final threshold. This implication is for the specified free natural source.

A numerical endpoint would still require the complete raw/positive-child and physical return, including both signed coprimality projectors, all original family reconstruction and root/slot holes, fixed-inducing and exceptional rows, physical radii and amplifier charges, clipped rectangles, every shortening/Euler shift, principal cases, and the actual-supremum/common-Delta contradiction. No such new transfer is proved here. The original descendant/fallback budgets remain unchanged, and c11 remains the endpoint input.

The strongest limiting example for this method is an admissible coefficient pattern, not a high-zero realization. With no slots, squarefree n gives

    c(n)=(D1D2)^(-1/2)mu(n)nu(n)
             sum_(d|n)W1(Nd/D1)W2(N(n/d)/D2).                  (R24)

The independent twists stay on their respective divisors. This extra divisor-profile weight is not the canonical coefficient permitted by B3.6. Coprime squarefree n,n' can have `Q1` of order `N0^2`, `Q2=Q3=1`, and within-column gcd one. They satisfy every new support restriction and remain in R22. The available absolute envelope `U N0` is much too large; that is an upper-bound obstruction to these positive estimates, not a lower bound for the actual signed norm. A common zero does not make the two witnesses probabilistically independent.

The next mathematical action is therefore to estimate R23 using the actual Mobius/divisor-profile coefficient, or derive an identity that changes it while paying every complement. R20 identifies short repeated-prime factors that can be kept outside such an attack. A further clean Poisson transform or repeated optimization of paid cutoffs alone leaves the squarefree signed obstacle intact.

## 10. Uniformity, tails and independent checks

The proof starts with a fixed allowed parameter tuple. For rowwise choices, use tensor Sobolev in the common bounded real parameter, both independent inverse heights, all originally allowed slot heights, and log scale variables. Differentiating the normalized inverse replaces W by `-W/2-yW'`; other derivatives supply the original norm twists and fixed powers of logarithms on polynomial supports. The cutoff `N gcd(d1,d2)>=G` is fixed at the row scale U and is not differentiated. Write all q/h sums over a fixed global support bound if parameters vary; smooth profiles vanish at their support boundary. Every differentiated expression retains the same coefficient identities and support statements.

Scalar outside phases have modulus at most one; their log derivatives, when that presentation places heights outside W, have only logarithmic polynomial-support cost. Nonempty restored scales are bounded below and above by the already licensed ranges. B0.9 is used after restoration at fixed q,h, uniformly in those scales; it is not a theorem about a rowwise-selected moving arithmetic coefficient. Hilbert Minkowski pays all restored labels before Sobolev is used to dominate actual rowwise choices. Constants may depend on the fixed dictionary and slot system, not on live q, row, zero or height.

For a coupled common product profile, B3.3 fixes its measure on the entire ambient box before any current row or q label. Larger individual cutoffs and Fourier separation yield the above product estimates. The two Fourier coordinates remain distinct. Integrate their polynomial height cost against a sufficiently differentiable common Fourier measure. Substituting q,h changes scales; it neither changes that measure nor creates a new arithmetic profile family. Demand child derivative orders first and work backward through the bounded dependency graph.

Any common geometric mesh or buffer refinement is chosen from the bounded parameter ranges and requested reserve before the arithmetic family and eventual slot count, preserving G147's original order. Subsequently fixed slot/profile systems determine the finite seminorm and height orders; their auxiliary epsilons and the internal height power can then be chosen before the final threshold. Nothing is chosen from a live row, zero, amplitude or q label. The gcd threshold itself has no mesh dependence.

The genuine detector/Fourier tails, H,V cutoffs, prefix and easy witnesses remain paid by G147 with both frozen profile families. This review does not remove V from the complete divisor sum, reopen a truncated identity, or infer a source moment from an omitted tail. The current paired polynomials have compact annular support. Any newly used common Fourier tail is terminated only after the raw polynomial label count and all demanded height orders are known, by B3.3--4; choose its decay order before the final threshold. No infinite pair tail is left in R14.

Independent `verify.py` uses stdlib rational arithmetic and was executed only in this review scope. It reconstructs the continuous margin polynomial and its three positive Bernstein coefficients, all four exact margins and a concrete aggregate loss budget. Six full finite coefficient diagnostics carry two different nonconstant profiles and multiplicative characters with actual zero primes through the direct projection, divisor-extracted expression and mask-restored expression. It checks the eight local tuple types and all 64 pair types for the new intrinsic support lemma and complete diagonal. These are targeted diagnostics; the ideal convolution proofs, norm estimate, conductor estimate and quantifier arguments are supplied in this report, not proved by finite examples. No author helper was imported or executed.

All checks passed. The Python launcher emitted its existing path-location warning but the actual helper completed with exit code zero and exact output. No provider, child agent, formalization, kernel, canonical, tracker, Git, or author-scope mutation was used. The old frozen reviews remain untouched. statement:
# [research revision]: the small-core principal term and its exact cutoff obstruction

**Status: independently accepted within the stated source, profile and
input scopes.** Author: `c21_all_branch_h`; independent reviewer:
`c20_cubic`. This is new work after the accepted SQ and MO packets.
It proves an actual-source cutoff-transfer identity with an error smaller
by \(K^{-1/2}\), and an explicit counterexample to a uniform small-core
estimate for the B2.29 coefficient class. The counterexample does **not**
replace the physical infinity coefficient by an arbitrary coefficient
and then claim a lower bound for the physical H sum. No all-branch H
estimate or improvement of \(c_0\) is asserted.

The useful conclusion is specific. Completing the squarefree-removal
sum to infinity does not pay the original finite low-core sector: it
transfers its principal term to a complementary dual tail. At the unit
dual core, the complete coprime Euler operator can be exactly rank one
on prime columns. A further argument must use the actual cubic-Gauss
column phases or cancellation between dual sectors; coefficient mass
and the Möbius operator alone cannot uniformly pay this sector.

## Sources, normalization, and retained scope

All source paths below are relative to the repository root.

- M, `zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md`: B0.1--B0.2 for the field,
  primary ideals, units, self-dual measure, and natural character zeros;
  B0.14 for buffered reciprocal and logarithmic-derivative bounds;
  B1.1--B1.5 and B1.9--B1.11 for quadratic Gauss phases and CRT;
  B2.24--B2.30 for the quadratic/cubic sieves, original decomposition,
  and the exact coefficient-independence contract.
- SH, `[restricted mathematical source]`: SH1--SH4
  for actual pair coefficients, primitive conductors, and deleted
  zeros; SH5--SH11 for the exact finite squarefree-removal cutoff and
  the infinite Poisson sum; SH12 and SH27--SH29 for the unchanged
  infinity coefficient and corrected Gauss factors.
- D, `[restricted mathematical source]`: D11--D16 for the
  sharp true-gcd support and both original removed diagonals.
- HG, `[restricted mathematical source]`: HG9--HG17,
  especially HG13a, for exact z allocations, mark independence, and
  the common column mass across g and its complete projector d.
- SQ, `[restricted mathematical source]`: SQ1 and
  SQ4--SQ13 for the full square-power identity, uniformly bounded
  theta error derivatives, conductor cancellation, density, and the
  exact source main. Reviewed draft SHA256:
  `CF9718BD15D72DD74EC376DD775C2D4E0AFE6D737DA7176E0E9D894B82C1F91F`.
- MO, `[restricted mathematical source]`: MO1--MO7 for the
  source and exact union/intersection Euler factors; MO8--MO17 for
  the common Hilbert-valued density and coefficient-wise bound;
  MO18--MO20 for sharp Perron, its removable singularity, and the
  restricted paid range. Reviewed draft SHA256:
  `705CB0C23C3E58B140E5705BE3BE9B067379139BFFCE0F29447BF6BBC3FCBCD5`.

Use \(\mathbb K=\mathbb Q(\omega)\), \(\mathcal O=\mathbb Z[\omega]\),
\(q_x=N(x)\), and the exact primary-generator convention of M.
Divisor variables and \(h_0,t\) below are ideals counted once; full
lattice rows retain the six units. The additive character is
\(e(z)=\exp(2\pi i\operatorname{Tr}(z/\lambda))\),
\(\lambda=i\sqrt3\), and the self-dual measure is
\(2\,dx\,dy/\sqrt3\). All character powers retain their zeros.

Fix one original radial profile component and one fixed-S primitive
sector from SQ/MO. Every original component coefficient, scalar
normalizer, endpoint, finite-place factor, and height seminorm remains
outside the estimates with its actual value. The coefficient is

\[
c_i=\frac{a(P_i)}{\sqrt{q_{P_i}}}\,
\beta_H(n_i,b_i)\chi_{P_i}(n_i)^{-2}1_{(P_i,b_i)=1},
\qquad |a|,|\beta_H|\le1.
\]

Here a is independent of the row and of n,b; beta is independent of
the row and P. No factorization of beta is assumed. The own-column
zero is \((P_i,n_i b_i)=1\). Write
\(n_i b_i=j_iw_i^2\), \(j_1=ga,j_2=gb\), with the good squarefree
parts and coprimalities of SQ. The primitive character is exactly
\(\kappa=\kappa_S\chi_{ab}^3\), with conductor
\(\mathfrak f=\mathfrak f_Sab\), norm \(F=F_Sq_aq_b\), and exact
SH4 deletion ideal T. We are in the principal-square case:
\(\overline{\kappa_S}^2\) induces the principal character.

Retain the sharp true-core selector
\( |\mathfrak h(g)|\le1, q_g\le A_0Y<c_*N/(LB)\).
Both original preprojection diagonals have empty support by D,
with D's stated physical and endpoint hypotheses. In particular the
good conductor ab is nontrivial on every retained physical pair.
The d-projector is complete, not a truncated divisor sum.

Let \(\Phi\) have original support \([A_-,A_+]\), let \(\Omega\) be
its SH9 Fourier transform, and put
\(S_0=\sqrt{A_+K}\ge2\). Select a common bounded unit-invariant
squarefree-core weight \(\sigma(h_0)\), supported on a finite block
\(q_{h_0}\asymp J\le c_1\min(A_1,A_2)\), as in SQ1. This includes
the singleton \(h_0=1\). Fixed squarefree S-parts are retained, and
all square powers at all places remain in t. Put

\[
\mathcal H=KB S(N,L),\qquad
\mathcal B=B S(N,L)\sqrt{K A_1A_2/J},\qquad
S(N,L)=N+L+(NL)^{2/3}.                              \tag{SC1}
\]

## 1. Extending the removal cutoff: which expression is unchanged

For a finite \(R\ge S_0\), define \(\mathcal T_\sigma(R)\) by the
**same** SH10 source form, changing only the upper limit on \(q_s\)
from \(S_0\) to R and imposing \(\sigma(h_0)\) in the unique
factorization \(h=\epsilon h_0t^2\). In full, its pair summand is

\[
\begin{split}
&\sum_{\substack{q_s\le R\\(s,\mathfrak fT)=1}}
\mu(s)\sum_{z\mid T}\mu(z)\kappa(z)
\frac{K\gamma_\kappa U_\kappa}{q_s^2q_z\sqrt F}\\[-1mm]
&\quad\cdot
\sum_{h_0\ {\rm sf}}\sigma(h_0)\overline{\kappa(h_0)}
\sum_t\overline{\kappa(t^2)}
\Omega\!\left(\frac{Kq_{h_0}q_t^2}{q_s^2q_zF}\right),
\qquad
U_\kappa=\sum_{\epsilon\in\mathcal O^\times}
\overline{\kappa(\epsilon)}.                         \tag{SC2}
\end{split}
\]

Multiply this by the original
\(c_i\overline{c_j}\mathfrak h(g_{ij})\) and both preprojection
indicators, and sum the original columns. The omission of
\(\kappa(s^2)\) in SC2 is exact: it is one on the retained units in
this principal-square case. The t zeros include the entire conductor.
No scalar multiple of a Gauss index replaces F.

The same definition makes sense for \(\sigma=1\): for every fixed
s,z, the combined \(h_0,t\) sum is absolutely convergent, since it is
exactly the Schwartz-convergent nonzero lattice h sum. The zero
frequency vanishes because the retained primitive conductor is
nontrivial. If \(q_s>S_0\), the original pre-Poisson sum is zero:
for nonzero v,
\(q_vq_s^2q_z/K>A_+\). The v=0 term also vanishes. Therefore

\[
\mathcal T_1(R)=\mathcal T_1(S_0),\qquad
\mathcal C_\sigma(R):=
\mathcal T_{1-\sigma}(R)-\mathcal T_{1-\sigma}(S_0)
=-\bigl(\mathcal T_\sigma(R)-\mathcal T_\sigma(S_0)\bigr).
                                                               \tag{SC3}
\]

This is a finite-cutoff equality with the original source. It does
not say \(\mathcal T_\sigma(R)=\mathcal T_\sigma(S_0)\).
It remains true with every original g, d, z, ray, and fixed-place
factor: the vanishing occurs for each physical pair and each s,z
before any inequality or auxiliary off-coprime extension.

## 2. The added theta error is uniformly small

Applying SQ4--SQ7 to SC2 gives the exact decomposition

\[
\mathcal T_\sigma(R)=\mathcal M_\sigma(R)+\mathcal E_\sigma(R),
                                                               \tag{SC4}
\]

where \(\mathcal M_\sigma(R)\) is precisely SQ9--SQ10 with

\[
\mathfrak M(R;Q)=
\sum_{\substack{q_s\le R\\(s,Q)=1}}\frac{\mu(s)}{q_s}
\]

in place of its original \(\mathfrak M(S_0;Q)\). Nothing else in
the source main changes.

The SQ proof of the error works for **every** fixed ideal s, with
no upper bound on its norm. This uniformity needs three checks.

First, all logarithmic derivatives of \(E_\psi(y)\) are uniformly
bounded for every \(y>0\), by SQ5. In the compact normalized column,
dual-core, and divisor variables, changing \(q_s\) changes only the
unnormalized argument y. Hence the profile-separation mass and the
original height costs do not acquire a power of \(q_s\).

Second, \(\sqrt{Q_\psi}/\sqrt{F_S}\le1\) is still the exact SQ8
conductor cancellation. Fixed-place square-power tails have already
been included in t; no new family of fixed-place powers is counted.

Third, by the exact MO6 radical identity, the mask is
\((s,D\mathfrak A_i\mathfrak A_j)=1\). For fixed s it consists of
a fixed-place mask, a P-only mask, and an \((n,b)\)-only mask.
Thus it preserves mark independence, even for \(q_s>Z^C\). There is
no need to expand the divisors of s or pay \(q_s^\epsilon\). HG13a
still makes the g-profile factor external; the z allocations,
divisor-inside-column theta weights, and common g/d/z0 mass are
exactly those in SQ. In particular one is not choosing unrelated
coefficient sequences for each g.

Consequently, after the complete z and g/d budgets, the error of
one fixed s is \(\ll_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
Z^\epsilon\mathcal H/q_s^2\). The z1 sum still uses its original
allocation/density proof; the z0 sum stays inside the common column
mass. Summing ideal norms, using
\(\#\{s:q_s\le x\}=O_{\mathbb K}(x)\), proves

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal E_\sigma(R_2)-\mathcal E_\sigma(R_1)|
\ll_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
\frac{Z^\epsilon\mathcal H}{R_1},
\qquad R_2\ge R_1\ge S_0.}
                                                               \tag{SC5}
\]

Thus the error has an absolutely summable s-tail in the proved
operator bound. The same assertion has not been made for the main
or for an unbounded sum of separate h0 main/error terms.

## 3. The disappearing main returns in the complementary tail

For this step retain MO's explicit **I-HECKE** input: the supplied
whole-family finite-order Hecke zero-free/reciprocal hypothesis in
every buffered half-plane \(\Re v\ge b>b_0=1-c_0\). The step below
uses only its principal \(\mathbb K\)-character instance, not ordinary
Riemann-zeta nonvanishing. Fix \(b_0<b<1\).

MO7--MO19 may be applied with cutoff R in place of \(S_0\), retaining
the auxiliary-height powers instead of absorbing them into Z.
Take \(X=\lfloor R\rfloor+1/2\), Perron height \(2X^3\), and choose
the reciprocal-height losses independently. For every
\(\eta>0\), this gives

\[
|\mathcal M_\sigma(R)|
\ll_{b,\eta,\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}
Z^\epsilon\mathcal B R^{b-1+\eta},\qquad R\ge2.
                                                               \tag{SC6}
\]

The source feature norms and MO17 remainder bound have no R cost;
the displayed \(R^\eta\) pays the contour-height powers and ideal
norm counts. The horizontal and sharp-truncation errors decay more
rapidly. There is no residue at the apparent Perron pole: the finite
source Dirichlet series has the common factor \(F_D(v)\), so it
vanishes at \(v=1\), while all its other Euler factors are regular
there. This is the exact MO union/intersection factorization.

Choose \(\eta<1-b\). Then \(\mathcal M_\sigma(R)\to0\). Combining
SC3--SC6 shows that the ordered limit
\(\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\mathcal C_\sigma(R)\)
exists and satisfies

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)=
\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)
+\mathcal E_\sigma(\infty)-\mathcal E_\sigma(S_0),
\qquad
\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)
=\mathcal C_\sigma(\infty)
+O_{\epsilon,\mathrm{orig}}\!\left(
Z^\epsilon\sqrt K B S(N,L)\right).}
                                                               \tag{SC7}
\]

The fixed \(A_+^{-1/2}\) in \(1/S_0\) is part of the original
endpoint constant. A finite and quantitatively priced version is

\[
|\mathcal M_\sigma(S_0)-\mathcal C_\sigma(R)|
\ll Z^\epsilon\left(
\mathcal H/S_0+\mathcal B R^{b-1+\eta}\right).
                                                               \tag{SC8}
\]

This is an actual-source identity and estimate, with beta unchanged.
In the definition of \(\mathcal C_\sigma\), first sum all h0,t for
each fixed s,z, then take the s-cutoff limit. It supplies no license
to reverse those operations or sum separate SQ principal parts over
all h0. Completing s kills the selected main only in a **different**
selected sector; its difference from the physical sector is exactly
the complementary tail in SC7.

## 4. At the unit dual core the exact Euler operator can be rank one

The next calculation is an exact compression of the source matrix.
It identifies what remains of the actual phase; it is not a
replacement of the complete physical column family by primes.

Take the admitted unit-mark endpoint \(P=1,L=1\), original \(b=1\),
\(N=A\), and the sharp selector \(\mathfrak h(g)=1_{g=1}\).
Choose \(1\le A_0Y<c_*A\). Restrict both column indices to good prime
ideals p of norm comparable to A, in one sufficiently fine **fixed**
identity ray class. All these primes have norm exceeding \(S_0\).

The ray modulus can simultaneously include 3, 4, the fixed conductor,
and the conductors of the finitely many quadratic characters obtained
by evaluating at fixed deleted primes. It ensures, for distinct
retained p,q,

\[
\gamma_3(pq)=1,\quad
\kappa_S(pq)=1,\quad
\chi_{pq}(\mathfrak f_S)^3=1,\quad
\chi_{pq}(z)^3=1\quad(z\mid T_S),
                                                               \tag{SC9}
\]

where \(T_S=\operatorname{rad}(D_0)/
(\operatorname{rad}(D_0),\mathfrak f_S)\), and
\(D=\operatorname{rad}(\mathfrak f_ST_S)\) is exactly the original
fixed deletion/conductor radical. For the first identity, M B1's
quadratic Gauss phase is \(\Gamma_q(pq)\), which equals one when
the primary generator \(pq\equiv1\pmod4\). The other conditions
are finitely many fixed ray conditions; no moving conductor or
pair-dependent ray class has been introduced.

On this compression, \(j=p,w=1\), the true gcd is one for distinct
primes, \(T=T_S\), and \(\mathfrak f=\mathfrak f_Spq\).
Every prime in pq exceeds \(S_0\), so exactly
\(\mathfrak M(S_0;\mathfrak fT)=\mathfrak M(S_0;D)\).
The complete z-sum is the fixed nonzero product
\(Z_S=\prod_{r\mid T_S}(1-\kappa_S(r)/\sqrt{q_r})\).
In this principal-square sector \(\kappa_S\) is quadratic on units.
Any radial component nontrivial on units vanishes; otherwise
\(U_\kappa=6\). Each factor in \(Z_S\) is positive. CRT retains
the fixed factor \(\gamma_{\kappa_S}\), rather than setting the
full Gauss sum to one.

Let \(v_p\) be the original normalized column coefficient on these
primes, including its unchanged smooth column profile and original
finite/height twists. Put \(\rho_p=1-q_p^{-1}\). SQ9 with the
singleton selector \(\sigma=1_{h_0=1}\) gives exactly

\[
\boxed{
\mathcal M_{\{1\}}^{\rm prime}(S_0)
=C_{\Phi,S}\sqrt K\,\mathfrak M(S_0;D)
\left(
\left|\sum_p\rho_p v_p\right|^2
-\sum_p\rho_p^2|v_p|^2\right),
\quad
C_{\Phi,S}=6c_\Omega\rho(\mathfrak f_S)
\gamma_{\kappa_S}Z_S.}
                                                               \tag{SC10}
\]

The original finite-sector expansion coefficient and any original
outside scalar multiply both sides. For two different separated
column profiles, replace the square by the product of their two
sums, and the diagonal by the corresponding inner product.

Both original removed diagonals are present in this calculation:
with \(P=1,b=1\), they both mean p=q. That case also has true gcd
p and is outside the sharp support. The subtraction in SC10 is an
algebraic way to express the distinct-prime sum, not a restoration
of a physical diagonal. The complete d-projector is one on each
remaining pair. Every z is a fixed z0 divisor and z1=1; there is no
missing ambient z count. All original s, all square powers t, and
all fixed-place zeros have already been included in SQ9.

For the actual unextracted infinity source, \(v_p=f(p)W(q_p/A)\),
with its **actual**
\(f(p)=\overline{\alpha(p)}\gamma_2(p)\nu(p)\) from SH12.
Thus SC10 exposes a cubic-Gauss first moment. The sign
\(\overline{\kappa(h_0)}\) is exactly one at this core, and the
Euler/Möbius operator is a common scalar. Neither sign supplies
additional column cancellation. SC10 does not assert that the
actual first moment is large.

## 5. A quantitative failed-inequality counterexample

This section tests the stronger, false proposed assertion that the
unit-core sector is always \(O(Z^\epsilon K B S(N,L))\) for **every**
coefficient allowed by B2.29. Its coefficient choice below is not
the physical beta. It proves a limitation on that uniform method,
not a lower bound for the physical H sum.

Choose a fixed nonzero nonnegative smooth row profile supported in
\([A_-,1]\), with upper support endpoint 1. Its SQ zero-frequency
coefficient is nonzero. Indeed one-dimensional Fourier inversion
on a line, with M's additive pairing and self-dual measure, gives

\[
\int_0^\infty\Omega(u^2)\,du
=\int_0^\infty\Phi(r^2)\,dr,
\qquad
c_\Omega=\frac{\pi}{3\sqrt3}
\int_0^\infty\Phi(r^2)\,dr>0.                    \tag{SC11}
\]

For example, integrate the radial two-dimensional transform along
the real frequency line. The inverse transform in the perpendicular
coordinate evaluates the original radial function on its real line;
the factor \(2/\sqrt3\) in the measure cancels the corresponding
factor in the additive pairing. Schwartz decay justifies that
one-dimensional inversion. This proves SC11 without assigning a
sign to the full oscillatory transform.

Take any fixed nonvanishing unit-trivial principal-square sector;
the primitive principal fixed-S factor is already a permitted
example. Then \(|C_{\Phi,S}|>0\). Let \(\ell\) be a rational prime
\(\ell\equiv1\pmod3\), avoiding D. There are exactly two prime
ideals of norm \(\ell\), each with Möbius value -1. Since ideal
norms are integers,

\[
\mathfrak M(\ell;D)-\mathfrak M(\ell-\tfrac12;D)
=-\frac2\ell.
\quad\text{Hence}
\quad
\max\{|\mathfrak M(\ell;D)|,
|\mathfrak M(\ell-\tfrac12;D)|\}\ge\frac1\ell.
                                                               \tag{SC12}
\]

For each arbitrarily large such \(\ell\), choose the endpoint
\(S_0\in\{\ell-1/2,\ell\}\) attaining this lower bound, and set
\(K=S_0^2\). Thus
\(\sqrt K|\mathfrak M(S_0;D)|\ge1/2\), for large \(\ell\).
This exact jump is not a conjectural lower bound for Mertens sums
and uses no zero near the boundary of I-HECKE.

Let \(W\ge0\) be fixed, smooth, bounded by one, supported in a fixed
prime-column annulus and positive on a subannulus. Choose
\(a(1)=1\) and
\(\beta(n,1)=1\) on good primes in the fixed ray class of SC9,
zero otherwise. This satisfies every B2.29 independence condition;
the smooth factor is \(W(q_n/A)\). In particular \(v_p=W(q_p/A)\)
is nonnegative. No coefficient depends on the row or mark.

For clarity, the prime-count input follows from the fixed finite
ray-character part of the supplied I-HECKE hypothesis. Finite ray
orthogonality and Mellin inversion of \(-L'/L\), shifted to any
fixed line between \(b_0\) and 1, give
\(\sum_{p\ {\rm in\ class}}W(q_p/A)\log q_p=c_W A+o(A)\),
with \(c_W>0\); B0.14 prices the logarithmic derivatives and smooth
height tails. Prime powers contribute \(O(A^{1/2+\epsilon})\).
Consequently \(\sum_p W(q_p/A)\asymp A/\log A\), and the same
argument applied to a positive subannulus gives the needed lower
bound. This uses only finitely many fixed Hecke characters, but is
explicitly placed under I-HECKE here; it is not inferred from the
principal zeta reciprocal alone.

The bracket in SC10 is therefore
\(\gg A^2/(\log A)^2\), since its subtracted diagonal is only
\(O(A/\log A)\). Combining with SC12 yields

\[
\boxed{
|\mathcal M_{\{1\}}^{\rm prime}(S_0)|
\gg_{\Phi,S,W}\frac{A^2}{(\log A)^2}.}
                                                               \tag{SC13}
\]

This lies in the narrow short-divisor corridor. For any fixed
\(\kappa_0>0\) and \(0<\delta<0.006322\), define Z along this
sequence by \(K=Z^{\kappa_0}\) and set
\(A=Z^{\kappa_0+\delta}\). Then \(K<NB=A<KZ^{0.006322}\),
\(B=L=1\), and \(S(A,1)\asymp A\). Put \(Y=A/K\). For large Z,
\(1\le A_0Y<c_*A\), with the original fixed endpoint constants.
All selected primes exceed \(S_0\), and \(J=1\) satisfies SQ1 and
lies below \(A^2/K^{2-b}\) for every fixed \(0<b<1\).

For any \(\epsilon<\delta\), SC13 divided by
\(Z^\epsilon K S(A,1)\) tends to infinity as
\(Z^{\delta-\epsilon}/(\log Z)^2\). SQ's error is
\(O(Z^\epsilon KA)\); choosing a smaller epsilon shows that the
exact unit-square-class fragment with these auxiliary coefficients
also has the SC13 scale. This does not give a lower bound for the
sum of all dual classes.

Likewise SC7 shows that its added complementary tail has this
scale, since the transfer error is only
\(O(Z^\epsilon\sqrt K A)\). Thus an argument that declares the
added tail negligible merely because each **complete** dual sum
vanishes is quantitatively false. The example includes the full
finite s cutoff, every z, every square power, and both preprojections.

## 6. Exact remaining gate for the physical source

For the unchanged infinity source, the prime compression requires
control of the actual quantity

\[
\sqrt K\,\mathfrak M(S_0;D)
\left\{
\left|\sum_p(1-q_p^{-1})
\overline{\alpha(p)}\gamma_2(p)\nu(p)W(q_p/A)\right|^2
-\sum_p(1-q_p^{-1})^2|W(q_p/A)|^2
\right\}.                                                   \tag{SC14}
\]

Every part of nu, including SH12's raw infinity angular and finite
twists, is retained. SC14 is one necessary test of a uniform
source-sensitive estimate, not a sufficient estimate for all
original columns or marks. An estimate of this actual Gauss first
moment, and its marked/deleted generalizations, is not supplied by
the B2.29 coefficient mass or by the Euler operator. Conversely,
cancellation with other squarefree dual cores is a logically
different route; SC7 gives its exact ordered-tail formulation.

This packet therefore stops at a proved cutoff-transfer identity
and a concrete failed uniform inequality. It does not claim the
physical SC14 is large, does not replace physical coefficients by
the auxiliary nonnegative coefficients, and does not promote the
pointwise Mertens jump or an individual theta sector into a lower
bound for H. Moving-sector conductor cancellation, angular row
profiles, and the full unbounded h0 main/error interchange remain
outside its scope. The previously accepted MO estimate is unchanged.

Independent review accepted SC1--SC14 with the two mechanical TeX
repairs recorded in the ignored promotion receipt. The original saved
source, including its bytes preceding the author stream interruption,
and the independent review remain unchanged under
`[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`.

### S24: complete replica determinant and sparse-graph certificate cost

On the K squarefree q-units at most x, put a_n=mu(n)chi(n), so |a_n|=1. Exactly

    sum_(m<n) |a_m-a_n|^2 = K^2-|M_chi(x)|^2.

For the principal character this is 4K_+K_-. Positivity alone does not give the required lower bound K^2-O(x^(2gamma+epsilon)). That one-sided deficit is the full signed arithmetic problem.

For a simple d-regular graph on these K vertices, 1<=d<=K/2, let Ltilde=(K/d)(dI-A) and Lcomplete=KI-J. From tr(A^2)=Kd and the constant eigenvalue d,

    ||Ltilde-Lcomplete||
      >= K sqrt((K-d)/(d(K-1))) >= K/sqrt(2d).

Thus a uniform operator-norm comparison paying the quadratic error by K times this norm needs d at least x^(4-4gamma-o(1)), since K is a positive constant times x plus O(sqrt x). At gamma11 the degree exponent is .5005838544; at 5/6 it is 2/3; at 3/4 it is 1. The latter rules out every fixed-power saving d<=x^(1-delta) by this certificate, not x^(1-o(1)) under epsilon losses. It is not a lower bound for the actual Möbius vector's signed error, nor a theorem about weighted/nonregular constructions.

The finite independent checks support exact identities and indexing only: actual principal, complex and imprimitive character replica identities and three graph trace examples. The asymptotic statement follows from the displayed proof, not samples.
