## 8. Physical capacities, every shortening, and all free shifts

Independent reconstruction gives

    theta = 874861/1000000,  c = 125139/1000000,
    h = 3969737987/5000000000,
    ell = 11/3-4theta = 125417/750000,
    x = 1+ell-h = 5599126039/15000000000,
    y = h-2ell = 6892533961/15000000000,
    kappa_* = 2theta-1 = 374861/500000.

They satisfy `0<ell<x<y<2x`, `y<1/2<h<2y`, `1/6<ell<1/5`,
`h>4ell`, `x+y=1-ell`, `theta>.87`. Principal-probe tests are
`-599126039/5000000000`, `-24583/150000`; the exact identity is
`(5x+y)/12=theta-(5/6-x/3-ell/6)`.

Let `d_-=h-.001`, `d_+=h+10^-10`, `d0=1/200`, and `u0=.001`.
For a retained near-endpoint row `U=Z^d` and free Euler shift `U^u`,
`0<=u<=u0`, reflection gives plain ceilings `n=1-y/d+u`. The selected
TARGET capacity is

    z_A = (B-2n)/Lambda,
    d z_A(0) = [2y-(2-B)d]/Lambda.

This pays the full affine intercept deficit. Its exact extrema are

    n_min = 5001680000/11894213961,
    n_max = 402287137237/952737117000,
    z_min = 65807969436717121/1839925920350400000,
    z_max = 841262571937768693/22970106001483200000.

Thus `.41<n_min<=n_max<N=.4224<.44` and
`.034<z_min<=z_max<z_safe=.037<.04`. In particular
`N-n_max=745104919/4763685585000>0` and
`.037-z_max=8631350117109707/22970106001483200000>0`.
Capacity decrement and width padding fit below these and the row saving.
The actual slot maximum is repriced; the older `.0365` cap would fail.

The exact `fixedSourcePrincipal` source has relative power `33/50`,
conjugate common profile and independent heights `-Im z_i`. Whole-product
conjugation preserves natural holes. The coefficient/initial-state identity
in `finite_physical_pair_positiveAt` is reused with the proved affine moment;
its old capacity wrapper is not simply called with new parameters.
Fixed-inducing free rows have fixed norm and disappear for `d>=d0`;
finite remnants belong to the small/principal cases.

`zero_error_whole_slots` keeps every original width in `L=ell/d`, errors
included. With `q=(sum w_i g_i)/L=delta p`, `0<=p<=1/2`, it returns
a fixed positive-main subset with `z_I<=z_A` and spike
`U^(2qz_A-delta*mesh-small)`. Exhaustion gives full gain `qL>=qz_A`;
no positive-main supply lower bound or reinserted zero-gain slot is needed.

Coverage of all actual scale/selection complements is complete:

* If `z_I<=.034`, the old budget is at most `2N+4.5(.034)`, leaving
  `11/5000`. The TARGET gain `qz_A` remains valid.
* If either plain is at most `.41`, the other is at most `N` and
  `z_I<=.037`; the old budget leaves `11/10000`. This covers both
  asymmetric shortenings and all smaller reflected scales.
* Otherwise both plains and the selected width are in the new window,
  and their sum plus `Lambda z_I` is at most `B`. Use the strict atlas.
* Empty selection uses the unrestricted eligible physical zero-slot
  input. It has no hidden plain-sum constraint.

Normalize fixed-parent padding to width `1+nu` before the atlas choice.
Lower edges `.034(1+nu)`, `.41(1+nu)` cost the old complements at most
`.153nu`, `.41nu`. Fix nu below their reserves before target thresholds.
Upper edges relax and `B<=B(1+nu)`, so padded coverage is complete.

The supply checks give `ell-d_+z_max>0`,
`ell/d_+-4/21=44784748/2223053273>0`,
`2ell-1/3=139/125000>0`, and `4ell-y>0`.
For `d<.5` the original selector applies because `ell/d>=2ell>1/3`
and `1/(6kappa)<=5/21` for the unchanged physical `kappa>=.7`.
The transformed `.68` split has not replaced this physical parameter.

Euler expansion retains `h0*h_r<=const Y` and weighted mass
`sum |c(h0,h_r)| h0^(delta/2)<=U^epsilon`. Reflection scales are at most
`const(U/Y)h0`; restoration only shortens them. Combined damping is paid
once. For `u<=u0`, lost gain `q u/Lambda<=delta u/2` is covered.

For every `u>=u0`, put `b=2y/d-1` and use the old capacity
`z_old(u)=max(0,(b-2u)/(9/2))`. The needed surplus is bounded below by

    delta [ u/2 - ((b-(1-B))/Lambda-z_old(u))/4 ].

If the capacity difference is negative, payment is immediate. Otherwise
this bound follows from `q<=delta/2`. The bracket has slopes `7/18`
and `1/2`, continuous where old capacity becomes zero. Since
`b<=1890853961/11894213961<4/25`, its value at `u0` is at least
`4035883/69523200000>0`; at the exact maximum it is
`7636096506749509/118131973721913600000>0`.
Thus the entire large-shift continuum is paid, without the old `.18` bound.

At zero capacity, physical `finite_pair_zeroAt` and its reflected Fourier
adapter allow each plain up to `U^2` without a sum gate; actual scales
are below `U^(1+o(1))` from `h0<=const Y`. This is the eligible physical
input, not the `max(1,2m)` unmarked count. Independent heights remain;
rows below `d_-` keep the old argument and its shifts.

## Current checkpoint

Same approved session recovered twice, with its original history and
frozen-input boundary. Sections A--D now contain the completed mechanism
tests: an exact allocation obstruction and failed external amplifier;
an exact two-cutoff signed return with unit/composite/common-core tests;

Remaining mathematical work is the signed original-prime row covariance,
including unit self and unit/nonunit low-allocation interactions, and

### Initial saved checkpoint (retained as recovery evidence)

Read the three frozen H inputs in `[restricted provenance path] mathematical source]`
and their manifest; inspected the actual M B1.5/B1.9--11, B2.8,
B2.11--23, B2.24--30, B2.34 and B2.37--40 coefficient/profile slices.
Read the maintained H attempt entries through [research revision], JPS14--32,

obstruction. Work remains in progress. This checkpoint is not a theorem
submission or a completed handoff.

The direction being tested is an upstream prime-weight decomposition
with the native cubic cocycle retained before either positive sieve.
The first structural test is whether changing the allocation can make
actual distinct primes enter a paid common-divisor sector. It cannot
within product-preserving divisor allocations: every divisor label of
a prime is either 1 or that prime; two distinct prime ideals have
coprime labels in all four possibilities. Artificial external common
factors require changing the long length and the mark/profile contract.
An exact quantitative check of that apparent amplifier is pending.

A separate continuation is a two-cutoff von Mangoldt decomposition.
Its bilinear remainder retains a genuine cubic interaction, rather than
the factorable ordinary Hecke character appearing after the JN transform.
The unit term and the complete Type-I return must be paid; a balanced
auxiliary bilinear term cannot stand in for the prime source. The aim is
to obtain the best valid estimate and locate the first failed exponent,
not rename the old low-gcd norm as a new theorem.

## Frozen source contract

Write q_n for ideal norm. All ideals use M's actual good primary and
fixed finite-ray conventions, with squarefreeness on ideals rather than
integer norms. The infinity coefficient and short coefficient are

    a(n)=alpha(n) eta(n) chi_n(lambda)^(-2) gamma_2(n),
    xi(g)=alpha(g)^3 eta(g)^3,
    a(de)=a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4                 ((d,e)=1).

The zero extension supplies the zero at shared d,e. On a separated
linear side the actual characters and projector are

    chi_R(ng)^3 chi_P(n)^4 1_(P,Rg)=1,

with mark coefficient u_i(P)/sqrt(q_P) independent of live n,g,R,
two independent arrays and independent height variables. Put

    Omega_i=sum_P |u_i(P)|^2/q_P,
    S(N,L)=N+L+(NL)^(2/3).

The two perpendicular product masks are (n,g)=(n,bar(g))=1.
They belong to the evaluated JPS auxiliary extension. The original
short-core weight remains h((g,g')); it is never recomputed from an
auxiliary long composite. The sharp gap is

    |q_n-q_n'| > H0,  H0=floor(Z^.05).

Both equal-rational-norm orientations stay excluded. The physical
outside squared scalar is N^(-1)G^(-2), not a root in an introduced
divisor. Profiles remain C_i(n), A_i(g) at the original scales. The
domain is JPS3: N>C_orig(K+L+G^2), C_orig G<A_0,
1<=L<=sqrt(N), G>=1.

At the frozen pressure point, k=.835507578307735986...,
N=Z^(k+.003), K=Z^k, G=Z^.001,
L=Z^.170813789153867993..., S(N,L) is comparable to N.
The target raw size is G K S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.
The incumbent G(K+NG)S loses Z^.004. This is an upper-bound deficit,
not a lower bound for the true signed covariance.

JPS's exact coefficient is

    lambda(n)=Lambda_K(n)/log(q_n)
             =sum_(v|n) mu(v) log(q_n/q_v)/log(q_n).

On the squarefree nonunit source lambda is exactly the all-prime
indicator. On n=pq the nonzero weights are 1,-log(q_q)/log(q_pq),
-log(q_p)/log(q_pq); they multiply the same recombined a(pq), row,
mark, short-source and profile factors. On n=p only v=1 survives.
Thus the unit self cell is not a prime projection, and its ordered
unit/nonunit interactions cannot be dropped.

For the high extracted-gcd selector the accepted complete contraction
is R25--26, with n=s p,n'=s p' and signed coefficient

    r_U(s) log(q_p)log(q_p')/[log(q_sp)log(q_sp')].

For U>1 it has no original prime pair. The low form is the original
all-prime form minus this paid auxiliary counterterm. This finding is

## Source bindings and novelty boundary

The manifest binds frozen JPS to SHA256
`c81472d2a79cf92113354761507286e15a30b9ce53943d2e98a5ad4d34c717cf`,

and the common-divisor review to
`c022d55004ab06b755d02afb069bd12296321ee52c99435f58500b10acd51f68`.
These are source bindings; no new review or theorem acceptance follows.

The native Mobius/Gauss convolution is already AG17 and JPS14--16.
Full allocation contraction and its fixed-cell correction are already
R25/R27. The separate-moment .004 obstruction is NF. The scalar
cuspidal substitution and its moving-level failure are JN. None is
counted as new here. Any new result below will be novelty in this
maintained record only, unless a separate literature claim is checked.

## Recovery receipt and retained failure history

Same-session recovery on 2026-10-11; original deadline unchanged.
The controller reports turn [private operational identifier omitted]
interrupted/notLoaded, original launcher and worker absent, exit code
uncaptured; a subsequent remote-compaction attempt ended with exit 1
and native turn [private operational identifier omitted] failed.
Neither event completed the mathematical assignment. At 17:58 UTC
the entire saved draft was read and reconciled with its earlier text:
5,175 bytes, SHA256
`7598e41ff6baba6413da83b71249cd0efc0c1943d4d061b41d79c344177a0c20`.
This append resumes the pending calculations; it does not replay the
original source selection, draw a new sample, or start another lane.
History reads are bound to published snapshot
`db697bb1b11d871e8231b0b71349fff82ebca841` and the frozen input manifest.

## A. External common-factor amplifier: exact obstruction

**A1 (allocation no-go, elementary).** Let p and p' be distinct prime
ideals. Any product-preserving divisor allocation with labels v|p,
v'|p' has (v,v')=1. This holds for every coefficient assigned to the
four possible labels, even if a different prime identity transfers
weight from the unit label to the endpoint v=p. Consequently no such
change can move an original distinct-prime pair into a selector
q_(v,v')>=U>1. This is an obstruction to that allocation strategy,
not a lower bound for the covariance or an impossibility theorem for H.

Proof: v is 1 or p, and v' is 1 or p'. Every one of their four gcds
is the unit ideal. This test precedes all analytic estimates.

**A2 (test of an external multiplier).** Artificially put n*=t n,
q_t~T, with t squarefree and (t,n)=1. The exact native summand changes
by

    a(t) chi_t(n)^4 chi_R(t)^3 chi_P(t)^4,             (A2)

and its profile becomes C*(tn). For each t a desired pullback must
take C*(tn)=C(n), retaining the original endpoint and independent
height; it cannot use the original profile at norm tn. This
pullback depends on t and cannot be declared a single function of
n* on overlapping representations without retaining that label.
The physical root also satisfies the exact identity

    1/(sqrt(q_n)q_g)=sqrt(q_t)/(sqrt(q_t q_n)q_g).

Thus inheriting a physical theorem at the new length would require
the compensating linear sqrt(q_t), not its silent deletion.
On surviving units, inverting (A2) inserts t-dependent row and
mark multipliers and a
new n-dependent cubic twist. At a collision (t,RP)>1 the new character
is zero; there is no inverse. Thus at minimum all omitted collision
terms require an explicit restoration. The (n*,g) and (n*,bar(g))
masks also acquire conditions on t and cannot replace the original
ones silently. The original short common core remains (g,g').
The common-divisor Lambda contraction additionally supplies
log(q_n)/log(q_t q_n), so an exact pullback must account for that
factor on each side. It is bounded in a fixed polynomial range but
is not identically one.

The [research revision] estimate has neither arbitrary t-dependent mark arrays
nor permission to remove these zeros. In its successful proof the
same original-n mark polynomial is used when t is summed before the
cubic sieve. The attempted inverse in (A2) changes that hypothesis.
Accordingly no direct application of that estimate to this amplifier
has been proved.

There is also an affordable decisive size check, even granting a
more favorable theorem than is available. Ambient long length is
N*=TN, and extraction at U=T would give the quadratic factor

    K+N*G/U = K+NG.                                   (A3)

It has not become K+NG/T. Grant even a normalization by T for a
family with T^(1+o(1)) auxiliary multipliers. The resulting certificate
would be

    G(K+NG) S(TN,L)/T,
    S(TN,L)/T = N+L/T+T^(-1/3)(NL)^(2/3).             (A4)

At the actual pressure point N>=L^2 and T>=1, this is comparable to
G(K+NG)N. Its ratio to GKN remains 1+NG/K~Z^.004. This is a failure
of the proposed proof budget, not a lower bound on its true sum.
The generous normalization in this calculation is hypothetical;
the missing coefficient adapter in A2 is an additional obstruction.
Increasing U by adjoining a common factor and forgetting the increase
in N is therefore not a new payment for the original prime pairs.

The different continuation below uses cancellation in a prime-weight
identity before either sieve; it does not adjoin common factors.

## B. Two-cutoff decomposition with the original n retained

All convolutions here are ideal convolutions; no integer-norm
factorization is substituted. Let 1 be the constant ideal function,
delta the convolution unit, Lg(n)=log(q_n), and Lambda the actual
ideal von Mangoldt function. For U,V>=1 put mu_<=U, mu_>U and
Lambda_<=V, Lambda_>V for their exact norm truncations. Then

    Lambda = Lambda_<=V + mu_<=U * Lg
             - mu_<=U * 1 * Lambda_<=V
             + mu_>U * 1 * Lambda_>V.                 (B1)

This classical convolution identity is derived here rather than
imported with an unverified range. Indeed Lg=1*Lambda and
mu*1=delta; expanding the right side and grouping Lambda_<=V and
Lambda_>V gives precisely Lambda. Equality holds on every ideal,
including the unit. In the actual squarefree long window q_n>V,
the first term vanishes. Define there

    I(n) = sum_(d|n,q_d<=U) mu(d) log(q_n/q_d)
         - sum_(d k m=n,q_d<=U,q_k<=V) mu(d)Lambda(k),
    beta_U(d) = sum_(r|d,q_r>U) mu(r),
    II(n) = sum_(d e=n,q_d>U,q_e>V) beta_U(d)Lambda(e).

Then

    lambda(n) = [I(n)+II(n)]/log(q_n).                 (B2)

Here beta_U(d)=0 for q_d<=U and |beta_U(d)|<=tau(d).
For squarefree n the nonzero e in II is a prime ideal, and d is
squarefree and coprime to e. No nonsquarefree prime powers have been
added. The first Type-I term has d<=U. In the second, grouping
z=d k produces z<=UV with its exact signed coefficient
sum_(d k=z,d<=U,k<=V) mu(d)Lambda(k). Neither grouping is a new
prime projection on z or a shortening of the original long n.

Multiply (B2) by the COMPLETE actual summand at n: a(n), the two
perpendicular masks, original row and mark characters/projector,
original C_i(n), xi(g)A_i(g), and their own independent height.
Every identity then holds for each original R,P,g,n separately.
The equality exclusions and sharp far selector depend on n,n',
and the true short-core weight on g,g'; they are applied to these
same original variables after expanding the two linear identities.
Thus (B2) gives the exact four ordered covariance terms

    C_prime = C_(I,I)+C_(I,II)+C_(II,I)+C_(II,II),     (B3)

where I,II are divided by log(q_n) on their respective sides and
the second side has the original conjugation. This equation is
valid for the all-prime extension; JPS6 is still required to return
to the original degree-one projection. It does not assert that an
individual term of (B3) is an original-prime subfamily.

**B4 (unit, composite and shared-core tests).** If n=p is prime
and q_p>max(U,V), I(p)=log(q_p) and II(p)=0. In particular this
identity has not given original primes balanced factors. If
n=p q with q_p,q_q>max(U,V), then

    I(pq)=log(q_pq),
    II(pq)=-log(q_p)-log(q_q)=-log(q_pq).              (B4)

The two native factors recombine by
a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4=a(de), with the identical original R,P,g masks
and profile. They are not independent random phases. For a pair
of such semiprimes the normalized coefficient matrix of (B3) is

                         second I     second II
    first I                  1             -1
    first II                -1              1.

For a prime versus such a semiprime the surviving row is (1,-1);
for two primes only (I,I) survives. These statements include the
ordered cross terms and do not rely on positivity or equal heights.
They remain true for n=s p, n'=s p' with a shared prime ideal s,
provided s,p,p' are pairwise distinct and exceed the cutoffs. The
common native factor on the pair is a(sp) conjugate(a(sp')), not
an invented scalar at s. The
original short core is still (g,g'), and the original far norm gap
is still |q_sp-q_sp'|>H0. No coefficient argument replaces it by a
gap on the residual primes.

Consequently a proposed dispersion identity that deletes either
ordered Type-I/Type-II cross term fails already on these actual
semiprime coefficients. Replacing signed (B3) by the sum of its
four absolute coefficient contributions changes 0 into 4. This is
a counterexample to that manipulation, not to an upper bound for
the complete prime covariance. The same check is compatible with
the unit/nonunit decomposition of JPS: its unit coefficient is 1,
and the sum of nonunit coefficients is -1 on every squarefree
composite. The new cutoffs reorganize that cancellation; they do
not remove its necessity or create additional original prime pairs
in the paid high-gcd allocation.

**Exact internal check.** An in-memory deterministic Python check
used four labeled prime-ideal norms 7,13,19,31 (each a permissible
split-prime norm in the Eisenstein field), all 16 squarefree products,
and U,V independently in {1,6,7,12,13,18,19,30,31,90,200}. Logarithms
were represented by their four integer coefficient coordinates, not
floating point approximations. All 1,936 B1 identities passed,
including the small-prime Lambda_<=V term and cutoff endpoints.
This checks the algebra only, not admissibility of these finite
labels in an unspecified frozen ray/deletion set, and not an
analytic estimate. The proof above holds for every admissible set.
No random sample or Gauss-phase surrogate was generated.

## C. Where the original-order positive argument stops

Keep n through the quadratic Cauchy step as required. At fixed
short-core inversion label f and mark/row label Delta the quadratic
column is j=n b, g=f b, of norm O(NG/q_f), with its actual zeros.
For B2, summing ALL decompositions at a given n before Cauchy gives
exactly a(n)lambda(n), not a coefficient at N/U. The residual mark
polynomial is at this same n:

    M_(Delta,f,b)(n)=sum_Q u(Delta Q)/sqrt(q_Q)
                  1_(Q,f b)=1 chi_Q(n)^4,             (C1)

with the inherited fixed supports, combined Delta characters and
outside q_Delta^(-1/2). The original n stays live when applying the
cubic sieve. In particular its sieve length remains N. Independent
source heights and cyclic phases used for the exact far mask are
bounded column factors at this step, as in JPS19--24.

The resulting proved bound is still

    |C_prime[h]| << Z^epsilon G(K+NG)S(N,L)
                         sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2)P_orig. (C2)

It has the correct coefficients, roots, projectors and original
prime projection, but it does not save a positive power. Applying
the same method separately to I and II is no stronger: their
normalized coefficients are divisor-bounded, while the negative
terms in B3 have been lost. This locates the failure before any
claim about a reduced column length. No full H theorem, Hecke
prime theorem, spectral theorem or arbitrary-mask inheritance is
being used.

The next calculation tests whether the retained cubic interaction
can give a useful alternative estimate BEFORE this original-order
argument. Its different positive step is displayed explicitly and
is not inserted into C1 with a changed meaning of n.

## D. A marked bilinear consequence, with the far-cutoff cost paid

This is a derived estimate, not another proposed norm contract. It
uses only the admitted cubic sieve M B2.25 and elementary Cauchy.
Its application below fails at the pressure point. It concerns
auxiliary bilinear pieces of B2; it is not a bound on a balanced
subfamily of original primes, because that subfamily is empty.

Take a dyad q_d~D, q_e~E, DE comparable to N, in one B2 piece.
After keeping log(q_de)^(-1) in the original smooth norm profile,
let c(d),b(e) denote its actual source coefficients. They are
independent of R,P,g and divisor-bounded. The Type-II choice is
beta_U(d) and Lambda(e)/log N, with its exact prime support and
cutoffs; the bounded factor log N/log(q_de) stays in the profile.
Define the linear block, with n=de retained as the original label,
by

    V_(R,g) = sum_P u(P)/sqrt(q_P) 1_(P,Rg)=1
              sum_(d~D,e~E) c(d)b(e)a(d)a(e)
                 chi_d(e)^4 chi_R(de)^3 chi_P(de)^4
                 C(de) 1_(de,g)=1 1_(de,bar(g))=1.   (D1)

All original good/ray/deletion restrictions remain, and
xi(g)A(g)chi_R(g)^3 is applied on the outside, including its zero
at (R,g)>1. Natural character zeros impose the
required coprimalities; no inverse is used at a zero. Fixed ray
conditions on de can be separated by their finite characters.
Original norm heights split as (q_d q_e)^(it) on each side, with
the two heights still independent. C(de) has the actual product
endpoints, not a substituted window on e or on a new mark.

For an exactly separable normalized norm profile put

    T(D,E;L)=min{S(E,LD), S(D,LE)}.

Then for EACH original R,g, including their collisions,

    |V_(R,g)|^2 << Z^epsilon N T(D,E;L) Omega.        (D2)

The same bound holds with the original smooth common-profile
seminorm and a subpower logarithmic factor for its sharp product
endpoints. This uniformity is justified below; no rapidly
oscillating additive product phase is included in this assertion.
In contrast to JPS24, D2 does not assert uniformity for an arbitrary
additional bounded function of n. Its scope is the actual separated
smooth norm profiles, sharp product intervals and independent norm
heights just specified.

Proof of D2. First use the orientation t=P d. The surviving
chi_P(d)^4 forces (P,d)=1, so t is a squarefree ideal. Put

    A_(R,g)(t)=sum_(P d=t) u(P)/sqrt(q_P) c(d)a(d)
                       chi_R(d)^3 chi_P(d)^4
                       1_(P,Rg)=1
                       1_(d,g bar(g))=1,              (D3)

retaining the actual P,d supports, fixed deletions and their
separable profile factors. The remaining e coefficient is
b(e)a(e)chi_R(e)^3 1_(e,g bar(g))=1 with its original support.
Because chi_P(e)^4 chi_d(e)^4=chi_t(e)^4, the exact inner sum in
D1 is sum_e B(e) sum_t A(t)chi_t(e)^4. The character zero at
(e,t)>1 includes both the original (e,P) and (e,d) exclusions.
The original projector (P,Rg)=1 is still inside A; no residual
coprimality was inserted or removed. In particular this proof
does not require an incomplete Delta expansion.

For each t there are at most tau(t) pairs P,d. Thus

    sum_t |A_(R,g)(t)|^2
       << Z^epsilon sum_P |u(P)|^2/q_P sum_(d~D)|c(d)|^2
       << Z^epsilon D Omega.                         (D4)

The mark root in D3 is STILL q_P^(-1/2). Replacing it by
q_t^(-1/2) changes the original form; its compensating factor
q_d^(1/2) is exactly what restores the D in the mass bound D4.
The mark-side coefficient is not being asserted to satisfy the
original H contract at the new t length.

Cauchy in e and the squarefree-IDEAL cubic sieve, with its actual
exponent 4 character, give

    |V_(R,g)|^2
      <= (sum_e |B(e)|^2) sum_e |sum_t A(t)chi_t(e)^4|^2
      << Z^epsilon E S(E,LD) D Omega.

Even reciprocity gives chi_d(e)^4=chi_e(d)^4 in the fixed source
conventions. Reversing d,e therefore proves the other orientation
S(D,LE). All unit, angular and native Gauss factors were kept until
the displayed norm. The proof actually allows any source-only
divisor-bounded c,b, so the actual Lambda coefficients are covered.
No ordinary Hecke or scalar cuspidal replacement has occurred.

Here the original label remains n=de everywhere in D1. This is an
upstream bilinear calculation with R fixed; it does not perform a
quadratic Cauchy step on a shortened n and does not apply the
original cubic mark theorem C1 at length E. Its new cubic input is
proved directly with the transformed coefficient and mass D4.
That distinction is necessary to respect the original H contract.

**Product endpoints.** For a bound A on the integer norm q_de,
first evaluate its exact strict/non-strict convention on integers.
There is a smooth cutoff in x=log(q_de/N), agreeing with the
resulting indicator on EVERY attainable integer norm, whose
transition is centered between the two adjacent integers and has
width comparable to 1/N. On the fixed annular x support its Fourier
transform is bounded by

    O(min(1, |t|^(-1), N |t|^(-2))).

This follows respectively from its L1 bound, its derivative's L1
bound O(1), and its second derivative's L1 bound O(N), by integration
by parts. Its Fourier L1 norm is O(log(2N)). Each Fourier component
is q_d^(it)q_e^(it) times a unit scalar; D4 and the cubic sieve are
uniform in t. Lower and upper cuts, and the original smooth
profile, are treated together or by a fixed number of products.
Only logarithmic factors are lost. The existing common-profile
integral is then paid with its original seminorms and height mass.
This is not an AG12 contour shift with a hidden high-derivative
cost; the sieve bound here is uniform for every unit norm height.

**The additive-phase objection.** The cyclic phase used by JPS to
impose a far mask is exp(2 pi i ell q_d q_e/M). It does NOT in
general split into a d factor and an e factor. Its cross ratio on
(d_1,d_2) and (e_1,e_2) is

    exp(2 pi i ell (q_d1-q_d2)(q_e1-q_e2)/M).          (D5)

For ideal norms 7,13 and 19,31, ell=1, M=1031, the cross ratio is
exp(2 pi i 72/1031), not 1. All four products are squarefree and
M exceeds twice their norm range. Thus multiplying D1 by that
phase cannot be waved through D3 as independent coefficients.
This is an explicit algebraic failure of that proposed adapter.
These finite labels test the claimed factorization identity; they
are not claimed to lie in every frozen ray or deletion set.

The exact far mask can nevertheless be paid by subtracting its
ENTIRE near band after the bilinear estimate, at a stated cost.
Let C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h] denote the literal ordered covariance of
two D1 blocks with DE,D'E' comparable to N and the two original
mark arrays. Then

    |C_(D,E;D',E')^far[h]|
      << Z^epsilon K G^2 N
          [sqrt(T(D,E;L) T(D',E';L))+(H0+1)L]
                      sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig.   (D6)

For the complete covariance before the gap, invert the original
short core h((g,g'))=sum_(f|g,g') r_h(f), |r_h(f)|<=tau(f).
At f there are O(G/q_f) possible original g values. Triangle in
that linear vector, D2, and Cauchy between the two independent
arrays give K (G/q_f)^2 N sqrt(T T') sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2).
The original row norm contains O(K) ideals; its exact sharp row
window and bounded normalized weight have not been extended by a
new row theorem. Sum f using sum_f tau(f)/q_f^2<infinity (or the
permitted subpower loss). The original xi(g), finite signs, all
perpendicular masks, and fixed squarefree/rational-primitive
restrictions remain in every child until this positive estimate.

For the near band regroup each block at ORIGINAL n=de. Its source
coefficient is divisor-bounded and its native factor is a(n).
The number of ideals of integer norm m is at most tau(m), by the
two-prime factorization law in this quadratic field. Therefore
there are O(Z^epsilon N(H0+1)) pairs with |q_n-q_n'|<=H0.
Cauchy on the exact original mark sum gives pointwise squared
mass at most O(L Omega_i), with its root q_P^(-1/2). Count O(K)
rows and O(G^2) short pairs and use |h|<=1. This bounds the near
band by the second term of D6. It includes BOTH equal-norm
orientations, not just n=n'. Subtracting this entire band gives
the original strict far condition. There is no signed-form
monotonicity step and no unsupported near-prime theorem applied
to the auxiliary composites.

D6 is therefore an exact, restricted covariance bound with its
common core, marks, endpoints and gap paid. The complete scalar
return of this bound multiplies by N^(-1)G^(-2), exactly as before;
the introduced bilinear indices do not create an extra physical
normalization. C2 remains a second bound on the same piece after
regrouping its divisor-bounded coefficient at n, so the smaller
of these two available bounds may be used for that piece.

**Pressure calculation and failure.** For every factor split DE=N,
both alternatives in T contain the term (NL)^(2/3). The best
balanced choice for the first orientation has E=LD, namely
D=sqrt(N/L), E=sqrt(NL), giving T of order (NL)^(2/3) for NL>=1.
The best certificate supplied by D6 consequently has, relative to
the desired raw GKN scale, the sizes

    G(NL)^(2/3),             G(H0+1)L.                (D7)

At the frozen pressure point their exponents are respectively

    .673880911641069319333...,  .221813789153867993...

The mixed cubic term is already much worse than the incumbent's
.004 deficit; compared to that incumbent its surplus exponent is
.669880911641069319333.... This is a lower bound on this PARTICULAR
positive certificate, not on the true covariance. Even free
near-band removal would not repair it. Restrictions imposed by
U,V can only make the optimized D7 certificate worse, not better.

For perspective the bound is a real arithmetic improvement over
the old G^2 N^2 term in the different range
K L^(2/3)<N^(1/3) with the near term also smaller. It does not pay
GKN there and it does not apply that different range to the frozen
pressure point. The mark absorption puts the mark-count cost
inside S(E,LD). In the mixed-term range it saves L^(1/3) against
estimating each mark separately; it does not remove every L cost.
That saving is insufficient here. The unit Type-I block D=1,
E~N has T~N in the actual L range and also remains unpaid.

This ends the tested bilinear route: two cutoff choices cannot
repair a mixed cubic term independent of those choices. An
improvement must retain joint row cancellation before the K row
count or exploit the signed I/II covariance before separate
positive estimates. Neither has been proved in this draft.

Even a hypothetical removal of the cubic sieve's mixed term would
leave min{E+LD,D+LE}>=2sqrt(NL), up to fixed dyadic constants.
After the same row count and short-source triangle the target ratio
would still be at least of certificate size G sqrt(NL), exponent
.5056606837308019895 at the pressure point. Thus replacing just
that cubic sieve constant by its conjectured two linear terms
cannot fix this particular argument. This is again a statement
about the argument's cost, not a lower bound for its true sum.

## E. Full return, explicit unpaid estimate, and c threshold

Let B_H=G K S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2)P_orig denote the raw
target for this packet. The new formulas always preserve its
outside N^(-1)G^(-2). In particular D6 returns the physical bound

    Z^epsilon K [sqrt(T T')+(H0+1)L]
                      sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2)P_orig,

against the target K S(N,L)/(N G), comparable to K/G in the
pressure box. No normalization concealed in a(d), a(e), or the
new t label improves this comparison.

To return B2 from all-prime ideals to the original degree-one
source, use the EXACT JPS11 all-minus-inert identity, retaining
the two ordered mixed terms and the inert square. Its paid raw
cost, from JPS6, is

    G^2(K+N)[sqrt(N)L+sqrt(S(N,L)sqrt(N)L)]
                         sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2)P_orig. (E1)

At the pressure point the cross and square terms divided by B_H
have exponents -.12022 and -.24444 respectively. Return to the
original degree-one row expression BEFORE the RH representation;
no inert version of a fibre theorem has been assumed. The original
transport error and Jacobi mean are then restored once, from
JPS32, at raw costs

    G^2(K+N)S(N,L)sqrt(L/K),       G^2 K L/N,           (E2)

times the same mark/profile mass. Their B_H-relative exponents
are -.3283468945769339965... and -1.505201367461603979....
The complete-unit Jacobi subtraction retains its original signs;
it has not become a density depending only on a short common core.

The original degree-one near graph |q_n-q_n'|<=Z^.05 with its
two equal-rational-norm orientations excluded has the already
accepted JS/JSR payment. Its allowed graph exponent is
.0560353466788..., leaving the quoted .006035... margin. That
prime theorem is not what paid D6's auxiliary near band: D6 paid
all of it by its separate explicit (H0+1)L cost. No theorem for
auxiliary mixed or nonprime near pairs is borrowed from JS/JSR.
The equal-norm exclusions in the hard packet are exact; any
global H contributions removed before defining that packet keep
their original return obligations.

At U0=NG/K the accepted high extracted-gcd estimate is already
O(Z^epsilon B_H). Its full-allocation contraction contains only
auxiliary common-core composites for U0>1. The low allocation is
the original prime covariance minus that paid counterterm, so
bounding that low allocation at B_H is still the unresolved prime
problem. None of A--D has relabeled a paid composite as a prime.

More explicitly, the first unpaid estimate in the present return is

    |C_(P_all,P_all)^far[h]|
       <<_epsilon Z^epsilon B_H                    (E3)

for all original eligible dyads, independent mark arrays and
heights, profiles and bounded original true-core weights in JPS3.
Equivalently one must bound the SIGNED sum B3, with the original
prime projection and all its unit and nonunit interactions.
C2 supplies only G(K+NG)S. A bound replacing its second term by
NG Z^(-sigma) would have relative cost 1+Z^(.004-sigma) at the
pressure point. Sigma=.004 pays this particular packet; any
fixed 0<sigma<.004 is a power improvement in this local certificate
but does not itself prove a larger c. No such sigma is obtained here.



For the identities here, finite cutoffs are removed exactly by
the frozen JPS Section 8/M B2.22--23,37--40 procedure. Separate the
single original common profile before a positive row enlargement.
Retain its linear envelope min(Y^(1/4),(1+Y)^(-A)) once on each
side and integrate both independent heights against their original
rapid densities. The additional divisor coefficients are bounded
by arbitrary small norm powers, and the endpoint separation in D
adds logarithms only. These are fixed polynomial majorants; choose
the original Schwartz order after that polynomial. Bound a tail
against the full other side before choosing the order, so both
mixed errors and the squared tail are paid. This supplies no
arithmetic improvement in the retained finite part and no new
uniformity outside the original theorem domain.

**Concrete sufficient threshold for a first reported c gain.**
The frozen complete return is `[restricted mathematical source]`
Sections 1--3 at the bound history revision. It would give
c=.12551>c0 if the ACTUAL all-branch H estimate

    H <<_epsilon (KNBL)^epsilon K B S(N,L)             (E4)

were proved uniformly for K<NB<=K Z^.006322, u_h=z_a
(equivalently v>=2z_a), with all three cusp sources, fixed phases,
original masks, roots, common profiles and independent-height
costs required there. Existing estimates handle NB<=K. The
certificate uses tau_*=.006321367461603978..., so the positive
slack exceeds .0000006325; reflection tolerance and preliminary
epsilon losses must be fixed below fractions of that slack.
It includes the compensator subsets and their unchanged roots;
it is not a certificate for E3 alone.

For another candidate c, the same geometry's scalar gate is
tau_max>tau_*(c), with all its other inequalities checked at that
c, where b=1-c, kappa=2b-1, delta_* is the smaller root of

    (324 kappa^2-3)delta^2
      +(-756 kappa^2+54 kappa+5)delta
      +300 kappa^2-40 kappa=0,

    ell_b=4(c-1/12),
    f(ell,kappa)=(1+ell)/2+delta_*/2
                  +delta_*ell(1+1/(3kappa))/2,
    A_ell=[1+delta_*(1+1/(3kappa))]/2,
    A_tau=1/2+delta_*/(12kappa),
    tau_*(c)=[f(ell_b,kappa)-b]/[A_tau-A_ell/3].       (E5)

The invoked checked point is the frozen .12551 certificate; no
new optimization or baseline audit was run. E4 is a sufficient
threshold with a full conditional return, not a necessary or
optimal threshold. It is still unproved. Thus neither a favorable
review of D6 nor a local saving in E3 alone would establish any
increase over the accepted c0.

## F. Research disposition and next mathematical action

The productive delta is a directly proved marked bilinear bound
D2/D6, including its true root mass and a valid separate treatment
of the exact far mask. The two-cutoff identity B1 is classical;
native twisted multiplicativity and the unmarked balanced bound
are already AG17. No literature priority is claimed. Within the
inspected maintained record the D3--D6 calculation and its exact
failure budget are additional evidence, not a new paid H sector.
The amplifier and additive-phase failures are retained explicitly.

The strongest objections checked were: original primes cannot
acquire a common divisor by changing divisor labels (A1); an
external factor changes length, twists, zeros and profiles (A2--4);
semiprime and shared-core cancellation depends on both ordered
cross terms (B4); the original quadratic and cubic proof retains
n, not n/d (C1); absorbing a mark changes its mass but does not
change the original root (D3--4); the exact cyclic phase is not
factorable (D5); and a near-prime graph theorem does not apply to
the auxiliary composites (D6). The failed positive estimates are
upper-bound failures, not covariance lower bounds.

The next action should target a JOINT row/label estimate before
either positive sieve, with B4 as its first coefficient test.
A concrete cut choice is U=V=Z^.002: the second Type-I label has
size at most UV=Z^.004, and at its upper endpoint the fixed-label
residual quadratic length NG/(UV) is K. The known fixed-label
triangle still loses the label count, and primes themselves
remain in the unit Type-I term. Therefore the useful next step
is a signed estimate joining that unit term, the nonunit Type-I
labels, and their Type-II cross terms, not another estimate of
the large labels alone.

At the kernel level the original row factor to retain is

    Q_(P,P')(j,j')=sum_(R original) W(R)
                      1_(R,PP')=1 chi_R(jj')^3,
    j=n g,  j'=n' g'.                                (F1)

Here W is the original paired row profile; the two independent
heights and mark arrays remain outside with their actual source
coefficients. The remaining masks (P,g) and (P',g'), both long
source masks and the natural mark zeros remain outside exactly.
For actual distinct long primes and true short gcd f, write
g=f b,g'=f b'. The kernel character is exactly

    1_(R,f)=1 chi_R(n n' b b')^3,                     (F2)

including the zero at a shared f. Replacing chi_R(f^2)^3 by 1
on ALL R would fail at precisely that natural zero. A successful
new dispersion identity must estimate the weighted F1 with the
signed B2 factors before separating its R dependence. Merely
repeating the known JN Gauss elimination or applying an ordinary
Hecke-prime theorem would not supply the required native bound.
The total original n in F1/F2 and every product endpoint remain
unchanged while such an estimate is attempted.

No new external theorem was imported in this draft. D2 uses the
accepted frozen M B2.25 in its explicit squarefree-ideal domain
(no squarefree integer-norm or rational-prime exclusion); B1 and
the additional cutoff/counting arguments were proved directly.
The previously inspected primary-source screens in AG/JN remain
screens only: no GRH prime theorem, fixed scalar cusp-form theorem,
or moving-conductor uniformity is assumed.

Internal verification consists of the displayed algebra, the
1,936 exact coefficient checks, explicit phase cross-ratio D5,
and decimal evaluation of the fixed pressure exponents. Those
checks do not validate a full H theorem. There is no new c gain.
Only this assigned artifact has been written. Final whole-file
readback, exact byte count and SHA-256 are reported in the handoff;
that evidence is for controller review, not theorem acceptance.

Final internal scope check: D1 includes the outside chi_R(g)^3
with its natural zero, D4 uses the original q_P root, and D6 pays
the auxiliary near band directly. Two attempted qualification
patches failed their context checks before changing any bytes;
the corrected patch then saved these qualifications. One read-only
lookup used a nonexistent frozen NF filename; no result from that
lookup was used, and JPS32 supplied the actual return formulas.
These local failures did not trigger another lane or source change.

# G170-G172: adaptive completion and the limits of cutoff mixing

The new paid region follows the nonlinear phase surface instead of a
single worst-case product cutoff. Its complete complement is still a
signed arithmetic problem. Root accepts the restricted results below;
the written constant remains

    c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636,
    gamma11=2187135091/2500000000=.8748540364.

Sources are the [author proof](adaptive-source/report.md), [partial
independent review](adaptive-source-review/report.md), and
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json). The reviewer reconstructed
the consequential arguments and added the bounded-variation result in
G171. Its helper/receipt, newest full-index and outside ancestry checks
were unfinished. Root independently reconstructed the addition, inspected
the helper and every receipt case, reconciled all six source pins, checked
the current changed index and exact inherited tail/Mellin paragraphs, and
opened the cited primary ancestry. This does not rewrite the review as a
completed full audit. Original missed deadlines and both STOPs remain.

## G170. A moving small-product region with its complete return

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, a prime p not dividing q, and

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n), q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    c_p=q_p*a, b_p=q_p*h=chi(n)(1-p 1_(p|n)).

The periodic b_p has zero mean and period Q=pq; retain all natural and
squareful coefficients. Let 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma and

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), x in[X,2X],
    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

Choose tau=tau_X in[0,1] before the real shell variable x. For each n,
freeze U(n)=B(n)^tau,V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau), using B^0=1 even when B<1.
The exact coefficientwise completion is

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),
    Q_U(n)=sum_(de=n,d<=U(n)) a(d)q_p(e),
    S_tau(n)=sum_(de*l=n,d<=U(n),e<=V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_(de*l=n,d>U(n),e>V(n)) a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

This is not one convolution identity with globally fixed cuts. Ordered
pairs, strict complements and endpoint cuts are literal. The two short
sources cost at most (p+1)(floor(L^tau)+floor(L^(1-tau)))=O_p(L).

For 0<tau<1 put W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). A contributing row has
de<=W<=L, and its entire allowed cofactor set is the single prefix

    l <= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).

At tau=0 use d=1,W=e; at tau=1 use e=1,W=d. Thus
de(de*l)^(k-1)<=eta X^k. Expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes.
For F_j(t)=jt/Q-(de*t/x)^k/(2pi), the decreasing phase derivative and
every applicable integer increment stay in[1/(2Q),1-1/(2Q)]. Discrete
summation by parts with 1/(exp(2pi*i*v)-1) gives O(Q) per undamped prefix.
Abel summation pays the actual decreasing damping. There are at most L
rows, so uniformly in tau and every real x,

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_(p,q,k) X^gamma.

The omitted alias region belongs to R; it has not been called
nonstationary. With |R_tau(n)|<=p d_3(n), the prefix n<=L is affordable.
The complete divisor-bounded tail from [G152](../[research revision]/compensated-source-integration.md)
is

    ||sum_(n>M) v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2 [X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)],
    |v_n|<=A_delta n^delta, 2delta<k-2.

It majorizes the whole positive square, retaining the diagonal, both
orientations and actual damping. Since k+(2-k)r=2gamma, choose delta
after epsilon. On dx/x over[X,2X], the literal finite core

    T_tau(x)=sum_(L<n<=M) R_tau(n)f_x(n)

satisfies ||C_p-T_tau||_j<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2,
where C_p=sum c_p(n)f_x(n). These are separate L1 and L2 comparisons;
L2 implies L1, and no converse or signed-subset monotonicity is asserted.

For tau=1 collapse before masking. With h_p=q_p-b_p,
h_p(1)=0,h_p(p)=-chi(p), the core becomes

    sum_(L<n=dj<=M,d>B(n),j>=2) mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j)f_x(n),
    j<n/B(n)=max(n/X^gamma,n^k/(eta X^k)).

Near n~X the cofactor cap is O(X^(1-gamma)); the far cap is retained.
The transition is n*=eta^(1/(k-1))X^((k-gamma)/(k-1)). For gamma=.8748,
k=6 the near exponent is .1252, while the far exponent remains .3756;
transition exponent1.02504. This pays a genuinely larger small-source
region than the constant cutoff's worst-case exponent. It does not
estimate the remaining cancellation.

OPEN-AD asks for the complete every-epsilon, every-large-shell L1 core
bound at one common gamma<gamma11, for every fixed character and a
fixed covering pair of unramified primes. The inherited all-height
Mellin return is exact: at b=3/2,k=6 its leading term is
Gamma(s/6)e^(-i*pi*s/12)P_p(s)/(6L(s,chi)), P_p=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
with holomorphic remainder on Re(s)>1/2. Two fixed primes cover numerator
zeros; for nonprincipal chi choose one with chi(p)!=1, and preserve the
principal pole at1. General fixed b,k use every shifted reciprocal in
a finite expansion and strip descent, never delete those terms. No
growing-conductor, native H or old positive-slot estimate is inferred.
Targets .1252,1/6,1/4 remain conditional; even the elementary full-source
bound remains X^(1+epsilon).

## G171. Arbitrarily many cuts at bounded total variation

For each X choose any finite J_X, parameters tau_j,X and complex weights
lambda_j,X, all fixed before x, with sum lambda_j=1 and
sum|lambda_j|<=Lambda for a fixed Lambda. The complete bank
T_bank=sum lambda_j T_tau_j obeys the same paid comparison with an extra
factor Lambda, uniformly in J_X. For a PRINCIPAL character its selected
semiprime projection nevertheless has L1 and L2 norm >> X/log X.

Here is the reviewer extension independently checked by root. Write
c=1-gamma,t_j=gamma*tau_j and

    F(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j[
       1_(t_j<alpha<t_j+c)+1_(gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j)].

F is symmetric, |F|<=2Lambda and integral_0^1 F=2c. Set
delta=c/(4Lambda),m=c/(8Lambda). The set ReF>=c/2 in[delta,1/2]
has measure at least m. Define the endpoint measure nu with mass
|lambda_j| at each of t_j,t_j+c,gamma-t_j,1-t_j; its total is<=4Lambda.
Variation of F on an interval is bounded by the nu-mass there.
For n=rs, alpha=log r/log X and kappa=log(n/X)/log X, the actual merged
coefficient G shifts both upper endpoints by kappa; its error from F
is bounded by nu([alpha-|kappa|,alpha+|kappa|]).

Choose a fixed grid of width h=c^2/(4096Lambda^2). Discard the terminal
strip[1/2-m/4,1/2] and the at most two boundary cells. A cell is bad
when its h-enlargement has nu-mass>c/8. A point lies in at most four
such closed enlargements, so bad length is<=128Lambda*h/c=m/4.
The total discarded length is<=m/2+2h<m. Some full good cell I contains
a point with ReF>=c/2. Throughout I, variation and displacement each
cost<=c/8 whenever |kappa|<=h. Thus ReG>=c/4, |G|<=2Lambda,
without a bound on the number of breakpoints.

Choose a fixed a in(0,1/4] with(2a)^k<=c/(64Lambda), and select primes
X^(inf I)<r<=X^(sup I), aX/r<s<=2aX/r. For large X these give distinct
unramified semiprimes in the literal core, B(n)=L and |kappa|<h.
Their phase on every real shell point is small, so the real part of
G f_x(n) is bounded below by a fixed positive constant. Ordinary PNT
on polynomially large fixed-ratio intervals and partial summation of
sum1/r give >> X/log X selected products, uniformly in the grid cell.
This proves the projected norm bound.

No coefficient was replaced by its absolute value. The projection may
depend on X and the bank. This rules out paying all such selected pieces
separately at the desired power merely by adding more normalized cuts
at bounded variation. It does NOT lower-bound T_bank or C_p, exclude
cancellation against their complements, or treat unbounded Lambda as
free. The author proved the fixed-J version; the uniform finite-J_X
extension belongs to the reviewer, with independent root reconstruction.

## G172. Deflation changes the obstructing cell and preserves its cost

For fixed K>=1 use

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h, c_K=v_K*a, h_K=v_K-b_K.

This equals a difference of two compensators, with v_K(1)=0 and
b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_(p^K|j)-p^(K+1)1_(p^(K+1)|j)]. It has zero
mean, period Q_K=p^(K+1)q. The adaptive proof works for each FIXED K
with eta_K=1/(100kQ_K), paying all K-dependent constants. Since
h_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_(p^K)*h_p, its prime values vanish. At tau=1
the entire semiprime projection vanishes where B(n)>=1; otherwise the
long label d=1 must be retained. The whole-core statement follows when
u=2gamma-r>0 for large X, including the three displayed targets.

The Mellin numerator gains the nonvanishing factor
chi(p)^K p^(K(1-s)); the fixed two-prime return survives. This is a
fixed multiplicative dilation, not a new cancellation theorem. For
principal chi, the actual cell n=p^(K+1)d, d prime in
(X/(4p^(K+1)),X/(2p^(K+1))], has entire merged coefficient+p^K:
the d term contributes, the pd term has h_K(p^K)=0, and higher p powers
in the Mobius variable vanish. Its projected norm remains comparable
to X/(p log X).

If p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta) for fixed0<delta<1-gamma, the same
selected-cell lower bound remains uniform. That diagnostic does not
import the full comparison uniformly in K. Existing short and row
upper budgets grow with K and must be reproved for a growing-depth
architecture. Their growth is not an impossibility theorem for a
better estimate of the complete signed source.

## Evidence, ancestry and next estimate

Nine frozen artifacts retain original proofs, partial review, helpers,
receipts and missed deadlines. The author's single exact run checked
16 adaptive cases through600 with four actual characters,1024 row-prefix
memberships, nine signed profiles, eight deflations and three rational
targets. Root read it without rerunning; these checks prove no asymptotic.
The inherited G140-G142 and G152-G154 tail/continuation/compensator
components retain credit. [Helfgott and Thompson](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40993-022-00408-8)
provide primary ancestry for completion and product-dependent divisor
geometry, not a nonlinear cancellation estimate or imported running-time
exponent. Ordinary PNT is the only prime-counting input here.

The next target is the complete signed transition core, with correlations
between its cells, or a different architecture with a fully paid return.
Increasing cutoff-bank size alone at bounded variation is insufficient
for the separate-piece strategy. No increased c, formalization, native-H
adapter or external record admission follows. The original29-family/
109-child portfolio and nearer,1/6,1/4 targets remain intact.

## 3. Finite arithmetic seeds cannot repair the fixed grid

THEOREM. For every finite E subset of positive integers,

  dist_(H_sigma)(1, W_q + span{f_n:n in E}) > 0.              (B6)

Proof. First suppose a fixed S=sum_(n in E)c_n f_n satisfies 1-S in W_q. Evaluating at every nonzero s_k=s_(q,k) implies

  zeta(s_k) P(s_k)=1,
  P(s)=sum_(n in E)c_n(n^(-1)-n^(-s)).                       (B7)

Put alpha_n=log n/log q. Simultaneous Dirichlet approximation supplies, for every integer Q>=2, an integer 1<=k<=Q^r with max_n ||k alpha_n||<=1/Q, where r=|E| (terms n=1 may be removed; if no terms remain B4 applies). To prove this directly, put Q^r+1 orbit points j*(alpha_n)_n mod1 into Q^r equal coordinate boxes and subtract two in the same box. If such k remain bounded along Q->infinity, one nonzero k has all phases exactly integral, so P(s_k)=0 and B7 fails. Otherwise choose k->infinity. Since k<=Q^r, the phase bound gives

  |P(s_k)| <= (2pi/Q) sum_(n in E)|c_n|/n.

The elementary bound |zeta(1+it)|=O(log(2+|t|)) then makes zeta(s_k)P(s_k)->0, since log(k)/Q<=r log(Q)/Q->0. This contradicts B7.

For completeness the zeta bound follows without an unproved zero-free input: for integer N>=1 and Re(s)>0, s!=1,

 zeta(s)=sum_(n<=N)n^(-s)+N^(1-s)/(s-1)
              -s integral_N^infinity {u}u^(-s-1)du.

At s=1+it choose N=max(1,ceil |t|); the finite sum is O(log(2+|t|)) and both remaining terms are O(1) for |t|>=1.

Finally W_q is closed and adding a finite-dimensional space gives a closed subspace. If the distance in B6 were zero, a fixed S of the preceding form would exist. This proves strict positivity uniformly over all varying seed coefficients, even if those coefficients diverge before projection. No numerical conditioning assumption is used. The empty seed case is B4.

For a specified fixed S there is the explicit evaluable lower bound

 dist(1-S,W_q)^2 >= sup_(k!=0)
  2(1-sigma)|1-zeta(s_k)P(s_k)|^2/|s_k|^2.                  (B8)

B6 does not supply a useful numerical lower bound uniform over every finite E. Its strict positivity is enough to disprove convergence for any fixed finite patch.
title: 3. Finite arithmetic seeds cannot repair the fixed grid

## 3. Linked development W41-01 / wildcard W41-21

### B1. Finite-prime f3 parity is much smaller than the full unknown parity

For a finite set P containing2 and not3, put

    Q=product_(p in P)p,
    a_P(n)=product_(p in P)(1-2*1_(p|n)),
    r_P(n)=f(n)a_P(n), so f=a_P*r_P pointwise.               (B1)

The last product is pointwise, NOT Dirichlet convolution. Card01's initial squarefree-cube toy is not identified with this arithmetic law: B is the source-adapted continuation after recovering the all-integer f3 coefficients. The bounded sequence a_P is Q-periodic. Its exact mean is product_(p in P)(1-2/p)=0. Let h_tau(t)=g_tau(log t) for t>0, extended by0 for t<=0. For any Q-periodic |a|<=1 of mean zero, finite Fourier expansion and Poisson summation give, for every integer m>=2,

    |sum_(n>=1)a(n)g_tau(log(n/x))|
      <=2 zeta(m)(Q/(2pi))^m x^(1-m)||h_tau^(m)||_1.         (B2)

There is one bounded Fourier coefficient at each nonzero frequency k/Q; no extra Q factor is inserted. Flatness at0 pays all integration-by-parts boundaries. The current Gaussian derivative contract G7 supplies

    ||h_tau^(m)||_1<=K_tau 4^m m! exp(tau(m-1)^2/2).

Fix0<delta<1. Uniformly over ANY moving P=P_X as above with Q<=X^(1-delta), choose m=2+floor(delta log X/tau) in B2. On X<=x<=2X,

    F_P(x):=sum_n a_P(n)g_tau(log(n/x))
       =O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) for every fixed A>0.           (B3)

Indeed the logarithm of the bound is at most -delta^2(log X)^2/(2tau)+O_(delta,tau)(log X loglog X). The estimate is uniform in the actual prime list and includes all positive prime powers. A finite set of primes can therefore exhibit arbitrary-power partial-parity cancellation even though the full f3 target remains open.

This is not the W38 squarefree occupation law. There the occupation probability is1/(p+1) and partial parity has a logarithmic lower bias. Here the positive measure is on ALL integers; occupation probability is1/p and the literal p=2 factor has zero bias. Confusing these source laws reverses the conclusion. The periodic analytic ingredient is inherited W34/G7 machinery; this distinct f3 consequence and the return below are the claimed limited delta.

### B2. Every revealed syndrome has a uniformly paid product law

Let Z(x)=sum_n g_tau(log(n/x)) and define the actual probability law

    mu_x(n)=g_tau(log(n/x))/Z(x), n>=1.

Period1 Poisson gives Z(x)=exp(tau/2)x+O_(A,tau)(x^-A). For any occupancy pattern s in {0,1}^P, its indicator is Q-periodic. Its exact uniform residue density is

    pi_P(s)=product_(p:s_p=1)1/p * product_(p:s_p=0)(1-1/p).

Subtract that density and apply B2. Since2^|P|<=Q, summing the errors over all patterns still preserves arbitrary-power decay under Q<=X^(1-delta). Thus the full pattern law under mu_x is within O_(A,delta,tau)(X^-A) in L1 of these independent Bernoulli occupations, uniformly on the whole shell. This is a true derived finite-marginal theorem, not an assumed independence of the unexposed arithmetic.

### B3. Exact remaining conditional-bias target and return

Use covariance with respect to mu_x and set

    C_P(x)=Cov_mu_x(a_P,r_P)
           =E_mu_x[a_P r_P]-E_mu_x[a_P]E_mu_x[r_P].

Then literally

    F(x)=Z(x) C_P(x)+F_P(x)E_mu_x[r_P].                    (B4)

Because |E r_P|<=1, B3 pays the second term to every power. Since Z(x) is comparable to X on the shell, for any fixed gamma>.5 the current complete moment target is equivalent to

    integral_X^(2X)|C_(P_X)(x)|^2 dx/x
                      <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon).     (B5)

This equivalence is uniform for every chosen family P_X satisfying B3, including a fixed P={2}. It is not a new estimate. At gamma=.874864 it asks an L2 covariance amplitude X^(-.125136+epsilon); the1/6 and1/4 goals ask X^(-1/6+epsilon) and X^(-1/4+epsilon). Every complement has been kept in r_P. The fixed original field F, rather than the moving F_P, enters the existing zero-exclusion transform. Thus no moving-detector analyticity is silently asserted. This normalized covariance exponent is a different proof quantity from G14's .24973/.24898 moment exponents and H's .004 deficit; their numerical savings cannot be added.

In syndrome form, if m_P(s;x)=E_mu_x[r_P|occupancy=s], then

    C_P(x)=sum_s P_mu_x(s)(a_P(s)-E_mu_x[a_P])m_P(s;x).      (B6)

All conditional means, including rare patterns, remain. B2's unconditional product law does not bound B6: the tail phase may correlate with parity after conditioning. Even perfect independence among exposed bits is not independence from r_P. This pinpoints a precise source-exact missing estimate rather than treating high entropy, a small partial parity, or a large number of exposed primes as a gain. No new c follows from B1–6.

For each fixed ordinary chi, replace r_P(n) by chi(n)r_P(n), including its zeros, and define the complex bilinear covariance by the explicit expression E[a_P r]-E[a_P]E[r]. Since |r|<=1, B3–6 and their full norm equivalence still hold verbatim for F_chi, while A13 supplies its own zero return. No independence from the character or change to the positive law is assumed. This extension does not treat ideal norms as integers or claim an Eisenstein transfer.

## 8. Additional survivor: the repeated-prime part is short

**R20. Exact support lemma.** For any tuple contributing to c(n), put `g=gcd(d1,d2)`, `d1=gx,d2=gy`, and `p=prod_i p_i`. The ideals g,x,y are pairwise coprime and squarefree; p is squarefree by disjoint original pools. Let

    A=gcd(g,p), b=gcd(xy,p), g=A g0,
    xy=b z, p=A b p0.

These factorizations use actual ideal gcds and retain the original tuple labels. The ideals

    A, B=g0 b, C=z p0

are pairwise coprime and squarefree, and

    n=A^3 B^2 C,
    n/rad n=A^2B=g A b,     A b divides p.                      (R20)

Hence `N(n/rad n)<=Ng Np<G Np`. Because `Np<=C P0` on the fixed slot annuli, every contributing tuple satisfies

    W(n):=N(n/rad n)<C G P0,
    N A<=min(Ng,Np).                                           (R21)

The ideals A,B,C are also the intrinsic valuation-3, valuation-2, and valuation-1 radicals of n; the normal form is unique once n is given. Different admissible tuple factorizations change their allocation to the original factors, not these radicals. Thus c(n) is identically zero outside R21. Cancellation between coefficients is not needed. With zero slots, p=1, A=1, and `n/rad n=g` exactly.

For a pair of supported columns, the local inequality

    (|v_p(n)-v_p(n')|-1)_+
       <=(v_p(n)-1)_+ +(v_p(n')-1)_+

shows that the ideal `q2 q3^2` divides `(n/rad n)(n'/rad n')`. A valuation difference of three also requires a cubic prime in one column, so q3 divides `A(n)A(n')`. Therefore

    Q2 Q3^2 <=W(n)W(n')<C G^2 P0^2,
    Q3<=C P0^2,

proving R2. One may also retain the bound `Q3<G^2`; the slot bound is stronger on the current v range. At its largest v, `Q2Q3^2<<U^(1/2)` and `Q3<<U^(1/10)`. These fixed-constant inequalities convert to exponent support with arbitrarily small pads, without claiming false exact powers at finite U.

This is not an estimate on the gcd of two merged columns. It follows separately from every small-within-column-gcd tuple in each coefficient. It survives fixed profile derivatives, independent heights and common-profile integration because those operations change weights, not the arithmetic support. It does not replace c by an arbitrary coefficient having this support.

The lemma narrows the genuine target: its hard conductor comes primarily from the valuation-difference-one radical, while its squared/cubic components have the displayed short budgets. It does not remove the generic coprime squarefree sector, where `W(n)=W(n')=1`, `Q2=Q3=1`. No extra norm saving, literature novelty, or arithmetic impossibility follows merely from this structural restriction.

## 2. Test01: signed scale drift, and its paid diagonal

Fix tau>0, a fixed ordinary character chi modulo q, and

    U(y)=sum_n mu(n)chi(n) g_tau(log n-y),
    g_tau(v)=(2 pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2 tau)).                 (1)

Here y=log x. The entire Gaussian series converges locally absolutely, as do fixed derivatives. It has the same fixed-character reciprocal Mellin transform supplied in the compact brief. Take a fixed h>0, j>=0, and

    E_j=integral_[jh,(j+1)h] |U(y)|^2 dy,
    a=exp(gamma h), D(y)=U(y+h)-a U(y).

Translation and expansion give the EXACT identity

    E_(j+1)-a^2 E_j
      =integral_[jh,(j+1)h] (|D(y)|^2+2a Re(D(y)conj(U(y))))dy. (2)

Thus a one-sided upper bound on the full signed expression, at most
`C_epsilon exp((2gamma+epsilon)jh)` for every epsilon>0 and all large j,
implies `E_j=O_epsilon(exp((2gamma+epsilon)jh))`. Iterate the recurrence;
the equal-exponent case introduces at most j, absorbed in epsilon. A
finite initial set is paid by a fixed constant. Conversely an all-shell
bound of this exponent implies the stated one-sided bound, since E_j>=0.
This is an exponent equivalence, not an independently cheaper criterion.
All h-shells cover the dyadic shells with O_h(1) pieces, and conversely.
No density-one or average-in-j hypothesis is substituted.

For the exact exponential test U(y)=exp((beta+it)y),

    (E_(j+1)-a^2 E_j)/E_j=exp(2beta h)-exp(2gamma h).            (3)

It is positive for beta>gamma at every height t. Phase cancellation in
the innovation cannot make a faster Mellin mode dissipative. This is
the first decisive test of the proposal, not an arithmetic counterexample.

There is a small actual arithmetic payoff. The full diagonal has

    E_j^diag=kappa_q C_tau (exp(h)-1)exp(jh)+O_(q,tau,h)(exp(jh/2)),
    C_tau=exp(tau/4)/(2 sqrt(pi tau)),
    kappa_q=product_(p|q)(1-1/p) product_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2)>0.  (4)

For clarity, squarefree counting proves this without a prime theorem:
`mu(n)^2=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d)` and counting integers coprime to fixed q give
`sum_(n<=t)mu(n)^2 1_((n,q)=1) = kappa_q t+O_q(sqrt(t))`.
The tail of sum d^-2 and the O_q(1) error over d<=sqrt(t) each cost O_q(sqrt(t)).
Partial summation against `g_tau(log n-y)^2`, whose weighted derivative
integrals converge, gives the pointwise diagonal
`kappa_q C_tau exp(y)+O(exp(y/2))`; integrate it over the shell.
The displayed value of C_tau follows by completing the square in
`integral_R exp(v)g_tau(v)^2 dv`.

Consequently its drift is

    E_(j+1)^diag-a^2 E_j^diag
     =kappa_q C_tau(exp(h)-1)(exp(h)-exp(2gamma h))exp(jh)
       +O(exp(jh/2)),                                          (5)

strictly negative eventually whenever gamma>1/2. The full off-diagonal
drift is still unestimated. An unsigned diagonal lower bound never becomes
a lower bound on E_j. This result neither implies a new exponent nor
refutes cancellation in the complete square. Prior scale/Lyapunov
criteria, especially AH11/T49, already supply the main recurrence idea.

### 2.1 A local logarithmic comparison, with a proof

Let I be any real interval of length1, let t0 in I, and let f be analytic on a neighborhood of the closed disk |z-t0|<=R, R>=16. Assume f(t0)!=0, choose B>=sup_disk |f|, and let M=|f(t0)|. If there are no boundary zeros, then

    integral_I log|f(t)|dt
      >= log M - (8/log R) log(B/M).                    (L1)

Boundary zeros are avoided by choosing a nearby radius; the application below permits any R in a whole growing interval. Interior real zeros have integrable logarithmic singularities. The identically-zero case is excluded by f(t0)!=0.

Translate t0 to0 and set h=f/f(t0), A=log(B/M)>=0. Then v=A-log|h| is a nonnegative superharmonic function in the disk, with v(0)=A. Its elementary disk factorization/Poisson formula is

    v(z)=H(z)+sum_a G_R(z,a),
    G_R(z,a)=log|(R^2-conj(a)z)/(R(z-a))|,              (L2)

where a runs through zeros with multiplicity and H is the positive harmonic extension of the nonnegative boundary values of v. This identity follows by removing each disk Blaschke factor, then applying the harmonic Poisson formula to the nonvanishing quotient. There are finitely many zeros in the closed disk. No external estimate is imported.

For a positive harmonic function on the disk, the explicit Poisson kernel gives H(t)<=((R+1)/(R-1))H(0) for |t|<=1. This factor is at most1+8/log R.

For |a|<=sqrt R, subtraction at0 gives

    G_R(t,a)-G_R(0,a)
      =log|1-conj(a)t/R^2|+log|a|-log|t-a|.

The first term is at most R^(-3/2). If |a|<=2, the integral of -log|t-a| over any unit interval is at most1+log2: removing Im(a) only increases it, and the largest real logarithmic potential is obtained when Re(a) is at the interval midpoint. Thus the integrated difference is less than4. If |a|>2, the triangle inequality bounds the second difference pointwise by log2, again giving less than4. Meanwhile G_R(0,a)=log(R/|a|)>=.5 log R. Hence

    integral_I G_R(t,a)dt <= (1+8/log R)G_R(0,a).

For |a|>sqrt R, G_R(.,a) is positive harmonic in |z|<sqrt R. Its Poisson-kernel bound is (sqrt R+1)/(sqrt R-1)<=1+8/log R for R>=16. Integrating L2 now gives integral_I v<=(1+8/log R)v(0), which is L1. This proof does not assume a zero separation or multiplicity bound.
title: 2.1 A local logarithmic comparison, with a proof

### Full prime powers and the moving row AND column

For gamma>1/2,

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2) log p*p^(-j*gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1) sum_(n>=2)log n*n^(-2*gamma)<infinity.

Truncate z only above R, retain its whole past, and use translation contraction and Cauchy. Then |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed sufficiently large Y, using y>=Y on the tail. For every eta>0,

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                      (R2)

B_eta is finite from fixed bounded intervals and the Gaussian left tail; no assumed future norm is hidden in it. This relative form bound does not assert cancellation in K2 itself.

For the author's small-prime cutoff p<=(2+y)^A, A(1-gamma)<1, eventually log p<=y/2. Thus v=y-log p is in [y/2,y]. The row sum is at most C(2+y)^(A(1-gamma))log(2+y)=o(y), by summing over integers. In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables separately for each p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded by the same sum with p<=(2+2v)^A, hence o(v). Its upper endpoint satisfies v<=R. The initial bounded y interval uses finitely many primes and a fixed bounded v interval. Therefore, uniformly in every R,

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                (R3)

The column payment is necessary; a row estimate alone would not prove this quadratic-form statement. The written proof does pay both. There is no assumption about z at future points beyond R.

## G130. Raw principal finite-polynomial global contraction fails

For principal chi,0<gamma<1, let P(s) be a finite Dirichlet polynomial.
If R=1-L(s,chi)P(s) is bounded and holomorphic on the whole half-plane
Re>gamma, its pole at1 forces P(1)=0. If P=0 the norm is1. Otherwise
finite-frequency torus recurrence supplies unbounded T_k with
P(s+iT_k)->P(s) locally uniformly. Choose a disk centered at1 inside
the half-plane, with no P-zero on its boundary. Rouche supplies a zero
of P(s+iT_k) inside the disk. Translating back produces P-zeros with
unbounded heights away from the unique L-pole; at each, R=1. Therefore

    sup_(Re s>gamma)|1-L(s,chi)P(s)|>=1.            (17)

If the pole is not removed the supremum is infinite. Thus no sequence
of finite members yields globally uniform strict contraction in this
raw principal formulation. This does not obstruct compact convergence,
an open strip gamma<Re<1, one line, infinite filters, or the normalized
source(1). In particular the older W37 open-strip proposal excludes the
pole and is not rejected by(17). The escape is explicit, not a universal
Bezout impossibility claim.

statement:
## Uniform S04: what a positive character-pair detector preserves

For a fixed ordinary Dirichlet character chi, write F_chi(s)=1/L(s,chi). On Re s>1 the coefficient identity gives

F_barchi(s)=conj(F_chi(conj(s))),                                                 (B1)

and the relation continues wherever the meromorphic reciprocals are defined. A pole of F_chi at rho=beta+i*tau induces a pole of F_barchi at conj(rho), not automatically at rho. Substituting F_barchi(conj(s)) creates an antiholomorphic expression, not a new holomorphic two-component Dirichlet series. This distinction is essential at nonzero heights.

Set f(s)=(F_chi(s),F_barchi(s))^T near a possible rho and suppose its leading singular term is v*(s-rho)^(-m), v nonzero. Let A(s) be continuous there, with W=A^*A. Then

lim_(s->rho) |s-rho|^(2m) ||A(s)f(s)||^2 = v^*W(rho)v.                            (B2)

This follows simply by multiplying out the leading Laurent vector. W positive semidefinite does not force a nonzero limit: it may kill v. A sufficient source-independent signal condition is W(rho)>=delta*I with delta>0. More economically one may prove a lower bound just on all actual residue directions, but that remains a source obligation. For a finite bank use sum_j A_j^*A_j instead; every associated source and cross term must be retained in its arithmetic estimate.

For example |z1+z2|^2+|z1-z2|^2=2(|z1|^2+|z2|^2). Either single observation can miss a direction; the pair restores it at the original norm scale. For a real character, F_chi=F_barchi identically and the difference detector is exactly zero, including at every possible pole. This is an exact counterexample to positivity plus one difference observation being a universal detector.

The corresponding actual arithmetic pair is particularly restrictive. At every real x>=1,

M_chi(x)=sum_(n<=x) mu(n)chi(n),  M_barchi(x)=conj(M_chi(x)),
||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))||^2=2|M_chi(x)|^2.                                     (B3)

This retains all natural zeros and all sharp real endpoints. It also holds with common REAL weights. With a complex phase, conjugating chi alone is insufficient: the phase must also be conjugated to use (B3). At heights, the conjugate partner has the opposite height. Neither a changing height nor a complex source weight can be silently dropped.

Here is a complete conditional return for this exact pair, to avoid stopping at local detection. Fix 0<gamma<1 and the ordinary character. If for every epsilon>0 and every X>=2,

integral_X^(2X) ||(M_chi(x),M_barchi(x))|| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon), (B4)

then dyadic summation gives locally normal convergence of integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx on Re s>gamma. Indeed on a compact set with Re s>=gamma+2epsilon, each dyadic tail is O(2^(-j*epsilon)); the finite initial integral is harmless. It is holomorphic there, including all finite heights. On Re s>1 partial summation gives s times this integral =1/L(s,chi). Uniqueness of meromorphic continuation therefore excludes zeros of L in Re s>gamma. At s=1 the principal L pole produces a ZERO of its reciprocal and remains permitted. Imprimitive natural zeros are already in chi; no conductor-uniform constant is asserted. This is a complete sufficient return, not a proof of (B4).

By (B3), (B4) is exactly the scalar shell-L1 estimate up to sqrt(2). A uniformly well-conditioned positive change of coordinates is quantitatively comparable; a degenerating observation needs its inverse loss. For instance A_X=diag(X^(-eta),1), f_X=(X^beta,0)^T reduces the observed exponent by eta while leaving the original first component unchanged. This ambient example proves the need to pay observation conditioning, not an arithmetic lower bound.

Verdict: local Laurent residue coverage and full scalar-to-pair return are rigorous; conjugate-height and principal-pole qualifications are explicit. The elementary positive pair gives no exponent advantage over the actual scalar source. A useful survivor would be a genuinely different source-specific observation with proved residue coverage and a strictly cheaper COMPLETE arithmetic norm. Existing paired-detector, observation and bank work is ancestry; no novelty or c increase is inferred from (B1)-(B4) alone.
title: Uniform S04: what a positive character-pair detector preserves
