statement:
## 2. A: coefficients, stable inverse and zero return

Fix tau>0 and one ordinary Dirichlet character chi with its presented-modulus zeros. Put g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)), f(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))),

    F(x)=sum f(n)chi(n)g(log(n/x)),
    M(x)=sum mu(n)chi(n)g(log(n/x)),       x>0.

Prime2 is included in f. No squarefree-only replacement, chi-squaring, ideal character, angular family or growing conductor is implicit. The full coefficients, all powers and both real-scale tails remain.

For z=chi(p)p^-s, f's factor is (1-2z)/(1-z) for p!=3 and (1-z)^-1 for3. Hence D_f=N2 J/L with Np=1-2chi(p)p^-s, J2=J3=(1-z)^-2 and Jp=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2 for p>=5. At a ramified prime z=0 and the factor is1. For p>=5, j(p)=0, j(p^k)=1-k for k>=2; inverse coefficients k(p)=0, k(p^k)=2^(k-2). At2,3, j(p^k)=k+1 and inverse coefficients are1,-2,1,0,... . Twists are inserted exactly once.

Both absolute coefficient masses converge for every sigma>1/2. The infinite local errors are O_sigma(p^-2sigma), since2p^-sigma<1 for p>=5; the two finite-prime power series also converge. None of J's factors vanish there: the p>=5 numerator lines log_p2 are below1/2, and finite denominators have zeros only on real part0. Thus J is a holomorphic unit on this half-plane. N2's unramified zero line is real part1; N3's is a3=log2/log3. These lines must not be interchanged.

Use N_sigma(V)=sup_(T>0)T^-sigma||V||_[T,2T], with dx/x. Write Dp=I-ap S_p, ap=2chi(p), S_pV(x)=V(x/p). For unramified p and sigma<log_p2,

    E_p^-Y=-sum_(j>=1)ap^-j Y(p^j x),
    N_sigma(E_p^-Y)<=N_sigma(Y)/(2p^-sigma-1).       (A*)

Each exact shifted shell contributes (p^sigma/2)^j. Local L2 convergence and telescoping prove both inverse identities on this space. More importantly, for an actual field only known at the incumbent exponent,

    -sum_(j=1)^J ap^-j DpV(p^j x)=V(x)-ap^-J V(p^Jx).

The accepted fixed-character baseline gives M at a strictly buffered beta with .874861<beta<1. It is source-relative to the accepted written endpoint and its fixed-strip reciprocal-growth/Gaussian return, not deduced from holomorphy alone. Thus the p2 boundary has local-shell norm O_X(2^(-(1-beta)J)), independently of a proposed improved exponent. F and F2 below inherit this baseline by the absolutely paid J convolution. A homogeneous p2 state of size x^(1+it0) is excluded by this baseline; algebra alone would leave it.

The exact identities are

    F=T_j D2M,       D2M=T_k F,
    T_jV(x)=sum_r j(r)chi(r)V(x/r),                (A**)

and T_k similarly. A weight>1 first justifies the coefficient convolutions and complete local Gaussian series absolutely; finite weighted masses then pay their action at any sigma>1/2. For an all-large-dyadic every-epsilon bound at gamma, the Gaussian small-x tail and coverage by at most two dyads give a finite global shell norm at each strictly buffered sigma>gamma. Choosing sigma<1, A* and the previously paid actual boundary give M from F. Finite D2 and T_j give the converse. Therefore F and M have the SAME every-epsilon exponent class for1/2<gamma<1. There is no sigma=1 endpoint, moving finite future-window theorem or easier arithmetic estimate.

For f2(n)=mu(rad(n/2^v2(n))) and its complete field F2, local coefficients give

    D2F2=D3F,       F2=T_jD3M.

The second identity directly pays its incumbent baseline. Hence F2=E2^-D3F by the same vanishing future boundary. The causal inverse E3^+Y=sum_(j>=0)(2chi(3))^jY(x/3^j) costs (1-2*3^-sigma)^-1 for sigma>a3 and has a vanishing Gaussian left boundary. Consequently F=E3^+D2F2. General F/F2 equivalence holds for a3<gamma<1. If chi(3)=0, D3=I and the sufficient range extends to1/2<gamma<1; if chi(2)=0, D2=I and no division by a zero phase occurs. A baseline beta>a3 cannot pay a future-p3 boundary at a3, and that false inversion is not used.

Mellin initially gives integral M(x)x^-s dx/x=exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi) for Re(s)>1. An actual complete every-epsilon exponent gamma makes the integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma: dyadic Cauchy--Schwarz pays infinity with a strictly smaller epsilon; the Gaussian left tail pays0. Analytic continuation after multiplication by L excludes every zero in that half-plane, of any multiplicity and every fixed height, because the exponential never vanishes. A principal pole at1 gives a reciprocal zero, not a prohibited L-zero. A family conclusion needs its hypothesis for EACH fixed chi with one common gamma; constants may depend on chi/tau. No unbounded-conductor constant is produced.

**Verdict A:** correct paid composition and source organization. G28 supplies the exact convolution; RCC3 already supplies actual-Mobius future inversion with beta<1; W01 supplies the future-resolvent family; G70 already gives the literal f3 prime2 future inverse and [1,-3,1,...] channel. [research revision] G73 now also records the finite mixed composition and its full errors. A's language of a new inverse family is not accepted as novelty. None of these source-relative returns proves the improved moment they require.

### 4.3 Outer reconstruction and all cross terms

After choosing X_0 beyond the fixed four-diagonal geometry threshold,
replace each local P source in (C3) by its rectangular, capped or

Z^(-A_0+o(1)); hence for each fixed sigma>1/2 it is bounded by
C_sigma Z^sigma uniformly for Z>=X_0. Compact lower scale ranges
can be absorbed using absolute coefficient bounds. Summing with
|k(r)| and (C2) reproduces GC15's X^(1/2+epsilon) global error.
It does not assert an X^(-A_0) error after the outer reconstruction.

The source-tail estimates are applied locally before the r sum.
A global d_3 majorant for the reconstructed coefficients is neither
needed nor established. This avoids misusing the original label
majorant after a new arithmetic convolution.

The exact all-height reconstructed Mellin amplitude is GC20:

    D_X^rec(t)=E_tau(a+it)eta(a+it)
       sum_{r<=X/X_0}k(r)r^(-a-it)
          sum_{i+j=-2,-1,0,1}C_ij^6(a+it;X/r).          ([research revision])

The r^(-a-it) factor follows from (x/r)^(a+it); omitting its phase
would change the field. Its exact local Gram uses (C9) with Z=X.
Expanding the two finite outer sums therefore retains every
r,r',i,j,i',j' interaction with both independent heights.

If each local field is height truncated, the summand for r contains
its own indicator 1_{|t|<=D sqrt(log(X/r))}. The conjugate summand
for r' has its own indicator at t'. There is no collapse to one
height or to a common local cutoff. The field error bound followed
by the Hilbert-space inequality (C6) prices all mixed terms together.

Although ([research revision]) uses non-dyadic scales X/r, this creates no new
hypothesis: (C1) and the tail estimates are uniform for real local
scales. When only all-dyad arithmetic bounds are assumed, transport
first uses the fixed F_tau field as in GC14. Directly covering a

## Choice of forward proof and evidence limits

The old SP source had a fixed positive error exponent, a smooth-part
state partition and a logarithmic restoration span. The new detector
has four ordinary-bin diagonals, O(sqrt(log X)) intervals/heights,
subpower restoration and arbitrarily small fixed-power analytic errors.
Its count is not claimed asymptotically smaller than SP's different
loglog X count times60^55. The removal of arithmetic state filters and
the error floor is the useful change. This meets the admission rule by
removing a real prerequisite upstream of the remaining moment.

Both architectures retain a complete signed moment with no newly proved
power saving. Their component energies are not identified. SP's actual
RN/RNE bands, W34's support reductions, and the stronger [research revision]
transfer stay available in their own scopes; no new Gaussian analogue
of RN is asserted. The strongest objection is that the simpler factors
still encode the full hard Möbius cancellation and may give no new
estimate. The decisive test is a complete signed four-diagonal estimate,
or a genuinely useful sector that transfers with all complementary
terms paid. The independent direct lane is assigned precisely this test.

For the near-pair alternative the controller chooses tau=1,r=2.
The true diagonal and full absolute far sector then each cost
X^(1+o(1)), affordable for any fixed gamma>1/2. The remaining signed
off-diagonal near scalar is the actual target. This specialization is
a deduction from R35.14–19, not a separately discovered arithmetic theorem.

The coarse baseline at a=.75 is.2498 and the named target.24898.
The accepted c0 endpoint with a positive buffer gives the better
limiting baseline.24977329407992826... . Neither is improved here.
Keep raw benchmark and best limiting baseline distinct in the scorecard.

## 3. The source permission is genuinely available

The decisive source is literal B3.40, not the prose sentence describing PR9's original contradiction. For positive slots its hypotheses are

    7/10 <= kappa <= 3/4,
    beta_* >= 51/100,
    2 beta_* - 1 <= kappa.

Its capacity is n1+n2+6kappa z<=M. The theorem expressly fixes the common mesh before the arithmetic family, eventual slot count, profiles and target height, uniformly over that compact kappa interval. The original canonical good-prime pools, individual relative ray characters, one common slot profile, natural state, literal FixedInducingRow exclusion and common puncture remain part of the theorem. The zero-slot result is the separate unconditional, unrestricted-bounded-length nonprincipal result. Arbitrary coefficients or prime subsets allowed by MI do not thereby become allowed by MP.

PR9 T0 defines beta_* using the entire finite-order trivial-infinity Hecke family, with a 1/2 sentinel; imprimitive deletion does not add positive-real zeros. The accepted c10 review concludes beta_*<=theta10 for exactly that family, by its common-Delta argument. This is also explicit in current canonical integration. Therefore, under a contradiction beta_*>theta11,

    theta11 < beta_* <= theta10=.87485404,
    kappa10=2theta10-1=9371351/12500000=.74970808,
    7/10<kappa10<3/4,
    2beta_*-1<=kappa10.

    original accepted contracts -> independently accepted c10 family bound

An ordinary-characters-only c10 statement would be insufficient, but that is not the accepted input actually used. Three parameters must remain distinct in integration:

### A2. Lossless range and critical cost

Let r_X>=0 be arbitrary, and set

    d=limsup_(X->infinity) r_X loglog X/log X < infinity. (A8)

Suppose for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large DYADIC X,

    N_(r_X)(X) <<_epsilon X^(eta+epsilon), eta>0.         (A9)

Then

    ||F||_(L2([X,2X],dx/x))
         <<_epsilon X^(eta+d/2+epsilon)                 (A10)

on all sufficiently large dyadic shells. Proof: choose any A>0 and fix M>2(B+A)/nu. Set T=sqrt(M log X). The high part in A7 is O(X^-A). By A8,

    log[(1+M log X)^(r_X/2)]/log X <= d/2+o(1).

Finally g_kappa has a fixed positive minimum on [0,h], so the original shell norm is at most a fixed multiple of ||W_X||_2. All choices are frozen before X; epsilon in A9 is chosen smaller than the final requested buffer. No finite numerical sample or typicality label enters A10.

In particular r_X=o(log X/loglog X) has ZERO power loss. A fixed negative order, or one tending to infinity arbitrarily slowly below this threshold, gives the same every-epsilon exponent as the complete shell moment. This strengthens the fixed-order interpolation sketch without asserting a new arithmetic estimate.

The converse exponent implication is also exact: if the complete shell moment is O_epsilon(X^(eta+epsilon)), then N_(r_X)(X) has that bound for EVERY choice r_X>=0. Since N_r<=||W_X||_2, split the whole v-line into fixed dyadic-length intervals. On v in[kh,(k+1)h], the field argument lies on the shell of scale X2^k. The Gaussian g_kappa(v)^2 makes the sum of exp(2(eta+epsilon)kh) times its maximum on that interval finite. The assumed large-shell bound extends to all positive shells: on a bounded range use local convergence, and near zero the original source has a Gaussian left tail. To see that last assertion directly, write log n-log x>=0 for x<=1 and use (log n-log x)^2>=(log n)^2+(log x)^2, then A1. If the original hypothesis is only dyadic, two neighboring dyadic shells cover every shifted real shell. Hence

    d=0: A9 iff the original complete moment at eta,     (A11)

with the usual every-epsilon quantifiers. For d>0 we claim only the sufficient return A10 and the unshifted converse just proved, not exponent equivalence.

statement:
## Protected S28: an exact orthogonal coprimality realization

Let P be ANY finite set of K primes not dividing a fixed ordinary character modulus q. Index subsets A of P by n_A=product(p in A), including1. Retain a_A=mu(n_A)chi(n_A)=(-1)^|A|chi(n_A), and D=diag(a_A). Natural ramified zeros are handled by excluding those sites, not dividing by chi(p)=0. The local disjointness gate is

    G=[[1,1],[1,0]],  G_P=G tensor ... tensor G,
    (G_P)_(A,B)=1_(A intersect B empty).

With phi=(1+sqrt5)/2, set

    U=(phi^2+1)^(-1/2) [[phi,1],[1,-phi]].

Direct multiplication gives U^T U=I and U^T G U=diag(phi,-phi^(-1)). Consequently U_P=U^tensor K is orthogonal. Its own condition number is1: changing to this basis has no reconstruction loss in Euclidean norm. The gate eigenvalues are

    lambda_e=(-1)^j phi^(K-2j),  j=number of minus choices,

with multiplicity binomial(K,j). Thus rank(G_P)=2^K, ||G_P||_op=phi^K, ||G_P^(-1)||_op=phi^K, and ||G_P||_F^2=3^K. These are gate costs, not basis-change costs. Multiplying both sides by the unit-modulus diagonal D preserves singular values, even for complex chi; one must not confuse the bilinear D G_P D with a Hermitian conjugation.

Most importantly, take an arbitrary complex physical weight/mask W_(A,B), including its exact zero extensions. The full arithmetic contraction has the identity

    F(W)=sum_(A,B) a_A a_B 1_(A intersect B empty) W_(A,B)
        =sum_e lambda_e Z_(e,e),
    Z=U_P^T D W D U_P.                                  (A1)

Proof: the original sum is tr(G_P^T D W D); G_P is symmetric, then orthogonal conjugation and trace cyclicity give(A1). No mask is commuted through G_P or dropped. Frobenius norm is preserved: ||Z||_F=||W||_F. The generic absolute/Cauchy price is at most

    (sum_e |lambda_e|^2)^(1/2) (sum_e |Z_(e,e)|^2)^(1/2)
      <=3^(K/2)||W||_F.                                 (A2)

The signed diagonal sum in(A1) can be smaller, but that is an arithmetic estimate on the transformed complete boundary. Diagonalizing the local gate alone supplies no such estimate. Conversely the large generic price does not lower-bound F(W). This is a constructive realization, not a rejection of the proposed basis.

For the actual product cutoff W_(A,B)=1_(n_A n_B<=X)Phi(n_A n_B), grouping DISJOINT pairs yields exactly

    F(W)=sum_(n<=X, squarefree, p|n implies p in P)
                 mu(n)chi(n)2^omega(n)Phi(n).             (A3)

Every prime of n has two assignments to the ordered pair. Thus this simple masked network has coefficient2^omega(n)mu(n)chi(n), not mu(n)chi(n). An intended detector must preserve its own weight W, or prove a separate return for(A3). An appealing tensor picture does not license replacing the actual source coefficient.

There are two different size regimes. For a single divisor cube of an integer N with radical supported on P, product(P)<=N implies (K+1)!<=N, hence K=O(log N/loglog N). ### F03.OM — Physical orientations first

Use a single common fixed completion
\[
\mathbf S_h(s)=F(s)\mathbf D_h(s),\qquad
F(s)=L^{(S)}(3s-1,\xi_{\rm ang}),
\quad D_h(s)=\sum_{c\ {\rm sf}}\beta(c)\vartheta_c(h)q_c^{-s}.
\]
The finite vector is the actual ray orbit closed under the required arithmetic switches. Do not manufacture a geometric period for a component merely because its analytic D-series is defined. T01 transfers completed/uncompleted means without a dimension penalty, using separate holomorphy and buffered-strip means. T02 also transfers directly in the completed selector without division.

T03 reduces \(h=ab^2d^3\) to cube-free physical rows \(ab^2\), preserving all extra cube-prime deletions and overlaps. The sharp universal positive lift works for weight exponent \(v>1/3\); this is different from the [research revision] scalar-shell obstruction. The target is
\[
\sum_{q_aq_b^2\le X}\|\mathbf S_{ab^2}(s)\|^2
\ll X^{35/32+\epsilon}T^A.
\]
The physical norm is \(q_aq_b^2\), primitive conductor essentially \(q_aq_b\), and reduced sixth Fourier index \(a^4b^2\). These are three different quantities.

A sufficient rectangular bound is \(A^{1+\eta}B^{2+2\eta}\), or the stronger useful fixed-\(b\) form \(A^{35/32}B^{1+\epsilon}\). Combine genuinely different box estimates \(A^{r_j}B^{s_j}\) by the exact frontier
\[
R=\max_{0\le z\le1/2}\min_j\{r_j(1-2z)+s_jz\};
\]
A02 records its proof. An optimistic pointwise mixed bound \(q_aq_b^{1/2}\) only pays a narrow inverse edge for the \(35/32\) target. The actual prime-square inverse sector is already \(\ll X^{3/2-\sigma+\epsilon}\), but cube descendants can delete new primes and create ordinary orientations. It is not an isolated closed family.

**First method:** average the actual translated current covariance before separate tests:
\[
q_h^{-1}\sum_{x,y\bmod h}^{*}\overline{\psi_h(x)}\psi_h(y)
P_{h,x}\overline{P_{h,y}}.
\]
At a prime, adding the two nontrivial cubic orientations gives \(3\,1_{y/x\ {\rm cube}}-1\), not a Kronecker delta. Keep that sign with the physical orientation weights. Compute the ordinary face \(b=1\), its diagonal and one off-diagonal orbit, after the actual incoming calibration.

**Second method:** project the test onto an independently defined finite current/spectral image before estimating its Riesz norm. A prescribed deck character and controlled spectral window is a legitimate definition; “the unknown useful part” is not. The two unprojected cusp channels already cost \(Q(Q-1)\) centrally. A new restriction may do better, but another minimization of the same seed does not.

**Bounded auxiliary child:** tensor an ordinary cusp at \(a\)-primes with a broad inverse cusp at \(b\)-primes. Test \(pq^2\) first, including CRT multipliers, incoming tails, nonunit Fourier indices and a shared cube prime. Prime formulas cannot simply be multiplied. Promote an inverse-composite extension only if it opens a new box beyond the already-paid edge. A18 screens the simple diagonal oldforms: r=0,1 vanish, and the first unit-compatible r=2 still costs Q at the central edge before any new current-norm cost. General combinations and actual projected tests remain open.

### F04.C — The new hard sector

Use the actual fully compensated field \(S_c\) containing every completed column \(A=cn^3\) with squarefree core \(c\), all descendants, marks and embeddings. With
\[
Q=q_{b_*}XY,\quad P_a=Y^2/Q,\quad L=Z^\ell,
\quad \mathcal F_A=1+P_a^{1/6}+LP_a^2/Y,
\]
T06 proves
\[
\mathcal D_{\rm core}=\sum_c\|S_c\|_2^2
\ll (Z^\epsilon/Y)\mathcal F_A.
\]
This is the actual square function, not a bound on \(\|\sum_cS_c\|_2^2\). For a smooth true-gcd dyad,
\[
\mathcal C(G)=\sum_{c\ne c'}w(q_{(c,c')}/G)\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle,
\]
T07 gives, relative to the stronger inherited finite-order Hecke inputs,
\[
|\mathcal C(G)|\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A
 {Z^{1+b_0/2}L^{1+3b_0/2}\over G^2}.
\]
The actual product-slot structure is essential. Thus dyads above
\[
G_0=Z^{1/2+b_0/4}L^{1/2+3b_0/4}
\]
are affordable; at the saved .12551 geometry \(\log_ZG_0=.91621058\ldots\). A rigorous proof works first at a fixed \(b>b_0\), then allocates the final small loss. Rational \(b=7/8\) gives \(G_0=Z^{23/32}L^{37/32}\). The result does not follow from rational-zeta nonvanishing alone.

The exact remaining target is a one-sided upper bound, or the stronger absolute bound,
\[
\boxed{\ \sum_{G<G_0}\mathcal C(G)
\ll {Z^\epsilon\over Y}\mathcal F_A\ }
\tag{CORE}
\]
with a smooth complete partition and all inherited uniformities. At the saved geometry \(LP_a^2/Y\) is harmless and \(\mathcal F_A\asymp P_a^{1/6}\) up to allowed losses. This leaves a large arithmetic sector; the tail exponent .9162 is a useful reduction, not evidence that only a negligible set remains.

For \(c=gu,c'=gv\) and embedded products \(D=G_*d,E=G_*e\), the live common-core character is
\[
\psi(g)=\vartheta_g(ve)\overline{\vartheta_g(ud)}.
\]
The exact collision masks \((u,e)=(v,d)=1\), together with the two gcd decompositions, make every surviving off-core good character nonprincipal. A marked prime enters the squarefree Euler identity through
\[
f_s(p)={t_p\over1+t_p},\qquad t_p=\psi(p)q_p^{-s};
\]
a same-slot coincidence contributes \(f_s-f_s^2\). The first two powers carry nonprincipal cubic characters; the first possible principal power is paid by its cubic decay. This is the mechanism already exploited in the large-gcd tail. A small-gcd proof must improve its averaging order or its use of the remaining cofactors.

statement:
## 4. Primary-source constant terms and actual source slots

The primary formulas used here are the zero-frequency matrices immediately after (4.23) and the 24-cusp equation (4.28) in [DDHL v4](https://arxiv.org/html/2306.11875v4), and the definitions (6.11)–(6.15), square relation (6.18), and fourth-power periodicity (6.16) in [de Faveri–Dunn–Hoffstein v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.07911v1). In particular (6.12) includes the actual constant 4pi Psi_ij(0) v^(3/4). These are residual quartic theta forms, not cuspidal forms.

Write lambda=1+i, let i1 denote cusp 0 and i2 cusp eta_c=lambda^4/(1+lambda^3), and put

    f=(V theta_i1, -V theta_i2),
    zeta_lambda(w)=zeta_Q(i)(w)(1-2^-w),
    R=Res_(w=1) zeta_lambda(w), C=pi R/zeta_lambda(2).

Here V is the source torus volume (16 in its convention). Direct residue calculation gives the following constant vectors, all multiplied by v^(3/4):

| Expansion cusp | Constant vector of f |
|---|---|
| infinity | (C,0) |
| 0=i1 | (2C,0) |
| eta_c=i2 | (0,-2C) |

For clarity, this table is a deduction, not an assumed symmetry of a complex-character matrix. DDHL's displayed columns have the common quotient R(xi)=zeta_lambda(4xi-4)/zeta_lambda(4xi-3); the self-cusp entry has multiplier 2/(2^(4xi-4)-1). At xi=5/4 that multiplier is 2, and the quotient residue is R/(4 zeta_lambda(2)). The other relevant column entries are R(xi) for the infinity/i1 pair and zero for the infinity/i2 and cross pairs. Where a row rather than the displayed column is required, zero-frequency double-coset inversion gives

    phi_ij(xi)=conjugate(phi_ji(conjugate(xi))).

Indeed gamma -> gamma^-1 swaps the two cusp double-coset sets, replaces the lower-left entry by its negative without changing its absolute norm, and inverts the unitary multiplier. The entries just used are real on the real initial convergence line, so their residues transpose as stated. Multiplication by the archimedean zero-mode factor 4pi and the signed V gives the table. This also avoids extending a formula stated only for nonzero Fourier index to index zero without proof.

Let r(nu0)=(a,b) !=0 and R0=|a|²+|b|². The literal ray sources are

    f_1=(conjugate(a) f1+conjugate(b) f2)/R0,
    f_eta=(conjugate(b) f1-conjugate(a) f2)/R0.

Each ray term uses its own f_ray in BOTH quartic slots. In general it is not theta_i1 tensor theta_i2. At infinity the constants of these two ray sources are C conjugate(a)/R0 and C conjugate(b)/R0; at 0 they are twice these; at eta_c they are -2C conjugate(b)/R0 and 2C conjugate(a)/R0. All cross terms arising from these expressions belong to the actual source. Since the two raw-source constants at 0 and eta_c form a nonsingular diagonal matrix, no nonzero linear combination in this two-dimensional global seed span is cuspidal at both cusps.

This obstruction is deliberately limited. The complete U' period imposes nu1=nu2=-nu3, and its odd unary theta has no zero Fourier coefficient. Thus every literal term containing a source constant disappears after the appropriate full unipotent average. Odd parity persists under Weil translation; its possible zero-index theta contribution comes only from m=0 and vanishes. Source constants must be retained while constructing or unfolding a boundary map, but their mere existence does not prove an uncancelled boundary in the final period. A cusp zero mode and a relative asymptotic germ are different functionals.

The two components above specify global cusps and bad-place ray data. Away from the level their source vectors are unramified. Neither cited primary formula declares them an independent two-dimensional good-prime scattering basis. No local Whittaker multiplicity-one or multiplicity-two claim is needed or proved here. In particular the 24-cusp global functional equation cannot simply be reduced to a guessed local two-by-two relative matrix.

The actual bin prime estimate B0.16 gives |Q_u|^2<<H_J U^(delta v+epsilon), with its original common profiles, holes and fixed real bin buffer. Therefore

    sum_(u in E_pre)|Q_u|^2
                 << H_J U^[J(delta,lambda)+delta v+epsilon]. (R14)

This step uses the actual pointwise bin slot estimate only after bounding a positive exceptional set. It does not put E_pre into a Poisson kernel. Finite attaining dictionary labels have fixed cost; separate rowwise heights are handled by the already retained polynomial-height Sobolev estimate. The statement is not for an arbitrary coefficient family or a principal detector with a residue.

For the comparison retain exactly

    h=5-2delta, rho=1-10delta/(3h), k=rho+delta-1,
    D_K=15K-10-6Kdelta,

    E_K=rho+delta v-min(3kv,a_K+b_K v).                 (R15)

All denominators are strictly positive on the rectangle; k=delta(5-6delta)/(3h)>0 and b_K>0. Set lambda0=1/2500 and J0=23/18-4delta/3. For v<=1/25 and lambda<=lambda0,

    E_K-(J+delta v)-1/5000

The inequality uses b_K>0 and1-delta>0, and min(3kv,a_K+b_K v)<=a_K+b_K v. Multiply the right side by3hD_K and substitute delta=17/25+x/50, 0<=x<=1. Its four degree-three Bernstein coefficients, in increasing index order, are

    17291065395149/1464843750000000,
    35476907047777/109863281250000,
    25900645202087/43945312500000,
    24797299722/30517578125.

All are strictly positive. This is a whole-interval rational certificate, not an endpoint sampling argument. It establishes the first restricted consequence in R1.

For the complete marked norm R13, use min(3kv,a_K+b_K v)<=3kv. At v<=1/200, lambda<=lambda0, it suffices to prove

    rho-J0-(1-delta)/2500
      -(5/3-delta+3k)/200-1/5000>=0.                   (R17)

The coefficient5/3-delta+3k is positive. Multiply by3h and use the same delta parameterization. Its degree-two Bernstein coefficients are

All fixed bin padding, endpoint errors, moment epsilon shares and derivative logarithms can be chosen to spend less than1/10000, leaving a strict saving of at least1/10000; the displayed1/5000 is the algebraic margin before those shares. Heights retain H_J and must be assigned the usual final small powers, not silently set to one.

At v=1/20 the source counting ledger already fails at delta=17/25, lambda=0 by R1. Increasing lambda decreases it. Thus neither of the restricted conclusions licenses a whole-v estimate. No claim of global optimality is inferred from that failure.

statement:
# W41 immutable initial cards



Each p is an uncalibrated estimate of mechanism typicality in this research context, NEVER a correctness probability. Each card is an initial proposal, not a theorem, not an achieved increase, and not yet screened against history. Where the source form is unknown, a toy object is explicitly distinguished. Existing masks, projectors, signed coefficients and quantifiers must be recovered before transfer. The accepted written endpoint remains c4=.125135; new-endpoint formalization/kernels are pending.

## Group 1: free invention

**W41-01 | factorization noise spectrum | p=.045.** On a squarefree divisor cube, signed Mobius summation is its top Fourier coefficient. Bound that coefficient by repeatedly applying a noise derivative, and charge the complement by observed low-degree influence. Hope: a full signed moment bound with power saving, rather than positivity. First test: derive the exact cube identity with the actual arithmetic weights and determine the cost of exposing enough independent primes. Main danger: support masks put all their mass at top degree. Ceiling: a reusable power-saving signed estimate, potentially reaching 1/6 if quantitatively strong enough.

**W41-02 | jointly optimized zero witness | p=.21.** A hypothetical zero creates a family of correlated detector witnesses; optimize a single dual functional against all of them instead of bounding each separately. First test: formulate the finite Gram feasibility problem and ask whether the shared witness is actually smaller than individual worst cases. Bridge: prove every zero in the target strip yields a vector violating the same certified inequality. Danger: forbidden data-dependent coefficients or conductor constants. Reach: near gain without changing original transfer.

**W41-03 | signed boundary flux | p=.065.** Replace a large interior absolute moment by flux through a slightly enlarged contour, retaining cancellation between opposite faces. First test: an exact Green/Stokes identity for a finite Dirichlet polynomial and its signed fourth moment. Bridge: quantify enlargement and poles, then recover the original strip estimate. Danger: boundary flux has the same uncontrolled arithmetic correlations. Reach: .25 moment barrier bypass if signed flux has genuine decay.

**W41-04 | one-prime Schur complement | p=.16.** Isolate one prime's local factor as a rank-one update of a Dirichlet convolution inverse. Iterated Schur complements might retain cancellation hidden by a global norm. First test: write the exact block inverse on squarefree divisors of three primes. Bridge: a uniformly convergent inverse implies zero exclusion through a proved identity. Danger: local conditioning costs accumulate like the full Euler product. Reach: 1/6 or 1/4 through a new inverse architecture.

**W41-05 | moving cutoff compensation | p=.12.** Couple two neighboring cutoff values so the difficult shell appears with opposite signs and the core remains stable. First test: derive the differentiated moment in the cutoff parameter without dropping zero extensions. Bridge: integrate the differential inequality and pay both endpoint shells. Danger: a true inequality cannot gain just by renaming a positive boundary mass. Reach: small rigorous improvement if the bottleneck is endpoint loss.

## Group 2: free invention

**W41-06 | adaptive prime involution | p=.08.** Pair squarefree divisors by toggling a prime selected from the local geometry; Mobius signs reverse. Preserve the fixed points as an explicit boundary set. First test: construct an actual involution, not a greedy map, for a multiplicative interval mask. Bridge: bound all fixed points and weight differences by a power-saving quantity. Danger: every point is boundary when prime scales are large. Reach: full signed cancellation and high ceiling.

**W41-07 | two-scale anti-concentration | p=.24.** Divide arithmetic correlations into near-collision and separated scales. Use a weak but uniform cancellation bound only on separated scales; count the collision set exactly. First test: calculate the collision mass with original projectors. Bridge: one full estimate with no unpriced intermediate zone. Danger: largest mass occupies the collision set. Reach: near gain with an intentionally coarse lemma.

**W41-08 | prime deletion stability | p=.07.** Measure how much a detector changes when one prime is removed; an Efron-Stein style decomposition could turn bounded influences into a signed estimate. First test: exact conditional expectation on a finite product probability space matching arithmetic density. Bridge: quantify the discrepancy between arithmetic sampling and product sampling. Danger: discrepancy is the entire desired theorem. Reach: restricted result plus clear arithmetic residual.

**W41-09 | transport across norm shells | p=.008.** Match positive and negative coefficient mass using multiplicative transport, paying a Lipschitz cost for the test kernel. First test: determine whether signed mass has zero total on every fiber and compute an explicit transport plan on a divisor cube. Bridge: transport cost times actual kernel modulus bounds the full signed form. Danger: normalization and mask boundaries destroy mass balance. Reach: a signed estimate that survives rough kernels.

**W41-10 | exact witness attenuation | p=.055.** Instead of improving an upper moment bound, prove a hypothetical zero forces a larger lower witness after averaging a small continuum of shifts. First test: calculate the zero contribution and all cross terms for two shifts. Bridge: stronger uniform lower bound beats unchanged upper estimate. Danger: phases make the new witnesses cancel. Reach: near gain or 1/6 if lower growth changes.

## Group 3: multiplicative structure / noncommutative probability / coarse sector bound

**W41-11 | alternating conditional expectations | p=.04.** Treat independent prime blocks as conditional expectations E_j; multiply centered operators (I-E_j) before taking norms. Algorithm: reveal blocks, keep their alternating signs, telescope only commutator errors with the masks. First test: prove the exact decomposition with two noncommuting masks. Bridge: a cheap bound on total commutator mass pays the complement. Danger: arithmetic expectations do not commute. Reach: rigorous restricted sector with an explicit error ledger.

**W41-12 | noncommutative martingale budget | p=.065.** Encode a signed correlation as the trace of a product of prime-block martingale differences. A very coarse operator-norm bound might suffice if a large external scale budget survives. First test: construct matrices reproducing all signs exactly on four squarefree variables. Bridge: bound the trace plus a counted exceptional fiber sector. Danger: matrix dimension swallows the nominal gain. Reach: full moment improvement if dimension is subpower.

**W41-13 | free-product arithmetic surrogate | p=.009.** Replace prime-block interactions by freely independent operators, then use the defect from freeness as the sole arithmetic residual. First test: compare the first four joint moments for an exact toy divisor model. Bridge: a quantitative noncommutative Lindeberg replacement with an explicit total error. Danger: primes are commutative, so free independence may be structurally wrong. Preserve even an incoherent result. Reach: high-ceiling replacement representation.

**W41-14 | completely positive signed dilation | p=.007.** Dilate a signed coefficient operator into an off-diagonal corner of a positive block matrix; apply a coarse positive inequality to the dilation while recovering the sign in a chosen corner. First test: test whether the dilation norm equals or exceeds the original signed norm for a 2x2 example. Bridge: recover a zero detector without dimension/norm inflation. Danger: dilation only repackages absolute values. Reach: unlikely but potentially an exact positivity bridge.

**W41-15 | multiplicative stopping-time sector | p=.035.** Stop revealing primes when a local conditional variance becomes large. Bound the stopped good sector by martingale orthogonality and the bad sector by a very crude count paid from a larger budget. First test: define a deterministic stopping rule and prove the two sectors partition the actual coefficients. Bridge: original form equals controlled good plus completely priced bad. Danger: bad mass is not sparse. Reach: restricted theorem with a usable full return if stopping tails decay.

## Group 4: analytic continuation / control or realization / ambient representation

**W41-16 | Dirichlet passive realization | p=.025.** Realize a reciprocal L-object as the transfer function of a passive system whose energy estimate forbids poles. First test: does a finite Euler product admit a positive storage function with constants independent of the prime cutoff? Bridge: a quantitative limiting realization yields analyticity and nonvanishing. Danger: the energy inequality itself encodes the missing zero-free theorem. New invariant: minimum storage cost versus cutoff.

**W41-17 | balanced truncation of multiplicative Hankel | p=.015.** Form a multiplicative Hankel matrix from inverse coefficients and retain only directions with large singular value. First test: derive the exact tail bound and compare with an additive low-rank surrogate. Bridge: a certified operator tail plus a small inverse residual proves a Bezout identity in the target strip. Danger: translation from l2 operator control to pointwise evaluation is unbounded. Reach: 1/6 or 1/4 if the tail decays.

**W41-18 | pseudospectral continuation barrier | p=.08.** Track the smallest singular value of a finite coefficient convolution operator as sigma moves left; certify it cannot cross zero before the desired line. First test: distinguish finite triangular invertibility from a uniform infinite inverse. Bridge: bound finite-section inverses and tails in one evaluation-compatible norm. Danger: every finite section is invertible even when the infinite analytic function vanishes. Reach: precise no-go invariant or a new inverse proof.

**W41-19 | two-port scattering detector | p=.006.** Place the detector and its complement in a two-port scattering matrix; conservation makes the omitted sector an observable outgoing channel. First test: build a unitary dilation for a finite signed convolution and recover its defect formula. Bridge: a strict contraction at the zero witness contradicts conservation. Danger: unitary dilation adds exactly the missing loss and yields no strict contraction. Reach: systematic accounting of complement losses.

**W41-20 | observability of a zero mode | p=.055.** A zero corresponds to a hidden mode of a shift realization. Prove a coarse observability lower bound from arithmetic sampling that prevents hidden modes in a larger strip. First test: explicit exponential-polynomial toy system with one planted zero. Bridge: controllability/observability constants must be uniform in truncation and height. Danger: a planted mode can evade every finite sample. Reach: direct replacement zero exclusion.

## Group 5: Mobius compensation / sieve and information or coding / exact invariant

**W41-21 | parity syndrome Möbius transform | p=.006.** The Mobius sign on a squarefree fiber is parity; retain parity-check syndromes as an exact sufficient statistic instead of absolute-value summing each factorization. First test: express the signed sum through conditional Fourier coefficients on every syndrome. Bridge: small bias of the parity given all source masks bounds the global signed form. Danger: a mask reveals parity completely. Reach: precise entropy-independent arithmetic residual.

**W41-22 | erasure-correcting divisor fibers | p=.004.** Couple two divisor factorizations as two encodings of the same integer. Erasure recovery might expose a togglable prime whose sign remains unknown after both masks. First test: characterize fibers with no recoverable prime and count their mass. Bridge: a sign-reversing involution plus explicit erasure failures. Danger: unique factorization leaks every bit. Reach: full global cancellation if failures are sparse.

**W41-23 | entropy is not cancellation | p=.003.** Reverse the tempting implication: high conditional entropy alone should NOT imply small Mobius bias; construct the extremal parity-supported measure and determine the additional inequality that would suffice. First test: exact finite-cube entropy-versus-parity optimization. Bridge target: conditional bias or a strong data-processing coefficient, not entropy. Danger: yields only a useful obstruction, no arithmetic gain. Reach: eliminate a broad false route and state a sharp replacement hypothesis.

**W41-24 | coding-theoretic dual detector | p=.008.** Choose coefficient weights orthogonal to all low-complexity mask codewords while preserving the zero witness. First test: solve the exact finite linear constraints and check witness survival in the quotient. Bridge: full remainder bound for high-complexity codewords and quantitative witness lower bound. Danger: desired witness lies in the annihilated span. Reach: a new detector family potentially escaping .25.

**W41-25 | two zeta transforms one checksum | p=.005.** Couple additive and multiplicative incidence transforms by the integer identity underlying both descriptions; their mismatch is a checksum. First test: find an actual nontrivial common invariant on a finite set. Bridge: bound the mismatch while exactly reconstructing signed Mobius weights. Danger: no such useful invariant exists; preserve this incoherent possibility. Reach: radical representation change if a valid checksum survives masks.

## Group 6: high ceiling / invented connection / reverse implication and converse

**W41-26 | chemical reaction detailed balance | p=.006.** Toy connection: divisor toggles are reversible reactions with opposite-sign charge. Reverse “balanced reactions imply cancellation”: characterize when a signed masked fiber admits local detailed balance with bounded conductance. First test: solve edge-flow conservation on a Boolean cube with boundary leakage. Bridge: arithmetic flow energy controls the signed moment through kernel gradients. Obstruction: conductance may concentrate on forbidden edges. Reach: high-ceiling signed transport with a coarse energy budget.

**W41-27 | topological boundary of a divisor complex | p=.004.** Toy connection: Mobius signs are orientations of a cubical chain. Reverse “boundary has zero interior”: construct a bounded filling of the source coefficient chain so only boundary terms remain. First test: discrete Stokes with interval masks on a 3-cube. Bridge: a uniform filling norm plus actual arithmetic kernel regularity. Obstruction: mask holes create large homology classes. Reach: signed global moment gain with an explicit geometric invariant.

**W41-28 | one-dimensional inverse scattering | p=.002.** Build a toy potential whose scattering determinant is a finite Dirichlet polynomial; reverse pole exclusion to recover a coercive potential bound. First test: check whether finite Euler products admit such a realization without artificial negative energy. Bridge: pass to an arithmetic potential with a rigorously finite norm. Obstruction: arbitrary determinant realizations can hide every bad constant. Reach: 1/4 via a different analytic object; likely incoherent.

**W41-29 | homogenization of logarithmic prime phases | p=.007.** Toy connection: rapidly oscillating media. Reverse “phase mixing gives effective damping”: find an exact cell problem whose corrector norm is equivalent to signed arithmetic cancellation. First test: a two-frequency polynomial with a resonant ratio and its corrector blowup. Bridge: bound every resonance cell and its complement at actual height. Obstruction: close logarithmic relations create large small denominators. Reach: high-ceiling oscillatory route with an honest Diophantine residual.

**W41-30 | persistent excitation from one Euler factor | p=.005.** Toy connection: synchronization and system identification. Reverse “rich input observes all modes”: characterize how many prime phases suffice to detect any hypothetical zero mode with a fixed nonzero gain. First test: two exponential modes with near-colliding frequencies. Bridge: an explicit uniform frame lower bound coupled to an exact L-function zero witness. Obstruction: frame constants may decay exponentially in height or dimension. Reach: replacement detector, or a rigorous finite-sampling obstruction.

## Frozen initial-state record

All 30 draws are retained exactly as initial ideas, including likely incoherent W41-13, W41-25 and W41-28. No outcomes, detailed-history duplicates, ranking or rare selection has been observed or made in this artifact. Semantic stimuli are the four unchanged prepared recipe combinations, respectively applied to groups 3–6. Groups 1–2 are free invention. Literal p-threshold eligibility will include cards from ALL groups; the p labels do not quantify correctness or novelty. Original PR9 and Gao PR15 credit and the fixed arithmetic scope are retained from the problem snapshot.

statement:
## 4. Review of the author's full square-row and cross-row estimates

Set f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^(3/2)-i(n/x)^6), and use dx/x on every real x in
[X,2X]. All amplitudes, prefixes and cuts are fixed before x. For any
1<=A<=pX^alpha0 with fixed alpha0<1 and any root prefix endpoint R,
including infinity, the author proves

    ||sum_{r<=R}beta(r)f_x(Ar^2)||_2 << 1+X^(3/8)A^(-1/4).          (R3)

I reconstructed the complete proof. Put F=(X/A)^6 and
R0=c0 F^(1/11). On each nonzero Fourier mode of beta the phase derivative
is j/(pq)-(6/pi)(A/x)^6 t^11. Choose c0 fixed so that it stays separated
from integers on the low prefix, including one extra unit for the last
discrete increment. Since R0 tends to infinity uniformly under alpha0<1,
all small-X exceptions enter a fixed constant. Discrete first-derivative
summation gives O(1) for every undamped low prefix; Abel summation retains
the actual decreasing damping and the exact endpoint min(R,R0).

For the entire high prefix, a fixed positive C^2 shell majorant and two
integrations by parts give

    |K_A(r,s)| << exp(-cA(r^2+s^2)/X^(3/2))
                     min(1,(F/|r^12-s^12|)^2).

The diagonal costs X^(3/4)A^(-1/2). For r>s>R0 use
r^12-s^12>=r^11(r-s) and sum min(1,(F/(r^11 h))^2) over h>=1.
It is O(F/r^11), including F/r^11<1. Summation in r costs
F R0^(-10)=F^(1/11), which is at most the diagonal price for A>=1.
Both orientations and all aliases have been paid. The low/high interaction
is paid by the norm triangle inequality. Arbitrary R only removes terms
from a positive absolute coefficient majorant; it is not used as a signed
norm monotonicity principle.

For Q_D, remove these exact low prefixes in each d,e row, d<=D, e=1,p.
The low total is pointwise O(D). If z_X(n) is the complete merged high
coefficient, then

    |z_X(n)| <= C_p #{r:r^2|n, r^2>=n/(pD)},
    n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11)X^(12/11)D^(-1/11).                       (R4)

For each r and n each e determines at most one d, so shared square
divisors and collisions between different d rows retain their multiplicity.
The strict support follows before any absolute values from r>R0(ed).
No divisibility, character or row-dependent prefix has been replaced by a
different signed source. Since D<=X^alpha0, N0/X tends to infinity.

On a comparable block n in[N/2,4N], take T_N=sqrt(N/(8pD)) and
w_N(n)=#{r>T_N:r^2|n}. The positive majorant in (R4) is bounded by C_p w_N.
The exact W24 argument gives

    sum_{n in I}w_N(n) << H sqrt(D/N)+min(N^(1/3),D),
    sum_{n in[N/2,4N]}w_N(n) << sqrt(ND),                        (R5)

for every interval of length H in that block. To see the error term,
split roots at N^(1/3) when T_N is below that point and reverse all larger
roots to complementary multipliers. If T_N is larger, reverse all roots.
The real root interval has length O(H/(sqrt(N)sqrt(m))), and each such
interval contributes its length plus one. This proves both cases, with
nonintegral thresholds, endpoint atoms and H<1 retained. It counts pairs,
not just distinct physical integers. Constants absorb fixed p.

Let H_N=X^6/N^5. The full integer kernel is bounded by

    exp(-c(n+m)/X^(3/2)) min(1,(X^6/|n^6-m^6|)^2),              (R6)

interpreted as1 on the diagonal. On comparable blocks its gap is bounded
below by a constant times N^5|n-m|. Apply (R5) to the central interval and
both geometric annuli. The squared kernel decay makes the density and
endpoint contributions summable. Multiplying by the outer mass in (R5)
pays the complete comparable block at

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2))[X^6 D N^(-5)
                         +sqrt(ND)min(N^(1/3),D)].              (R7)

This includes the actual diagonal multiplicity and both orientations.
Summing its first term from N0 yields X^(6/11)D^(16/11). Summing each
alternative endpoint price through the entire damped range gives the
minimum of X^(3/4)D^(3/2) and X^(5/4)D^(1/2).

For far pairs with max(n,m)~N and max>=2min, the gap is at least cN^6.
Both the outer mass and the entire smaller-variable cumulative mass are
O(sqrt(ND)), directly from sum_{d<=D}sqrt(N/d). Thus both orientations cost
O(X^12 D N^(-11)), whose complete sum from N0 is O(D^2). The diagonal
belongs only to the comparable region. This proves the author's (4A.1)
without deleting a cross term or an infinite tail.

The stated original corridor follows from its norm exponents
alpha,(3+8alpha)/11,min(3/8+3alpha/4,5/8+alpha/4), and is valid at equality.
It is a proved complete source estimate, although the endpoint error in
(R7) is unnecessarily expensive when the frequency gap is already large.

## Decisive objections tested and limits of the conclusion

| Potential objection | Assessment at the pinned sources |
| --- | --- |
| A new arbitrary prime coefficient family replaced the natural slots. | No: relative characters, canonical pools, common profile and exact zero extensions survive allocation. |
| Low bins are transformed by Poisson, or require heredity after deleting slots. | No: attach them only to positive energy after both transforms, remove slots pointwise, then enlarge and call the old theorem. |
| The height-uniform density is only proved for each fixed height. | No: the internal small-height construction and large-height absolute count produce one threshold before all heights; external exponent is distinct. |
| Abstract character choice has no conductor bound. | True objection to that shortcut; resolved by the natural constructor and coefficient equality, not by using `RowData.character` for conductor. |
| Fixed dictionary silently includes principal twists from another translate. | No: bins remain inside the actual parent translate; fixed union is only for constants/outer partition. |
| Signed exponent zero was replaced by one. | No: its coprimality hole is retained; primary-generator units are also retained. |
| Both projectors were called divisors of the row. | No: only the first is; the second count is paid with both allocation scalars. |
| Finite valuation checks do not cover arbitrary multiplicities. | Correct concern, answered by the support Rankin bound and explicit missing-radical count. |
| Smaller actual canonical width invalidates the nominal defect budget. | Resolved by the inequality in Section 5, valid also for negative width difference. |
| Fourier separation independently repeats each label count. | No: common majorant and diagonal contractions preserve the joint norm. |
| The advertised main radius is only an upper-bound change. | No: the exact pinned `mainCommonRadius/main_energy_common` constructs and dominates the chosen smooth ball. |
| Amplification errors are absorbed as an arbitrarily small power despite fixed `a`. | No: their positive numerical margins, normalized average and exceptional margins are explicitly paid. |
| Mesh depends on the target's height degree, destroying the common endpoint strip. | No such dependence is necessary; only the later height exponent/orders/threshold do. The compact normalized interface in Section 9 must be preserved. |
| Supporting component checks establish the endpoint. | They do not. This is a written source-relative local proof; endpoint assembly and formal replay have distinct statuses. |

No narrow mathematical repair was required for the head reviewed. Some invalid shortcuts above are already explicitly corrected in that head, including the second-projector distinction and the exact `-4a` exceptional equality. Those corrections should not be reverted during integration. A rigorous acceptance of the new **global constant** still requires the endpoint lane's complete weighted/shortened-scale/continuation bridge, source-preserving integration, and the controller's overall assessment. A clean full formalization/checker receipt would be stronger independent evidence, but its current absence is not a refutation of this written proof.

The next mathematical action is to compose this exact local theorem with the endpoint lane's fixed original slot system and target-uniform continuation, keeping Section 9's quantifier order explicit. There is no justification to generalize the local theorem to growing parent conductor, arbitrary coefficients, arbitrary global length geometry, or a union of unrelated translates in one eligibility bin.

## 2. Primitive Poisson and both orientations

For each actual pair define psi(u)=chi_n(u)^e conjugate(chi_n'(u)^e). At every good prime of nn', its local exponent is 1 or 5. Thus psi is primitive and nonprincipal on its full good conductor nn'. In particular it is not principalized by the fact that some individual inducing row may have a principal character.

The finite identity

    1_(u sixth-power-free)=sum_(a^6|u) mu(a)

is used on the original nonzero row support. Setting u=a^6 z leaves the exact natural mask (a,nn')=1 and row scale U_a=U/q_a^6. The original ball gives q_a<<U^(1/6). Extending z to include zero in Poisson is harmless because psi(0)=0. It does not delete any original nonzero row.

For a primitive character and the prescribed additive pairing, the finite Fourier transform is

    sum_(x mod nn') psi(x)e(ell x/(nn'))
       =sqrt(q_n q_n') gamma(psi;nn') conjugate(psi(ell)). (R2)

It is zero when ell shares any good conductor prime, including ell=0. This is a zero, not a square-root gcd loss. In particular a fixed original slot prime dividing ell kills the term.

The CRT factor is worth computing rather than inferring from a norm. With x=n' y+n y', it is

    chi_n(n')^e chi_n'(n)^(-e)=R(n,n'),                 (R3)

where R is the fixed ray sign of B1.1-B1.5. Sextic reciprocity makes the ratio a sign, and e=1 or -1 gives the same sign. There is no additional variable cubic phase between the two copies.

Put a0(n)=conjugate(alpha(n)) gamma_2(n). B1.10 gives

    mu(n)gamma_1(n)=conjugate(a0(n))G(n),
    mu(n)gamma_-1(n)=a0(n)chi_n(-1)conjugate(G(n)).     (R4)

Consequently, before the finite ray expansion, the exact arithmetic factor from the two mu signs, Gauss sum and dual character is

    e=-1:
      R(n,n') chi_n(-1) conjugate(G(n))G(n')
        *a0(n)conjugate(a0(n'))chi_n(ell)conjugate(chi_n'(ell));
    e=+1:
      R(n,n') G(n)conjugate(G(n'))chi_n'(-1)
        *conjugate(a0(n))a0(n')conjugate(chi_n(ell))chi_n'(ell). (R5)

The source factor nu(n)conjugate(nu(n')) is still present. G, chi_n(-1) and R are fixed ray data, so their finite expansion produces a finite sum of separated column factors. It does not exchange W1 with W2 or either of their height coordinates.

Fixed ray/unit row restrictions do not spoil (R2). One can see this directly by combining the good conductor c=nn' with a coprime fixed S-supported modulus m0. CRT factors the finite transform of psi times any fixed m0-periodic row function into the primitive good transform and a bounded fixed-modulus transform. The good factor is still zero at a frequency divisible by a good prime. Factors involving c modulo m0, and psi(m0), belong to a finite dictionary and separate between n and n'. After u=a^6 z the periodic row function may also depend on a's fixed residue class; retain that class or its bounded coefficient. This has a fixed cost, not a power of q_a. Clearing the fixed dual denominator must rescale the cutoff with its fixed comparison constant. The author defines the cutoff on the actual fixed dual lattice, which avoids an equality claim between two differently normalized cutoffs.

The original pair coefficient contributes N0^(-1); primitive Poisson contributes U_a/sqrt(q_n q_n'). Their product is

    U_a/N0^2 * [N0/sqrt(q_n q_n')].                    (R6)

The bracket is part of the smooth profile on the original compact normalized source supports. The radial kernel keeps its exact argument U_a q_ell/(q_n q_n'), with the prescribed fixed factors. It is not replaced by a hard support condition.

Define R_unique,<=Y by the literal condition 0<q_ell<=Y in this exact expansion, where Y is fixed before live a,ell,n,n', slots or height suprema. The complementary dual sum is retained in full. Pair transposition and complete conjugation preserve this radial frequency condition; hence the scalar pieces can be made real without positivity. This is not signed-subset norm monotonicity.

## 8. Existing large-cube branch, with its all-marked physical map

For completeness, the external all-source large-cube estimate also has a direct coefficient-preserving transfer. Here is the short proof needed to use its actual tails and marks.

For fixed squareful \(u\), use (XM17) with ordinary completion \(\sqrt{h_{\rm act}}\), and retain
\[
h_{\rm act}\le q_tR_u C N\ll YCN/(D_uE_u).
\]
The Gauss amplitude and principal divisor sum are at most
\[
D_u\sqrt{q_tR_u}\sum_{f\mid\mathfrak e_u}q_f
\ll (YT)^\eta\sqrt{YD_uE_u}.
\]
Their product with completion is therefore at most
\((YT)^\eta Y\sqrt{CN}\), independently of \(u\). There are \(O(YC/U)\) source/core pairs and \(O(N)\) cube labels. Multiplying their coefficients gives
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N;u}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
\frac{C\sqrt{YN}}U.
\]
The series \(\sum_{u\ {\rm squareful}}U^{-1}\) converges, proving
\[
|\mathcal M_{C,N}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta
C\sqrt{YN}
\asymp(1+|v|)^{J_0}(YT)^\eta T\sqrt Y\,N^{-5/2}.
\tag{XM35}
\]
This proof retains every source power.

Restrict \(q_J\ge N_0\ge1\), with \(N_0\) polynomial in \(Z\). The sum of \(N^{-5/2}\) over cube dyads \(N\gtrsim N_0\) is \(O(N_0^{-5/2})\). Summing \(T\) against (XM28), using the version of (XM29) with one extra factor \(T\), gives
\[
|\mathcal M_{D;\,q_J\ge N_0}|
\ll (1+|v|)^{J_0}Z^\epsilon
N_D\sqrt{Y_D}\,N_0^{-5/2}.
\tag{XM36}
\]
There is no assumption that the original Gaussian is compactly supported near \(N_D\).

Since \(N_Dq_D\asymp ZL\), multiplication by the physical branch factor and summation using (XM33) yield
\[
\boxed{
|I^{\rm comp}_{q_J\ge N_0}|
\ll_\epsilon Z^\epsilon
\frac{ZL\sqrt Y}{\sqrt Q\,N_0^{5/2}}.
}
\tag{XM37}
\]
In particular it costs \(Z^\epsilon\sqrt{Q/Y}B_{\rm tar}\) when
\[
N_0\gtrsim (ZLY/(QB_{\rm tar}))^{2/5}.
\tag{XM38}
\]
If the right side is below one, take \(N_0=1\). The low-active and large-cube sectors can be combined by disjointizing their intersection, because both proofs allow bounded row-independent label masks.

statement:
## G109. Fixed countable banks, exact buffering and the complete source

Let lambda_j>1, w_j>0 and 0<W=sum_j w_j<infinity be fixed. Write
ell_j=log(lambda_j), r_j=exp(-delta ell_j), for delta>=0, and

    F_delta(t)=sum_j w_j |1-r_j exp(-it ell_j)|^2,
    A(delta)=sum_j w_j (1-r_j)^2.

Both sums converge uniformly in real t by domination with 4w_j. Exactly

    F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      =2 sum_j w_j r_j (1-cos(t ell_j)) >=0.             (75.1)

For any finite head of length r and integers H,L>=1, divide the unit
r-torus into H^r boxes. Two of the H^r+1 points nL(ell_1,...,ell_r)/(2pi)
modulo1 lie in the same box. Their difference gives t=Lq with
L<=t<=L H^r and distance(t ell_j/(2pi),Z)<=1/H for every j<=r.
Consequently, uniformly for delta>=0,

    0<=F_delta(t)-A(delta)
      <=4pi^2 W_head/H^2+4W_tail.                      (75.2)

Given any fixed T>=0, first take L>=max(1,ceil(T)), then a sufficiently
small full tail and sufficiently large H. Equations75.1-2 prove

    inf_(t>=T) F_delta(t)=A(delta).                    (75.3)

This uses no independence assumption on the logarithms. It keeps every
channel and never changes character to manufacture adverse phases. The
principal character modulo1 already defeats a shortcut required for all
ordinary characters. Arbitrarily prescribed complex target phases on
related scales are outside this identity-target recurrence proof. The
large bound L H^r gives no useful arithmetic power estimate in height.

At delta=0 the infimum is zero. At delta>0 it is positive and also equals
F_delta(0). Dominated convergence gives A(delta)->0 as delta decreases
to zero. Furthermore,

    A(delta)/delta^2 -> sum_j w_j (log lambda_j)^2,

where the limit may be +infinity. For a finite second log moment use
dominated convergence; otherwise arbitrarily large finite partial moments
force the liminf to infinity. Summability alone does not supply a finite
quadratic coefficient or a universal decay rate. For lambda_j=2^j,
w_j=2^-j, j>=1, the exact checks are A(1)=10/21 and second log moment
6(log2)^2.

On the global space L2(R_+,x^(-2sigma) dx/x), put sigma=beta+delta and
D_j V(x)=V(x)-lambda_j^beta V(x/lambda_j). The unitary logarithmic change
f(u)=exp(-sigma u)V(exp u), Tonelli and Plancherel give

    sum_j w_j ||D_j V||_global^2 >= A(delta)||V||_global^2.

Continuity of the uniformly convergent symbol and localized Fourier
packets show sharpness, also near arbitrarily high near-minimizers.
These are unrestricted test functions, not arithmetic sources. A single
point frequency is not a nonzero L2 extremizer. The theorem is not an
exact constant for a joint physical-shell norm, nor for a sum of separate
shell suprema. Those distinctions from G52/Sol03 remain essential.

### Formation is paid for the actual Gaussian source

Fix tau>0 and the normalized Gaussian g_tau(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)
exp(-v^2/(2tau)). Let

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), U(y)=sum_n a(n)g_tau(log(n/y)).

For any A>max(1,beta), the elementary bound |a(n)|<=1 proves for all y>0

    |U(y)|<=C_A y^A,
    C_A=zeta(A)(2pi tau)^(-1/2) exp(tau A^2/2).

Indeed n^A g_tau(log(n/y)) is at most y^A times the supremum of
exp(Av)g_tau(v), and sum_n n^-A=zeta(A). Hence |D_j U(x)|<=2C_A x^A
uniformly in j, since lambda_j^(beta-A)<=1. In particular

    sum_(j>r) w_j |D_j U(x)|^2 <=4C_A^2 x^(2A) W_tail.

The entire bank is therefore well defined locally and on every finite
shell, with its complete tail paid. This closes the source-formation
qualification in the shared review. It supplies only an exponent A>1;
the desired subtrivial arithmetic moment remains OPEN.

### Endpoint correction: gamma=beta is admissible

Suppose the COMPLETE bank obeys, for every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently
large dyadic X,

    sum_j w_j integral_X^(2X) |D_j U(x)|^2 dx/x
      =O_(chi,epsilon)(X^(2gamma+epsilon)),
    0<gamma<1, beta<=gamma.                            (75.4)

Choose one fixed channel with positive weight. For every sigma>gamma,
choose epsilon<2(sigma-gamma). Dyadic covering, finite initial shells
and the preceding all-y bound give its finite N_sigma norm, where
N_sigma(V)=sup_(X>0) X^-sigma ||V||_[X,2X]. Since sigma>beta, its causal
inverse converges geometrically, with cost

    w_j^(-1/2)/(1-lambda_j^(beta-sigma)).

The K-th telescoping remainder is lambda_j^((K+1)beta)
U(x/lambda_j^(K+1)), bounded by C_A x^A
lambda_j^(-(K+1)(A-beta)); it tends to zero. Thus (75.4) returns the
same every-epsilon exponent gamma for U, INCLUDING gamma=beta.
The inverse constant may diverge as sigma approaches beta; that is
permitted in an every-epsilon conclusion. No inverse at sigma=beta is
asserted. This corrects the shared review's unnecessarily strict beta<gamma.

The direct Mellin check gives the same result: the numerator of this
channel is (1-lambda_j^(beta-s)) exp(tau s^2/2), which has no zero in
Re(s)>gamma when gamma>=beta. Its transform is holomorphic there under
the complete shell hypothesis and the paid left tail, so the reciprocal-L
identity excludes every zero in that half-plane. For gamma<beta one
channel leaves numerator zeros on Re(s)=beta. Two multiplicatively
independent scales leave a possible simple real zero at beta; the existing
G47 exception must still be addressed. No automatic stronger family
theorem follows.

The live alternatives outside the obstruction are height-dependent or

## Fixed powers below one half

Fix 1/3<rho_0<=rho<=rho_1<1/2, tau>0, and a buffered Mertens
exponent 1/2<beta<1 with sum_(n<=u)mu(n)=O_beta(u^beta). The retained
baseline permits beta=.8749; the new accepted endpoint permits any
fixed beta>.874872. Put L=log X, delta=(1-2rho_1)/4 and
eta=delta(1-beta)>0. Then

    R_(X^rho)(x)=C_f e^(tau/2) B(rho) x/L^3
                       +O(X/L^4+X^(1-eta)L),
    C_f=9log2 product_(p>=5)(1-1/(p-1)^2)>0,
    B(rho)=2log((1-rho)/rho)-2/(1-rho)-1/(1-rho)^2.

B is strictly negative and decreasing on (1/3,1/2). Hence the band
T_(X^b)-T_(X^a), for fixed 1/3<a<b<1/2, is positive with leading
coefficient C_f e^(tau/2)[B(a)-B(b)]. For a=3/8,b=2/5 this difference
is exactly 79/225+2log(10/9)>0. The complete terminal complement at
any fixed rho_plus>1/2 is O_A(X^-A), so the band from such a fixed a
to rho_plus is negative of order X/L^3. Signs of individual threshold
jumps have not been proved.

The mechanism is source-specific. Its Euler series is H(s)/zeta(s),
where H has absolutely summable coefficients for Re(s)>1/2 and a
simple zero from p=2 at s=1. Transferring the buffered mu-Mertens
bound through its actual convolution proves the f partial-sum bound.
The reciprocal series consequently has a double zero at1, giving
ordinary-order signed core moments 0,0,2C_f. It is not legitimate to
derive these partial sums merely by inverting a Gaussian norm bound.

Below a fixed power U<z^3 the original source has exactly n=rpq,
p<q both greater than z, each of valuation one, r<z, coefficient f(r).
Outside U the completed formula can fail; its full divisor-weighted
Gaussian tail is paid. Signed Abel summation removes r>X^delta before
prime-density substitution. The p=q correction and both sharp PNT
endpoints are paid. Two sequential fixed-order Stieltjes replacements
give the exact unordered density phi_t(A)=A^-1 log((A-t)/t), A>2t.
The Taylor remainder and its derivative are summed by signed Abel,
not an unsigned harmonic bound. The resulting C_f phi_t'' gives B.
The complete proofs price every source-completion and reciprocal-core
tail before reading off its sign.

The compact rho interval is fixed. No uniformity at rho=1/3, at
rho=1/2, or through a moving transition is asserted. In particular
[research revision]'s negative subpower bands cannot be extrapolated into this
positive fixed-power band range.

## 5. Independent protected audit X23: an exact divisor Bellman contract

This audit was selected from the original seed before outcomes. It is separate from the author's six tests. Set a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), c(n)=chi(n), so a*c=delta on all integers, including ramified zeros and all prime powers. The exact sequential recurrence is

    a(1)=1; a(n)=-sum_(d|n,d<n)a(d)chi(n/d).

Let x_n=(a(1),...,a(n)) and let T_n append that divisor row to x_(n-1). Its entries are literally -chi(n/d)1_(d|n), not unsigned incidence weights. With ell_N=(1,...,1), M_chi(N)=ell_N x_N.

For Hermitian matrices P_n>=0, possibly depending on N, a complete Bellman certificate consists of

    P_N>=ell_N*ell_N,
    T_n*P_nT_n<=P_(n-1)+E_n.                         (R17)

The E_n may be Hermitian signed debts. Evaluating on the actual source and telescoping gives

    |M_chi(N)|^2<=x_1*P_1x_1
                      +sum_(n=2)^N x_(n-1)*E_n x_(n-1).     (R18)

The whole actual right side must be bounded. Replacing every debt by a positive bound is a sufficient but possibly wasteful choice, not part of the identity. A bound O_(chi,epsilon)(N^(2gamma+epsilon)) for every epsilon and all N returns M=O(N^(gamma+epsilon)) after relabeling epsilon. Abel/Mellin continuation of sum mu(n)chi(n)n^-s then excludes L-zeros in Re s>gamma at every height; the principal pole is matched by a zero of the reciprocal. The same gamma is required for every fixed ordinary chi. No cancellation is proved merely by writing(R17).

The seed specifically proposes testing only reachable states. For that formulation, it is enough to require each inequality in(R17) after evaluation on the actual x_(n-1), and the terminal inequality only on x_N; the identical telescoping proof gives(R18). Global matrix inequalities are a stronger sufficient certificate, not an inferred property of the reachable set. Even a diagonal terminal form can then escape the quadratic global price below: at N=2,chi=1, x=(1,-1) has output0, so the zero form is sufficient on that state. The uninformative choice D=|M_chi(N)|^2 I/K also has the exact reachable energy but already requires the unknown output. A finite usable description of reachability and a noncircular signed bound remain the live high-ceiling part of X23.

The exact no-debt backward metric is instructive. Define a row, for d<=n,

    w_(N,n)(d)=sum_(j<=n/d)chi(j) M_chi(floor(N/(dj))).       (R19)

To verify it without missing a tail, start from an arbitrary prefix x_1,...,x_n. Set b(k)=sum_(d|k)x_d chi(k/d) for k<=n and b(k)=0 for k>n. The continuation is b*(mu chi), and its sum through N is sum_(k<=n)b(k)M_chi(floor(N/k)). Reordering gives(R19). Hence w_(N,N)=ell_N, w_(N,n-1)=w_(N,n)T_n, and w_(N,1)=M_chi(N). The matrices P_n=w_(N,n)*w_(N,n) satisfy(R17) with E_n=0, but P_1=|M_chi(N)|^2. This exact certificate is circular unless constructed/bounded by new arithmetic information. It shows precisely where the full signed response resides.

A concrete restricted class already has exponent-two cost. Even remove every forced-zero coordinate at the terminal time: I={n<=N:mu(n)chi(n)!=0}, K=|I|. Every remaining actual source coordinate has modulus1. A positive diagonal D dominating ell_I*ell_I must satisfy sum_(i in I)1/d_i<=1. Consequently its actual terminal energy is sum_i d_i>=K^2; equality is attained by d_i=K. Natural zeros do not erase this cost. Direct squarefree counting gives

    K=kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N),
    kappa_q=1/zeta(2) product_(p|q)(1+1/p)^-1>0.      (R20)

Indeed sum_(d<=sqrt N,(d,q)=1)mu(d) times the number of q-units m<=N/d^2 gives the formula; the coprime-prefix error and the convergent d^-2 tail each cost O_q(sqrt N). Thus a diagonal terminal majorant on this active subspace costs Theta_q(N^2). This is NOT a lower bound on |M_chi(N)|^2 or on every reachable/source-specific Bellman certificate. Signed off-diagonal geometry remains live. It is the actual divisor-source specialization of the known U-VARIATIONAL/W38 magnitude-only SDP obstruction, with the exact adjoint response and conditional return now stated.

statement:
## 4. CU: exact sixth-power holes and the clipped repetition sum

Write uniquely (Delta*ell)=kappa*t^3*z^6 with kappa cubefree and t squarefree. Primewise the exponents are

    v_kappa=v_ell mod3,
    v_t=floor(v_ell/3) mod2,
    v_z=floor(v_ell/6),

where v_ell here means v(Delta*ell). They need NOT have disjoint support. A prime of valuation4 occurs in both kappa and t; valuation10 occurs in all three. The exact identity is

    chi_m(ell)^eta = fixed_Delta_unit_factor
       *chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1).        (V7)

The quadratic factor is real, so its exponent is unchanged for eta=-1. The last factor cannot be replaced by one: at a good source prime p with valuation6 in (Delta*ell), the local kappa and t valuations are zero and the z valuation is one. The original local factor is zero, while dropping the z-hole would give one. Fixed-place factors do not change this local counterexample. This is the first decisive obstruction to an incautious repeated-row argument.

Fix kappa AND z before averaging t. The inner coefficient is c_f(m)chi_m(kappa)^eta 1_((m,z)=1), with any fixed Delta/unit factor. It remains squarefree, satisfies (V3), and is independent of live t. An overlap with t remains the quadratic symbol's own zero; overlaps among kappa,t,z impose no additional mask. The outer common f-hole is retained independently.

The primary [Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642), dated 31 May 2012, allows arbitrary inner coefficients for a quadratic Hecke family, with BOTH ideal variables squarefree, and price M+N up to a subpower. Its family hypotheses include primitivity, trivial infinite type, finite-group reciprocity, and the primitive product conductor for coprime equal-class indices. PR9 B2.24 supplies the actual family check: the lambda sign correction, its primitive inducing convention, fixed primary square classes modulo4, and ray reciprocity. These are retained source assumptions, not replaced by a generic power-symbol analogy. Finite class splitting and transpose duality identify the present m,t orientation.

More explicitly, PR9's character on an ideal (x) is vartheta_m((x))=epsilon_lambda(x)^(e(m)) (x/m)_2, with e(m)=(q_m-1)/2 modulo2 and primitive conductor m*lambda^(e(m)). After fixed S-parts are removed, the difference from chi_m(t)^3 is precisely this lambda unit factor. Splitting e(m) and the fixed ray classes makes it an outer t factor of modulus one. Equal-class products cancel that lambda correction and have primitive good conductor equal to the product, as required. Neither an extra moving conductor cost nor a live-t coefficient is introduced.

The t-energy for q_t<=T0 is therefore <<H_J U^epsilon(T0+X). The independent pointwise input is G185 on the two original colors of ONE copy:

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].                        (V8)

The new z-hole splits between x,y and the ORIGINAL remaining slots; it does not create an arbitrary joint coefficient. Fixed kappa and other holes do the same. Thus (V8) applies after the exact conditioning in (V7), using the actual shortened colors on each side and their common S0 upper bound. Those two colors are not cross-copy products.

Set B=(H_A/q_kappa)^(1/3). For fixed z, T0=B/q_z^2; q_z<=sqrt(B) on every nonempty fiber, up to fixed support constants. Two available bounds are T0+X and T0*S0. For 1<=Z<=sqrt(B), ideal counting gives

    sum_(q_z<=Z)(B/q_z^2+X) << B+XZ,
    sum_(q_z>Z) B*S0/q_z^2 << B*S0/Z.                 (V9)

In particular XZ, the repeated-row price, has NOT disappeared. Put Z0=sqrt(B*S0/X). If 1<=Z0<=sqrt(B), balancing proves B+O(sqrt(B*S0*X)). If Z0<1, the all-pointwise price B*S0 is at most sqrt(B*S0*X). If Z0>sqrt(B), then S0>X, and the all-quadratic price B+Xsqrt(B) is at most B+sqrt(B*S0*X). This proves in every regime

    sum_(t,z) |B_f(kappa*t^3*z^6)|^2
       << H_J U^epsilon [B+sqrt(B*S0*X)].              (V10)

Thus no unproved S0<=X restriction is hidden in the choice of split. Coefficients are different for different z, which is permitted because each quadratic application fixes z; they are not different for live t. Any core priority selector remains an outer t restriction after kappa,z are fixed.

Sum cubefree kappa up to C. The powers q_kappa^(-1/3), q_kappa^(-1/6) give

    H_J U^epsilon [H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3)
                       +sqrt(S0*X)H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6)]. (V11)

A general divisor-bounded merged coefficient would give (V3) but would not necessarily give (V8). The cube proof genuinely uses both the arbitrary-sequence quadratic contract and the original-color pointwise structure.

## 1. The complete arithmetic average

Let R be the positive integers or the nonzero integral ideals of
K=Q(omega). Write q_a=a or Na, respectively. Fix tau>0, a finite prime set S,
and one ordinary Dirichlet character eta, or one finite-order,
trivial-infinity Hecke character. Retain the original zero extension.
For the sextic construction S includes the primes above6. Define

    U_Q(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,SQ)=1) g_tau(log(q_a/x)),
    U=U_1,  g_tau(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).       (R1)

Q denotes a finite radical outside S. All sums in this review are COMPLETE
Gaussian sums. Fix the label sets

    Fset={f squarefree: F<q_f<=2F, (f,S)=1},
    Eset={e: q_e<=E, (e,S)=1},
    P_FE(x)=(N_F N_E)^(-1) sum_(f,e) U_rad(fe)(x),              (R2)

with their exact positive cardinalities. Shared primes between f and e
are allowed, and e=1 is present. For large F,E, N_F~_S F,N_E~_S E.
The ideal count counts one ideal, not six associates.

For Q squarefree, put h(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-1),
D(Q)=prod_(p|Q)(1+q_p^-1)^(-1), and S_a(Q)=sum_(d|Q)q_d^-a.
The elementary ideal lattice count is

    A_K(T)=kappa T+O(sqrt(T)), kappa=pi/(3sqrt(3));
    A_Z(T)=T+O(1).

Inclusion-exclusion, then mu^2(a)=sum_(r^2|a)mu(r), gives uniformly in Q,
for T>=1,

    A_Q(T)=kappa T h(Q)+O(sqrt(T) S_1/2(Q))                  [K],
    A_Q^sf(T)=kappa T D(Q)/zeta_K(2)
                     +O(sqrt(T) log(2T) S_1/2(Q))          [K],
    A_Q(T)=T h(Q)+O(d(Q)),
    A_Q^sf(T)=T D(Q)/zeta(2)+O(sqrt(T) d(Q))                [Z]. (R3)

There is no Q<=T restriction. In the squarefree main term the factors
h(Q) prod_(p|Q)(1-q_p^-2)^(-1) are exactly D(Q).

Consequently the two avoidance probabilities for a fixed a have main terms

    A(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) q_p/(q_p+1),
    B(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S) (q_p-1)/q_p.

Their product is w(a)=prod_(p|a,p notin S)(q_p-1)/(q_p+1).
The errors after division by the EXACT sample counts are, respectively,
F^-1/2 log(2F) S_1/2(rad a), E^-1/2 S_1/2(rad a) over K;
F^-1/2 d(rad a), E^-1 d(rad a) over Z. Since all probabilities and
main terms lie in[0,1], the product error is bounded by the sum of the
two errors. No additional mixed error or independence of prime events is
assumed; independence here is simply the Cartesian choice of f and e.

With the ONE fixed field

    W(x)=sum_a mu_R(a)eta(a)1_((a,S)=1)w(a)g_tau(log(q_a/x)),

the full comparison is

    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x log(2F)(F^-1/2+E^-1/2)              [K],
    |P_FE(x)-W(x)| << x(1+log(2+x))(F^-1/2+E^-1)           [Z]. (R4)

These bounds include both infinite source ends and hold uniformly for x>0
when the label counts have reached their fixed-S asymptotic range. Indeed
sum_(q_a<=T) S_1/2(rad a)<<T and sum_(n<=T)d(rad n)<<T log(2T).
Gaussian integration gives the stated whole-source bounds; at x<1 the
left tail is smaller than every fixed power of x. The complete sources
also satisfy |U_Q(x)|<<x uniformly in Q by the absolute coefficient count.

Minor clarification1: the author's(A2) should explicitly say T>=1 or replace
log(2T) by log(2+T). No use in the report requires a logarithm of negative
sign at tiny T. The underlying A1 remains valid at T<1.
