## Group 1: free invention

**W41-01 | factorization noise spectrum | p=.045.** On a squarefree divisor cube, signed Mobius summation is its top Fourier coefficient. Bound that coefficient by repeatedly applying a noise derivative, and charge the complement by observed low-degree influence. Hope: a full signed moment bound with power saving, rather than positivity. First test: derive the exact cube identity with the actual arithmetic weights and determine the cost of exposing enough independent primes. Main danger: support masks put all their mass at top degree. Ceiling: a reusable power-saving signed estimate, potentially reaching 1/6 if quantitatively strong enough.

**W41-02 | jointly optimized zero witness | p=.21.** A hypothetical zero creates a family of correlated detector witnesses; optimize a single dual functional against all of them instead of bounding each separately. First test: formulate the finite Gram feasibility problem and ask whether the shared witness is actually smaller than individual worst cases. Bridge: prove every zero in the target strip yields a vector violating the same certified inequality. Danger: forbidden data-dependent coefficients or conductor constants. Reach: near gain without changing original transfer.

**W41-03 | signed boundary flux | p=.065.** Replace a large interior absolute moment by flux through a slightly enlarged contour, retaining cancellation between opposite faces. First test: an exact Green/Stokes identity for a finite Dirichlet polynomial and its signed fourth moment. Bridge: quantify enlargement and poles, then recover the original strip estimate. Danger: boundary flux has the same uncontrolled arithmetic correlations. Reach: .25 moment barrier bypass if signed flux has genuine decay.

**W41-04 | one-prime Schur complement | p=.16.** Isolate one prime's local factor as a rank-one update of a Dirichlet convolution inverse. Iterated Schur complements might retain cancellation hidden by a global norm. First test: write the exact block inverse on squarefree divisors of three primes. Bridge: a uniformly convergent inverse implies zero exclusion through a proved identity. Danger: local conditioning costs accumulate like the full Euler product. Reach: 1/6 or 1/4 through a new inverse architecture.

**W41-05 | moving cutoff compensation | p=.12.** Couple two neighboring cutoff values so the difficult shell appears with opposite signs and the core remains stable. First test: derive the differentiated moment in the cutoff parameter without dropping zero extensions. Bridge: integrate the differential inequality and pay both endpoint shells. Danger: a true inequality cannot gain just by renaming a positive boundary mass. Reach: small rigorous improvement if the bottleneck is endpoint loss.

# [research revision] independent headroom review — bounded partial audit



## 1. Decision and limits

The inspected proof supports the author's moving-product completion, its
uniform small-row estimate, the bounded signed bank's projected semiprime
obstruction, and fixed-depth compensator deflation at their stated scopes.
I found no consequential analytic gap in those reconstructed arguments.
The actual full signed long-factor core remains unbounded at a useful power;
there is no new zero-free constant. The current comparison remains
c11 = 312864909/2500000000 = .1251459636, theta = .8748540364, with inherited
F0, positive-slot, and external-admission obligations open.

There is a substantive reviewer addition: the projected bank obstruction can
be made uniform in an arbitrary finite, X-dependent number of cuts, provided
the total variation of the signed weights stays bounded. Section 6 records
the endpoint-variation proof developed during this review. It still gives no
lower bound for the complete signed bank. Root must independently assess this
addition before canonical acceptance.

This is a **partial audit**, not a claim that every requested check finished.
The entire frozen author report, manifest, assignment, and source-evidence
file were read. The exact row-prefix algebra and the consequential arguments
below were independently reconstructed. The author helper and its numerical
receipt were not read or rerun; the newest full research index was not
re-audited in this pass; the new outside ancestry source was not independently
opened. Those omissions remain explicit. No finite computational check is
being represented as a proof.

## 2. Frozen intake and evidence

Author scope: `[restricted provenance path] research revision]-drafts/headroom/`. Author mathematical freeze:
2026-10-12T19:17:57.593980Z. Its original 19:10 deadline was missed. The author
reported normal own release in 824bc6 and absence in 1d40e0 at 19:18:28Z.
No author file was changed, and its writer helper was not executed.

| File | Bytes | SHA-256 |
|---|---:|---|
| report.md | 30810 | 623d3bbfb43cf193a3984e289aaae50c740deb7b1c9ff0dcc334004f0d2a81b5 |
| check.py | 7284 | 4be44a0d026e21e12fd304ea05695a61c5c3b2b1469dc4c6af30e59ce5563318 |
| checks.json | 14545 | d0d861a67ea242e2cae6216dbd8cc88d0752bff27887f10add23edbeca763a7a |
| source-evidence.json | 3134 | ec2cc1789c70a3dfde6589cdc0bd2aca5cc1ea6be2fc7e9a49019cdc781e9654 |
| freeze.json | 3321 | 89496e995c42f6da1fb7743b55b1ffb593c7442929e6f4cdc66f1bd54064d2ee |

Completed reads: assignment/manifest ce3b35; full report ccd7cb, e36f9a,
20bf10; source-evidence 2b8f4b. Own claim bdb738 was acquired at 19:19:23Z. Before the third
recovery only the 1770-byte worklog and own claim had survived on disk.

The outside Helfgott–Thompson paper is used by the author for ancestry of
product-dependent decompositions, not for a new analytic estimate. I have
read the author's source contract but have not independently checked that
ancestry claim against the publisher in this pass. The Ramaré–Zuniga Alterman
and Matomäki–Teräväinen sources supply no imported power estimate here.
The ordinary prime number theorem used below is the same classical input
already inspected in the preceding review. No prime progression theorem,
short-interval power saving, growing-conductor theorem, or GRH input is used.
Novelty below means useful new structure in this project record, not a
literature priority claim.

## 3. Exact moving cuts and the small-source estimate

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q with its natural zeros,
and a prime p not dividing q. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), h(n)=chi(n),
q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p, c_p=q_p*a, and b_p=q_p*h. Then

    b_p(l) = chi(l)(1-p 1_{p|l}).

It has period Q=pq and zero mean. The sum over a period equals
p(1-chi(p)) times the character sum modulo q, which is zero for a
nonprincipal character and also zero for a principal character because
chi(p)=1. All squareful terms introduced by the compensator remain present.
The coefficients of c_p are bounded by p+1.

Fix 1/2<gamma<1, integer k>2, 1<b<=2gamma, and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), L=X^gamma, M=X^r,
    eta=1/(100kpq), B(n)=min(L,eta X^k/n^(k-1)).

For tau=tau_X in [0,1] fixed before the shell variable x is chosen, set
U(n)=B(n)^tau and V(n)=B(n)^(1-tau). Use B^0=1, including when B<1.
For each physical integer n, freeze these two numbers before applying the
ordinary convolution identity. This yields the exact coefficient identity

    c_p(n)=Q_U(n)+Q_V(n)-S_tau(n)+R_tau(n),

where Q_U(n)=sum_{de=n}q_p(e)a(d)1_{d<=U(n)}, Q_V is analogous, and

    S_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n; d<=U(n),e<=V(n)} a(d)a(e)b_p(l),
    R_tau(n)=sum_{de l=n; d>U(n),e>V(n)} a(d)a(e)b_p(l).

This is a coefficientwise identity, not one convolution with globally fixed
cutoffs. Ordered pairs, strict complements, and both endpoints tau=0,1
must be retained. It remains valid for B<1. At interior tau and B<1 the
small sums disappear and R is the complete coefficient; at endpoint tau the
cutoff equal to one must still be treated literally.

For f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k), x in the full real shell [X,2X], the two
short sums have total absolute bound
(p+1)(floor(L^tau)+floor(L^(1-tau))) <<_p L.

The moving small source has the stronger full pointwise bound

    |sum_n S_tau(n)f_x(n)| <<_{p,q,k} L,

uniformly in tau and real x. Here is the decisive row calculation. For
0<tau<1, a contributing ordered pair satisfies d<=L^tau, e<=L^(1-tau).
Write W=max(d^(1/tau),e^(1/(1-tau))). Then de<=W<=L, and its exact allowed
l-values form the single prefix

    l <= (eta X^k/W)^(1/(k-1))/(de).

For tau=0 one has d=1,W=e; for tau=1 one has e=1,W=d. These are genuine
endpoint formulas, not limiting conventions that discard a row.

Expand the zero-mean periodic b_p into its nonzero Fourier modes. In each
mode the real phase divided by 2pi is

    F(t)=jt/Q-(de t/x)^k/(2pi),  1<=j<=Q-1.

On the whole permitted row, de(de t)^(k-1)<=eta X^k. Consequently the
negative correction to F' has magnitude at most k eta/(2pi), and the
monotone discrete phase increments stay a fixed distance at least 1/(2Q)
from the integers. The elementary discrete first-derivative estimate gives
an O_Q(1) bound for every undamped prefix. Abel summation against the actual
decreasing damping exp(-de t/x^b) preserves O_Q(1). There are at most
floor(L^tau)floor(L^(1-tau))<=L rows. This proves the assertion. An alias
region has not been discarded: coefficients outside the permitted small
prefix belong to the exact R complement.

This is more than a relabeling of a norm: it pays the actual small source
uniformly with moving product cuts. It does not estimate the remaining
arithmetic cancellation in R.

## 4. Whole complement and zero-exclusion return

The elementary divisor bound |R_tau(n)| <<_p tau_3(n) is uniform in X,tau.
The part n<=L costs O_delta(L^(1+delta)). For the whole tail n>M the earlier
accepted nonlinear tail lemma gives, for |v_n|<=A_delta n^delta,

    ||sum_{n>M}v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2 [X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)],

when 2delta<k-2. Norms use dx/x on [X,2X]. This is the whole-tail statement
with a smooth positive shell majorant and two integrations by parts; both
off-diagonal orientations are included. It is not an estimate of only a
separated tail cell. Since b<=2gamma and k+(2-k)r=2gamma, choose delta after
epsilon to pay this tail at X^(gamma+epsilon). The triangle inequality for
the complete sums also pays their interactions with the retained core.

Thus, with the literal finite core

    T_tau(x)=sum_{L<n<=M} R_tau(n)f_x(n),

the conclusion is

    ||C_p-T_tau||_j <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),  j=1,2,
    C_p(x)=sum_n c_p(n)f_x(n),

uniform in tau. The adaptive complement theorem needs no additional u>0
condition. The number u=2gamma-r matters for comparisons with the old
constant cuts and for whole-core support of the deflation statement.

For tau=1 put h_p=q_p-b_p. Then h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p); away from the
two point corrections it equals -chi(j)(1-p1_{p|j}), with |h_p|<=p-1.
The core can be written exactly as

    sum_{L<n=dj<=M; d>B(n),j>=2} mu(d)chi(d) h_p(j) f_x(n).

Its cofactor cutoff is strict:

    j < n/B(n) = max(n/X^gamma,n^k/(eta X^k)).

The switch occurs at n*=eta^(1/(k-1)) X^((k-gamma)/(k-1)). At n comparable
to X the allowed cofactor length is O(X^(1-gamma)); the far endpoint still
has the old scale. The comparison of adaptive and constant-cut cores is a
comparison of complete signed sources with paid complements, not monotonicity
of norms under taking subsets.

The return is conditional on a complete every-epsilon, every-large-shell
L1 bound for T (or the stronger L2 bound) at the stated exponent, for a fixed
covering pair of unramified compensator primes. At b=3/2,k=6 the Mellin
extraction already established in the earlier nonlinear review is

    H_p(s)=Gamma(s/6) exp(-i pi s/12) P_p(s)/(6 L(s,chi))+E_p(s),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),   E_p holomorphic for Re(s)>1/2.

The small-x exponential decay is paid. Shell summation gives holomorphy on
Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly at every finite height. The gamma multiplier
has no zeros there. Two fixed unramified primes prevent numerator masking:
their possible common zeros lie on Re(s)=1, and a nonzero common height
would force a rational ratio log(p1)/log(p2). At height zero choose a prime
with chi(p)!=1 for a nonprincipal character. The principal pole at s=1 is
an allowed exception. Natural zeros of imprimitive L-functions stay in the
statement; conductor-uniform extension is not asserted.

For general fixed b>1 the continuation must retain every shifted reciprocal
in the finite expansion. Choose fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma; the j-th term
contains P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi), with its actual coefficient.
Descending-strip induction, not deletion of these terms, supplies the return.
No growing K or growing k is justified by this argument.

The candidate numerical targets remain conditional. For k=6 the rows are
(gamma,r,u)=(.8748,1.0626,.687), (5/6,13/12,7/12), and
(3/4,9/8,3/8), corresponding to c=.1252,1/6,1/4. The present work proves
none of their required full signed core bounds.

## 5. What the author's bank obstruction actually proves

For a principal character, take a normalized signed bank with cuts tau_j,
weights lambda_j, sum lambda_j=1 and sum |lambda_j|<=Lambda, and initially
fixed cardinality J. Cutoffs and weights may depend on X but not on x.
The paid complement remains uniform with an extra factor Lambda.

For distinct unramified primes n=rs comparable to X, B(n)=L for all large X.
The only long-long factorizations are (r,s,1) and (s,r,1), including the
endpoint cuts because their long inequalities are strict. Put c=1-gamma,
t_j=gamma tau_j and alpha=log r/log X. The ideal coefficient profile is

    F(alpha)=sum_j lambda_j [1_{t_j<alpha<t_j+c}
                       +1_{gamma-t_j<alpha<1-t_j}].

It is symmetric under alpha -> 1-alpha, bounded by 2Lambda, and its
signed integral on [0,1] is exactly 2c. This integral cannot be replaced by
an integral of absolute weights. With delta=c/(4Lambda), the central left
half has integral of Re F at least c/2. The set where Re F>=c/2 in
[delta,1/2] has measure at least m=c/(8Lambda).

With fixed J the at most 4J breakpoints supply an interval of fixed positive
length where F is constant and its real part is positive. Trim its ends
before inserting the O(1/log X) displacement in log s/log X. Ordinary PNT
then supplies >> X/log X actual distinct prime products in that interval,
uniformly for exponents in a fixed compact subset of (0,1/2). Their phase
on the whole shell lies in a fixed short arc and damping is positive. Rotate
the fixed complex coefficient if necessary. The selected projection has
both L1 and L2 norm >> X/log X.

This is a lower bound for a specifically selected positive semiprime
projection. It is not a lower bound for the full signed core, a larger box,
or the sum of all projected pieces. Cross-piece cancellation is exactly the
unpaid possibility. The same distinction applies to all lower bounds below.

## 6. Reviewer addition: bounded variation suffices without fixed J

Here is the completed refinement from the pre-deadline proof reconstruction.
Let J=J_X be any finite number, keeping sum lambda_j=1 and
sum |lambda_j|<=Lambda with Lambda fixed. Retain the same principal-character
source, fixed gamma,k,p,q, and moving-cut definition. There is a selection
of semiprimes in the literal core for which the bank projection still has
norm >>_{gamma,Lambda,k,p,q} X/log X, uniformly in J_X and the bank data.

Proof. Use F,delta,m from Section 5. Define a positive endpoint measure

    nu=sum_j |lambda_j|(delta_{t_j}+delta_{t_j+c}
                            +delta_{gamma-t_j}+delta_{1-t_j}).

Its total mass is at most 4Lambda. For any two arguments the change in F
is bounded by the nu-mass between them, including endpoints. If
kappa=log(n/X)/log X, the actual coefficient G(alpha,kappa) is obtained by
shifting each of the two upper endpoints by kappa. Hence, for |kappa|<=h,

    |G(alpha,kappa)-F(alpha)| <= nu([alpha-h,alpha+h]).

Choose h=c^2/(4096Lambda^2) and a fixed grid of cells of length h. Discard
the terminal strip [1/2-m/4,1/2] and the at most two partially intersecting
boundary cells of [delta,1/2-m/4]. Mark a full grid cell bad when the nu-mass
of its enlargement by h on both sides is greater than c/8. A point belongs
to at most four such closed enlarged cells. Therefore the sum of these
masses is at most 16Lambda, there are at most 128Lambda/c bad cells, and
their total length is at most c/(32Lambda)=m/4.

The good set E={alpha in [delta,1/2]: Re F(alpha)>=c/2} has measure at least
m. The discarded and bad portions have total length at most m/2+2h<m.
There is therefore a full good grid cell I containing some alpha_0 in E.
For every alpha in I the variation of F is at most c/8, and for every
|kappa|<=h the additional displacement error is at most c/8. Thus

    Re G(alpha,kappa)>=c/4,   |G(alpha,kappa)|<=2Lambda.

Choose a fixed a in (0,1/4] so small that (2a)^k<=c/(64Lambda). For all
sufficiently large X and n in [aX,2aX], one has |log(n/X)|/log X<h and
B(n)=L. For every x in [X,2X], theta=(n/x)^k satisfies
theta<=c/(64Lambda), and

    Re[G exp(-i theta)] >= c/8-2Lambda theta >= c/16.

The damping has a fixed positive lower bound. Select primes r with
log r/log X in I and s in (aX/r,2aX/r]. The cell has fixed length h and
is contained in [delta,1/2-m/4], so r<s for large X and each product has
a unique selected factorization. Ordinary PNT, followed by partial
summation for sum 1/r, gives >> X/log X such products uniformly in the
location of I. Removing the finitely many primes dividing pq is harmless.
All selected integers satisfy X^gamma<n<=X^r for large X. Their complete
merged bank coefficients have the positive real part just established.
The real part of the resulting projected sum is >> X/log X at every x
in the shell, proving both norm bounds.

No coefficient was made positive by replacing it with its absolute value.
The projection can depend on X and on the bank. The proof uses a fixed
coarse grid and bounded variation, not a fixed number of breakpoints.
It therefore rules out improving the separated positive-cell budget merely
by using more normalized cuts at bounded total variation. It does not rule
out cancellation with the complementary signed cells, unbounded variation,
or the different compensator used next. This addition has not undergone a
separate critic pass; its exact proof is supplied for root review.

## 7. Fixed-depth deflation and its qualifications

For a fixed integer K>=1 define

    v_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_{p^K}*q_p,
    b_K=v_K*h, c_K=v_K*a, h_K=v_K-b_K.

Equivalently v_K=q_{p^(K+1)}-q_{p^K}. Its coefficient at 1 is zero, and

    b_K(j)=chi(j)[p^K 1_{p^K|j}-p^(K+1)1_{p^(K+1)|j}].

This is zero-mean periodic with period Q_K=p^(K+1)q. The moving-row proof
works with eta_K=1/(100kQ_K), keeping all K-dependent constants. One has
h_K=(p chi(p))^K delta_{p^K}*h_p, so h_K(1)=0 and h_K(l)=0 for every
prime l. At tau=1, provided B(n)>=1, the possible d=1 contribution is
excluded and the entire semiprime projection, including prime squares,
vanishes. If B(n)<1, d=1 may remain. This exception is essential. If
u=2gamma-r>0, B(n)>=1 throughout the finite core for large X, as in all
three target rows above.

The Mellin numerator gains the factor chi(p)^K p^{K(1-s)}, which never
vanishes, and keeps P_p(s). The same two-prime return survives for fixed K.
This operation is a fixed multiplicative dilation and does not itself save
an exponent.

For a principal character the positive obstruction moves to
n=p^(K+1)d with d prime in (X/(4p^(K+1)),X/(2p^(K+1))]. The complete
merged long coefficient is +p^K: h_K(p^(K+1))=-p^K and mu(d)=-1;
the potential pd row has h_K(p^K)=0; rows with higher p-valuation have
zero Mobius coefficient; fixed small powers of p do not pass the long cut.
PNT supplies asymptotically X/(4p^(K+1)log X) such d for fixed K, hence
a projected norm of order X/(p log X).

There is also a valid selected-cell diagnostic for growing K satisfying
p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta), with fixed 0<delta<1-gamma. Then d exceeds
X^(gamma+delta), B(n)=L on this cell for large X, and pure p powers are
below L because gamma>1/2. PNT is uniform for the resulting polynomially
large prime arguments, so the projected lower bound remains >> X/log X.
This does not prove a growing-K full complement theorem. Row and short-term
upper budgets grow with K; failure of those upper budgets is not an
impossibility theorem for a better method.

## 8. Value, unresolved work, and final mathematical status

The useful established structure is a complete moving-cut small-source
estimate with all real shell variables and literal physical endpoints;
the conditional return has a precisely specified actual signed core. The
semiprime calculation identifies what separated-cell budgeting cannot do,
and fixed-depth deflation shows that the particular semiprime obstruction
is not invariant under admissible compensators. The bounded-variation lemma
narrows the cutoff-bank escape without asserting a full-source obstruction.
These are restricted analytic and structural results. They are not a power
estimate for the full Mobius source and do not increase c11.

The next mathematical action is to bound the actual signed transition core,
including correlations between cells; alternatively, determine whether a
growing deflation architecture has a complete uniform complement and return.
That is a future assignment, not work authorized beyond this deadline.

Unfinished audit obligations are the author's helper/receipt inspection,
the latest full index comparison, and the new ancestry source verification.
The full source report and the consequential proof reconstruction above are

statement:
### A2. Even the best rank-two spectral approximation retains the hard field

Retain p=2 and p=3 exactly, and at every p>=5 retain the positive local eigenvector A4. The resulting operator B_sigma has rank2. It is a spectral block of T, not a coefficientwise truncation:

    B_sigma=H_2 tensor (w_3 w_3^T)
                  tensor [(product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+) |u><u|]. (A5)

For completeness it is in fact the truncation to the two largest singular values. On p!=3 let r_p=|lambda_p^-|/lambda_p^+. Because sigma>.5, 0<R_p<1. The ratio

    r(R)=[sqrt(1+6R+R^2)-(1-R)]/
         [sqrt(1+6R+R^2)+(1-R)]

is strictly increasing on (0,1): (1-R)/sqrt(1+6R+R^2) has derivative -4(1+R)/(1+6R+R^2)^(3/2)<0. Thus 1>r_2>r_5>r_7>... . For a finite prime-semigroup compression, the nonzero tensor eigenvalues are

    Lambda_sigma product_(p in S)(lambda_p^-/lambda_p^+),
    Lambda_sigma=lambda_2^+/(1-q_3) product_(p>=5 retained)lambda_p^+,

for subsets S of its retained primes other than3. The first two in modulus have S empty and S={2}. The finite optimality is elementary: every rank-two R kills some unit vector in the top-three singular subspace, giving operator error at least the third singular value. For Hilbert–Schmidt error, projection onto range(R) captures at most the two largest squared singular values; diagonalize T_j^2 to see this from weights between0 and1 summing to at most2. The displayed truncation attains both bounds. Let P_j be increasing prime-semigroup projections including2,3. Then T_j=P_j T P_j tends to T in Hilbert–Schmidt norm by A1. Its rank-two truncation B_j tends to A5: the positive eigenvector products converge in l2 because sum R_p is finite, and their eigenvalue products converge. For any rank-two operator R, the compression P_j R P_j still has rank at most2, so ||T-R||>=||T_j-P_j R P_j||>=||T_j-B_j||. Passing to the limit proves A5 optimal in operator norm. The same compression argument in Hilbert–Schmidt norm proves optimality there. This avoids assuming an unproved completeness theorem for an infinite tensor eigenbasis.

Its first column has the exact coefficient form

    B_sigma(n,1)=C_sigma b_sigma(n)n^(-sigma),
    C_sigma=product_(p>=5)lambda_p^+/(1+c_p^2 R_p)>0,          (A6)

where b_sigma is multiplicative, b_sigma(2^k)=-1, b_sigma(3^k)=1, and b_sigma(p^k)=-c_p for p>=5,k>=1. It is crucial that2 and3 remain literal. Changing the prime-two factor would destroy the cancellation at s=1 and introduce a different numerator.

Here is the decisive arithmetic persistence theorem. For every fixed rho>1/2 there exist mutually inverse Dirichlet convolution kernels a_sigma,d_sigma satisfying

    b_sigma=a_sigma*f, f=d_sigma*b_sigma,
    sum_n(|a_sigma(n)|+|d_sigma(n)|)n^(-rho)<infinity.         (A7)

At2 and3 both kernels have local factor1. At p>=5, with z a formal variable, their exact factors are

    A_p(z)=(1-(1+c_p)z)/(1-2z)
           =1+(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)2^(k-1)z^k,
    D_p(z)=(1-2z)/(1-(1+c_p)z)
           =1-(1-c_p)sum_(k>=1)(1+c_p)^(k-1)z^k.             (A8)

For z=p^(-rho), both absolute nonconstant sums are at most

    (1-c_p)p^(-rho)/(1-2p^(-rho))
       <= C_(sigma,rho) p^(-2sigma-rho).

The prime sum converges because 2sigma+rho>1. The denominator is uniformly positive since p>=5 and rho>.5. Euler products of these nonnegative absolute majorants prove A7 and coefficientwise inverse identities. No continuation hypothesis is used.

Let Bfield_sigma(x)=sum_n b_sigma(n)g_tau(log(n/x)). The same all-real-shell Minkowski argument as G28 gives, for each fixed gamma>.5, equivalence of the complete moment statements

    ||Bfield_sigma||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)
          iff ||F||_[X,2X] <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon)       (A9)

on all sufficiently large dyadic X. Both fields have Gaussian left tails and bounded coefficients. Apply A7 at rho=gamma+epsilon/2 and use two dyadic neighbors to cover each real shell; this pays every convolution scale and the small-x tail. There is no missing cross term, since this is a full field-norm identity, not a signed-submask domination.

Thus the literal arithmetic readout of an optimal rank-two approximation already has the entire current f3 exponent problem. This is stronger and more source-specific than merely observing that a generic compact matrix has an expensive evaluation. It is not a lower bound on F or a proof that all operator methods fail. The complementary spectral modes may cancel; an argument exploiting that cancellation must price their full physical readout. The result also does not say that every arbitrary rank-two matrix has this property.

statement:
### N28.C — New pass 2: continuum dilations and overlap rigidity

A's discrete detector uses \(\Delta_bM(x)=M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)\), \(b=2,3\), fixed \(0<\alpha<1\); its two multipliers have only the common real zero \(s=\alpha\), where zeta is nonzero. Their simultaneous near-zeros at large heights are irrelevant to the qualitative pole contradiction, but complicate quantitative estimates.

A new variation averages **b continuously**:
\[
\mathcal E_\alpha(X)=\int_X^{2X}\int_2^3
|M(bx)-b^\alpha M(x)|^2\,db\,{dx\over x}.
\tag{CD}
\]
T10 gives the conditional transfer \(\mathcal E_\alpha(X)\ll X^{2a+\epsilon}\Rightarrow c=1-a\). Its multiplier calibration is explicit:
\[
G_\alpha(s)=\int_2^3|b^s-b^\alpha|^2db
=\int_2^3 b^{2\sigma}db+\int_2^3 b^{2\alpha}db
-2\Re{3^{\sigma+\alpha+1+it}-2^{\sigma+\alpha+1+it}\over\sigma+\alpha+1+it}.
\]
On each compact real strip it is bounded below away from zero for \(|t|\ge1\); its only zero is \(s=\alpha\), where it vanishes quadratically. Under the same energy hypothesis this also gives \(|1/\zeta(s)|\ll1+|t|\) on every fixed compact real strip strictly to the right of a: the absolutely convergent Hilbert-valued Mellin transform is uniformly bounded, while its norm equals \(\sqrt{G_\alpha(s)}/|s\zeta(s)|\). The continuum therefore supplies uniform multiplier calibration. It does **not** prove a better Möbius energy.

The new analytic construction is to set \(f(t)=e^{-\alpha t}M(e^t)\). Then CD is an explicit positive weighted integral of \(|f(t+h)-f(t)|^2\) over overlapping finite log-intervals. Seek a source-specific overlap/Poincaré comparison with a power-law-detrended shell variance, charging endpoint intervals and weights. A general graph spectral gap merely bounds residual from the given difference energy; the arithmetic theorem is a bound on that energy. The cheapest useful test is an exact finite-window comparison, followed by one genuine signed cross-scale covariance estimate. A fallback uses finitely many dilation intervals with uniform width, still avoiding discrete small divisors. This is a changed quantitative formulation of N28, not an independent second proof of its cancellation hypothesis.
title: N28.C — New pass 2: continuum dilations and overlap rigidity

## 8. What identity and opposite operations actually define

| Object actually defined | Verified information | Missing information |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed cusp residue sources | Nonzero square coefficients, constants in section 4, ray functionals | A good-prime boundary basis and local Whittaker transport |
| Identity square-index readout | (B), J_s, primitive 1-z, phase (P) | Identification with each H-boundary germ |
| Explicit trilinear integral (L) | H covariance in its stated cover convention | Actual global normalization, bad-place binding and full unfolding |
| Unary Fourier/Weyl operation | Exact exterior completion and selected-vector symmetry | Coupled source-dependent relative Hankel/intertwining map |
| Ordinary source constant term | C_p(xi), exceptional zero/residue data | Opposite-cell matrix after both exceptional specializations |
| Global 24-cusp functional equation | Genuine source continuation/transport formula | A reduction to this H-model, its four divisors and phase family |

No phase-preserving coupled boundary matrix is defined by combining the entries in this table. The missing information is structural, not an uncomputed numerical coefficient. There is also no warrant for replacing a guessed 2x2 matrix by a guessed 9x9 or 4x4 one: orbit and divisor counts do not identify the actual space of equivariant boundary distributions.

A useful repaired next task is to fix the local modules and all torus lifts; define the H-equivariant functional and its density before exceptional specialization; construct restriction/asymptotic maps on D_0,D_1,D_2,D_3, including their intersections or a justified resolution; and explicitly transport the chosen Whittaker functionals under the relevant source intertwiners. Then evaluate the resulting maps on finite E(a_(u,2J)), including the phase derivative, with a bound uniform in J and the phase interval. A justified quotient could reduce the boundary coordinates, but that is a theorem to prove, not an input supplied by the two rays.

The first coefficient contract remains (P_J) and its primitive specialization 1-z. A new analytic gain requires a complete signed vector estimate, for the SAME arithmetic source and actual ray corrections, of the form

    integral_I ||F_t||_[X,2X]^2 dt <<_epsilon X^(2a+epsilon),
    a < .874864,

or a fully stated alternative norm that returns it with all losses paid. The physical relative field has the X^-5/2 normalization, so its corresponding norm must be O(X^(a-5/2+epsilon)). The common phase must remain until vector zero return; independent primewise scalar phase averaging simply recreates hard deletion. Finite-source limits, cross terms, tails, bad-place complements and nonzero detector multipliers remain in the contract. For the Q(i) source this controls zeta_Q(i), hence the ordinary zeta factor; it is not automatically a construction for every Hecke family in the project's larger fixed-family scope.

### 5. The remaining small-gcd problem

The strongest bound pays a smooth dyadic tail above
\[
 \boxed{G_0=Z^{1/2+b_0/4}L^{1/2+3b_0/4}.} \tag{T07.13}
\]
At the inherited \(.12551\) geometry, \(\log_ZG_0=0.916210583782689249\ldots\). A rational buffered choice \(b=7/8\) gives \(G_0=Z^{23/32}L^{37/32}\), with exponent \(0.916253443709159867\ldots\). The earlier physical-tail thresholds were \(0.9635172364\ldots\) from ordinary Poisson and \(0.9375816697\ldots\) from the Hecke strip with absolute mark counting. These compare bounds for the same physical gcd; they do not improve or identify the different reflected quadratic-core threshold in inherited SG §10.

Choose a complementary smooth partition \(w_<+w_{\ge}=1\). The exact sufficient residual is
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{c\ne c'}w_<(q_{(c,c')})\langle S_c,S_{c'}\rangle
 \ll Y^{-1}P_a^{1/6}Z^\epsilon.} \tag{OPEN-SMALL-GCD}
\]
The bound is one-sided and concerns the actual fields. It is **UNPROVED**. The tail theorem bounds full gcd-localized covariance, not its zero and nonzero pieces separately. The global complete zero may be removed using (T06.9); a gcd truncation does not preserve positivity of that form (A15 gives a two-by-two counterexample). At \(g=1\) there is no common-divisor length in which (T07.2) can cancel. Controlling that case requires a new estimate in the remaining columns, marks, or rows. Together with T06, an estimate of this strength would complete the inherited \(.12551\) physical transfer with its original numerator, contour, fixed-family, and all-height requirements. Neither T06 nor T07 establishes it.

### Character phase and the complete conditional return

For a finite set of unramified primes and `w(S)=(-1)^|S|chi(product S)`,
an exact toggle C has

    w(S xor C)/w(S) = (-1)^|C| product_(p in C)chi(p)
                                  product_(p in S intersect C)chi(p)^(-2).

It equals -1 for every state of the full Boolean cube exactly when
`chi(p)^2=1` for each p in C and `(-1)^|C|product_C chi(p)=-1`.
Necessity uses the empty state and each singleton; sufficiency is substitution.
No ramified character value is inverted. A cutoff-restricted state set can
have additional exchanges; this universal-cube test does not forbid them.
For the quartic character modulo 5 with chi(2)=i,chi(3)=-i,chi(11)=1,
the toggle {2,3,11} reverses 1 and 66 but gives the same coefficient -i
at 2 and 33. The state-specific exchange 6<->11 remains valid.

`O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))` for every epsilon>0. Pairs wholly
below x cancel exactly. Crossing pairs have distinct lower endpoints in

    |M_chi(x)| <= C x^theta+O_(chi,epsilon)(x^(delta+epsilon))+O_chi(1).

For a common `gamma=max(theta,delta)>0`, normal convergence of

Re s>gamma gives continuation of the actual reciprocal 1/L(s,chi).
Choose epsilon below each compact's horizontal margin. The meromorphic
identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros there; a principal pole forces

## 7. Euler identity: useful, but no hidden inverse-square estimate

On absolute lines Re s1,Re s2>1 the original signed coprime inverse product is exactly

    sum_((d,e)=1) mu(d)mu(e)phi_u(de)/(q_d^s1 q_e^s2)
      = product_p(1-X_p-Y_p)
      = [L_u(s1)L_u(s2)]^(-1) H_u(s1,s2),              (7.1)
    X_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s1), Y_p=phi_u(p)q_p^(-s2),
    H_p=1-X_pY_p/[(1-X_p)(1-Y_p)].

The exact formal coefficients are H_(a,b)=-phi_u(p)^(a+b) for a,b>=1, and zero when precisely one exponent is positive. H converges absolutely, uniformly in u, when the two real parts are bounded below by a positive constant and their sum exceeds1 by a fixed amount. Nonunit factors phi_u(p)=0 give H_p=1. On the equal-variable diagonal the squarefree coefficient is (-2)^omega(n); off that diagonal both variables are necessary.

Equation(7.1) is the controller-suggested identity verified at its literal source. It replaces the coprime product by a joint inverse-square-type object plus higher-prime-power corrections. It does not estimate the required fourth moment, shift through zeros, erase the independent annuli or resolve the terminal theta gate. No result is imported from a scalar Euler-product analogy.

statement:
## 1. Exact imported dependencies and frozen form

The imported arithmetic premise is

\[
M(U)=\sum_{n\le U}\mu(n)\ll_\delta U^{b_0+\delta},\qquad
b_0=.874886647039964131\ldots .
\tag{SP1}
\]

This is [MG1](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#1-imported-inputs-and-the-actual-finite-form).
Consequently one may fix any \(b\in(b_0,1)\) and use
\(M(U)\ll_b U^b\). The numerical choice is
\(b=8749/10000=.8749\), strictly above \(b_0\).

Keep exactly [MG2--MG8](../[research revision]-continuation/mobius-gcd.md#1-imported-inputs-and-the-actual-finite-form):

\[
\begin{gathered}
L=\log X,\quad Y=\lfloor\sqrt X/L^2\rfloor,\quad
T_l=X/L^4,\quad T_u=XL^2,\quad J=\lceil8L^6\rceil,\\
V(u)=e^{-u-u^{-1}},\qquad
\phi(u)=(uV(u))'=(1-u+u^{-1})e^{-u-u^{-1}},\\
\Xi(q;x)=\rho(q/T_l)\chi(q/T_u)
               \sum_{\ell\le J}\phi(\ell q/x),\qquad X\le x\le2X.
\end{gathered}
\tag{SP2}
\]

The fixed smooth cutoffs obey \(0\le\rho,\chi\le1\),
\(\rho=0\) on \((0,1]\), \(\rho=1\) on \([2,\infty)\),
\(\chi=1\) on \((0,1]\), and \(\chi=0\) on \([2,\infty)\).
Every arithmetic parameter is frozen as \(x\) varies. The exact
approximation of the original detector, with arbitrary power errors and
each fixed Euler derivative, is imported from
[T09.2](../[research revision]/[restricted mathematical source]#frozen-dyad-balanced-finite-form).
No cutoff or third-factor endpoint in that theorem is changed here.

In particular,

\[
\Xi(q;x)=0\quad\hbox{unless }T_l<q<2T_u,
\qquad
\sup_{q,x}|(q\partial_q)^r\Xi(q;x)|\ll_r L^6.
\tag{SP3}
\]

The latter bound follows by bounding the \(J\) individual summands and
the fixed cutoff derivatives; no additional Poisson estimate is needed.
Every nonzero individual factor lies in

\[
Y<d_i<U_{\max}:=2T_u/Y\ll\sqrt X L^4.
\tag{SP4}
\]

There are \(O(1+\log L)\) dyadic intervals in this range. All mixed Euler
derivatives using each variable at most once of
\(\Xi(de;x)\overline{\Xi(fh;x)}\) are \(O(L^{12})\).

## 6. The remaining arithmetic calculation and its precise scope

Complete multiplicativity permits the exact merge

    sum_(ml=n)a(m)b0(l)
       #{ordered(d,e):de=m,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G}.             (R22)

This retains one actual sign times an ordered divisor count; it proves no cancellation. The author's first-gain calculation removes the gcd restriction only by paying the full G182 difference. That is lawful. It then dyadically resolves the finite d,e,l,n ranges, with O(log^4 X) labels. Swapping the original d,e labels if needed retains both colors, and makes D>=E in a cell.

For balanced cuts, gamma>6/7, n~N>=X, d~D,e~E, DE l~N, put T=(N/X)^6. Cauchy in d removes only the modulus of a(d). The actual e-pair difference has derivative in d comparable to T h/(DE), h=|e-e'|, and maximum O(T/D). As N<=M,

    T<=X^(3(1-gamma))=o(X^(gamma/2))<=o(D).

The first derivative is therefore away from any nonzero integer alias, with a consistent sign and monotonicity. The intersection of the two product-cut d intervals and the fixed dyadic/cut interval is one interval or empty. Its actual endpoints are kept. The two damping factors have bounded variation. Thus the complete weighted inner correlation is

    |K_(e,e+h)|<<min(D,DE/(T h)).                           (R23)

Summing all h, both orientations and the diagonal, followed by Cauchy, gives

    |sum_(d,e in cell)a(d)a(e)f_x(del)|
       <<DE[E^(-1/2)+T^(-1/2)sqrt(log(2E))].               (R24)

All constants here depend only on the fixed data. Summing the actual bounded b0(l) over its full dyadic label yields, up to X^epsilon,

    N X^(-gamma/4)+X^3/N^2.                               (R25)

At the top output r-gamma/4=3/2-3gamma/4<=gamma exactly when gamma>=6/7. Hence the diagonal term is paid across this interval. The second term reaches the target only at N>=M; near N=X it is X. Outputs L<n<X also cost at most X^(1+epsilon) by the full coefficient bound. Therefore the whole calculation truly proves only exponent1. There is no omitted low-output interval in this failure diagnosis.

Before taking absolute values, the Gram off-diagonal is exactly

    B_(l,x)=2 Re sum_(e<e')a(e)conjugate(a(e'))
          sum_(d in I_e intersect I_e')
          exp(-d(e+e')l/x^(3/2))
          exp(-i[(del/x)^6-(de'l/x)^6]).                    (R26)

The coefficient is lambda(ee')chi(e)conjugate(chi(e')), with its natural zeros. It is not a freely chosen sign. The diagonal is <=DE and total Gram nonnegative. The sufficient one-sided condition is, for EVERY original cell L<n<=M, EVERY retained l and EVERY real x in the shell,

    B_(l,x)<=C_epsilon D E^2 X^epsilon (X^gamma/N)^2.       (R27)

For gamma>=6/7, E>=constant X^(gamma/2) and (N/X^gamma)^2<=constant X^(3(1-gamma)), so the diagonal also obeys this budget. Multiplying the Gram by D and taking square roots then gives DE X^(gamma+epsilon)/N. Sum the full l labels (DE~N/l) and dyadic cells: only harmonic/logarithmic factors arise. This would prove the target. A negative B helps; no absolute-value strengthening of (R27) is needed.

For N>=X the actual absolute derivative estimate misses (R27) by (M/N)^4, up to logs. For L<=N<X the full trivial bound misses by (N/L)^2. Both regions are covered by the proposed condition. At N~X the missing squared power is X^(2(1-gamma)). Liouville multiplicativity rewrites the sign as lambda(e(e+h)); it supplies no estimate for the complete weighted shifted correlations in (R26). The natural arithmetic repair is therefore exact but open.

The equality gamma=6/7 in the DIAGONAL argument is valid. It cannot be used to extend (R23) automatically, since the maximum derivative would only be O(1), which need not avoid integer aliases. The author correctly states the coarse nonstationary test for gamma>6/7. The full source transfer (R21) remains valid throughout3/4<=gamma<1, independently of this test.

### 5b. Actual row kernel, not an invented orthogonality

For a primitive nonprincipal relative character of conductor norm Q and a fixed smooth radial Phi, literal PR9 equation B3.5 gives

    |sum_w xi(w) Phi(Nw/V)| << min(V,sqrt(Q)).         ([research revision])

The primitive dual zero frequency vanishes. The normalized Gauss sum has modulus one, and radial decay/lattice counting bound `A sum_(h!=0)|F Phi(A Nh)|` by a fixed seminorm. This proves the square-root-conductor branch. Ordinary lattice counting proves the V branch. For V below a fixed positive threshold the compactly supported original sum is empty; the same bound follows uniformly. Fixed ray restrictions are first expanded into their finite characters, retaining each phase and any additional fixed conductor holes.

To impose sixth-freeness, use its EXACT Möbius sum over b^6|u and put u=b^6 w. The relative sextic factor at b^6 is one when coprime, zero otherwise. A fixed ray factor from the finite expansion can leave a phase of modulus one, which is retained. Expand the remaining row hole by d|rad E. With d,b restricted by the actual nonempty scale, the absolute majorant is

    sum_(d|rad E) sum_b min(U/[(Nb)^6 Nd], sqrt Q)
      << U^(1/6) Q^(5/12)
                     product_(p|E)(1+(Np)^(-1/6)).

Split at `(Nb)^6=U/(Nd sqrt Q)`. Ideal counting below and the sixth-power tail above give the displayed power; if that split is below one the same upper bound follows from the whole convergent tail. The product is at most `(NE)^epsilon` for every fixed epsilon. E is in a fixed polynomial range, so its loss is preallocated. Natural shared-prime zeros therefore cost a subpower, not a lost radical factor.

Removing the fixed finite exceptional free rows changes the kernel by `O_fixed(1)`, absorbed since U,Q>=1. Thus for the stated clean natural family, with or without those rows,

    |K_e(l,l';U)|
      << H_J U^epsilon min(U, U^(1/6) Q^(5/12)).      ([research revision])

This is uniform over the actual pair's holes. It does NOT apply after inserting an arbitrary high-bin or amplitude indicator. For a full raw-row variant, primitive Poisson gives min(U,sqrt Q); excluding a fixed list of sixth-power core families costs O_fixed(U^(1/6)). For Q<=U^2 both fit ([research revision]), and for Q>U^2 the trivial U bound fits. This raw variant assumes precisely that fixed list and is not a statement about all physical child exclusions. The free family above is the primary proved contract.

## 4. D2/S21: unordered insertions and a precise weighted escape

Let S_N be all squarefree q-units n<=N, and B_p e_n=chi(p)e_(pn) if p does not divide n and pn<=N, zero otherwise. Distinct unramified insertions commute: if the product fits, either order fits, and if not, both products vanish. These unordered commuting operators are not the ordered CAR boundary from W59 or G145's sorted creation.

For p!=r, the mixed commutator C_pr=B_p^*B_r-B_rB_p^* acts only as

    C_pr e_(pm)=-conjugate(chi(p))*chi(r)e_(rm),
    m squarefree, (m,qpr)=1,
    N/(pr)<m<=min(N/p,N/r).                                    (R8)

The lower endpoint is strict: at equality the two compositions cancel. The upper endpoints are inclusive. This is a phased partial isometry with norm 1 when its domain is nonempty and 0 otherwise. With a_N=sum_(n in S_N)mu(n)chi(n)e_n,

    <a_N,C_pr a_N>=-#domain(R8).                               (R9)

Every character phase cancels, including complex and imprimitive cases. For a profile f it is exactly -sum_m conjugate(f(rm))f(pm); arbitrary complex profiles cannot be replaced by a positive count.

For the k unramified primes in (N/2,N], the sum of all ordered C_pr on their span is -D_chi(J_k-I_k)D_chi^*. The actual source -D_chi 1 is an eigenvector with eigenvalue -(k-1), giving quadratic value -k(k-1) and norm k-1 for k>=2. Transporting a gauge together with the source preserves this value. This refutes the specific unweighted independence/orthogonality shortcut, not signed cancellation across every sector.

The strongest escape deserves an explicit formula. If external prime weights are allowed, define C(lambda)=sum_(p!=r)conjugate(lambda_p)lambda_r C_pr on that terminal span. Then

    <a_N,C(lambda)a_N>=sum_p|lambda_p|^2-|sum_p lambda_p|^2.    (R10)

For two primes, weights (1,1),(1,-1),(1,i) give -2,+2,0. Thus the unweighted commutator's coherence does not exclude all weighted compensation. This qualification does not contradict G164's different positive E=B^*B obstruction for arbitrary moving weights. The operators and the scalar being bounded differ.

The complete source remains a_N=product_(p<=N,p not|q)(I-B_p)e_1, with every prime inserted once and exact cutoff; M_chi(N)=<1,a_N>. No estimate for this full readout follows from (R8)-(R10). If the readout has a common all-scale N^(gamma+epsilon) bound for every fixed ordinary chi, Abel continuation gives the usual all-height reciprocal return. That hypothesis is still open.

Record value is the explicit unordered mixed-adjoint boundary, full character contraction and profile formula. G145's sorted operators, G160's phase obstruction, G162's terminal cut and [research revision] G164-G166's ordered complex/harmonic results retain their own credit. In particular a critical basis need not be harmonic, the natural covariant incidence kernel is span(mu chi), and the character heat/supertrace bulk cannot be erased. None of those accepted statements licenses a lower bound for M or a blanket rejection of source-sensitive compensation.

## 5. The other three selected first tests

### T-F05: the natural divisor-poset normal operator squares conditioning

On the exact squarefree diamond {1,p,q,pq}, put u=chi(p)p^(-s), v=chi(q)q^(-s). The convolution matrix and its exact inverse are

    Z=[[1,0,0,0],[u,1,0,0],[v,0,1,0],[uv,v,u,1]],
    U=[[1,0,0,0],[-u,1,0,0],[-v,0,1,0],[uv,-v,-u,1]].    (W39.29)

Both products ZU and UZ equal I; the pq inverse coefficient is +uv, not a deleted cross term. If the proposed Hodge metric is the natural normal operator L=Z*Z, then

    lambda_min(L)=lambda_-(|u|)lambda_-(|v|),
    lambda_-(r)=(2+r^2-r sqrt(4+r^2))/2,
    ||Z^(-1)||=lambda_min(L)^(-1/2).                     (W39.30)

This follows from the tensor product of the two local matrices [[1,0],[u,1]], whose two squared singular values are lambda_-(|u|),lambda_+(|u|) with product1. The local chi phases are unitarily removable. Positivity therefore does not improve this inverse conditioning; it squares it. A different genuine chain complex would require a proof that its Laplacian solution reproduces the original inverse/readout. The test does not rule out such a new construction and is not a bound on the full arithmetic detector. Broader finite-inverse/readout limitations were already established in Sol match01 Max Astra review AM19--AM21 and current-proof G32; those receive prior credit.

### T-D02: translated-field Gram determinants miss a dangerous rank-one mode

Let v_j(t)=F(t+h_j), and G_jk=integral_I v_j(t)conj(v_k(t))w(t)dt with w>=0. For F(t)=A exp(rho t),

    G_jk=|A|^2 exp(rho h_j+conj(rho)h_k)
                    integral_I exp(2 Re(rho)t)w(t)dt.    (W39.31)

It has rank1, so every determinant of size>=2 is zero despite arbitrary positive Re(rho). For F=Ae^(rho1 t)+Be^(rho2 t), rank is at most2. With two shifts, its determinant is exactly

    |AB|^2 |e^(rho1 h1+rho2 h2)-e^(rho2 h1+rho1 h2)|^2
      *[J11 J22-|J12|^2],
    Jkl=integral_I e^((rho_k+conj(rho_l))t)w(t)dt.       (W39.32)

As rho2 approaches rho1, both factors vanish quadratically for a nondegenerate interval and distinct shifts; the determinant is fourth order in the frequency/exponent separation. Thus determinant-only SMALL upper bounds cannot exclude a single growing mode. A trace or coercive observable retaining that mode is necessary and needs its own arithmetic estimate. This is a diagnostic of the stated translated-field Gram detector, NOT a counterexample to the distinct reciprocal Hankel D3 construction or an actual-Möbius lower bound.

### T-B05: the exact mask defect includes both mixed terms

For any original split F=U+V in the actual physical Hilbert space,

    ||F||^2-||U||^2=2 Re<U,V>+||V||^2.                  (W39.33)

An inherited upper bound for ||F|| therefore gives no upper bound for ||U|| without a lower bound on the right-hand defect. Two opposite equal profiles give F=0 and ||U||>0, the simplest diagnostic. The first actual-coefficient two-label Gaussian cell uses mu(1)=1, mu(2)=-1 for the principal character modulo1 (zeta):

    U(y)=g_tau(y), V(y)=-g_tau(y-log2).

On the full unweighted y line, ||U||^2=g_(2tau)(0), and

    ||U+V||^2=2 g_(2tau)(0)[1-exp(-(log2)^2/(4tau))].    (W39.34)

For tau>log2/4, including tau=1, this is smaller than ||U||^2. The coefficient signs and both mixed terms are literal. This finite cell is not claimed to lower bound or model the whole uncut Möbius field; it refutes only automatic inheritance from the generic Hilbert identity, while retaining the exact defect that an actual mask proof must pay. W35/current-proof already forbid this shortcut, so no new-sector credit is taken.

For the actual f3 signs on a finite interval, the accepted buffered summatory estimate gives asymptotically equal positive and negative counts: sum_(n<=N)f(n)=O(N^beta), choosing .874865<beta<1, via the source's absolutely summable convolution with A. Thus a nearly complete pairing of the N unit charges requires cost Omega(N); adding a balancing reservoir of mass O(N^beta) does not change that conclusion if reservoir cost is charged separately and only that imbalance is removed. On the single half-open dyadic interval [N,2N), there is not even an internal edge n<->pn. This rejects a sublinear global log-Wasserstein certificate supported only on these edges. It does NOT lower-bound the smoothed signed field, an unrestricted transport cost, kernel-adapted signed flow, or multi-prime ratios near1. W01/W03/CV already own general flow/pairing interfaces; this elementary scoped test receives no new broad-mechanism credit.

**W41-30, very rare frame draw.** For normalized two-frequency observation vectors t->exp(it log N), exp(it log(N+1)) in L2([-T,T],dt/(2T)), their Gram eigenvalues are1 +/- |sin(T Delta)/(T Delta)|, Delta=log(1+1/N). If0<T Delta<=1, the smaller eigenvalue is at most (T Delta)^2/6<=T^2/(6N^2), by1-sin u/u<=u^2/6. Thus a source-blind frame lower bound fixed independently of N already fails at two nearby integer frequencies. At T=O(sqrt(log X)), N comparable to X, the cost is at least X/sqrt(log X) at norm level. This is a generic two-mode diagnostic, not a realization of an actual zero witness or f3 coefficients. The earlier finite-data and W39 observability records already warn of this; no general arithmetic-observability impossibility is asserted. **W41-28, most-different draw.** No honest inverse-scattering realization was constructed. The first natural prerequisite, an unrenormalized finite Euler reciprocal, already fails inside the desired strip. For real0<sigma<1, E_P(sigma)=product_(p<=P)(1-p^-sigma)>0 and tends to0 because sum_p1/p diverges and p^-sigma>=p^-1. ## G194. The literal matrix and its complete positive price

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q with its natural zero extension.
For every real x>=1 use the finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu²(n)=1,(n,q)=1}, N=|D_x|.

Order its indices increasingly. Let e be the coordinate of1, v=1-e, and

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime), P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

Every prime-cover path stays in the original downset. Its product is
chi(n/d), and each ordering of the k distinct factors gives one path:

    B^k(d,n)=k!chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z, exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).

These are finite polynomial exponentials. The determinant lemma, detZ=1,
gives exactly detR=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n). No zero character value is inverted.
If K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n)>=1, define

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k).

Strict chains correspond to ordered partitions into k nonempty blocks.
For y=lambda-1, the finite resolvent identity and polynomial continuation
through y=0 yield

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].

The multiplicity at1 can exceed N-K-1 when a twisted top coefficient
cancels. K=0 means R=(1). The product of j distinct primes is at least
(j+1)!, so K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)); this alone bounds no determinant.
The classical ancestry is [Wilf's finite-poset construction](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1)
and [Vaughan's characteristic calculation](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).
No full-integer spectral conclusion is imported to this altered support.

Put F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k). Ordering each block internally,
then concatenating with marked cuts, proves F_j<=2^(j-1)j! for j>=1.
For any sigma>1, split primes at a fixed Y with
R_sigma=sum_(p>Y)p^-sigma<1/4. The tail elementary symmetric function
of degree b is at most R_sigma^b/b!. If a is the number of chosen small
primes, its entire remaining contribution is bounded by a fixed multiple
of sum_b(2R_sigma)^b(a+b)!/b!, which converges. The finitely many small
prime choices therefore prove

    sum_(n squarefree)F_(omega(n)) n^-sigma<infinity,
    P_q(x):=sum_(n in D_x)F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon)x^(1+epsilon).

This pays ALL depths, including growing depths. For principal chi it is
the permanent of R: each nonidentity permutation cycle is a strict chain
through1. It is also1+sum_k|A_k| in that case. Moreover

    P_q(x)>=|D_x|=delta_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.

The density follows directly from mu²(n)=sum_(d²|n)mu(d), paying floors
and the tail of sum d^-2. Hence the full positive price has exact exponent1.
This is not a lower bound for the signed determinant.

Two tempting operator shortcuts also fail in their stated norms.
The unitary diagonal diag(chi(n)) gauges B to the principal matrix, but
changes the closing vector v. Parity diag((-1)^omega(n)) conjugates B to
-B, so ||exp(-B_chi)||_2=||exp(B_1)||_2. The Hermitian part of -B_1 has
a two-dimensional compression with positive eigenvalue sqrt(pi_q(x))/2.
There is no contraction in this Euclidean norm. This says nothing about
a different signed observable or a lower bound for M_chi.

## G195. Every fixed low-chain sector under one common filter

Fix p not dividing q and integer J>=2, independent of x. Define

    Q=delta1-p chi(p)delta_p, v_J=Q^(*J),
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),
    b=Q*chi=chi(n)(1-p1_(p|n)),
    f_t(n)=mu²(n)t^omega(n)chi(n), f_0=delta1.

b has period pq and mean zero, including principal/imprimitive characters.
Choose D>=max(1,||b||_infinity,sup_y|sum_(n<=y)b(n)|); D=p²q suffices.

For any fixed bounded mean-zero periodic b, the full ordered hyperbola
identity proves

    |sum_(n<=x)b^(*t)(n)|<=C_t x^(1-1/t),
    C_t<=(2D)^t(t!)².

Indeed each t-tuple of product<=x has a coordinate<=Y=x^(1/t).
In inclusion-exclusion with j<t short coordinates and m=t-j, induction
costs C_m x^(1-1/m)[sum_(n<=Y)|b(n)|n^(-1+1/m)]^j,
at most C_m(Dm)^j x^(1-1/t). For j=t the product cutoff is automatic:
the term is the bounded quantity(sum_(n<=Y)b(n))^t. All overlaps and real
floors are retained. The recurrence and m!m^(t-m)<=t! prove the stated
constant bound.

The exact Euler correction is

    sum_n f_t(n)n^-s=L(s,chi)^t G_t(s),
    G_t(s)=prod_l(1+t z_l)(1-z_l)^t, z_l=chi(l)l^-s.

The local linear term vanishes. The absolute coefficient series
Gabs_t(sigma)=sum|g_t(n)|n^-sigma converges for every fixed t and sigma>1/2.
Consequently, for1<=t<=J,

    v_J*f_t=b^(*t)*v_(J-t)*g_t,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_t)(n)|
      <=C_t Gabs_t(sigma)(1+p^(1-sigma))^(J-t)x^sigma,
          sigma>1/2, sigma>=1-1/t.

Each finite p^a coefficient is evaluated at x/p^a; arguments below1
contribute zero. All colors on the left use the SAME filter v_J.

The independent review sharpens the two low endpoints without assuming
Euler convergence at1/2. For t=1, g_1 is supported on r² with coefficient
mu(r)chi(r)². For t=2, the local polynomial1-3z²+2z³ has absolute
coefficients dominated by(1-z²)^-3(1-z³)^-2. Thus

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_1)(n)|<=D(1+sqrt p)^(J-1)sqrt x,
    sum_(n<=x)|g_2(n)|/sqrt n
      <=zeta(3/2)²(1+0.5log x)³,
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*f_2)(n)|
      <=3D²zeta(3/2)²(1+sqrt p)^(J-2)sqrt x(1+0.5log x)³.

The second inequality follows by writing the majorant as
sum_(a²c³=n)d_3(a)d_2(c): the c-series converges, and the a-series is
bounded by the cube of a harmonic sum. The periodic two-variable
hyperbola bound is3D²sqrt x. All p shifts remain in these bounds.

Set a_0=delta1 and a_k(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)k!S(omega(n),k). Finite differences
give the complete first-J chain combination

    L_J=sum_(k=0)^J(-1)^k a_k
       =sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)f_t.

Combining ALL colors and their common filter proves, for every real x>=1,

    |sum_(n<=x)(v_J*L_J)(n)| <<_(p,q,J) x^(1-1/J), J>=3;
    |sum_(n<=x)(v_2*L_2)(n)| <<_(p,q) sqrt x log³(2x).

The exponent for J>=3 has no epsilon loss. This is a complete arithmetic
estimate of the low source, including principal characters.

Growing depth is not free. Splitting primes at t^(1/sigma) proves
logGabs_t(sigma)<<_sigma t^(1/sigma)log(2t) for fixed1/2<sigma<1.
The factorial hyperbola constant, finite p-shift factors and binomial
combination must all be paid, and sigma>=1-1/t still applies. These upper
prices establish no impossibility theorem for a better growing-depth proof.

## G196. The complete linked remainder and its weaker sufficient norm

With0^0=1 define

    W_J(j)=(-1)^j-sum_(t=0)^J(-1)^t binom(J+1,t+1)t^j,
    r_J(n)=mu²(n)chi(n)W_J(omega(n)),
    mu chi=L_J+r_J.

The exact generating function is

    sum_(j>=0)W_J(j)z^j
      =(-1)^(J+1)(J+1)!z^(J+1)/[(1+z)prod_(t=1)^J(1-tz)].

In particular W_J(j)=0 for j<=J; for J>=2 its remaining coefficients
have fixed sign(-1)^(J+1), since the denominator reduces to
(1-z²)prod_(t=2)^J(1-tz). Nevertheless |W_J(j)|<=C_J J^j, hence
|r_J(n)|<<_(J,epsilon)n^epsilon. The full factorial representation cost
has disappeared, without removing any chain depth.

Let T_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*r_J)(n) and
S_(p,J)(x)=sum_(n<=x)(v_J*mu chi)(n). Then

    |S_(p,J)(x)-T_(p,J)(x)| << x^(1-1/J), J>=3,
    |S_(p,2)(x)-T_(p,2)(x)| << sqrt x log³(2x).

For n=p^a m, p not dividing m, m squarefree, j=omega(m), the literal
coefficient is

    chi(p)^a chi(m)[(-p)^a binom(J,a)W_J(j)
                  +(-p)^(a-1)binom(J,a-1)W_J(j+1)].

At a=0 the second term is absent. a=J+1 is retained; only a>J+1
vanishes. Out-of-range binomial coefficients are zero; nonsquarefree m
or ramified factors give zero. These linked valuations cannot be bounded
as arbitrary independent signed subsets.

Fix ONE gamma with1/2<gamma<gamma11 and choose fixed J with
max(1/2,1-1/J)<=gamma. For every fixed chi and a fixed covering pair of
distinct unramified primes, the following complete hypothesis suffices:

    OPEN-L1-CHAIN:
    integral_X^(2X)|T_(p,J)(x)|dx/x
      <<_(chi,p,J,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon)
    for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X.

G195 pays the entire difference from S in the same norm. Initially for
Re s>1, ordinary partial summation gives

    P_p(s)^J/L(s,chi)=s integral_1^infinity S_(p,J)(x)x^(-s-1)dx.

On a compact set Re s>=gamma+delta, choose epsilon<delta/2. Each dyadic
shell, including any fixed s derivative, costs
O((log(2X))^m X^(-delta+epsilon)); the sum converges normally. The finite
initial interval is entire. Therefore the quotient is holomorphic in
Re s>gamma, with every sharp endpoint and filter term retained.

P_p zeros lie on Re s=1. A common nonzero-height zero for two distinct
primes would make logp1/logp2 rational, since character values are roots
of unity. For a nonprincipal character choose one prime with chi(p)!=1
to cover height0. Such a prime exists by factoring a unit integer on
which chi is nontrivial. For principal chi, the pole of L at1 is the
allowed exception. This fixed pair exposes every hypothetical ordinary
zero in Re s>gamma. No growing conductor or uniform height bound is used.

A pointwise T bound implies shell L2, and shell L2 implies shell L1.
This corrects the reversed norm wording at author line376; its original
bytes are retained. No reverse implication or attained norm estimate is
claimed. Both pointwise and complete shell hypotheses remain OPEN.

| Prospective gamma | Fixed J | Paid low exponent | Conditional c |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| .8748 |7|6/7|.1252|
|5/6|6|5/6|1/6|
|3/4|4|3/4|1/4|

The nearer prospective gain is135091/2500000000=.0000540364. Equality
with the paid low exponent is allowed. The full coarse bound is still
|T_(p,J)(x)|<<x log^(J-1)(2x), since J^omega=d_J on squarefree integers
and every p^a coefficient meets x/p^a. It supplies no first power gain.
Color8's available exponent7/8 misses gamma11 by.0001459636; improving
only that color would leave all higher depths.

For principal chi, the p-free subfamily n=A*l, with A a fixed product of
J primes avoiding pq and l another prime, has nonzero constant residual
coefficient. Its absolute price is at least a constant times x/log x,
using the [ordinary prime bound](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12).
This obstructs separately paying that projection below exponent1. It
does not lower-bound the full filtered sum, whose linked p valuations
can cancel. Setting J>=K(x) kills the residual below x but changes the
filter with x and makes the paid exponent tend to1; it has no fixed-source
Mellin return under the present estimates.

## Evidence, usefulness and next action

The [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json) preserves13 original
files,10 source bindings and the preceding raw scorecard. The author and
reviewer stopped and normally released their own scopes. Root read the
full author and review mathematics, helper, receipt and metadata and
reconstructed the consequential arguments. No unchanged helper was rerun;
finite matrix/valuation checks establish only their stated finite identities.

The useful new contract pays every fixed low chain sector under ONE
filter, with a complete all-depth residual and a complete shell-L1 return.
Its determinant, compensation and prime-insertion ancestry are credited
to the prior index and primary sources. Potential1/4 is a conditional
target, with the full signed estimate explicitly unpaid. This pass is
not evidence of a larger c, formalization or external admission.
The next decisive attack must control the entire linked valuation source
or prove a uniform growing-depth estimate together with its moving-filter
return. The direct incumbent same-zero lane remains separately active.

## 6. Actual marks, every completed dyad and both infinite tails

For the embedded subset \(D\), retain exactly
\[
K_D(A)=
\sum_{\substack{U'\mid A\ {\rm in\ complementary\ slots}\\(U',D)=1}}
\omega_{U'}\overline{\eta(U')}V(q_A/(Zq_{U'})).
\tag{XM27}
\]
The symbols \(U'\) and \(u\) are unrelated: the former is a marked product and the latter is the squareful source part. The number of marked tuples dividing \(A\) is divisor-bounded. Also \(q_{U'}/L_D\) lies in a fixed compact multiplicative interval. Hence, for any prescribed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
|K_D(A)|\ll_\eta q_A^\eta E(q_A/N_D),
\tag{XM28}
\]
where \(E\) is nonnegative and decays faster than every power at both endpoints. This follows directly from the original Gaussian and bounded marked weights. In particular there is no separate count by the total complementary slot lengths and no factor \(q_{U'}^{-1/2}\).

On each \(q_A\asymp T\) dyad, (XM8) permits (XM25) with a bounded compact completed window, multiplied by \(T^\eta E_*(T/N_D)\), where \(E_*\) is another two-sided rapid envelope. For fixed \(T\), the number of nonempty pairs of core/cube dyads \(C,N\ge1\), \(CN^3\asymp T\), is \(O(1+\log(2T))\). Their bounded overlap and all unit choices cost only fixed constants or logarithms.

For every fixed \(\alpha>0\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{T=2^j\\j\ge0}}
(1+\log(2T))^B T^\alpha E_*(T/N_D)
\ll_{\alpha,B} N_D^\alpha(1+\log(2N_D))^B
\tag{XM29}
\]
when \(N_D\ge1\). To verify it, write \(T/N_D\) on geometric intervals. Above one use rapid upper-tail decay stronger than \(\alpha+B+2\); below one use rapid lower-tail decay stronger than \(B+2\). The resulting geometric sums converge, uniformly in the fractional position of \(N_D\) between dyads. A power of \(\log(2T)\) is bounded by a power of \(\log(2N_D)\) plus a fixed power of \(|\log(T/N_D)|\), which is absorbed by the same endpoint decay.

The finitely many bounded lower dyads include the unit ideal. The upper dyads are not truncated. Small powers of arbitrarily large \(A\) are absorbed using (XM29), with \(N_D\) polynomial in \(Z\). Source divisor losses contribute only \(Y_D^\eta\). Choose all these losses sufficiently small before fixing the final \(\epsilon\). This proves the full original-profile statement (XM26).

The passage from finite completed truncations agrees with the original field. Indeed, ideal counting and the same rapid envelope give, for every fixed small \(\eta>0\),
\[
\sum_{I,J}\frac{q_{IJ^3}^{\eta}}{\sqrt{q_I}\,q_J}
E(q_Iq_J^3/N_D)
\ll_\eta N_D^{1/2+\eta}\sum_Jq_J^{-5/2}<\infty.
\]
For the inner \(I\)-sum this uses the bound at scale \(N_D/q_J^3\); its subunit scales follow from rapid upper-tail decay. Source labels and physical rows are finite on their original annuli, and the Mellin density is integrable. Thus the original sum is absolutely defined before the sharper row estimates; taking its completed truncations and passing to the limit is legitimate.

All bounds were taken after the exact row calculation. The signed phases and the exact masks remain in the defining field; only their actual coefficient magnitudes were majorized. Thus the argument applies to a restricted linear probe without replacing its defining marks by an unrelated coefficient sequence.

The Mellin integral in (XM9) is now absolutely controlled by
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|\widehat W_0(iv)|(1+|v|)^{J_0}\,dv<\infty.
\tag{XM30}
\]
This proves the all-height passage with the original window. Any real inverse completed height appears only as a modulus-one label phase and never needs differentiation. If it is integrated in the original inverse representation, its original rapidly decreasing density remains available. The proof does not create a moving profile depending on the chosen labels.

## 4. A concrete alternating chain and another stage

One allowed chain is

    F_o → S_no F_o=F_n → A_beta F_n
        → (S_gn direct-sum S_gn) A_beta F_n
        = A_beta F_g → R_a A_beta F_g=F_g → A_beta F_g.

It uses a bank, forward smoothing of the whole bank, a paid left inverse, and a further bank. S_h,D_lambda,E_lambda commute on the just established domains because they are scalar convolutions in log scale. The causal sums and convolution interchange by their positive-weight absolute bounds. No stage inverts M_g/M_n. Recombination is useful for retaining a simple source for another argument, though the displayed final bank equals the preceding Gaussian bank and is not an independent gain.

A less redundant explicit two-level bank, with smoothing between levels, is

    G_ij = D_i S_gn D_j S_no F_o = D_iD_j F_g,
                     i,j in {2,3}.                      (H11)

Its four channels retain H=L²(I). Applying R_a to either index and then the other reconstructs F_g, with global norm <=A^(−1) and all-shell norm <=2/A. Its global frame bounds are A² and B²: the symbol is d tensor d. This supplies a fully specified alternating construction and a paid route to another stage. Depth m costs A^(−m/2) globally and at most (sqrt(2/A))^m in the stated shell bound; it is not free if depth grows with X.

For a fixed finite composition the product of all C_h(a), frame, shift and reconstruction constants is a fixed constant. If depth depends on X, the whole product must be X^o(1) to preserve an every-epsilon exponent, or its explicit power must be subtracted from a strict gain. For a uniform stage bound C>1, depth o(log X) suffices for subpower cost, while depth proportional to log X generally costs a power. The source/profile choices must also be consistent: the direct chain has only the allowed forward arrows, and growing-depth identities must still reconstruct one fixed source before its Mellin return. Moving profiles cannot simply be assigned the fixed Mellin identity. At beta=a the causal series no longer contracts and A=0; the easy inverse and frame lower bound fail.

For H11 the actual profile, with z=log(Nm/x), is

    kappa_ij(z)=g_tau(z)−i^beta g_tau(z+log i)
       −j^beta g_tau(z+log j)+(ij)^beta g_tau(z+log(ij)).   (H12)

This formula includes repeated indices, whose equal middle terms add. Each kernel has left/right Gaussian decay and Mellin multiplier M_g(s)d_i(s)d_j(s), nonzero at Re s>beta. One can instead stop at the compact bank if that source admits a cheaper arithmetic estimate; H6 carries such an estimate forward. One cannot obtain an old-compact bank estimate back from a Gaussian one by these operators.

For reference, even the one-stage square has the complete expression

    ||D_lambda F(x)||_H²=||F(x)||_H²
      +lambda^(2beta)||F(x/lambda)||_H²
      −2lambda^beta Re<F(x),F(x/lambda)>_H.               (H13)

The last term, all original signed ideal pairs within it, and the integral in t are part of the task. For two stages there are the full sixteen ordered profile cross terms per channel before equal terms are collected. Taking absolute values before a proposed cancellation pays only an upper bound; it cannot be credited with a negative cross term. A weighted signed recombination of different detectors also creates all its cross terms and needs a nonvanishing combined multiplier. H9 avoids that uncertainty by proving its exact left-inverse identity.

## 10. The complete hard correlation cannot be bounded piece by piece

The [[research revision] actual-source proof]([research revision]/f3-hard-correlation-integration.md)
and its independent review preserve the complete critical rough field R
at z=kappa sqrt X, kappa^2>=2exp(3tau), with F=T+R. Writing L=log X,
the gcd-one Gaussian bilinear form satisfies

    C1(R,R) asymp X^2/L^4,
    C1^H(T,R)=C1^H(R,T)=-C1^H(R,R)
                          +O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4),
    C1^H(T,T)=C1^H(R,R)+O(X^(1+beta)+XH+X^-4).        (G41)

Here H=X/L^6 removes small shifts while preserving the leading term;
the frozen proof uses a fixed historical buffer beta>.874872. The
general C1(F,fA)=O(X^(1+beta)) holds for one original mask0<=A<=1,
with the other factor complete, not for two masks or arbitrary pair masks.
C1 is not positive semidefinite. No lower bound for the full F norm follows.

Retain the exact low-gcd hard sum of G34 with h>H, g<D, both ordered
mixed pieces and the original scales, masks and two Mellin heights. Then

    Q_off=Q_hard+O_epsilon(X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta)
                          +XH log(2D)+X^-4),
    Q_hard(R,R)=||R||^2+O(X^2/D+XH log(2D)+X+X^-4)
                  asymp X^2/L^4.                       (G42)

The second line uses a separate positive high-gcd count, not a signed
submask transfer. It holds for fixed D=X^theta with theta>0 and H=X^alpha
with alpha<1; its error is small relative to X^2/L^4, not automatically
to the desired power. A power-small complete Q_hard would prove OPEN-F3
when theta>(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1),0<=alpha<2gamma-1 and gamma>.5.
Both mixed terms have the opposing leading size. This eliminates a
separate R,R power-saving route even after gcd and shift truncation;
it leaves the joint cancellation entirely open. The historical near
example gamma=.874871 no longer improves the current .8748540364 boundary.

## 5. Reconstructing the inherited raw graph contract

The transport claim must start with the radial graph theorem, not assume that a positive sieve is hereditary under every signed mask. JSR10 supplies the required sharp row bound. Its central conductor exponent is `a=103/512`; balancing the all-height smooth estimate `X^(1/2) [C(3+|tau|)^2]^a H^(2a)` against the full sharp boundary error `X/H+1` gives

`beta=(1/2+2a)/(1+2a)=231/359`, `delta=a/(1+2a)=103/718`.

The row bound is

`(2 C X q_T)^epsilon X^beta C^delta (3+|tau|)^(2delta+epsilon)`.

The +1 pays literal endpoints; subunit intervals are empty, and the bounded regime uses the absolute estimate. The original row set remains the full good squarefree norm interval with its fixed ray and punctures. No arbitrary row subset or additive row phase is licensed by this input. The smooth radial factor is paid by its supremum and total variation. JSR's natural-zero Euler quotient keeps every ramified prime removed even when the character is squared, and the primitive numerator stays nonprincipal at the long good primes. These are part of the accepted source contract; the present review does not import or strengthen its external subconvex input.

To check both mark projectors, expand them completely. With P=DP1 the first coefficient retains `mu(D)/sqrt(q_D)` and residual rooted array `u(DP1)/sqrt(q_P1)`. At a shared D prime the exponent is `3+4=1 mod 6`, with its natural zero. There is no extra `(P1,R/D)=1` condition after the full expansion, and the original prime length remains N. For the pair D,D', put J=[D,D'] and R=Jr. The row length is K/q_J, with all actual phases and the puncture `(r,Jd)=1`.

The cubic sieve in M B2.25 applies to the squarefree ideal mark coefficients common across live primes. It yields `||b_D||_2^2 <= Z^epsilon S(N,L/q_D) Omega_D`, where `Omega_D=sum |u(DP1)|^2/q_P1`. Both roots produce the vectors `x_D=(Omega_D/q_D)^(1/2)`. The remaining kernel is `q_[D,D']^(-beta)`. With Schur weight `q_D^(-beta)`, its row sums are bounded by

`zeta_K(2beta) sum_(f|D) q_f^(-beta) <= C_epsilon q_D^epsilon`.

Here `2beta>1`. Moreover `sum_D x_D^2<=Z^epsilon Omega`. This is the full D,D' estimate, including cross terms, and no ambient mark-count factor is omitted. It is different from the later absolute transport bound, where both mark counts are explicitly paid.

For fixed original g,g', write d=(g,g'), u=g/d, v=g'/d. The exact natural-zero row identity is

`chi_R(pi g)^3 conjugate(chi_R(pi' g')^3)=chi_R(pi*pi'*u*v)^3 1_(R,d)=1`.

The good primitive conductor is exactly pi*pi'*u*v and has norm at most `C_orig N^2 G^2/q_d^2`. Opposite ideal orientations do not cancel as CRT characters; a square rational norm is not a square ideal character. Distinct long primes remain nonprincipal even for g=g'. Original core and rational-gcd screens reduce to h(d) and the actual short screen under the stated endpoint inequalities, without a new opposite row/mark exclusion.

For a graph independent of live marks and rows, with both degrees at most B, edge Cauchy is

`sum_E |b_D(pi) b_D'(pi')|<=B ||b_D||_2 ||b_D'||_2`.

It also follows from absolute Schur row sums. The graph may be frozen with each short pair. Summing the at most O(G^2) ordered original short pairs and using conductor exponent delta gives

`|C_E| <= Z^epsilon G^(2+103/359) B K^(231/359) N^(103/359) S(N,L) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig`.

This is exactly JSR19, already accepted. The new report does not count it as a second proof of a newly paid raw-H sector. The inherited proof requires neither a separable graph mask nor an additive row-character estimate.

## A16. Unequal Type I cutoffs

**PROVED bounded extension of the inherited Type I theorem.** Sources: BB R04b; M (3.15), (M.4)–(M.7), (M.35).

Let \(m_i=\mu1_{q\le Y_i}\), \(u_i=\delta-m_i*\mathbf1\), and \(R=Y_1Y_2\). Convolution algebra gives
\[
 \mu=m_1+m_2-m_1*m_2*\mathbf1+\mu*u_1*u_2.
\]
For the completed product Type I array \(a=-m_1*m_2\), one has support \(q_r\le R\), divisor-bounded coefficients, and prime valuations at most two. The unchanged central estimate M (3.15) costs
\(DK\|a\|_2^2\ll(DKR)^\epsilon DKR\).
The mixed estimate M (M.35) has outer weight
\(q_{\operatorname{rad}(rs)}^{1/2+\epsilon}/q_r\); the two divisor-weighted sums have sizes \(R^{1/2+\epsilon}\) and \(R^{3/2+\epsilon}\). Their product is \(R^{2+\epsilon}\). The double-residue factors \(q_r^{-1},q_s^{-1}\) have only subpower summed cost, exactly as in M (M.4)–(M.7). Therefore
\[
 |\mathfrak Q[I,I]|\ll(DKR)^\epsilon
 \{D^{5/3}K^{1/3}+D^{4/3}K^{7/12}R^2+DKR\}. \tag{A16.1}
\]
Both original Mellin roots and whole profiles remain in force. At \(K=D^k\), the two cutoff-dependent terms are affordable when
\[
 \log_D R<\min\{1-k,(8-7k)/24\}. \tag{A16.2}
\]
This enlarges the choice of decomposition geometry; it proves no improved remainder estimate.

## G79. Exact drift and normalized Ward defects

For h>0, a_h=exp(gamma h), E_j=int_(jh)^((j+1)h)|U(e^y)|^2dy and
D(y)=U(e^(y+h))-a_h U(e^y),

    E_(j+1)-a_h^2 E_j=int (|D|^2+2a_h Re(D conjugate(U)))dy.

An every-j one-sided drift estimate at exponent2gamma is equivalent to
the energy bound. The actual squarefree diagonal has density
kappa_q=prod_(p|q)(1-1/p)prod_(p not|q)(1-1/p^2) and pointwise main term
kappa_q exp(tau/4)e^y/(2sqrt(pi tau)), with O_(q,tau)(e^(y/2)) error.
Its drift is negative for gamma>1/2; the signed off-diagonal is unbounded
by this calculation. This is an adaptation of the existing scale family.

For a finite prime exterior space, Q=sum w_p a_p^*, W=sum|w_p|^2>0,
and even diagonal Z, the CAR identity yields

    Str(Q^*[Q,Z])=W Str(Z).

For actual Gaussian entries, Str(Z)=U_P. Every individual prime term is
|w_p|^2 U_P, so no prime-count cancellation occurs. Primes through N_X
give full omitted error X^(1-C^2/(2tau)+o(1)). Exponent equivalence is
for the normalized defect divided by W, or W=1; arbitrary moving W is
charged. This corrects the unqualified raw-defect wording in the author.
