## 5. Constant-cut source transfer, with all complements

Fix3/4<=gamma<1. Let

    L=X^gamma, M=X^r, r=(6-2gamma)/4,
    U=X^(gamma tau), V=X^(gamma(1-tau)), G=X^(1-gamma),
    max(gamma tau,gamma(1-tau))<=(11gamma-3)/8.              (R18)

Tau is chosen before real x, and UV=L exactly; real endpoints remain closed on the short side and strict on the long side. The complete coefficient identity is

    c=Q_U+Q_V-S+R,
    Q_U=a_(<=U)*(v*s), Q_V=a_(<=V)*(v*s),
    S=a_(<=U)*a_(<=V)*b0, R=a_(>U)*a_(>V)*b0.               (R19)

This follows by expanding the two a colors, not by assigning signs after a mask. Every ordered tuple survives in exactly the required inclusion-exclusion combination.

For S, merge only the two bounded short coefficients:

    A_m=sum_(de=m,d<=U,e<=V)a(d)a(e), m<=L, |A_m|<=d_2(m).

For each epsilon choose a small divisor exponent after epsilon. Applying H to the WHOLE cofactor sum gives ||S||_(1,2)<<X^(gamma+epsilon), because gamma>=3/4. This is the new arithmetic-source payment. No cofactor/output/gcd mask is inserted into H afterward.

Both Q faces use exactly the accepted [research revision] square-source theorem, with their infinite root endpoints, beta(r)=chi(r)^2(1-p1_(p|r)), and physical labels1,p of weights1,-p chi(p). Its norm exponents at D=X^alpha are

    alpha, (3+8alpha)/11, 3/8+alpha/4,
           min(3/10+7alpha/10,15/32+alpha/4).

They are all <=gamma under (R18), including equality. This check does not replace the square-source theorem; its merged collisions, natural zeros, both label orientations and every root prefix are inherited literally. For a fixed gamma the whole closed tau corridor has alpha bounded strictly below1, so its constants are uniform. Infinite root endpoints are explicitly in that theorem's scope.

Every tuple in R has de>UV=L. Consequently R(n)=0 for n<=L EXACTLY, and |R(n)|<=(p+1)^2d_3(n). The full coefficientwise tail estimate gives

    ||sum_(n>M)R(n)f_x(n)||_2^2
       <<X^(3/2+epsilon)+X^6 M^(-4+epsilon)
       <<X^(2gamma+epsilon).                               (R20)

Here M>X and6-4r=2gamma. Divisor losses are chosen after epsilon. This bounds the complete infinite tail, its diagonal and both cross orientations; triangle pays the interaction with the finite piece. The generic divisor-bounded tail theorem applies to R, whereas the sharper actual-c variance theorem alone would not suffice for an arbitrary R.

On the remaining finite source impose gcd(d,e)<=G. The removed part has literal shell-frozen mask

    1_(L<del<=M)1_(d>U)1_(e>V)

and strict gcd>G. G182 applies to precisely these ordered tuple colors and this full mask; it costs

    X^epsilon[X/G+X^(3/4)/sqrt G]
      =X^epsilon[X^gamma+X^(1/4+gamma/2)]<<X^(gamma+epsilon).

There is no new condition on gcd(d,l) or gcd(e,l). In particular the mean-zero property is never reapplied to an already gcd-restricted cofactor. With

    T_rect(x)=sum_(L<n<=M)f_x(n)
                 sum_(del=n,d>U,e>V,gcd(d,e)<=G)a(d)a(e)b0(l),

the exact conclusion is

    ||C-T_rect||_1+||C-T_rect||_2<<X^(gamma+epsilon).         (R21)

All thresholds, every epsilon and fixed-data dependencies are retained. The source C itself is fixed; the core may depend on the shell.

The old adaptive core T_ad has B(n)<=L, hence its U(n),V(n) are no larger than U,V. T_rect is indeed a subset of its original tuple set, but that fact supplies NO signed norm comparison. The payment is instead

    ||T_ad-T_rect||_j<=||T_ad-C||_j+||C-T_rect||_j,

using the two separately proved full transfers. This proves that the removed wedge is paid, with all its signs, not merely that it has smaller support.

For every retained tuple, l<n/L<=M/L, so the new cofactor exponent is r-gamma=3(1-gamma)/2. At the old high boundary the cap was eta^-1 X^(3(1-gamma)). The new exponent is .1877189454 at gamma11, .1878 at gamma=.8748,1/4 at5/6 and3/8 at3/4. These are complete source restrictions, not attained zero-free constants.

### 3.2 The corrected main term uses the same energy

First restrict the main sum to k>=rH. Every shift j occurring in psi obeys0<=j<rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X). For X<=x<=2X,

    log((k+j)/x)=v+b,   |b|<=ell.

Consequently

    f_x(k+j)^2/w_X(k)
      =(2 pi tau)^(-1)
         exp([-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2]/tau)
      <=(2 pi tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2tau)). (5)

The last inequality follows from 2|bv|<=v^2/4+4b^2. Using the absolute coefficient sum of Q_r, (5) applies to |psi_x(k)|^2 with the extra factor (2^r-1)^2.

For any positive unimodal function with maximum1, its positive-integer sum is at most its integral plus2. Substituting k=X exp(v) therefore gives

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2tau))
       <=X sqrt(2 pi tau) exp(tau/2)+2 <=K_tau X.           (6)

Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, using the ENTIRE sum defining E and restricting only the test-function norm, now yields

    |(1/H) sum_(k>=rH) B_H(k) psi_x(k)|
          <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H)).               (7)

For the remaining indices1<=k<rH use |B_H(k)|<=H. Every positive argument of f_x in psi is <2rH<=X<=x, where f_x increases toward its maximum. Thus this whole part is at most

    rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2tau)).           (8)

This is why the extremely small w_X(k) near k=1 causes no uncontrolled inverse-weight factor. Applying (5) indiscriminately there would be false for long windows. The explicit split pays that strongest endpoint objection.

## 3. Reconstructing the complete integer-state coefficient

For the rough source

    R_chi(t,y)=sum_(n<=t;P-(n)>y)mu(n)chi(n), P-(1)=infinity,

least-prime factorization gives R=1-sum_(y<p<=t)chi(p)R(t/p,p). Let F be floor-invariant and define its actual defect by the same recurrence. Every increasing-prime path is a distinct squarefree product d, with sign mu(d)chi(d). Grouping by p=P+(d) and m=floor(N/d), rather than by path depth, gives exactly

    F(N,1)-M_chi(N)=Delta(N,1)+sum_(p,m)C_(N,chi)(m,p)Delta(m,p),
    C_(N,chi)(m,p)=-chi(p)
      sum_(N/[p(m+1)]<v<=N/(pm);P+(v)<p)mu(v)chi(v).     (V4)

The lower endpoint is strict and the upper endpoint inclusive. The v=1 term is included. Strict prime ordering removes repeated primes; zero character values remain zero. This is G92's actual complete coefficient, not its unmerged norm.

Fix an integer r>=1 and an exact integer collar m<=p^r. The norm on independently bounded remaining defects is

    B_(r,chi)(N)=1+sum_(p,m>p^r)|C_(N,chi)(m,p)|.

For a principal chi0 and unramified p, the intervals for all m>p^r form a disjoint cover of

    (0,U_p], U_p=N/[p(p^r+1)].

Therefore

    sum_(m>p^r)C_(N,chi0)(m,p)=-W_q(U_p,p-).            (V5)

The plus one is mandatory in this exact identity. It comes from the first allowed integer m=p^r+1; replacing it by p^r before telescoping would change the source. The later asymptotic replacement U_p=(N/p^(r+1))(1+O(p^(-r))) is legitimate and explicitly paid.

statement:
## 6. The other five tests and the original card04 proposal

**03, divisibility coercivity.** For sigma>0, in the explicit Hilbert norm sum_n |v(n)|^2 n^(-2*sigma), a prime dilation becomes z_p S_p on orthonormal prime-power chains, z_p=chi(p)p^(-sigma). For a finite prime tensor B=product_p(I-z_p S_p),

    ||B||=product_p(1+|z_p|),
    inf_(||v||=1)||Bv||=product_p(1-|z_p|).

Long phase-aligned chains approximate both extremes: their squared ratios are (1+/-|z|)^2 minus/plus 2|z|/K. Tensoring the finite approximants proves the product formulas. Ramified primes with chi(p)=0 contribute identity. For sigma<=1 the lower product collapses as more unramified primes enter. The vacuum norm squared product(1+p^(-2*sigma)) stays finite for sigma>1/2, but the Gaussian dual readout costs X^(sigma+1/2), so this alone gives no gamma<1. AM18--21 already establishes the stronger appropriate finite-N inverse behavior, including subpower costs at sigma>=1/2. A full prime tensor, a finite divisor section, and an actual source readout are different objects. This is duplicate/scoped failure, not an actual arithmetic lower bound.

**04, first-test lag deletion.** Bounding each lag by the diagonal O(X), then summing O(H) lags, costs O(XH); the resulting requirement theta<2*gamma-1 was already G22/G42. The later finite adjoint correction is an explicitly changed continuation using G72. The useful W48.1 increment should not be attributed to a new autocorrelation identity.

**22, fixed-arity inverse.** Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), ell(n)=chi(n), m(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y) as a pointwise truncation, and r0=a-m. All stars below denote Dirichlet convolution. The exact identity a*ell=delta gives, for every fixed integer k>=1,

    a = r0^{*k}*ell^{*(k-1)}
        +sum_(j=1)^k (-1)^(j+1) binom(k,j) m^{*j}*ell^{*(j-1)}.   (R6)

This follows by expanding (a-m)^{*k} and canceling a*ell; all shared primes, lower support endpoints and character zeros remain. It is the W01 RA4 identity, with the LP5 k=3 specialization already explicit. For a prime p not dividing the character modulus, q_p=delta-p delta_p makes ell*q_p periodic and mean zero, for principal as well as nonprincipal chi. Multiplying (R6) by q_p^{*(k-1)} gives the author's filtered identity. For fixed k and Y<X^(1/k-eta), the short restoration terms have arguments X/d tending to infinity; fixed periodic mean-zero Gaussian convolution decays by any prescribed power, with its polynomial coefficient mass paid. This is W01/W35 restoration ancestry.

The Mellin multiplier (1-p^(1-s))^(k-1) is nonzero in 0<Re(s)<1, but has zeros ON Re(s)=1. Thus this filtered identity gives the claimed return within the open strip; a statement about the entire region Re(s)>gamma must retain the independently inherited right-edge complement. It cannot obtain that boundary from this numerator alone. This qualification does not affect the direct unfiltered W48.1 return.

**16, one-term dominance.** The finite mu*chi Dirichlet polynomial has constant term 1. At sigma>0 any single other term has modulus at most n^(-sigma)<1, so it cannot strictly dominate the constant term plus the other absolute terms. Constant-term dominance reduces to an absolute sum less than 1; unramified prime terms already make that criterion fail in the sigma<=1 range as the cutoff grows. The Euler-product version similarly demands product_p(1+p^(-sigma))<2. Only this ungrouped triangle criterion fails; phase-aware grouping remains untested.

**20, all-height anchored budget.** In a half-plane Re(s)>a, let rho=beta+iT, beta>a, and

    B(s)=(s-rho)/(s+conjugate(rho)-2a), F(s)=B(s)/B(s0),

where real s0>a and T!=0. B has its pole left of the half-plane and |B|<=1 there. F(s0)=1 and F(rho)=0, while

    log sup|F|
      <= (1/2) log(1+4(s0-a)(beta-a)/((s0-beta)^2+T^2))
       ->0 as |T|->infinity.

A conjugate pair gives real symmetry with twice this budget. Therefore an unspecified small fixed boundary budget plus one anchor cannot exclude arbitrarily high zeros in this abstract holomorphic class. This retains F21/F22/W22/R33 ancestry. It is not a constructed Dirichlet L function or a disproof of an arithmetic boundary estimate.

**02, fractional inverse.** For the raw principal source L^(-1/k), k>1, a complete Gaussian exponent gamma<1 would supply a holomorphic Z with Z^k L=exp(k*tau*s^2/2). The simple pole of L at 1 would require k*ord_1(Z)=1, impossible for holomorphic Z. Normalizing the principal pole changes this source, exactly as W22/R35.21--23 already records. Nonprincipal characters do not share this particular obstruction. Convolution recombination alone does not divide the growth exponent: k convolutions of exp(beta*y)1_(y>=0) equal exp(beta*y)y^(k-1)/(k-1)!, up to normalization. The exponent remains beta. This is a scoped raw-source failure and a duplicate normalized bridge, not a universal fractional-method impossibility.

### 2.3 A moving small-prime sector is also fully paid

Choose A>0 with alpha=A(1-gamma)<1 and split K_1 at

    p<=(2+y)^A for y>=0; the hard sector has p>(2+y)^A. (5)

The threshold is real, with equality in the small sector. Write Q_small and Q_hard for the exact corresponding pieces of Q_1. For sufficiently large y, A log(2+y)<=y/2. Thus every small-prime delay v=y-log p has y/2<=v<=y. Its weighted row sum is bounded by

    sum_(p<=(2+y)^A)log p*p^-gamma
      <=C_(A,gamma)(2+y)^alpha log(2+y).                (6)

This deliberately coarse estimate sums over ALL integers. For a column v from that large-y region, y<=2v, so the same bound holds with p<=(2+2v)^A and a changed fixed constant. Apply 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, sum and change variables in the second term. Since (2+v)^alpha log(2+v)=o(v), for every eta>0

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_(eta,A,gamma,tau),           (7)

uniformly in R. The bounded initial y region has finitely many primes and input v in a fixed interval, so its full bill is part of B. The upper endpoint y<=R implies v<=R; no future values of z or unpriced transfer occur. This is a quadratic-form relative bound on the actual delayed source, not an operator contraction on arbitrary growing functions.

### 2.4 Global density error, complete core, and exact coefficient 2

Set p=sqrt(X)v, q=sqrt(X)w with v,w>=kappa>=1. For a=L/2 and
b=log v,c=log w>=0, elementary subtraction gives

    |1/((a+b)(a+c))-1/a^2| <= (b+c)/a^3.

This is a GLOBAL inequality, not a Taylor series on a bounded prime
rectangle. It replaces the prime density by 4/L^2 with an error at
most 8(log v+log w)/L^3. The error is integrable over every core:

    sum_r integral_(v,w>=kappa)
       (1+log v+log w)g(log(rvw/s))dvdw < C_(tau,kappa). (R2.5)

For full details, set y=vw. The r-th integral in (R2.5) is

    integral_(kappa^2)^infinity
       (1+log y)log(y/kappa^2)g(log(ry/s))dy.

Now put v_r=log(rkappa^2/s) and log(y/kappa^2)=h>=0. This equals

    kappa^2 integral_0^infinity
       exp(h)(1+2log kappa+h)h g(h+v_r)dh.

For any fixed B>0, the bound g(u)<=C_(tau,B)exp(-(B+2)u), valid for
all real u by completing the square, bounds this by C r^(-B-2)
uniformly in s. Summing r proves (R2.5), including the finite small
cores. It also proves absolute and compact-q uniform convergence of
the series defining Phi. No conditional moment has been completed.

The leading integral without the logarithmic weight is exactly

    integral_(v,w>=kappa) g(log(rvw/s))dvdw
       =integral_(kappa^2)^infinity log(y/kappa^2)g(log(ry/s))dy
       =(s/r)J(log(rkappa^2/s)).                      (R2.6)

The factors in (R2.4) are therefore: unordered 1/2, Jacobian X,
prime density 4/L^2, and (s/r) from (R2.6). Their product is
2x/(rL^2), giving exactly (R2.1). The full density error is
O(X/L^3) by (R2.5). All constants are uniform in x, but no moving
kappa or varying tau uniformity has been proved or claimed.

# [research revision]: compensated nonlinear source and paid cutoff coupling

The author develops the actual mean-zero compensated source; the independent
critic extends it to arbitrary product-bounded cutoffs and a one-Mobius core.
Root accepts G152–G154 after complete written review. These are useful
restricted estimates and an actual coupled cancellation. The complete
signed power estimate is OPEN. Written source-relative
c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636 is unchanged. F0/analytic ancestry,
inherited positive-slot uniformity and external admission remain OPEN.

Evidence: [author](compensated-source/report.md),
[independent review](compensated-source-review/report.md),
[retention manifest](retention-manifest.json), and the prior
[G140–G142 nonlinear source](../[research revision]/nonlinear-source-integration.md).
Twelve original files are byte-preserved. Nine review-input pins include
five author files and four earlier mathematical sources. Original claims
are never copied. Both mathematical deadlines were met. A fourth reviewer
stream failure occurred after its normal own-claim release and full hash
readback; the frozen STOP/report and native release are the handoff evidence.
No missing final chat text is represented as received.

## G152. A complete compensated small-divisor estimate and zero return

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo q, with all natural zeros,
and choose a fixed prime p not dividing q. Put Q=pq and use Dirichlet
convolution, with delta_m denoting the coefficient at m:

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),  h(n)=chi(n),  a*h=delta_1,
    q_p=delta_1-p chi(p)delta_p,
    b_p=q_p*h=chi(n)(1-p 1_(p|n)),
    c_p=q_p*a=a(n)-p chi(p)1_(p|n)a(n/p).

The Q-periodic b_p has mean zero. Indeed its complete sum is
p(1-chi(p)) sum_(r mod q)chi(r), zero by orthogonality or, for a
principal character, chi(p)=1. The unramified-prime hypothesis matters.
The changed c_p can be nonzero on squareful integers; retain these terms.
It has |c_p|<=p+1, and still vanishes on nonunits modulo q.

For fixed b>1 and integer k>2 define

    f_x(n)=exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k),
    C_p(x)=sum_(n>=1)c_p(n)f_x(n),
    ||F||_j=(integral_X^(2X)|F(x)|^j dx/x)^(1/j), j=1,2.

All cutoffs depend on X, chi and fixed parameters, and are frozen before
real x varies. Use literal closed n<=U and strict n>U for real U.
The tempting identity f_x(pn)=f_(x/p)(n) is false when b>1.

With m_U=a 1_(n<=U), u_U=a-m_U, set

    S_(U,V)=m_U*m_V*b_p,  R_(U,V)=u_U*u_V*b_p.
    c_p=q_p*m_U+q_p*m_V-S_(U,V)+R_(U,V).        (91.1)

Every ordered factor pair and every cofactor remains. Each S or R
coefficient has absolute value <=p d_3(n)<<_(p,eta)n^eta, uniformly
in U,V. The two short terms cost O_p(U+V) in both shell norms.

### Full divisor-bounded tail

If |v_n|<=A_eta n^eta and 2eta<k-2, the complete tail satisfies

    ||sum_(n>M)v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      <<_(b,k,eta) A_eta^2
          [X^(b(1+2eta))+X^k M^(2-k+2eta)].    (91.2)

Use a nonnegative C2 majorant equal to one on the original shell,
supported in [1/2,4], with flat endpoints. After v=u^(-k), the
off-diagonal amplitude and two derivatives are uniformly bounded:
powers of A=(n+m)/X^b are absorbed by exp(-cA). Two integrations by
parts give the kernel

    min(1,(X^k/|n^k-m^k|)^2).

For m<n, n^k-m^k>=n^(k-1)(n-m). Writing delta=X^k/n^(k-1), the
full sum over gaps of min(1,(delta/gap)^2) is O(delta), including
delta<1. Sum n^(2eta)delta over n>M; the damped diagonal supplies
the first term in (91.2). Finite expansions followed by summable
domination justify the infinite calculation. Both orientations and
every cross are included; no off-diagonal part is dropped.

For 1/2<gamma<1, b<=2gamma and

    r=(k-2gamma)/(k-2), M=X^r,

(91.2) gives an O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) tail in L2 and L1 for every
epsilon>0, choosing eta after epsilon. This includes b=2gamma.
The tail proof needs no r<b restriction; damping helps when r>=b.

### Completed small-divisor source

Assume u=k-(k-1)r=2gamma-r>0 and put eta_0=1/(100kpq).
For ANY real U,V>=1 with UV<=eta_0 X^u,

    ||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_1
      +||sum_n S_(U,V)(n)f_x(n)||_2
               <<_(p,q,b,k,gamma,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (91.3)

On n<=M, expand b_p in its nonzero Fourier modes j/Q. For D=de,
the phase as a function of the cofactor is

    F_j(t)=jt/Q-(Dt/x)^k/(2pi).

Since D<=UV and Dt<=M, its derivative correction is at most
k UV M^(k-1)/(2pi X^k)<=k eta_0/(2pi)<1/(2Q).
Thus F_j' and each discrete phase increment lie monotonically between
1/(2Q) and 1-1/(2Q). Summation by parts with
1/(exp(2pi i v)-1)=-1/2-(i/2)cot(pi v) bounds every prefix by O(Q).
Abel summation preserves that bound under the actual decreasing damping.
This includes empty and one-term prefixes. Summing all ordered d,e costs
O_(p,q)(UV)=O(X^u); u<gamma. The complete n>M contribution is (91.2).
No Fourier gap is asserted beyond M. Also U+V<=UV+1 pays the short
terms, uniformly in the asymmetric choices.

This is an actual unrestricted small-product estimate, not an arbitrary
coefficient model. It does NOT allow UV=X^gamma without a new argument.

### Complete core and all-height return

For b=3/2,k=6 and gamma>=3/4, set L=X^gamma and freeze
U=V=floor(sqrt(eta_0) X^(u/2)). For sufficiently large X these exceed
one. Define the full balanced core

    T_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>U,e>V,L<del<=M)
       mu(d)mu(e)chi(del)(1-p 1_(p|l))f_x(del).

Its low prefix costs O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) by the divisor bound; its
full tail, S and short terms are already paid. Consequently

    ||C_p-T_(p,chi,X)||_j << X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.4)

Every-epsilon whole-shell bounds for T and C_p are equivalent separately
in L1 and L2. L2 is sufficient for L1; the converse is not inferred.

The G140 Mellin calculation applies to the bounded changed coefficients.
After v=nt and rotation by a fixed admissible angle alpha, it gives

    integral_0^infinity C_p(1/t)t^(s-1)dt
       =A_0(s)P_p(s)/L(s,chi)+E_p(s),
    A_0(s)=Gamma(s/6) exp(-i pi s/12)/6,
    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),                              (91.5)

where E_p is holomorphic for Re s>1/2 and A_0 has no zero for Re s>0.
Initially the identity holds in an absolutely convergent right half-plane.
The rotated remainder is locally uniform at EVERY fixed height; constants
can depend on height and chi. At x down to zero,
|C_p(x)|<=(p+1)/(exp(x^(-b))-1). The hypothesized every-epsilon L1 shell
bound therefore makes the left side holomorphic on Re s>gamma.

Choose two distinct fixed unramified primes p1,p2. For a nonprincipal
character choose p1 with chi(p1)!=1: a unit with nontrivial character
value has a prime factor with nontrivial value. Each P_p zero has Re s=1.
A common zero 1+it with t!=0 would make both t log(p_j)/(2pi) nonzero
rationals, contradicting irrationality of log(p1)/log(p2). At t=0 the
chosen nonprincipal p1 prevents a common zero. For a principal character
the possible common point is its allowed L pole, not an ordinary zero.
Thus bounds for both fixed compensated cores exclude ALL ordinary zeros
with Re s>gamma. No line-one nonvanishing theorem is hidden in the return.
Actual imprimitive Euler holes stay present; their zeros lie on Re s=0.

More generally, for each fixed gamma>1/2 choose k large enough that u>0,
1<b<=2gamma, and fixed K with 1-(b-1)K<gamma. Retain ALL shifts
A_j(s)P_p(s+(b-1)j)/L(s+(b-1)j) in G140's K-term expansion.
Starting above Re s=1, finite-strip descent of width b-1 gives the same
return. No growing k,K, uniform limit gamma down to 1/2, or endpoint
theorem is claimed. This extends the previous conditional architecture;
its required arithmetic power premise remains open.

## G153. Asymmetric completion and a one-Mobius core

The independent critic takes A=floor(eta_0 X^u), V=1. Since m_1=delta_1,

    (a-delta_1)*b_p=q_p-b_p=:h_p,
    R_(A,1)=u_A*h_p.

Explicitly h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p), and otherwise
h_p(j)=-chi(j)(1-p 1_(p|j)); |h_p(j)|<=p-1.
The two exceptional coefficients must remain. This h_p is not globally
periodic mean-zero after those corrections.

The actual asymmetric core is

    A_(p,chi,X)(x)=sum_(d>A,j>=2,L<dj<=M)
                    mu(d)chi(d)h_p(j)f_x(dj).            (91.6)

Its coefficients are bounded by (p-1)d_2(n); the literal cofactor cap is
j<=M/(A+1)<<_(p,q,k)X^(r-u), not a unit-constant cap. Applying (91.3)
with these cutoffs and retaining all complementary sources gives

    ||C_p-A_(p,chi,X)||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon), j=1,2.       (91.7)

The same two-prime return applies. This is an exact simplification of the
remaining source, not a proof of its power bound.

When p does not divide n the merged residual coefficient is

    (u_A*h_p)(n)=-chi(n)sum_(d|n,A<d<n)mu(d).

It vanishes on primes. For distinct primes r,s not dividing pq it equals
chi(rs)(1_(r>A)+1_(s>A)); it vanishes when both primes are <=A.
This coefficient identity retains the original product cut and all signs.

| Conditional c | gamma | r | u | Balanced cut exponent | Asymmetric cut exponent | Cofactor exponent r-u |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| .1252 | 2187/2500 | 5313/5000 | 687/1000 | 687/2000 | 687/1000 | 939/2500 |
| 1/6 | 5/6 | 13/12 | 7/12 | 7/24 | 7/12 | 1/2 |
| 1/4 | 3/4 | 9/8 | 3/8 | 3/16 | 3/8 | 3/4 |

Every row is conditional. The first would improve c11 by
135091/2500000000. At the first two rows u>1/2 and 2u>r, so the
asymmetric core absorbs the balanced semiprime cell near n~X and
comparable semiprimes near the upper product cap. Neither holds for
the displayed 1/4 row. The old 2/5 architecture also remains conditional.

## G154. Actual coupled cancellation, and the surviving obstruction

For a principal character let B_X be the selected ordered source with
distinct primes d,e in (sqrt(X)/2,sqrt(X/2)] and cofactor l=1. For large
X these primes are unramified and satisfy every balanced-core cutoff.
If J is their number, the ordinary prime number theorem gives
J~2(1/sqrt(2)-1/2)sqrt(X)/log X. Uniformly on the full real shell,

    Re B_X(x)>=exp(-X^(1-b)/2)cos(2^(-k))J(J-1).

Thus ||B_X||_1 and ||B_X||_2 are comparable to X/log^2 X. The only
external input is ordinary PNT, e.g. [Selberg's original theorem (1.1),
printed p.305](https://www.math.lsu.edu/~mahlburg/teaching/handouts/2014-7230/Selberg-ElemPNT1949.pdf),
used here for fixed-proportion prime counts. This is a lower bound for
the selected arithmetic cell. It is NOT a lower bound for an unselected
dyadic factor box, T, R or C_p. It obstructs a triangle budget that pays
this cell separately at X^(gamma+epsilon), epsilon<1-gamma.

When u>1/2 the asymmetric core has zero coefficient on this cell, while
the balanced core has coefficient two per unordered pair. Put

    D_X=T_(p,chi,X)-A_(p,chi,X), K_X=D_X-B_X.

Equations (91.4) and (91.7) UNCONDITIONALLY give

    ||B_X+K_X||_j<<X^(gamma+epsilon)=o(||B_X||_j), j=1,2.

K_X contains every other exact term in the difference, with its signs
and cutoffs. In L2 this implies

    ||K_X||_2/||B_X||_2 -> 1,
    Re <B_X,K_X>=-||B_X||_2^2
                   +O(||B_X||_2 X^(gamma+epsilon)).

Their normalized real correlation tends to -1. By Markov's inequality,
outside logarithmic measure O_delta(X^(gamma-1+epsilon)log^2 X),
Re K_X<=-(1-delta)Re B_X. This is an actual paid cancellation across
representations; neither OPEN core estimate was used.

The asymmetric source still has an actual large positive cell. Take
j=p and primes d in (X/(4p),X/(2p)]. They satisfy d>A and L<pd<=M;
mu(d)h_p(p)=+1 for principal chi. The FULL merged coefficient at pd
is also +1: the other divisor labels contribute zero. This selected
source has both norms comparable to X/log X. Paying it alone therefore
still misses every fixed gamma<1. The balanced representation excludes
this fixed-small-prime factor, whereas the asymmetric representation
excludes the previous balanced semiprimes. These facts concern selected
cells, not lower bounds for either full signed core.

The next useful test must couple the terminal prime–cofactor cell with
its composite partners before taking absolute values, or replace the
upstream detector with a fully priced bridge. Repeating only the tail
bound or paying each positive cell separately cannot close this route.

## Comparison, source limits and verification

The generic full divisor bound is X^(1+epsilon), above every target.
G142's actual Green–Tao logarithmic estimate transfers to the bounded
compensated source with fixed p, yielding the previous X^(3/4) plus
X(log X)^(-D) scale. Fixed D cannot grow with X and supplies no power
gain. That earlier theorem is reused, not counted as new [research revision] credit.

The published [Matomaki–Teravainen paper](https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/32826?nt=1)
was inspected as outside-source motivation: Theorems1.1/1.5 give
logarithmic short-interval savings, and Lemma3.1 retains its restricted
prime range, small residual factor and explicit extraction error. None
is imported as the missing nonlinear, character-uniform power estimate.

The author helper checks four actual characters, three cutoff pairs
through n=480, natural zeros, the squareful correction, a ramified-prime
negative control and four rational target rows. The independent helper
checks four characters and three asymmetric cutoffs through n=720,
merged semiprime/terminal coefficients and the same budgets. Root read
both complete helpers and receipts; no unchanged helper was rerun.
Finite algebra is diagnostic evidence, not an analytic proof.

The accepted arguments retain all signs, shared primes, real shells,
strict endpoints, principal/imprimitive cases and every complementary
term. L1 and L2 premises remain distinct. No native positive-slot
improvement or full physical return is inferred. All29 families/109
children, later developments, nearer targets,1/6 and1/4 remain available.
No formalization, kernel work, new proof packet or public-record claim.

## 3. W43-15: exact Newton feedback and the missing detector

Write m_Y(n)=mu(n)1_(n<=Y), d_Y=delta-1*m_Y, M_Y(s)=sum_(n<=Y)mu(n)n^(-s), D_Y(s)=1-zeta(s)M_Y(s). For fixed integer k>=1,

    q_(Y,k)=m_Y*(delta+d_Y+...+d_Y^{*(k-1)}),
    delta-1*q_(Y,k)=d_Y^{*k}.                         (R43-N1)

This is the geometric identity in Dirichlet convolution. Because d_Y(n)=0 for n<=Y, its kth power vanishes for n<(Y+1)^k, and convolution by mu gives q_(Y,k)(n)=mu(n) on that strict prefix. There is no free improved coefficient list there: truncating below the cap returns the ordinary longer Mobius prefix. The equality endpoint need not vanish.

For the Dirichlet series Q=M_Y sum_(j<k)D_Y^j, at every zeta zero rho in the critical strip, D_Y(rho)=1 and Q(rho)=kM_Y(rho). These values are finite; Q is a polynomial in zeta and M_Y locally at rho. If Q^tr is the prefix polynomial and T=Q-Q^tr, then

    1-zeta Q^tr=D_Y^k+zeta T.                        (R43-N2)

Both sides equal1 at rho. The apparent quotient(1-D_Y^k)/zeta has a removable singularity, not the required nonzero reciprocal pole. A small Gaussian norm of the defect alone does not have the old detector's zero return. This is an analytic issue independent of finite coefficient agreement or a formal squaring gain. T here means the exact continued difference; absolute convergence of its coefficient series in the critical strip is not asserted.

For Y-rough n>1, only divisor1 contributes to1*m_Y, so d_Y(n)=-1. Consequently d_Y^{*k}(n)=(-1)^k F_k(n), where F_k counts ordered factorizations into k factors>1. It vanishes for Omega(n)<k and equals k!/product_p v_p(n)! for Omega(n)=k. Prime powers and collisions are included. This gives a one-sign complete rough Gaussian subfield, not a one-sign full defect.

Put Y=floor(X^theta), k fixed. If0<theta<=1/k, take k distinct primes from(X^(1/k),2X^(1/k)]. They all exceed Y, including at equality. Their products lie in[X,2^kX]. For x in[X,2X] the fixed Gaussian has a positive minimum on the resulting compact logarithmic range. Prime counting gives at least a constant times X/(log X)^k such weighted products after ordered/unordered multiplicities are paid. Thus the rough field has magnitude at least that amount. This rules out a fixed power saving from its absolute majorant; it is not a lower bound for the full signed defect, whose complementary terms can cancel it. The complete rough field is well defined by the divisor bound and Gaussian decay.

If theta>1/k, the exact support starts beyond X^(k theta). Since |d_Y|<=d_2 and |d_Y^{*k}|<=d_(2k), divisor summation bounds the entire absolute Gaussian field by O_A(X^(-A)) for every fixed A. The logarithmic gap is(k theta-1)log X+O(1), so its Gaussian square decay beats the positive counting factor and fixed logarithmic powers. This small physical defect still has D_Y(rho)^k=1: moving Y with X and moving its support beyond the observed scale do not create a fixed reciprocal-pole detector.

The dichotomy includes theta=1/k in the obstruction branch and excludes growing k from both fixed-constant arguments. Growing-order signed analysis remains a distinct reopening, owing every k-dependent constant, exact truncation correction and zero return. For fixed ordinary chi, twisting commutes with convolution even at ramified primes because chi is completely multiplicative with its natural zero extension. The corresponding defect identity and prefix result hold for L(s,chi); rough absolute lower bounds can omit finitely many conductor primes, but no signed lower bound after complex twisting follows. No Eisenstein, moving-conductor or H transfer is implicit.

The independent finite check uses divisor sums through800, Y=3,7 and k=1,2,3. It verifies all coefficient identities, strict prefixes and rough signs; the uniform proofs above establish what finite checking cannot.

statement:
## 5. Full product moment: two added slots and every diagonal

Let

    V_D,2(x)=W_P(x) (log D/log(Dx))^2.

Its required Euler, real and scale derivatives are uniformly bounded on
the original annulus because m has a fixed positive lower bound. The exact
convolution identity is

    S^[omega](D)=1/(log D)^2 sum_(p,q in J)
       (log Np)(log Nq) phi_u(pq)/sqrt(Np Nq)
                         S(D/(Np Nq);V_D,2).         (10)

No primality multiplicity, fixed hole or natural zero is changed. Both
p=q and p!=q occur, and each cofactor is unrestricted except for its
original plain support and character zeros.

First take p!=q and dyads P1<=Np<2P1, P2<=Nq<2P2, with the exact J
endpoints kept in the arithmetic supports. Their log_U lengths satisfy
eta-small<=lambda_i<=2eta, so the total new slot width is at most4eta.
Put E=D/(P1 P2) and separate the common profile V_D,2(y1 y2 z), where
y1=Np/P1, y2=Nq/P2 and z=Nc/E. The normalization is EXACT:

    P1^(-1/2) P2^(-1/2) E^(-1/2)=D^(-1/2).

Use fixed coefficients log Np/log U and log Nq/log U, extracting the
common scalar(log U/log D)^2=1/m^2. They are bounded, row independent
and are not differentiated when D varies. The sharp band endpoints stay
frozen when scales or heights are differentiated.

Apply(4) to the shortened plain first. Once the disjoint-support/collision
steps below are paid, MI on M(R), Q and the two new slots gives

    ||M Q * this complete off-diagonal dyad||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta(P1 P2)^(-beta).     (11)

Indeed the first gate is at most
1-.01017+8eta<=1-.00217 before fine losses. The second is at most
2-.02034+4v+32eta<=3-.78834. Both have fixed slack on the WHOLE window.
No new hypothesis about MP or arbitrary merged column weights is used.

Here is the complete collision payment. The original pools are disjoint,
so each of the two distinct new primes can equal at most one old slot
prime; if both do, those old slots are distinct. Split into these finitely
many equality patterns before taking norms. For each new/old equality,
remove that old slot and extract its common prime. Its exact normalizers
are (P_i0 Np)^(-1/2); nonempty annuli force P_i0 comparable to the new
prime dyad. The absolute mass sum_p(P_i0 Np)^(-1/2)<<1 by ideal counting.
The shortened plain factor still contributes the full(P1 P2)^(-beta/2).
The phase phi_u(p)^2 is a contraction with its natural zero, and its
original coefficient and height are retained. Removing slots only eases
MI. With two equalities the two absolute masses are each paid once.
Any remaining prime is required to differ from the extracted fixed primes
by deleting those primes from its row-independent support for that outer
term. This is within MI's arbitrary prime-support contract.

For the remaining distinct active prime variables use a single finite
coloring on the UNION of their full prime-IDEAL pools. If there are h
active indices, assign each prime independently one of h colors. Then

    1_(p_1,...,p_h all distinct)
       =h^h E_color product_i 1_(color(p_i)=i).        (12)

For distinct primes the event has probability h^(-h); if two indices
coincide it is impossible. Under each coloring the active supports are
disjoint and all coefficients remain bounded and row independent. Hilbert
Minkowski under the NORMALIZED measure costs h^h, a fixed constant, not
the number of colorings. If no active prime variables remain, the empty
product is1 and the unmarked MI is applied without coloring; h=1 is trivial.
The original slot count K0 and h<=K0+2 are fixed
before U. Different ideals of the same norm have different color labels.
This covers two new primes lying in the same old pool, in overlapping
new dyads, or in different old pools. No equality pattern is omitted.
The inverse may contain any of these primes: that interaction remains
inside literal MI and is never declared coprime.

For p=q retain the COMPLETE old Q inside its original MI norm. Apply the
plain upper bound and take absolute values only over p. In a dyad P,

    sum_p (log Np/log D)^2 (Np)^(-1-beta)
       << U^epsilon P^(-beta).                       (13)

Thus the squared diagonal norm is at most
H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta Z^(-2beta). A coincidence of this p with an old
slot or the inverse needs no extra omission: the extracted phi_u(p)^2
is only removed as a row contraction, while the full Q and inverse stay
in the norm. This also pays the possible triple equality p=q=p_i.

Summing all dyads and finite patterns by Hilbert triangle gives

    ||M S^[omega] Q||_Omega^2
       << H_J U^(1+epsilon) D^beta Z^(-2beta).        (14)

This estimate is independent of the old joint cut. The only elementary
count used here is O(x) ideals of norm<=x, obtained from the original
primary Eisenstein lattice; no prime density theorem is used.

### 3.3 Error budget and surviving arithmetic target

For any desired gamma in(1/2,1), put c=1-gamma. Choose P_X and D_X with Q<=X^(1-delta) and

    Pr(K>D_X)<=X^(-2c-eta)                            (C6)

for a fixed eta>0. Then C4 has size O(X^(gamma-eta/2))+O_A(X^-A). Thus a complete shell bound ||F_(P,D,chi)||_2<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon) is sufficient for the same original exponent gamma and its full zero exclusion.

A coarse explicit order suffices. If P is contained in primes<=z with z<=C log X, the elementary integer harmonic bound gives lambda<=4(1+log z)=O(loglog X). For any fixed eta>0,

    D_X=ceil((2c+eta) log X/loglog X)                  (C7)

makes C3 at most X^(-2c-eta+o(1)), so C6 holds with any smaller positive buffer, for example eta/2; if D_X>=|P| the error is simply zero. Near the current endpoint this coefficient is about.250278; for c=1/6 it is1/3, and for c=1/4 it is1/2. One must also select P to satisfy its literal Q bound; P may be fixed or the maximal prime prefix under that bound. C7 is a sufficient asymptotic bound, not a claim that a fixed small degree is adequate. The finite exact tail in C2 is the preferred constructive certificate.

To expose the rare22 drift, let m(B;u)=E_mu_u[r_P(n)chi(n)|B(n)=B], so |m|<=1. Up to the paid full-pattern error,

    F_chi/Z=sum_S A_S mhat_S,
    mhat_S=E_pi[m Z_S].                              (C8)

Degree truncation leaves the exact retained scalar sum_(|S|<=D) A_S mhat_S. Bounding its corresponding low-degree m-energy by X^(-2c+epsilon) would suffice by Cauchy. This is a deterministic signed conditional-response estimate, not a concentration conclusion. Coarse orthogonality gives only <=1 and hence field exponent1. The exact legal reference example m=a_P has norm1 and E_pi[a_P m]=1 despite independent exposed bits and E_pi a_P=0. Random revelation therefore does not create the required saving. C2–7 pay the CODEC error but leave its arithmetic retained response open.

Relative to W41 B1–6/G54, the new candidate delta is the explicit degree-energy law, certified truncation error and literal centered-dilation reconstruction. It does not replace the existing full covariance problem by exposed marginal independence. No claim of literature novelty is made for Walsh expansions, Chernoff bounds or sieve truncation.

statement:
## 8. Remaining selected tests and independent uniform audit C05

**F05.** The displayed divisor diamond Z and U multiply to identity
in both orders, including the +uv coefficient at pq. Z is the
tensor product of [[1,0],[u,1]] and [[1,0],[v,1]], in the stated
ordering. Each local normal operator has trace 2+|u|^2 and
determinant 1, so its smaller eigenvalue is exactly
(2+|u|^2-|u|sqrt(4+|u|^2))/2. Thus W39.30 and the inverse-norm
formula follow. Complex phases are unitarily removable. Passing
to Z*Z squares the condition number; it supplies no independent
gap. This is the natural normal-operator test, not a theorem about
every genuine cochain/Hodge construction. AM19--21 and G32 already
separate finite inverse bounds from the unbounded physical readout.
In particular, unconditional N^epsilon finite inverse bounds above
1/2 cannot themselves imply a new reciprocal half-plane.

**D02.** For a single exponential, translated fields are proportional
and their Gram has rank 1 regardless of its real growth exponent.
For two exponentials G=CJC*, so det G=|det C|^2 det J gives exactly
W39.32. The fourth-order coalescence statement needs nonzero mode
amplitudes, distinct shifts and a nondegenerate **weighted** measure.
To see the precise condition, let rho_2=rho+delta,
J0=integral e^(2Re(rho)t)w(t)dt>0, and let Var_mu(t)>0 under its
normalized weighted measure. Then

    det J=J0^2 Var_mu(t)|delta|^2+o(|delta|^2),
    |det C|^2=|AB|^2 e^(2Re(rho)(h1+h2))
                   (h2-h1)^2 |delta|^2+o(|delta|^2).

Expand e^(delta t) on the fixed finite interval to obtain the first
formula; its constant/linear pieces cancel in the Gram determinant,
leaving the centered second moment. Expand the two-shift determinant
for the second. Their product explains fourth order. A zero weight
or zero amplitude is degenerate and should not be called exact
fourth order. This is a precision qualification, not a repair of the
rank-one obstruction. No actual-Mobius lower bound or failure of
the different reciprocal Hankel D3 determinant follows.

**B05.** The full defect is 2Re<U,V>+||V||^2. An upper bound on
||U+V|| needs a **lower** bound on that defect before it can bound
||U||. The literal mu(1)=1,mu(2)=-1 Gaussian cell has overlap
g_(2tau)(log 2) and exact norm ratio
2[1-exp(-(log 2)^2/(4tau))]. This is <1 exactly when
tau>(log 2)/4, so the author's finite-cell test is correct. It is
the ordinary mu coefficient in W39.1, not a substitution of -1
for the original A(2)=-3 in G1. A two-label, full-line cell does
not estimate the whole uncut arithmetic field or a native masked
moment; it verifies the already known noninheritance mechanism.

**C05, frozen uniform parked audit.** Let F_tau be the normalized
fixed-coefficient Gaussian, V_tau(y)=e^(-gamma y)F_tau(y), and
E_tau=integral_a^b |V_tau|^2 dy on a finite interval. Termwise
differentiation is locally justified. The exact equations are

    partial_tau F=(1/2)partial_y^2 F,
    partial_tau V=(1/2)V_yy+gamma V_y+(gamma^2/2)V,
    dE_tau/dtau=[Re(conj(V)V_y)+gamma|V|^2]_a^b
                       -integral_a^b|V_y|^2+gamma^2 E_tau. (R39.13)

The bracket is equivalently Re[e^(-2gamma y)conj(F)F_y]_a^b.
This retains both endpoints. A whole-line identity without the
bracket requires separately proved integrability and vanishing
boundary flux. Those are not available for free at a target gamma.

For the **raw kernel in the seed**, Phi_tau=sqrt(2*pi*tau)F_tau,
the equation has the additional Phi_tau/(2tau) term. Its weighted
energy derivative has the additional E_raw/tau term. Thus its
zeroth-order energy term is (gamma^2+1/tau)E_raw, not gamma^2 E_raw.
The source report consistently switches to normalized kernels;
this distinction must survive if the parked card itself is used.

The normalized heat mode exp(tau*rho^2/2+rho y) has unchanged
log-scale real exponent Re rho. The raw mode has the additional
sqrt(2*pi*tau) amplitude only. For real beta>gamma, finite-interval
flux restores the exact derivative beta^2 E_tau (or
(beta^2+1/tau)E_raw), so suppressing that flux would give a false
monotonicity inference. This is the existing W38-06/R38.10 and
U-SCALE/F26.H failure, now checked with the seed normalization.
It does not refute a future source-specific coercive flux theorem.
It gives no new c, and no density or submask theorem by itself.

statement:
## 6. Independent transport and Jacobi derivations

Only the original smooth row factor moves from `rho(R/sqrt(K))` to `rho((R+P+P')/sqrt(K))`. Its compact-annulus smooth extension is defined on the whole plane. The mean-value theorem gives

`|rho((R+P+P')/sqrt(K))-rho(R/sqrt(K))| <= C sqrt(L/K) ||grad rho||_infinity`.

This is valid even if the joining segment leaves the annulus; one uses the global smooth extension and its bounded gradient. Every sharp support remains on the original R,P,P',pi,pi',g,g'. No indicator is differentiated or transported to the additive total.

For each frozen short pair there are at most C N B graph edges, since there are O(N) possible original prime ideals and the degree is bounded. There are O(G^2) ordered short pairs and O(K) rows. Each native phase and natural-zero character has modulus at most one, as does the complete core. Cauchy for each rooted mark sum gives

`sum_P |u_i(P)|/sqrt(q_P) <= C sqrt(L) sqrt(Omega_i)`.

Therefore the exact signed difference, after taking its absolute value and charging all counts, satisfies

`|C_E^tr-C_E| <= C G^2 K N B L sqrt(L/K) sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig`.

This proves [research revision].6 with the gradient seminorm in P_orig. No signed-subset monotonicity, common-array alteration, graph Fourier mass or radial theorem for an additive row twist was used. It is deliberately more expensive than the old norm-gap transport lemma, but the sparse degree makes it affordable.

For centering, the native local exponents are (3,4,0) at pi and (3,0,2) at pi'. The absent factor is an unrestricted constant. On the actual support both marks are units at both long primes because their norms are smaller; the row factor already enforces its own units. Only there may one insert the common-unit indicators without changing the incomplete sum.

At one prime q, count triples r,p,p' all nonzero with total t. Inclusion-exclusion yields

`h_q(t)=q^2-3q+3-1_(t=0)`.

For mark exponent b=4 or 2, convolution with the unit indicator is the negative of the two-character Jacobi convolution because convolution with the unrestricted constant vanishes. Consequently

`chi^3 * chi^b * 1_units (t) = -J(3,b) chi(t)^(3+b)`.

At t=0 this is zero, since 3+b is nonprincipal modulo six. Both Jacobi sums have absolute value sqrt(q): inputs and product are nonprincipal. The two minus signs cancel under CRT, giving exactly

```
C1(T)=J_+(pi) J_-(pi') chi_pi(T) chi_pi'(T)^(-1),
h1(T)=product_(p|pi*pi') [q_p^2-3q_p+3-1_(p|T)].
```

Thus `|C1/h1|<=C Q^(-3/2)<=C N^(-3)`, including exceptional totals where its numerator vanishes. The original short-row character, d puncture and every other coefficient stay in the folded weight; they are not silently averaged with the long-prime kernel.

The same explicit counts now give

`|M_E^(J,tr)| <= C G^2 K B L/N^2 sqrt(Omega_1 Omega_2) P_orig`.

The N^(-2) is exactly `N B * N^(-3)`, after extracting B; it is not a second Fourier normalization. All mark off-diagonals are counted. The actual primary elements are injected into the additive lattice without adding units or dividing by six.

A supported total has `T=R+P+P'`. The difference of two possible totals has norm at most C_orig(K+L). If they were congruent modulo pi*pi' and different, its norm would be at least Q. Hence `Q>C_orig(K+L)` gives one supported total per residue. The transported profile is therefore constant on each occupied residue-total fibre, with that value extended when taking the common-unit counting mean. The exact sharp row support remains `R=T-P-P'`. This verifies the needed commuting interpretation of the mean, rather than assuming it from a formal change of variables.

The centered form is exactly `R_E^(J,tr)=C_E^tr-M_E^(J,tr)`. Triangle inequality with the inherited raw graph theorem proves [research revision].8. The proof treats three separate terms; it does not require that the signed covariance or its fluctuation be positive.
title: 6. Independent transport and Jacobi derivations

## R10. What is genuinely new, and what remains open

The source identities and fixed prime dilation are old ancestors. G149's full return is also already accepted. The present Type I proof is nonetheless a substantive additional source estimate: the integrated restoration kernel has an L1 norm controlled by bounded partial sums, so it acts on ordinary L2 inputs without the Sobolev derivatives, smooth high-atom cutoff or Green-metric compression of W29. It does not claim that those older atomic norms coincide with this integrated norm.

The new frequency decomposition retains the actual endpoint and the full hyperbolic interaction. It proves a complete price for its discarded high-frequency range. The gcd and diagonal estimates are coarse elementary payments, not deep cancellation. Together they leave an exact, narrower low-frequency arithmetic task. That task remains equivalent, up to the displayed paid error, to the hard full-source growth estimate and is not automatically easier in exponent. The prime-corner obstruction, now extended to each fixed chi, explains why a further triangle inequality over arithmetic sectors cannot supply the missing power saving.

The required next estimate is the full jointly signed T^lo bound with (R11)'s endpoint and masks, at the H15 cutoffs, for every fixed ordinary character and a common gamma. The exact coefficient form, common product dependence and all restoration labels must remain inside the operator before taking its norm. A frequency sample, separately small sector, toy Hankel model, positive Hilbert--Schmidt bound or a reread of the reciprocal return is not that estimate.

No native H coefficient/mask, physical amplifier margin, separate-height Hecke estimate or new endpoint rectangle is imported. This branch can return an ordinary zero-free region directly only when its own entire norm hypothesis is proved. The accepted c11 and its source-relative limitations remain unchanged.

statement:
## Uniform S09: exact source-specific linear dual and its hidden scalar

Use the actual finite set V={n<=N:mu(n)^2=1,(n,q)=1}. Put a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), including a(1)=1. Include every internal edge e=(n,pn) with p prime, p not dividing nq, pn<=N. Define

    (Bf)_e=f(pn)+chi(p)f(n).

Writing f(n)=a(n)g(n) gives (Bf)_e=a(pn)[g(pn)-g(n)]. The graph is connected by prime deletion, so ker B is exactly span(a). This is G165's native incidence fact, reused rather than claimed new. The exact constraints Bf=0, f(1)=1 determine the actual source uniquely. They are therefore legitimate, but uniqueness alone supplies no magnitude estimate for a target sum.

For arbitrary complex weights w_n let L_w(f)=sum_n w_n f(n). A complete exact dual identity

    L_w(f)=lambda f(1)+sum_e t_e(Bf)_e for EVERY f         (A4)

exists, and its unit coefficient is FORCED to be

    lambda=M_w:=sum_n w_n a(n).                           (A5)

Necessity follows by substituting f=a. Sufficiency follows since w-lambda e_1 annihilates ker B and hence belongs to range(B^T); all pairings here are bilinear, with the appropriate transpose, not a silently changed conjugate pairing. This range statement is finite-dimensional and applies to complex characters.

There is a constructive exact formula. Choose for each v>1 one parent v/p with p dividing v. These prime-deletion parents give a tree rooted at1, whose edges directed away from1 are original prime-adjoining edges. For a child v define F_v=sum_(u in subtree(v))w_u a(u). Since g(u)=g(1)+sum_(v on path1->u)(g(v)-g(parent(v))), exchanging these FINITE sums gives

    L_w(f)=M_w f(1)+sum_(v not1) [F_v/a(v)] (Bf)_(parent(v),v).
                                                               (A6)

All phases have modulus1 and all natural zero states were removed before inversion. For approximate constraints, the same identity retains the FULL residual bill sum_v |F_v| |(Bf)_e|. Changing the tree can change this bill but cannot change the coefficient M_w of the unit observation. Subtree sums are actual signed arithmetic sums, not a free positive constant.

A precise optimization formulation sharpens the issue. Allow any complex lambda,t and set r=w-lambda e_1-B^T t. Then

    M_w=lambda+sum_n r_n a(n),
    |M_w|<=|lambda|+||r||_1.

Moreover

    inf_(lambda,t) (|lambda|+||w-lambda e_1-B^T t||_1)=|M_w|. (A7)

The lower bound is the preceding triangle inequality. Equality is attained with lambda=M_w and an exact solution(A4), for which r=0. Thus the unrestricted dual optimization is exactly the actual signed target in another representation. This does not make a CONSTRUCTIVE certificate useless: explicit lambda,t whose full residual price is N^(gamma+epsilon) would prove the desired source bound. It does prevent claiming a saving merely from feasibility, compression, or the presence of multiplicative constraints.

Adding coprime multiplicativity identities does not add information to this already singleton feasible set. Enforcing false periodicity of mu(n)chi(n) is impermissible; chi is periodic, the twisted Mobius sequence is not generally periodic. A promising new restriction must supply a quantitatively controlled certificate or observation beyond the internal gradients, with all boundary terms paid. A positive norm of Bf alone cannot see a(n); adding outgoing zero-extension observations is precisely the already priced boundary route of G165.

This audit develops the complete tree dual and exact residual optimization, while preserving the possibility of an arithmetic certificate. It gives no Mertens lower bound, no fixed-character impossibility theorem, and no new c. The next useful test is an explicit structured t whose residual sum is proved small WITHOUT placing the desired sum in lambda. The one-way all-height return then needs the complete every-scale source bound, with the principal pole convention and natural zeros retained.

Both audited routes remain open for signed arithmetic development. Neither finite universal algebra nor a favorable review certifies a larger zero-free constant.

statement:
## 3. The entire positive chain mass really has exponent one

Write F_0=1 and F_j=sum_(k=1)^j k!S(j,k) for j>=1. The map that orders each block internally, concatenates the blocks and records cuts injects ordered set partitions into permutations with cuts. Therefore F_j<=2^(j-1)j!.

Fix sigma>1. With w_p=p^-sigma, choose a finite prime cutoff Y so that R_sigma=sum_(p>Y)w_p<1/4. If r is the number of small primes, the elementary symmetric functions obey

    e_j(all)=sum_(a+b=j,0<=a<=r)e_a(small)e_b(tail),
    e_b(tail)<=R_sigma^b/b!.

For each fixed a, the complete contribution after multiplying by the bound for F_j is bounded by a fixed constant times

    sum_(b>=0)(2R_sigma)^b (a+b)!/b!.

The factorial ratio is a polynomial of fixed degree a; this converges. Summing the finite choices of a proves

    sum_(n squarefree) F_(omega(n)) n^-sigma < infinity.  (3.1)

The n=1 term is harmless and included. This argument pays ALL depths at once, including those increasing with x; it does not substitute a fixed-depth model. Rankin's inequality gives

    P_q(x):=sum_(n in D_x)F_(omega(n)) <<_(q,epsilon)x^(1+epsilon). (3.2)

For the principal character the actual Redheffer matrix is nonnegative. Every nonidentity cycle in a contributing permutation must contain 1, and it is exactly a strict divisor chain; all other coordinates are fixed points. Consequently P_q(x) is its permanent, and 1+sum_k|A_k|=P_q(x) for that character. For a twisted matrix it is an upper bound on the sum of absolute determinant terms and on 1+sum_k|A_k|. No norm or determinant lower bound is inferred after introducing phases.

The positive price is at least |D_x|. Directly expanding mu^2(n)=sum_(d^2|n)mu(d) and counting q-units yields

    |D_x|=delta_q x+O_q(sqrt x),
    delta_q=(phi(q)/q)prod_(p not dividing q)(1-p^-2)>0.    (3.3)

The O_q(sqrt x) pays every floor and the omitted tail of sum mu(d)/d^2. Hence log P_q(x)/log x tends to 1. This is the exact meaning of a sharp exponent-one positive price; no precise logarithmic asymptotic is claimed.

The claimed semigroup warning is also correct. On D_x, U=diag(chi(n)) is unitary and U B_chi U^(-1)=B_1. With J0=diag((-1)^omega(n)), J0 B_1 J0=-B_1. It follows that

    ||exp(-B_chi)||_(2->2)=||exp(B_1)||_(2->2).

The rank-one closing column transforms to Uv and retains the character. It cannot be dropped. Compressing the Hermitian part of -B_1 to the span of e and the normalized unramified-prime vector gives off-diagonal entries -sqrt(pi_q(x))/2; its largest eigenvalue is at least sqrt(pi_q(x))/2. Thus the proposed contraction fails at the time-zero derivative whenever the prime vector is nonempty. This is an exact operator obstruction for this proposed norm, not a lower bound for M_chi.

## 1. Transfers between fixed smoothers

For the SAME coefficient sequence a(n), write

    F_k(x) = sum_n a(n) k(log(n/x)),
    M_k(s) = integral_R k(u) exp(su) du.

The geometric compact kernel k_o is the convolution of uniform densities on
[-2^-j,2^-j], j>=1. The new compact kernel k_n uses normalized positive widths
asymptotic to1/[(j+1)log(j+1)^rho], rho=1+eta/4>1. Let g_tau be the fixed
Gaussian. Their Mellin multipliers are nonzero in Re(s)>0. Section4 of the
Concrete review proves

    F_new(x) = integral h_no(v) F_old(x exp(v)) dv,
    F_Gaussian(x) = integral h_gn(v) F_new(x exp(v)) dv,
    integral |h(v)| exp(gamma v) dv < infinity  (every fixed gamma>0).

The quotients are M_n/M_o and M_g/M_n, in that direction. The lower bounds
exp(-C log²(2+|t|)) and exp(-C(1+|t|)log(2+|t|)) for the two compact
multipliers, combined with the stronger decay in each numerator, justify
inversion and weighted integrability. All shifted shells and small-scale tails
are paid. Therefore complete dyadic norm estimates pass along

    geometric compact --> near-log compact --> Gaussian

without a loss of power, for each fixed positive growth exponent and its
epsilon buffers. The same argument applies to a Hilbert-valued coefficient
sequence with the corresponding polynomial coefficient-mass bound.

The opposite multiplier quotients are unbounded: Gaussian smoothing cannot
be undone as a bounded general weighted-L2 operation. For the actual ordinary
arithmetic field there is another, logically different route back: a complete
every-epsilon bound gives zero exclusion, buffered zero exclusion gives
polynomial reciprocal-zeta growth, and contour shifting gives a bound for a
different fixed kernel. This does not transfer a submask, local component,
conductor-uniform family, or an unproved Hecke numerator condition.

The merged review adds a bridge for the actual rational coefficient
A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2). If R(y)=F2(exp y), where
F2(x)=sum_(n<=x)A(n)(1-n/x)^2, then

    D(D+1)(D+2)R = 2 sum_n A(n) delta_(log n),
    G_tau(exp y) = [.5 D(D+1)(D+2)g_tau] * R(y).

The convolution kernel has every exponential L1 weight. Thus the Riesz field
also transfers to Gaussian with every shell/tail paid. This is not an
identification of the rational A(n) source with the different ideal-Mobius
source over Q(i).

# Actual arithmetic dilation: a global theorem and the unpaid local estimate

Root accepts G95-G97 below after complete reads of the frozen
[author](arithmetic-dilation/report.md) and
[independent review](arithmetic-dilation-review/report.md). Eleven exact
artifacts preserve both proofs and finite-check evidence. The review's
normal own-claim release completed before its final stream failure; native
readback confirms the frozen bytes and release, so no work was replayed.

The highest accepted written endpoint remains c8=.12514261,
gamma8=.87485739, under the unchanged PR9/Gao source obligations. The
author's historical c6/c7 calibrations remain unchanged in its frozen
report. The periodic source below is for each fixed ordinary Dirichlet
character, with a common exponent and character-dependent constants.
No Hecke or growing-conductor scope is inferred. No formalization or
public-record claim occurred. Near gains,1/6,1/4 and the full original
29-family/109-child portfolio remain.

Classical Davenport/Bernoulli and gcd identities receive their existing
credit. The author and critic separately verified the primary paper of
Aistleitner, Berkes, Seip and Weber, Acta Arithmetica168.3(2015),
Section3(3.2)-(3.5), and directly proved the exact instance used here.
The new components are developments within this research record, not
claims of literature priority.

## G95. An exact source with a positive signed global leading term

Fix chi modulo q with its original zeros, and an integer r>=2 satisfying
chi(-1)=(-1)^r; r=2 for even and r=3 for odd characters suffice. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    Phi(x)=sum_(k in Z,k!=0)chi(k)e(kx)/k^r,
    R_N(x)=2cos(2pi x)-sum_(n<=N)a(n)n^-r Phi(nx).

Absolute convergence and sum_(d|n)mu(d)=1_(n=1) give the exact full tail
R_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^-r Phi(nx). Its Fourier coefficients vanish through
|k|<=N, while for N<|k|<=2N they are mu(|k|)chi(k)/k^r. Natural zeros
and negative frequencies are included.

Writing g=(n,m), the complete-period Gram is

    <Phi(nx),Phi(mx)>
      =2L(2r,chi0)chi(m/g)conj(chi(n/g))g^(2r)/(nm)^r.

The phases cancel against a(n)conj(a(m)) only in this COMPLETE-PERIOD
formula, and only q-units survive. Let

    d_q=1/zeta(2) product_(p|q)p/(p+1),
    d(D)=1/zeta(2) product_(p|D)p/(p+1).

The elementary squarefree count is d(D)t+O(2^omega(D)sqrt(t)). With
n=gu,m=gv,(u,v)=1, it yields

    ||R_N||_2^2=C_r(q)N^(1-2r)+O_(q,r)(N^(1/2-2r)),
    C_r(q)=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      sum_((u,v)=1,(uv,q)=1)
      mu(u)mu(v)d(uvq)min(u,v)^(2r-1)/(uv)^(2r).

Both main and error sums converge absolutely for r>=2. The region
min(u,v)>N costs O(N^(2-4r)); it is not passed through an invalid
large-divisor density estimate. Parseval on the actual first band proves

    C_r(q)>=2d_q(1-2^(1-2r))/(2r-1)>0.

Thus even the complete signed global norm has order N^(1-2r), independent
of the choice of chi at fixed q,r. Its half-power remainder cannot be used
as an upper bound on a restricted arc: subtracting a scalar main term
removes the required positive-measure comparison.

For fixed distinct positive scales lambda_j and any coefficients with
sum|b_j|^2=1, including N-dependent coefficients,

    ||sum_j b_j R_floor(lambda_j N)||_2^2 >= C N^(1-2r)

eventually. The earliest nonzero source has a Fourier band untouched by
later scales; squarefree density gives its positive mass. Compactness
of the fixed finite coefficient sphere makes the lower constant uniform.
The independent review further derives the real symmetric positive
definite limiting Gram matrix

    M_jk=2L(2r,chi0)/(2r-1)
      sum_((u,v)=1,(uv,q)=1)
      mu(u)mu(v)d(uvq)/(uv)^(2r)
      max(lambda_j/u,lambda_k/v)^(1-2r),

with scaled Gram error O(N^-1/2), including floor errors. There is no
uniform claim when the number of scales grows or their gaps close.

## G96. The complete shrinking-arc return and finite signed core

For fixed 0<c<1/2, gamma=1-c, let h=1/(qN). The every-integer-N input

    E_arc(N)=integral_0^h |R_N(x)|^2 dx
       <<_(chi,r,epsilon)N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon)

is equivalent, up to arbitrary epsilon losses, to the full Mertens bound
M_chi(X)<<X^(gamma+epsilon) at every real X. It remains OPEN for an
improvement over c8. Its equivalent notation does not establish a gain.

Finite Fourier inversion of chi and the Bernoulli formula show that Phi
is a single polynomial of degree<=r on[0,1/q], with nonzero constant
beta=2L(r,chi). An endpoint reproducing polynomial p_r satisfies
integral_0^1 p_r(u)u^j du=1_(j=0), j<=r, and ||p_r||_2=r+1.
For O_N f=integral_0^1 p_r(u)f(hu)du and
T_N=sum_(n>N)a(n)n^-r, this gives

    beta T_N=O_N R_N-eta_N, eta_N=O(h^(r+1)),
    |O_N R_N|<=(r+1)sqrt(qN)E_arc(N)^(1/2),
    M_chi(N)=1/L(r,chi)-N^r T_N
                +r integral_1^N t^(r-1)T_floor(t)dt.

Every original n<=N stays in the same first polynomial cell. The reverse
implication uses global Lipschitz continuity of Phi and Abel summation
on the entire infinite tail; derivative jumps add no point masses.
The full Mertens bound then gives holomorphic1/L on Re(s)>gamma at every
height by its Mellin integral. Original imprimitive factors remain; the
principal pole at1 is excluded from the zero-free statement.

Choose fixed kappa>0 with2c+kappa<1, and set

    G=ceil(N^(2c+kappa)),
    T=ceil(N^(1+2c/(2r-1)+kappa)),
    K_N(n,m)=integral_0^h Phi(nx)conj(Phi(mx))dx,
    Core_N=sum_(N<n,m<=T,(n,m)<G)
                  a(n)conj(a(m))(nm)^-r K_N(n,m).

The exact remaining input is the one-sided bound
Core_N<<N^(1-2r-2c+epsilon). Core_N is real, not necessarily positive.
The complete large-gcd absolute price is
O(N^(1-2r)/G+N^-2r), including diagonal and all far terms. The infinite
completion is exactly R_T and has squared norm O(T^(1-2r)). The squared
triangle inequality pays every cross term without an unpaid global norm.
Both costs are strictly below the target, and the reverse comparison gives
equivalence. Positivity of the full finite energy also bounds Core_N from
below by minus the paid complement, so an absolute bound on the WHOLE
core is equivalent here. Absolute values on individual pairs are not.

The missing energy gain is2c, independent of fixed r. Current first gain
requires strictly more than.25028522. At c=1/6 the completion exponents
before kappa are10/9 for r2 and16/15 for r3; at c=1/4 they are7/6 and11/10.
No entry supplies the required signed estimate.

For each fixed character there is eta>0 such that the real part of K_N
is>=A/(2N) for N<n,m<=(1+eta)N, where
A=integral_0^(1/q)|Phi(u)|^2du>0. Lipschitz continuity proves this from
the value at equal scales. Squarefree q-unit density and the O(N^2/G)
large-gcd pair count imply an absolute-pair price>>N^(1-2r), even with
the actual character and Mobius coefficients. This disproves that positive
certificate, not the signed core estimate or RH.

## G97. Exact local diagnostics and a growing filter's reconstruction cost

On the first cell, the source often simplifies drastically. For even chi,
r=2 and m_chi=q^-1 sum_(j mod q)chi(j),

    Phi(x)=2L(2,chi)-2pi^2 m_chi x+2pi^2 chi(0)x^2.

For q1 use chi(0)=1. For every even nonprincipal character both extra
coefficients vanish. On the complete shrinking arc,

    R_N(x)=2L(2,chi)T_N+2cos(2pi x)-2,
    abs(sqrt(E_arc)-sqrt(h)*abs(2L(2,chi)T_N)) << h^(5/2).

Thus in this class the proposed arc estimate is explicitly a single
weighted tail estimate. For odd chi and r3,
Phi(x)=2L(3,chi)-4pi^2L(1,chi)x^2 on the first cell. The finite Bernoulli
formula justifies the endpoint differentiation; convergence of L(1,chi)
suffices, with no assumed left-half-plane nonvanishing.

Localized squarefree averaging preserves the signs and phases on reduced
quotients u,v. For the signed sector u,v<=H<=N the author proves

    E_(N,H)=N^-2r D_H
       +O_(q,r,epsilon)(N^(-2r-1/2)H^(3/2+epsilon)), |D_H|<<H.

The localized derivative bound lacks the extra(uv)^-r from complete-period
orthogonality. At H~N the accumulated error has no power saving, and
quotients>N are still omitted. H=N^(1-2c-kappa) pays only a sector already
inside the large-gcd complement. Neither limitation is an arithmetic
lower bound; better signed summation remains eligible.

The critic develops a genuine shrinking-spacing filter:

    F_(N,H)=R_N-R_(N+H), 1<=H<=N,
    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2<<H N^-2r.

For unequal n,m in the block, (n,m)<=H. The exact global Gram and at most
4H^2/g^2 distinct pairs of multiples yield the bound. More precisely,

    ||F_(N,H)||_2^2=2L(2r,chi0)d_q H N^-2r
       +O(N^(1/2-2r)+H^2N^(-2r-1)+H^(2r+1)N^-4r).

For H=N^alpha,1/2<alpha<1 this is a positive leading asymptotic. Choosing
H=N^(1-2c) has the desired formal energy gain for0<c<1/4; at c1/4 the
upper bound survives but the elementary asymptotic error is not smaller.

Recovering the original signal remains essential. Use a common arc of
length1/(2qN), partition(N,2N] into aboutN/H blocks, and pay the actual
endpoint observer on each. Separate norms and triangle reassembly give

    |sum_(N<n<=2N)a(n)n^-r|<<N^(3/2-r)H^-1/2.

At H=N^(1-2c) this is N^(1+c-r), weaker than the elementary full-tail
bound. Cauchy-Schwarz on block labels alone does not improve that cost.
The small filtered norm is valid but cannot also pay an unproved signed
reconstruction. A coupled growing filter or genuinely new observation
remains open; its complete reconstruction is the next decisive test.

## 5. The whole paired diagonal

Merge the actual low-gcd tuple into

    n=d1 d2 prod_i p_i, N0=D1D2 P0,
    B_{<G,u}Qslots_u=sum_n c(n)psi_u(n)^(+1 or -1).               (R12)

The coefficient c includes `(D1D2P0)^(-1/2)`, both Mobius signs, both independent inverse profiles, all fixed nu and relative slot phases, all original pool restrictions, and `N gcd(d1,d2)<G`. Every factorization contributing to c must obey that tuple condition. It is not replaced by a condition on a gcd of two merged columns. The source B3.6 does not admit this extra c as a canonical coefficient, and is not invoked on it.

Each inverse contributes exponent 0 or 1 at a prime; the disjoint slot pools contribute at most one further appearance. Thus `v_p(n) in {0,1,2,3}` including every collision. For n,n', the difference is in `[-3,3]`; it is zero modulo six exactly when it is zero. The complete ideal sixth-power class is therefore `n=n'`. The fixed generator/unit sectors retain their finite phases. No unequal-root sum has been discarded: unequal ideal sixth-power roots cannot occur in this finite paired source. This observation would be false for the older completed Mobius-convolution source with unbounded prime powers.

Tuple multiplicity is divisor bounded. Linear ideal counting on the fixed product annulus, or Cauchy inside each factorization sum, gives

    |c(n)|<<H_J N0^(-1/2)U^epsilon,
    sum_n|c(n)|^2<<H_J U^epsilon.                               (R13)

It holds for all fixed derivatives, with larger finite seminorm orders. Dropping the small-gcd restriction only after taking this absolute majorant is legitimate. The entire diagonal, with its natural zeros and retained holes, is at most `H_J U^(1+epsilon)`. This is an upper bound for the diagonal contribution, not a lower bound for the full norm.

## 2. Literal sampling and portfolio comparison

The author's recipe hash is cfdc230e0d9eb589c0379a25c65531b780555cffdc59b2c721e3b714a3a40971; its fixed local PRNG seed is 63290690781877729360377832095639447436. The replay is a deterministic verification of recorded draws, not new sampling. First-test order is 03,04,22,16,20,02. There was no reroll, group-specific rarity exclusion or later relabeling. The p labels are subjective typicality judgments, not success probabilities or token probabilities. No binary branching was used.

The maintained index was refreshed through [research revision], including W47 and both Sol03 reviews, with the original 29 families/109 children retained. Relevant exact sources read or retained and checked here include:

- [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 14f4efd8cca6b5586f23e889fdcd19d9b9fe8629716046207746af0bec6cf49b; [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 8fb7584f01f3ca51b118dfa6e35818d505077ba9f06d6f06d8bae1873a7809d7.
- [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 bb92cb932fd31fc5bf6c6dc9017baa5901116e1cb5548a11b8eb0a1354d3361d: exact G71 and G72 objects and quantifiers.
- [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 71470d3e14754cdbc001f159bb98f91c9c3a6947a38306d7e69b5b823387ee9e: AM18--21 finite inverse norms and physical readout cost.
- [restricted mathematical source] and round35-review.md: fixed-arity inverse identity/periodic restoration and normalized fractional inverse, including the principal pole obstruction.
