- [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 d3ae72d9548766474784273afecb5937bedd9d093fe7e7be8a8e98094f4ae292, and [restricted mathematical source] SHA256 48042d7c421c5953ae4c9ba2c01b4d3141bb91ceffb1bb227d346388ee6551b4: the literal native H dictionary and its residual contracts.
- W39 interpolation/compression and W38/[research revision] observation failures; W43 seed12 already proposed log-periodic invisibility. These precedents constrain credit for audit06 below.

These are mathematical sources, not instructions or automatic theorem acceptance. Canonical f3 includes prime2 and excludes only prime3 through mu(rad(n/3^v3(n))); this review does not substitute a p>=5 variant or import an unpaid f3/ideal transfer.

## 3. Independent proof of W48.1

Fix tau>0 and an arbitrary complex sequence |a(n)|<=1 for n>=1, with a(n)=0 for n<=0. Define

    g(v)=(2*pi*tau)^(-1/2) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)),
    f_x(t)=g(log(t/x)) (t>0), and f_x(t)=0 (t<=0),
    F_a(x)=sum_(n>=1) a(n) f_x(n).

The SAME G72 energy is

    B_H(k)=sum_(j=0)^(H-1) a(k-j),
    w_X(k)=exp(-log(k/X)^2/(4*tau)),
    E_a(X,H)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) |B_H(k)|^2 w_X(k).

It includes the first partial window, the complete positive line, every coefficient zero and both tails. Its exact signed lag expansion is

    E=(1/H) sum_(|h|<H) sum_(n>=max(1,1-h)) a(n) conjugate(a(n+h))
              *sum_(j=max(0,h))^min(H-1,H-1+h) w_X(n+j).

Thus neither deleting off-diagonal terms nor replacing the inner weight by a constant triangular count is allowed.

Put h_tau(t)=g(log t), extended by zero at t<=0, and

    J_j = integral_0^infinity |h_tau^(j)(t)| dt,
    ell=log 2, K_tau=sqrt(2*pi*tau) exp(tau/2)+2,
    C_(tau,r)=(2^r-1) sqrt(K_tau/(2*pi*tau)) exp(3*ell^2/(2*tau)).

Every derivative is a fixed polynomial in log t times t^(-j)g(log t); h_tau is smooth and flat at zero and rapidly decreasing at infinity. In particular every J_j is finite and ||f_x^(j)||_1=x^(1-j)J_j.

**Accepted exact inequality.** For fixed integer r>=1, X>=1 and integer H>=1 with 2rH<=X,

    sup_(X<=x<=2X) |F_a(x)|
      <= C_(tau,r) sqrt((X/H) E_a(X,H))
       + ((H-1)/2)^r [J_r X^(1-r)+J_(r+1) X^(-r)]
       + rH (2^r-1) g(0) exp(-log(X/(2rH))^2/(2*tau)).       (R1)

Constants depend only on tau,r. This is not a claim of controlled constants for growing r.

### 3.1 Orientation and exact adjoint

Use the FORWARD average T f(n)=H^(-1) sum_(j=0)^(H-1) f(n+j). Set

    Q_r(T)=sum_(j=0)^(r-1)(I-T)^j
          =sum_(k=0)^(r-1)(-1)^k binom(r,k+1) T^k.

The exact identity T Q_r(T)+(I-T)^r=I and its coefficient l1 norm 2^r-1 give, with psi=Q_r(T)f_x and R=(I-T)^r f_x,

    F_a(x)=(1/H) sum_(k>=1) B_H(k) psi(k) + sum_(n>=1) a(n)R(n).   (R2)

Indeed k=n+j in the first sum yields sum_n a(n)T psi(n); indices n<=0 vanish by the stipulated extension. Each T^k is a probability average of shifts from 0 to k(H-1). No backward adjoint, missing boundary term or altered coefficient sequence occurs.

### 3.2 The weighted norm and small-index objection

For k>=rH, every shift j in Q_r lies below rH<=k. Write v=log(k/X), b=log((k+j)/k)+log(X/x), so |b|<=ell. Then

    f_x(k+j)^2 / w_X(k)
      =(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp((-3v^2/4-2bv-b^2)/tau)
      <=(2*pi*tau)^(-1) exp(3ell^2/tau) exp(-v^2/(2*tau)).

The underlying difference after replacing ell^2 by b^2 is (v/2+2b)^2>=0. This directly verifies the exponent and constant, rather than invoking an unpriced change of Gaussian width. The unimodal sum satisfies

    sum_(k>=1) exp(-log(k/X)^2/(2*tau)) <= K_tau X.

Its integral is X sqrt(2*pi*tau)exp(tau/2), and comparison to the integral costs at most 2. The absolute coefficient sum of Q_r and weighted Cauchy--Schwarz now give the first term of (R1):

    (1/H) sqrt(sum |B_H|^2 w_X) sqrt(sum |psi|^2/w_X)
       <= C_(tau,r) sqrt(X E/H).

For 1<=k<rH, the preceding ratio estimate is not available uniformly. Instead |B_H(k)|<=H, every test argument is <2rH<=X<=x, and the Gaussian is monotone there. Summing at most rH indices gives exactly the last term of (R1). This pays the strongest inverse-weight objection; applying the large-index ratio everywhere would be invalid.

### 3.3 The complete repeated-difference remainder

For nonnegative integer j,

    f(n)-f(n+j)=-integral_0^j f'(n+u)du.

Iterating gives the signed r-fold derivative integral for (I-T)^r, averaged over j_1,...,j_r in {0,...,H-1}. If f and f' are integrable and f is absolutely continuous, then for all v>=0,

    sum_(n>=1)|f(n+v)| <= ||f||_1+||f'||_1.

Compare f(n+v) to f(t) on [n+v-1,n+v], integrate, and sum disjoint intervals in the positive half-line. Applying this to f_x^(r), integrating the r shift lengths, and using their mean (H-1)/2 proves

    sum_(n>=1)|R(n)|
       <=((H-1)/2)^r [J_r x^(1-r)+J_(r+1)x^(-r)].

For r>=1 and x>=X the displayed powers are bounded by the corresponding X powers. This proves (R1), including the whole right tail and the flat left extension. H=1 has exactly zero remainder, consistent with the formula.

## 4. Exponent return and precise arithmetic gap

For fixed 0<theta<1 take H=floor(X^theta). For every fixed r, 2rH<=X eventually. The last term in (R1) is smaller than every negative power of X, since its logarithm has leading term

    -(1-theta)^2 (log X)^2/(2*tau).

The middle term is O(X^(1-r(1-theta))). Consequently the full hypothesis

    for every epsilon>0 and all large dyadic X:
    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) <<_epsilon X^(e+epsilon)             (OPEN-W)

gives the complete pointwise and dyadic L2 exponent

    gamma_r=max((1-theta+e)/2, 1-r(1-theta)).                 (R3)

The order r may be chosen after fixed theta and a fixed target exponent, then kept fixed as X tends to infinity. There is no theta=1 theorem or silent growing-order substitution. Endpoint equality has the usual every-epsilon interpretation. This is a sufficient return, not an asserted energy equivalence: oscillatory window-null directions can carry other information.

For a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), with chi any fixed ordinary Dirichlet character including its natural zeros,

    integral_0^infinity F_a(x) x^(-s) dx/x
        = exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi),       Re(s)>1.

The small-x tail is superpolynomial. The complete all-scale bound from (R3), or its dyadic L2 version followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, makes this Mellin transform holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma_r. Multiplying by L and analytic continuation excludes every zero there: the numerator is nonzero at every finite height and multiplicity. The principal pole of L produces a reciprocal zero, not a forbidden pole. No estimate for vertical reciprocal growth, Phragmen--Lindelof assumption, primitive replacement or conductor uniformity is needed for this forward implication.

The family statement needs a COMMON exponent for each fixed chi, with constants allowed to depend on chi. Neither Eisenstein/Hecke families nor a growing conductor nor a replacement f3 source has been proved by this argument.

To improve c6, both strict inequalities are necessary in this interface:

    e < 2*theta6-1+theta = .749722+theta,
    1-r(1-theta) < theta6=.874861.                           (R4)

The absolute energy bound is O(XH)=O(X^(1+theta)); its required arithmetic saving remains

    (1+theta)-(.749722+theta)=.250278=2*c6.

Only the old first-order approximation ceiling theta<theta6 is removed. For example theta=.9 and r=2 pay remainder exponent .8, but still require the unproved energy exponent e<1.649722. Under the hypothetical e=1, examples (theta,r,gamma) are (.26,1,.87), (1/3,1,5/6), (.5,1,.75), (.8,2,.6), (.9,5,.55), (.98,25,.51). These are conditional calibrations, not estimates. A growing r at theta=1 cannot be inferred from them.

## 5. W48.2: strengthened scope of the accepted countermodel

The accepted G71 construction supplies one fixed bounded, squarefree-supported, multiplicative complex sequence with fixed finite prime prescriptions and the stated fixed-character/fixed-affine qualitative properties, together with

    F_a(X)=C X^beta+O(X^sigma), C!=0, 1/2<sigma<beta<theta6.

I use that accepted construction with precisely its scope. This is not the actual global Mobius prime law or its prescribed convolution inverse. For the new conclusion only boundedness and the displayed asymptotic are needed.

Fix ANY 0<theta<1 and choose the fixed integer r so that r>(1-beta)/(1-theta). The last two terms of (R1) are o(X^beta), whereas |F_a(X)|>=|C|X^beta/2 eventually. Rearranging its first term gives

    E_a(X,floor(X^theta)) >> X^(2*beta-1+theta)              (R5)

for every sufficiently large X. This extends the former theta<beta restriction to every fixed theta<1. The same already constructed sequence works: no new random construction or uncountable intersection is used.

For any candidate gamma<theta6 choose beta between max(gamma,1/2) and theta6. The gap between (R5)'s exponent and 2*gamma-1+theta is 2(beta-gamma)>0. Thus the retained coarse qualitative properties alone cannot imply that improved window bound at ANY fixed sublinear theta. For beta=.8747 and theta=.9, the lower exponent is 1.6494. The equality boundary is not settled. This is a limitation of deduction from those coarse properties, not a counterexample to a conjectured actual mu*chi estimate.

## 6. The other five tests and the original card04 proposal

**03, divisibility coercivity.** For sigma>0, in the explicit Hilbert norm sum_n |v(n)|^2 n^(-2*sigma), a prime dilation becomes z_p S_p on orthonormal prime-power chains, z_p=chi(p)p^(-sigma). For a finite prime tensor B=product_p(I-z_p S_p),

    ||B||=product_p(1+|z_p|),
    inf_(||v||=1)||Bv||=product_p(1-|z_p|).

Long phase-aligned chains approximate both extremes: their squared ratios are (1+/-|z|)^2 minus/plus 2|z|/K. Tensoring the finite approximants proves the product formulas. Ramified primes with chi(p)=0 contribute identity. For sigma<=1 the lower product collapses as more unramified primes enter. The vacuum norm squared product(1+p^(-2*sigma)) stays finite for sigma>1/2, but the Gaussian dual readout costs X^(sigma+1/2), so this alone gives no gamma<1. AM18--21 already establishes the stronger appropriate finite-N inverse behavior, including subpower costs at sigma>=1/2. A full prime tensor, a finite divisor section, and an actual source readout are different objects. This is duplicate/scoped failure, not an actual arithmetic lower bound.

**04, first-test lag deletion.** Bounding each lag by the diagonal O(X), then summing O(H) lags, costs O(XH); the resulting requirement theta<2*gamma-1 was already G22/G42. The later finite adjoint correction is an explicitly changed continuation using G72. The useful W48.1 increment should not be attributed to a new autocorrelation identity.

**22, fixed-arity inverse.** Write a(n)=mu(n)chi(n), ell(n)=chi(n), m(n)=a(n)1_(n<=Y) as a pointwise truncation, and r0=a-m. All stars below denote Dirichlet convolution. The exact identity a*ell=delta gives, for every fixed integer k>=1,

    a = r0^{*k}*ell^{*(k-1)}
        +sum_(j=1)^k (-1)^(j+1) binom(k,j) m^{*j}*ell^{*(j-1)}.   (R6)

This follows by expanding (a-m)^{*k} and canceling a*ell; all shared primes, lower support endpoints and character zeros remain. It is the W01 RA4 identity, with the LP5 k=3 specialization already explicit. For a prime p not dividing the character modulus, q_p=delta-p delta_p makes ell*q_p periodic and mean zero, for principal as well as nonprincipal chi. Multiplying (R6) by q_p^{*(k-1)} gives the author's filtered identity. For fixed k and Y<X^(1/k-eta), the short restoration terms have arguments X/d tending to infinity; fixed periodic mean-zero Gaussian convolution decays by any prescribed power, with its polynomial coefficient mass paid. This is W01/W35 restoration ancestry.

The Mellin multiplier (1-p^(1-s))^(k-1) is nonzero in 0<Re(s)<1, but has zeros ON Re(s)=1. Thus this filtered identity gives the claimed return within the open strip; a statement about the entire region Re(s)>gamma must retain the independently inherited right-edge complement. It cannot obtain that boundary from this numerator alone. This qualification does not affect the direct unfiltered W48.1 return.

**16, one-term dominance.** The finite mu*chi Dirichlet polynomial has constant term 1. At sigma>0 any single other term has modulus at most n^(-sigma)<1, so it cannot strictly dominate the constant term plus the other absolute terms. Constant-term dominance reduces to an absolute sum less than 1; unramified prime terms already make that criterion fail in the sigma<=1 range as the cutoff grows. The Euler-product version similarly demands product_p(1+p^(-sigma))<2. Only this ungrouped triangle criterion fails; phase-aware grouping remains untested.

**20, all-height anchored budget.** In a half-plane Re(s)>a, let rho=beta+iT, beta>a, and

    B(s)=(s-rho)/(s+conjugate(rho)-2a), F(s)=B(s)/B(s0),

where real s0>a and T!=0. B has its pole left of the half-plane and |B|<=1 there. F(s0)=1 and F(rho)=0, while

    log sup|F|
      <= (1/2) log(1+4(s0-a)(beta-a)/((s0-beta)^2+T^2))
       ->0 as |T|->infinity.

A conjugate pair gives real symmetry with twice this budget. Therefore an unspecified small fixed boundary budget plus one anchor cannot exclude arbitrarily high zeros in this abstract holomorphic class. This retains F21/F22/W22/R33 ancestry. It is not a constructed Dirichlet L function or a disproof of an arithmetic boundary estimate.

**02, fractional inverse.** For the raw principal source L^(-1/k), k>1, a complete Gaussian exponent gamma<1 would supply a holomorphic Z with Z^k L=exp(k*tau*s^2/2). The simple pole of L at 1 would require k*ord_1(Z)=1, impossible for holomorphic Z. Normalizing the principal pole changes this source, exactly as W22/R35.21--23 already records. Nonprincipal characters do not share this particular obstruction. Convolution recombination alone does not divide the growth exponent: k convolutions of exp(beta*y)1_(y>=0) equal exp(beta*y)y^(k-1)/(k-1)!, up to normalization. The exponent remains beta. This is a scoped raw-source failure and a duplicate normalized bridge, not a universal fractional-method impossibility.

## 7. Protected audit27: what a full H-to-sieve witness must actually pay

The seed proposes extracting a sieve-law violation from excessive native H correlation. ## 2. S28: an exact deletion channel whose inverse is affordable at a true size cutoff

For real X>=1 and fixed q let D_X be the squarefree q-unit integers n<=X, including1. This is a divisor downset. Coordinates outside it have value zero. Write k(n)=omega(n), K_X=max_(D_X)k(n), 0<rho<=1, lambda=1-rho, R_rho=(2-rho)/rho. Let B_rho delete each occupied prime independently with probability lambda:

    B_rho(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^k(d) lambda^(k(n)-k(d)), d,n in D_X.    (A1)

The 0^0 convention is1. This channel acts on a finite complex measure, not a claim that prime factors of an arithmetic integer are independent. Each column sums to1. No deleted prime value or size condition is replaced by a probabilistic approximation.

### A. Exact inverse and exact norm

The inverse is

    C_rho(d,n)=1_(d|n) rho^(-k(n))(-lambda)^(k(n)-k(d)).           (A2)
    ||B_rho||_(l1->l1)=1,
    ||C_rho||_(l1->l1)=R_rho^K_X.                               (A3)

For d|n every intermediate e with d|e|n is still in D_X. Expanding (CB)(d,n) factors over the primes of n/d and gives (lambda-lambda)^k(n/d), with coefficient1 for d=n; the other product is the same binomial cancellation. Thus the cutoff causes no missing intermediate state. The absolute column sum of C at n is rho^(-k(n))(1+lambda)^k(n)=R_rho^k(n); taking a maximal-degree column proves equality, not merely an upper estimate.

Every squarefree integer with k primes is at least (k+1)!. Consequently

    K_X <= (1+o(1)) log X/loglog X,
    fixed rho>0: R_rho^K_X=X^o(1).                             (A4)

The factorial lower bound and integral estimate for log(k!) prove the needed upper bound without a prime theorem. This corrects a possible full-cube objection: exp(const*pi(X)) is the wrong inverse price on D_X. The number of sites may be enormous, but a surviving column occupies at most K_X sites.

For moving retention, log R_(rho_X)=o(loglog X) still suffices for subpower loss. If rho_X=(log X)^(-b), fixed b>0, then the norm is X^(b+o(1)). Here equality uses K_X~log X/loglog X, obtained from the ordinary prime number theorem and primorial products, with only finitely many q-primes removed. This is a genuine debit: such increasingly severe deletion cannot be called exponent-neutral. The PNT input is [NIST DLMF27.12](https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.12); no growing-q uniformity is used.

### B. Literal arithmetic coefficients and readout

Take nu_chi,X(n)=chi(n) on D_X, equivalently mu(n)^2 chi(n) with the full cutoff and zeros. Its output is

    b_chi,X(d)=rho^k(d) chi(d)
       *sum_(m<=X/d, (m,dq)=1) mu(m)^2 chi(m)lambda^k(m).       (A5)

The erased cofactor retains chi(m); replacing it by1 for a nonprincipal character changes the source. Exact inversion of the parity observer f(n)=(-1)^k(n) gives

    h_rho(d)=(-R_rho)^k(d),
    M_chi(X)=sum_(d in D_X)h_rho(d)b_chi,X(d).                  (A6)

Indeed, conditional on a squarefree n, the sum over d|n is
product_(p|n)(lambda+rho*(-R_rho))=(-1)^k(n). Hence every size boundary and complementary deletion pattern is included. Applying B instead to mu(n)chi(n) and reading total mass would preserve M trivially; that is not a smoothing gain.

For an arbitrary approximant btilde_X, keep e_X=b_X-btilde_X as a full signed vector. Then

    M_chi(X)=<h,btilde_X>+<h,e_X>,
    |<h,e_X>|<=R_rho^K_X ||e_X||_1.                           (A7)

For fixed rho, bounds for BOTH the entire first contraction and ||e_X||_1 by X^(gamma+epsilon) for every epsilon>0 imply the same every-epsilon bound for M, after splitting epsilon to absorb (A4). A selected output sector or a low-degree approximation without its full e_X is insufficient. For rho=(log X)^(-b), the residual exponent must instead pay b. This is a complete quantitative adapter, not a proved approximation theorem.

One common gamma<gamma11, for every fixed chi and all large real X, gives the ordinary all-height return through

    F_chi(s)=s integral_1^infinity M_chi(x)x^(-s-1) dx=1/L(s,chi)

initially on Re s>1 and then normally on Re s>gamma. Differentiated integrals converge on every compact after an epsilon buffer. The meromorphic identity L F=1 excludes regular zeros; the principal pole at1 becomes a reciprocal zero. No height-uniform bound or native-H implication is asserted. The analytic/Euler and imprimitive conventions are [DLMF25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). Targets gamma=.87485,5/6,3/4 would give c=.12515,1/6,1/4; the first conditional gain is .0000040364.

### C. Strong objection: the actual output is not power-small

For principal chi and fixed 0<rho<1, b_X is nonnegative. For any fixed squarefree q-unit d,

    b_X(d) >= rho^k(d)lambda[pi(X/d)-O_(q,d)(1)]
            >>_(q,d,rho) X/log X.                            (A8)

Only cofactor primes m not dividing dq were used. Thus any unweighted l2 or l1 certificate for the full b_X has exponent at least1. Removing a FIXED finite list of labels does not repair it: choose one fixed d outside that list. This is an actual arithmetic lower bound for that positive output norm, not for M or the signed readout. Growing deletions, weighted norms, exact signed centering and correlations with the removed labels remain possible; their reconstruction must be paid.

At rho=1 the map is the identity; ||b||_2 is of order sqrt X, but ||h||_2 is also of order sqrt X, so Cauchy still gives exponent1. More generally, on the principal basis b(d)<=1+lambda X/d and hence ||b||_2^2<=2X+4lambda^2X^2. Taking lambda<=X^-1/2 gives a small l2 norm but no improvement of the full readout estimate. This upper calculation is deliberately coarse and already exposes the missing covariance rather than disguising it as a channel gain.

The useful reopening target is a growing, signed, explicitly evaluable centering btilde with the complete residual in (A7), not merely a positive small-prime model. Fixed-rho inversion is affordable; constructing that arithmetic centering remains open.

## 3. S30: complete parity/size compression and a uniform positive-norm obstruction

Retain the actual cutoff polynomial, not an untruncated Euler product:

    Z_chi,X(z)=sum_(n in D_X)chi(n)z^k(n),
    P_chi,X,rho(z)=sum_(d in D_X)b_chi,X(d)z^k(d)
                 =Z_chi,X(lambda+rho z).                      (B1)

Thus P(-R_rho)=M_chi(X). For nonprincipal chi the coefficients contain the full erased character phase from (A5); they need not be positive. The local prime/size generating product

    product_(p<=X,p not|q)(1+z chi(p)p^(-s))

records every squarefree subset, including products exceeding X. Recovering Z requires the exact product-size projection. This projection cannot be omitted before evaluation at z=-1. Equation(B1) already performs that projection coefficientwise, so no Perron tail or sharp-endpoint convention is borrowed for free. The proposed joint transform has not made the size boundary independent of parity.

For any polynomial P of degree at most K_X, normalized circle Parseval and Cauchy give

    |P(-R_rho)| <= [sum_(j=0)^K_X R_rho^(2j)]^(1/2)
                    *||P(e^(it))||_(L2(dt/2pi)).              (B2)

At fixed rho this transfer costs X^o(1). It would therefore be enough to prove the whole circle norm at a new exponent. The following actual principal source calculation rules out this particular sufficient estimate.

### A. The prime layer survives every retention schedule

For principal chi write P(z)=sum_j beta_j z^j. All beta_j>=0. Every unramified prime contributes lambda+rho z; therefore, for EVERY 0<rho<=1, even X-dependent,

    beta_0+beta_1 >= pi_q(X),
    ||P(e^(it))||_2^2=sum_j beta_j^2 >= pi_q(X)^2/2.           (B3)

Since pi_q(X)~X/log X, this circle norm cannot be O(X^(gamma+epsilon)) for gamma<1 and every epsilon. This is stronger than just noting R_rho>1: even a small inverse cost and adaptive retention do not remove the coherent positive prime mass. It obstructs an uncentered scalar/cardinality circle certificate, not the value P(-R_rho), which retains cancellations between all coefficients.

### B. Finitely many original degree layers cannot repair it

Remove all original terms with k(n)<=r, where r is fixed, before the affine substitution. The remaining polynomial is

    P^(>r)(z)=sum_(n in D_X,k(n)>r)(lambda+rho z)^k(n)         (B4)

for principal chi. Fix k=r+1. Products of k distinct unramified primes in ((X/2)^(1/k),X^(1/k)] lie in (X/2,X] and are distinct. PNT gives at least c_k X/(log X)^k such products for all large X. Each contributes the same degree-k polynomial, with nonnegative coefficients summing to1. Its coefficient l2 norm is at least1/sqrt(k+1). Other layers only increase every coefficient. Hence, uniformly over every retention schedule,

    ||P^(>r)(e^(it))||_2 >>_(q,r) X/(log X)^(r+1).            (B5)

This rejects finite original-layer subtraction as a repair of the positive circle norm. It does not cover exact deflation with signed quotient coefficients, growing r, or a full signed combination of the retained and removed layers. In particular it does not refute G106's actual root/quotient return. The selected fixed-k layer is used only to lower-bound a nonnegative coefficient norm, never the signed arithmetic sum.

### C. What the high-ceiling idea retains

The complete multivariate inverse (A2) and scalar transfer(B2) cost subpower at fixed rho. That is a usable quantitative fact; it avoids declaring the architecture impossible because of the number of available primes. Its simplest global positive norm is nevertheless impossible by(B3), and every fixed original-layer repair is blocked by(B5). A candidate must retain a growing signed boundary/correction and establish its complete contraction. This is a precise restriction on the proposed realization, not a failure of all joint transforms, coding methods or c=1/4 mechanisms.

An observation deleting output labels has a separate exact limitation. If an output coordinate n is unobserved, the vector C_rho delta_n produces zero in every observed coordinate, while its parity readout equals (-R_rho)^k(n), not zero. This synthetic linear-algebra witness is not an alternative Mobius source; it shows why an observer restricted to selected syndromes requires a source-specific bound for the full missing readout.

## 4. S02: the critical logarithmic prime cutoff with its margin paid

This develops the actual G173 Gaussian logarithmic source, not a new generic resolvent. Fix tau>0, ordinary chi mod q and 1/2<gamma<1. Set

    g(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)mu(n)chi(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=e^(-gamma y)U(y).

Local convergence, derivatives and the left Gaussian tail follow from the absolute Gaussian majorant. The coefficient identity is

    mu(n)chi(n)log n = -sum_(d|n)chi(d)Lambda(d)mu(n/d)chi(n/d).

It retains every prime power. It gives exactly

    tau z'+(y+tau gamma)z+K_(1,gamma)z+K_(2,gamma)z=0,
    K1 z(y)=sum_p chi(p)log p p^(-gamma)z(y-log p),            (C1)

with K2 the j>=2 prime-power delays. For I_R=int_0^R y|z|^2 and E_R=int_0^R|z|^2,

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2,
    Qj=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z) Kj z.                         (C2)

G173 proves |Q2|<=eta I_R+B_eta for every eta>0 using the summable higher-power coefficient norm and the fixed past. It also pays the same-output prime diagonal D_R=O(1), since its nonnegative weights sum at each squarefree q-unit n to at most log n and the whole-line Gaussian integral is a constant times n^(-2gamma). These facts are reused exactly.

### A. New paid interface

For fixed a>0 take

    b=1/(1-gamma), Y_a(y)=a(1+y)^b, y>=0,
    kappa(a,gamma)=a^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).                     (C3)

Equality belongs to the small-prime sector. Let Q_small use precisely p<=Y_a(y). Then for every eta>0,

    |Q_small(R)| <= [kappa(a,gamma)+eta] I_R+B_eta,a,chi,tau,  (C4)

for every R, with B using only a fixed bounded interval of the actual source and its left tail. It does not require any unknown future bound.

Proof: PNT and partial summation give

    S_gamma(t)=sum_(p<=t)log p p^(-gamma)
                 ~t^(1-gamma)/(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum at y is (kappa+o(1))y. Apply 2|z(y)z(y-log p)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(y-log p)|^2. For the column put v=y-log p. The mask implies log p<=log a+b log(1+y)=o(y); hence v/y->1 uniformly over all admitted primes as y->infinity. More explicitly, for any fixed small epsilon>0, eventually y<=v/(1-epsilon), so the column is bounded by

    S_gamma(a(1+v/(1-epsilon))^b)
       <=[kappa/(1-epsilon)+o(1)]v.

Choose epsilon and the tail onset to absorb both errors into eta. The remaining y are bounded and have only finitely many permitted primes and a bounded past interval. Their contribution is B. No second factor2 survives in the asymptotic coefficient; both rows and columns were counted. PNT is used only in this classical scalar prime-weight sum. Replacing it by G173's theta(t)<=4(log2)t gives the entirely elementary, weaker coefficient 4(log2)kappa and the same cutoff power.

This is larger eventually than the G173 cutoff ((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^b, by a growing logarithmic factor. The price is a nonzero, explicitly budgeted kappa; the old cutoff had relative bound0. It is not legitimate to enlarge that mask while retaining its old arbitrarily small price.

      *log p*e^(-2gamma y)*g(log n-y)*g(log(pm)-y),           (C5)

summed over all m,n and integrated over0<=y<=R. Both infinite sums, the diagonal complement, both independent arithmetic labels and all character zeros remain. Its diagonal D_a,R is the same nonnegative bounded type as G173 for this new exact mask.

Suppose, for this a and some delta>kappa(a,gamma),

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+[(delta-kappa)/2]I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'.   (C7)

Its bilateral transform continues normally on Re s>gamma, equals exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi) initially on Re s>1, and this nonzero Gaussian numerator excludes every ordinary L-zero there. The principal pole and imprimitive factors are handled exactly as in G173. One common gamma is chosen before characters and possible zeros; a,delta,constants and onsets may depend on fixed chi.        /int y|f_T|^2 -> kappa(a,gamma).                     (C8)

## R6. A proved positive prefix lemma

Here is the additional source result completed in this review. It uses the accepted PR9 inverse moment, not a new arithmetic hypothesis.

Fix a finite natural dictionary and one whole orientation, smooth V as above, and a smooth prefix H with0<=H<=1, H=1 on[0,1] and H=0 beyond a fixed C>1. Put

    t=4/3, R=U^t, L=U^(t+lambda), Y=U^B,
    P_u(s)=sum_n phi_u(n)A_R(n)(Nn)^(-s)
                      exp(-Nn/Y)H(Nn/L).                (R7)

The n=1 term is omitted, equivalently restrict Nn>R since every other Nn<=R has A_R(n)=0. All n are ideals with the original natural prime support. B and an upper bound for lambda are fixed. No arbitrary growing inverse-coefficient mask is added. The lemma applies to all nonzero sixth-free element rows in a smooth ball, including units; any permissible subset can be removed after the positive norm is formed.

For delta in[17/25,7/10], set a=(1+delta)/2. On the fixed positive-width real interval I_delta=[a,1] and a height interval[-T-1,T+1], let N0(P) be the positive squared tensor Sobolev norm: sum of the squared L2 norms of derivatives partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j, i,j in{0,1}, summed over the free rows with a smooth nonnegative radial majorant. Explicitly,

    N0(P)=sum_free u Phi(Nu/U) sum_(i,j in{0,1})
       integral_(I_delta x[-T-1,T+1])
                       |partial_sigma^i partial_tau^j P_u|^2.

Its constants are uniform for these delta because 1-a>=3/20. Enlarging to finitely many higher derivatives only changes the finite orders. Then, for every epsilon>0,

    N0(P) << H_J U^[J(delta,lambda)+epsilon],
    J(delta,lambda)=1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda.     (R8)

H_J denotes fixed finite smooth seminorms and polynomial height cost. Any fixed endpoint constants are retained in these costs, and a sufficiently large final U threshold can follow the fixed dictionary and profiles. Taking a one-sided real interval avoids assuming a zero below the bin's lower endpoint; using a wider interval below a instead would require spending its real buffer explicitly.

Proof. R2 gives the exact finite coupled expression

    P_u(s)=-sum_(Nm<C L/R)phi_u(m)(Nm)^(-s)
       *sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)(Nd)^(-s)[1-V(Nd/R)]
                    H(Nd Nm/L)exp(-Nd Nm/Y).             (R9)

For a dyad Nd~D, its nonzero terms have D comparable to or larger than R and D<<L/Nm. The inverse coefficient is precisely mu(d)phi_u(d); the factor depending on m is a smooth profile, not an inserted arithmetic coefficient. On fixed positive annuli every Euler derivative of [1-V(Ax)]H(A'xy)exp(-A''xy) is uniformly bounded in positive dilation parameters A,A',A''. Real powers and height twists introduce only the prescribed finite polynomial height costs. Apply B3.3 on the full normalized box before selecting the live m or row, with larger individual cutoffs. Relations among D, Nm, R, L, Y restrict the evaluation point of that common measure. Freeze this entire profile if using the restoration/scale-supremum proof; resetting R at a shortened inverse scale would be an error.

For the centrally normalized inverse on a dyad, B0.9 and its Sobolev consequence give

    sum_free u |D^(-1/2)sum_d mu(d)phi_u(d)W(Nd/D)|^2
                 << H_J U^(1/6)D^(5/6)U^epsilon,         (R10)

because D is at least a fixed multiple of U^(4/3). A ball is handled by its row dyads; the displayed upper bound also pays their smaller scales and the unit window. For a dyad of the weighted inverse in R9, multiply by D^(1-2a)=D^(-delta), giving squared exponent U^(1/6)D^(5/6-delta). All required mixed derivatives obey the same bound: derivatives of outside powers give logarithms absorbed in epsilon; normalized profiles have the source's finite height and smooth costs.

The exponent5/6-delta is positive throughout the closed interval. Sum the inverse dyads by the Hilbert triangle, dominated up to permitted logarithmic losses by D<<L/Nm. The outside character phi_u(m) is a contraction in this same Hilbert space, including its natural zeros. The remaining norm is bounded by

    H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon) L^((5/6-delta)/2)
       *sum_(Nm<C L/R)(Nm)^[-a-(5/6-delta)/2]
     = H_J^(1/2) U^(1/12+epsilon) L^((5/6-delta)/2)
       *sum_(Nm<C L/R)(Nm)^(-11/12).                    (R11)

The ordinary ideal count O(X) and dyadic summation bound the last sum by O((L/R)^(1/12)), including the unit ideal. After squaring, the bound is

    H_J U^(1/6+epsilon)L^(5/6-delta)(L/R)^(1/6)
      =H_J U^[1/6+(5/6-delta)t+(1-delta)lambda+epsilon]. (R12)

This proves R8 and thus the author's S11 with an explicit source-legal uniformity argument. No assumption about cancellation between different m was made. The count of m was paid once through its Hilbert triangle mass, rather than being hidden as a divisor loss.

u=2gamma-r>0 for large X, including the three displayed targets.

The Mellin numerator gains the nonvanishing factor
chi(p)^K p^(K(1-s)); the fixed two-prime return survives. This is a
fixed multiplicative dilation, not a new cancellation theorem. For
principal chi, the actual cell n=p^(K+1)d, d prime in

the d term contributes, the pd term has h_K(p^K)=0, and higher p powers

If p^(K+1)<=X^(1-gamma-delta) for fixed0<delta<1-gamma, the same
selected-cell lower bound remains uniform. That diagnostic does not

## 6. The decisive signed-projector transport

Both Poisson transformations apply first to the complete signed expression. Zero-bin indicators are inserted only into the positive child energies afterward. For either consistent first-side orientation, SignedReconstruction and LA.11 give the literal row

    w=u0 e F_c G_c V_id h',
    W=M-R-(c-d)_+ +L_c-6a,
    L_c=log_Z NF_c<=5(R-R0).                           (R11)

The actual main radius is K0+(d-c)_++6a+omega. Its favorable -omega in (R11) can be dropped after using that actual ball, never by declaring the old row ball smaller. The two residues are 1+t_p and 1-t_p modulo six. A residue zero is a puncture. The two first-side F_c can differ; apply the argument to each side separately. Inside a side's second pairing the reflected row and whole conjugation are covered by the fixed unit/parent dictionary. The child width remains M'=M-(c-d)_+-6a-omega-g2+t2, with its actual enclosing padding; this new argument does not shorten it.

Here is why the weighted sum does not acquire an unallowed moving slot coefficient. The first projector s and every genuine second common prime divide w. Among first common primes, active nonzero residues occur in F_c and selected mask-divisor primes occur in e. The missing first radical has width at most p-R-E+R0. Freeze it first, paying that count once. At fixed w and missing radical, arbitrary-valuation labels and the first projector are divisor-many, as proved in SignedReconstruction's Rankin support bound. All common support already dividing w is automatically a natural zero of each surviving slot. Its extra deletion makes no change to that slot. The remaining holes are a subset of the frozen missing radical, together with the original already fixed common puncture. Summing over its divisor-many subsets costs only the existing small-power allowance. The surviving slot index sets and fixed relative characters have finitely many possibilities after the original slot list is fixed. The common Fourier majorant is chosen before labels; its label-dependent multiplier is a contraction inside the joint norm.

Partition by these fixed subsets, orientations and parent labels before applying the weighted row theorem. Divisor multiplicity is uniform in w, with no additional Z^p or Z^s0. Arbitrary row-dependent masks or a changing parent dictionary would invalidate this argument; the literal source has neither.

The second projector t is expressly different: it need not divide w. Freeze it and keep the full B3.65 inclusion-exclusion priority allocation. If a selected plain becomes d*l, retain psi_w(d), including its zero, and leave l unrestricted. If a slot is selected, freeze that prime. Do not add a quotient puncture at d. Let r_clip,j be the nonnegative clipped reductions for the two actual rectangles, and let z_j be their surviving total slot widths. Put

    rbar=(r_clip,1+r_clip,2)/2,  zbar=(z_1+z_2)/2.

B3.68--69 gives, for a divisor dyad,

    t_- -rbar +(e1+pi0,1+e2+pi0,2)/2 <=2theta_N.        (R12)

Thus the t-count is paid by both exact normalization scalars. It is not paid by assuming t is reconstructible from w. The four clipped rectangle pairs are treated separately; no common clipped reduction is assigned to an entire signed difference.

On side j, use the physical bin's pointwise bound only for its plains. Their squared normalized exponent is delta(A_clip,j-z_j). Keeping Q_j in the row sum, the paired plain price is therefore

    delta(A-c-b2-rbar-zbar)+small.

At fixed t, missing radical and finite allocation, Cauchy in w and the two raw weighted estimates give a paired slot exponent rho W+gamma zbar, replacing rho W+delta zbar. The t-scalars already used in (R12) are not reused: the separate -delta rbar comes from the shorter plain lengths. The net gain over the old high formula with all clipped reductions discarded is exactly

    eta(delta) zbar +delta rbar.                       (R13)

The whole products and independent heights are preserved. The natural conductor bound is that of the actual representative, <<fixed Nw. The fixed-inducing predicate is transported through FD/FE1/FE2, not replaced by nonprincipality of a preferred primitive representative. No other parent translate is inserted into its zero maximum.

The support terms in LA.13 also have the stronger usable bound

    E1<=(4rho-1-delta)min(c,d)
            -(rho+delta-1)(c-d)_+-E-Bc <=-c/28,
    E2<=-delta b2-t2.                                  (R14)

Indeed L_c<=5(R-R0), R<=min(c,d), 4rho-1>0 and 1-5rho<0. On [.68,.75], delta-4rho+1>=1166/6825>1/28 and rho+delta-1>=1/28. These retain arbitrary multiplicities and both source signs.

Every genuinely frozen slot incidence divides the relevant complete extracted column. Its total logarithmic norm is bounded by c+c2 on one side and c+d2 on the other, including repeated occurrences of the same prime. Newly frozen t-slots are part of r_j. Since r_j-r_clip,j is bounded by the aggregate clipping tolerance, this proves

    zbar>=z-c-b2-rbar-small.                            (R15)

The endpoint errors are aggregated over the fixed original slot system; no fixed loss is charged anew for every slot.

Now delta lies in [.68,.70]. If c+b2+rbar>=z/2, (R14) and the retained projector gain already save at least z/56, because each of c,b2,rbar has coefficient at least 1/28. This case uses the old density and needs no new raw-width premise. If c+b2+rbar<z/2, then zbar>=z/2-small and

    W>=M-c-6a>M-z/2-6a.

For the new atlas, z<=M/25 and the independently checked reserve is

    1-1/50-6a_max/M-21/25
        =269586511/4021080000>0.                       (R16)

Hence W>21z and each z_j<=z meets the raw theorem. Equation (R13) saves at least (14/135)z/2=7z/135>z/56, with room for the reserved losses. Exhausted slots fall in the first case. Bounded or slightly negative nominal row windows in that first case are handled by the old supported-window completion; no nonempty population is assigned a negative-power count. This proves the claimed **uniform z/56 gain in every configuration**, not only the empty-common-support sector.

For delta>=.70 the old high estimate is used. Bins straddling .68 go to the low branch with the original rounding allowance. A bin with lower edge at most .70 may use (R9) with that prescribed lower edge and its physical upper prime price differing by O(e). A bin wholly above .70 uses the old bound. The internal buffered maximum is not substituted at this boundary.

statement:
## 2. Exact source and Mellin reconstruction

Fix one ordinary complex Dirichlet character chi modulo q. Set
a_n=mu(n)chi(n), including all squareful and nonunit zeros. For fixed b>1
and integer k>2 define, for every real x>0,

    W_(b,k),chi(x)=sum_(n>=1) a_n exp(-n/x^b-i(n/x)^k).

Absolute convergence is immediate at each x and locally uniform in x>0.
The selected author source is b=3/2,k=6. The phase contains n^k, while the
damping contains n; confusing them changes the reciprocal-L shifts.

For sigma=Re s>0, write

    I_n(s)=integral_0^infinity exp(-nt^b-i(nt)^k)t^(s-1)dt
          =n^(-s) integral_0^infinity
                    exp(-n^(1-b)v^b-iv^k)v^(s-1)dv.

All powers use the principal branch. Choose a FIXED
0<alpha<min(pi/(2b),pi/(2k)). On the clockwise sector from 0 to -alpha,
Re(v^b)>0 and |exp(-iv^k)|<=1. On a large arc the damping is at most
exp(-n^(1-b)R^b cos(b alpha)); for each n this beats the polynomial arc
factor. The small arc tends to zero for sigma>0. Uniformity on compact
s-sets is sufficient here; a large-arc bound uniform in n is not needed
to rotate each term before forming the normally convergent remainder.

On v=r exp(-i alpha), the oscillatory modulus is
exp(-r^k sin(k alpha)). Taylor's integral remainder obeys

    |exp(-z)-sum_(j<K)(-z)^j/j!|<=|z|^K/K!, Re z>=0.

Consequently

    I_n(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)n^(-s-(b-1)j)+R_(n,K)(s),
    A_j(s)=(-1)^j Gamma((s+bj)/k)
                       exp(-i*pi*(s+bj)/(2k))/(k j!),

and

    |R_(n,K)(s)| <= n^(-sigma-(b-1)K) exp(alpha Im s)
       Gamma((sigma+bK)/k)
       /[k K! sin(k alpha)^((sigma+bK)/k)].                 (R1)

The sign of the phase and the gamma exponential are correct. The gamma
coefficient comes from u=i v^k, followed by rotation of a decaying gamma
ray in the right half-plane. The relevant integrals and their s-derivatives
are locally dominated by powers of r times exp(-c r^k), with log factors;
this proves holomorphy of each remainder. On every compact subset of
sigma>max(0,1-(b-1)K), (R1) gives a summable n-majorant. Hence
R_chi,K=sum a_n R_(n,K) is normally holomorphic there.

The absolute Fubini calculation is performed ONLY first on sigma>b:

    integral_0^infinity sum_(n>=1)exp(-nt^b)t^(sigma-1)dt
       =Gamma(sigma/b)zeta(sigma/b)/b.

Thus for H(s)=integral_0^infinity W(1/t)t^(s-1)dt,

    H(s)=sum_(j<K) A_j(s)/L(s+(b-1)j,chi)+R_chi,K(s).     (R2)

For b=3/2,k=6,K=1,

    H(s)=Gamma(s/6)exp(-i*pi*s/12)/(6L(s,chi))+R_chi,1(s), (R3)

where the remainder is holomorphic on sigma>1/2. A_0 is holomorphic and
nonzero on sigma>0. The actual character and all its Euler holes survive;
no primitive-character replacement is made.

Suppose that a FIXED gamma>1/2 satisfies, for every epsilon>0 and every
sufficiently large dyadic X,

    integral_X^(2X)|W(x)| dx/x <<_(chi,epsilon)X^(gamma+epsilon). (L1)

On a compact set with sigma>=gamma+eta, choose epsilon<eta and sum shells.
Factors (log x)^j for each fixed s-derivative are absorbed by the remaining
geometric buffer. The x near zero complement is bounded by
1/(exp(x^(-b))-1), so it is integrable against every fixed Mellin power.
H is therefore holomorphic throughout sigma>gamma. The L2 premise
integral|W|^2 dx/x<<X^(2gamma+epsilon) implies (L1) by Cauchy--Schwarz.

Identity (R3), initially on sigma>3/2, then continues the reciprocal
holomorphically to sigma>gamma. A zero of the ordinary meromorphic L there
would create a pole of its reciprocal, impossible since A_0 has no zero.
The principal pole at s=1 instead creates a reciprocal zero and is allowed.
Imprimitive Euler factors were already included. Each arbitrary compact
height range is covered, so this reaches every finite height without
assuming a height-uniform constant. For all fixed characters the common
gamma is chosen first; constants and onsets may depend on chi and epsilon.

This implication uses the ordinary analytic L-function and does not itself
resolve the project's external root-definition/import obligation. Neither
a reverse Mertens theorem nor equivalence to zero exclusion is being
asserted for this shell norm.

statement:
## G173. The complete hard-prime off-diagonal criterion

Fix an ordinary Dirichlet character chi modulo fixed q, principal or
imprimitive allowed, tau>0 fixed, and 1/2<gamma<1. Put

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    g(v)=(2pi tau)^(-1/2)exp(-v^2/(2tau)),
    U(y)=sum_(n>=1)a(n)g(log n-y), z(y)=exp(-gamma y)U(y).

The unit, prime2, squareful zeros and character zeros are literal.
Gaussian majorants justify local absolute convergence and derivatives;
the entire left tail is bounded by a polynomial times a Gaussian.
Coefficientwise logarithmic differentiation of a*chi=delta gives

    a(n)log n=-sum_(d|n)a(n/d)chi(d)Lambda(d),
    tau U'+yU+K1 U+K2 U=0,
    K1 U=sum_p chi(p)log p U(y-log p),
    K2 U=sum_(p,j>=2)chi(p)^j log p U(y-j log p).

The last two surviving local terms cancel at squareful n. Deleting higher
prime powers would change the source. This identity has W35/G118 ancestry.
In z coordinates each delay d has coefficient chi(d)Lambda(d)d^(-gamma).
For every R>=0 define

    I_R=int_0^R y|z(y)|^2dy, E_R=int_0^R |z(y)|^2dy,
    Qj(R)=-Re int_0^R conjugate(z(y))(Kj,gamma z)(y)dy.

The exact energy equation, including the initial value, is

    (tau/2)(|z(R)|^2-|z(0)|^2)+I_R+tau gamma E_R=Q1+Q2. (1)

Three full payments leave a more precise arithmetic problem.

First, the sum of absolute higher-power coefficients is finite:

    C_gamma=sum_(p,j>=2)log p p^(-j gamma)
      <=(1-2^(-gamma))^(-1)sum_(n>=2)log n n^(-2gamma).

Truncate z only above R, retaining its whole past. Translation contraction,
Minkowski and Cauchy give |Q2|<=C_gamma int_(-infinity)^R |z|^2. The past
is unconditionally finite. Split the positive integral at a fixed large Y;
for every eta>0 this proves

    |Q2(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta.                                  (2)

B_eta uses only a fixed bounded interval and the Gaussian left tail, not
an unknown future norm. This is a relative form bound, not prime-power
cancellation.

Second, the author pays p<=(2+y)^A whenever A(1-gamma)<1. The reviewer
enlarges that region to the exact monotone cutoff

    Y_gamma(y)=((2+y)/log(e^2+y))^(1/(1-gamma)), y>=0.        (3)

Equality belongs to the small sector. Elementary binomial prime counting
gives theta(t)<=4(log2)t. Partial summation yields

    sum_(p<=Y)log p p^(-gamma)
      <=[4log2/(1-gamma)]Y^(1-gamma).

Thus the row sum for (3) is O_gamma((2+y)/log(e^2+y))=o(y).
For large y, log p<=y/2 on this sector, so v=y-log p belongs to[y/2,y].
In the second half of 2|z(y)z(v)|<=|z(y)|^2+|z(v)|^2, change variables
separately for every p. Since y<=2v, the column is bounded using
p<=Y_gamma(2v) and is o(v). Also v<=R. The bounded initial region has
finitely many primes and a fixed bounded input interval. Therefore

    |Q_small(R)|<=eta I_R+B_eta                              (4)

for every eta>0. Both row and column are paid. Formula (3) is larger
asymptotically than every fixed subcritical power (2+y)^A. It does not
transfer an assumed residual estimate between different masks for free.

Third, expand the hard-prime contribution with p>Y_gamma(y) before taking
absolute values. Its literal summand is

    -Re[conjugate(a(n))chi(p)a(m)] log p exp(-2gamma y)
          *g(log n-y)g(log(pm)-y),

over all m,n>=1 and 0<=y<=R. For n=pm its coefficient is +1 exactly when
pm is a squarefree q-unit, otherwise zero. For fixed n the retained prime
log-weights sum to at most log n. The exact whole-line integral is

    int exp(-2gamma y)g(log n-y)^2dy
      =exp(tau gamma^2)n^(-2gamma)/(2sqrt(pi tau)).

Consequently the exact diagonal D_R is nonnegative and bounded by the
fixed finite constant obtained by summing log n n^(-2gamma). Define
H_R=Q_hard-D_R, precisely the complete n!=pm form. Every sign, phase,
infinite source sum and the complementary prime mask remains inside it.

**OPEN-PF.** For one common gamma in(1/2,1), suppose every fixed ordinary
chi admits delta_chi>0, B_chi and R0_chi such that

    H_R <= (1-delta_chi)I_R+B_chi, every R>=R0_chi.           (5)

Take eta=delta_chi/4 in (2) and (4) and absorb the finite initial range.
Then (1) gives, for all R>=0,

    (tau/2)|z(R)|^2+(delta_chi/2)I_R+tau gamma E_R<=B'_chi.  (6)

Thus U(y)=O_chi(exp(gamma y)) on every sufficiently large real y. The
bilateral transform F(s)=int U(y)exp(-sy)dy is holomorphic on Re s>gamma,
locally uniformly with all derivatives. On Re s>1 absolute Fubini gives

    F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2)/L(s,chi).

Continue L(s,chi)F(s)=exp(tau s^2/2). Its right side never vanishes, so
there is no ordinary L-zero in Re s>gamma at any finite height or
multiplicity. The principal pole at1 is allowed and forces a zero of F;
imprimitive factors and natural zeros were never removed. The standard
continuation and Euler-product conventions are those of [DLMF
25.15](https://dlmf.nist.gov/25.15). No height-uniform lower bound for the
Gaussian multiplier, unsmoothing theorem or native-H adapter is needed
for this one-way return.

The gamma is common to all fixed characters; margins, constants and
onsets may depend on chi. Neither gamma=1/2 nor growing-conductor
uniformity is supplied. Conditional c=.12515 would improve c11 by
.0000040364; 1/6,1/4 and values below1/2 remain conditional possibilities.
None has (5) proved. Even if a bound U(y)=O(exp(beta y)), gamma<beta<1,
is GRANTED, absolute prime summation gives the coarse flux exponent
1+beta-2gamma, against I's exponent2beta-2gamma. The gap1-beta remains.
This failed upper-budget trial is not a signed lower bound, and the
granted U bound is not inferred from a bare zero-free statement.

W35/G79/G118 retain credit for Gaussian renewal, energy drift and the full
logarithmic identity. The increment is the combined complete payments,
the enlarged moving cutoff and its exact residual criterion. No strict
coercivity follows from the equation alone.

It does not establish the old D20 estimate, transfer its real-shift interval to delta=3/5, or make its signed subfamilies hereditary. The four qualifications in R10 should accompany integration. Current worklog: frozen source bindings verified; complete report, helper and receipt read; relevant [research revision] source and review reconstructed; ordinary-character coefficients, projection, both complements, 24 shifted terms, norm equivalence and all-height return independently proved below; one independent exact algebra check passed. ## G162. All finite comparable matchings have a terminal-prime cut

In the finite squarefree q-unit set n<=X, each unramified prime p in
`(X/2,X]` has exactly one distinct comparable vertex, namely 1.
It has no other divisor and no proper multiple inside the cutoff.
Every disjoint pairing along divisibility therefore leaves at least
`#{X/2<p<=X,p not dividing q}-1` terminal primes unmatched.
For a nonnegative fractional matching with vertex capacity 1, their total
incident weight is also at most the capacity of 1; the same bound applies
to unmatched mass. Character restrictions can only remove edges.

Ordinary PNT makes this asymptotic to X/(2 log X), for fixed q.
No acyclicity is used: the result covers adaptive pivots and comparable
pairs differing by several primes. It does not apply to arbitrary complex
shared-vertex homotopies, incomparable pairs or partners beyond the cutoff.
It is not a lower bound on G150's global future-partner displacement cost.

The exact decomposition `M_chi(X)=A_p(X)-chi(p)A_p(X/p)` with
`A_p(Y)=sum_(n<=Y,p not dividing n)mu(n)chi(n)` is already G144 ancestry.
Choosing chi(p)=1 does not bound the remaining boundary term.
The new cut has wider matching scope but a weaker numerical lower bound
than the linear count for G144's specified cone. W59's additional homology
argument remains separately frozen, root-pending evidence; this acceptance
does not promote it. Incomparable exchanges such as 6<->11 avoid this cut,
but bounded short replacements still face G161.

## 1. Actual coefficients and a uniform modified family

Fix tau>0. Write g=g_tau and retain EXACTLY

    K_X(m,n)=integral_X^(2X) g(log(m/x))g(log(n/x)) dx/x.

Use f(n)=f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^v_3(n))). For each integer r>=1 define

    f_r(n)=product_{p|n, p does not divide 3r}(-1),
    F_r(y)=sum_{n>=1} f_r(n) g(log(n/y)),
    E_r(Y)=integral_Y^(2Y) F_r(y)^2 dy/y.                 (S1)

Thus f_1=f and every f_r has values +/-1. A prime dividing 3r
contributes +1 at ALL its positive powers; every other prime
contributes -1 at ALL its positive powers. In particular no exponent
or repeated-prime contribution is erased. Direct primewise checking gives

    f(rn)=f(r)f_r(n),
    f_r(qn)=f_r(q)f_{rq}(n),
    f_r(q)^2=1.                                        (S2)

Let 1/2<beta<1 be any FIXED exponent for which the accepted Mertens
input is available:

    M(t)=sum_{n<=t}mu(n)=O_beta(t^beta), t>=1.           (S3)

The inherited numerical choice is beta=.8749. With the CURRENT
accepted written endpoint theta_G=.8748866 one may instead take
beta=theta_G+eta, for any fixed eta>0 with beta<1, using the accepted
buffered Mertens consequence. This report does not assert S3 on the
boundary beta=theta_G, does not make its constants uniform as eta
tends to zero, and does not identify the new endpoint's pending formal
replay with a completed kernel receipt.

Here is the needed uniform dependence on r; it is not a hereditary
bound asserted for an arbitrary masked coefficient family. Define h_r
by its local generating factors, z=p^(-s):

    H_{r,p}(z)=(1-z)^(-2),                 p|3r;
    H_{r,p}(z)=(1-2z)/(1-z)^2,             p not |3r.

The latter equals 1-sum_{j>=2}(j-1)z^j. The exact finite coefficient
identity is f_r=h_r*mu. At beta>1/2 its absolute norm satisfies

    B_r(beta):=sum_a |h_r(a)|a^(-beta)
      = product_{p|3r}(1-p^(-beta))^(-2)
        product_{p not |3r}
           [1+p^(-2beta)/(1-p^(-beta))^2]
      <= C_beta product_{p|r}(1-p^(-beta))^(-2)
      <= C_(beta,delta) r^delta                         (S4)

for every fixed delta>0. The second product converges because
2beta>1. For the last inequality, the factor at sufficiently large p
is <=p^delta; the finite set of smaller primes contributes one fixed
constant. Prime 3 is always in the first product, and prime 2 is
handled by the displayed applicable local factor. There is no division
by 1-2*2^(-s), hence no hidden prime-two pole in this bound.

Finite convolution of S3 gives, for every t>=1,

    |sum_{n<=t}f_r(n)| <= C_beta t^beta B_r(beta).       (S5)

For 0<t<1 this sum is zero. Abel summation over the entire half-line,
with both endpoint limits paid by the Gaussian, then gives

    |F_r(y)| <= C_(beta,tau) B_r(beta)y^beta,
    E_r(Y) <= C_(beta,tau)B_r(beta)^2 Y^(2beta).         (S6)

Indeed the derivative integral is
y^beta integral_R e^(beta v)|g_tau'(v)|dv<infinity.
The same proof works for each fixed log derivative. Independently,
|f_r|=1 gives the UNIFORM-IN-r left-tail estimate

    |F_r(y)| <= C_(A,tau)y^A, 0<y<=2, for every A>0.   (S7)

This estimate, not an r-dependent bound carried to arbitrarily large
r, pays the entire small-scale tail below.

For finite prime blocks the logarithm of the nonzero finite Euler product is fixed by its absolutely convergent local series on Re s>0. Subtracting its first-prime terms gives

    V_P(s)=exp(sum_(p<=P)p^-s) product_(p<=P)(1-p^-s),
    log V_P=-sum_(p<=P)sum_(j>=2)p^(-js)/j.              (D1)

For every fixed rho>1/2 this converges normally and is bounded above and away from zero uniformly on Re s>=rho and in P. The first-order prime channel has been removed, not estimated. Its exact local coefficient is

    (1-z)exp(z)=1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j/j!.                (D2)

The needed analytic package is modest. Ordinary periodic character sums give A(x)=c x+O_q(1). For the Eisenstein family the fixed residue-lattice argument gives A(x)=c x+O_f(sqrt x+1): count complete fixed-conductor lattice cells in a norm disk and O_f(sqrt x+1) boundary cells, divide by the six units, and exclude the zero vector. statement:
## 3. Development03: a complete prime2 bridge and a very small first-gain reconstruction

### 3.1 Exact Euler algebra and the source correction

Put z_p=chi(p)p^-s. For Re(s)>1,

    D_b(s)=sum_n b(n)chi(n)n^-s = H_chi(s)/L(s,chi),
    H_p=(1-z_p)^-2,                            p=2,3,
    H_p=(1-2z_p)/(1-z_p)^2,                    p>=5.    (2)

The inverse K=1/H has

    K_p=(1-z_p)^2,                             p=2,3,
    K_p=(1-z_p)^2/(1-2z_p)
       =1+sum_(j>=2)2^(j-2)z_p^j,             p>=5.    (3)

Thus K(s)=sum k(n)chi(n)n^-s, with k(2)=k(3)=-2, k(2^2)=k(3^2)=1, k(p)=0 for p>=5, and k(p^j)=2^(j-2) for p>=5,j>=2; all higher2,3 powers vanish. Both weighted absolute coefficient norms are finite for every fixed sigma>1/2. For example, writing r=p^-sigma,

    ||H_p||_sigma <=1+r^2/(1-r)^2,     p>=5,
    ||K_p||_sigma <=1+r^2/(1-2r),      p>=5.              (4)

Since2*5^-sigma<1 and sum_p p^-2sigma converges, the products converge. The finite prime2/3 factors have their exact displayed expansions. These estimates are uniform under deleting ramified factors because z_p=0 there. They also prove H is nonzero above1/2: every displayed factor is nonzero there and the product of its deviation from1 converges normally. This is the G28 compensation mechanism with the alternate source and target correctly identified; it is not a new cancellation theorem.

Absolute convolution and Minkowski on the actual dilated shell give

    U(x)=sum_r k(r)chi(r)B(x/r),
    B(x)=sum_r h(r)chi(r)U(x/r),
    ||U||_sigma<=K_sigma||B||_sigma,
    ||B||_sigma<=H_sigma||U||_sigma.                     (5)

The Gaussian left tail makes the norms finite at small X whenever the large-scale estimate is available. General real shells can be covered by two dyadic ones. No cutoff is held fixed at an incorrect dilated scale.

Literal prime2 coefficient subtraction gives, at EVERY integer and for every character including chi(2)=0,

    f3(n)chi(n)=b(n)chi(n)
                 -2chi(2)1_(2|n)b(n/2)chi(n/2),
    F(x)=B(x)-2chi(2)B(x/2).                            (6)

Consequently the canonical Mellin multiplier is

    Mellin(F)(s)=exp(tau*s^2/2)
                       (1-2chi(2)2^-s)H_chi(s)/L(s,chi). (7)

If chi(2)!=0, the prime2 numerator has zeros on Re(s)=1, not in1/2<Re(s)<1. If chi(2)=0 it equals1. The classical right-boundary complement remains necessary for the canonical detector. The full inverse at prime2 is not an absolutely convergent *past-scale* Dirichlet convolution below1.

### 3.2 The stable inverse runs to larger scales

Let c=chi(2)!=0. Iterating (6) in its stable direction yields the finite identity

    B(x)=-sum_(j=1)^J (2c)^-j F(2^j x)
                           +(2c)^-J B(2^J x).           (8)

This is an exact telescoping identity, not a formal analytic continuation. The inherited calibrated bound ||U||_beta<infinity for any fixed theta6<beta<1, together with (5), gives ||B||_beta<infinity. Hence the last term tends to0 in every fixed shell L2 norm, proving

    B(x)=-sum_(j>=1)(2c)^-j F(2^j x)                    (9)

in that norm. Pointwise equality is not needed. If ||F||_sigma<infinity with sigma<1, Minkowski gives the exact convenient upper constant

    ||B||_sigma <= [2^(1-sigma)-1]^-1 ||F||_sigma,
    ||F||_sigma <= [1+2^(1-sigma)] ||B||_sigma.         (10)

The boundary condition is essential: (6) also has homogeneous solutions on Re exponent1, and simply discarding the last term under the absolute O(x) bound would be invalid. We use the already accepted buffered exponent, not the desired new one, to remove it. If chi(2)=0, F=B and no inverse is needed. Together (5),(10) give the full exponent equivalence between F,B,U for each1/2<gamma<1, and with the usual positive buffers at gamma=1/2. This does not assert exact-power endpoint norms there.

The inverse constant at sigma=.87486 is approximately11.0358757. This number is a diagnostic; the exact formula in(10) is the proof. The future-scale idea has explicit [research revision] ancestry. The present contribution is the literal corrected f3/b bridge and the finite complete price below, not a new general dilation-inverse architecture.

### 3.3 A finite retained source with both complementary errors paid

Choose theta6<beta<1, 1/2<sigma0<beta, a,b0>0, R=floor(X^b0) and J=ceil(a log_2 X). For c!=0 define on X<=x<=2X

    Q_X(x)=-sum_(r<=R) k(r)chi(r)
                        sum_(j=1)^J (2c)^-j F(2^j x/r). (11)

The letter b0 is a length exponent, distinct from the coefficient b(n). Each term is the same fixed full field F. Every r,r',j,j' interaction stays inside its L2 norm. For c=0 use Q_X=sum_(r<=R)k(r)chi(r)F(x/r).

Insert (8) into the full (5). The exact difference is the sum of the two complements

    E_2(x)=sum_(r<=R) k(r)chi(r)(2c)^-J B(2^J x/r),
    E_K(x)=sum_(r>R) k(r)chi(r)B(x/r).                   (12)

The inherited global beta norm pays even x/r<1. Weighted absolute coefficient norms give deliberately coarse but complete bounds

    ||E_2||_[X,2X] <= K_beta||B||_beta X^beta 2^-J(1-beta),
    ||E_K||_[X,2X] <= K_sigma0||B||_beta
                                     X^beta R^-(beta-sigma0).

Therefore

    ||U-Q_X||_[X,2X] << X^e2+X^eK,
    e2=beta-a(1-beta), eK=beta-b0(beta-sigma0).           (13)

Rounding changes only a fixed constant. For chi(2)=0 there is only E_K. No prime-density theorem, favorable cross term or signed-submask dominance is used. If a square moment is the desired statement, the COMPLETE difference is bounded by

    | ||U||^2-||Q_X||^2 |
         <=2||Q_X||||U-Q_X||+||U-Q_X||^2.               (14)

This pays both mixed terms and the square of the full error. The sharp r<=R endpoint is literal.

For an explicit coarse constant at sigma0=3/4, use 2^-3/4<3/5, 3^-3/4<4/9, 5^-3/4<3/10 and sum_(n>=5)n^-3/2<=1. Equations(4) and log(1+u)<=u give

    K_(3/4) <= (8/5)^2(13/9)^2 exp(5/2) <70,
    H_(3/4) <= (5/2)^2(9/5)^2 exp(100/49) <264.

The rational comparisons follow by fourth powers; exp(5/2)<13 follows from its Taylor sum through degree5 plus the geometric bound (5/2)^6/[6!*(1-5/14)] on the remainder. These are intentionally loose, character-independent coefficient bounds. If M_beta=||U||_beta and beta>3/4, the first table's choices consequently give

    ||U-Q_X||_[X,2X]
       <=18480 M_beta X^e2+36960 M_beta X^eK.

The factor2 in the second term pays floor(X^b0)>=X^b0/2. M_beta is the inherited fixed-character norm, not a newly bounded conductor-uniform constant.

Here is the weakest developed complete first-gain specialization. Use the inherited beta=437431/500000=.874862 and sigma0=3/4. Then:

| Desired gamma | Conditional c=1-gamma | a | b0 | e2 | eK | strict margin below gamma |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
|.87486|.12514|1/50000|1/50000|.87485949724|.87485950276|12431/25000000000|
|5/6|1/6|1/3|1/3|312431/375000|624931/750000|23/250000|
|3/4|1/4|1|101/100|187431/250000|37437569/50000000|69/250000|

The first row would improve the accepted c by.000001. Its retained field uses scales between roughly X^(1-1/50000) and X^(1+1/50000), with fixed factors2 from rounding, and only correction divisors r<=X^(1/50000). Because k is supported at exponents>=2 for p>=5 and at exponents0,1,2 for2,3, its support count up to R is O(sqrt R): write the part coprime to6 uniquely as u^2 v^3 with v squarefree and sum sqrt(R)/v^(3/2). Thus(11) has O(X^(1/100000)log X) nonzero shifted-field summands, with constants depending on the fixed choices. This is a count of source terms, not an algorithm for evaluating an infinite field or a cancellation estimate.

For any fixed gamma>1/2, choosing1/2<sigma0<gamma, a>(beta-gamma)/(1-beta) and b0>(beta-gamma)/(beta-sigma0) gives strict error exponents below gamma. The architecture therefore has no present analytic ceiling at1/6 or1/4; its arithmetic ceiling has not been determined. Approaching1/2 makes the compensation norm grow and does not prove a uniform endpoint theorem.

The exact OPEN input is, for every epsilon>0 and all sufficiently large dyadic X,

    ||Q_X||_[X,2X] <<_(chi,tau,epsilon) X^(gamma+epsilon). (15)

With(13), this returns the same bound for the FIXED U. The left Gaussian tail and shell Cauchy summation make its Mellin transform holomorphic on Re(s)>gamma. Initially at Re(s)>1 it equals exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,chi). Multiplication by L continues the identity; the exponential never vanishes, so every hypothetical L-zero in that half-plane is excluded. The principal pole at1 is handled as the usual removable zero of1/L. The known right boundary completes the stated ordinary zero-free conclusion. Moving Q_X is not itself assigned a fixed Mellin detector or trusted to retain a pole; the return first reconstructs fixed U.

Conversely a full U gamma estimate gives full F gamma by(5),(6), hence (11) is bounded with a uniform geometric j sum and K_(gamma+epsilon). Thus this is an equivalent complete arithmetic target, not a proved easier one. Reusing only the inherited beta estimate in(11) still yields exponent beta and cannot cross theta6. The retained arithmetic input(15) is unproved at every new exponent in the table.

## B. Two-cutoff decomposition with the original n retained

All convolutions here are ideal convolutions; no integer-norm
factorization is substituted. Let 1 be the constant ideal function,
delta the convolution unit, Lg(n)=log(q_n), and Lambda the actual
ideal von Mangoldt function. For U,V>=1 put mu_<=U, mu_>U and
Lambda_<=V, Lambda_>V for their exact norm truncations. Then

    Lambda = Lambda_<=V + mu_<=U * Lg
             - mu_<=U * 1 * Lambda_<=V
             + mu_>U * 1 * Lambda_>V.                 (B1)

This classical convolution identity is derived here rather than
imported with an unverified range. Indeed Lg=1*Lambda and
mu*1=delta; expanding the right side and grouping Lambda_<=V and
Lambda_>V gives precisely Lambda. Equality holds on every ideal,
including the unit. In the actual squarefree long window q_n>V,
the first term vanishes. Define there

    I(n) = sum_(d|n,q_d<=U) mu(d) log(q_n/q_d)
         - sum_(d k m=n,q_d<=U,q_k<=V) mu(d)Lambda(k),
    beta_U(d) = sum_(r|d,q_r>U) mu(r),
    II(n) = sum_(d e=n,q_d>U,q_e>V) beta_U(d)Lambda(e).

Then

    lambda(n) = [I(n)+II(n)]/log(q_n).                 (B2)

Here beta_U(d)=0 for q_d<=U and |beta_U(d)|<=tau(d).
For squarefree n the nonzero e in II is a prime ideal, and d is
squarefree and coprime to e. No nonsquarefree prime powers have been
added. The first Type-I term has d<=U. In the second, grouping
z=d k produces z<=UV with its exact signed coefficient
sum_(d k=z,d<=U,k<=V) mu(d)Lambda(k). Neither grouping is a new
prime projection on z or a shortening of the original long n.

Multiply (B2) by the COMPLETE actual summand at n: a(n), the two
perpendicular masks, original row and mark characters/projector,
original C_i(n), xi(g)A_i(g), and their own independent height.
Every identity then holds for each original R,P,g,n separately.
The equality exclusions and sharp far selector depend on n,n',
and the true short-core weight on g,g'; they are applied to these
same original variables after expanding the two linear identities.
Thus (B2) gives the exact four ordered covariance terms

    C_prime = C_(I,I)+C_(I,II)+C_(II,I)+C_(II,II),     (B3)

where I,II are divided by log(q_n) on their respective sides and
the second side has the original conjugation. This equation is
valid for the all-prime extension; JPS6 is still required to return
to the original degree-one projection. It does not assert that an
individual term of (B3) is an original-prime subfamily.

**B4 (unit, composite and shared-core tests).** If n=p is prime
and q_p>max(U,V), I(p)=log(q_p) and II(p)=0. In particular this
identity has not given original primes balanced factors. If
n=p q with q_p,q_q>max(U,V), then

    I(pq)=log(q_pq),
    II(pq)=-log(q_p)-log(q_q)=-log(q_pq).              (B4)

The two native factors recombine by
a(d)a(e)chi_d(e)^4=a(de), with the identical original R,P,g masks
and profile. They are not independent random phases. For a pair
of such semiprimes the normalized coefficient matrix of (B3) is

                         second I     second II
    first I                  1             -1
    first II                -1              1.

For a prime versus such a semiprime the surviving row is (1,-1);
for two primes only (I,I) survives. These statements include the
ordered cross terms and do not rely on positivity or equal heights.
They remain true for n=s p, n'=s p' with a shared prime ideal s,
provided s,p,p' are pairwise distinct and exceed the cutoffs. The
common native factor on the pair is a(sp) conjugate(a(sp')), not
an invented scalar at s. The
original short core is still (g,g'), and the original far norm gap
is still |q_sp-q_sp'|>H0. No coefficient argument replaces it by a
gap on the residual primes.

Consequently a proposed dispersion identity that deletes either
ordered Type-I/Type-II cross term fails already on these actual
semiprime coefficients. Replacing signed (B3) by the sum of its
four absolute coefficient contributions changes 0 into 4. This is
a counterexample to that manipulation, not to an upper bound for
the complete prime covariance. The same check is compatible with
the unit/nonunit decomposition of JPS: its unit coefficient is 1,
and the sum of nonunit coefficients is -1 on every squarefree
composite. The new cutoffs reorganize that cancellation; they do
not remove its necessity or create additional original prime pairs
in the paid high-gcd allocation.

**Exact internal check.** An in-memory deterministic Python check
used four labeled prime-ideal norms 7,13,19,31 (each a permissible
split-prime norm in the Eisenstein field), all 16 squarefree products,
and U,V independently in {1,6,7,12,13,18,19,30,31,90,200}. Logarithms
were represented by their four integer coefficient coordinates, not
floating point approximations. All 1,936 B1 identities passed,
including the small-prime Lambda_<=V term and cutoff endpoints.
This checks the algebra only, not admissibility of these finite
labels in an unspecified frozen ray/deletion set, and not an
analytic estimate. The proof above holds for every admissible set.
No random sample or Gauss-phase surrogate was generated.

    F=F_6=sum_n f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    R_z=F-T_z=sum_(omega_z(n)>=2) f(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    a=||T_z||_2, b=||R_z||_2, d=||F||_2.             (F44)

The accepted full-field baseline supplies d=O(X^beta) for a fixed beta<1. The explicit inherited calibration beta=.8749 follows from G21 and G28; more generally one may use any actually accepted full-field bound at beta=1-c_G+eta<1 with fixed eta>0. This is the sole place where the existing whole-field result enters. The prefix proof F4 did not use it. The use of G28 here is legitimate for FULL fields and implies no masked transfer.

From F5,F39,

    a is comparable to X/(tL^2),
    eta_X=d/a=O(X^(beta-1)tL^2)=o(1),
    |a-b|<=d, hence b/a=1+O(eta_X).                  (F45)

The exact field identity R_z=F-T_z yields

    <T_z,R_z>=-a^2+<T_z,F>=-a^2+O(ad),
    b^2=a^2-2Re<T_z,F>+d^2=a^2+O(ad+d^2).            (F46)

Therefore, NORMALIZED BY THE ACTUAL a^2,

    a^(-2) Gram(T_z,R_z)
       = [[1,-1],[-1,1]]+O(eta_X+eta_X^2)             (F47)

entrywise, with the first diagonal entry exactly1. This power-small normalized error is stronger than a conclusion obtained by substituting an asymptotic formula for a. In particular the actual cross scalar is eventually negative. Since the two coefficient supports are disjoint, it is an actual off-diagonal signed f3 interaction. It is not a depth-by-depth positivity assertion and is not new cancellation beyond the accepted full-field baseline.

The exact cosine/mismatch identity is

    rho=Re<T_z,R_z>/(ab),
    d^2=(a-b)^2+2ab(1+rho),                           (F48)
    0<=1+rho=[d^2-(a-b)^2]/(2ab).

Consequently the baseline gives

    |a-b|/a << X^(beta-1)tL^2,
    0<=1+rho << X^(2beta-2)t^2L^4.                   (F49)

The one-sided cross ratio in F46 has the LINEAR rate beta-1; the cosine defect has the SQUARED rate2beta-2. Equivalently,

    2Re<T_z,R_z>/(a^2+b^2)
                     =-1+d^2/(a^2+b^2).

For any proposed full target d<<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon), with1/2<gamma<1, the following pair is necessary and together sufficient, after renaming epsilon:

    |a-b| <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),
    1+rho <<_epsilon X^(2gamma-2+epsilon)t^2L^4.       (F50)

Necessity uses F48 and a,b comparable to X/(tL^2). Conversely the first bound makes b comparable to a, and F48 with the second bound gives the requested d estimate. For the already known baseline b is positive eventually; the same follows from the first proposed target when proving sufficiency without that baseline.

At beta=.8749 the linear/squared powers are -.1251/-.2502. The current c_G frontier gives -.1251134/-.2502268 with the chosen positive baseline buffer. At gamma=.87449 the powers required are -.12551/-.25102. These rate requirements are not established improvements. The polylog case has t=B loglog X, so its mismatch and cosine factors are respectively (log X)^2 loglog X and (log X)^4(loglog X)^2, up to fixed constants.

The ACTUAL difference a-b is mandatory in F48--F50. The available error bound after replacing either norm by a leading expansion is much larger than X^gamma for gamma<1. Even F4's second term leaves only an exponent-one remainder bound; no lower bound for that actual remainder is asserted. A leading rank-one Gram with a vanishing coefficient sum does not establish the exact small eigenvalue needed for a stronger whole-field norm.

For completeness, append R_zm to the fixed finite components in §8. Its leading coefficient is b_(m+1)=-lambda_m^(-1), since F is power-small compared with N_X. Then

    <C_i,C_j>=[b_i b_j+O(epsilon_X+d/N_X)]N_X^2,
    (C_0,...,C_(m+1))=(B_0,...,B_m,R_zm),
    sum_i b_i=0,  sum_i C_i=F.                        (F51)

This is the complete leading Gram INCLUDING the actual late complement. Its complement entries use the accepted full-field estimate; they are not separately proved depth estimates. Exact telescoping and F48 retain the residual that this leading Gram cannot measure.

## 1. Inputs and the new results

Use the notation of [M](../../zeta_zero_free_validated_merged.md), [CP](../cubic-packets.md), [BC](../[research revision]/cubic-mobius-core-moment.md), and [the independently accepted SR packet](../[research revision]/cubic-square-row-moment.md). The independent SR review, recorded in [[research revision]](../review-cycle-23.md), checks the original CP normalization and fixed-class statement. Write \(q_a=Na\), and put \(\vartheta_c=\chi_c^2\) for the cubic character. Every power retains its nonunit zeros.

The exact inputs used here are:

* **I-C3CF:** M (5.15), the cubic sieve with cube-free ideal rows and columns, arbitrary column coefficients, and its stated finite ray/reciprocity variants:
  \[
  \sum_{q_a\le A}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
  \left|\sum_{q_c\le X}^{\mathrm{cube\!-\!free}}
       z_c\vartheta_c(a)\right|^2
  \ll_\epsilon(AX)^\epsilon
       \{A+X+(AX)^{2/3}\}\sum_c|z_c|^2.
  \tag{MQ1}
  \]
  The actual columns below are squarefree. This is the cube-free theorem already stated in M, not an unmentioned extension of the squarefree-only version B2.25. Fixed column exclusions can be imposed through zero coefficients. Its constants do not depend on the arbitrary coefficients.

* **I-HECKE, used only for the all-repetition result:** the inherited all-primitive-finite-order zero-free strip with boundary \(b_0=.874886647039964131\ldots\), together with buffered conductor/height bounds for reciprocal Hecke functions, exact deleted factors, and finite profile orders. Relevant anchors are M Theorem B0 and (B0.14), and BC (BC13), including its interval-endpoint version. This is stronger than ordinary-zeta nonvanishing. It is explicitly required wherever the parameter \(b>b_0\) occurs.

* **I-CP:** M (2.8), (2.14)--(2.15) and CP (21)--(25), with the original coefficient, all total-column masks, fixed components, zero terms and single product kernel. Original column profiles and their fixed derivatives are rapid at both endpoints; the row Fourier profile is Schwartz. The fixed core twists have the finite-order scope of BC section 8. Angular outside-cube factors remain outside the core moment.

No assertion from the enlarged plain family M (B3.40) is silently applied to a Möbius polynomial. In particular, its moving-support contract does not identify a row-varying twist with fixed datum.

Write each nonzero element row in its quadratic class as

\[
n=d a^2,\qquad q_n=q_dq_a^2,
\tag{MQ2}
\]

where \(d\) is squarefree at every prime, with a prescribed unit representative modulo squares. The choice of generator for \(a\), modulo its bounded unit ambiguity, indexes every row with bounded multiplicity. There is no condition \((d,a)=1\). Separate the finitely many fixed-prime parity and unit choices; no moving prime is added to \(S\). Let \(d(n)\) denote this representative and use \(q_{d(n)}\) for its norm, rather than a character conductor.

For a frozen ideal \(R\), an interval \(\mathcal I\) of core norms, a fixed permitted finite-order twist \(\nu\), and an original common profile \(F\), set

\[
\mathcal M_n^R(X;F,\mathcal I)
=X^{-1/2}\!
 \sum_{\substack{c\ {\rm squarefree},\ (c,R)=1\\q_c\in\mathcal I}}
 \mu(c)\nu(c)\overline{\vartheta_c(n)}F(q_c/X).
\tag{MQ3}
\]

The original exclusion \(S\) is understood. The interval may have an infinite endpoint. Its endpoints are frozen independently of the row. For a fixed nonnegative Schwartz radial majorant \(\Omega\), let \(\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)\) be the sum of \(|\mathcal M_n^R|^2\Omega(q_n/H)\) over \(q_{d(n)}\le\Delta\) and rows sixth-power-free **away from \(S\)**. Let \(\mathcal E_{\rm all}\) have the same class cutoff and every row valuation. All fixed-prime valuations and element units are retained in both definitions.

Uniformly for \(H,X,\Delta\ge1\), \(1\le\Delta\le H\), and frozen polynomial-norm deletion ideals, the new bounds are

\[
\boxed{\mathcal E_6(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_\epsilon (HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S(F,\Omega)^2
\left\{(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\right\}.}
\tag{MQ4}
\]

For every fixed \(b_0<b<1\), I-HECKE additionally gives

\[
\boxed{\begin{split}
\mathcal E_{\rm all}(H,X,\Delta)
\ll_{b,\epsilon}(HX\Delta q_R)^\epsilon\mathscr S_b(F,\Omega)^2
\bigl\{&(H\Delta)^{1/2}+X\Delta+
       H^{1/3}X^{2/3}\Delta^{2/3}\\
       &+H^{1/6}X^{(2b+1)/3}\Delta^{5/6}\bigr\}.
\end{split}}
\tag{MQ5}
\]

These are estimates for the actual joint row family. The class representative is allowed to grow in the entire range being summed, and the constants are uniform in it. The first bound in particular gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_6\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ6}
\]

Put

\[
\kappa_b=\frac{4b+2}{5}>1.
\]

Then the all-repetition bound gives

\[
\Delta\le H/X^{\kappa_b}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\mathcal E_{\rm all}\ll H(HXq_R)^\epsilon.
\tag{MQ7}
\]

Fixed profile and height factors are suppressed in MQ6--MQ7. Their finite orders are uniform in every moving label. All preliminary losses are chosen below the final loss. No uniformity is asserted as \(b\) approaches \(b_0\).
