statement:
# [research revision]: direct attack on the complete Gaussian central moment



## Current checkpoint

Objective: obtain a strict field exponent below 1-c0 for the complete
W35 Gaussian source, or a consequential original-source partial estimate
with its actual remaining limitation. No increased c is established.

Read the frozen W35 generation and review, including R35.16--20. The
review hash is ccdb8ce3a52cf1cc793b09e20239b1f7bc9beba0718b16c13309e986b88ce7bf;
the generation hash is c3f53fa22e2b4d69a5bd1230c0e9aa3aa8bc0026416d781f6446386e58d022dd.
For a fixed tau>0, the discarded fields can be made X^(-A+o(1))
for any prescribed fixed A. This is accepted input, not a result
claimed again in this packet. The full local two-height moment and
all four product-bin diagonals remain the arithmetic object.

Initial independent tests, before consulting the maintained attempt
index: (1) eta times a finite inverse leaves a genuine finite remainder;
the completion still carries one reciprocal zeta, not zero reciprocal
factors. (2) Separately pricing ordinary intervals from M(t)<<t^.8749
still gives moment exponent .2498 at a=.75. (3) The fourth bin diagonal
is in a Gaussian upper tail; deleting it alone would merely repeat an
already paid tail mechanism and is not the substantive target.

The maintained [restricted mathematical source] and relevant keyword entries
were then inspected. Exact finite inverse stability, formal inverse
completion, profile-only contraction, and amplitude/cosine identities
already exist. They will not be relabeled as new progress. The next
calculation must retain the literal arithmetic remainder or price an
actual signed sector of it. No external provider or child is launched.

Final author result, submitted for independent review: a quantitative return from one literal
primitive original-pair cell, (d,e)=1 and (de,6)=1. The contracted
coefficient is f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^{v_3(n)})). A complete one-short field
has size O_epsilon(X^(.495+epsilon)); two weighted Dirichlet convolution
operators are bounded on every all-dyad growth class above 1/2. Their
use reconstructs the complete Gaussian detector with pointwise error
O_epsilon(X^(1/2+epsilon)). This is a source-prerequisite removal, not a
new moment exponent. The complete target remains open. The derivation
below is complete; the first failed finite-inverse inequality is also
proved on the actual original coefficients. Equation labels GC1--GC27
refer only to this file.

## 1. Literal primitive cell and its exact contraction

Fix tau>0 and theta=.495. Put Y=floor(X^theta), and retain the W35
g_tau, S_tau, b(ell)=(-1)^(ell+1), A(n)=mu(n)-2*1_(2|n)mu(n/2).
Write n_(6)=n/(2^{v_2(n)}3^{v_3(n)}), and set

    f_3(n)=mu(rad(n/3^{v_3(n)}))
          =b(n)*mu(rad(n_(6))).                         (GC1)

Thus f_3(n) is always +1 or -1. At 3^j it is +1; at every other
positive prime power it is -1. It is multiplicative but not completely
multiplicative. Prime powers have not been set to zero.

Consider the following literal mask of the original two Mobius factors:

    P_Y(x)=sum_{d,e>Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                      mu(d)mu(e) S_tau(x/(de)).          (GC2)

This is a changed, explicitly specified original-pair cell, not a
claimed hereditary bound for the full W35 field. In particular, it is
not the current-SP mask or RN source. All original coefficients inside
this cell, complete alternating restoration and strict lower endpoints
remain. All series below converge absolutely before the finite divisor
identities are used: the coefficient majorant is at most d_3(n),
which the Gaussian in log(n/x) dominates.

Define

    F_tau(x)=sum_{n>=1}f_3(n)g_tau(log(n/x)),
    J_Y(x)=sum_{n>=1}f_3(n)1_{rad(n_(6))<=Y}
                                  g_tau(log(n/x)),
    I_Y^prim(x)=sum_{d,e<=Y; (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                            mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(x/(de)).

The exact identity is

    P_Y=F_tau-2J_Y+I_Y^prim.                             (GC3)

Proof of the uncut coefficient: d and e are odd, hence b(n/(de))=b(n)
whenever de divides n. At each prime p>=5 dividing n, the allowed local
allocations to the coprime squarefree pair (d,e) are neither, d alone,
or e alone. Their signed sum is 1-1-1=-1. Primes 2 and 3 cannot be
allocated. The coefficient is exactly b(n)mu(rad(n_(6)))=f_3(n).
This treats every original prime power and the ordered-pair convention.

For the one-short source d<=Y, fix an allowed d dividing n. The inner
sum over e cancels unless d contains every prime p>=5 dividing n:
each missing prime contributes 1-1=0. Since d is squarefree and
6-free, the surviving d is exactly rad(n_(6)); its coefficient is
mu(d)b(n). Thus the one-short source equals J_Y, with the exact <=Y
endpoint. Inclusion-exclusion of the two lower cuts proves GC3.
No infinite Dirichlet series was moved to a new line in this argument.

## 2. A paid small-radical field, including its unbounded prime powers

For every fixed epsilon>0, the positive Dirichlet series

    C_epsilon=sum_{n>=1} n^(-epsilon)/rad(n_(6))
      =(1-2^(-epsilon))^(-1)(1-3^(-epsilon))^(-1)
       *prod_{p>=5}[1+p^(-1-epsilon)/(1-p^(-epsilon))]
      <infinity                                                (GC4)

converges. For all sufficiently large p, the denominator is >=1/2;
the remaining prime sum is bounded by sum_{m>=2}m^(-1-epsilon).
The finitely many small-prime factors are finite. The constant may be
large as epsilon tends to zero; epsilon is fixed before X varies.

Since 1_{rad(n_(6))<=Y}<=Y/rad(n_(6)) and
g_tau(log(n/x))<=sup_v[e^(epsilon*v)g_tau(v)]*(x/n)^epsilon,

    |J_Y(x)|<=C_(epsilon,tau) Y x^epsilon.             (GC5)

This estimates the entire restoration-coalesced field without an n
cap, and it is uniform in all Y>=1 and x>0. In particular, on every
shell X<=x<=2X,

    |J_Y(x)| <<_(epsilon,tau) X^(.495+epsilon).         (GC6)

The controller independently supplied the short proof GC4--GC5 after
being informed of the primitive-cell contraction. The present author
had obtained the same exponent by summing fixed radical fibers with a
positive Dirichlet weight. GC4 is the incorporated controller check,
not an independently novel author claim.

For I_Y^prim, every de<=Y^2<=X^.99, so x/(de)>=X^.01.
R35.4, with its already verified growing derivative constants and one
common order 1+floor(.01*log(X)/tau), applies to every pair before
absolute summation of at most Y^2 pairs. Thus, for every fixed B>0,

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|I_Y^prim(x)| <<_(B,tau) X^(-B).     (GC7)

This is an application of the accepted Gaussian Type I estimate, not
a newly claimed tail theorem. Combining GC3, GC6 and GC7 proves

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|P_Y(x)-F_tau(x)|
                    <<_(epsilon,tau) X^(.495+epsilon). (GC8)

The result is unconditional apart from the elementary W35 profile
identities and tails; it does not use Mertens, a prime theorem, an SP
estimate, a fixed-depth asymptotic or an unproved covariance hypothesis.

## 3. Exact arithmetic reconstruction of the complete detector

Let h and k be multiplicative sequences given by these local values:

For p=2 or 3:

    h(p^j)=j+1 (j>=0),
    k(1)=1, k(p)=-2, k(p^2)=1, k(p^j)=0 (j>=3).

For p>=5:

    h(1)=1, h(p)=0, h(p^j)=-(j-1) (j>=2),
    k(1)=1, k(p)=0, k(p^j)=2^(j-2) (j>=2).

Here local occurrences of h(1)=k(1)=1 specify the same unit coefficient.
Their Euler products, initially in the common absolute half-plane, are

    H_6(s)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-s))^(-2)
           *prod_{p>=5}(1-2p^(-s))/(1-p^(-s))^2,
    K_6(s)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-s))^2
           *prod_{p>=5}(1-p^(-s))^2/(1-2p^(-s)).       (GC9)

At p>=5 the first nonconstant term has degree two. For every fixed
sigma>1/2, 2p^(-sigma)<1 for all such primes, and the nonconstant
absolute local masses are O_sigma(p^(-2sigma)). Consequently

    H_abs(sigma)=sum_n |h(n)|n^(-sigma)<infinity,
    K_abs(sigma)=sum_n |k(n)|n^(-sigma)<infinity.        (GC10)

More explicitly, their positive local products are

    H_abs(sigma)=prod_{p|6}(1-p^(-sigma))^(-2)
       *prod_{p>=5}[1+p^(-2sigma)/(1-p^(-sigma))^2],
    K_abs(sigma)=prod_{p|6}(1+p^(-sigma))^2
       *prod_{p>=5}[1+p^(-2sigma)/(1-2p^(-sigma))].

These are genuine uniformly-in-height bounds for the two Dirichlet
multipliers, since |H_6(sigma+it)|<=H_abs(sigma) and similarly for K_6.
They require no finite-height exception. Also H_6 K_6=1 throughout
Re s>1/2, by absolute convergence and the local factors.

The exact coefficient identities are

    f_3=h*A,       A=k*f_3.                            (GC11)

They may be checked coefficientwise, without continuation. At p>=5,
the f_3 factor is (1-2z)/(1-z), the A factor is 1-z, and their ratio
is (1-2z)/(1-z)^2. At p=3 the f_3 factor is (1-z)^(-1),
while A has 1-z, giving (1-z)^(-2). At p=2 the f_3 factor is
(1-2z)/(1-z) and A has (1-2z)(1-z), again giving (1-z)^(-2).
Thus the original exceptional prime-two coefficients 1,-3,2,0,...
are recovered exactly; they have not been replaced by ordinary mu.

For any sequence c write (T_c V)(x)=sum_{r>=1}c(r)V(x/r).
Coefficientwise absolute Fubini against the Gaussian gives

    F_tau=T_h G_tau,        G_tau=T_k F_tau.           (GC12)

For example, at a fixed sigma>1, GC10 and sum n^(-sigma)<infinity
bound the absolute double coefficient sum after multiplying by
C_(sigma,tau)x^sigma. This justifies the initial rearrangement for
every x>0. No low-height truncation or product cap is interchanged
with T_h or T_k without an error estimate.

The exclusion of BOTH primes 2 and 3 from the primitive original pair
is deliberate. With only prime 2 excluded, K has a p=3 denominator
1-2*3^(-s), and its absolute series requires sigma>log(2)/log(3).
With neither excluded, p=2 gives the worse threshold sigma>1.
The fixed mask (de,6)=1 removes these finite obstructions and gives
GC10 for the full useful half-plane sigma>1/2. This is an arithmetic
choice of source with its reconstruction paid, not an assumption that
deleting small primes from a signed energy is harmless.

## 4. Cross-dyad norm transport and a quantitative field reconstruction

For sigma>0 set

    ||V||_{B_sigma}=sup_{Z>0} Z^(-sigma)
                   (integral_Z^{2Z}|V(x)|^2 dx/x)^(1/2).

Whenever sum|c(r)|r^(-sigma)<infinity, Minkowski gives

    ||T_c V||_{B_sigma}
       <=[sum_r |c(r)|r^(-sigma)] ||V||_{B_sigma}.      (GC13)

For a fixed shell, change variable x/r=y in each summand. Its norm
is bounded by ||V||_{B_sigma}(X/r)^sigma. Sum these bounds before
taking a limit; the convergent majorant also justifies the limiting
operator. No orthogonality is asserted. In particular all ordered
cross terms of the reconstructed source are retained in its true
Hilbert norm. If the hypothesis is given only on dyadic Z=2^j,
each shifted interval [X/r,2X/r] meets at most two consecutive such
shells; the same conclusion holds with a fixed factor depending on
sigma. The bound is not restricted to one frozen shell.

The far-left tails of G_tau and F_tau make their small-Z contributions
finite for every sigma>0. For x<=1, (log n-log x)^2 is at least
(log n)^2+(log x)^2, and their coefficients are bounded by 3 and 1.
Both fields are therefore O_tau(exp(-(log x)^2/(2tau))). On any
remaining fixed compact x interval they are bounded. Thus an all-large-
dyad power estimate extends to the B_sigma estimate, after fixing its
exponent buffer, without an unpriced small-scale input.

It follows from GC8, GC10--GC13 that for every fixed 1/2<=gamma<1,
the following three all-dyad assertions are equivalent:

    (i)  ||G_tau||_{L2[X,2X]} <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon);
    (ii) ||F_tau||_{L2[X,2X]} <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon);
    (iii)||P_{floor(X^.495)}||_{L2[X,2X]}
                                  <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon). (GC14)

They quantify every epsilon>0 and every sufficiently large dyad,
with constants independent of X. The measure is dx/x throughout.
Choose a smaller fixed exponent buffer before applying GC13; it
remains >1/2. GC8 is below gamma even with a small further buffer.
For gamma>1/2 the exact-power version, with O(X^gamma) and no epsilon
in each of (i)--(iii), is also equivalent: apply GC13 at sigma=gamma
and choose the error buffer in GC8 below gamma-.495. At gamma=1/2
this argument proves the displayed all-epsilon equivalence, not
boundedness of the convolution operators at the unbuffered endpoint.
This is an equivalence of the complete growth estimates, not a claim
that the masked cell's local energy dominates the original local
energy on the same shell.

There is also an explicit finite reconstruction with a paid error.
Fix X_0>=2. For Z>=X_0 set P^sc_Z=P_{floor(Z^.495)} as in GC2;
the superscript distinguishes a scale Z from the original lower-cut
parameter Y in P_Y.
For x in [X,2X], define

    R_X(x)=sum_{1<=r<=X/X_0} k(r) P^sc_{X/r}(x/r).

The floor in each P^sc_{X/r} is fixed throughout the shell in x.
For every epsilon>0,

    sup_{X<=x<=2X}|G_tau(x)-R_X(x)|
                           <<_(epsilon,tau,X_0) X^(1/2+epsilon). (GC15)

To prove it choose sigma=1/2+epsilon, reducing epsilon harmlessly if
needed, and choose delta>0 with .495+delta<sigma. For r<=X/X_0,
GC8 gives an error <<(X/r)^(.495+delta)<=(X/r)^sigma.
The sum is <=X^sigma K_abs(sigma). For r>X/X_0, the argument x/r
lies in (0,2X_0). The far-left and compact bounds give
|F_tau(x/r)|<=C_(sigma,tau,X_0)(x/r)^sigma. Its entire tail is
bounded by the same convergent weighted sum. GC12 now proves GC15.
Thus every arithmetic reconstruction endpoint and all small scales
are paid. This bound does not count the r labels as a subpower family;
it prices them by their actual weighted coefficient mass.

The accepted baseline gives ||G_tau||_2<<X^beta, beta=.8749. GC12--13
give the same bound for F_tau; GC8 gives it for P_Y. From GC15,
the literal additive scalar comparison, including both mixed terms,
has bound

    | ||G_tau||_2^2-||R_X||_2^2 |
                                  <<_epsilon X^(beta+1/2+epsilon). (GC16)

Here beta+1/2=1.3749 is strictly below 1.74898. This comparison uses
the accepted baseline only for the scalar cross term, not for GC15.
There is still no proof that ||R_X|| has exponent below beta.
Applying the original W35 field approximation to G_tau gives the
same additive comparison between the COMPLETE original finite-band
or four-diagonal scalar and ||R_X||_2^2 at this target. At a much lower
target where the baseline scalar error would be too large, GC14 gives
the valid norm equivalence instead. R35.1 then supplies zero exclusion
only IF the equivalent all-dyad estimate has actually been proved.

## 5. Return through the actual four diagonals and both height variables

Here the primitive source is connected to the frozen W35 arithmetic
format. Fix once and for all A_0>0 and tau>0 and choose exactly the
reviewer's R35.16 constants

    kappa=C=sqrt(2*tau*(1+A_0)),
    D=sqrt(2*(1+A_0)/tau).

For a local scale Z, use all the R35 definitions with X replaced by Z:
Y_Z=floor(Z^.495), L_Z=log Z, H_Z=kappa*sqrt(L_Z),
T_Z^prod=Z*exp(-H_Z), B_Z=2Z*exp(H_Z), and
Dmax_Z=B_Z/(Y_Z+1). Let I_i(Z) be the original sharp interval

    {d in N:Y_Z<d<=Dmax_Z,
            i=floor((log d-.5*log Z)/H_Z)}.

The left bin edge is included, the right bin edge excluded, and the
real Dmax_Z endpoint is not rounded outward. For all sufficiently
large Z, J_Z=1 and the exact four ordered diagonals are i+j in
{-2,-1,0,1}. Define

    P_Z^rect(y)=sum_{i+j in {-2,-1,0,1}}
       sum_{d in I_i(Z),e in I_j(Z); (d,e)=1; (de,6)=1}
                        mu(d)mu(e)S_tau(y/(de)).        (GC17)

The bounded pair mask 1_{(d,e)=1,(de,6)=1} is independent of ell.
R35.5 therefore pays exactly the low-product omissions for this
source. Every additional omitted d>Dmax_Z, e>Dmax_Z or i+j>J_Z
has de>B_Z and is paid by the absolute R35.6 bound. These observations
prove, uniformly on y in [Z,2Z],

    P_{Y_Z}(y)-P_Z^rect(y)
                                  =O(Z^(-A_0+o(1))).   (GC18)

Only after the complete alternating restoration has been used in the
low-product estimate may total indices n=de*ell>B_Z be deleted.
This second deletion is absolute, again R35.6. The remaining exact
restoration length is <=2*exp(3*kappa*sqrt(log Z)). Nothing asserts
that the low-product estimate is hereditary under an ell-dependent
mask. These are the original W35 endpoint conventions and sequence of
operations, now applied to an explicitly allowed original-pair mask.

For any fixed a in (0,1), put

    C_ij^6(s;Z)=sum_{d in I_i(Z),e in I_j(Z);
                         (d,e)=1;(de,6)=1} mu(d)mu(e)(de)^(-s),
    D_Z^6(t)=E_tau(a+it)eta(a+it)
                    *sum_{i+j in {-2,-1,0,1}} C_ij^6(a+it;Z).

The two factors in C_ij^6 are still coupled by their literal gcd
condition. It is not replaced by a product of independently sieved
one-variable polynomials. The exact full-height local scalar is

    ||P_Z^rect||_2^2=(2*pi)^(-2) integral_R integral_R
       D_Z^6(t) conjugate(D_Z^6(t'))
       *{(2Z)^(2a+i(t-t'))-Z^(2a+i(t-t'))}
                                   /{2a+i(t-t')} dt dt'. (GC19)

The value of the fraction when t=t' is its literal nonzero value;
2a>0 precludes a denominator singularity. Every ordered bin-pair
interaction, independent height and complex phase remains. The
identity uses the entire transform E_tau eta of the complete S_tau,
as proved in R35.11. It does not interchange the alternating ell
Dirichlet series with integration on Re s=a<1.

The R35 height-tail argument is valid here by absolute majorization
of the subset of ordered pairs: |eta(a+it)|<=(|a+it|/a), each original
pair has its original (de)^(-a) weight, and the upper pair scale is
<=Z*exp(3H_Z). Thus |t|>D*sqrt(log Z) costs a field
O(Z^(-A_0+o(1))). For the fully capped coefficient form one can
instead use the exact Fourier Gaussian with its finite coefficient
polynomial; the same proof uses its d_3 majorant. Both presentations
retain the full local two-height kernel. Their arithmetic coefficients
are not asserted equal term by term; they have the paid field
comparison R35.17 with this permitted pair mask.

GC14 consequently remains true with P_Y replaced by any of these
complete primitive four-diagonal/capped/finite-height approximants.
The implication to the original COMPLETE W35 scalar is through
GC12--GC15 and all scales, not through a positivity claim for its
primitive subenergy. GC15 and GC16 also remain valid with P_Z^rect
replacing P^sc_Z, or with its capped/height-truncated field: combine
GC18 with GC8 before the same weighted sum. Choose X_0 above the
fixed eventual threshold; every smaller scale is already accounted
for by the tail argument in GC15.

For clarity, the complete reconstructed all-height Mellin amplitude is

    D_X^rec(t)=E_tau(a+it)eta(a+it)
       *sum_{r<=X/X_0} k(r)r^(-a-it)
                       sum_{i+j in {-2,-1,0,1}}
                                   C_ij^6(a+it;X/r).  (GC20)

Its local Gram has exactly the GC19 kernel with Z replaced by X and
D_Z^6 replaced by D_X^rec. Expanding it retains EVERY r,r',i,j,i',j'
interaction and both independent heights. If each constituent is
height-truncated, its own cutoff is inserted before summation, and
the already paid field error applies. In particular, no independent
absolute estimate of each scalar cross cell is being imported.

An equivalent simpler readout is the fixed f_3 field itself. On the
finite window Z*exp(-H_Z)<n<=B_Z its coefficients are exactly f_3(n).
The omitted low end is bounded absolutely by

    Z*exp(-H_Z)*g_tau(-H_Z)=O(Z^(-A_0)*exp(-H_Z));

the high end and Fourier-height tail follow the same bounded-
coefficient Gaussian estimates as R35.6/R35.8. This last optional
finite readout removes restoration multiplicities, but it does not
supply a moment bound. Its kernel is still R35.14, with coefficients
f_3(n)f_3(m), all signs and both height variables retained.

## 6. What arithmetic estimate is still missing

The theorem above removes the need to establish an independent
compensation estimate between the primitive cell and all of its
original common-prime/small-prime complements. Their return is the
explicit weighted convolution GC12, with the genuine boundary cost
GC8 and reconstruction error GC15. It does NOT bound the primitive
source below the accepted exponent, and it does NOT say that its
literal complement is a small field on the same shell.

The accepted arithmetic input still gives only beta=.8749. Its
available estimate on the new primitive component can be reconstructed
directly, without a hereditary mask assertion. Insert
1_{(d,e)=1}=sum_{q|d,e}mu(q); retain q squarefree and (q,6)=1.
Write d=qu,e=qv. Natural Mobius zeros impose (uv,6q)=1, and there is
no remaining (u,v)=1 condition. Therefore

    C_ij^6(s;Z)=sum_{q>=1;(q,6)=1}mu(q)q^(-2s)
                         V_(i,q)(s)V_(j,q)(s),
    V_(i,q)(s)=sum_{qu in I_i(Z);(u,6q)=1}mu(u)u^(-s). (GC21)

The coefficient is mu(q)^3=mu(q), not a positive replacement, and
the exact divided interval endpoints are retained. MG9--MG10 give
uniform coprime partial sums O_(eta)(U^beta*(6q)^eta). Abel summation
on the actual interval, for any fixed 0<a<beta, then gives

    |V_(i,q)(a+it)|
      <<_(a,beta,eta) (1+|t|)(6q)^eta
                                     (D_i^*/q)^(beta-a),

whenever the divided interval is nonempty. Here
D_i^*=min(Dmax_Z,sqrt(Z)*exp((i+1)*H_Z)), with the unchanged sharp
interval I_i(Z) inside this real enclosing endpoint. Summing the convergent
q^(-2beta+2eta) series, with eta<beta-1/2, proves

    |C_ij^6(a+it;Z)|
      <<(1+|t|)^2 (D_i^*D_j^*)^(beta-a).               (GC22)

All constants are uniform in the original bins and in t. At a=.75,
the resulting Gaussian one-height moment bound has exponent
2beta-2a=.2498, exactly the prior available exponent. The target
gamma=.87449 still requires .24898. Neither GC21 nor the absolute
q-series supplies the missing .00082. No termwise sign deletion,
suppression of t!=t', or collapse of the four diagonals is licensed.

Equivalently, GC10--GC13 transfer the original baseline to F_tau;
they preserve the exponent. The first coefficient of both arithmetic
operators is 1, so a norm bound for the reconstruction is not a strict
contraction of the retained source. A gain still requires arithmetic
cancellation in its complete signed moment. This is the precise
remaining obligation, rather than an unproved claim that the
primitive source is automatically smaller.

## 7. A decisive failed finite-inverse inequality on the original data

One tempting shortcut is to use exact finite Dirichlet inversion and
then promote the tiny completed-field error to a tiny operator norm.
The second step is false for the literal W35 coefficients, even at
fixed Gaussian width and zero modulation height. The following proof
does not substitute a generic bounded-coefficient counterexample.

Fix sigma>=0. Let N=floor(B_X), and for any coefficient sequence c
define the N-by-N divisor-convolution matrix and Gaussian readout

    [L_sigma(c)]_(n,m)=1_(m|n)c(n/m)(n/m)^(-sigma),
    [W_X(v)](x)=sum_{n<=N} n^sigma v_n g_tau(log(n/x)),
                                          X<=x<=2X.   (GC23)

The input norm is ordinary l2 on {1,...,N}; the output measure is
dx/x. For the unit vector e_1,

    W_X L_sigma(c)e_1=sum_{n<=N}c(n)g_tau(log(n/x)).

The finite identities are exact:

    L_sigma(mu)L_sigma(1)=I,
    L_sigma(b)L_sigma(mu)=L_sigma(q_2),
    L_sigma(b)L_sigma(mu)^2=L_sigma(A).                (GC24)

Here q_2=delta_1-2delta_2. All factors contributing to an output n<=N
also lie <=N, so truncating the divisor matrices introduces no missing
coefficient in GC24. These identities supply no estimate for the
following output operator difference.

Take c_X(n) to be the EXACT finite literal W35 coefficient from R35.7:

    c_X(n)=sum_{de*ell=n; d,e>Y; de>T_X^prod}
                             mu(d)mu(e)b(ell), n<=N.

It vanishes whenever n<=T_X^prod. At the actual source vector e_1,
R35.17 together with its absolute A-tail bound proves

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]e_1||_2
                                    << X^(-A_0+o(1)). (GC25)

But the full operator norm satisfies

    ||W_X[L_sigma(A)-L_sigma(c_X)]||_(l2->L2[X,2X])
                                    >=c_(tau,sigma)X^(sigma+1/2)
                                                        (GC26)

for all sufficiently large X. This is incompatible with a proposed
uniform operator version of GC25.

Proof: let M_X be the integers m in

    [2*exp(4tau)*X, 4*exp(4tau)*X].

For sufficiently large X this interval is inside {1,...,N}, since
B_X/X=2*exp(kappa*sqrt(log X)) tends to infinity. Its cardinality
is comparable to X, with constants depending only on tau. Every
column m in M_X of L_sigma(c_X) is zero: a nonzero quotient q would
require q>T_X^prod, whereas m*T_X^prod>N for all sufficiently large
X. This last inequality is just log X>2kappa*sqrt(log X)+O_tau(1).

The corresponding column for A has readout

    m^sigma sum_{q<=N/m}A(q)g_tau(log(qm/x)).           (GC27)

Uniformly for m in M_X and X<=x<=2X, log(m/x)>=4tau. Thus, for q>=2,

    g_tau(log(qm/x))/g_tau(log(m/x))
      =q^(-log(m/x)/tau)*exp(-(log q)^2/(2tau))
      <=q^(-4).

Using A(1)=1 and |A(q)|<=3, the q>=2 part in absolute value is at
most 3*sum_{q>=2}q^(-4) times the q=1 Gaussian. The elementary bound

    3*sum_{q>=2}q^(-4)
      <=3*(1/16+integral_2^infinity t^(-4)dt)=5/16

shows that GC27 is at least (11/16)*m^sigma*g_tau(log(m/x)).
The ratio m/x belongs to the fixed compact interval
[exp(4tau),4*exp(4tau)], so its Gaussian is bounded below by a
positive constant depending only on tau. Every one of these literal
columns is therefore >=c_(tau,sigma)X^sigma across the entire shell.

Use the positive unit vector |M_X|^(-1/2)*1_(m in M_X). Adding the
columns gives output >=c_(tau,sigma)X^(sigma+1/2) everywhere on the
shell; integration over logarithmic length log 2 proves GC26.
The finite cap, ordered coefficients, prime-two values and the strict
original product cut have all been retained.

This is a failure of a PARTICULAR unrestricted operator transfer. It
is not a lower bound for the actual source vector e_1, for the full
Gaussian detector, for the primitive field, or for its signed local
moment. It does not contradict GC13, which acts on the physical
all-dyad growth norm using specific arithmetic convolution identities.
It also does not rule out a source-sensitive operator estimate with
an independently justified domain. The reopening condition is such
a paid source-sensitive readout bound, or a new signed estimate for
the primitive moment in GC19. Finite inverse identities alone do not
provide it.

## 8. Prior scope, mathematical status, and next action

The initial finite eta/inverse and separate-bin tests were made before
consulting the maintained attempt index. The index and relevant source
families were then used to reject duplicate claims. In particular:

- MG12--MG16 in [restricted mathematical source] already
  prove the original two-factor common-divisor tail
  X^(beta+epsilon)G^(1-2beta) for the old actual profile. MG17--MG30
  already supply four-singleton incidence and cross-gcd cancellation.
  [research revision] BT and [research revision] BP extend the same mechanism to other actual
  restored sources. These are useful components, not new arithmetic
  estimates discovered here. A Gaussian transfer would pay sectors,
  but it is not counted as this packet's main result.
- Exact finite Mobius inverses, finite-matrix stability and readout
  limitations already occur in the maintained index and R35's C03
  discussion. W29 R29.3 proves a different unrestricted norm failure
  by finite prime-phase approximation. GC26 instead uses the actual
  Gaussian completion error, literal moving support, fixed physical
  shell and positive high-index columns. It needs no large modulation
  height. Novelty is confined to that exact failed implication.
- R35.2--R35.20 provide the Gaussian convolution identities, analytic
  tails, two-height local scalar and original zero-exclusion return.
  Their growing-order tail payment is imported, not reproved or
  relabeled as new progress. The coprime Mertens input in GC21--22 is
  MG9--MG10. No new literature theorem or external provider input is
  used.
- Searches of the maintained early/late attempt indices, [research revision]/51
  deltas and the relevant creative/library sources did not locate
  the particular fixed-six primitive-cell contraction GC1--GC3,
  its unbounded small-radical field payment GC5--GC8, and its two-way
  all-dyad reconstruction GC9--GC16. This is a novelty statement about
  the inspected project record, not a claim of priority in the
  mathematical literature. The elementary Euler factors by themselves
  are not presented as a new analytic principle.

The substantive proved candidate is the combination of an ACTUAL
primitive source, a quantitative boundary estimate, and a bounded
reconstruction of the COMPLETE detector. An identity alone would
not have paid the moving lower cuts or the cross-dyad transport.
Here their respective costs are X^(.495+epsilon) and
X^(1/2+epsilon), and the complete additive energy comparison costs
X^(1.3749+epsilon) under the accepted baseline. All are below the
requested 1.74898 scalar target where that comparison is used.

The complete signed estimate at gamma=.87449 is OPEN. So is every
strict improvement below 1-c0 obtained from this route. There is no
new numerical c, no lower bound for the full signed source, no
hereditary claim under further masks, and no transfer to current SP,
RN, the cubic source or H. In particular, the primitive-cell theorem
cannot be used as though the literal unweighted complement were a
small field on a fixed shell.

The next mathematical action is to attack the exact f_3 covariance
or, if factor structure is needed, GC19 on the single primitive
original-pair cell. A proposed new estimate must beat GC22 in the
complete signed scalar, uniformly on all large dyads and with both
height variables present. The original common-prime and fixed-small-
prime reconstruction no longer needs a separate conjectural moment.

## 9. Evidence and verification record

Primary in-project source pointers:

1. [restricted provenance path] mathematical source] G1--G30;
   41,640 bytes, SHA256
   c3f53fa22e2b4d69a5bd1230c0e9aa3aa8bc0026416d781f6446386e58d022dd.

4. [restricted mathematical source] BT4/BT7/BT10--14;
   [restricted mathematical source] BP8 and
   its original-incidence positive-majorant restrictions.
5. [restricted mathematical source] R29.1--R29.4;
   [restricted mathematical source] RA11--RA13: distinct older
   norm and all-dyad recovery mechanisms used for scope comparison.
6. [restricted mathematical source] [restricted mathematical source]
   [restricted mathematical source] [restricted mathematical source] research revision].md, [restricted mathematical source] research revision].md.

The proofs above were checked symbolically for every prime type,
sharp lower endpoint, entire restoration, absolute Euler convergence,
far-left tail, all-dyad norm, finite cap and scalar cross-term exponent.
A supplementary integer check through n=3000 verified the uncut
primitive coefficient, one-short coefficients at Y=1,2,5,17,31,
h*A=f_3, k*f_3=A and h*k=delta_1. It returned all checks true.
Those finite checks are transcription evidence; they do not prove an
asymptotic moment or the all-dyad theorem. No numerical zero search or

The controller supplied the separately attributed short argument in
GC4--GC5. After the author had saved GC13--GC16, the controller relayed

### 2.5 Summing all blocks and proving H

Sum (14) in norm over dyadic M<=D and N=2^j X, retaining every block in (3). The M contributions sum geometrically to O(D) for each N; their damping sum contributes O(log(2X)). The sqrt(N) contributions sum with actual damping to O(X^(3/4)log(2X)), multiplied by at most O(log(2D)) row blocks. The far infinite N tail converges exponentially; no polynomial truncation is imposed. The low part costs O(AD). Fixed logarithmic powers are bounded by log^4(2X). Finite-measure Cauchy gives L1 from L2. This proves H and H'. All low/high, inter-row and inter-block interactions are paid by norm inequalities after each whole source estimate.

statement:
## PS2. Fixed-input affine certificate for the current majorants

Let ell0 be the root in `(0.16712007850680,0.16712007850682)` of

`927 ell^4 - 3135 ell^3 + 2433 ell^2 + 275 ell - 100 = 0`.

Set

\[
b_0=11/12-\ell_0/4,\quad
\kappa_0=(5-3\ell_0)/6,\quad
\delta_0=\frac{25-60\ell_0+27\ell_0^2}
 {6(5+4\ell_0-3\ell_0^2)}.
\tag{PS6}
\]

The input kappa is fixed at kappa0 throughout this proposition. Consider
geometry `M=x+y`, `h=1+ell-x>0`, `x,y>ell>0`, `h<=2y`, for which the
original moment/profile hypotheses and capacities are admissible. Use
the original direct majorant, including the empty-subset branch and
the triangle summation of rescaled compensator subsets, and use the
unchanged B0.46 averaged-numerator majorant for every amplitude class.

The proposition concerns what these upper-bound formulas can certify.
It does not assert that the actual sums or row counts attain any of them.
In particular, a new coefficient-specific estimate for the later paid
or unpaid sectors could change the formulas and evade the proposition.

First, S.5 with `N=1+ell,z=ell` gives the three branches

\[
k(M,\ell)=\max\{0,(1+3\ell-2M)/4,M+\ell-1\}.
\tag{PS7}
\]

The hypotheses `x,y>ell` imply `ell<M/2`, as required in S.5. A fourth
branch `(3ell-1)/2`, appearing in Liu's broader packaging, is redundant
here: it is nonpositive for `ell<=1/3`; otherwise `M+ell-1>3ell-1`.
The Gram majorant contains `(y-x)/12`. With the original signal exponent
`C(B)=B-5/6+x/3+ell/6`, the empty-subset direct estimate therefore demands

\[
B\ge L_0:=5/6+M/12-\ell/6,\qquad
B\ge L_K:=1/3+7M/12+\ell/3.
\tag{PS8}
\]

These are necessary constraints for certification by that majorant,
not necessary conditions for the actual physical probe to be small.

At the fixed critical class `delta=delta0,p=1/2,q=delta0/2`, B0.48 gives

\[
R_{\kappa_0}(\delta_0,1/2)=5/9+\delta_0/(18\kappa_0).
\tag{PS9}
\]

Write `a=(1+delta0)/2`. B0.46 at d=h is

\[
F(h)=a-y/2-\ell/2+\ell q
 +h(1/12+3R/4)-\frac q{12\kappa_0}\min(h,2y-h).
\tag{PS10}
\]

Since `min(h,2y-h)<=2y-h`, set

\[
A=1/2+\delta_0/(12\kappa_0),\qquad
C=\delta_0/2+\delta_0/(12\kappa_0).
\]

Substitution of PS9 and `h-y=1+ell-M` yields

\[
F(h)\ge H_4:=1+C-AM+C\ell.
\tag{PS11}
\]

Equality holds for `h/2<=y<=h`. The regime `h<=2y` is retained because
the original positive-length numerator capacity is not asserted beyond
it. No extension to inadmissible reflected scales is made.

Let `W=1+4A+4C` and

\[
w_0=\frac{8A+14C}{3W},\quad
w_K=\frac{4A-2C}{3W},\quad w_H=\frac1W.
\tag{PS12}
\]

These weights are positive and sum to one. Direct algebra gives

\[
(w_0+7w_K)/12-Aw_H=0,\qquad
-w_0/6+w_K/3+Cw_H=0.
\tag{PS13}
\]

Thus `w0 L0+wK LK+wH H4` is independent of M and ell. Evaluate it at
`M=1-ell0,ell=ell0`. Then `L0=LK=b0`; the second identity in B0.48,

\[
\delta_0=\frac{\kappa_0(5-9\ell_0)}
 {6\kappa_0+(6\kappa_0+2)\ell_0},
\]

gives `H4=b0`. Consequently

\[
\boxed{\max\{L_0,L_K,H_4\}\ge
w_0L_0+w_KL_K+w_HH_4=b_0.}
\tag{PS14}
\]

This proves the claimed fixed-input barrier, including admissible
`M+ell>1`. It does not cover an improved arithmetic majorant, changed
observable, or a different kappa input/feedback theorem. In particular,
it is not a universal obstruction to increasing c0. Approximate weights
are `(0.6453188308,0.1251133530,0.2295678162)`; the proof uses PS12--14,
not numerical optimization.
title: PS2. Fixed-input affine certificate for the current majorants

## R42.7. Sixth extraction improves the paid error, not the proved exponent

Define V6=product(1-R)^-1 using the **actual** b(p), and h=E V6 Rhat. The V6 coefficients at a^6 are b(a)(Na)^3; its inverse has mu_K(a)b(a)(Na)^3 at a^6. Their positive majorant is sum_a Na^(3-6sigma), finite precisely in the needed absolute range sigma>2/3. This is an explicitly defined Euler series, with no appeal to an angular-family estimate.

The exact residual is

    rhat_p=(1-R)(1-tD)h_p,
    rhat_p-1=[t(1-t)D^2-tR+t^2DR]/(1-D).             (R42.14)

For sigma>1/2 its norm is at most [t(1-t)d^2+tr+t^2dr]/(1-d), hence O_sigma(Q^-1-2sigma+Q^(2-6sigma)). The inverse denominator is (1-tD)N. Its difference from1 has the negative of the same numerator, so

    ||rhat_p^-1-1||_sigma
      <= [t(1-t)d^2+tr+t^2dr]/((1-td)(1-(1-t)d-tr)).  (R42.15)

Here r<1 and (1-t)d+tr<(1-t)Q^-1/2+t<1. The denominators are uniformly positive for fixed sigma; finite small primes cause no hidden zero. Both local series sum absolutely above1/2. Applying the full product argument R42.11 gives

    ||product_(Q>P)rhat_p-delta_1||_sigma
      << P^-2sigma+P^(3-6sigma).                     (R42.16)

Let What_P have transform exp(s^2)E V6(product_(Q<=P)rhat_p)/L. E and V6 include **all** primes; the omitted part is only Rhat. The complete field W is unchanged. At inherited beta>3/4, the second term in R42.16 is smaller than the first. Thus

## 2. Application after the exact row-dependent removals

Use the author's Q_D, with arbitrary shell-fixed |u_d|<=1 and arbitrary
shell-fixed root prefixes, retaining both e=1,p rows and q1(e). Remove
precisely each low prefix r<=c0(X/(ed))^(6/11), as in the author's proof.
Its full norm is O(D). Let z(n) be the complete merged remaining coefficient.
Every contributing physical multiplier ed is <=pD and has at most two
e-label realizations, so

    |z(n)| <= C_p W_{pD}(n),
    sum_{n<=Y}|z(n)|^2 <<_p sqrt(YD).                  (I3)

This remains true after arbitrary row-dependent prefix masks because it is
coefficient domination by a positive multiplicity count. It does not invoke
domination of one signed norm by a signed subset. The strict support
n>N0=c0^2 p^(-1/11)X^(12/11)D^(-1/11) is unchanged.

In a comparable dyadic block n,m~N, let H=X^6/N^5. The smooth-shell kernel
is bounded by exp(-cN/X^(3/2))min(1,(H/|n-m|)^2), with diagonal value1.
For every n, the full unweighted integer row sum is O(1+H). Indeed the
off-diagonal sum over integer distances is O(H) if H>=1, and O(H^2)<=O(H)
if H<1. Applying 2|z(n)z(m)|<=|z(n)|^2+|z(m)|^2 and (I3) pays the COMPLETE
block by

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) sqrt(ND)(1+H).                   (I4)

The author's independent multiplicity-local-count bound for the same
complete block is

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) [H D+sqrt(ND) E_N],
    E_N=min(N^(1/3),D).                              (I5)

Both bound the same positive expansion, including its diagonal. Taking
their minimum, then using min(A+B,C)<=A+min(B,C) for nonnegative A,B,C,
gives an upper bound by a constant times

    exp(-cN/X^(3/2)) [H D+sqrt(ND)(1+min(E_N,H))].     (I6)

No intersection of signed subsets is involved. Differences in fixed kernel
constants are absorbed into a common fixed constant and weaker exponential.

Sum H D over N>=N0 to obtain X^(6/11)D^(16/11). The isolated1 in (I6)
costs X^(3/4)D^(1/2) by actual damping over the entire infinite dyadic sum.
The remaining dyadic sum can be extended to all N>=1 and bounded without
damping. Its summand is

    sqrt(ND) min(N^(1/3),D,X^6 N^(-5)).

It grows geometrically until the decreasing third entry meets the first
two, and then decays as N^(-9/2). If D<=X^(3/8), the meeting occurs at
N=X^(6/5)D^(-1/5), where its value is X^(3/5)D^(7/5). If D>=X^(3/8),
it occurs at N=X^(9/8), where the value is X^(15/16)D^(1/2). Thus its
sum is bounded by the smaller of those two expressions. All geometric
exponents are separated from zero, so there is no logarithmic loss.

Far pairs retain the author's O(D^2) total: on max(n,m)~N the full gap
kernel is O(X^12 N^(-12)), while both the shell mass and cumulative mass
are O(sqrt(ND)); summing from N0 gives X^12 D N0^(-11)=O(D^2).
Both orientations are included. The triangle inequality between complete
low and high sources pays their mixed term.

Consequently the full source satisfies the strengthened uniform estimate

    ||Q_D||_2^2 << D^2 + X^(6/11)D^(16/11)
                    + X^(3/4)D^(1/2)
                    + min(X^(3/5)D^(7/5),X^(15/16)D^(1/2)). (I7)

All quantifiers of the author's short-source theorem are preserved.

## 6. Pressure arithmetic and the unchanged arithmetic obstruction

For DE=N, both cubic bounds contain the same mixed term:

    (E LD)^(2/3)=(D LE)^(2/3)=(NL)^(2/3).

Thus T>= (NL)^(2/3), independent of the split. Taking
`D=sqrt(N/L)`, `E=sqrt(NL)` makes E=LD and attains this order, since
`S(E,LD)=2 sqrt(NL)+(NL)^(2/3)` and NL>=1. This is a lower bound on the
available positive CERTIFICATE, not on the covariance itself.

At the stated pressure parameters

    k=.835507578307735986...,
    nu=k+.003, gamma=.001,
    ell=.170813789153867993...,

S(N,L) is comparable to N. Dividing the raw (R10) certificate by the
required `G K S(N,L)` gives optimized scale `G(NL)^(2/3)` and exponent

    gamma + (2/3)(nu+ell)
      = .673880911641069319333... .                  (R12)

The eliminated old near-band contribution had exponent
`gamma+.05+ell=.221813789153867993...`; it was smaller. With a
hypothetical two-linear-term cubic bound the same fixed-row argument
would still have exponent `.5056606837308019895...`. Even replacing
the row count K by K^(1/2) in this certificate leaves
`.256127122487201326333...`. These are diagnostics of this particular
order of inequalities, not universal requirements on a future H proof.

For comparison the actual established joint bound is

    G(K+NG)S(N,L),

whose ratio to `G K S(N,L)` is `1+NG/K`; its pressure exponent is
`nu+gamma-k=.004`. The surplus of (R12) over that incumbent is
`.669880911641069319333...`. No comparison of these upper bounds gives
arithmetic cancellation or a new zero-free constant.

On an original prime, the normalized Type-I coefficient is one and
Type-II is zero; the source stays in the unit cell D=1,E comparable N.
Since L<=sqrt(N),

    T(1,N;L)=min{S(N,L),S(1,NL)} comparable to N.

The new certificate is then `K G^2 N^2`, target-relative `GN`, exponent
`.839507578307735986...`. Recombining all signed allocations first
restores the accepted original-prime bound and its `.004` deficit;
it does not shorten the live prime source. The next arithmetic target
is therefore a genuinely joint original-row interval-vector or signed
I/II estimate BEFORE the positive fixed-R loss. The proven interval
adapter would return its exact far mask, but supplies no such estimate.

# [research revision]: square and cube cores in the actual R4 middle

G204-G206 pay two larger subsets of the actual primitive dual middle,
relative to the retained PR9 and [G185-G187](../[research revision]/primitive-low-dual-integration.md)
contracts. The complete signed nonunique companion and the middle outside
both subsets remain. The written source-relative value
`c11=312864909/2500000000=.1251459636` is unchanged.

The [author proof](r4-middle/report.md) and [independent review](r4-middle-review/report.md)
are retained verbatim. The reviewer develops original-dyad adaptive caps;
root checked the complete argument, exact source family, both primary
large-sieve permissions, and saved diagnostics. This is a restricted analytic
result. Inherited ancestry, original positive-slot uniformity and external
definition/import/admission obligations remain open. No formalization is performed.

## Source and complete normalization

Use the literal two-inverse ordered-slot free row
`F=M(D1)M(D2)Q` in G185-G187, with both sextic orientations, independent
inverse heights, and the full conjugated right copy. Put

    D1=U^r, D2=U^s, P0=U^v, N0=D1 D2 P0, L=r+s,
    T=delta L+E_K, E_K>=rho=1-10delta/[3(5-2delta)].

The box is `17/25<=delta<=7/10`, `17/20<r<47/50`,
`33/25<s<141/100`, `s-r>3/8`, `0<=v<=1/20`.
Thus `217/100<L<47/20` and `T>=123353/67500`.
The unique sector has squarefree coprime merged columns; define the exact
signed companion `R_nonunique=R4-R_unique`. Do not impose positivity on it.

Keep G186's paid low cut `U^(39/25)` and the genuine Schwartz far tail.
For each ORIGINAL a-dyad `N(a)~A`, the remaining frequency range is

    U^(39/25)<N(ell)<=H_A,
    H_A=U^tau A^6 N0^2/U, tau=1/1000.

A fixed S-denominator Delta makes `(Delta ell)` integral; its fixed unit
and character factors are retained. Constants depending on this fixed
choice do not disappear into an exact equality. On good original columns
the Delta character factor is a unit.

Expand the entire mutual-gcd restriction as `sum_(f|n,n') mu(f)` only after
the licensed formal extension. Allocate f independently through all original
colors and slots on both sides. Both residual lengths are
`X=N0/N(f)`. Restoring both roots gives exactly

    U/[N(a)^6 N0 N(f)].

There is no second P0 mass or extra f factor. Whole merged coefficients
sum the actual original factorizations. Their divisor multiplicity bound
and normalized squared mass `U^epsilon` hold for each fixed allocation.
The common Fourier measure is chosen before every live a, f, core or
power label. Natural character zeros and every original cutoff survive.

The original-color pointwise estimate is

    |B_f(ell)|^2 << H_J U^epsilon S0,
    S0=P0[D1+D2+(D1D2)^(2/3)].

This remains valid with the explicit punctures below. It is useful precisely
because merging the coefficient sequence does not erase its original colors.

## G204: small square cores with unrestricted cubic rows

Write `(Delta ell)=kappa b^2`, with kappa squarefree; kappa and b may overlap.
Fix kappa and put `B=(H_A/N(kappa))^(1/2)`. The arbitrary squarefree inner
sequence has length X. [Dunn, arXiv2403.13151v3, Section4 Theorem4.1 and
Corollary4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2403.13151v3) permits the unrestricted
outer cubic variable and supplies price `B^(1/3)(B+X)`, up to the stated
small powers. Use reciprocity/duality and fixed unit/ray classes as in the
full proof. No cuspidal coefficient theorem or arbitrary extension of
PR9 B3.6 is invoked.

Summing squarefree cores through C gives the energy bound

    H_A^(2/3) C^(1/3) + X H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).

Each independent column has this bound. Cauchy combines the two positive
outer energies once; it does not square their price again. Summing the
O(A) original labels and restoring the exact prefactor gives

    U^(1/3+2tau/3) A^-1 N0^(1/3) N(f)^-1 C^(1/3),
    U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(1/3) N(f)^-2 C^(5/6),

times `H_J U^epsilon` and the paid divisor multiplicities. This is a bound
for the actual signed restricted contribution through its complete energy
majorant, with both original coefficient copies retained.

## G205: small cube cores with paid sixth-power punctures

Write `(Delta ell)=kappa t^3 z^6`, with kappa cubefree and t squarefree;
overlaps among these factors are allowed. The character identity contains

    chi_m(kappa)^eta chi_m(t)^3 1_((m,z)=1), eta in {+1,-1},

in addition to the retained fixed unit factor. The hole at z is necessary:
a prime of valuation six still forces zero when it divides m.
Fix kappa and z before averaging the squarefree t variable. The puncture
is part of the arbitrary inner sequence; it is not dropped after taking
a sixth power.

Set `B=(H_A/N(kappa))^(1/3)` and `T0=B/N(z)^2`.
[Goldmakher-Louvel, arXiv1112.1642v2, Definition1 and Theorem1.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1112.1642v2)
gives price `T0+X`. The literal PR9 B2.24 family supplies primitivity,
trivial infinite type, the fixed finite reciprocity classes and the
equal-class coprime product-conductor condition. Its local convention is
retained in the complete reports; this is not permission for an arbitrary
quadratic family.

The alternative original-color pointwise price is `T0 S0`.
Split z at a threshold Z clipped to `[1,sqrt(B)]`. The complete cost is
bounded by

    B + X Z + B S0/Z,

with the endpoint interpretations paid separately. If the formal optimum
is inside the interval, balance the latter two terms. If it lies below one,
use the pointwise bound throughout; if above sqrt(B), use the sieve
throughout and `X<S0`. In all regimes the resulting bound is

    B + sqrt(B S0 X).

Summing cubefree cores through C gives

    H_A^(1/3) C^(2/3) + sqrt(S0 X) H_A^(1/6) C^(5/6).

The two complete normalized prices are therefore

    U^(2/3+tau/3) A^-3 N0^(-1/3) N(f)^-1 C^(2/3),
    sqrt(S0) U^(5/6+tau/6) A^-4 N0^(-1/6) N(f)^(-3/2) C^(5/6).

Both independent f allocations are divisor bounded. The f^-1 sum has a
paid small-power allowance; the f^-2 and f^(-3/2) sums converge after a
sufficiently small divisor loss. All fixed S-parts, slots, heights, ray
classes and both full orientations are retained.

## G206: enlarged caps tied to the original a-dyad

The initial author caps are `C_sq=U^(13/40)` and `C_cu=U^(3/4)`.
The independent review proves the larger original-A caps

    C_sq(A)=U^(13/40) A^(24/5),
    C_cu(A)=U^(3/4) A^(24/5).

These are fixed before live a and artificial f. Give square-core selection
priority, then select cube cores outside it. Define `R_hard,adapt` by
failing both tests. This partition applies to the original signed source
and commutes with the complete mutual-gcd expansion.

After substitution, the first A powers in the square and cube bounds are
respectively `3/5` and `1/5`; both second A powers are zero. Summing
`A<<U^(1/6)` gives first-term exponents `4027/3000` and `477/1000`,
including tau. Against the lower bound for T, the limiting second terms
have raw margins `23813/2730000` and `2768/170625`. The exact box check
uses a positive derivative floor `21481/24300`. After tau/6, auxiliary
loss `1/500`, and retained saving `1/200`, the respective reserves remain

    177/113750 and 8241/910000.

All remaining divisor/profile small powers and eventual thresholds are
chosen in the order specified by the full source proof. Near the largest
A, the caps reach scales `U^(9/8)` and `U^(31/20)`; fixed constants and
nominal dyadic endpoints are retained.

An f-dependent selector is not licensed. For a common prime p, the
unrestricted gcd weights give `1-1=0`, whereas retaining only f=p gives
`-1`. This blocks a tempting enlargement that would change the source.
The adaptive original-A selector avoids that defect.

Combining low, square-core, cube-core and far-tail payments yields the
complete signed identity

    ||F_<||_U^2 = R_nonunique + R_hard,adapt
                   + O(H_J U^(T-1/200+epsilon)).

Generic large squarefree frequencies fail both caps and survive. The
entire nonunique companion also survives. A bound for one signed subset
cannot be subtracted monotonically from another. A useful next input is
a one-sided saving for the SUM of these two complete residuals.

Even such a saving would still need the original detector return: physical
projectors, ancestry, exceptional rows, radius/K_phys, amplification,
shortenings, mesh and tails. In the retained free-row return the prospective
margin is capped by `1/200`; the actual two-inverse witness plus prefix
also retains its `1/2000` cap. Neither margin is a proved increase in c.

## Provenance and acceptance

Credit the moving quadratic and sixth-repeat strategy in
[[research revision]](../[research revision]/cubic-moving-quadratic-classes.md), and the exact
primitive source and common normalization of G185-G187. I-C3CF and
I-HECKE supply no unproved theorem here. G156/G157 concern original
conductors and do not substitute for these first-dual core conditions.

The author helper records 720 phase/zero checks, 24 tuple checks and 729
independent-allocation checks. The reviewer separately checks adaptive
arithmetic. Root read the helpers and their saved results without rerunning
unchanged diagnostics. These finite checks support algebra and bookkeeping;
the analytic permissions come from the versioned primary theorems and
the retained PR9 contract.

Nineteen original evidence/input files, 23 source bindings and the previous
raw scorecard are preserved by the [retention manifest](retention-manifest.json).
The original reviewer source-pin dates saying October12 remain immutable;
the later correction records the actual October13 review. Original missed
deadlines and all recovery histories remain. Both owners normally released
their exact scopes. No new proof packet, kernel evidence, external record
admission or endpoint promotion is claimed.

# [research revision] hierarchical idea ledger

**Persistent coverage, not a priority list.** F01–F26 are the original agenda families. N27–N29 are useful additional constructions retained from the supplied reviews. Child IDs below remain stable when rankings change. `03_MERGED_AND_AUGMENTED_RESEARCH_PORTFOLIO.md` develops the objects and quantitative contracts; Txx are proofs in document01 and Axx auxiliary results in document02. Source keys AG/SUM/M/CP/FD/SG/QD/Cj/BA/BB/BG/BM/SA/SB/GS resolve in portfolio §13 and the provenance document.

**Two labels must be read separately:** origin = carried/merged/revived/source-new/merge-new; mathematics = PROVED, CONDITIONAL transfer, OPEN estimate/construction, METHOD-BLOCKED, REFUTED, or SUPERSEDED. “Paid” means the relevant proof is available relative to its named accepted inputs. Every open estimate retains original profiles, natural zeros, finite sectors, actual norms/conductors and height/scale uniformity unless explicitly stated otherwise. No entry proves c>c0.

## Quantitative gate index

| Gate | Target / useful threshold |
|---|---|
| CUB | Whole signed remainder O(D^(2+ε)), K≤D^(1/2+3c−κ); .12551 uses .87653; existing completion reaches 1/6 with strict margins |

| FIN | K^(1+u)G^v(KG)^εT^A, u,v≥0, 3u+v<1; c=(1−u)/(6(1+u+v)); sufficient corridor G≤C K^((1−u)/(2+v)) for fixed C; (1/8,1/32)→14/111 |

| QUAD | Full CM2_θ for H≥D^(θ+κ); c=1/2−θ/4; θ<1.498 crosses .1255, θ=1→1/4 |
| APP / HARDY | Actual H_σ residue closure gives c=1−σ; repaired all-height Hardy squared residual≤32/15 gives c=1/4 via overlap |

## F01. Multiscale Möbius decomposition and signed block control

- **F01.R — Carried/revived; OPEN CUB.** Unequal two-cutoff identity μ=m1+m2−m1*m2*1+μ*u1*u2; Type I is paid with R*=Y1Y2. At k=.87653 require log_D R*<.07767875. Third collisions retain ordered Π,U,C and a long outer 1-convolution. Seek an averaged ratio-sensitive two-block estimate, not coefficientwise negativity. First test: rough two-prime full-period Gram with the actual profile. [AG A1–A3; BB R04b/C05–C06; CP §§4,7; A16.]
- **F01.M — Carried/merged; T09 CONDITIONAL, energy OPEN.** Fixed φ=(u exp(−u−1/u))′, frozen-dyad balanced μ(d)μ(e) sum. Prefer MOB's scale L² norm; retain short multiplicity, shared primes and equal Mellin modes. Children: product-difference dispersion, low Mellin frequencies, VAR norm comparison. [[research revision] V1–V10; BA §7D1; BB D01/R06.]
- **F01.N1 — Merge-new pass1; exact kernel/diagonal PROVED, saving OPEN.** MOB energy = O(X) diagonal plus complete weighted μ(m)μ(m+h) shifts; finite log-scale averaging has broad ratio support. Bound the full signed shift aggregate, or all pieces of a complete partition. Stop fixed-shift-only arguments. [Portfolio §7; T09.]
- **F01.N2 — Merge-new pass1; T05 PROVED, CUB saving OPEN.** Physical cube-row I–I is affordable with its exact completed density; compare projected remainder to C–C. Test polar differences before splitting principal/nonprincipal; bare I_Y(c)=−μ(c) cannot replace completed I_Y(ct³). [SA II C1–[research revision]; T05; portfolio §6.]
- **F01.X — METHOD-BLOCKED.** Further cutoff averaging/depth does not erase rough coefficient−2; positivity changes the signed coprime form. Escape: retain the exact mixed covariance and price every new source length. [CP; [research revision]; BG K03; BA §12.]

## F02. Large-prime null packets and common-core dispersion

- **F02.P — Carried/merged; nullity PROVED, cross estimate OPEN.** Above cube threshold each designated-prime packet has zero self-covariance; 0/1/2-prime cross sectors remain. Keep phase conjugate(G(p))θ_p(mk), opposite column, whole kernel and full period rab with primitive conductor ab. Target CUB. [AG B1; CP §§2–3,12; BA §6C2; BB C07.]

## F03. Sixth-order sparse-index and ordinary means

- **F03.OM — Merged; reductions T01–T04 PROVED, OM OPEN.** Study common-F-completed cube-free rows ab² ordered by q_a q_b²; finite ray orbit must really exist. First test ordinary face b=1 after calibrated averaging. η=3/32 gives29/228. [BA F03.A/R1–R3; BB C01/H01,C02/H03,R01–R03; SB N1–N3; BM R2.2 corrected.]

Mixed cusps/reduced indices can pay inverse wedges; they do not cover ordinary boxes automatically. Actual inverse-prime-square descendants generate new ordinary deletions. [BA D4; BB R04/C03; T03–T04.]

Full ambient positive energy diverges; a fixed ordinary loss does not imply INF. Escape: exact sparse restriction or FIN. [FD §§18–19;(63)–(73); C8; BA F03.B; BG P17.]
- **F03.Z — Revived; identity PROVED, continuation OPEN.** Positive row series or anisotropic a,b series (physical specialization v=2u), with full common-core factor and unit neutrality. - **F03.E — Source-new; conditional budget PROVED.** A fixed line1/2+e costs D^(1+2e)K^(1+η)G^((η−2e)+), not an ε. Offcentral mean and amplitude-sensitive exceptions can trade costs only through that exact budget. [BB R05/main§3.2; T08.]

## F04. Sextic reflection, physical covariance, probe and numerator

- **F04.C — New synthesis; T06/T07 PROVED, CORE OPEN.** Full same-core square function≤Z^εF_A/Y; true-gcd tail≤that×Z^(1+b0/2)L^(1+3b0/2)/G². G0=Z^(1/2+b0/4)L^(1/2+3b0/4). Remaining full small-gcd covariance includes gcd one, all marks/descendants/embeddings. [SA III–V; portfolio§3.]

- **F04.H — Carried; conditional transfer PROVED, H OPEN.** Actual e=1 short-column restriction, then every source/branch. Infinity/b=1 paid diagonals/tail do not automatically cover other H branches. Index e⁴R³P⁴ is not its conductor. [SG§§1–3,14–18;(67)–(69); BA§5; BB S01; BG R02.]

Not nonprincipal sixth-frequency packets, mixed embeddings or a positive restricted norm. [BB R08/S02; [research revision] AA19; A01.]
- **F04.P — Source-new/repaired; A14 CONDITIONAL, PROBE OPEN.** Improve actual compensated probe against its theta witness. Pair-dependent sixth-power Gram labels do not define A^(6); first construct polarization/factorization or estimate full Icomp. Stronger saving may be weakened; detached equality window is not a limitation. [GS§§2–7; A14.]

Localized zero-mode PSD fails generically (A15). Escape: actual signed aggregate, exact paid-sector addbacks or full-probe pairing. [BM R3.1 corrected; BA§12; BB S03/S08; BG K04–K05.]

## F05. Möbius-aware polar projection and spectral sieve

- **F05.P — Carried; OPEN.** Identify true residual coefficient vector in actual metric, expand residual/complement including mixed terms, and pay every polar contribution. Gate CUB/OM/H as chosen; generic sieve lower bounds do not refute this special target. [AG F05; BA F05/A1.3; BB C08/H12.]

- **F07.Q — Carried; identity/transfer PROVED, QUAD OPEN.** Keep uncontracted J_n(t), all positive rows, square repetitions, finite restoration and nonunit zeros. Generic H+D√H still loses. - **F08.A — Carried; criterion/Schur identity PROVED, APP OPEN.** Exact heavy-tail Gram of (k modn)/n; nested capture δ_j with divergent sum. First test second shell plus full future tail nearσ<b0, not only the old first-shell inverse. [AG D1–D7; C9 R6–R10; BA§7D2; BB A01.]

- **F16.J — Carried/revived; OPEN.** Extra Euler jet, second channel or repeated prime with preserved principal map; compute all6 valuations, bad places, collisions and coefficient/profile growth, then rerun full physical/numerator minimax. [M B0.29–33; BA F16; BB S09.]

- **N27.F — Source-new merged; T08 CONDITIONAL, trace OPEN.** Actual FIN-weight uses exactly-once divisors; g1 still requires OM at scaleK, while large prime rows pastK are absent forG≤K. Prove finite-window comparison then signed cross-scale bound; Poincaré only converts a bound, not supplies arithmetic saving. Fixed-width dilation intervals are fallback. [Portfolio§7.]

- **N29.L — BA/BB merged; A11 exact criterion PROVED, growth OPEN.** Log[(s−1)ζ(s)] under Cayley vs s′ξ′/ξ Taylor coefficients are derivative-related by explicit nonvanishing gamma factor. Write `||F||_U^2=sum_(free u) Phi(Nu/U)|F_u|^2`. Multiplication by a phase of modulus at most one is a contraction in this Hilbert norm; no division by a natural zero occurs. Apply Minkowski to the EXACT signed sum (3.3), then (4.1) separately to its two factors. Use the trivial annular estimate

    |M_u(E1;W1)| << H_J E1^(1/2)

on nonempty scales, with a fixed constant for bounded subunit windows. Use (2.2) for the second factor, and (2.1) for all original slots. The h sums have total subpower mass (4.2); their scales only decrease. Consequently for q of norm x,

    ||M_u^(q)(D1/x) M_u^(q)(D2/x) Q_u||_U
       << H_J U^(v/2+epsilon) (D1/x)^(1/2)
                [U+U^(1/6)(D2/x)^(5/6)]^(1/2).      (5.1)

Both terms decrease by a fixed positive power of x. In a dyadic q range x~X, the ideal count and divisor bound give `sum |a_G(q)|/(Nq)<<X^epsilon`. Summing the resulting geometric dyadic tail from G proves

    ||B_{>=G} Q||_U^2
      << H_J U^(v+epsilon) (D1/G)
                      [U+U^(1/6)(D2/G)^(5/6)].       (5.2)

This includes every q up to its genuine support endpoint; no single-prime approximation or missing middle regime is used. It also includes all shared primes between d1,d2 and the slots. The entire q label count was paid in Minkowski, not omitted through a spurious normalized average.

Take `G=U^(1/5)`. Since `s-1/5>1`, the second branch dominates and (5.2) has exponent

    E_gcd=v+r+(5/6)s-1/5.                            (5.3)

Against (2.4), throughout the closed coarse box,

      >=rho+(delta-1)r+(delta-5/6)s+1/5-v
      >=rho+(47/20)delta-393/200
      >=2809/273000 >1/100.                          (5.4)

For the last minimum, the derivative is `47/20-50/[3(5-2delta)^2]`, positive on `[17/25,7/10]`; its minimum is at 7/10. Substituting delta=17/25 gives the stated exact fraction. The companion rational receipt checks this continuous proof and its positive derivative floor; it is not a sampled grid. The slack above 1/100 is `79/273000`.

Choose all internal small losses below the algebraic slack between 1/100 and 1/200. Alternatively,

This handles every low/high cross term if a bound for the small-gcd norm is subsequently supplied. It does NOT prove that those cross terms individually have the large-gcd saving while the small-gcd norm is still open.

statement:
## 6. A precise limit of the profile-moment argument

The following countermodel concerns a proposed inference from bounded
one-variable sums, squarefree support, and the actual derivative profile.
It is not a counterexample for the Möbius function.

Let

\[
D_j=2^{2^j},\qquad
a(n)=\mu(n)^2n^{b-1}
1_{\{n\in\bigcup_j[2D_j,\frac72D_j]\}}.
\tag{SP30}
\]

Then \(|a(n)|\le1\), the support is squarefree, and for every modulus
and every bounded divisor mask,

\[
\left|\sum_{n\le U}a(n)(\text{mask})\right|
\le\sum_{n\le U}n^{b-1}\ll_b U^b.
\tag{SP31}
\]

These bounds are uniform even without modulus losses. At
\(X_j=D_j^2\), the frozen individual range (SP4) contains nonzero
coefficients from only the \(j\)-th block, for all large \(j\): the
previous block ends at \((7/2)\sqrt{D_j}\ll Y_j\), while the next
starts at \(2D_j^2\gg U_{\max,j}\).

All contributing individual factors are therefore at least \(2D_j\),
so \(de/x,fh/x\ge2\). Since \(\phi(u)<0\) for
\(u>(1+\sqrt5)/2\), every summand in each finite profile is negative.
Every expanded quartic summand with coefficients \(a\) is nonnegative,
including after the masks (SP5), (SP28).

Restrict to squarefree, pairwise-coprime tuples in

\[
d,e\in[2D_j,\tfrac52D_j],\qquad
f,h\in[3D_j,\tfrac72D_j].
\tag{SP32}
\]

There are \(\gg D_j^4\) such tuples. Here is an elementary justification
of that density assertion. At a prime \(p\), the permitted residues
modulo \(p^2\) have relative density
\((1-p^{-1})^4(1+4p^{-1})\): either no coordinate is divisible by
\(p\), or exactly one is divisible by \(p\) but not by \(p^2\).
The product over primes is positive because each factor is positive and
equals \(1+O(p^{-2})\). Finite CRT counting gives the finite-prime
density in the four fixed proportional intervals. After cutting at
\(p>B\), square-divisibility failures have total
\(O(D_j^4/B+D_j^{7/2})\), while shared-prime failures have total
\(O(D_j^4/B+D_j^3\log D_j)\). First choose \(B\) large, then
\(j\) large. A positive proportion survives.

The union of the rational near-cofactor strips excludes at most

\[
O(J^2D_j^3(K+1))=o(D_j^4)
\tag{SP33}
\]

of these tuples, by fixing one factor on an edge and then the other two
unconstrained factors. Thus \(\gg D_j^4\) tuples still satisfy the
first part of (SP28). For \(\ell=m=1\), their products satisfy
\(fh-de\ge(11/4)X_j>P\). All original gcd cuts hold, since the
tuples are pairwise coprime.

On these boxes the cutoffs are one for large \(j\), and the arguments
of the two \(\ell=m=1\) profile factors lie in the compact interval
\([2,49/4]\). Their absolute values are bounded below by a positive
constant. Each coefficient product is
\(\gg_bD_j^{4b-4}\). Positivity of all the other model summands
therefore gives

\[
Q_{{\rm far},a}(X_j)\gg_b D_j^{4b}=X_j^{2b}.
\tag{SP34}
\]

Thus a universal saving over \(X^{2b}\) cannot follow solely from
(SP31), squarefree support, the retained gcd restrictions, and the
actual profile's zero moment. The sequence (SP30) is not Möbius and
does not preserve every Möbius convolution identity; that is exactly
the scope limitation of the countermodel.

q^{-(\alpha+\beta)/2}\sum_k|b_k|q_k^{-1/2}
\le q^{-\max(\alpha-2s,\beta-2t)/2}(1+q^{-1/2}),
\]
where a zero outer exponent contributes zero to the maximum. This finite check is not the proof; FR6-FR10 give the general local argument.

Independent review accepted the full weighted mass within the stated fixed-place/profile scope. The remaining analytic target is the original signed physical covariance with
\[
R>(QY)^{4/9}
\]
and small true core gcd, including gcd one, with every original mark and unequal embedding. The true-gcd conductor in T07 is a separate object. The original numerator, contour, same-core theorem and all-height requirements are unchanged. No larger \(c\) follows from this record alone.

statement:
## 6. Exact high moment, paid sectors and positive price

On a fixed line 1/2<sigma<1 the uncapped source has Mellin multiplier

    (-1)^(K+1) exp(tau s^2/2)(1-s)^(K-1)
                  L(s,chi)^(K-1) M_Y(s)^K,
    M_Y(s)=sum_{n<=Y} a(n)n^(-s).                         (14)

The pole at 1 is canceled before shifting; M_Y is an entire Dirichlet polynomial. Its complete nonnegative majorant is

    H=integral_R exp(-tau t^2/2)|1-sigma-it|^(K-1)
              |L(sigma+it,chi)|^(K-1)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^K dt.

The shell norm is at most C_{sigma,tau}X^sigma H, and the balanced/unbalanced difference is paid by Section 4. Thus H<<X^(eta+epsilon) is sufficient for gamma=sigma+eta.

The fixed-line bound |L(sigma+it,chi)|<=C_{q,sigma}(1+|t|) follows from one summation step for a periodic character, treating its possible mean term separately; alternatively the finite Hurwitz representation gives the same bound. No reciprocal L estimate is used. Also |M_Y|<=C_sigma Y^(1-sigma). For T=3sqrt(L/tau), the |t|>T portion of H is

    <=Y^(K(1-sigma)) exp(-tau T^2/2+o(L))
     =X^(1-sigma-9/2+o(1))=O(X^(-3)).                     (15)

Indeed the polynomial factor has degree O(K) and logarithm O(Klog(K+T))=o(L) at T; beyond T the Gaussian derivative dominates it. This proves the all-height tail, not the missing central-band estimate.

For K=2m, absorb the remaining L and derivative factors into a second half of the Gaussian:

    H <= exp(O_{q,sigma,tau}(Klog(K+2))) Q,
    Q=integral_R exp(-tau t^2/4)|M_Y(sigma+it)|^(2m)dt.    (16)

The factor is X^o(1) in both bands. The exponent required of Q is eta, not 2eta: Q is already the Kth power integral. No square root is taken in this majorization.

Let N_m,Y(n) count all ordered factorizations into m squarefree factors at most Y, with N=Y^m. Every contributing Möbius product has sign (-1)^Omega(n)=lambda(n), and complete multiplicativity gives character factor chi(n), irrespective of the factorization. Hence

    M_Y(s)^m=sum_{n<=N} lambda(n)chi(n)N_m,Y(n)n^(-s).     (17)

Squareful outputs remain; ramified outputs vanish by chi(n)=0. There is no internal sign cancellation between factorizations of a fixed product. Fourier integration of the Gaussian gives exactly

    Q=sqrt(4pi/tau) sum_{n,k<=N}
        lambda(n)lambda(k)chi(n)bar(chi(k)) N_m,Y(n)N_m,Y(k)
        (nk)^(-sigma) exp(-log(n/k)^2/tau).                (18)

This is a real nonnegative total, but its restricted off-diagonal sectors need not be nonnegative.

The diagonal bound is uniform in the growing m. Since N_m,Y<=d_m and

    d_m(p^j)^2 <= d_{m^2}(p^j),

its price is at most sqrt(4pi/tau) zeta(2sigma)^(m^2)=X^o(1). To prove the prime inequality, take a pair of weak compositions of j into m parts as row and column margins; a nonnegative integer matrix with those margins exists by a greedy allocation. Select one deterministically. Its margins recover the pair, giving an injection into the m^2-part compositions. This argument is valid for every m,j, not a finite-check extrapolation.

For the large-gcd sector write n=ga, k=gb, (a,b)=1. Its exact phase is lambda(a)lambda(b)chi(a)bar(chi(b))|chi(g)|^2. The submultiplicativity d_m(uv)<=d_m(u)d_m(v) follows by splitting a composition of each combined prime exponent into prescribed total sizes; the pair recovers the original composition, so a deterministic splitting is injective. For fixed delta>0,

    sum_{a<=N/g} d_m(a)a^(-sigma)
       <=(N/g)^(1-sigma+delta)zeta(1+delta)^m.

Dropping coprimality, phases and the Gaussian therefore prices the full g>=G sector, including any diagonal, by

    C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta) zeta(1+delta)^(2m)
        sum_{g>=G} d_m(g)^2 g^(-2-2delta)
    <=C_tau N^(2-2sigma+2delta)G^(-1-delta)
        zeta(1+delta)^(m^2+2m).                           (19)

Now log N=(1/2+o(1))L and m^2=o(L), uniformly in either band. Choose delta small relative to the requested epsilon, then X large. Since G>=1, (19) gives

    P_{g>=G} <<_{sigma,tau,epsilon} X^(1-sigma+epsilon)/G,
    1<=G<=N.                                             (20)

No hidden fixed-m divisor estimate or growing-conductor constant enters this bound. The ratio tail |log(n/k)|>=L^(2/3) has Gaussian price exp(-L^(4/3)/tau); the unrestricted positive coefficient mass is exp(O(L)). It is O_A(X^(-A)) for every fixed A, in both order bands.

Put gamma=sigma+eta<1, eta>=0, c=1-gamma, choose 0<kappa<gamma-1/2 and G=X^(c+kappa). Then G<N eventually. Define Core exactly as (18) on n!=k, gcd(n,k)<G and |log(n/k)|<L^(2/3), including the same Gaussian constant. The domain is invariant under n,k interchange, so Core is real. Its complement has diagonal X^o(1), large-gcd absolute price X^(eta-kappa+epsilon), and arbitrarily small ratio tail. Therefore

    Core <= C_epsilon X^(eta+epsilon)                    (21)

implies Q<<X^(eta+epsilon). Conversely the Q upper bound implies (21), by subtracting the nonnegative diagonal and bounding the remaining omitted signed terms absolutely. Overlaps can be partitioned once, or overestimated by the already proved absolute prices. This equivalence uses eta>=0, including eta=0, to absorb the diagonal with every epsilon. It does not require Core>=0 or |Core| to satisfy the same bound.

The positive cone is also valid in the actual coefficients. Let B=floor(X^(1/K))<=Y. There are at least c_q B squarefree integers coprime to q in [B/2,B]. Expanding mu^2 by square divisors gives the positive density and O_q(sqrt(B)) error. Since a(d)=mu(d)chi(d) takes finitely many unit phases there, one phase class D has size at least c'_q B. Every ordered m-tuple from D contributes the same phase zeta_X^m. For every output n it reaches, all other factorizations have that same phase by (17).

The weighted mass of those outputs, using their full multiplicities, is at least (c'_q)^m B^{m(1-sigma)}. Their logarithms range over an interval of length at most m log 2. One interval of length at most 1 carries this mass divided by O(m+1). All pairs of its outputs have phase product 1 and Gaussian at least exp(-1/tau), giving selected positive mass

    >=C_tau(c'_q)^(2m) B^(2m(1-sigma))/(m+1)^2
     =X^(1-sigma-o(1)).                                  (22)

The diagonal and large-gcd price (20) are strictly smaller powers after choosing epsilon<(c+kappa)/2. Thus this much positive price survives in Core. The ratio restriction already holds. Also (B/2)^K<=nk<=B^K, where B^K=Xexp(-o(1)). Since W/K tends to infinity in both bands, these pairs have nk in the balanced product window (2). The lower bound is not manufactured solely from products that completion discarded.

This is a lower bound for a selected positive subcollection and for the coefficientwise absolute price. It is not a lower bound for signed Core, Q, or the physical C^bal norm. Negative cross terms may cancel it. That distinction preserves the possibility of (21), but shows why taking absolute values term by term cannot prove it: the required eta=gamma-sigma is less than 1-sigma by exactly c>0.

### D04.5 Baseline consistency and the strongest objection

The exact inverse to a has at an excluded prime the series

    (1-chi(p)z)/(1-2chi(p)z)
       =1+sum_(v>=1)2^(v-1)chi(p)^v z^v.

For log_5 2<sigma<1 its absolute mass is

    B_P(sigma)=product_(p in P)(1-p^-sigma)/(1-2p^-sigma),
    log B_P(sigma)=O_sigma(z^(1-sigma)).                (D04.8)

Hence V_(P,chi)=b_(P,chi)*F_chi as an absolutely justified field identity in a sufficient weighted range, with ALL powers retained. In the zeta case the inherited buffered bound F(t)<<t^beta with beta=.8749 therefore gives

    |V_(P_X,1)(t)| <<_beta t^beta B_(P_X)(beta).

Whenever A(1-beta)<1 this is a subpower-cost bound. On t>=X^delta, the parent-X subpower factor can be absorbed in t^epsilon. It reproduces only the baseline beta exponent; it does NOT give the smaller gamma in OPEN-D04. Exact prime conditioning is an equivalence at fixed cutoff and does not generate the needed arithmetic saving. The new theorem saves a *range obligation*, not the open full signed exponent. At the near row A=6 the baseline cost exponent is 6(1-.8749)=.7506<1.

Functional signature: actual f3*chi rough field; full smooth-part reconstruction with a paid small-cofactor head; cancellation remains in the complete signed rough field; first unpaid estimate OPEN-D04 uniformly on X^delta<=U<=X with frozen parent cutoff; proved return gamma plus q_head/complement cost. Closest record ancestry is matched-Max D35, inherited smooth-state A4/A5 and current G28/G29. Novelty claimed only for this explicit f3 all-power/head-paid contract relative to the inspected sources, not a new rough-detector architecture or literature priority.

Next decisive mathematical action: attack OPEN-D04 for one row with the full rough f3 coefficient, or compare the all-power source against a tractable signed rough-depth band. A prime-only norm or source at its own U-cutoff is insufficient. The lower-head debt is already paid; re-proving it is not the next bottleneck.

statement:
### 6.1 Conservation and the full finite dual

A usual finite signed or complex coupling has equal total row and column masses. If its additive marginal is a(n), 1<=n<=N, while its multiplicative marginal is (a*chi)(n)=delta_(n=1), the two totals are M_chi(N) and1. Such a coupling can exist only when M_chi(N)=1. At N=2, q=1 the totals are0 and1; for the quartic mod5 character they are1-i and1. A ghost/remainder repairing this particular mismatch must carry M_chi(N)-1. This refutes only that conservative interpretation, not a weighted, nonconservative divisor identity.

For a feasible version, partition {1,...,N} into additive cells I_i and another partition C_j. Let E contain precisely permitted nonempty intersections and let

    Z^0_ij=sum_(n in I_i intersect C_j)a(n),
    r_i=sum_j Z^0_ij, c_j=sum_i Z^0_ij.

Both marginal totals are now M. The exact minimum-TV problem has dual

    inf_(rows r, columns c, support E) sum_E |Z_ij|
      =sup_(|u_i+v_j|<=1 on E)
          Re[sum_i conj(u_i)r_i+sum_j conj(v_j)c_j].

Weak duality follows by substituting the two marginals and applying |u_i+v_j|<=1 to each entry. For equality, regard the marginal map B as a real linear map on a finite complex vector space. The minimum is the quotient norm inf_(BZ=b)||Z||_1 on range B; its unit ball is compact. A supporting functional at b has dual norm1, extends to the ambient marginal space in finite dimension, and gives B*phi with entries u_i+v_j. This proves the formula, including redundant marginal constraints. For real coefficients this is an LP after positive/negative splitting; for complex character coefficients it is a convex modulus/SOCP problem, not literally the same real LP. No arithmetic estimate is inferred from generic duality.

Taking all u_i to have the phase of M and v=0 gives minimum TV>=|M|. If every additive cell is a singleton, row marginals force

    sum_E |Z_ij|>=sum_(n<=N)|a(n)|,

and the actual intersection array attains equality. The squarefree unit count is kappa_q N+O_q(sqrt N), kappa_q>0, by the same square-divisor calculation as in B. Thus **full coupling TV** with singleton source rows is linear. This is not a lower bound for the TV of an intelligently chosen defect. Conversely, if two arrays have the exact same two marginals, their difference has both marginals zero: a small difference alone says nothing about the common M. Taking the arrays equal gives defect zero at any M. A useful defect argument must specify an independently controlled comparison readout and a full return, rather than infer cancellation merely from marginal invariance.
title: 6.1 Conservation and the full finite dual
