## 4. Whole complement and zero-exclusion return

The elementary divisor bound |R_tau(n)| <<_p tau_3(n) is uniform in X,tau.
The part n<=L costs O_delta(L^(1+delta)). For the whole tail n>M the earlier
accepted nonlinear tail lemma gives, for |v_n|<=A_delta n^delta,

    ||sum_{n>M}v_n f_x(n)||_2^2
      << A_delta^2 [X^(b(1+2delta))+X^k M^(2-k+2delta)],

when 2delta<k-2. Norms use dx/x on [X,2X]. This is the whole-tail statement
with a smooth positive shell majorant and two integrations by parts; both
off-diagonal orientations are included. It is not an estimate of only a
separated tail cell. Since b<=2gamma and k+(2-k)r=2gamma, choose delta after
epsilon to pay this tail at X^(gamma+epsilon). The triangle inequality for
the complete sums also pays their interactions with the retained core.

Thus, with the literal finite core

    T_tau(x)=sum_{L<n<=M} R_tau(n)f_x(n),

the conclusion is

    ||C_p-T_tau||_j <<_epsilon X^(gamma+epsilon),  j=1,2,
    C_p(x)=sum_n c_p(n)f_x(n),

uniform in tau. The adaptive complement theorem needs no additional u>0
condition. The number u=2gamma-r matters for comparisons with the old
constant cuts and for whole-core support of the deflation statement.

For tau=1 put h_p=q_p-b_p. Then h_p(1)=0, h_p(p)=-chi(p); away from the
two point corrections it equals -chi(j)(1-p1_{p|j}), with |h_p|<=p-1.
The core can be written exactly as

    sum_{L<n=dj<=M; d>B(n),j>=2} mu(d)chi(d) h_p(j) f_x(n).

Its cofactor cutoff is strict:

    j < n/B(n) = max(n/X^gamma,n^k/(eta X^k)).

The switch occurs at n*=eta^(1/(k-1)) X^((k-gamma)/(k-1)). At n comparable
to X the allowed cofactor length is O(X^(1-gamma)); the far endpoint still
has the old scale. The comparison of adaptive and constant-cut cores is a
comparison of complete signed sources with paid complements, not monotonicity
of norms under taking subsets.

The return is conditional on a complete every-epsilon, every-large-shell
L1 bound for T (or the stronger L2 bound) at the stated exponent, for a fixed
covering pair of unramified compensator primes. At b=3/2,k=6 the Mellin

    P_p(s)=1-chi(p)p^(1-s),   E_p holomorphic for Re(s)>1/2.

Re(s)>gamma, locally uniformly at every finite height. The gamma multiplier
has no zeros there. Two fixed unramified primes prevent numerator masking:
their possible common zeros lie on Re(s)=1, and a nonzero common height
would force a rational ratio log(p1)/log(p2). At height zero choose a prime
with chi(p)!=1 for a nonprincipal character. The principal pole at s=1 is
an allowed exception. Natural zeros of imprimitive L-functions stay in the
statement; conductor-uniform extension is not asserted.

For general fixed b>1 the continuation must retain every shifted reciprocal

No growing K or growing k is justified by this argument.

# Independent controller review of the actual f3 gcd sector

11 October 2026. Source: [frozen author report](gaussian-signed/report.md),
SHA-256 `60d5da9a989bf598f6757c17d88f2bb0761237e891693f0b54f52090e7c2a97c`.
The controller read the entire report and reconstructed the identities and
summability arguments below. **Accept S10–S23 as written, conditional only
on the explicitly buffered accepted Mertens input.** S24–S31 are valid
additional identities and a useful limitation. None proves a larger c.
The report's numerical choices retain its [research revision] baseline; formulas with
an arbitrary fixed beta remain the reusable statements.

## Coefficients, sectors and uniform tails

For p not dividing 3r, the local series of f_r is (1-2z)/(1-z).
Dividing by the Möbius factor 1-z gives
1-sum_(j>=2)(j-1)z^j. For p dividing 3r the quotient is
(1-z)^(-2). Thus the exact all-power convolution in S4 has finite absolute
beta norm for beta>1/2, bounded by C_(beta,delta)r^delta. This pays prime
2 and prime 3 without introducing a reciprocal factor 1-2*2^(-s).
Its constants are not uniform as beta approaches the accepted boundary.

For m=ga,n=gb and (a,b)=1, the two factors f(g) square to one.
After inserting sum_(q|a,b)mu(q), the next two f_g(q) factors also
square to one. The remaining whole field is exactly f_(gq), so the
signed coefficient of E_r(X/r) is sum_(g|r,g>=D)mu(r/g).
This proves S9 without assigning positivity to a correlation sector.
The Gaussian majorant makes the complete rearrangement absolute.

For r<=X the convolution estimate and the convergent sums in g and q
give X^(2beta+epsilon)D^(1-2beta). For r>X use the bound independent of
r, |F_r(y)|<=C_A y^A for y<=2. When D>X the ratio of the resulting
tail to the advertised bound is

    X^(delta-epsilon)(X/D)^(2A-2beta-delta) <= 1

after choosing delta<=epsilon and 2A-2beta>delta. When D<=X the same
tail is O(X^(1+delta)) and is absorbed at the worst endpoint D=X.
This independently closes the report's all-real-D quantifier.

The diagonal is the literal sum_(n>=D)K_X(n,n), since f(n)^2=1.
Subtracting it proves the off-diagonal statement. The complementary
sector retains all ordered pairs; writing b=a+h gives f_g(a(a+h))
only because (a,h)=1. The factor two and both Gaussian heights remain.
For gamma>1/2, the strict threshold
(2beta-2gamma)/(2beta-1) in S13 pays the large-gcd error and the
O(X) diagonal. The remaining one-sided signed estimate is still open.

## Prime switches and the self-containing reduction

Split integers into p-adic valuations before estimating. Their exact
local signs give F_r=U-V and F_(rp)=U+V, hence the energy difference is
4 integral U V. The V-square cancels. The p-deleted U has convolution
factor (1-z)^(-1) at p, with a uniformly bounded absolute beta norm.
Summing all positive p powers therefore gives p^(-beta), including the
complete power tail. Telescoping switches proves S19.

The decisive remaining sum is

    sum_r r^(-2beta+delta) sum_(p|r,p>P)p^(-beta)
      = zeta(2beta-delta) sum_(p>P)p^(-3beta+delta).

It converges for sufficiently small fixed delta and pays exactly the
P^(1-3beta+delta) error. S22 has the correct diagonal subtraction and
retains the signed high-gcd scalar. In S23, P>=D forces every g<D
dividing st to divide its P-smooth part s. This proves the factorization
with mu(t), including nonsquarefree t.

This estimate simplifies auxiliary prime switches. It does not simplify
away the r=1 summand E_1(X), which is the unknown whole energy itself.
Absolute estimation of the remaining summands supplies no bootstrap.

## Rational rays and their actual reach

For coprime a,b, a prime dividing ab but not 3 contributes
2*1_(p|d)-1 to f(ad)f(bd), independently of every valuation. Expansion
gives the finite radical divisor formula and period mean in S24–S26.
When 2 divides ab the odd/even signs have mean zero. Ordinary Poisson
summation of the flat-at-zero logarithmic Gaussian gives S28; its
normalization is consistent with
g_tau(v)g_tau(w)=g_(2tau)(v-w)g_(tau/2)((v+w)/2).
Consequently the main coefficient and the diagonal constant in S29/S31
are correct. The error is uniform only in the displayed low-radical
region; no sharp common-multiplier truncation has been introduced.

Independently counting coprime factorizations of n gives 2^omega(n).
The Rankin product in S30 converges for s>1/3, with the prime-3 factor
handled separately. Thus the region with arbitrary-power cancellation
already has absolute cost X^(4/3-delta/3+epsilon). It is already below
the stated near, 1/6 and 1/4 scalar targets. This is a valid useful
failure of that proposed attack on the hard region, not a general
impossibility result.

## Disposition

The large common factor sector is now paid for the actual two-integer
f3 correlation. W36 concerned a different four-factor overlap and was
not used as an unproved restriction principle. Retain the exact shifted
correlation S15 as the principal remaining obligation, plus the switch
bound as a reusable comparison. Finite arithmetic receipts check
transcription only; the argument above supplies the independent analytic
review. No formal kernel result or literature priority is claimed.

## 4. The fixed Eisenstein and literal f3 returns

### R39-E. The Hecke counting argument supplies the needed package

The statement is for each fixed finite-order Hecke character psi of
trivial infinite type over K=Q(sqrt(-3)), with a fixed **presented**
ray modulus f. Any fixed omitted Euler primes are included in f.
The coefficient is exactly mu_K(a)psi(a), over nonzero integral
ideals, including squareful and nonunit zeros.

The Eisenstein lattice with basis 1,omega has covolume sqrt(3)/2
and covering radius 1/sqrt(3)<1 in the norm N(alpha)=|alpha|^2.
Nearest-lattice division gives Euclidean division, hence class
number 1. Every nonzero ideal has exactly six generators. The
function psi((alpha)), extended by zero away from elements coprime
to f, is periodic modulo f and invariant under those six units.
A nonprincipal such Hecke character is a nontrivial character of
the residue-unit quotient, so its mean over O_K/f is zero. The
principal mean is |(O_K/f)^*|/N(f)>0.

Tile the disk |alpha|<=sqrt X by cells of the fixed f-lattice.
Complete cells contribute that residue mean. The O_f(sqrt X+1)
boundary cells have bounded total weight per cell. Exclude alpha=0
and divide by six. This proves

    sum_(N(a)<=X) psi(a)=c_psi X+O_f(sqrt X+1),
    c_psi=0 for nonprincipal psi,

The displayed constant follows from the unit disk's area and the
covolume; the exact value is not needed for the theorem, but its
positivity proves that the regularized principal pole is nonzero.

is uniform in moving f. Nontrivial angular weights are not periodic
in these residue cells and are outside this proof.

parts against the real Gaussian, or summation in unit log bins,
then proves the same C_tau exp(u) positive majorant for u>=0 and
the same Gaussian left tail. The ideal sum is therefore entire
with the required complex bound. Euler inversion on Re s>1 gives
its exact Mellin transform exp(tau*s^2/2)/L(s,psi).

Abel summation of R39.9 gives a meromorphic continuation for
Re s>1/2 and a polynomial upper bound there after multiplying a
principal L by s-1. The residue is c_psi in the principal case.
Every replenishment disk may be kept strictly in Re s>1/2 when
gamma>1/2. The Euler product at 2 supplies the same center bounds.

I-HECKE reciprocal estimate as a hidden premise.

The family agrees with root's stated finite-order, trivial-infinity
scope. This does not give a moving-conductor, angular or general
number-field theorem. A common zero-free conclusion for every
member requires the small-set hypothesis separately for every
member (or a separately proved uniform hypothesis). A zeta-only
small-set bound does not supply the family hypothesis.

The source f3 is multiplicative with f3(p^k)=-1 for every k>=1
and p!=3, and f3(3^k)=1. Thus its local Dirichlet factors are
(1-2z)/(1-z) for p!=3 and (1-z)^(-1) at 3. Dividing by the local
factor of 1/zeta gives exactly

logarithmic series have summable O_b(p^-2b) tails; 2*5^-b<1
excludes every numerator zero. H and its inverse are consequently

one must not pretend B is nonvanishing on that edge. Replenishment
uses the independently established reciprocal bound for zeta and
the bounded actual B. R39-A--D therefore prove the f3 criterion for
every fixed gamma>1/2 and kappa<1/2.

pointwise Gaussian exponent. The reverse direction simply takes

and G29--31 price the moving cutoffs only in their stated order.

 |S_(theta,L)(D/NL)|

statement:
## 2. The literal matrix source, including its characteristic polynomial

Fix an ordinary character chi modulo q, with its natural zero extension. For every real x>=1 take the actual finite divisor downset

    D_x={n<=x: mu^2(n)=1, (n,q)=1}.

Every divisor of an element remains in this set. Nonunits and nonsquarefree integers already contribute zero to mu(n)chi(n); excluding them changes neither M_chi(x) nor an endpoint convention. All matrix indices below are the increasing ordering of D_x. Let N=|D_x|, e be the coordinate of 1 and v=1-e. Define

    Z(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(d|n),
    B(d,n)=chi(n/d)1_(n/d prime),
    P=Z-I, R=Z+v e^T.

No character value zero is inverted. The matrices B,P are strictly upper triangular. If d|n, the ratio n/d has distinct prime factors. A path of exactly k prime-cover edges exists precisely when omega(n/d)=k, and then all k! permutations of those factors lie inside the original downset. Their weights telescope to chi(n/d). Thus for k>=0,

    B^k(d,n)=k! chi(n/d)1_(d|n,omega(n/d)=k),
    exp(B)=Z,
    exp(-B)(d,n)=mu(n/d)chi(n/d)1_(d|n).                  (2.1)

All exponentials are finite polynomials, so no limiting operator norm or analytic semigroup assertion is hidden here. Since det Z=1, the determinant lemma gives

    det R=1+e^T Z^(-1)v=sum_(n<=x)mu(n)chi(n).             (2.2)

The identity retains the closed cutoff n<=x and all ordinary natural zeros. It is the independently derived twisted squarefree specialization of the finite-poset construction. Wilf's Theorem2 supplies its classical ancestry, not the new arithmetic bounds below. [Wilf, pp.1-4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0408263v1).

Let K=max_(n in D_x)omega(n). If K>=1, strict divisor chains give

    A_k=e^T P^k v=sum_(n in D_x,n>1)chi(n) k! S(omega(n),k),
    P^(K+1)=0.

Indeed a strict chain from 1 to n is an ordered partition of its distinct prime factors into k nonempty blocks. For y=lambda-1 and y!=0, the rank-one resolvent formula is

    det(lambda I-R)=y^N[1-e^T(yI-P)^(-1)v].

The k=0 resolvent coefficient vanishes because e^T v=0. Expanding the finite inverse, then using polynomial identity at y=0, proves

    det(lambda I-R)
      =y^(N-K-1)[y^(K+1)-sum_(k=1)^K A_k y^(K-k)].        (2.3)

At least N-K-1 eigenvalues are 1. The multiplicity may be larger if the twisted top coefficient A_K cancels. No full-integer exact-multiplicity theorem is imported. If K=0, D_x={1} and R=(1); this is handled separately. At y=-1, (2.3) agrees with det(-R)=(-1)^N det R, so the alternating chain sign is correct.

The product of j distinct primes is at least (j+1)!, giving K=O(log(2x)/loglog(3x)). This degree estimate does not bound the value at y=-1 or the product of the nontrivial roots. Vaughan's characteristic calculation is classical ancestry only; its full-integer spectral conclusions are not transferred to this altered support. [Vaughan, printed pp.283-286](https://personal.science.psu.edu/rcv4/personal/Publications/REDCONF.pdf).

# S04 development: overlapping prime removals and the complete correction

Status: source-exact overlap identities and quantitative return costs; no new signed estimate. This develops the strongest deliberate card after the protected Fock calculation. Existing [research revision]/G81, [research revision]/G92, [research revision]/G108 and [research revision]/G135 renewal ancestry is retained.

Fix a presented ordinary character chi modulo q and a finite set B of primes not dividing q. Write P_B=product_(p in B)p and

    a(n)=mu(n)chi(n),
    a_B(n)=a(n)1_((n,P_B)=1),
    e_B(d)=mu(d)chi(d)1_(d|P_B),
    r_B(m)=chi(m)1_(every prime factor of m lies in B).

The unit belongs to both e_B and r_B. r_B includes EVERY prime power, whereas e_B is squarefree. Coefficientwise, including all natural zero coefficients,

    e_B*r_B=delta_1,  a=e_B*a_B,  a_B=r_B*a.          (R1)

At a prime in B the first product is (1-z)(1-z)^(-1)=1; at other primes it is one. The factor of a_B at a prime in B is one, otherwise 1-chi(p)p^-s. Thus R1 is not a heuristic independence statement or an equation only on squarefree n.

For finite sets A,B the exact overlap invariant is

    e_A*e_B=e_(A union B)*e_(A intersection B),
    a_A*a_B=a_(A union B)*a_(A intersection B).        (R2)

Every common prime is counted twice. For Re(s)>1 let F=1/L(s,chi) and E_B=product_(p in B)(1-chi(p)p^-s). Then F_B=F/E_B and R2 is F_A F_B=F_(A union B)F_(A intersection B). All four channels share the same unknown scalar F. Therefore the exact rank-one overlap relation cannot by itself exclude a pole: multiplying every channel by any common meromorphic scalar preserves it. This is a SCOPED obstruction to using only the overlap invariant, not to a source-specific joint estimate.

## Complete fixed-block return

For any gamma>0, finite B gives

    sum_d |e_B(d)|d^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1+p^-gamma),
    sum_m |r_B(m)|m^-gamma=product_(p in B)(1-p^-gamma)^(-1). (R3)

Both are finite. If U is the fixed Gaussian or exponential field formed from a, and U_B the same fixed kernel with a_B, R1 yields

    U(x)=sum_d e_B(d) U_B(x/d),
    U_B(x)=sum_m r_B(m) U(x/m).                        (R4)

Absolute Fubini follows on a sufficiently right half-plane from the bounded original coefficients and the finite-prime geometric series; it also follows directly for these rapidly decaying kernels. Minkowski on the all-real-shell norm sup_(T>0) T^-gamma ||U||_[T,2T] gives exactly the two constants R3. Small scales have their genuine decaying tails. Thus fixed-block exponents agree, with the usual positive epsilon buffers; a finite block has no automatic exponent saving.

Every E_B is nonzero in Re(s)>0 because |chi(p)p^-s|<1. For a precise field return, take U_B(x)=sum_n a_B(n) exp(-n/x), or use exp(-(n/x)^2). Use shell norm L^2([T,2T],dx/x). If that norm is O_(chi,epsilon)(T^(gamma+epsilon)) for all large T and every epsilon>0, then the small-x exponential tail and Cauchy--Schwarz on dyadic shells make its Mellin integral holomorphic for Re(s)>gamma. For Re(s)>1 that integral is respectively Gamma(s)/(L(s,chi)E_B(s)) or Gamma(s/2)/(2L(s,chi)E_B(s)). The gamma factors never vanish in Re(s)>gamma>0. Multiplication by the literal meromorphic L and nonzero E_B gives zero exclusion there at every finite height. Principal poles and imprimitive factors remain in that identity. This supplies a complete return but no field estimate. If B varies with X, all R3 constants and all shifted-shell U_B hypotheses must remain uniform and be paid; one cannot take a different fixed-B Mellin transform on each shell. A same-shell statement at X alone is insufficient for R4.

## Exact two-scale localization and the coarse budget

For sharp sums M_B(x)=sum_(n<=x)a_B(n), suppose a single set B=B_N has min B>sqrt N. In R1 every divisor d involving two primes of B exceeds N. Therefore, exactly at every real 1<=x<=N,

    M(x)=M_B(x)-sum_(p in B,p<=x)chi(p)M(x/p).        (R5)

The inner source is the ORIGINAL M: x/p<min B, so no B-prime can divide its index. This is a useful exact localization of the correction, not a replacement by an independently favorable rough source. If B contains no prime <=x the sum is empty. At x=p the inner unit M(1)=1 remains.

Take fixed 1/2<alpha<b<1 and B_N subset (N^alpha,N^b], and assume a bound |M(t)|<=C t^beta for 1<=t<=N^(1-alpha). Absolute treatment of the correction gives the deliberately coarse but rigorous estimate

    sum_(p in B_N)|M(N/p)|
      <= C N^beta sum_(n<=N^b)n^-beta
      <= C[1+1/(1-beta)] N^[beta+b(1-beta)],          (R6)

for 0<beta<1. No PNT is needed. At fixed beta, the best limiting b>1/2 gives exponent (1+beta)/2, which is LARGER than beta. Consequently even an improved estimate for M_B(N) does not improve the current exponent using this absolute correction. Even GRANTING a prior beta just above the current source-relative .8748540364 leaves a correction exponent above .9374270182; that prior estimate is not claimed proved here. This is a bound produced by a method, not a lower bound for the actual signed correction.

If an independently proved small-scale beta were available, reaching gamma through R6 would require beta<(gamma-b)/(1-b). As b decreases to1/2 the conditions approach:

|returned gamma|c|necessary beta for this sufficient absolute method in the b->1/2 limit|
|---|---|---|
|.87485|.12515|beta<.74970|
|5/6|1/6|beta<2/3|
|3/4|1/4|beta<1/2|

These are deliberately coarse budgets for a source estimate that is NOT supplied. A purported 3/4 small-scale input would miss even the current near target after this correction. Assuming the final improved exponent at all smaller scales merely to pay R5 would be circular unless a genuine induction with strict contraction and initial data is proved; R6 gives no such contraction.

The signed opportunity is the FULL joint difference in R5 or R4. For the same shell, U=U_B-C_B exactly, where C_B is the whole restoration field. Therefore

    ||U||^2=||U_B||^2+||C_B||^2-2Re<U_B,C_B>.         (R7)

No component may be erased because one bound is favorable. R2 offers compatibility of overlapping prime removals, but its vanishing determinant does not force the relative phase or magnitude in R7 at the required power precision. For bivariate or multi-block formulations every overlap cofactor and ordered cross term stays in this identity.

## New content and next action

The R1/R3/R4 core is classical finite Euler-factor removal, already represented in the project. R2 gives the exact overlap invariant proposed by this seed but has no independent pole information. R5–R6 are the first decisive calculation for the proposed coarse two-scale small-gain route. Their role is to prevent a false improvement from dropping the short original-source correction. No broad rejection of cross-prime coupling follows.

The next useful estimate would control the complete signed prime restoration in R5 jointly with M_B, or derive a real contraction on a source-specific space whose norm already includes their relative phase. Existing independent-error and positive-norm failures do not close that possibility. The all-character/all-height return is available only AFTER an actual common gamma bound on the reconstructed original source.
